Q&amp;A May I violate the rules of the system when I trigger another buy or sale signal? A: yes you may, that depends on your trading skills. For example trading a long after touching first time an important support would be a reason after confirmation, but it has nothing to do with the system. Trading the THV you should wait for all parameters confirmed. Sometimes I see a clear entry signal and take the trade, after a move of some pips my trade goes in red pips, what is the reason? A: No system is perfect, that are those trades that we need to cover with a good MM. What is the SL for the THV system? A: that depends on the TF you are working, as higher the TF as higher your SL. You may declare me crazy but I don’t use system based SL while trading my favorite TF, the 1M. I lost more money on Brokers SL hunting than in bad positions. I have 50 pips fixed and a mental SL that I execute manually. Where I should set the SL? A: Find the amount of pips you are agreeing too lose depending on your MM, it should be set always some pips above or below important S&amp;R lines. This system don’t show the shadows of the HA candles, how I can make to show them up? A: It is recommended to have a separate chart with real candlesticks on 4 different TF’s open to take additional trading decisions, the shadows in the THV are not shown for better overview, if you insist, you can go to the HA properties and color the 1 and 2 settings. I worked some weeks with the system and don’t need the rules shown on the chart anymore, how to delete? A: Right click on your chart, select indicators and delete the L THV indicator, right click again on chart, go to Object list and delete all objects named THV there, ready. May I add more indicators to the system? A: yes you can if you feel more secure but the system is made to have a clear, fast and stress less view to take a fast and correct trading decision. As more stuff you need to look at as slower your decision. What is the trading direction to avoid counter trend trades? A: The trading trend depends on the TF you are working with, in a 4H downtrend you find a lot of up and down trends in smaller TF’s. you should look to 15M and 1H if you trade the 5M to definite the trade direction. How long should I train myself on THV before going live? A: I would suggest for newbees to trade at least 2 month with positive results before trading any system live. Experienced traders will need may be less than a week to get firm on it. I hate to baby-sit the monitors waiting for a perfect entry, I want more action, may I go to hunt some pips on 1M? A: The 1M THV chart is for extreme scalping only and needs excellent trading skills, I don’t recommend it for newbees, if you want the action you might want to do it on a Demo account until being 100% sure to be profitable on that TF. What is the best time to trade the THV? A: The THV is a trend system and works best on high volumes during London and NY overlapping session but lately you have strong moves on the Asian session as well. What pairs are the best to trade the THV? A: all fast moving currency pairs, each pair has a different character and I would suggest trading it primary on you favorite pair, mine are the E/U and AUD/USD. What is the best pip value trading THV? A: that depends on your account equity; we don’t want to risk more than max.1 to 2% each trade. Let’s say you have a 5k account and accept to lose 1% each bad trade you can lose 50$, divided by for example 50 pips SL on 15M TF you get a 1$ pip value. In my website you find a MM calculator to find your best value. What else I should be aware of trading THV? A: All systems need good basic knowledge of FX, a system is like the hammer for a carpenter, if he doesn’t use it well he will always have bloody fingers. I recommend visiting the web page from acumen, he is a experienced trader and teaches Pivots, R&amp;S and psych levels, a good page to get better trading skills. Very important: never get motioned from other trader’s calls, only trade what you triggered by yourself, it is the only way to learn mastering your system and be successful. During trading I never post or do anything else than concentrating my small brain on my chart. Spend some bucks and time on trading education; it will be the best inversion for your FX business. Is there an EA for the THV system? A: I’m sure that it is only a matter of time till RonaldRaygun, Tdion and others will come up with an EA. I don’t believe in EA’s, haven’t seen any that can replace the feeling of a human being, but who knows? Why don’t you answer my post or PM? A: Cobra is a busy man and can’t answer question that are already explained here in the thread, don’t be lazy, re-read the thread. All other question or suggestions will be answered as soon as I can. Will be updated with the time

Here a brieve manual how to install Step By Step : Download/unzip/Copy/Save the MQ4/EX4 file into your C:\Program Files\(your broker)MetaTrader 4\experts\indicators folder copy and paste the template file .tlp in C:\Program Files\(your broker)MetaTrader 4\templates folder. Close your MetaTrader application (assuming it’s currently open … Ignore this if the application hasn’t been launched) Launch your MetaTrader application Open a new chart and right click on it, select the THV template, ready We had some issues with the MT4 V220 platform version, because of that I uploaded the basic version template, please execute the missing files in the chart manual. Hi Dennis, good question because in Yen related pairs is not 5 or 6 digits. You can define what digit broker you have on E/U for example, the price shown on the vertical scale of your chart, 1.27349 is 6 digit, 1.2735 is 5 digit.

--- 帖子 #24 ---
If your price shows the "pipettes" (as in Oanda for example = 1.26023, or 101.236 for two-decimal pairs) those are 6 digits ( FxPro is one). If your price shows only 4 decimals, or two, it is a 5 digit broker (almost all MT4 are). Edit: (Oops Cobra, we wrote at the same time, LOL)

This is precisely why an expert advisor following the rules in post 1 will fail. I've attempted to code the rules in the attached ea. Given the subjective nature of PA around Pivots, PA at potential S/R, and the individual trader's interpretation of Price Action itself, all three of which are nearly impossible to code, I heartily agree with TradeWell. Inserted Code //external variables extern int Slippage =1; extern string Ordercomment ="ap.cobra thv 1.0"; extern int MagicNumber =1776; extern bool Use.Money.Mgt =true; // if false, uses Minimum.Lot extern double Minimum.Lot =0.01; double T3=iCustom(Symbol(),0,"T3 THV",8,0.04,0,0); double hao=iCustom(Symbol(),0,"Heiken Ashi THV",CLR_NONE,CLR_NONE,MediumVioletRed,Green,0,0); double hac=iCustom(Symbol(),0,"Heiken Ashi THV",CLR_NONE,CLR_NONE,MediumVioletRed,Green,1,0); double ib=iCustom(Symbol(),0,"Ichimoku THV",2,5,8,3,0); double osma1=iCustom(Symbol(),0,"OsMA",12,26,7,0,0); double osma2=iCustom(Symbol(),0,"OsMA",12,26,7,0,1); entry rules Inserted Code //ORDER ENTRY SETUP 0-buy,2-buylimit,4-buystop sprice=0;bprice=0;ssl=0;bsl=0; if(OrderSelect(Sticket,SELECT_BY_TICKET)==false || (OrderSelect(Sticket,SELECT_BY_TICKET)==true &amp;&amp; OrderCloseTime()&gt;0)) { if(Bid&lt;hull &amp;&amp; T3&lt;hull &amp;&amp; hac&lt;hao &amp;&amp; Bid&lt;ia &amp;&amp; Bid&lt;ib &amp;&amp; shorttime&lt;Time[0] ) { ordertype=1; sprice=Bid; ssl=Ask+(50*Point); stp=0; slippage=Slippage; expire=0; Color=LightSalmon; Sell(); return(0); } } if(OrderSelect(Bticket,SELECT_BY_TICKET)==false || (OrderSelect(Bticket,SELECT_BY_TICKET)==true &amp;&amp; OrderCloseTime()&gt;0)) { if(Ask&gt;hull &amp;&amp; T3&gt;hull &amp;&amp; hac&gt;hao &amp;&amp; Ask&gt;ia &amp;&amp; Ask&gt;ib &amp;&amp; longtime&lt;Time[0] ) { ordertype=0; bprice=Ask; bsl=Bid-(50*Point); btp=0; slippage=Slippage; expire=0; Color=Green; Buy(); return(0); } } exit rules Inserted Code if(OrderType()==1) { if((hao&lt;hac &amp;&amp; osma1&gt;osma2) || (Bid&gt;T3) || (Bid&gt;ia &amp;&amp; Bid&gt;ib) &amp;&amp; shorttime&lt;Time[0]) { OrderClose(OrderTicket(),OrderLots(),Ask,Slippage,Black); shorttime=Time[1]; } } if(OrderType()==0) { if((hao&gt;hac &amp;&amp; osma1&lt;osma2) || (Ask&lt;T3) || (Ask&lt;ia &amp;&amp; Ask&lt;ib) &amp;&amp; longtime&lt;Time[0]) { OrderClose(OrderTicket(),OrderLots(),Ask,Slippage,Black); longtime=Time[1]; } }

I have traded this live for 3 days, and due to having to make teeth, I have placed about 15 trades with 1 loss due to setting S/L too close(12 pips). I have loaded the Ichikomu set-up and compared the two. Any newbie should only test this on demo, and when going live use money management not risking more than 1-2% of account balance on any trade! I have found this strategy to be successful on all TF's, but I like scalping and use the 1 min mostly. The higher time frames give a bigger overall picture, but it is also important to incorporate pivots ( Acumen's bread and butter), psyche levels, and keep the trend of market always in mind! Hi Cobraforex.. At first glance this system looks very impressive on the shorter time frames. I would appreciate it if you would answer a few questions. The only thing that may keep you from taking trades 2,3 and 4 is the Hall MA is yellow and some what flat at points 5 and 6. I know you mentioned the Hall MA being yellow for a prolong period of time might signal a choppy market but I'm not sure if you would consider this a choppy market on a 5 minute chart. My other question has to do with using the Hall MA. In the past I have seen a few systems that us the Hall MA and it looks great, painted green for up and red for down, but in real time the Hall MA repaints for maybe 2 candles before it actually sets the trend color...which will put you in the trade way too late. Now when you go back and look at the Hall MA after the fact it looks like it gave you a buy/sell signal on the exact candle that signaled the trade entry. So does this Hall MA repaint and how many candles need to close before it sets and doesn't repaint? This would be a critical thing to know if you're going to use this on 1, 5 or 15 minute time frames to trade. I'm going to give this a go starting on Monday and I'll report back with my results.

If your MT4 is version build 220, you have to copy to the "C://ProgramFiles/YOURBROKER_MT4/expert/indicators" folder all the files (mq4 AND ex4) because the version has a bug and doesn't compile automatically mq4 files on open. If you don't, indicators won't be able to show as they are not readable by the system.

OK, let’s talk one moment about one of the indicators, The Fibonacci Pivot level indicator. Those levels are calculated on the broker’s prior day HLC data, they are respected points where the PA may pause, bounce back or break and retest. They are calculated on your brokers daily open and close time, now what will be the best broker time to watch them? I have the Fibonacci Pivot indicator since more than 2 years on my chart and found it absolutely best on GMT London time (ex. ODL, IBFX etc.) All TL, HL, pivot and Psych lines work well because they are seen and respected by traders, not only retail traders like we are. They take profit, set SL or simply buy and sell at those levels, that’s why they are working. Now why London time? London moves the biggest part of the FX cake. I highly recommend not changing the Pivot indicator that is standard on the THV chart; it is very accurate, here a screenshot from today on 5M scaled out. May be a good coder can set a parameter to adjust the brokers time to GMT London time for the ones that use brokers with GMT +3 for ex. --- 帖子 #176 ---
The problem is if any indicator uses the "Point" into its calculations... on additional decimal brokers "Point" should be replaced with "Point * 10" because what the system interprets as "Point" is the pipette (or fractional pip) so any formula based on "Point" from a normal 4 decimal broker, will give strange results on 5 decimal brokers. Also, and what I think is the problem, the sunday candle will give bad results every monday if taken into account. Check tomorrow for example and you'll see that everything went back to normal... The "central part" has nothing to do... nor the MT4 version build. 1.26691 = 1.2669 = 30 pips lower than 1.2699... (beware of visual mind tricks... one can get fooled easily with things like that) I have added a pivot indicator which has the code to avoid sunday bar, maybe someone could recode the needed indicator so it doesn't take it into account. As a comment, this indicator and THV's Fib Pivots are giving me the same price for the pivot, so I am almost certain that Fib Pivots doesn't take the sunday bar in its calculations.

This is why I would like to stress the fact that it isn't a single line price but a ZONE (much like fibs and such, which have the very same problem if compared from one place to another). You should never try to get an accuracy "to the pip" when fixing targets or stops, there is always a floating margin and as I said before, better to be on the safer side of the range, even if this may mean sacrificing some pips. --- 帖子 #214 ---
SDX-TzPivots is a unique indicator that purports to be able to ferret out just the right HLC data for trading sessions not necessarily based on that of the MT4 server. In other words, if you want the "trading zone session", for the purpose of calculating pivots, to be based on London open and the next 24 hours, instead of what your MT4 server uses for open and close times of the 24 hour session, then this may be the indicator for you. I posted my upgrade to this indicator. Cobraforex mentioned to me that I should post it here and that he is going to check out how well it performs. Great! Because I started to use the original and very soon found some discrpancies. You can read my posts on it, on the Eur/Usd or Eur/Jpy thread....I won't go into it again here. Essentially I stripped it down, rounded off some rough edges and polished it.....and passed it on. I too, am anxious to learn of Cobra's results when he finishes bench testing it. The download hard code key settings are "2" for the MT4 time difference from GMT and "-5" for the NY time difference from GMT....as if to say, "Hey, I want my trading zone 24 hour session (for the purpose of calculating pivots) to be shifted 7 hours westward from 2 hours east of GMT (where the MT4 server is under KGB surveillance) to 5 hours west of GMT (where all those Wall Street Thieves are stealing our money)! Actually, maybe settings of "2" (pretty much fixed on this one unless Metaquotes moves) and "0" would be nice......We'd get to see our "day" (pivots for the day) the way the Londoners do! Hope this works....! In any case, it functions as any normal indicator would with "0", "0" settings......enjoy.

Cobra, I am surprised you use the Parabolic SARs as a scalper. They hold up most of the time on long term charts as valid trend indicator. But on smaller timeframes they are extremely vulnerable to being contradicted by whipsawing.....LARGE whipsawing. When I use them (infrequently now) I use two.....the standard settings (0.02 and 0.20) and quicker responding settings (4.44 and 4.44). Both need to be in agreement, expecially when a trend direction may be in the process. Edit: When stuff starts to happen....opposite movements, the 4.44/4.44 SARs will be the first to respond. If you get 3 TFs and then the .02/.20 SARs follows, the direction is likely changing for sure.

--- 帖子 #300 ---
Here a hint on how to get back your pips on a bad trade: I was reading a year ago the complete thread of Jacko , a must read for all traders, It took me days. The most interesting part was his Anti Hedge strategy. Let’s say you got stopped out in a strong downtrend, make a note where you had your SL and keep it sticked to your screen. Let the price fall to where it wants to and on the reverse or retrace you step in the trade again on the point that you got stopped out. That mostly worked for me but you should analyze where are strong R&amp;S levels to setup your target again. One other word on SL, never move your SL from where you have set it, you was analysing your trade before and know why you have done so. Happy trading

--- 帖子 #306 ---
Hi there! First of all, sorry for my english, cause it isn't my native On one site there are quite interesting calculations of S&amp;R levels. I'll post it here. As for me, they work very good. We can calculated S&amp;R levels for any period we want (day, hour, session). We just tak HLC prices and...do some maths. There are three types of S&amp;R lines. It depends on the movement before. So: Reduced - we expect the market to be silent. After big movements for example. R1 = ((High – Low)*0.146))/2 + Close R2 = ((High – Low)*0.236)+R1 R3 = R1+2*((High – Low)*0.236) R4 = R3 + (R1 - S1) R5 = R4 + ((High – Low)*0.236) S1 = Close - ((High – Low)*0.146))/2 S2 = S1 - ((High – Low)*0.236) S3 = S1- ((High – Low)*0.236)*2 S4 = S3 - (R1 - S1) S5 = S4 - ((High – Low)*0.236) -------------------------------------- Normal - for common market. R1 = ((High – Low)*0.236))/2 + Close R2 = ((High – Low)*0.382)+R1 R3 = R1+2*((High – Low)*0.382) R4 = R3 + (R1 - S1) R5 = R4 + ((High – Low)*0.382) S1 = Close - ((High – Low)*0.236))/2 S2 = S1 - ((High – Low)*0.382) S3 = S1-2*((High – Low)*0.382) S4 = S3 - (R1 - S1) S5 = S4 - ((High – Low)*0.382) -------------------------------------- Extended - we expect large movement after silent period. R1 = ((High – Low)*0.382))/2 + Close R2 = ((High – Low)*0.618)+R1 R3 = R1+2*((High – Low)*0.618) R4 = R3 + (R1 - S1) R5 = R4 + ((High – Low)*0.618) S1 = Close - ((High – Low)*0.382))/2 S2 = S1 - ((High – Low)*0.618) S3 = S1-2*((High – Low)*0.618) S4 = S3 - (R1 - S1) S5 = S4 - ((High – Low)*0.618) -------------------------------------- In attached image i illustrated S&amp;R levels for 19 of november. Also in attach you can find HLC.xls. It's an excel file with table to calculate S&amp;R levels. I just have made it for myself and i'd like to share it with others

--- 帖子 #317 ---
Yes some trades can be small - that is normal for scalping. I enter trades only when the 5min meets the rules AND the 1 min shows me a good entry point. From there, the rules say to TP when PA crosses the blue line or when candle changes color. I do it differently by scaling out some of my position early, then take a 2nd profit when I think it's really "turning" (subjective judgment), and maybe leave a small amount for a possible continuation - with stops at entry or better. Breakout trades would use the same criteria. If your indicators hint a breakout is coming, then THV gives you the right signals, then there is a good possibility of a breakout trade. Trading on the 1 min and 5 min TF's is what I do and what cobra has been using. However, others are trying different TF's. You may want to try 15 min as it is less choppy, but there will be less trades. I think cobra has experimented with 15 min, only using it when choppy, then going back to 5 min when direction is established. Keep in mind that I have been trading less than a year and this is only my experience - it is not necessarily THE way to use the system. Try it out on demo and leave all of us your feedback. Good luck!

--- 帖子 #358 ---
Sorry I was referring to the settings. However, we found out a better solution (as using the original Ichimoku THV leaves "holes" between lines when zoomed out): you can use the Ichimoku Kinko Hyo that comes with MT4, set the parameters as follows: Tenkan 2 Kijun 5 Senkou 8 Then on the colors tab: the first 3 colors get set to NONE, the remaining two get set to the same color of your preference, and the line thickness to 5. As Turhovach said, the Ichimoku Kinko Hyo has to be placed first on the chart so it remains on the background... so if it is much of a hassle, better to wait for the new template that Cobraforex will be uploading to his site with the new cloud. --- 帖子 #361 ---
Are you referring to the fact that the body of the Heiken Ashi candle doesn't "go in line" with the price? This is normal, as the indicator measures the relative strength of the move at each candle (usually the price level reached by the previous candle shows on the next one, indeed). It shows the price action and helps in seeing the trend because they are more regular (a series of up and down normal candles in a down trend will show as down Heiken Ashi with only variations in the wicks). Source: http://www.investopedia.com/articles.../04/092204.asp Those HAs do have shadows (wicks), though. On the THV template they have been removed, but maybe reactivating them would be of help to you? Go to the indicators properties, inputs tab, and set color1 same as color3, and color2 same as color 4. Then on the colors tab, check that they are showing correctly, if not, set 0 to the same color as 2 and 1 to the same color as 3. The wicks of the HAs will show. But neither they go in line with the actual price, for this you would have to set a color to the line graph in the chart's properties.

Amplifying the tip: Go to Menu &gt; Tools &gt; Options &gt; Email tab, check "enable" and fill out the form with your outgoing SMTP mail service data, and your cell phone mail account to receive the messages. Test the feature to be sure everything is ok, you should have an immediate response of success in the Journal tab, or any error message. And that's it! Some cell phone mail servers are slower than others, but the notification comes almost immediately.

--- 帖子 #399 ---
Cobraforex, in the attached chart note the OsMA and Trix axis lines terminate with current candle.....which makes for a chart that is easier on the eyes (reduce unnecessary lines). Another comment is note the Trix axis (white) floats up and down around the OsMA axis (green). A benefit in this is understanding that when the Trix axis is above the OsMA axis, the trend is biased to the upside. When the Trix axis is below the OsMA axis, the trend is biased to the downside. This is additional data to the OsMA picture and the Trix crossings, to help understand the trend. For example, if the OsMA and Trix were crossing up, but the Trix line was below the OsMA line, one could well expect less from any upside move than if the Trix line was above the OsMA line, thus adding additional confirmation of upside bias. I have modified the OsMA and Trix to display according to the picture....and available if you think there is merit. Edit: Added EU chart. Note the Trix axis is floating below the OsMA axis = bias to downside.

--- 帖子 #412 ---
You are faster than the police allow, lol. Let’s have a look to my private THV chart. Here I’m trying to improve the performance of the chart overview. As you may observe I gave priority to the Trix and took the Osma off and added it to my candlestick chart. The Trix in short words: The triple exponential average (TRIX) indicator is an oscillator used to identify oversold and overbought markets, and it can also be used as a momentum indicator. Like many oscillators, TRIX oscillates around a zero line. When it is used as an oscillator, a positive value indicates an overbought market while a negative value indicates an oversold market. When TRIX is used as a momentum indicator, a positive value suggests momentum is increasing while a negative value suggests momentum is decreasing. Many analysts believe that when the TRIX crosses above the zero line it gives a buy signal, and when it closes below the zero line, it gives a sell signal. Also, divergences between price and TRIX can indicate significant turning points in the market. Source: Investopedia So, we could see that the Trix give us early buy and sell signals that the THV have to confirm , oversold and overbought areas (The blue boxes) and divergence (the green lines). All this makes him a high valued multi task indicator and this change (without OsMA) will be included in the next release on Monday or Tuesday. The change does not affect the functionality of THV, we have only one indicator less to look at: the OsMA that more disturb the view than giving any great indication. I would not give too much attention on the difference of the axis of the two indicators you mentioned, I realized in the past that it could let you loose some good trades.

I hope it will make sense (I had the same settings as you and the same question): ************* non-DST here = 17:30 (GMT-4:30) USA non DST = 17:00 (GMT-5:00) broker = 00:00 (GMT+2) GMT real time = 22:00 under DST here = 16:30 (GMT-4:30) USA DST = 17:00 (GMT-4:00) broker = 00:00 (GMT+3) GMT real time = 21:00 There are always 7 hours difference between my broker server time and USA close time because both are subject to DST timezone. So in fact, the 00:00 start of the day on my platform IS ALWAYS the same as the 5pm close. Yellow start-end lines are showing a "start-of-the-day" at 00:00 USA time (EST)... Now I think this is not correct as I would like the day to start at 17:00 EST... so what are the vertical lines showing if at 07:00? non-DST (present condition) here = 00:30 USA (EST) = 00:00 !!! broker = 07:00 GMT real time = 05:00 !!! The only way for the day to start effectively at 17:00 EST is leaving both settings at 0, as there is no time shift between the broker's server time and the EST USA close. They move together. This is good for FxPro and FXDD which both are at GMT+2 (right now) and GMT+3 (under DST). I tested ODL (which is GMT time = two hours behind FxPro right now and 3 hours when DST is on) so if the first setting is left to 0, the second should be set at 2 (now) or 3 (DST). The 1 and 2 settings cancel each other when both in positive values. And they add up differently if one is negative and the other positive or vice versa). **************** I guess it is an issue with the negative and positive numbers... and maybe the sunday candle thing. I will come out with a more orderly solution later on.

SDX-SweetSpots_v4: This upgrade does away with the two fixed levels at the whole and half numbers, and allows the user to input up to four different levels of choice. By default, the first level is set to the whole number (input "0"), the second level is set to the half number (input "50"), the third level is set to the quarter (input "25") and the fourth level is set to three-quarters (input "75"). The user can change these. The user can select for each line the line style, line thickness (for solid lines), and the line color. And now each line can be separately toggled on/off with the "true/false" switch. The Range selection feature recognizes that the current price is in a base range bounded by upper and lower whole numbers. A selection of "0" for "RangesAboveBelowBaseRange" will fill out this base range with the selected lines. A selection of "1" for "RangesAboveBelowBaseRange" will also add a full range of the lines both above and below the base range. A selection of "2" will place two full ranges of lines above and below the base range, etc. As the price crosses whole number lines, the indicator appropriately deletes old and adds new ranges of lines. Enjoy.

SDX-TzPivots_v3: My apologies to Shimdax for saying a non-standard formula is used in the original. The formula used is not the standard formula for Fibonacci Pivots, but it is the standard formula for Daily Pivots. Both formulas are resident in this revision which the user can select in the indicator window. All the main pivot lines individually have color, style, and solid line thickness selection (overrides non-solid lines when greater than "1"). The Central Pivot line label shows "Daily" or "Fibonacci", depending on which was chosen. The MidPivots feature is added back and now includes line style and color selections. The feature to select lines that do not display across the entire screen is added back, but may still show lines across the screen on small timeframe charts when the "startofday" for calculations is already off the left side. Coding of lines and labels is enchanced. The selection to NOT display across the entire screen assures the lines and labels cannot exceed (to the left) the "today" Period Separator, regardless of a higher "MoveLabel..." setting. Period Separator labels "Yesterday" and "Today" now have color selection. HoursMT4TimeZoneFromGMT: Enter the number of hours difference between the MT4 server time zone, and GMT. For example, FXDD uses a server that is two hours before GMT, hence enter "2". If the server is in NY, 5 hours after GMT, you would enter "-5" ("-4" during DST). Use default value "0" for normal, non-time shifted pivot calculations. HoursSelectedTimeZonefromGMT: Enter the number of hours difference between your selected time zone to start the day (as regards the indicator's calculations), and GMT. For example, if you wish to have the day start at NY time, then enter "-5". If you wish to have the day start at Zurich time, then enter "1". Use the default value of "0" for normal, non-time shifted pivot calculations. Show_1Daily_2FibonacciPivots: Either formula can be used to produce the main pivot lines. Resistance/Central/Support Pivots: Coding enhancement allows user to select color, style and solid line thickness individually. Style entries: 0=solid, 1=dash, 2=dashdot, and 3=dashdotdot. A thickness setting greater than "1" will override any non-solid style setting and display a solid line of that thickness selected. MidPivots: Select color and style for these lines and turn them on or off. YesterdayTodayLabelsColor: Color the "Yesterday" and "Today" labels for the Period Separator lines. These labels will display when the Period Separators are selected. PeriodSeparators: Enter the color and line style of choice for the Period Separators. The choice of "true" will place a pair of vertical lines on the chart showing the start and stop of the new 24 hour period you have selected for calculating pivots. Choosing "false" cancels display of the pair of lines and their "Yesterday" and "Today" labels. PivotLineLabels: Enter the color and font size of your choice. FullLinesWithMarginLabels: "true" displays lines across entire screen with labels in the right margin. "false" displays lines starting at the "Today" Period Separator. PivotLineLabelsIncludePrice: Lines are always labeled R#, PV, or S#, but selecting "true" will add the price. Remember, on full screen lines, even if the price is not displayed it appears in the line label in the right margin of the chart. MoveLabels_LR_IncrDecr: Increasing the number moves the line labels to the left on the chart. Decreasing the number moves the line labels to the right on the chart. This feature is inoperative in the original indicator. If "false" is selected for "FullLinesWithMarginLabels", the labels will only display to the right of the "Today" Period Separator, no matter how large a number is input. ShowComment: If "true" then key prior day and current day data appears in upper left of chart. Enjoy. - Traderathome, November 24, 2008

There are seven "ObjectMove" functions in the Pivots indicator(the one preceded by // isn't operative though, so it would be 6 of them): //+------------------------------------------------------------------+ //| Helper | //+------------------------------------------------------------------+ void SetLevel(string text, double level, color col1, int linestyle, int thickness, datetime startofday) { int digits= Digits; string labelname= "[PIVOT] " + text + " Label", linename= "[PIVOT] " + text + " Line", pricelabel; // create or move the horizontal line int Z = OBJ_TREND; if (FullLinesWithMarginLabels == true) { Z = OBJ_HLINE; startofday=0; //if not = 0, then lines extend only from start of yesterday } if (ObjectFind(linename) != 0) { ObjectCreate(linename, Z, 0, startofday, level, Time[0],level); ObjectSet(linename, OBJPROP_STYLE, linestyle); ObjectSet(linename, OBJPROP_COLOR, col1); ObjectSet(linename, OBJPROP_WIDTH, thickness); } else { ObjectMove (linename, 1, Time[0],level); ObjectMove (linename, 0, startofday, level); } // put a label on the line if (ObjectFind(labelname) != 0) { //ObjectCreate(labelname, OBJ_TEXT, 0, MathMin(Time[BarForLabels], startofday + 2*Period()*60), level); ObjectCreate(labelname, OBJ_TEXT, 0, Time[MoveLabel_LR_IncrDecr], level); } else { // ObjectMove (labelname, 0, MathMin(Time[BarForLabels], startofday+2*Period()*60), level); ObjectMove (labelname, 0, Time[MoveLabel_LR_IncrDecr] , level); } pricelabel= " " + text; if (LineLabelShowsPrice &amp;&amp; StrToInteger(text)==0) pricelabel= pricelabel + ": "+DoubleToStr(level, Digits); ObjectSetText(labelname, pricelabel, LineLabelFontSize , "Arial", LineLabelColor); //line labels } //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ //| Helper=draws vertical timelines &amp; gets "yesterday/today" from elsewhere and displays them.| | //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ void SetTimeLine(string objname, string text, int idx, color col1, double vleveltext) { string name= "[PIVOT] " + objname; int x= Time[idx]; if(ShowNewPeriodSeparators == true) { if (ObjectFind(name) != 0) ObjectCreate(name, OBJ_TREND, 0, x, 0, x, 100); else { ObjectMove (name, 0, x, 0); ObjectMove (name, 1, x, 100); } } ObjectSet(name, OBJPROP_STYLE, SeparatorLineStyle_01234); ObjectSet(name, OBJPROP_COLOR, NewPeriodSeparatorsColor);//vertical separators ObjectSet(name, OBJPROP_WIDTH, 1); if (ObjectFind(name + " Label") != 0) ObjectCreate(name + " Label", OBJ_TEXT, 0, x, vleveltext); else ObjectMove (name + " Label", 0, x, vleveltext); ObjectSetText(name + " Label", text, 9, "Arial Bold", Black); //"yesterday" and "today" labels } //------------------------End Program-----------------------------------------------------------------

Just be assured that you have set (in the settings) FullLineswithMarginLabels to FALSE. This is the condition which causes the indicator to give the "objectmove" time error. Anyway we don't need the pivots to go back down to euro's creation On the other hand, here's the MMPrice modified for FxPro (though I don't think this could be causing any slowdown but as I modified it for myself at the very start, I really don't know.) If you want the price to show bid/ask colors, just set it to "true" in the properties. If you don't and neither like my hot pink setting for the fixed color, just change it under the "default font color" line. This indicator will show 5 decimals (full FxPro price). You can change the font size as well, I have reduced it because I like it better that way. Before copying it to your indicators folder, please rename the old one (BOTH exq and mq4) to MMPrice THV.OLD and MMPrice THV.OLX so in case you want to change again you don't lose track of which indicator is what. Don't change the main name though of the present one, as the template won't recognize it under a new name. When the final updated template is definitive, I could spend some time making several versions for different brokers conditions. Another good idea is to have all the working indicators in the first post so it's easier to redirect newcomers to the latest versions.

Greetings! I just finished reading every single post made on this thread today since midnight. Lord have mercy, do I ever have a headache! Jeez Louise, I feel like I've created a monster, or, at the very least was involved in aiding and abetting the same. A couple of months ago I posted a chart of what I thought was a very simple, straightforward method of trading (scalping) a one/five minute chart. Below is an example. Since then this very simple, methodical scalping system has certainly gone through a bit of an evolution, and that's putting it mildly. CobraForex, Doblece, TraderatHome and others have gone to extraordinary efforts to create a system in MT4 which took off on my original, simple technique. For that, they need to be commended. They have truly made a significant contribution . I can't help but think Cobra's trading has suffered as a result of all the man-hour's he's put into coding and fielding the myriad of questions that have cropped up since his initial posting of the code for this system on his website. How he could continue with his method of trading while at the same time doing all this other work is beyond me. That being said, I really think now may be a good time for everyone to step back and take a deep breath. Assimilate what's been given you, relax, and experiment with what you've got, understand it and practice trading it. Speaking for myself, this thing has gotten way to complicated for my tastes. It certainly is NOT the simple system I outlined those few short month's ago. Again, that's just MY opinion. For others, it may be the perfect cup of tea. I've been trading for a very long time. And one thing I've noticed (among many things, obviously), is that we, as trader's, or maybe more appropriately, as human beings, have a tendency to overcomplicate the simple. We have this uncanny ability to turn something very simple, very easy, into something that's the exact opposite. Why we do this I have no idea, but we do. That much is clear. And, I'm afraid, that's exactly what I'm seeing here. Some of the most valuable advice I've been able to grasp is that the more complicated something is, the less chance one will have at being successful in using it. Once again, I'm not taking anything away from those who have put this thing together. They've done and continue to do a good job. I really, really do think, however, that its time for everyone to take a collective breath, step back, understand what's been put together here and just start trading the bloody thing. Equally important, cut Cobra some slack and allow him the time to get back to doing what he needs to do, and that is trading his own account The man's given way beyond the call of duty… Best regards to All, Bo

While I was at it, for the "Fibonacci" selection (not the "Daily"), I added two extra levels of R &amp; S, as well as the corresponding Midpivot lines....worked well today. These extra levels are not in the indicator window as they will automatically display the color of R3/S3 but with extra and increasing line thickness. If R3/S3 are single thickness non-solid lines, then R4/S4 will be solid with thickness 1, R5/S5 will be solid thickness 2. If R3/S3 are solid lines with single thickness, then R4/S4 will be thickness 2, R5/S5 thickness 3. Another change is that styles selected other than solid are NOT overridden when the solid thickness is &gt;1, they will display anyway. When the line style is reselected to solid, the solid line will be per the existing thickness setting. I hope this solves the problems. Please provide feedback. I intend to give R&amp;S levels 4 and 5 the individual choices of the other pivots, but in another release. I wanted to get this out to see if the problems are solved.

Being on EST myself, if I want data points to be midnight to midnight EST, since MT4 server is GMT +2 hours, I have to use +2, -5 settings (EST is GMT -5 hours). That yields the 1.2953 central pivot value. If I want to leave well enough alone and just go with Metaquotes server (midnight to midnight using GMT +2 hours) then I can use +2, +2 settings, or 0, 0 settings, which yield the 1.2982 central pivot value. IMHO this is all just splitting hairs anyway. In some previous post CobraForex suggested EST was maybe the best time for data point collection (midnight to midnight EST), which for me is the 2, -5 setting. For all we know, the biggest money traders may not even be using the Fib pivots, but the Day pivots instead! For me to get the 1.2971 central pivot value, then I have to use settings +2, 0 which is like saying I want to shift from Metaquotes server time data point collection, to London time instead! Ok, maybe that is what we all should be doing, if we want to be "on the same page"?

This has been bugging me for a while (should it? ). I am never sure if I am dealing with the right pivots. It creates more hesitation to enter a trade. My understanding is that pivots should be calculated at close of market ET. That then would be 5 pm, or 2200 GMT. That is why I set mine to -2, so it would calculate based on that time. Investopedia says: Because the forex market is a 24-hour market, there is often confusion about what time of day to use when calculating the closing price of one trading session and the opening of another. The generally accepted times used when calculating pivot points is 23:59 GMT for the close of a trading session, and 00:00 GMT for the opening of the new session. Actionforex website changes at 5pm ET, 2200 GMT. At forex-internet.com: The Forex day starts with the opening of Sydney’s (Australia) Forex market at 5:00 PM EST (10:00 PM GMT / 22:00), and ends with the closing of New York’s market, a day after, at 5:00 PM EST (10:00 PM GMT / 22:00). I know there are variations from broker to broker, but I think more of the discrepancies lie with these close times. There has to be a commonly used time or else we all have different pivots, then what's the point of having them? edit: ak4x also uses 5pm est and has just posted pivots on the EURUSD thread

--- 帖子 #669 ---
I am questioning the time basis of calculation, not the type of pivot. ak4x uses 5 pm ET, which would be -2,0 on my charts. It may not make a difference today but "yesterday" (market yesterday) it did, as evidenced by my last posting of our pivot discrepancies. For instance, the two hour difference between New York close and GMT 2400 would matter if between those two times the close changed substantially. Since pivot is H+L+C/3, every difference of 3 pips in close creates a difference of 1 pip in pivot. So a difference in close of, for example, 60 pips, creates a pivot change of 20 pips. Most of the time it would not make much difference.

--- 帖子 #670 ---
What a headache those different timezones are! Just to explain why it is accurate: 5pm EST = 2200 GMT (now at non-DST time) AND broker time is at "GMT+2 " hours (and NOT GMT 02:00!) that is: the broker is at 00:00 when GMT is at 22:00 and EST at 17:00 or 5pm.

--- 帖子 #679 ---
Yes, that is something interesting. And with the TzPivots it is easy since the indicator uses GMT as the base and references both the source (MT4 server) and destination (our choice, which is the point here) from the GMT base. If I want to experiment with setting up for the Asian session, basing it on Tokyo time (GMT +9 hrs), all I do is use the settings +2, +9......+2 since Metaquotes MT4 server is on that time, and +9 since Tokyo is nine hours ahead of GMT. Anyone, no matter where they live, if they are on the MT4 GMT +2 hrs server, can use these settings. For the Euro/London session (which is at GMT=0), settings would be +2, 0. The +2 setting for the MT4 server will never change, but the second number will change based on its timezone difference from GMT. So, setting up for US session based on EST, use +2, -5 since EST is GMT -5 hrs.

I can give you my opinion while you are waiting for cobra. The THV system is a very simple system with very simple rules. However, as with any system, trader experience is important also. In addition, cobra recommends having another chart open to be able to see "normal" candles because the ones in THV are not usable for standard candle analysis. Of course, you should always include fibs, s/r and psych levels on the second chart (you may already know but i wrote that in case you or someone else didn't). At times, for experienced traders, you can change the rules of THV to make it more aggressive (and risky). For instance, you can make your trade before the blue line crosses the hull and after the candle crosses the blue line. Again, that is risky, but an experienced trader could make it work. A trader could even add other rules, as I do, depending on experience and risk tolerance. My additional rules makes it more conservative. The point is, as you say, you can always add more confirmations which makes the trade more or less conservative. However, these are not added to THV because it goes back to the problem of the different candles. Fibs need to be drawn with normal candles and those plus the candles themselves could not be placed on the same chart. cobra can probably give you more tips but no indicators will be a substitute for experience and THV can't become so cluttered with extra indicators that less experienced traders can't use it. THV was intended to remain "clean" and simple. Perhaps you could add any suggested indicators yourself to your THV template, thus it is your own customization. However I don't know how you would add the normal candles. I am not so experienced so maybe someone who is can add something more of value to you. Good luck and keep trying.

--- 帖子 #722 ---
Yes it can be done. There are three kind of alerts possible on MT4: "alert" = pops up a window and plays a sound You can add any values, separated by commas. It can be up to 64 parameters. For example: Code: Alert (Symbol(),"(blank space) ",Period(),"text of the alert", Close[0]); This would print like this on the popup if on an EURUSD chart in M1 TF and current candle closing at 1.2631: Alert pop text box + sound: "playsound" = only plays the selected sound Code: PlaySound ("nameofsound.wav"); You can add any sound you wish to the "sounds" folder, provided it is in wav format. If you want a voice, there's a cool demo here at AT &amp; T where you can record text to voice and save it in wav format with very good quality. They have 15 voices (male and female, various languages) http://public.research.att.com/~ttsweb/tts/demo.php "send mail" = sends an email through the configured email parameters (you have to set up this first on your platform). Here's the Meta Editor sample for sendmail: Inserted Code double lastclose=Close[0]; if(lastclose&lt;my_signal) SendMail("from your expert", "Price dropped down to "+DoubleToStr(lastclose,Digits)); Where the first text is the title, and the second the body of the email. An alert (any of these) can be programmed to be triggered when a particular condition is met. It is easy to include the line in the code just after the condition to be met. There is also a Send FTP function though I don't think it would be of use as an alert. (sends a file to a server address) You can have both Alert OR Playsound WITH SendMail. Alert and Playsound can be triggered sequentially but only in an EA, by setting a delay between both (if not, only the Alert would sound). However, you can use any of those simultaneously with SendMail (you can test this also in the Alerts tab of the Terminal window, by setting two alerts at the same price or time both to sound and mail)

The rules are simple (I have copied them complete for you at the end of this post). Though you could use the Trix for a riskier entry as it indeed usually shows the changes much earlier, I think it is better to follow the rules, at least while we are learning the system and adapting ourselves to its characteristics, in order to maintain a consistency throughout all our trading experience. It is not an inmediate signal of reversal, but a heads up. In both entries you show in your chart with a yellow vertical line, all the conditions for an entry are met: Trix has crossed before, showing the "early possible trend change", and: Besides, Hull and T3 are close and almost parallel and this is a good sign for a successful entry. Be aware that when you are trading on such a small timeframe as M1, strong changes in trend occur constantly and so RSI is prone to show overbought/oversold conditions more often than in other higher timeframes. Exactly... Conditions aren't met yet, but of course if you're highly risk tolerant and you got a gut feeling and your MM allows to "test" a particular entry without much damage...... but this wouldn't be following the system with discipline. Under this premise, a loser trade entered by the rules is a better trade than a good trade entered outside of the system... However, and as scalpers, there are sometimes where rules can be slightly bent... but this only will come with experience and total mastery of a particular system. It is not recommendable to tweak here and there until you master it completely as it is and with its rules. Well, that is only my opinion anyway (Please re-read the rules in the first post, FF won't let me quote so long a text. Sorry and thanks.)

--- 帖子 #752 ---
Impatience, anxiousness and impulsivity (the "need for action") are the most difficult issues to master in Forex (as well as following rules and discipline). Waiting for a perfect setup can be boring, a clear focus is needed and has to be sustained, and sometimes it just doesn't happen.... or it happens when we've already diverted our attention out of tiredness or boredom... (best setups for me usually happen when I finally decide to go to bed, lol...) One has to know when to focus and when to release focus, be able to alternatively hold and let go, and this takes hours of screen time to finally assimilate the feeling of "being in sync" with the market (even if we might sometimes be wrong) and feel confident that whatever occurs, we did our job well and as it was intended to be done. The system is the edge... the core has to be consistency, and above all a good money management. With this, the trader ends being "the edge" him/herself and can master any situation.

--- 帖子 #757 ---
Provided that your broker allows scalping, I don't see why it would be "abnormal". Though you can change the conditions of a trade if you see it has potential for developing in a higher timeframe, I think you should stick to a defined timeframe of your choice, and set up the parameters (stoplosses, MM, etc...) in regard to that specific timeframe. For example, if one uses the ATR (average true range) as a measure of the needed stoploss, it can vary from 15-20 pips on M15 to 350+ pips on monthly... so define that first, as stops set should NEVER be moved (usually the first impression is the good one - no second guessing running trades, this is my opinion anyway). Scalping is usually referred to as: very frequent and very short time trades (usually a few minutes) executed on M1 or M5 timeframes and usually for a few pips (1-5). Of course if the trade develops and goes on, one can decide to continue in the trade and have several options (scaling out or trailing stops, etc...) I don't know (as you don't mention which one you're using) if your platform allows for trailing though. This is something I have had to deal with (principally because I wasn't sure that my broker would allow so many short timetrades - now I know that scalping is allowed as they have changed lots of conditions, like for example SL, trailings and TP at 2 pips distance...) and mostly also because when I started trading, my teacher had the idea that "scalping wasn't trading", that trading had to be done on higher timeframes (H4-Daily preferrablly) and the whole lot of prejudices and wrong ideas about what is correct or "normal" and what is not. For example, on 100 positive trades, I can have 3 or 4 "long runs" (more than 150-200 pips), a dozen higher than 40 pips, a few dozens of 1 and 2 pips trades (mostly stopped out on "entry stop") and the core 50-60% is composed of trades between 7 and 25 pips. I usually tend to close early, this is why I have set a daily target in pips, instead of expecting an infinite number to be reached and feel frustrated if "I did it again"... I'm working on it though, it usually happens when I've had to wait too much for a trade to develop and I want out as soon as it comes on my favor... Anyway I say to myself that "there's no early", as pips are there all over the place and opportunities arise all day long. The thing is to be there and alert to enter with the best and safer entry point possible so to keep on the trade the longer time possible. But if you "cash out" quick, at least be as quick or even quicker to stop your losses given the case... don't let losses grow out of hope. I have been an expert at this Some scalpers never take more than 5 pips at a time and can perform 100+ trades in a day. Some long term traders entered a position in January and keep on checking and moving stops if needed. Some other intraday traders have a series of different approaches. But in the end the important thing is that you're here to make pips, and 10 times 1 pip is as good as 10 pips, it will all depend on your personal perception and your goals. Scalping is not easy (though one can be out very fast so maybe it's safer... if one is swift enough to get in and out rapidly at the right time). It depends on your personality, for example I used to trade on longer timeframes when I had more capital, now I'm mostly scalping for a faster capitalization, and besides I need a system that doesn't require for me to be monitoring a trade for hours or days. There is no "normality", there are as much different styles as traders exist. 1. I do that until the trade has at least 10-15 positive pips. Depending on the market conditions, I will then set a stop at entry and let it develop. If I see it goes against me, I'll close no matter how many pips are left. I have a mental stop at the correct level of risk so to close as soon as the price reaches that level against me. However, I have very few real losers because I try to close at 0 and price always oscillate around my entry enough to allow me to do so. This is quite risky though in case there is a connection problem, but I prefer mental stops as they are often run through if fixed, especially if very tight as the ones I use (8-15 pips max - I trade on M5-M15 with an eye on M1). (question 2 replied ) I usually trail the stop manually now (I used to work with the trailings but only do it now if I am not going to monitor the trade personally) and set them with the parabolic SAR on M5 (0.04-0.2) three candles behind the current candle. I also use S/R levels and other trendlines, etc... to gauge the possible place for a safe trailed stop. Trading the 1 min chart requires indeed very tight stops. Whipsaws are frequent. I do not trade the 1min chart myself because my finger wouldn't be fast enough, lol... but I can manage M5-M15.

I hear what you are saying. I use entry orders when we are about to bounce or cross a fib or psych level. I anticipate, with THV, an entry that corresponds to entry as it will happen. I also have to mention I am on satellite internet which has a 1-2 second delay so that has created problems for me. This tactic helps me get around that.

--- 帖子 #882 ---
Regarding TRIX....the larger the TF, the more significant. Line crossings, one over the other are most significant the farther from the zero line they happen. Both lings crossing the zero line tells you where the bias, or tendency is, which you might not want to be trading against. Lines can cross each other far out from the zero line and be a righteous call about the PA reversing (for a while). And the PA can reverse, but this may not be long lasting on shorter TFs, as the lines can come to proximity of the zero line and cross each other again without crossing the zero line iteself. The PA reverses again. The lines start moving away from the zero line and farther out again, cross each other once more and proceed back to the zero line. It is often this second (sometimes third, if stubborn not to breech the zero line) that the lines crossing each other (multiple times while remaining on one side of the zero line) becomes truely predictive of a longer move. At least this has been my experience.

--- 帖子 #883 ---
A fast trigger finger is funny but can cost you your account balance. Try to take only the best trades. That means a break and retest of important R&amp;S levels. Draw TL's and watch out for Fibs after large moves. Look the chart, the first yellow box was a good setup but the second, the red box, breaking the DP and retest it was a perfect setup. --- 帖子 #884 ---
And, yes, keep an eye on the trend line of the tops, or of the bottoms these TRIX lines create. That in itself is another clue of bias. A series of rising "tops" never lasts. When you see it as a result of long run of waves in one direction, and then you see the next "top" is lower than the last, and the PA did a lower high than the last, this can be predictive of further PA highs that are lower than the last......more trust that the "reversal" will continue.

--- 帖子 #886 ---
Overall, and this can be contrary to the quick scalper, possibly a good rule of thumb would be.....only go long if the TRIX lines are doing their thing above the zero line, remembering there might only be 1-3 good times up there. Reverse this logic for shorts. And the only time you violate this is, for example, go long if the TRIX lines cross each other below the zero line IF the crossing is sharp, and the angles of both lines are steeply heading towards the zero line, and the crossings happened a good distance AWAY from the zero line.....this is like trying to pick a real top, or bottom, at least on the TF chart you are on. In otherwords, don't go long when the TRIX lines are doing their thing below the zero line until they have done so for two or more crossings down there, and only then iif you see what looks like a sharp crossing from a nice distance below the zero line, with good angle and separation heading back to the zero line. This can all be very subjective, and relative to what has gone before on the TRIX scale.

--- 帖子 #921 ---
My only comments would be as follows: RSI in the THV system indicator window is not a line but rather green and red "worms" that only show up when RSI is oversold or overbought. The red and green lines in the indicator are both T3 TRIX. The green is a faster trix and the red is a slower trix. Read through this site thoroughly to get a good idea of how trix works: http://www.investopedia.com/articles...2.asp?viewed=1 From my experience, if you want to use the trix in and around the 0 for long and short calls, in addition to your other analysis and THV setup, then it is safer and probably more accurate to rely on the slower trix - the red trix. I can post dozens of charts where the green trix goes in and out of the 0 for misleading trades. For divergence calls, from my limited experience, [doblece, tradewell, cobra and traderathome might elaborate] it is usually the red trix that indicated the reversal. Trading the trix crosses, of one another and the 0, in combination of the THV is something that was discussed on the thread earlier. I think we came to the conclusion that that strategy is based on higher risk tolerance and would probably require more technical analysis. The jist of my post is that I believe that the slower trix, the red one, is more of a reliable indicator when used as a momentum indicator passing through 0. Any comments? You know what...I take back what I said. I should leave it to the more experience to discuss this. I usually use trix to note oversold and overbought and for divergence, I use the red trix cross of 0. I looked at a 5 min chart and I am not yet comfortable with the green trix as an indication of a setup just yet. I need to review the previous week or more...good thoughts though. I would wait for one of the others to comment before anyone adopts this as a supplemental strategy.

Good points Cashmeer, but remember this is not an exact science. Sometimes it might be better to exit by following the green trix line, sometimes it might be better when the price breaches the aqua, as THV indicates. Price action is always different. Even if you are better off exiting one way for a whole month, the next month the currencies personality may change a little, and you might be better off with THV exit. Either way, neither way would be a mistake. The trick is to make money long term, not to agonize about squeezing every pip out of every trade, as this is not possible and nobody can do it consistently long term. --- 帖子 #960 ---
The most important thing about MM is determining how much are you willing (or can you afford) to lose on a single trade. As Cashmeer said, anywhere between 1% and 3% is reasonable, and it has then to match the particular timeframe you will be using, as well as the number of lots (full, mini or micro) that you will be able to place for that trade. For example, it is quite usual to employ ATR (average true range) indicator to calculate probable stoploss, for example, 2*ATR(20) which in a M1 TF have been ranging (on EURUSD) between 4 (8) and 9 (18). So let's say that a max SL of 20 pips would be quite safe. Then, how much do those 20 pips represent in $ on your position? 1 microlot = 20 x 0,1 = $2 1 minilot = 20 x 1 = $20 1 lot = 20 x 10 = $200 Let's say that you have a total capital of $1000 and will to risk 2% on each single trade, which would be $20, your position shouldn't be higher than 1 minilot ($1 per pip). Now, if you are able to trade microlots, you can increase the SL as much as you decrease the number of lots traded. But always with the maximum risk in mind, and of course, also matching the risk to the potential reward (it wouldn't make much sense to have a 100 pips S/L for a 5 or 10 pips potential gain, for example). In that ATR based S/L calculation you also have to take S/R into account, both sides, as Cashmeer said.

--- 帖子 #1057 ---
Here is a very simple way to get the longer term trendline (say, from a 1 hour chart) and put it on the trading chart (say, 5 minute chart). Go to your 5 minute chart, switch it to a 1 hour chart. Draw the trendline(s). Switch it back to the 5 minute timeframe. You are ready to go! This is best done using regular candlestick charts, or the heiken ashi THV chart with the candle shadows, or wicks. If you attempt to draw trendlines without candle shadows, especially if first on a long TF chart and then reduce the chart to a small TF, you can be substantially off because you were off to begin with on the large TF chart that had no candle shadows to help you be more exacting.

--- 帖子 #1065 ---
I think that it's better to specialize in one or two pairs to be able to grasp fully their own characteristics and style of Price Action, however you can do that study individually on demo for each of the pairs you are interested in. Unless you use a pure mechanical system that doesn't involve your direct decision, or use very long timeframes (and have a huge equity balance) trading on discretion, even with strict rules, with so many pairs can become a really stressful task.

--- 帖子 #1066 ---
Triangles and ellipses are some of the chart objects in MT4. My question is how do you make them large enough to see? When first selected, they are just itsy bitsy dots on the chart......hardly visible. How does the user enlarge them enough to be of use? Seems to me they need to be about 100,000 times bigger than they are!

--- 帖子 #1067 ---
For a triangle, spot the three points that form it, with enough separation so to see the object thereafter (click and a cross will appear in the place, then after the third point is clicked, the triangle appears, and you can resize it by doubleclicking it and moving its points). For an ellipse, click and drag in a single motion, to an appropriate width, it should appear more or less round when you release the mouse, however, sometimes it appears as a line but you can see its points (it has 5, center and 4 "sides") so you can drag from there if needed to resize it. If you already have the itsy bitsy point and can see it, you can also drag from there (doubleclick it and drag). But the immediate drag is better.

So you want to always trade in the direction of the hull: Up = Long (green) Down = Short (red)

--- 帖子 #1112 ---
the cande has an open high low and close... usually like.. | &lt;----- high ----these are the wicks... | -- Open or Close (depending on the color) | | | | | | -- Open or Close (depending on the color) | | &lt;------ low ----these are the wicks... if that thing above was a candle, you have the open, close and the high and the low...the high and the low make up the wick of the candle...some people I think are reffering to it as a shadow... I hope this makes sense ... maybe someone else could do a better job of explaining, or draw a better diagram...

Yes you can, though you'll have to use the "Trendline" (the diagonal line tool) for that. You can do the same for horizontal, there you'll have to invert the parameters (same price, different times). And diagonal, of course. Here a tip on how to trade news (a bit dangerous) Mostly before out coming news you see the price ranging up and down, the market is nervous. You take pending orders in both directions about 15 to 20 pips away from the range. Once the price spices out you are in and take profit at first sign of retrace. This mostly works, but sometimes you have spices in both directions and that will give you double headache. Cashmeer , don't worry, that is nothing in comparison to other threads but best is never giving a signal here, some new traders could take the oportunity and follow it.

--- 帖子 #1330 ---
The SDX-TzPivots_v4 verions(s) floating around ARE NOT the _v4 released version.....they are "in-work" version(s) which have already been surpassed! The current "in-work" version is already several upgrades above what you have. The current version automatically senses the shift and scale of the chart and replaces labels approaching the left chart boundary where they will normally disappear once they, and the period separator reach that boundary. Furthermore, the user will be able to advance or delay triggering replacement of the labels. Once the labels move to the left of the screen and then get "replaced", the lines become full screen lines and the labels appear exactly as in the "full-screen lines = true" mode. The only difference is that there are no price labels in the chart margin as with the "true" mode. And in either of these modes, the user can move the labels left and right. If new code was used to right justify the labels as shown in the post, please post the code, or explain any changes to the code you might have made, if aside from from using the "move labels" function already in the indicator. I can add any such code additions or changes to the indicator. Please reply as to what you did....new code or simply using the move labels feature. Thank you.

Money Tec has 6 digits Interbank FX has 5 digits My Solution: The Money Tec platform had the original v1 indicators in the Exp/Indi directory so V2 was able to find T3 THV. The IBFX platform had all the orginal v1 indicators deleted before v2 was installed. I renamed the THV T3 file to T3 THV...this did not work well. The only problem here would be if the T3 in v2 has been enhanced from the T3 in v1.

--- 帖子 #1340 ---
Before answering your questions, I want to make clear that any goal in pips or $ has to be a consequence of a disciplined money management rule, adequate to your own equity. This should be the first thing to consider. I personally range from 0 to 20 daily orders, as extremes, 3-4 being the most frequent. I usually traded from M5 and watching M15 for the trend, then now with THV switched to M1 - M5 but still taking M15 into account as overview. (the smaller timeframe is for the entries) Actually my daily plan is to make 20 pips daily as a minimum. If I surpass the quota, I stop trading for the day and can then keep watching PA on the charts as training, test other systems on demo, study or just turn off the computer. If the quota is not met, I sum it up to the remaining days and so on (example: if there are 21 trading days and on day 1 I do 0 pips, then I'll have a goal of 21 daily pips for the rest of the days on that month, etc.) I risk 2-3% of total equity, risk which I'll be reducing as the capital grows, with an aim of risking no more than 0,25-0,50%. I open one position at a time, or maximum two if I happen to hedge it.

--- 帖子 #1374 ---
Hello THV Traders, In haste to make money, it is easy to lose money on a premature trade that follows most but not all of Cobra's rules. Take the two charts for example. On the first one, I was monitoring the M5 timeframe (TF), looking for a long. Since we'd earlier been to 1.4719, I was fairly confident that we'd go back there. Since price was already over the Coral line, I waited for it to crawl over T3 and the Ichimoku cloud. In my overconfidence of the action, I took the long just over the T3 but NOT the cloud. My trade entry is shown in the ellipse in the top chart, an M5. If you want to check it on your own chart, I took the trade at 1040gmt. Entry was 1.4590. What happened from there is the object of this lesson. It rose to 4604, +14, and then immediately reversed for 7 5-minute bear candles! It got all the way to -39, which is more equity drawdown than you should normally have to use with the THV system. Now faced with problem-solving, and since I still felt confident of today's early trend, I started looking for a reasonable Stop Loss when price took me to -25 PIPs (ouch!). The closest support was 1.4538, so I set my SL at 1.4535, which God forbid, would set me back -55 PIPs if hit. That's 2/3 of a day in trading for me. Luckily, support held and I was eventually able to collect a profit, a measly +7 PIPs which in this case I was elated to take. What did I do wrong, and what could I have done differently? Well, I did not wait for price to climb above the cloud, one of the fundamental rules of THV. If I had gone to the M1 TF to get verification of my trade entry, I would have seen that I was indeed jumping the gun. Look at my second chart, an M1, and you will see that M1 clearly showed that at the point I took my trade (see yellow up-arrow), the T3 had not yet crossed Coral. I got lucky because of a strong trend and understanding of support and resistance, but this trade could have set me back more than a half-day's work if it had done what I probably deserved. I took my lucky +7, became more patient for the rest of the morning, followed Cobra's rules to the "T", and now, +91 PIPs later, I am done for the day. I am not bragging on the +91, just emphasizing the power of THV and the importance of following the simple rules of the system. Sorry for the book, but I hope this helps a new trader. Good trading to all.

Here's a great example of the power of scaling out of profits and letting your trade run unimpeded. Some of you took the THV short at around 1400gmt (0900est). If you set a Stop Loss at entry/break-even at about +30 or +40, and took partial profits along way but left some of your trade open to be TSL'd out, you could have picked up as much as +271 PIPs over three hours. If you don't like trailing stops, pick a fairly long-term point of support, like MR1 and set your TP just above that. Another way would have been to set TP at a psych like 4350 or 4320. Then, as Algirdas likes to say, the market will give you a nice little surprise. Here's the chart. It spiked down 100 PIPs in about 10 minutes and it's still moving! At 4266 now. I'm offline.

--- 帖子 #1409 ---
I can try to help you while Cobra is enjoying some well-deserved relaxation. Yes you are right in that this system is trend-based but that is not the whole story. As previously mentioned, S/R levels as well as trend lines are also important. So, for the trend part, it will always be lagging to some degree. That is the nature of trend. Consequently, all of the indicators in THV will have some lag to them. The point is they will not always come together at the right time for a good trade. Any system will miss trades. Traders cannot trade 24 hours anyway (unless you have some superpowers ) so by definition you will miss trades. We use THV with a goal of taking only the best trades. My philosophy is conservative, so 2 out of 3 indicators is not good enough. All indicators need to agree at the same time or it's no trade. You have to be comfortable with the trade at the time. There are exceptions for experienced traders but only they will know when they can go outside the rules. For now I suggest you try it in DEMO and stick to the rules. There is no need to change them because they work well. We had many experienced traders back and forward test the system with very good success.After you gain experience then later you may want to change things here and there, if you desire. In the meantime, trust the system.

--- 帖子 #1442 ---
Good morning fellow THV traders, My first trade today went for a loss, -25 PIPs. Why? Because after that drastic drop at 0830GMT, I started reading my correction bias into the THV chart. The M5 was not ready. Price had crossed the T3 but was not out of the cloud and it had not crossed Coral. I had just sat down to trade and was wanting to "get every pip", so I anticipated - and got a loss. Had to cut it off at -25; it eventually ran to -40 or so. The M1, by the way, appeared "ready" - all rules in place. The problem was I was just in the middle of a very short up-run, and about as soon as I executed my Buy, it reversed on me. Lessons to Learn from that Trade: 1. If THV is not ready on M5, don't go trade on M1 unless you are a very experienced trader who is looking only to scalp. 2. Don't be so eager to trade when you first sit down at the computer. Take time to review the daily trend (was clearly down). Take some time to absorb the action and get into the right frame of mind - follow the rules. 3. Don't read your wishes into the chart. Wait for the conditions to develop and the opportunity will appear. I only took 2 more trades on the day. One profited for +55 and the other for +60. How did I turn my "luck" around so quickly? I waited for an M5 opportunity to develop. The 4020-to-3996 area today was indeed a battleground for bulls and bears. I got one trade down to 3984. THV set up real nice for it on the M5, and of course I had more confidence because I was going with the trend. For my next trade, the +60, I had to wait more than an hour and a half. The market was consolidating, in the battleground area. I hung with my short for two reasons: 1. All conditions on M5 and M1 were favorable; and 2. During the 1 1/2 hours, I kept referring back to my M15, M30 and H1 timeframe charts to confirm that there was indeed downward motion. In fact there was a Bear Flag in play on each of these longer term charts. In the consolidation, I had to get all the way to -35 before it finally turned loose and dropped for my +60. Believe me, I was on the outer limits of SL ground but the trend was clearly down and the higher TF charts urged PATIENCE. Posting a couple of charts for illustration. The first chart shows my M5 THV chart with the hour and a half consolidation. The second chart shows one of my M30 charts so that you can see that Bear Flag, or downward wedge plus the daily trend. Hope this helps someone. Have a nice weekend.

--- 帖子 #1450 ---
Yes, I do it like that. If you see something is cocking on 5M and you await a breakout, than switch to 1M to search a good entry after drawing your TL's in 5M. Once you got it, you need to be prepared to chicken that trade out early enough in case that it runs against you. You need to baby-sit the position in 1M until it is in good green pips to switch back to 5M and let it run, even better if you can setup your SL in BE. I want to underline again the importance of the trading time. We always want strong moves because a ranging market will be boring and waste of time because we mostly don’t get entry confirmations. For me the overlapping London – NY session is the most appropriated. I also avoid Friday trading if there is no important news that may move the market.

1. Holidays aren't particularly easy, though given the fact that indeed the trend was quite clear and strong (be it a retracement on long term downtrend or a reversal) there were many opportunities to get in and succeed, but also a very risky move on thursday that occurred in a very short span of time. Low volume, high volatility, not the best conditions though. 2. If you are strictly following the exit rules and only watching M1 behaviour, you can't expect much more than 20-50 pips on a given trade. However, if you wish to stay longer and take exits on a higher timeframe (M5 or M15 for example), stops and trailings should be set accordingly as well. I personally think that a 30 pips trailing is very tight to remain for a long time on a trade, given the volatility and choppiness that this pair has been having lately. A 30 pips stop with a correct entry should allow you to reach positive pips, provided that you set it to breakeven as soon as possible so if it turns against you at least you won't lose anything, and as you are trading with the trend, maybe enter at a better price after the retracement. It will also depend on the entry, on M1 TF a late entry is more difficult to take back. It would be better to wait for a setup on a higher timeframe and then pinpoint the entry on M1, as you might be in the middle of small retracements. Could you post a few examples of those stopped out trades (can be charts or entry points) so we can analize what went wrong with them?

--- 帖子 #1593 ---
Calculation of standard Pivots is: PP =(HIGH+LOW+CLOSE)/3 S1 =(2*PP)-HIGH S2 =PP-RANGE S3 =S2-RANGE R1 =(2*PP)-LOW R2 =PP+RANGE R3 = R2 + RANGE Ah, before you ask, Range is High - Low

--- 帖子 #1594 ---
And FPV are Fibonacci Pivots, which formula is: R3 = Pivot + 1.000 * (High - Low) R2 = Pivot + 0.618 * (High - Low) R1 = Pivot + 0.382 * (High - Low) Pivot = ( High + Low + Close ) / 3 (same as for Standard) S1 = Pivot - 0.382 * (High - Low) S2 = Pivot - 0.618 * (High - Low) S3 = Pivot - 1.000 * (High - Low)

--- 帖子 #1609 ---
You can see this with MT4 standard volume indicator and placing curson on current candle......when a new candle starts, look at the "volume" count rise as the price rises. If the talked about situtation is happening on that 1 minute candle, you will see the price jump a few pips on light volume, and then you will see the volume count continue to rise 2x, 3x, 4x, 5x that original count, while the price further rises little or not at all. And even if it does rise more, the additional rise and volume involved, compared to the first pop on light volume, will still tell the story that "a lot of addditional volume did not move it that much more, compared to the first pop on light volume."

--- 帖子 #1610 ---
Given that "volume" applies to both sides of the picture (long-short), you can have double the volume and no move at all if buyers and sellers are of equal weight at a certain point in time...

--- 帖子 #1623 ---
Well, I'm not very good with numbers, so I hope some of you guys can help me with this let's say I trade THV system and at the end of the month I had 65~70% winners, usually 2 to 5 trade a day, risking 1 to 3% max on each trade. Is there a formula I can use to calculate an expected average return? on a daily/weekly/monthly basis? Not sure if I made myself clear on this... thanks

--- 帖子 #1624 ---
Assuming a R/R of 1:1 (SL = TP) and average 2% risk (thus reward) and 3 trades a day, 70% winners, expected average return would be around 2,4% daily / 12% weekly / 48% monthly... Formula is simple: number of trades * % reward * % winners - % losers, in this case: 3 * 2% = 6% daily * 70% = 4.2% minus 30% losers (1.8%) = 2.4% daily weekly = daily * 5 monthly = daily * 20 in average Of course this will vary according to the final average number of trades and percentage of risk taken.
