--- 帖子 #1639 ---
What kind of money management can we aply to the sistem? I´m refearing to the size of the positions. For example a maximum of 2% per trade but there should be moments were you have to risk more or less because the risk of the trade?

--- 帖子 #1640 ---
There's a difference between "risk" and "size". A 2% risk will always remain the same, however if you need that 2% to represent more width in pips, the positions will have to be of a smaller size. Maximum 2% risk per trade only refers to the amount you are willing to lose if the trade goes wrong. For example: on a $5000 account, 2% is $100 = 100 pips at 0.1 lots, 50 pips at 0.2 lots, 20 pips at 0.5 lots, and 10 pips for a full lot. In any of those cases, you will always be risking $100, but you will have more or less room for the trade to evolve depending on the position size chosen, which will also depend on the timeframe being traded.

All these 3 criterias need to indicate buy or sell uninanmously ? Most of the time I'm seeing both Trix lines above zero level, what exactly is meant by "hide in our trading direction"? But maybe a thorough explanation would help others as well. Thanks for such a great system! All the best for 2009

--- 帖子 #1846 ---
More likely if you should "buy or hold", or "sell or hold", as color of the candle must match the direction of the crossing. If it crosses up but the candle is red and thus going down, we should hold. PA must be under the Cloud, and both under the Coral. That is: Price action crosses the aqua T3 and the Cloud, when above the cloud go long, when below go short, but check first if both are effectively above or under the Coral line. I guess it should read "heads in our trading direction", that is, both lines above zero level and other parameters signaling a long, it's a green light. Both lines below and same on the rest for a short. Usually though, the Trix lines appear earlier than the rest of the signals (a few candles before the effective PA crossing). If they are crossing back against the direction shown by PA, should be an early warning of a possible direction change so better not enter if in conflict, IMO.

--- 帖子 #1861 ---
The "Analyze" signals are only that. Human intervention is needed to identify what you did, which is a "no trade" because the rules have not been met. The signal is not perfect and cannot currently send a signal based on all the rules. Also, as you mentioned, a trade could be taken on the 1M if you were trading that chart only. This is not recommended for anyone except the very most experienced traders. The 1M can give too many false signals and change too rapidly so you have to be able to understand the PA to be successful. The best trades are the ones where everything comes together nicely, per the rules AND taking into account TL's, S&amp;R, fibs etc. Those are the trades to be looking for.

--- 帖子 #1923 ---
To Gofer Pips and others: Are the Fib pivots the same as standard equation? Central pivot yes. The rest is based on formulas with Fib numbers (those have been posted earlier in this thread, but you can also do a Google search for "fibonacci pivots formula"). IBFX opens 6:00pm est on Sunday, could this have an effect due to different broker openings and closings on what prices are used? No, pivots are based on last friday's data (sunday bars aren't taken into account). EDIT: If pivot = H+L+C/3 would my pivot be determined on Sunday as 1.3927 based on 1 hour trading from 6 til 7 when GMT= 0 again? The close would be taken from the hourly candle at the time you have set to be as your daily open/close timezone. The high and low would be taken from the previous 24 hour range from that candle back. Now: Independently of timezones (as everybody would be starting and ending the day at the same time if chosing GMT or maybe USA open/close?) the fact is that the High / Low and Close prices would have to be exactly the same also for the formula to give the same number. For example: My hourly candle marked 14:00 on the server at FxPro is at 13:00 on Fibo Group and Alpari, at 12:00 on Oanda (GMT), and at 9:00 on Marketiva. FxPro close = 1.35610 Fibo Group close = 1.3560 Alpari close = 1.3563 Oanda close = 1.35622 Marketiva close = 1.3553 No need to look for highs and lows as those will most probably have differences as well, slight or huge. Prices are not the same for each broker , thus calculations will forcefully give a different outcome, no matter if you all are taking the same 24 hour range into account. It would be nice indeed to have the same pivot numbers exactly to the pip, but then we would have to be all using the same broker (which is an option if you decide to use the demo for the charts and trade at your own broker based on those). However, this is not an absolute guarantee either that we will all have the same prices, I have seen 2-3 pips differences among different accounts (demo, and especially live!) on the same broker as well.

--- 帖子 #1980 ---
I can give you this tip to gradually get accustomed to noisy price action... I hadn't discovered this earlier because I never went any further than an hour on the trading simulator (MT4 Strategy Tester - on visual mode, and I use vhandstrade but I guess the other simulator would do the same trick, provided that you can let it run the same way...) In fact after seeing the positive effects my week-end backtestings have had this monday on my normal TF charts, as to tranquillity, focus especially, and understanding of patterns and price action (M30 chart looked to me as a Daily after that, LOL) as well as screen hours experience, I have decided that, as a part of my trading discipline, I will do at least one hour daily of trading simulation, and at least 4 hours continued during the week-end so not to lose "the hand"... until it really crystallizes as a second nature in my trading reactions... Set up the visual mode, at full speed (start with it in minimal though, as it will jump fast, then turn it off, set full speed - all the slider up to 32 - set it to "each tick mode", and use the mouse to start-stop the action - finger on the trigger at all times as the price moves REALLY fast...). You can also just watch the screen and price moving as a start, but I would recommend to really perform a trading test, as if you were trading normally, because if just watching price gone wild you will get sleepy or confused after a few minutes if you don't have the trading goal. Maybe you'll have to adjust the speed gradually so to get accustomed, Vhandstrade allows you to see the open positions on the screen through a "Terminal" indicator window, so you can act on them fast given the case. I personally started at around 26 (the number shows when you place the mouse on the slider) then 28 and now at full 32. This allows for a faster test of longer periods (roughly 3 hours for a month at full speed). You'll find the expert here: http://articles.mql4.com/301 Also, I do some scalping on Oanda 's 5 seconds charts. You could try the Oanda's FXGame (demo) for a little fun, the charts are very good (no missing candles or such and plenty of movement as they show micropips - the patterns are totally tradable and easily recognizable as if it were a higher TF chart) meanwhile you acquire a good practice for smaller timeframes like M1 or M5. In this setup, I have the main chart at 5 seconds on half the screen, 1 minute chart vertical at the right (smaller, just the last candles) and 5 minute chart much smaller but visible. As you can't place THV system on Oanda, I am using there the Ichimoku Kinko Hyo with THV settings of 2-5-8, to at least simulate THV's PA crossing of the cloud. I set all the windows (trades open, tickets and market order always open) so I can act fast as 5 secs is REALLY fast... If you have some time to try it during the week, it can give you lots of sharpness for scalping and clicking at the right time, of course Oanda's server response is quite faster than any MT4 but you'll get the idea.

--- 帖子 #1985 ---
If you're the graphic/visual type of person, vhandstrade is much better as you place the trades by dragging lines to the screen and can also move stops and pending entries that way. It takes a little time to learn it thoroughly and configure it to start with the settings you would like (something I usually forget when changing systems or demo platforms), you have to recompile the default settings so you don't need to change it all over again in a new test. Also it will depend on the brokers digits... stops, targets and trails need to be added a zero in the main file. Check it out at the link above (MQL4 site), maybe it will work better for you.

--- 帖子 #1987 ---
Usually a 2 or 3*ATR (20) of the TF you are following up (for example, M5 for the trend and M1 for entry, you would have to take M5's ATR value) is a quite safe stop (2*max ATR - 3*average ATR) for any pair. On my platform, EUR/AUD has an ATR range of 4 to 21 on M1 (that would be around 42 pips safer stop, 36 medium risk stop). And 14 to 41 on M5 which would be giving a 82 stop on both cases. Adding M5 + M1 to have an average would be giving around 60 pips stop to work on those TFs, IMO.

--- 帖子 #2007 ---
FxPro Broker 00:00 = GMT 22:00 = EST 17:00 If you would like to start your session at EST 00:00 = GMT +5 you would effectively place the -5 which is the difference, but as you start at the USA close which is the same time as the broker (EST 17:00 = FxPro 00:00) you have to place the same number (would work the same if placing 0-0 or 1-1, etc which means there is no difference between the broker time and the USA open/close time).

--- 帖子 #2011 ---
As far as pivots are concerned, Acumen's website will explain to you the importance and usage of pivots. The THV Tdz-pivot_v4 will set your pivots up daily and can be set as Doblece has explained. The pivots are areas that price likes to go to like a magnet. Alot of times it will retrace to a pivot. It has been my experience that the EUR/USD pair really respects the quarter pivots as well as the mid pivots and of course the S/R pivots. There is also sweet spots that the big boys load up on. They are .xx33 and .xx66, as well as any.xx00,.xx50,.xx20, and .xx80. These sweet spots are other areas to look at. Try this on demo until you are comfortable with seeing the PA in relation to the pivots and sweet spots. I hope I have helped with this answer and have not been too verbose. If not just ask for clarification, and if I can't help, there are wonderfully talented traders such as Cobra, Doblece, Tradewell, and Traderathome that can help you. Good luck and good pipping!

--- 帖子 #2020 ---
If they appear as expert advisors on the navigator, you have them in the wrong place. You have to move them to the "indicators" folder which is located inside the "experts" folder. They will then appear under "Custom Indicators" on the Navigator. Beware when using metaeditor if you have several different Metatrader platforms from different brokers, to check first where it will be saving the file (load the file, save in the appropriate folder before compiling, then compile). Sometimes it assumes by default the more used MT4 even if you are using the Editor from another broker. So, in short: Go to your broker's MT4 "experts" folder from the Windows Explorer, and move all the THV indicators to the "indicators" folder which is inside the "experts" folder. I guess the template is ok in its place as you were able to load it. Should you need any further help, just let me know.

--- 帖子 #2021 ---
FPV = FIBONACCI Pivot, same as Central Pivot or DP, but indicating that the rest of calculations are per Fibonacci Pivot Formulae.

--- 帖子 #2023 ---
Hi Personalme, Thanks for your nice words. Glad to see that the THV system is working for you too. Cobra, Doblece and Tradewell are more experienced than I on this subject, but in their absence, I will tell you what I do. I usually use kind of a manual stops, meaning that I watch price action and set them myself, but I use a stop loss of 25-30 PIPs. That minimizes my losses and gets me out of possibly bad trades, easy to make those PIPs up on the next one. Then, to maximize profit, when I initially set the trade, I use a trailing stop of 20 PIPs, but I don't allow the trailer to keep advancing once I get ahead. I manually turn trailing stops off at +20 and then let it run. As price runs, I will manually advance my stop from time to time. The only reason I don't use automatic trailing stop all the time is I don't want to get knocked out of a good trade too early. Hope this helps. Good luck working the THV. Edit: Personalme, if you do not have the patience to let a trade run, or are afraid of letting the positive pips get away, you can always just get out at +20 or +30 and then re-enter above the next resistance or below the next support. One thing to remember in this, however, is that you need to be very confident in the direction of the trend. I do this often, but when I do, I try always to be sure I'm re-entering within the rules of THV.

--- 帖子 #2024 ---
Thank you for your kind words On my side, I think that the market is always there and there will always be another opportunity should the one I decided to get in misses the "long run". The other thing is that the market moves in waves, and usually will go back a few to continue its way, then again and so on. After watching a lot of PA, I have seen that around 80% of the time if stopped early you can get in at a better price or at least where you were stopped, after it pulls back. Exceptions are the huge spikes or runs, of course... but one can't win all the time What worries me more are the losers (and computer or electricity issues... sigh), so I usually place stop at breakeven +1 as soon as possible (if trading on the M30 chart, as soon as price has touched 20 pips and reverses, if on M1 or M5, the same but at 11-12 pips). Then I use automatic trailing on MT4, at 25 pips distance (15 pips on M1-M5). It is quite near the entry but among the bunch of 1 pip and 15-30 pips trades, I sometimes hit some home runs that range from 90 to 200 (on M30 with 25 Trail - smaller TFs give smaller pips)! I also have noticed that when price is what I would call "hesitant" it is better to wait a little and you'll see that if it keeps coming and going and stopping you out for few pips, it is most probably sideways or about to reverse. Also, if you missed the "perfect" entry, wait for a pullback to enter even if the signal is good, there's a lag in timing sometimes in our head that makes us take the decision exactly at the moment it is pulling back and precisely those are the pips to the stop... so we're out when we shouldn't be. It will also depend on the PA and on what I see on the charts and if I am able to monitor the trade or not. Sometimes I will be adjusting the trail back and forth if it seems to have a further continuation but retraces heavily, but is energy consuming so mostly I will do that for the fun, usually I just accept what the market wants to give at that particular time. I sometimes place a target but is not current now. And on small timeframes (M1-M5) hard stops shouldn't be higher than 30-35 pips, IMO. Hope it helps

--- 帖子 #2093 ---
Oops sorry. I thought effectively that you were talking of Cobraforex's chart. (Both are the same link... is there another chart?) The "thick" line is the old Hull. Indeed, as per the cloud being above the coral line, the entry wouldn't be valid... and also, the 15 min chart of the pivot break at 15:45 ( FxPro GMT+2) happens just 45 minutes after New York open, and 15 minutes after NEWS (NFP, a BIG no-no for opening ANY position). Technically, if it wasn't news time and especially THAT news, maybe the fact that the candle broke the pivot line with force without even retesting it later (see on M1 chart) and didn't came back, having being rejected from psych level 1.3750 on the candle before the break (market open small spike) could give a green light for a short entry with a tight stop, because all the other conditions are met... but the fact that the cloud is still above means to me that the movement has been very volatile and with whipsaw (the cloud "hasn't had enough time to evolve and place itself where it should be"), price went way ahead and a too fast move brings about a similarly sharp reversal (typical BTW of NFP mornings...). So, all in all, the elements that make us avoid dangerous times also might sometimes prevent us to make quite a few pips... but remember that staying in the sidelines is also part of the trading... and that there are thousands of opportunities all 24 hours 5 days a week, which this system seems to harvest quite well There was an opportunity to enter later on, about an hour and a half later, when cloud went down the Coral which also gave a sell alert on M15, T3 and PA conditions kept signaling the short trend, entering just below 1.3550. BUT: the Trix lines were pointing up and RSI signaling oversold conditions. All in all, a risky situation, at least in M15. On M5 the Trix was quite choppy but the PA was more definite though in a quite of "choppy downside" (it kept crossing and re-crossing the cloud), giving then an opportunity to enter at 1.3490, down to 1.3430-1.3420. On M1 there were a few possible small entries, but with oversold RSI worms and choppy Trix. Each timeframe has its own panorama which can be quite different of the previous one or not. I personally wouldn't trade on late Friday morning especially on a NFP day. But also, in such a case, you can check the conditions in a smaller timeframe and do some cautious scalping.

--- 帖子 #2097 ---
Many questions bring about many potential lessons for both sides and expand to the rest of all who are sharing this method, so bring the questions on! In fact the entry I mentioned is quite a bit later on. As I said in the previous post, in my opinion technically it would have been a good entry if it hadn't been at that precise time of the day and with the NFP data just freshly issued. Even despite the cloud and worm thing. Especially because of the momentum with which it broke the central pivot line, barely tried to retest it and went down much further (and former candle strong rejection of the upper level). The entry would have been below 1.3533 (which is another psych level, along with the xx66, usually even stronger than the other as far as I have seen in my backtestings). But, with a warning of the RSI oversold and Trix coming back up, maybe one would have to ponder how much is the risk, and go to lower TFs to check that the entry is indeed a valid (tradable) one. Should this have been in a normal trading day out of news time or market open, I personally would have entered after the break and retest of the central pivot line, without waiting for the coral to change direction, but with a tight stop at the pivot level or even a little lower... because in fact, the trend was apparently up and about to finish what seemed to be a Flag pattern, in which I would maybe have expected a further leg up or second flagpole, but NFP changes here all the logic of the evolution of the pattern. The NY open spike up was probably caused by many traders thinking the same (continuation of up trend) but if you go to higher timeframes you will see that this apparent up trend was barely a retracement in a stronger downtrend that started in december after price was rejected at around 1.47xx (H4). And on the contrary, if you watch Daily chart, you'll see another bullish Flag with probabilities of continuation upwards, as coral is green and price and cloud are above... That's why it is very important to stick as much as possible to the TF you want to trade off, trying to match the best entries if trading longer timeframes, in shorter ones, or just entering and exiting in the main direction of the trend one or two TFs higher, as soon as the conditions are met for either action, and also match the expectation of the results with what the particular timeframe can really give (ATR 20 can give you an idea of what you could expect for a wave) and of course, if there is a continuation, stick with the wave the longer time possible, but acting fast against possible reversals and above all minimizing the risk of losses (that is, securing the trade as soon as it is in positive according to each TF, or trailing the stops, or both).

--- 帖子 #2202 ---
Sadly, yes. Unless you chose to risk more than that percentage. I had written something about it earlier on, but will summarize for you: usually a good "fixed" stop loss which will show the different scales for each timeframe, is the ATR (Average True Range). A 2 or 3 times ATR (20) is quite safe. You also should consider using the psych levels and pivots as stop areas, chosing the one that will fil inside your MM... for example, let's say that your capital allows a 20 pips stop and as per your entry, the stop would be barely above a support or below a resistance, or psych level, it will be much safer IMO to risk a few pips more and avoid being stopped out just to see the trade go in your direction (provided that you are effectively trading with the trend, and following all the rest of rules and indications). Something that I have been seeing these days while trading on much smaller charts, is that the price oscillates in waves of about 15 to 30 pips most of the time, then comes back for similar amount, then back in the direction again, etc... like "3 steps forward, 2 steps back", etc... This is what is called "noise" in higher timeframes, and is not recommended to risk trading (scalping) those waves unless more experienced, BUT it is interesting to understand how it moves, so to be able to wait for the "little retrace" before making an entry. Though it is true that entries don't matter and exits are more important, a good and precise entry will give you more for your stop loss and be safer, besides avoiding you lots of headaches waiting during those little retraces and biting nails

--- 帖子 #2205 ---
What you will be using from the ATR is the number for the amount of pips. Source: http://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/atr.asp In this case, ATR (20) would be a moving average of the True Ranges over the last 20 candles, on each TF. Here's a short article on ATR and its uses as stoploss. http://www.meta-formula.com/average-true-range.html Here's how I would be using it: M1 = ATR (20) maximum value reached in the last few hours is 0.0005 (5 pips) and minimum value 0.0002 (2 pips). I multiply max * 2 and min * 3 and take the higher value of those if significantly different. That would give 10 pips for M1. This on all the 4 decimal priced pairs. On Yen based pairs (2 decimal) it is a little different, you would have to skip the last digit I think but I never really used it on those pairs so if someone could confirm or comment on this I would appreciate. (edited - wrong statement) Here's a more technical explanation of the indicator: http://stockcharts.com/school/doku.p...true_range_atr

--- 帖子 #2241 ---
I am very sorry about your losses. But losing streaks happen. Even following the rules everytime (or thinking we are). As weird as this can seem, personal cycles also move in waves, and we as traders are not always responding (physically, emotionally and intelectually) exactly the same. One of those elements is usually the main leader in our own performance and when declining or at its lowest, will impair decisions that we make: overlooking a warning signal, clouding our analysis, or delaying our reaction time at entry... In my own case, I've found that the emotional cycle is the one that incides the most on my trading. For everyone it might be different, though emotions are usually the strongest impairment in this field. When getting the first loser trade, stop and go over all the steps you took, including what happened outside of the trading, thoughts, feelings, mood, etc. If everything seems ok, keep trading. If the next one is also a loser, take a closer look again at all those elements. I usually don't go past the second one and stop trading ASAP. I take some rest for the day and go back to demo so I can evaluate when the streak will end. Or also I check my biorhythm to see where are my cycles at that time. Don't laugh. It's amazing how everything is connected. Never trade if you are not totally focused and peaceful inside. And above all, NEVER trade for a revenge after a loser. Also, maybe your stops are too tight? If you want to post your lost entries maybe we can understand with you what might have happened...

--- 帖子 #2305 ---
It is up to everyone to adjust any trading system to one's own best comfort and results. However, there is a common mistake that we all make at one time or another of our trading journey, and it is not to stick with any system, changing and jumping from one to another as soon as results are not what we expect (usually, we ALL at one point or another expect trading to be a 100% win/win situation, which NO system will give, even the best ones). I personally HATE losing. But I've come to grips with it and now I trash happily and really fast any dubious position on my tablets. With no looking back, except for a thorough analysis of what really happened. It might be an outside distraction, a lag in entry, a stop too tight, or simply an error of criteria. Or overtrading. Even a fear or greed thought just passing by our minds, or an over-contentment feeling because of previous wins, can trigger the mistake. There is always a why. Each and every combination of any indicators in any system, is in the end just a tool that we use to give us the impulse to trigger the trade. The only most important thing to watch, is real time price action, and overall picture for the trend. The rest are filters that will alert us about the market conditions and will prevent us to make more mistakes that needed, also giving precise indications of which are the better entries at a given time. Furthermore, and even above price action, the most important thing to watch is the trader itself. Our state of mind. And have the courage to stop trading if our own trading conditions are not the best, even if the charts are sooo inviting with all those pips running up or down and we're not in the market to take them all... Geez, it's really hard indeed. It is very important to make a halt and analyze thoroughly what were the reasons for the trades that didn't work out as expected. After that, you will always have learned a new lesson which will remain with you forever and you'll grow in experience and confidence.

And also I was meaning to say that one should not change one's own trust in a particular system because others aren't having the same results or are discouraged... and that one should build up a bullet-proof confidence in one's own trading. Triple swap day: swap (or overnight rate) is deposited (or withdrawn) from accounts every day at USA closing time. However, as saturday and sunday there is no activities, on wednesday the swap given or taken is triple its amount, to make up for those two week-end days. That way there is 7 days of swap accounted for, and usually (but this more particularly on high swap pairs like GBP/JPY and others, though I've seen the move 80% of the time about half an hour before the close of the day) on one side shorters are closing their positions not to pay the triple swap (which is negative on EUR/USD) which makes the price go up, and buyers come in so to profit from its positive side... and more upside. Not much on small positions... but it moves the market anyway. A little bit. If the trend was opposite, you will see it resuming fast as soon as the first candle of the next day closes up.

--- 帖子 #2332 ---
Exactly what I thought. The candle you have where the start of the day indicator appears, is showing at your broker's 10:00am. This is not correct, as that would be equivalent to 12:00m EST... It should be showing on your 17:00pm candle, which is 17:00 EST. So, if you want to start with the USA open/close, your setting would have to be -5, 2 (please do check anyway, the vertical line labeled "today" should appear at your 17:00 candle). Just for info: My broker is at GMT+2 which 00:00 start always coincides with the USA open/close (as both have daylight savings time). Your 10am candle is on my chart the 17pm candle (7 hours difference) When my platform shows 00:00 (and its 17:00 EST) , it shows 17:00 of the previous day on yours. So in fact your platform is showing the real time, being in the same time zone as EST market. However, for the pivot indicator to take the range between 17:00 start and next day's 16:59 close, you have to set it up so the first candle (00:00) begins at 17:00 EST. That's why -5 and 2 settings, the 7 hours difference of your platform (5 on one side - EST to GMT, and 2 on the other side GMT to GMT+2) with mine which begins exactly at the EST time. GMT+2 is equal to 00:00 GMT. USA open/close occurs at 22:00 GMT. Now if you want to start the day at 00:00 GMT like Cobraforex, I'll be posting further calculations later on. Hope I didn't confuse you too much Summarizing: 1st setting = -5 2nd setting = 2 P.S.: That was easy. If you want your day to start at GMT 00:00 (two hours later) just substract the two hours on the second setting. That would be -5, 0 instead of the above. The line would be showing on your 19:00 candle, which is equivalent to GMT time 00:00.

--- 帖子 #2340 ---
It is simpler than it seems (only that I usually get all messed up when calculating all those timezones differences, lol). Sorry for the confusion. The second setting is the tricky one, as it uses positive value instead of negative, and besides you are not willing to start at 00:00 of USA time (which is already your own 00:00 time, being at EST) but 7 hours earlier (17:00 to 00:00 = 7 hours). For GMT 00:00 starting it's easier, as there is zero difference between start time and GMT time. For GMT 22:00 start (17:00 EST) you have to add the 2 hours on the second setting (because instead of a negative value, it works with positive ones).

Just a few thoughts on THV V 2.0....I've been testing it out now for the past two weeks and I'm pretty impressed with the results...I've kept to the rules as much as possible using the 1M chart.....I also look at the 5M and also the 15M as the two higher time frames will allow me to look at the "bigger" picture even though the real big picture of course will be on the Daily, 4H &amp; 1H, however I've scaled down my trading style to scalping and thus the smallest 3 time frame seem to work well with my personality. The key to Optimum entries is to follow the rules plain and simple. Once price crosses above/below the Coral and is above/below both the Cloud and the T3, and the Trix is above/below zero line - you enter. After the first initial break of price across the Coral you most always get a small retrace back to the Coral, however don't let that shake you out of the trade. As long as the T3 line is on the same side as your trade direction, you should be fine. Once 15pips in profit, move stop to BE and start unloading after 25pips profit...the move on the 1M time frame on avg seems to be between 25-50 pips..somes you get more, however that seems to be the norm. Being on the west coast I only trade between 5am (pst) and 11am. If you take a look at this mornings action beginning at 5am there were 5 valid entries on the 1M chart. All of them would have netted 20+ pips and some up to 100pips ...by looking at the PA on the 5M chart it allows me to see whether or not I wish to kill the trade with 20pip profit or trail stop my position until I get stopped out. I really enjoy this system and I want to thank CobraForex for providing it to us so generously. The key is to not overthink the market and believe in what your doing. To much thinking will cause you to second guess your decision which will in turn paralyze you with fear. Have no fear - just good MM. My two cents.

--- 帖子 #2577 ---
The THV T3 Trix, we refer to just as Trix, is an oscillator indicator used to help identify entries and exits. It is explained in many posts on this thread, and at http://www.investopedia.com/articles.../02/092402.asp The Hull is not officially part of v2. It was used in v1 and was replaced by the Coral line. We are considering using the Hull on higher TF's only and so some of us are experimenting with it, so you may see it on some charts. On SeerEye's chart posted below, you will see the Hull on the 1M but we don't recommend it being used on that TF. For now, follow the rules in the manual and read the posts to get caught up on the system's current incarnation. Then stick around to see what develops.

I have found that to be pretty much true for my time zone, but one can still get good trades working between 5:00am and noon EST. After noon is pretty much a crapshoot unless you're in a nicely trending market, where price will continue to move with the trend. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #2851 ---
hi cobra maybe byou have this 2 indis but if not you should try them out. i like them Mauro_Trailing manages the stop-loss and take profit. This is an EA not an indicator so place it on your metatrader/experts folder Attach it on the M1. For a 4 decimal set SL to 15, for 15 pip stop. For a 5 decimal broker, then simply set SL to 150, for 15 pips, etc just click the new order button when you see a setup being born and wait to click buy/sell when its time. Within seconds the EA puts my SL and TP which is the most important to me in case of internet or server troubles. sl-tp move by mouse This EA can work in conjunction with mauro_trailing. Put Mauro on your m1 and this one on your m5. When mauro activates your SL and TP you can double click the horizontal lines and drag them up or down as the trade progresses and it will adjust your SL/TP automatically. This great for the exit strategy where you set your stop just below/above any decent-sized candle. The only downside is if you drag it within 10 pips of current price, it wont be able to adjust stops immediately. It will however wait until price moves past 10 pips away and then complete your request.

--- 帖子 #2853 ---
Serj1: I am not an expert, you can see I have no vouchers....Cobra may comment... My comments would be that it is better, I feel and more safe, to use the red trix as the indicator of divergence....green is the leading indicator and moves quickly.. If you relook at your chart and try to draw out the divergence with the red trix you will see that it never retraced in the middle...your red line in the chart is 1 move down on the red trix...that one green candle only moved the green trix... --- 帖子 #2980 ---
The following chart is not a THV, but it is a chart I check and update daily as a reminder of where price has been met with support and/or resistance. I have found these historical numbers provide S/R when price meets them again. They are color coded from daily down to 15 minutes. As more of the lower time frames are hit in the 15 min area at different times, they will become hourly, hourly become daily(some of the dailies are already weeklies as inclusion of past history on one chart required this), and eventually I will have to put weekly up, or the chart becomes completely gold. To put strength of these lines in perspective I use the following analogy, if pushing up through a ceiling, what is it made of? Turquoise(15 min)= PAPER Firebrick( 1hour)= WOOD Gold(Daily/Weeekly)= STEEL This may help you to be aware of why price stalls in certain areas and how stubborn it can be, or even reverse. I hope this was understandable. P.S.- On my chart, the next STEEL S/R is at the 1.2692 area. We shall see.

--- 帖子 #3124 ---
Yes. For example, the pair could be initiating a small retrace (the price is always fluctuating) which won't show in the higher timeframe, but which we can catch on M1 and wait for a better entry after the fluctuation. Also keep in mind that the higher timeframe will be giving you the "big picture" (I personally use M30 - M5 - M1 together so I can see in which part of the cycle the price really is), and the smaller one will be full of "noise", but that noise is made of pips which you can save with a more precise entry as this will give you more room for your stops. But (unless just scalping both sides for small pips) don't forget the direction that the big picture is showing.

--- 帖子 #3125 ---
Yes, meaning timing the entry based on the THV rules on a smaller timeframe? i.e rules met on the 5 min time frame then move to the 1m time frame and enter once the THV rules are met?

--- 帖子 #3126 ---
Yup IMO. Maximizing entry is one of the most important thing in scalping. Without precise entry (thus means smaller TF and a little bit patience), it is difficult to find good ratio between SL and TP.

--- 帖子 #3127 ---
Exactly. Sorry if my previous answer wasn't clear enough

Just my 2 cents.... First of all I would zoom out, it is easier to see the patterns when the trix is zoomed out.... Secondly, you need to connect the highs together or the lows together, but not highs on the price action and lows on the trix... Take a look again at the divergence chart and you will see the lows are together and the highs are together... ADD: Lastly, you need to make a judgement which is more comfortable for you the green trix or the red trix...I have found the red trix to be more reliable...what is really nice is if you find both red trix and green trix at divergence with price action. That was the case today in the chart that I posted... Hope this helps...

--- 帖子 #3157 ---
Cashmeer, a bit of construtive criticism...not sure if you took 18 and then another 18 (for 54 total) or the 18 twice at the same level? No matter for what I want to point out. I certainly can not (nor will not) tell you how to trade, only what I have setteled on. I would never take one (or more) lots off at 18p's and leave my SL on the remaing lots at a loss. Usualy would have it at 2~3 in the profit zone from entry. If I've already cashed 18, there's no reason to take a loss on the remaining lots. All of mine would be at BE or just inside the profit zone. Now I might leave my runners at the BE/PZ for a while but each time I cashed more lots the SL would be moved up a bit and usualy the runners would be moved up as well. What you're trying here is (IMHO) the way to go, take some off and leave some on. Everytime you hear the "ka-ching", it is a great confidence builder. Nicely Done

--- 帖子 #3162 ---
Cash, See you removed the question about the bottom quote so you must understand it now. I'm very tight with my pips when they belong to me, I'm not going to give them up easily...therefore at my first cash I'm moving everything else into the PZ, not by much but worst case (barring a big news event) I'm going to come out with the first cash and BE or a pip or two on everything else. There are so many differnt ways to us SL's that I can't explain them all here. Some of them have been discussed on this thread (doblece ?)...ATR, fixed stop above/below the high/low (this method can be used with the HH2~7/LL2~7 (HighestHigh/LowestLow~n bars ago) as well. Trend lines...moving average...etc. Pivot H/L...this gives the most room for error but is pricy. Wait until you have a one or two (some use a three or four) bar pivot and place the stop above/below the pivot. The pivot stop leaves the *most* money on the table if you get stopped out. I use both manual and auto stops (I'm trying to get a coder to do one for me now). I use a bit of a different approach than what I've discussed here and have a meeting shortly, if I get time I'll PM you...don't want to hog the band width here. I'm still trying to get my head around MetaTrader charting but one trick I've found...if you left click on your closed order and drag it onto your chart it shows the entry and exit points.

--- 帖子 #3207 ---
Serj1, Both are correct but different... Yellow divergence line: Price is making higher highs and red trix is making lower highs (from beginning point to ending point of your trendlines). This is Bearish RD (regular divergence) and is indicating a sell. Blue divergence line: Price is making higher lows and red trix is making lower lows (from beginning point to ending point of your trendlines). This is Bullish HD (hidden divergence) and is a sign of bearish divergence...indicating a buy. If you look at your chart there was a downside correction which started at the end of your yellow line and at the end of your blue line price headed back up. Each divergence line (in this case) was spot on. Divergence is a bit hard to work with when you first begin but it is a good tool. Just keep in mind that it's only a tool...a hammer isn't much use unless you have a nail.

--- 帖子 #3323 ---
Pick a TF to trade like 5m. Use higher timeframes to watch and verify trend. When permission to enter on 5m, check in 1 min to see if good entry point, ( after you have made entry) sometimes 1m may retrace to a pivot and that might make you think it reverse, but as long as trade stay right direction ( keeps rules) on 5min you are okay. If 5 runs up many pips, check 15m if going your way you can bank some pips by part of position and move rest to break even, you can move stoploss to guarantee what you get, or use trailing stop. There are many ways, but you have to be comfortable how to treat your pips! They are at times like a woman.......a delicate creature

--- 帖子 #3435 ---
Yep. Cobra and I do things a bit differently, but I look only at M1 and M5 for scalping. Even then, I only have one chart on my screen at a time. Remember that Metatrader will let you open multiple charts and it keeps them in tabs along the bottom, like Microsoft Excel does with its workbooks. When I want to look at another, I just click over and back (I'm dealing with a 15-inch, old laptop). One thing to remember, THV is like any other system in that it is easier to scalp in the direction of the trend. Therefore, when the action is a bit slow or confusing, I will take periodic peeks at M15, M30, H1, H4 and Daily. That said, THV is the easiest system I've seen to scalp counter-trend. Just expect fewer PIPs in that case. BTW, before you go blaming yourself for "scuppering" the system, remember that price action has been especially challenging over the past few days. When there is a well-established trend, THV on the M5 is a smooth-running machine. Hope this helps.

My MT4 fib tool has the extensions. If your's doesn't, right click on the fib and you can define them in the "Fibo Levels" tab.

--- 帖子 #3440 ---
Use the Fibonacci Retracement on the toolbar. It lets you enter whatever extra positive and negative settings that you want. When you type in the percentages on each line in the "Fibo Levels" tab, you can show the percentage and any text that you might type after it (e.g., like a hypen to separate percentage from price). Just type "%$" - leave off the quotation marks, just %$. I'll post a chart to show you what it winds up looking like.

--- 帖子 #3441 ---
Mentos, here is a chart that shows you how I set up my fib retracements. For example, on a new line of the Fib Levels tab, I typed in whatever percentage I wanted and then typed " - %$". That gave me the percentage followed by a space, hypen and MT4 inserted price on the chart. I will not be back for an hour or so. Dinner time.

--- 帖子 #3578 ---
I have a system I follow on fibs. I have a chart with Low to highest historical high that just gives me a sense of the whole move up weekly chart. I have a fib on the highest historical high to last lowest low weekly chart. Using analogies, these are my telecopes to locate Earth. I draw one on the daily chart from the last high or low to the most recent high or low. This is my GPS to locate where on earth I want to go. Then on the hourly chart I will draw a fib from the weeks biggest move. This I keep relevant until we have a move on this chart to the +/- move of 61.8%( that is 61.8 past 100 retrace, or 61.8 below start of move) This is my map for Pipville. My last fib keep I call my intraday and I draw that as the day unfolds. It is relevant until I get a +/- 61.8% also, and then I redraw from the 0 or 100 of the move. This gives me the address of Mr. Pips house. Fibs at times can be subjective to user, but whatever works for you is good! I hope this is understandable, and addresses your question correctly.

Hi All, For all of those who are contributing to the thread – great job, and many thanks to Cobra for all of your hard work! SORRY for the long post, but I need everyone’s opinion here regarding the MACD and the 5 MIN T3 TRIX as an entry filter for trades to be taken on the 1 minute chart. In my opinion, the THV v.2 in its current form allows you to be both aggressive and conservative without having to do a lot of technical analysis. For the conservative trader , follow the rules of the Coral indicator: Only long when you get a THV entry signal above the Coral and vice versa. For the aggressive trader , you might take THV entries regardless of the Coral; for example going long when the T3 closes above the Hull Replace and the HA candle is out of the cloud, but you are still BELOW the Coral. This would be considered a contrarian trade. If you are unsure of the entry criteria, visit the first page of this thread to review Cobra’s rules. In either case, a filter would help make the right entry choices easier to obtain. Several weeks back, someone mentioned using a MACD as a “filter” to help sift the good entries from the bad ones on the THV chart. I agree. I have been testing the idea of using the standard MACD offered by MT4. You will find that most MT4 packages use this one as well as the Traditional MACD. I must admit that the way I use the MACD is NOT the traditional way of using it, which traditionally is used as a convergence/divergence tool (hence the name MACD - Moving Average Convergence Divergence). When watching the 1 MIN or 5 MIN chart, one can see many potential entries. But, when you combine the “filtering nature of the MACD” the way I do, it should reduce many of the entries that end up working against you. So, what if you want to do a contrarian trade against the Coral? Or what if you want more confidence on your trades where the Coral agrees? ** Even with the new TRIX coming in THV v2.1, the MACD and 5 MIN TRIX should still help with entry selection. ** The MACD as an entry filter: KEY POINT: The green bars must be above 0.0, at or near the same time the THV entry appears, or within 1-3 candles and the red signal line should be at or above 0.0. If the signal from THV has been given, but the MACD is “late”, better to pass on this trade – see the trade example marked by the thick PINK line . KEY POINT: If the MACD bars have been above the 0.0 line for a long time, AND you get a fresh entry signal from THV, the green MACD bars MUST be above the red signal line on the MACD, if not, it means the trend is weak at the moment. You will see this weakness on some of the potential entries marked by the red lines. KEY POINT: If you have been long on a position for a good period of time and you are up many pips, and the bars on the MACD begin to drop below the red signal line, you might think about exiting your long. KEY POINT: The red signal line on the MACD should be trending in the direction of your trade when you get the THV signal. If the green bars have popped above the red signal line and above the 0.0 line, BUT the red signal line is trending down, LOOK OUT – a reversal is coming. Long Aggressive: The T3 has closed above Hull replace, HA candle above T3 and out of cloud. T3 TRIX – green above red. MACD bar at or above the 0.0 line and trending upward and the red signal line at or above the 0.0 line – BUT you are still under the CORAL – That’s what makes this an aggressive trade or scalp. Long Conservative: The T3 has closed above Hull replace, HA candle above T3 and out of cloud. T3 TRIX – green above red. MACD bar at or above the 0.0 line and trending upward and the red signal line at or above the 0.0 line – AND your entry signal coincides with you being above the CORAL – this is a conservative trade. (FOR SHORT ENTRIES – DO THE OPPOSITE OF ABOVE) ENRTY EXAMPLES: EUR/USD on 1/29/09 from 8:00 am EST to 14:38 EST (2:38 PM EST). I have posted several charts to illustrate what I am describing here. The following entries are both conservative (those might agree with the CORAL) and aggressive (those that are entered against the CORAL) . All potential entries shown in either green or red are based on those entries where the T3 closed above/below the Hull replace, and above/below the cloud, and there T3 TRIX agreed on the 1 MIN. The GREEN lines : Longs or shorts that might be entered where the MACD indicator AGREED with the entry rules of THV. These are safer, less draw down risk. The RED lines : Longs or shorts that might be entered where the MACD indicator DISAGREED with the entry rules of THV. These are not as safe, much greater risk of drawdown. The thick YELLOW lines : Shows the US news today. So the potential entries right near the news were ignored. The thick PINK line : A perfect THV v.2 setup 9including CORAL agreement), but the MACD was “late” in agreement. I would have passed on this. But you can see there was a secondary entry on the retest around 11:28 EST. MACD SETTINGS Settings under the Parameters: Fast EMA 12 Slow EMA 20 MACD SMA: 9 Apply to: Close Settings under the Colors: I use green for the Main and red for the Signal. Make the Main a solid thick line and the red as you desire. Settings under the Levels: You will need to add a level, in this case “0.0”. Style: this is the color of your 0.0 line – I made mine a little thick and a Magenta color. The 5 Minute T3 TRIX as an entry filter for the 1 minute chart. In addition to using the MACD as a filter for entries on the 1 minute chart, you should only go long on the 1 minute chart if the 5 MIN T3 TRIX shows the green line above the red line and trending up. You should only go short on the 1 MIN chart if the 5 MIN T3 TRIX shows the green line below the red line and trending down. You should use extreme caution with entries on the 1 MIN chart if the T3 TRIX on the 5 MIN is showing “overbought or oversold.” Commentary: Using the MACD as a filter in this manner is only a tool to add to your trading tool box. The entry and exit rules established by Cobra FX for the THV system still apply and you should review the rules of this system carefully. The MACD filter and T3 TRIX on the 5 MIN can be used as a filter for potential trades taken with or against the CORAL if all other THV entry criteria are met. As with any trading strategy or tool, the trade may still work against no matter how perfect the entry signals look, and this is especially true when you choose to scalp the 1 minute time frame. Remember, every strategy works right up until it doesn’t – so always be ready to exit a trade if it goes bad – always use stops. You must always consider pivot points, support and resistance, and news events. I have found the pivot points in the THV system to be excellent. All of the above rules can be applied to trading the 5 MIN and 15 MIN charts as well (even higher time frames if you are that patient), if you prefer to stay away from the 1 MIN time frame. This post is in no way meant to challenge the entry rules of the current and future THV entry rules. I look forward to any feedback regarding this post and your opinion. Thanks.

Thank you very much for your input and collaboration to the system! My personal opinion and as a member of THV Team, is that indeed everyone is free to add as much filters and other non-included indicators to your own comfort. However, the main idea behind THV is to develop both an efficient and productive trading setup which can work on any timeframe, with also multiple choices as to its scope and risk level, AND at the same time, the less encumbered design, with only the most necessary filters and indicators so it is simple to learn and easy to understand, and at the same time giving the best possible results. I am certain that there are, besides MACD, many indicators that one or the other member of this thread and Forum is accustomed to or likes to see on his/her screen to help in the decision making (I for one was only using ONE single indicator and I keep it on my charts with the THV setup, in the same way there are indicators that I don't use so I don't have them). However again, the discussion of this thread is centered upon a particular setup with its rules and elements, so everyone can share his/her own experience with the system using the same tool, at least when posting charts, so others are able to understand and learn. Finally, we are always open to evaluate any changes or additions to the system, coming from any of you, be it a member or the Team or not, because many minds together can build better ideas. In any case, one has to keep in mind that if it is intended to simplify the system while increasing its effectiveness, it will assuredly be considered in a positive manner. We wouldn't want to diverge from the central idea, which is to teach and learn fully the THV system and its rules, and how it works or performs for everyone using it. When this is achieved, of course anyone can add as many lines and filters as he/she pleases, anyway remember that the core of the system is the Trix (and especially in the new version to be released soon). What we want to avoid is confusion, especially for the newbies or people new to this system, so I would consider more appropriate to discuss your views on MACD for THV directly with Cobra who then will in his turn discuss it with the Team so we can make a decision about it Thank you again for your enthusiasm to help with THV system and your interesting development about the MACD possibilities in it!

Royconnell, v2.1 is not available yet. The development team is still testing, but should probably be released by Cobra sometime next week. Regarding v2 alerts, on your MT4 menu, go to Chart/Indicators. There are alerts THV Coral and THV Trix. These names are not exact. Coral is in the main body of the chart, while Trix is in Indicator Window 1. If you hilite one of these indicators and press the Edit button, you'll see the settings (true/false) under the Inputs tab. Should be good to go. Good trading to you.

--- 帖子 #3749 ---
No set limit, but trailings in case it runs much higher (or lower). The range on M1 is very tight (see ATR) so you have to gauge from higher timeframes to have an idea of the potential of the trade. Usually, and if I entered correctly, I will wait until it reaches 20 pips approximatively and set the stop to BE. Then a trailing of 25. Sometimes if I consider that there's not enough momentum and the price stalls +1-1 at the same price for half an hour, I'll get out of the trade. And of course, fastly at the cross back if I'm countertrending. This on MT4. On smaller TF scalping, I take what the market gives me: between +3 and +7 usually, and I run fast! M1 will most usually (in a slow market) go like this: +15 -20 +10 +15 -15 -10 etc etc etc. You have to watch the channels to establish in which range it will be moving and evolving, in several TFs so to have the whole picture.

As a tip, on MT4 never click when the price is moving (and no allowing slippage either!), usually there's a 3 second "stall" when a new candle opens, and there is where I usually act. Also, when it has run fast up or down and it recedes a little, the 3 second stall happens, try to check how it behaves on your own computer so you can choose the best moment for reaction.

--- 帖子 #3819 ---
Pip count can measure the effectiveness of the system, now money management pertains almost exclusively to the trader's decision of not always following a particular rule on this sense. Of course we are talking here about a normalized pip count... in the example you mention, the 90 pips lost would have to be multiplied by "x" times that the 1 lot was increased to... thus the real pip count would be equivalent to the negative percentage obtained. (100 pips with 1 lot, loses 90 pips with 2 lots that's 180 pips! so he's down 80 negative pips as well). In general, we should all be working under the same premises: no more than a 2% risk (better 1% risk), size of position accordingly so with a 50 pip s/l the maximum position size would be 2% of the account, etc... But it is also true that everyone has a different risk appetite, some will use much more, some will make it depend on the market conditions and vary according to the occasion and pairs involved, etc... Percentage on the account balance is indeed a measure of the trader's success in applying all the rules to his trading. However, pip count is also the net result of opening a trade and closing it by the rules, thus BOTH are important, because the pip count measures the potential that a system has. Also, the percentage could mean nothing because it's real value will depend on the total capital... a trader can be very successful by making only 3% if the account is big enough. Anyway this is only MY point of view and as such should be considered

--- 帖子 #3823 ---
Your math is indeed correct. But the practical aspects of trading make your assumptions perhaps invalid. First, with a 20 pip S/L and a 10 pip T/P target, that would give you a 2:1 risk reward ratio. That means you would have to "win" 3 out of 4 trades in order to make your 10 pips. Not so easy to do consistently. Then there is the psychological aspect of trading. It is feasible to keep scaling your trades as the account grows, but at some point your tolerance for drawdowns will be very sensitive, and your objective trading may fall apart. Imagine that your have to trade 20 full lots to maintain your 2 percent risk, that's 200 per pip. For some, it would be unbearable to weather even slight moves against you. So even though the math works, the fact is that when your account grows, you would have to limit your position size to stay sane. This is a time proven fact. Many people are capable of growing small accounts fast, but when things get scaled up, the psychological aspects come into play. Hope this helps.

Because at a certain point it will be very difficult for a broker to find the correspondent liquidity for such a huge amount of lots. The fact is that no broker will allow you to trade 1000 lots (or you will have to go through a bank directly, with a totally different leverage, more like 1:1 on those big amounts. Exponential growth has a curve, in which at a certain point and if everything keeps being steady, the curve converts to somewhat a flat line slightly ascending or descending from time to time. Alike the market, we "move" in cycles, we are not always the same, we can even be contradictory at times, as seeing a bull market and selling the pair, for no known logical reason. We can be distraught, we can face personal issues that cloud our mind. I don't think that anybody can be following 100% perfectly and always in the same way, a given set of rules. All the more slightest details have to be included and have their own backup plan, because the most unpredictable thing is the one that will occur unexpectedly and usually precisely when we are thinking that everything is going soooo smoothly. Good emotions can be even worse than bad, because they will cloud the picture through a rosy pair of lens... A sudden drop in self-esteem, a sudden RISE in self esteem more particularly, a bad day, or a slight breach of the rules. Beware especially when you've been having a particularly great winning streak. Make a graph of your daily performance and treat it and read it as it was a forex chart. It behaves in the same way. After a huge spike, most probably comes a fall. Be prepared and keep on going. Flow with life and life will flow with you. Be in sync, with the markets and with all the aspects of your life. And at least, when you're not in sync (because that will happen more than we would like to) be aware that you aren't and be quiet then. And finally, be prepared to give twice as much as you receive. If you can keep discipline day after day and your own "real life" in a good balance, you will have great odds in your favour.

Here to end the numbers discussion (as it seems we are straying on the sidelines, lol) but I had to write it down With a 20 pips stop loss, you have to make 800 pips and lose 600 average so to have a net 200 pips (daily 10 pips per 20 trading days), based on a 70/30 win/loss average. This would give around 20% a month with a 2% risk. Starting with $2500, you would need 55-56 months (nearly 5 years) to reach the 5M goal, provided you don't take anything out. As this doesn't seem fair for the trader not to pay him/herself, let's say that you start taking half of your profits after you reach the first $100.000 (nearly the first two years). You would need 6 additional months to reach the goal. And would have banked about the same 5M with half taken out profits. Voilà!

I also posted the directions here according to the webpage: Time-Zone Inputs: LocalTimeZone: TimeZone for which MT4 shows your local time, e.g. 1 or 2 for Europe (GMT+1 or GMT+2 (daylight savings time). Use zero for no adjustment. The MetaQuotes demo server uses GMT +2. DestTimeZone: TimeZone for the session from which to calculate the levels (e.g. 1 or 2 for the European session (without or with daylight savings time). Use zero for GMT Example: If your MT server is living in the EST (Eastern Standard Time, GMT-5) zone and want to calculate the levels for the London trading session (European time in summer GMT+1), then enter -5 for LocalTimeZone, 1 for Dest TimeZone. Please understand that the LocalTimeZone setting depends on the time on your MetaTrader charts (for example the demo server from MetaQuotes always lives in CDT (+2) or CET (+1), no matter what the clock on your wall says. --- 帖子 #3848 ---
No. Both settings are to calculate the daily pivots according to the session (all-day session) you want to use as start/end of day. The first setting is to tell the indicator how many hours of difference there are at the server's 00:00 with GMT 00:00 (that would be -5 in your case). The second setting is to tell the indicator how many hours of difference there are at the session's start (if NY, 5pm EST = GMT 22:00) with GMT 00:00. The chart shows that you are starting your daily session at EST 00:00. The correct settings for starting at NY close (which would place your "today/yesterday" vertical line at 17:00 on your chart = 5pm EST) are on the link I gave you, as well as the ones to start the day at 00:00 GMT. In synthesis: Start of day at NY close: 1st setting: -5 (hourly difference EST/GMT) 2nd setting: 2 (NY close is two hours ahead of GMT 00:00) Start of day at GMT 00:00 1st setting: -5 (hourly difference EST/GMT) 2nd setting: 0 (GMT 00:00 is 0 hours ahead of GMT 00:00) You can't calculate on a partial session (only one market) basis.

No, not wrong impression. Money management is key, and hopefully when a trader goes live the first time they understand this, many rookies do not, they don't understand how sometimes a loss is a good trade when there risk exposure is limited to 1-2% of account equity, not account balance. Every trade you open eats away at the balance and equity is reduced according to your leverage, i.e. 100:1, 200:1, 50:1, etc. When traders speak of not risking more than 1-2% of your account, equity is what they are speaking about for every trade you open that moves against you, equity is diminished. You will read, in the threads, of traders trading 2-3, or even more currency pairs at one time, about during an existing trade adding on to your position. If you do not understand the "whole picture" and follow these "calls", you find in some threads, you may win for awhile, but without the education and discipline,rest assured, eventually, Mr. Margin Call will come a callin!If new to managing and trading currency, I would suggest you manage one trade on one currency pair at a time. Once trade is closed, then find another entry. We all talk about money management.There are those who say, out loud and/or to themselves " Well ,of course , I manage my money !" I like to think differently now,through my experiences," I manage my risk!" With that thought, I look at a 1% loss of money as minimizing my risk. That has helped me to emotionally separate myself from a trade, that has gone against me, and the fear of loss when entering a trade. No matter how good the system, there will be breakdowns. Trading currency is not for the weak of heart. It is good this topic was brought up before THV2.1 release. ( within a few pips, as different brokers may have a slight difference in the OHLC on their daily candle) Your time zone is not what the destination time zone is for. It is for determining what zone ( London, Sydney, New York) you want your pivots to be calculated from . The pivots are calculated using Open, High, Low, and Close of a DAILY candle--Hence the term Daily pivots. Weekly pivots are based on weekly candle data, monthly on monthly candle data. I hope this helps!

--- 帖子 #3862 ---
Indeed you raise an important point here. Every system (paired to the trader him/herself) has an average win/loss which is the result of previous thourough testing. For example, in the case of THV, Cobra stated earlier that the win/loss ratio was around 75/35 somewhat. This means that, for every 100 trades, you have to be prepared to accept 1/3 of them to be stopped out. Now: what is a "good trade"? How can a losing or stopped out trade be so? A good trade is a position that has been taken AS PER THE RULES , the ones of the system itself, AND your own money management rules. This way, you can have good losing trades, and BAD WINNING ones. Let's say your MM is "not risking more than 2% on a single trade", plus the system's rules. You suddenly decide to have a go at gambling, and open a position with half the money on your account and enter the trade without waiting for the entry rules to be met. And suddenly you're lucky! It goes in your direction and after a few minutes you close the trade with positive pips. Wow, what a winner! In fact, NO. That super-duper "winning" trade is a BAD trade in your books. Because you broke every rule of your trading plan, and doing so you put at risk much more than what your MM says, and finally you didn't execute it with discipline . Next time you happen to do this, who can guarantee you'll be as lucky? And you probably won't be! Every trade taken by the rules is a GOOD trade. Every trade that you take breaking the rules and without following your trading plan and discipline, is a BAD trade.

Here an excellent article from Darkstar to help you understand the markets (and brokers) a little better: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=7484 You don't have to place physical stops (unless maybe a disaster stop much wider, just in case of power or connection failures), but you've got to have a fixed number at which you will close the trade manually if it goes against you. And this especially if it is small, because the normal range of the market fluctuation might be greater. I really don't think that the Big Boys are after every single trader who opens a position of $1 or even $10 a pip. However it is true that there are certain levels at which everyone and his dog places the stops and that is what they will be hunting, if hunting there is. Source That's a pretty small percentage of the overall picture! But, leaving the stop hunt paranoia aside, what you are saying is very important indeed. Seems that this will be an "off-topic" week-end after all (and as we are all awaiting the new THV V2.1 release!) but I'll try to explain a bit about leverage, and what true leverage is. Usual leverage (as the one your broker allows) can be anything between 1:1 and 1:500. This refers to the margin needed to secure a position, 1:1 would mean that for opening a trade with 1 lot, you need to have at least $100.000 for the margin (or more if the main currency is not the USD) plus the spread*$10, plus your stoploss*$10, plus maybe a little more room just in case. At 1:500, you only will need 0,20% of the value of the lot (or $200 - $300) plus the mentioned additions, to open that same position. However, true leverage is the proportion of the overall positions size. Indeed if you open 1 lot with only $300 in your account you are using the full 1:500 true leverage . Now, if you open a position which, including the spread and risk, totals $300, you will be using 1:1 true leverage. That would be for example 300 units (3 nanolots - pip value $0,01 per nanolot). If you are using microlots (pip value $0,1) you will be using 1:10 true leverage. Should you open more positions, the total added value of your trades will vary the leverage accordingly (3 positions at 1:10 equal a 1:30 true leverage) and it will keep growing (which in fact is also growing your risk) as you keep adding. When we speak about not risking more than 2% of the account, let's say we want to use 20 pips maximum risk per trade. On that same $300 account, and using Cobra's handy calculator, you can open a position of 3 microlots (3000 units) at 2% risk with 20 pips stop. This will give you the above mentioned 1:30 true leverage, which is pretty much safe. In any case, and with any amounts, the risk percentage doesn't change (only the required stops and corresponding position sizing should you need more or less than 20 pips). If you are risking 2% of your total equity, you will never lose more than 2% of your total equity, independently of any leverage used. If you want to raise your stops, let's say you need 60 pips, still at 2% risk, you will only open one microlot. Your position will be then at 1:10 true leverage. But you still will be losing 2% of your account if stops are hit. Raise your stops to 100 pips, decrease the pòsition to 600 units or 6 nanolots. Your position is now at 1:2 true leverage but you will still be losing 2% of your account if stops are hit. Etc... etc... Also remember that indeed the calculations have to be made on your accoun'ts equity (thanks Gofer Pips!) and not the balance... you could have several positions open going down and thus your equity decreases, that remaining equity is the really available capital at that moment.

Thanks for the compliment, but I'm Gofer and Ed is on a shortbus to somewhere today! What you show is 10 pip spread ( the cost your broker charges you to open a position at your leverage level) Assume a $10,000 account 1 standard lot(100:1 leverage) controls $100,000 of currency backed by $1000 of your equity. If spread is 2 pips, and you open a 1 lot trade, you have $1000 of equity tied up in margin + $20 spread cost. Every pip that moves against you will cost you $10. This trade has risked, at open, 10.02% of your equity, every pip against you will add .01% to this risk. The part to use as determining S/L at a 2% risk( which 2% of $10000 being $200) is that little .01%. At $10 per pip, you now are required to close that position at a loss of 20 pips(18 pips + 2 pip spread). At the close of the trade( assuming S/L is hit), you receive your margin back ($1000) minus the 20 pip loss( $200) For a new account balance and equity of $9800. Your broker has rules that you need to be aware of regarding position size based on account type, and minimum margin level. My broker will close your positions automatically if your margin level reaches 50% I am not sure I have answered what you were asking, but I do the best I can!

--- 帖子 #3878 ---
*Since this is the THV thread, the terminology and system discussed will be based upon that. *Any applications to any other system will need to be translated by the author of that system Assumption 1 Using THV rules based on a 5m and 1m TF trade, we are looking for a good point of entry on the 5m chart, always checking back on status of rules being met on 1m also, paying attention to pivots,and whatever trader deems of value in his/her personalized analysis. Assumption 2 We open a position of X lots when THV criteria on both time frames is met. How do we manage the trade? 1. We can exit trade on candle color change against us, or fast trix color change, cross of trixi( is that the plural?), or even close of candle on the opposing side of the trade we took. These are all based upon whether you have aggressive view, safe view, or conservative. These are defined with THV2.1 2. We can close part of our position. How? If, on the time frame we are following trade, we get signal to exit by THV criteria, but a higher time frame shows we can stay in ( watching 5m but 15 m says okay to stay) We can close 25-50% of position, and move our stop/loss to the breakeven point. If trade goes against us we lose nothing and await new signal to pull trigger. However, if on lower timeframe it shows small retrace, and retrace does not trigger our break even/entry point, we can continue to follow the trade on 5m and 15m. As Price continues favorably in our direction, we can await an exit signal on the 5m time frame. We can close another 25% or complete position based on our analysis. At this point we can move our stop/loss into a profit area we deem somewhat safe from being triggered. If we close the position completely, we can await new signal to pull trigger. Assuming we have 50% of our trade still open, and have moved our stop/loss into profit, we now have assured that the complete trade will show a profit. Now we can watch on the 15m and 30m or 1h and await signal to exit. We close another 25% on exit signal on the 15m. We can close the complete position and await new signal to trigger, or set a trailing stop loss and forget about it as long as the trailing stop/loss, if price immediately reverses, will still allow for last portion of trade to be at even or in profit. If last portion is in profit with trigger of trailing stop loss, you may move on to look for another entry and let that dog run until it tires out! There are many variations of this philosophy, and there are very good traders in the THV thread that I am sure will share their techniques. Hope this was helpful!

I am a numbers guy so I am always analyzing and reanalyzing this. What I have come up with is increasing lots using squares of the number 2. Following a 1-2% maximum risk rule (usually 1.25-1.5%), I started with 1 microlot (10 cents each) then went 2. After gains supported an increase I went to 4 lots. So then it continues to 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 etc... but ONLY when MM supports it (I won't explain the MM as I think there is now a plethora of info here on that ). This gives me a great way to scale out. For example, on 16 lots I may take 1/2 profit at 10 pips if a countertrend trade, move SL to BE and take another 4 lots profit when M1 trix tells me the trend is turning. This still leaves me with 4 lots. Then when M5 trend starts to turn I may take another 2 lots. Then I still have 2 lots in just in case the trend resumes. I don't always do it exactly this way but I think you get the idea. I tried other numbers but, strangely, when I do I don't seem to do as well. Anyway, I don't expect anyone to copy this technique. The point is to continuously analyze your lots sizes (and your entire trading plan for that matter). Don't ever get complacent about anything in your trading plan.

--- 帖子 #3881 ---
I understand what you are going through. I struggled with this in the beginning too. Then this is what I decided to do: I only focused on changing the first number until it was correct. You know it is correct once you see that the recalculation of pivots occurs at the time you want. For example, when my broker's server was on GMT, and I wanted to set it for NY close, I put -2. In other words, a zero would imply "calculate pivots at GMT 00:00", which is midnight in London but 7 pm NY. A -2 brings pivot calculation to 5 pm NY which is the close of market there. I know it can be complicated but if you keep experimenting with the numbers you will get the right one. This is not "by the book" but to me is simpler and gets the job done. The key numbers are server time and what close you want pivots calculated for. Based on your server being -5, and that you want NY close pivots (you can't have them for both sessions unless you make 2 charts), I would guess your settings would be -7. A -5 setting would give you London midnight pivots and the additional 2 hour shift gives you NY close. Please try that and see if it looks right. Once you get it you are done but it can be until you do.

Forex trading has to be treated as a job. With a proper (and limited) schedule which accomodates in your life the best market hours for your strategy as well as the rest of your obligations: family, maybe still a standard job, recreation, friendship, study and (the most important thing) proper rest and sleep. As for a standard job, you should have the proper tools, and this includes not only a good Internet connection, a good computer and alternative elements to supply when one of the others falter, etc... You should "build your office" like you would for any other type of working situation. Free of distractions, a good and anatomical chair if your strategy asks for long hours of screen time, frequent short interruptions to relax the eyes if you have been looking at the screen for an hour, proper exercise, etc.... NEVER trade if you feel sleepy (imagine that your job involves operating a very dangerous machinery!) indeed Forex won't cut your hand neither you will slip and fall at the factory floor... but you could risk to blow your account as the risks of committing a mistake are way much higher when we aren't able to focus properly, i.e., lack of sleep, too many hours doing the same thing, physical pain because of improper furniture, a drink or two that lowered your attention capacity...etc... Choose your trading session carefully taking all those elements into account. Set yourself a daily goal in pips AND in time spent at the screen. If not met, tomorrow is another day and the markets never stop. I personally don't stay more (now) than 3 continuous (and interrupted) hours trading because that is the maximum attention span that I have on a single task. To rest, I change the task like doing some writing, reading, studying, answering emails, etc... then I "come back" to the charts refreshed. And I have two shifts (one is in the morning for one platform, at NY session, with THV, the other in the afternoon for the other platform and my other strategy) and I added a "mini" shift for the third platform where I set up trades and go to sleep, an hour before shutting everything down. I used to have a continuous day starting on sunday open till friday close... with only cat naps in the meantime, had my sleeping hours all messed up because I wanted to trade Europe and London and so had to sleep in the afternoons with all the normal people around me interrupting my sleep... etc etc... Now with this new schedule I can finally sleep at normal hours, and still trade (and be more efficient as everything has its own time and place and proper order) even more than before. P.S.: Just read TW post, it's exactly the same that happened to me "Surreal" is the word. Thanks for the input!
