--- 帖子 #3898 ---
Big Dogs are a (very important) part of the market. Usually the settings that are used by the greater number of people will work the best, because everybody will be reacting to those levels at the same time and place. However I would recommend to test different approaches, so you can determine by yourself which settings work more accurately on your charts. The key is support/resistance: former levels at which the price has been rejected many times, channels and trendlines too. Also, pivots should be considered as "zones" more than a particular and exact price (and especially because there are differences among most brokers on prices that can go as far as 10-12 pips!). I want to point out that this is my personal opinion: I check the pivots but personally prefer the psych levels to work with short term in M1, which I consider to be small pivots in themselves. Price goes in waves, not linearly. When PA is observed in a very small timeframe, you can see that at every smaller level there's a "decision" being made, a price is approved or rejected, bulls or bears win the small battle, then goes on to the next level or comes back to the previous, and later on "decides" to retest again until the level breaks, or the opposite party wins and rejects the "proposed" price, like on a staircase. Then the key levels (previous bigger staircases on higher timeframes) are made by the supports or resistances that held through many attempts of being crossed. Pivots are, as fibonacci lines, the result of a calculation made upon the analysis of historical data, and in a certain way and because of it, they can become a self fulfilled prediction, because everyone is watching the same prices go on and have the same information. So indeed, the best pivots will be those that are used by the greater number of traders.

Hi TradeWell, I agree with you. I live on the west coast too, in a small town called Medford Oregon. I had the same issue with wanting to work the London session in order to get big moves. Trading is all I do so I figured I could work at night and be fine. Well, while the rest of the house – and most of the US was asleep, I would be working. I knew I could not keep this up. I used to be a Paramedic and was used to getting up a lot to go on emergencies. I went back and looked at several months of charts for the E/U and found there just as many good moves during the US and Sydney/Asia as there was during the London session. In fact, in back testing, I would have made more money during these sessions. So I abandoned the late night and chose the early morning schedule. Most of the time I am done trading by mid morning and I have the rest of the day do fool around. I get up at 4:30 am PST, at my desk at 5:00 am and plan on working until 10:00 am – 1 PM PST. This is usually sufficient to find many good moves with the THV system trading both the 1 and 5 minute charts. So, to all of those folks who think you are missing moves by sleeping through the London session; rest (sleep) assured that there are plenty of moves during US session hours. Just review the charts for the past few weeks alone and you will see what I mean. If you work a regular job (like 8-5) during the day, there are plenty of Asia and early Euro session trades to take as well, and you still get to sleep through the night.

Hi FreddyFx, It looks like you have a great place to trade (whether from the pool with a laptop) or from your office, which I saw a picture you post many weeks back. I wanted to respond to your point about investing in the proper tools, in this case for trading. Look folks, this is a business. To be successful in most businesses, you need to have the right equipment and technology. To trade forex, or any market, I would recommend at least two monitors and one good computer with a fast processor and lots of memory (RAM). I run a two D*ll brand Precision 390s with Core 2 Duo processors. I have 4 gigs of memory and three 512 mb video cards – each running two monitors (6 dell widescreen). I used to have 12 monitors (when I traded stocks – okay – maybe a little obsessive). The second computer is for watching other markets (now only 2 monitors – not 6). Yes, the setup you see was expensive, but it sure makes trading a lot easier and it will pay for itself (already has). Since I have to sit for a long time, my chair was even expensive. A good desk, good modem, a good computer with two monitor support, and fast processor is cheap compared to not being well equipped for this business. Trust me, invest in the tools, learn the THV system, and follow this thread, and the money and time spent WILL pay off. NEWBIES - Like FreddyFx says, many in this thread and others have been doing this a long time and spent hundreds of hours studying this business. I have spent the last year alone immersing myself in forex – full time. I have lost money and made money as part of the learning process – hmm – just like a “real” business. Like a doctor who spent years (and a ton of money) learning to become a skilled medical technician (and to make a very good living), the investment of time and money as a trader will result in a good career for you, too. The best trading is ahead!

This way you'll be sure it is there...

--- 帖子 #4081 ---
If wanting to start the day at GMT 00:00, that would be 2,0 and your "today" line will be showing at 02:00 on your chart. If wanting to start the day at EST 17:00 (NY close - Sydney open), that would be 2,2 and your "today" line will be showing at 00:00 on your chart. Your own local time doesn't effect the calculations. Now, should you want to start the day at London open (GMT 08:00) settings would be 2, -8 and your "today" line will be showing at 10:00 on your chart.

Here's a little table for the Pivots indicator (SDX Pivots) timezone settings: This will be included soon in the manual as well. 1st setting: the GMT hourly difference of your broker to GMT (-5 EST, 0 GMT, +1 and +2 Europe, etc...) 2nd setting: The start candle happens "x" hours later (-) or "x" hours earlier (+) than the 00:00 candle on the broker. Some Brokers Time: IBFX, ODL = GMT ALPARI = GMT +1 FXDD, FXPRO , Ikon Royal, Windsor, FxSol, Altrade? AFB? = GMT +2 (please help with your own broker's timezone so we can add to this list) Note: some of these settings may vary when DST is in effect, you will have to adjust accordingly at that time but we then will issue a DST recalculation.

Hi Doblece, I've been reading the PP discussion in this thread and I need to comment regarding the broker's time and please correct me if I'm wrong. The broker time is very important to me as it affects the shape of the candles in various time frames &amp; simultaneously would affect my tech analysis. So, in the past I found an indicator in the MetaEditor online library which will show the GMT time, Broker time, &amp; Local time. The indicator's name is "Cloq". My research didn't just depend on this indicator, I even compared the candles of the metatrader brokers with FXCM &amp; FXSOL and here is my conclusion: -If you show the period separators on your chart and the new day starts at 00:00 then the broker is GMT time and it's following the real market in it's open/close time. -The GMT mentioned above (&amp; in the Cloq if you try it) is not the actual GMT "London", but it's the GMT of the market which differs from the real GMT by +3H. -So the forex market GMT = Actual GMT + 3. -I've been using THV V2 on my GMT broker and the Today vertical line shows on top of my period separator (00:00) broker time. -Therefore my comments on the brokers I made my research on are: Ikon Royal, Windsor = GMT-1 IBFX, ODL = GMT-3 ALPARI = GMT -2 Altrade, AFB, FXSOL = GMT &gt;&gt;&gt; Actual market time (new day starts with Sydney or to be more precise starts right after the close of NY) &gt;&gt;&gt; Actual candles. P.S. Mentioned GMT above = Actual GMT + 3 what you mentioned in your post about the brokers is correct if you consider GMT as the actual GMT "London". If anyone is confused by my post then please ignore it and stick to what you understand. Thanks &amp; Cheers.

--- 帖子 #4166 ---
Your local time doesn't enter into the equation. If Broker time is GMT+1 as it seems, your settings would be 1, 2 to start the day at NY close. If you want it to start at NY EST 00:00 (GMT time 19:00), your settings will be effectively 1, -5 (your start candle will be showing at 20:00). If you want it to start at NY OPEN though (GMT time 13:00), your settings will have to be 1, -13 (your start candle will be showing at 14:00).

--- 帖子 #4193 ---
Unless there's a tremendously big spike, it's value shouldn't change so much. In fact, the considered "safe" setting (IMO - most people use 1,5 to 2*actual ATR) is usually 2*max ATR or 3*min ATR (of the recent range). By setting it at 3*actual ATR it is really safe enough, however remember that if you are trading based on a higher timeframe, this should be the SL to consider, even if your entry is made on a lower TF. ATR*3 allows for three times the actual volatility at the moment the trade is taken. Here some articles about this subject: http://www.tradingsecrets.com.au/articles/forum-1.htm http://www.trading-plan.com/money_st...olatility.html http://www.meta-formula.com/stop-loss.html http://darmasdt.multiply.com/journal/item/309

--- 帖子 #4214 ---
The rules still apply, but don't expect as much movement up or down when Trix crosses or PA crosses the cloud. I would suggest you review various timeframes, like either the M15 or M30, to see where short-term tops and bottoms (i.e., recent support and resistance). You can sell off the tops and buy off the bottoms, but use very small stop loss, I think. Trix will usually show you when it is at the top or bottom. Again, don't expect giant pip counts. Be happy with 5-10 PIPs at a time. A sideways market is seeking direction. Trade very carefully, or not all.

How far do we need to go or zoom out to draw a trendline on a 5M or 1M chart? I have been trying to draw a tl in 5M chart in EU but not clearly getting it

--- 帖子 #4247 ---
Usually a trendline is made by connecting the two most recent lows (or highs). (Lower lows - Higher highs). However, you can go to a higher timeframe to see and verify if the line "comes from behind" from an earlier continuation, but usually the last two will be ok. As you are using a multiTF setup, you can maximize the individual window while you draw the trendline, then restore it to its usual position (middle button on the Windows frame).

--- 帖子 #4253 ---
Nice channels. Though the yellow line should be drawn from the wicks as are the other ones (or not be taken so far in time, as the last two seem to be correct indeed). Usually an ascending trendline is drawn from the lows, and a descending one is drawn from the highs. The corresponding opposite highs or lows line is what allows to see the channel, or if it forms a triangle pattern, etc.. Maybe you could use for this the analyze chart (I saw the template and indicators folder in the zip download in page and post 1) so you keep the THV charts clean, or maybe barely the main trenline as to see supports/resistances. Then you can draw all channels in the different timeframes too, as to see the big picture if you so wish... The change in slope is important to notice, as effectively the first lows are steeper, and then it seems to start to what I call "rotate": the angle of the different lines drawn from the last two lows (or highs) start becoming more and more flat, then slowly changing (or not) to a descending trendline, this way it is possible to anticipate a contrarian move, IMO. Also, you will be able to see if the market is flat, and so avoid to trade when it's ranging or apply more precautions when you do in those conditions.

--- 帖子 #4265 ---
The "right" time, for me, is 17:00 EST so any broker at GMT+2 has it. For you, any broker at GMT+3 will be at the right time. Time is only an illusion anyway... Forex is in fact about PRICE The ideal scene would be a price-based platform so we can more properly evaluate. By now, the only "accurate" charts for any broker are the hourly charts and below (and provided the prices don't deviate too much from one to the other!), and these are on what the Pivots Indicator is based, which you can tweak at your preference, on any broker, to have the correct calculations. Of course, H4 and Daily charts will have slight differences, but IMO one hour more or less doesn't change the overall trend.

--- 帖子 #4350 ---
Yes, it is usually good to get out of a trade when the trix is near the oversold or overbought line and changes colors. Protect every pip and then watch for your next set-up. In your case, if you are in a strong trend downward, you might not want to take all those little riskier longs when trix is changing green. You might just want to wait for longer, safer shorts. Trade with the trend as much as you can. I usually look to the M15 and M30 to be able to clearly see the trend. Good trading to you. BTW, I don't trade GPB, was just commenting on your chart.

--- 帖子 #4351 ---
Well, as you can see, considering money management, it was really only good for a brief long trade. The trix was deep toward oversold and changing to green, so I would have been looking to trade. Price could also be expected to bounce off that pivot, but not for a lot. It's often less risky to take your trade to the pivot, catch the very common bounce for a few, and then sit and watch. Let the market determine its direction. Watch your trix, cloud and trend, and get back on. Just my two cents.

--- 帖子 #4416 ---
Only note the numbers and colors in the right column, do not let the lines overwhelm. I have a key on the chart for daily,hourly, and 15 min S/R. The weakest being 15 min. This is a dynamic, changing chart that I use to keep a historical tracking of strong supports and resistances based on the different time frames. For example, as price continues to revisit a price on the 15 and bounces, either as support if movement is down or resistance as price moves up, I add a corresponding colored line. As these lines become stronger, you will see them become support and resistance in higher time frames, and their color will change to the higher timeframe until they become a daily. I do not trade these, I use them to keep track of historicals to watch and their correlation on the pivots on our THV, and trade based upon THV rules. I do the same with Fibs, which there was a discussion about last week( I think it was Thursday or Friday). This is my methods, and they are always subject to modification. I ascribe to Eimstein's theory of Stupidity, "Keep doing the same thing and expect a different result" As of now these work for me , when they quit, in the sh!t can they go,and I only share as others may see price differently and it could help them see the big picture. This is the method to my madness!

--- 帖子 #4580 ---
With all the buzz about divergence recently I'd like to share some thoughts. Divergence is a great tool but keep in mind that it's just that, a tool. A lot of times the divegence doesn't work and after several times of this most traders just start to ignore it. Cobra (or someone else) brought up the fact that on the shorter time frames it's not very dependable...spot on. I can't post a chart right at the moment as I'm overhauling them but if you look at the M5 E/U chart at the prior push to the top you'll see what I'm referring to. Price moves above the MR1 and pushes up to the R1 and is rejected. Comes back down to the MR1 and moves up strongly to just above the R2, then makes a correction back down to (just above) the MR2. Then price moves up nicely to just short of the R3 and pulls back to just above the R2. Price again moves nicely up through R3 and stops midway between R3 and MR4. This is a fairly reliable divergence... Reason: Price made three higher highs and the trix made three lower highs. While the last high of the trix is higher than the second one it's still good divergence. Point: A three point divergence is much stronger than a two point divergence and more reliable. You can see that the price move down after the third high was much larger than the down moves of the previous two highs... Just something to think about when your watching divergence. Cheers

--- 帖子 #4628 ---
You can use it on any timeframe. I personally tested it on M30 and H4, of course you will have to adjust your stops accordingly (and be more patient ). The formal definition of scalping is that of trades where you go in and out in a very short span of time, sometimes even less than one minute (usually around 5 minutes in average) and taking from 1 to 10 pips, depending on the volatility, with very tight stops. Sometimes a scalping trade can develop into a longer trending one, and this is why you can keep it going by checking a higher timeframe with the same parameters. I usually can scalp between 50-100 total pips in that slow Asia session, for me it's the best moment as there aren't big spikes going around and it's usually ranging so one can take trades both ways.

--- 帖子 #4630 ---
I don't set a fixed stop but usually close it under 20 which is my maximum stop. However, I wait until I can get the best possible entry so the trade goes my way immediately or barely goes back 5-10 pips max. My R:R is awful (average winner around 5 pips) but with a 85-90% win ratio is very acceptable. And only will I do that on a fast platform (would never scalp that way on Mt4). The 3*ATR indication on the system is a good S/L because it will take account of the actual volatility at the moment you place the trade.

--- 帖子 #4633 ---
Ok doblece, thanks for your answer. Now a question, why does one use a higher TF than 5 min, if with small TF is easier to analize the movement of market within short span of time..

--- 帖子 #4634 ---
1. To spot the trend more easily and be able to go with it if expecting a potential longer trade. 2. The small TF is used to get a better entry on the higher one: if you trade on M5, you look for an entry on M1 when you have the setup on M5. 3. Then, having entered the trade on M1, you can see if it is still going on on M5 despite the small pullbacks on M1, this will help you gauge the potential left (unless you are in and out for a fast scalping, but it will be still helpful to go with the trend). For example: I use M1 for my entries, but at the same time I watch M30 and M5. If all three are in agreement, the trade will be much safer than if "longer term" (compared to M1) trend is against my direction.

--- 帖子 #4641 ---
Mostly channels/trendlines. For example, if in M30 and M5 price is at the top of the channel (different channels, of course, each on its timeframe and evolution range), I won't be taking a long position even if M1 gives the green light, I will rather wait for all of them to be at a safe point (including pivots and psych levels) and for example at least the midline of the channel - where it could possibly bounce). Of course, the trend too, first of all the main trend in M30, then the secondary trend in M5 (where it could be traveling inside the M30 main in a contrarian direction) and finally M1 trend and signals. You shouldn't worry about the pips you leave on the table, provided you didn't pay for them The price moves (in average, and based on the slowest markets as Asia) 10 pips every 5 minutes, then reverses, then again, etc... even in a tight channel as we might have seen (barely 15-20 pip ranges). On a 1 minute chart, you can't expect much more per trade unless the pair starts trending (which seldom occurs in Asia), or unless you stay in the trade by managing your stops and watching the higher TF (M5). Especially if your entry is conservative. However, in more volatile market conditions, trades can yield a better return. So maybe you would have to settle for better trading conditions, like in Europe/NY markets, where a conservative entry will not hamper the evolution of the trade. But I'll repeat: what really matters is how much safe your trades are, and how many pips you didn't lose. There are thousands of pips of the table (and many more if you consider all the pairs that are moving at the same time). Cherish the ones the market is willing to give you, there is always plenty of opportunities throughout the day. I used to look down on scalping because it seemed to me that one couldn't have much results out of 2-3 pips trades. The funny part is that as soon as it didn't matter if I left pips on the table (and I leave a LOT!) I started having awesome results through the sum of all those insignificant little trades which I despised in the past... Edit: in fact, if the entry had been taken on M5, you should have entered in the next candle after your vertical line, after it was confirmed that the one you're signaling is effectively out of the cloud... so if based on M5 you would have entered 10 pips lower than on M1, where the conditions were met one minute earlier at a better price...) That trade looks as an average 30 pips trade which is really excellent if scalping.

--- 帖子 #4660 ---
Indeed, for a longer trade, a higher timeframe is better. However, it also needs much wider stops. This system fits any trading style, scalping, intraday or longer term trading, that's the beauty of THV3!! The confirmation works inversely: you trade on a timeframe (example M15) and you would confirm the entry on a LOWER timeframe = M5 in this case (for a more precise placement of the entry). Then you can extend the trade by looking at a higher timeframe, for example H1 (or even M30) to see if it is still trending and avoid that the small pullbacks take you out. I used to trade M15-M5 and indeed it's a good combination.

Speaking on (calculated) risks, here's a trade I just took about half an hour ago and closed on 8:45 candle at 1.2977 (so I could post and because of the doji HA and the vicinity of the Pivot) for 55 pips. I was having a look at M15 (as a continuation of the conversation with EATrader) and I happened to change exactly at the candle change, and the bearish divergence popped up. I did a quick check on M5 and M1 and decided to risk the entry for a quick 15-18 pip (at least back to retest MR1 - 1.3014). S/L very tight (10 pips) at 1.3044 (the Coral level). Projected R/R = 1.5/1 at least. My reasons to enter were based on: * M15 bearish divergence and Trix color change of Fast Trix, trend already red and down in the previous candle. PA crossed the cloud and opened outside (or so it seemed). PA above the Coral though. * M5 both Trixes had already crossed themselves and Fast Trix had crossed the zero Line. Late entry for M5... PA way down below the Cloud. PA above the Coral though here too. * M1 below the Coral line (and Coral red) PA above the Cloud though. A small reverse bearish divergence (not shown, but you can check on your charts). Trixes crossed up and trend bar green though. That would be somewhat 51% vs 49% chances but what made me trigger the trade was the certitude I have on psych levels, I have observed that it is true that when a level (00-20-33-50-66-80) is penetrated, there is a very high probability that the price goes (after pulling back a little) to test the next level, and on the previous candles it has gone as far as 1.3010 (making this also a penetration of the MR1 pivot). So I was at least 80% sure that it would go and retest the MR1, and most probably would continue then to 1.3000, as level 1.3020 had been breached previously. I controlled my exit finger (I would have usually closed as soon as it reached 16 pips) and even when it made a higher low in M1, because I was determined to see if both divergences (reverse in M1 and standard in M15) worked out, additionally to the psych levels observation. And for once in my life, try to control the impatience when a trade is going my way... (scalper's "bad" habit, lol... exit trigger happy!) I waited then (and set my trailings at 25 as soon as I saw the next red candle after the pullback - 8:24) and started taking the pictures and such. The trade was still going on when I took the pictures. Price came back very near my stop (phew! good I didn't see that!) thereafter but continued down and I finally closed manually when I saw the doji HA candle at 8:45. I wasn't looking for a trade, but the opportunity to test several things (among them the divergence theory) popped up and I took it. The above calculations and decisions took about a minute, mostly because M1 was green. I don't make a list (1 pro vs 1 con, etc...) but I have a mental idea of the pros and cons ratio for each element and their respective weight in the decision making so it's done automatically. Don't try this at home, though... unless you have enough screen time experience to be able to take all the variables into account and sum them up fast and, of course, with the proper stop in place (even if mental) if you happen to be wrong. The "official" TF on which this trade was taken under the rules, was indeed M5, in which it would be a late entry or re-entry trade, and catalogued as aggressive because I didn't take the M5 Coral into account on that TF.

--- 帖子 #4749 ---
Hello, I will try to answer this question, here is how it works, the divergence program will search for peaks and troughs of the fast trix and will draw divergences between peaks and troughs. The tricky part is when detecting the newest/last bar, there is no way you would be able to tell if the last bar will be the peak or the trough until you see what's coming next. The algorithm is using the last 2 bars to sort of "sense" if it is forming a peak or a trough. That is why there is no way to tell whether the last bar is the peak or the trough. I hope this short explanation will answer the questions, if it's not clear, let me know. Please note, I am not the original author of the divergence algorithm, I am just "merging" the Trix and the divergence indicator that was originally written by FX5. Hope this helps... Peter.

--- 帖子 #4782 ---
It would be indeed very useful to add this to the manual so not to have to post/copy/paste 1. You can first of all download the Excel file "FxCal" which is in the attachments (paper clip top right) of this thread. It will give you the exact prices at which to set your stoploss and TP according to % risk, entry price, balance and R/R ratio. 2. Never use more than a 2% risk, better 1% risk of your EQUITY. What does this mean? In the above example, $100 = $2 or $1 risk. With a $0,10 per pip (0,01 lots) that would be 20 pips or 10 pips. If your EQUITY (not your balance) increases, recalculate accordingly. 3. Use the stoploss indicator that comes with the THV3 system (300*ATR (20) depending on the timeframe, and trade on the timeframe that better matches your risk level. I guess that would be all.

--- 帖子 #4809 ---
You just CAN'T have both. Only in an EA can this be done through a "Sleep" command. But not in an indicator. The Alert will prevail upon the Playsound command (they can't play at the same time). You can check the Codebase at Metaquotes, I had asked about two years ago and it is impossible.

--- 帖子 #4812 ---
Thanks for the info, I didn't know both can't be done, it's by design then. So we should probably have the options: 1. EnableAlerts -&gt; true/false 2. SoundAlerts -&gt; true/false If No.1 is false then option 2 will be ignored. If No.1 is true then: - No.2 is true -&gt; only sound alert will be generated. - No.2 is false -&gt; only Display alerts will be generated. This way we still provide the options of giving the users the type of alerts the prefer. Peter.

--- 帖子 #4817 ---
Indeed. Not so much "by design" but because in an indicator, there's no way to make use of the "Sleep" delay (I don't know much about programming but might be because of the different ways indicators interpret the code compared to an EA). You can do this on an EA with a Sleep (x) command for example, where it will wait for "x" seconds after the Alert command (which is always prevalent) and then trigger the Playsound command. Thank you again for your eagerness in helping with all these details.

--- 帖子 #4856 ---
The signal given is an arrow that shows at the moment the divergence is spotted, and signaling if a reverse or classic divergence it is. In fact, there are several variations of the Fx5 indicator, with different names too: for CCI, Macd, OsMa, Stochs even. And though it might be used in another system, in fact it is one of the standalone indicators that you can find in the Metaquotes Codebase ( http://codebase.mql4.com/1040 ), and developed by Hazem who is one of the Metaquotes community members. So it's not, per se, "a system", nor either FX50 (which you can find here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=134759 ) I did a search inside the FX50 thread to see if they use the divergence and only in ONE post the word "divergence" is mentioned, in no way related to the above mentioned FX5 indicator. Maybe you're talking about another FX50 system but this is the one I know about here in FF... The arrow is in no way a buy or sell indication by itself (though thanks to pointing this out as maybe it isn't obvious enough), it only points at the candle where the Trix divergence has been calculated, which, added to the rest of the analysis alerts, will help in making the decision. Remember that we are still in pre-release, if I can call it like that, in the sense that as soon as the new system is under public testing, there will always be bugs to fix, ameliorations, or useless things depending on what the overall results will be giving throughout the testing and testimonials of the traders. So, to summarize: You get a divergence signal, you check the other parameters. If not met, there's no trade to take. If and WHEN ALL MET, trade is valid. You also can opt not to use the divergence indicator and spot and draw the lines by yourself, this is an optional addition designed to facilitate things for those of us who may have problems identifying the divergences (I am one who usually confuses the reverse bearish with a bullish one and have to go back any amount of times to watch the divergence chart... ) Finally, I hope you are not offended by my tenacious search for the utmost exactitude (I can be a true pain in the back office and especially when I get stubborn about something), my aim is that everyone has at his/her disposal the most truthful information possible so not to get into misunderstandings and useless confusions). Thank you!

--- 帖子 #4883 ---
Hi! For me it's more logical to start the day when Forex day "officially" starts at Sydney through NY close (5pm EST), in fact IMO it doesn't matter much as in the end, you won't have more than 24 hours in a daily candle... The pivot indicator is based on the High-Low and Close Price of the daily candle (calculated in respect of every different set of settings, based on 24 sequential hourly candles), which will show differently on each platform according to its own timezone. The "daily session" comprises the whole day (all the markets involved) and personally I don't think that a 2 hours difference can make much noise, unless there's a huge move at the end of the day (NY "close") and even then I don't think it would matter because it would be compensated by the hours not taken from the previous day... In fact, Cobra's settings start at GMT 00:00 (8 hours before the London session), maybe it's a more normalized time where more people calculate the pivots (we would have to know how many brokers start the day with GMT 00:00) mine starts with Sydney session 2 hours earlier, as it seems more logical to me being that most markets open on Sunday at Sydney open and close on Fridays at NY close. Cobra starts at Tokyo. Some other people may like to base the close/open of the daily candle on the NYSE close at 4pmEST. The more people uses the same setting, the more probabilities there will be for a pivot price to become predictable... it works like the fibs. As I see pivots more as a range level (or zone) than a particular exact price (and I prefer to take into account the psych levels anyway) it doesn't bother me much if my pivot is 5 pips up or 5 pips down (as anyway prices between brokers differ sometimes for as much as 10 or more pips, and in some there can be huge spikes that don't show on the others, etc... this in respect to HH and LL)... so... it's really relative, and real support/resistances which can be seen on the charts at the levels the price went and bounced back are for me more accurate. Same as for fibs, it is impossible to calculate prices to the pip because of all of the above, you can easily take a look at several sites who show the daily pivots and there will be differences among them too. The idea here has been to normalize the levels so everybody is seeing the same, but for this also (and even between two same broker's demo accounts you can have 1 to 5 pips differences sometimes!) everybody would have to be using the same MT4 demo platform (live accounts may have bigger differences depending on the account type and such... or the lag on the price feed, etc...). Hope it helps.

Is the following i found in the Internetspace right? &lt;&lt;&lt; I've heard of fibonacci pivots? how are those calculated? They differ from classical pivots. Fibo pivots are great. Here is the code from an indicator I use for Fibo Pivots. double R = yesterday_high - yesterday_low;//range double p = (yesterday_high + yesterday_low + yesterday_close)/3;// Standard Pivot double r3 = p + (R * 1.000); double r2 = p + (R * 0.618); double r1 = p + (R * 0.382); double s1 = p - (R * 0.382); double s2 = p - (R * 0.618); double s3 = p - (R * 1.000); So you can see that each res/sup level is worked out by the Pivot +/- the previous day's range multiplied by a Fibonacci number.&gt;&gt;&gt; Thanks for all the good postings.

--- 帖子 #4979 ---
It is probably an issue with everyone's broker's prices which might be different. The indicator is based on calculations, which if not met, won't show the lines... and remember that the divergences are being drawn from the same candle to the next same candle (in respect to time), so if the candle's high that corresponds to the indi's first change of color and the one that corresponds to the second indi's change of color are not of the appropriate price as per the formula to indicate such a divergence (you could be having a smaller high for example) it won't do it. On your chart, the candle line is not drawn properly (it's about two candles earlier than the indicator's line). The points have to be taken at the same moment in time.

--- 帖子 #5047 ---
Hey Cash...see you have a new signature. Congrats, you well deserve this. I'd like to share a thought of how I keep track of regular and hidden divergence. Keep in mind the Dow theory of drawing trendlines: Connect higher lows for an uptrend is correctly drawn. Connect lower highs for a downtrend is correctly drawn. Keep in mind that the trendlines always need to be drawn on the same side: If the trendline is drawn above the price it needs to be drawn above the oscillator. If the trendline is drawn below the price it needs to be drawn below the oscillator. If the trendline is drawn incorrectly on price and correctly on the oscillator, then it's regular divergence: Incorrectly connecting lower lows on price is regular bullish divergence. Incorrectly connecting higher highs on price is regular bearish divergence. If the price trendline is drawn incorrectly then it's regular divergence and price *should* move in the opposite direction of the price tendline. If the trendline is drawn correctly on price and incorrectly on the oscillator, then it's hidden divergence: Correctly connecting higher lows on price is hidden bullish divergence. Correctly connecting lower highs on price is hidden bearish divergence. If the price trendline is drawn correctly then it's hidden divergence and price *should* move in the same direction of the price trendline. It's a bit hard to get a grasp on at first...I hope this helps and makes sense to some. Given enough screen time it begins to make sense.

In 1M trix goes into O/B territory and turns to red, signalling reverse course, at this time I started looking at 5M chart for a confirmation. #2a. I see that the fast trix in 5M changes to red in O/B area. I prepare myself and start concentrating on 1M chart.I look at 1M chart every thing looks ok to me, or was it? I see that there was already a small run down in 1M, and the faster trix is close to O/S area. As with any run-up/run-down, I start to think it will retrace a bit before it continues the downward spiral. What if it does not go for retracement and next candle open even further down? I will lose my pips, no way. I want all the pips. Even if it retraces, its fine, any way it is going downward so the retracement will not be a big issue. I enter the short @1.28391 and next candle or so it starts it retracement, and goes up till 1.28568, I start to think, jeez, I should have waited for retracement and entered then I would have got more pips. After that it starts it downward travel and I put my stop loss at breakeven. #3. I see that it is getting closer to S1, now I start to think should I close the position or will it push through S1 and go further? I keep moving my SL up and down, finally I decide to put it back in break even and see what happens. After almost touching S1, it starts to go up, I think its another retracement. I look at 5M the faster trix is close to zero line. Now I'am in delimma, whether to close or not, I decide to let it go and continue watching 1M chart. #3a. Suddenly it goes up fast and takes out my SL at break even then start to come down. I start to think what a stupid was I, to leave the profit in table. #4. Next candle opens Red, I notice the faster trix in 1M is green and pointing up , trix in 5M is still Red, but close or almost in zero line. Now I panic and I'am mad at myself for losing the opportunity of making atleast 20 pips, I jump in take another short @ 1.28400, next candle in 1M is red, Ok, I am fine. #4a. The after placing the order, I notice that faster trix on 5M is starting to get green, I start to think it will continue downward in a while #5. The carnage begins, it runs up very fast before and I am still *thinking* what to do, finally by the time I close the position its all done but over. I cannot belive what happend to me, how could this happen to me? How can I lose from a position of making 20+ profit? I start blaming every body, market and myself. Well, that is how it started and ended. After a while, I come back to my senses and decide to disect the mistakes I made and post it here. Here is my analysis on what I should have done and I should not have. This is the post trade analysis. #1 &amp; #2:- I really do not see that I did anything wrong in #1 &amp; #2. I strongly believe I was looking for an opportunity there, which every trader should be doing. Looking for opportunity. #2a, I should have respected my thought process and signal from 1M trix, which clearly indicated there could be a possible retracement. I could have gotten a better entry point. I should also submit to the fact that I cannot get all the pips in the world, I will get there, it is a matter of time. #3. I should have closed the position when it got very close to S1, since 5M trix was close to zero line. If it continue to fall, I could have re-entered after S1. #3a. This is what I should have thought, "fine, I did not get profit out of it, but neither did I lose anything". #4. At this point of time, I was in total chaos, to be blunt, I was gambling, I want to take back all I could not make earlier. Very wrong thought process. #4a. Some sense kicks back in, if faster trix turns color in O/B, O/S area, it a very high possiblity of reversal(Remember, this is how I was looking for opportunity in #1) , I should have exited here at break even or minimal loss. #5. I have nobody else to blame other than myself, not market, not any body else. Thanks for reading such a length post. Wish you all more pips. Thanks again.

--- 帖子 #5168 ---
If you have changed timeframes and a contrarian signal happened in any other, the last label remains on the screen until it's again activated by another contrarian signal. This is why it is better to have several TFs open with the indicator in each (even if only the main one with the sound alerts).

I use their demo. Unfortunately I think all their servers are on the same timezone. However, in my personal opinion I think that even daily and H4 charts with a few hours difference because of the timezone, don't change the overall price pattern of a currency pair. Time is a convention, of course as we are using candlesticks some of the patterns will be showing here and not there... thus the hourly chart would in fact be the most accurate for those. But I have even compared 4 hour charts with Oanda 's 3 hour and the evolution is practically the same. Personally I prefer how candle patterns show on GMT+2. Here's something I found at Alpari's forum (posted by the Admin): Can't be switched.

--- 帖子 #5267 ---
Outside the fact that there are higher and lower levels of s/r that have to be tested, and retested backwards if broken, etc... I usually try to see what I have in front of me in the NOW. Price goes step by step and is being tested small level by small level, and if broken almost always goes to the next, etc... That's why I find the psych levels so useful. On a micro view, it's easily seen. If retested (maybe once, maybe later on many times more) and held, it can be believable up to a certain point. But thousands of decisions are being made every second by thousands of market participants, and what can give you the "believability" is the price action, its momentum, the bull/bear ratio you can feel at every candle's struggle. Using the visual simulator (only watching the price action) can give you many answers and you'll be able then to detect the possible changes almost as soon as they appear. Even sometimes before they appear, as there are momentum changes that are an early symptom. There will always be some unpredictability as well, so it's not a 100% thing. But at least a good 80% of the times you'll be able to see what comes next. It takes lots of screen time, but is worth the while. HA candles are really a great help for this.

--- 帖子 #5283 ---
In fact, there's no special indicator to change as THV uses the standard Ichimoku Kinko Hyo. However as it is a built-in indicator and is configured in the template, you will have to change the colors yourself, at your choice, and THEN save a new template so every time you reopen the chart it will show with the corrections you made. (Sorry, with all those color changes I've done to other indis, I didn't realize at first that.) Salut! P.S.: Right-click on the chart, Indicators List, select Ichimoku Kinko Hyo, Edit, Colors Tab. Just change Up Kumo and Down Kumo. Then, menu Charts, Template, Save Template as. P.P.S.: BTW: great indicator! Congrats.

--- 帖子 #5311 ---
Hello folks! Something I read caught my attention. It has always been said that you "can't buy time." But, in the Forex world, the opposite is actually true. When you break it down, pip movement is time in a sense. And a LOT of pip movement represents a LOT of time. If you have an account that is under-funded, you don't have much "time" if things go wrong. But, if you have a properly funded account (the more, the merrier) then you can ride out most bad situations. An under-funded account is your worst enemy!

--- 帖子 #5312 ---
Hey Sed34, I have been following your trade postings and noticed that you have not settled down into your own style of trading. In essence, you need to find your own style of trading and adapt systems/methods that you learn from others. You need to settle in on one that suits you the best and then work on it till you are good at it. Another thing I noticed is that you are switching TF for trading which is different from MTF analysis. Pardon me if my observation is wrong here. THV works on every TF BUT the dynamics, challenges, trade emotional and financials are all different. Stay with using THV on the TF that you are most comfortable with. Do not jump from one TF to another to trade. Instead using different TF for analysis. Like to share something here. For me, I went through what all of us went through - searching for the best indicators, systems, methods and finally came full circle. There is no holy grail in forex. I now trade H1 TF the way all of us came into this world - naked. My analysis is done on H4 and D1 for S/R or some like to call it demand and supply levels. As mentioned in my previous posts, I am using THV to squeeze more out of the market while waiting for my H1 S/R levels to do their magic. With THV, I do not look at the M1 TF as recommended for entry simply because it is too emotionally taxing for me - I just cannot handle the candles break dancing in front of me. I am a very visual person when it comes to intraday trading and thus combined THV on M5 TF with MMA (multiple MAs) on another chart for analysis. Some like to call it the Rainbow or Guppy. It gives me a visual of the market on M5 TF and tells me exactly where I am entering on THV entry signal. It gives me added confidence to trust THV on entry as is or be a little more agressive and enter before PA goes above Coral and Cloud. I am also new to THV but do recall Cobra saying to adapt THV to your own style. I have attached a chart here to show my visual style of trading the M5 TF. I am sharing the above not to say you need to undress and trade naked (just kidding) or use the rainbow. What I want to convey is that THV is a good and working system but you need to fit it into your style of trading not the other way around. Use THV for entry confirmation on top of your own analysis in your most comfortable TF. Just my 2 cents worth to help and encourage a fellow THV trader whom I see is working very hard at it by offering another perspective. Hope I am not adding to your information overload. Sorry for the long post. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #5362 ---
Checking on a lower timeframe to pinpoint a better entry price is recommended. However, you could also trade directly on a single TF according to the rules, but as price is always fluctuating, the lower TF will allow to pick it when it is at its ideal position in regard to the trend. On a higher TF (that could be ANY of the higher TFs, not only M5) when all rules are met there is some time for the trade to develop, which will be longer as we go up in time. So you first pick the timeframe on which you wish to be trading (as to scope of pips, timing of the trade, and stops) and then look on the smaller TFs to enter with more odds in your favour, especially as to the stops. You can use as much sequential lower TFs to check up but remember that the stops will have to be set as per the main TF (in this case, H1). For example, there was an entry on H1 on feb.02 at 13:00 (gmt+2), though under the Coral, just after a divergence signal. This could develop into a good trade as per H1 expectations, so you go to M30 and lower, and find out that Coral rule is met at M5 but price is descending. You'll have to wait until rules are met there at 15:00 at a better price, or go even lower at M1 where you'll have several better entry points previous to 15:00. If rules are met (including the position in respect to the Coral) on a higher TF, probabilities are higher for a trade continuation in the direction (less noise as we go up in the TFs), however, its success will also depend on the best possible entry available.

--- 帖子 #5565 ---
Under "Program Files" folder in your hard disk (assuming it is "C"), you will find another folder which is your MT4 folder (named as per your broker, example: FXDD MetraTrader4 or else). Inside that folder you have other several folders, among which: 1) "experts" - Inside "experts" there's another folder named "indicators", where the indicators should be copied. 2) "templates" (where the template has to be copied) 3) "sounds" (where the sounds have to be copied) It will be easier if you use Windows Explorer so you can see the whole folder tree of your computer, locate where you have the unzipped files, then copy to the respective folders as explained.

hey sparkz, that's just the analysis template cobra posted in first page, it's not actually a system by itself, it's just where you can draw your trendlines, channels, add fibs, psych levels and other stuff you may find interesting. What I'm doing now (with great sucess) is to scalp 1M and always aware of where PA is in relation to this LWMA 60 on 5M chart. I never trade if PA is directly above or below it. It's working very well for me. I don't trade 1M if trix in 5M is doesn't agree, and watch 15M or 30M for longer trend. trade your THV by the rules, any TF you like, but be aware of how PA behaves around that MA. For extreme scalpers that may be a good exit point, and even better when we have confluence of other things like psyche levels (1.3000) or fibs, or a pinbar, for example. hope I sound clear on this

Trading Parameters: - My goal with this test was to take 10 trades on one pair in one night. - Follow level rules one to the letter. As best as I could understand them that is. - Trade on M1 THV Rules Level 1 : Entry Long = Above Coral + Above Cloud + Both Trix Cross &amp; Same Color Sell = Below Coral + Below Cloud + Both Trix Cross &amp; Same Color Exit Fast Trix turns color Profit Target (ATR / 2 = TP) Stops = ATR My results were 8 winners and 2 losers. See thv-trades.png attachment - I believe I could have mitigated the losers and explanations are below. I am also hoping that I can get feedback from the experienced folks on what I could have done better. The actual trades part 1 - 6:30-8:30pm PST. See thv-trades-1.png attachment: The actual trades part 2 - 8:30-10:30pm PST. See thv-trades-1.png attachment: My observations... this is where I have specific questions: I entered my big loss right at the coral. Price had not firmly past it so it was very shallow. Due to large lots, I could not maintain the optimal stop loss according to ATR for my big loss. Minus 11 pips = -$110. Risk management rules broken there, max SL should have been $60 at 1.0 lots that’s only 6 pips. Not enough breathing room for error. Following all the rules, I minimized my risk by entering the market correctly and extracting pips. Need to add a 5 pts trailing stop to all orders, set the TP to 10 pips, most good entries had that much room if you act quickly and correctly. The +1 pip trade closed early as the SL was too shallow to withstand a small retrace. It then went on to push 18 pips down. If my SL was greater than 13 pips, I would have had more profit on this trade. The -$58 loss was due to not pulling the trigger fast enough. There would have been enough pips to cover 8-10 pips in this scalp. Here's were my observations and changes I'm going to make to adjust my trading tonite: Act quickly on the crosses. (adjusted Trix fast line to dotted so I can see both line better) Set stops to ATR = ~15 pips (2% risk or 0.04 lots on $3k equity) False signal = trix cross where price is close to crossing the coral but hasn’t yet Removing the coral thick line off the M1 chart and just react on crosses. Hi Basber: Actually, when we changed from the hull to the coral it was pretty much decided then that the color of the coral was not relevant...maybe in very high TFs (ask doblece or Cobra about that). The rule of the coral when trading in conservative mode is that we only short when PA is below the coral and go long when PA is above the coral.... In the charts you will see that in both the 5 min and the 1 min, PA was beneath the coral and the cloud... Also, trix in the 5 min had establised a lower low and was all red. In the 15 min, PA was below the cloud and PA was trading below the coral. Also, PA had been rejected at 61.8 and had broken through the 38.2 AND the trix had crossed. I was expecting it to atleast hit the T/L and the 23.6... Either is was a correct analysis OR it was pure luck!! LOL In short, the color of coral is not a consideration. The Level of PA in relation to the coral is a consideration for conservative trading. Anyone else want to chime in?

--- 帖子 #5681 ---
Any subsequent entry beyond the first one becomes progressively more risky. The movement based on the M5 will always have a limit and the further away you get from the beginning of that move the more likely it will end. That said, there are scalpers here who trade those M1 entries regardless of the amount the M5 has already moved. A more experiences trader can enter during those pauses or minor retraces. I try to look for and only take the best entries.

--- 帖子 #5699 ---
Welcome to the thread. This is normal for a new or even a fairly new trader. When you are not sure, don't trade. It takes a long time to get used to PA and feel comfortable with its behavior. There is no real need to be in a rush to "get it". Only take the perfect looking trades. Later, you may be able to recognize good potential in not so good looking setups. In the meantime, keep trading on the simulator and demo so you can familiarize yourself with patterns.

--- 帖子 #5724 ---
Ahhh, someone who understands. This is one of the hardest things to get across to a NuB. Trading is serious business and requires that the focus be on trading and trading only. Put the rest of the world on hold for the duration of your trading period, can be several small periods or just one large one but trading needs your full attention. Any distraction can be the cause of the resulting domino effect that will follow, just get one thing out of sync and the rest just seems to come tumbling down around you. The only real (and relative) safety in trading is attained by tight money management rules. This said, an early entry with just the Trix is part of the aggressive rules, if taken in the direction of the trend, the distance to stoplosses will be safer, however, the counterpart is that you can get plenty of whipsaws if you don't check the status of the market in higher timeframes before entering. If you are scalping for a pair of pips, it's a much better entry, but you have to be with the finger on the trigger to exit as soon as possible.

--- 帖子 #5778 ---
Hi Jerome, The 'worms' only show up when the value YOU set is hit. There are no lines. If the value is not hit, you should see nothing. To change the settings Edit THV Color RSI from the Indicator list and change the values of variables overBought and overSold. Experiment with your own values and remember it is not perfect. I like it because I can set my own values and when it shows up I know exactly how overbought/sold the situation is. Trix only shows a general overbought/sold area. The little multi indicator gives a look at other time frames. If you work on a laptop or a single screen machine, this lets you 'see' what is happening without having to change TF so often. For instance if you are using M15 to follow a trade, the indicator will show you what's happening on M1 without having to switch. File is attached. Hope this helps. p.s. Best to try and use as few indicators as possible. The more you use the more confusing things become and the less decisive your trading (usually) becomes. Have fun

--- 帖子 #5827 ---
Good question... You learn something new everyday. " While not yet anywhere near as popular as the headline stock indexes, the CRB Commodities Index is the most widely followed index today that acts as a proxy for this general commodities bull. If a trader is in a hurry and doesn’t have time to check gold, and silver, and platinum, and copper, and nickel, and oil, and natural gas, and whatever else, then he can take a quick look at the CRB to see if commodities are generally strong or weak." ' There are several critically important attributes of the CRB that are well known to veteran commodities investors that newcomers to this realm really ought to be aware of. The CRB index, now in its 10th major revision since it was launched in 1957, is comprised of 19 key commodities. These commodities are not equally weighted, either individually or by sector, and are arithmetically averaged and rebalanced monthly. The CRB’s 4 energy components, which are crude oil, heating oil, unleaded gasoline, and natural gas, make up the largest proportion of this index by far at 39%. Crude oil alone accounts for 23%! This large energy weighting is a double-edged sword. Since the energy sector is so strong it is great for the CRB’s performance, but if you are looking for equal exposure across commodities the CRB no longer does this. You probably don’t want equal exposure though. I sure don’t. The greatest gains in this commodities bull by far have been in the very capital-intensive hard-to-produce commodities, like metals and energy. Metals account for 20% of the CRB’s weight and once again energy is 39%. The remaining 41% is soft commodities like wheat, coffee, sugar, and livestock. The supply/demand profiles of these soft commodities are generally suboptimal."

--- 帖子 #5847 ---
It will depend on the highs and lows of both. Post 5777 it's a reverse bearish divergence, with HH in Trix and LH in price. Post 5781 it's a bullish divergence, HL in Trix and LL in price. Lower Highs = bearish If Price makes Lower Highs, it's a reverse bearish divergence If indicator makes Lower Highs, it's a classical bearish divergence Higher Lows = bullish If Price makes higher lows, it's a reverse bullish divergence If indicator makes higher lows, it's a classical bullish divergence In all 4 cases, of course, indicator and Price must be heading in contrarian direction from one another. Levels must be taken on the same candle for both.

I for one don't post losing trades for a very simple reason. Not that I am afraid of losing face or anything like that. But instead most losses come in when I try to be aggressive and preempt the THV indicators to get a better entry price. Now if the trade does not turn out well, I have a very tight SL of 5 to 10 in these cases to prevent disastrous loses. I do have a couple of these trades but if I post these losing trades, it will be so obvious after the fact from the charts that it does not really add value to anyone viewing them. Clearly in violation after the fact. And of course all of us will have these - bource or pullback trades that we know break the THV rules but are taken from our S/R analysis on higher TF. These should not be posted as they merely use THV as additional comfirmation tool and THV rules may not be strictly followed. I will try to post trades that are loses where THV rules are strictly followed. But these are hard to come by as THV coupled with S/R and TL analysis raises the probability of a good trade to a very very high level. Cheers, CaveMan

Caveman, you are confirming what I am seeing. My biggest flaw is taking trades when THV hasn't quite confirmed them. I am "jumping the gun" or anticipating THV is going to give me the permission to enter but sometimes does not. Patience is key to resolving that. Beyond those borders, probably the hardest time to NOT use THV is in a tightly ranging market, when you get a signal to trade THV but it goes nowhere. Usually a TL stops you from trading but not always. Identifying this kind of market takes some experience, but time of day usually gives you the clue. Trading only the London session is a great filter for that. Just some Saturday thoughts...

The volume of retail trading, according to Wikipedia, was around 2%+ for 2006 of the total volume traded in Forex. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_exchange_market Let's say that it could have grown 10 times in the last 3 years, that would still be only a 20% of the total volume... which I don't think would influence much, and neither would that 20% be trading the same system. The systems decrease their effectiveness if they are not adjusted to the changes in the market behaviour throughout the months or years, for example, volatility in EUR/USD was much lower a few years ago, thus a system based on this would become obsolete and of course wouldn't be yielding the same results over time.

--- 帖子 #5993 ---
Yes I do. My day starts an hour before Tokyo opens for preparation and leads right into the one hour overlap of London session. Then take a break to visit my daughter at my in-laws place and have dinner. After that, a short drive home and back to trade the London/US overlap sessions for another 3 hours. Asian sessions are forgiving. Movement is slow and it gives you lots of reaction time as compared to London and US sessions. What you noticed may be the last hour of Japan/London overlap. For the overlap, London session being large and mighty has its own mind about trend and does not usually take the lead from the Asian session. You will also see movements right around and after Japan lunch hours. Movements during these timing are erratic and caution should be taken.

--- 帖子 #6028 ---
Thanks Aries. The bars are based om MACD 2 - 4 - 9, the yellow bars show indecision or flat market. The red and green lines in the Trix are oversold or overbought levels. Each TF has different levels hard coded and if the Trix lines are deep over or under those lines you can expect a reversal soon.

Hi; Many Experience Traders Adhere To This Believe That You Should Risk 2 - 3% Of Your Account (Maximum) . Even 3% Of Your Account Is 6$ , So If You Want To Trade Eur/Usd Pair, Your Stop Loss Should Be Around 6 Pips , And It's Not An Appropriate SL. I Think You Should Trade Mini Accounts. And Also I Believe "Yes , It's Too Much." Regards, P.S. Here Is An Example From "BabpyPips" Site : Here is a little illustration that will show you the difference between risking a small percentage of your capital compared to risking a higher percentage. You can see that there is a big difference between risking 2% of your account compared to risking 10% of your account on a single trade. If you happened to go through a losing streak and lost only 19 trades in a row, you would’ve went from starting with $20,000 to having only $3,002 left if you risked 10% on each trade. You would’ve lost over 85% of your account! If you risked only 2% you would’ve still had $13,903 which is only a 30% loss of your total account. Of course, the last thing we want to do is lose 19 trades in a row, but even if you only lost 5 trades in a row, look at the difference between risking 2% and 10%. If you risked 2% you would still have $18,447. If you risked 10% you would only have $13,122. That’s less than what you would’ve had even if you lost all 19 trades and risked only 2% of your account!

Hi Basber, I would agree with you that THV is not as reliable in range-bound markets. That is pretty much true for any system. To improve profit potential, a lot of our THV traders use trendlines on the M5 timeframe, or a support and resistance indicator. When price breaks above or below, they act. Just don't expect as big a payoff as you might otherwise expect. Suggestion - complement your THV set-up with a normal M15 or M30 chart so that you can "step back" and more clearly see the range within which price is moving. Then, you can just about trade one way to a limit and the opposite on the way back to the other end. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #6109 ---
The goal is to take only the A+ trades, most new traders think they need to be always in the market and have the idea that if they don’t have an open position they are not trading but not trading if not sure is trading as well. Here a small tip how to trigger more potential trades: On your candlestick chart (we always should have one open like the THV Analyze chart) set Bollinger bands (20 - 2) and watch out of touch or break of the outer BB’s. In case that you see strong candle reverse signs like pin bar, engulfing pattern, inside bars or dojis (the last one can be a continuation as well, it’s only valid at a very bottom on a trend and needs confirmation of the next candle) after that touch or break look for a reverse sign in 5M and take the trade on THV rules in 1M (or 15M and take it on 5M). Notice as well the RSI, if it is very closed to overbought or sold areas the trade can be valid also S&amp;R, Fibs and TL's are very relevant for the decision. These trades mostly give you some additional pips.

--- 帖子 #6111 ---
Just an additional thought about this. When a pair is strongly trending, it will usually remain at the upper band (more exactly between bands (20 - 1,5) and out of bands (20-2) - in fact for EURUSD the channel that forms is mostly between 1,5 and 2,5 deviations) and will sometimes make a pullback to the median line just to bounce and push back in the original direction. This is why, when spotting a possible reversal from those boundaries, an effective cross back of the 1,5 deviation (a full candle opened and closed outside in the direction of the middle line) can be a good additional confirmation. In any case, if the price broke through but came back towards the ascending or descending channel, it is better to wait a little until all conditions are met.

--- 帖子 #6179 ---
Like to share my 2 cents worth on the way I trade with the coral. At times when I do not follow the coral, I still use her as a guide for my trades. One very important point is that I always respect the Ichi Cloud and use as entry signal. Higher Risk (counter trend of TF taking trade with) If taking a position to move towards the Coral with Trix signal and respecting Ichi cloud, meaning expecting for PA to close in on the coral, I take extra caution and lower target pips and tighter SL. Only trade this way if there is sufficient pips between price and Coral. Lower Risk If taking a position to move away from the coral with Trix signal and respecting Ichi cloud, meaning expecting PA to move away from coral, I am more liberal with profit target and SL. To mitigate risk, always trade in the direction of the next higher TF. Eg. If trade taken in M5, follow trend of M15 or higher. It is different from following Trix colors in higher TF because Trix colors also indicate retracements or bounce. Just my 2 cents worth. Hope it helps.

--- 帖子 #6245 ---
General observation for all: I have been looking at and using the Divergence Indicator extensively since I found this thread. This is a powerful tool if used properly and carefully because trading Divergence is in itself very powerful (if you're not familiar with this phenomenon, read about it at BabyPips). At present I have a MT4 platform running with 56 charts open; all of them ONLY have the Divergence Indicator applied with the alert function turned on. When the alarm sounds, I check the chart. The smaller the timeframe, the smaller the potential for a profit. But each signal possesses the potential for at least a small profit. If you use ATR for the selected timeframe, you have a potential profit target. Currently the ATR on the EUR/USD 5M chart is 10 pips. The signal you referred to personalme had the potential to yield 22 pips less spread. 10 pips on this signal would have been a respectable 'scalp-trade'. Larger timeframes will yield greater profits and the stop losses needed to trade this signal are usually very small. If interested, I suggest spending some time looking back at previous signals to appreciate the potential of Divergence Trading. I'll post more on this as time passes.

--- 帖子 #6276 ---
Kerty, What I typically see, and everyone please correct this, is during the 15M set up you will see the 5M go thru a few cycles of entries. That is if the trend holds. --- 帖子 #6291 ---
Here is a 5M chart that includes std BB (dotted brown) and non-std BB (solid blue) which can be used to spot price breakouts (=momentum). The std BB is period 20, deviation 2 (though I sometimes tweek to 1.9). The non-std BB is period 10, deviation 1.5. The best trades are when BOTH BBs pinch at the same time, not just one or the other. A good entry price is around the level of the pinch line of the inner BB, upper or lower depending on direction of breakout. A note of caution is that Head Fakes cannot be identified as such at this quick entry level, and sometimes the first run out of a pinch is in the OPPOSITE direction of the final, and maybe substantial run. A note of encouragement is that if a good run is afoot, many times there will be a pop out of the pinch, but later the price returns to the pinch span area....this is what many traders wait for, thus reducing exposure to Head Fakes and still getting a second chance to board.... The attached charts show this action...the first pop to the 162% level, then the pullback, then the resumption of the move. The MT4 Fibonacci Extension tool can be used to get exit targets. Apply the extension across the gap of the pinch of the inner BB. The resultant levels become targets. There is no guarantee how far a run will progress, but the Fibonacci Extension levels are prime areas outwards from the pinch where the PA (price action) may halt. Some traders take a bit off the trade at each level the PA attains, and up their SL (stop loss) on the remainder. Dual pinching of these BB can foster runs that go for many hours and that include consolidations and pullbacks, sometimes substantial ones, before the PA recovers and goes on to attain another level. An initial setup on a small TF (timeframe) chart may foster a good run that results in new setups on larger TF charts as the run progresses. And sometimes the better pinch span to be applying the extension to is that of the outer BB. So, it is good to experiment with this. A good pinch on the inner band will invariably achieve the 162% level, while one on the outer band nearly always acheives the 100% level. Nothing is guaranteed, however. Traders that do not want to be in a trade long, tend to look for the first pop to the 162% area and exit, regardless of what happens next...but that is Head Fake territory, too. Here is the start of a sequence of posts that followed a real good example on the EurJpy yesterday: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...postcount=1864 And the attached sequence of charts shows what can happen, too....happening while I was preparing this post!

--- 帖子 #6303 ---
Use the Bands provided in the Custom Indicators, not the one in the Indicators list. The Custom Indicator Bands window has tabs. The Inputs tab allows you to customize the Period and the Deviations. My outer band is used just as this is already set. For my inner band I change the Period to 10 and the Deviation to 1.5. The Colors tab is where you remove the center line, which is a simple moving average line of the Period selected in the Inputs tab (Period of 20 = a 20sma line for the center line). To remove this line, which is line #0 in the list, click on the color box as necessary to bring up the color palette....there you re-select the color "None" which is the box across the top of the palette. This will keep the center sma bias line from being displayed. Items #1 and #2 are the upper and lower BB lines which here you can re-select other colors for, too.

traderathome, nice post. indeed, using BBs (bollinger bands) is a fine way of detecting/predicting volatility/breakouts, or lack thereof.. by the way, John Bollinger, who invented Bollinger bands, call it the "squeeze" where did u learn about applying Fib. expansion on the inner BB's pinch, is there a thread on it? Or did u just thought of it yourself? i use Standard deviation (a standard/default indicator in MT4; alternatively, custom indicator "BBandwidth ratio" is similar; search for it in FF if needed) to detect the "volatilty run", that is, how far price will go after the breakout/pinch/squeeze. (Standard deviation is flat when price is in a range/low volatility period, expands/rises as volatility rises, peaks when volatility decreases, &amp; turns down when volatility dries up; settings used can be similar to settings in BB: example, BB 20,2, use 20 also in Stand.dev.). You could say this (using Standard deviation) is the "blind way" of exiting/taking profits, while the method in your post (using Fib. expansions) shows the "seer's/forecaster's way" (how about that, SeerEye? )

--- 帖子 #6340 ---
On the attached 5M chart you can see both the Coral line (G/R/Y) and the T3 line (Aqua). If you have ever wondered if these lines relate to the more common place, then this chart should give you increased confidence in them. Beside both the lines you can see a second line (black). In the case of the Coral line, the second black line is nothing more than the 89 MA line, which is in the Linear Weighted mode as opposed to the Simple or Exponential mode. Beside the T3 line (which I call the "THV3 Trigger") the second black line is nothing more than a 10 MA which is also displayed in the Linear Weighted mode. There you go. The THV3 Coral and T3 lines definately relate to the more basic, but through additional data processing they are nicely smoothed for us.

dorellino, if i may, the middle "0" is the "real zero", "where it should cross" as u said. the upper &amp; lower "0" lines are the overbought (red) &amp; oversold (green) areas, wherein when hit, price is "expected" to retrace/reverse.

--- 帖子 #6356 ---
It is actually not all that different from the stochastic. It is also an oscillator and has a fast and slow line. Fast line very high is overbought, fast line low is oversold. The white dashed line is zero, the red one indicates overbought and the green one indicates oversold. The difference is it works so much better than the stochastic, which is the main oscillator I used to use. Here is more info: http://www.investopedia.com/articles.../02/092402.asp

--- 帖子 #6367 ---
Acting on the feeling that a setup is HAPPENING and entry urgently needs to be made is most often followed by PAIN!!!!! I am teaching myself to calm down and be patient, so as to not fall victim to HEAD FAKES, by telling myself that if the setup is for a REALLY GOOD MOVEMENT, then there will be a pop, a pullback (for another entry opportunity), and then the real move will begin. I have seen this happen over and over. And I am convinced the reason for it is that the BIG GUNS often do not all enter together creating that first pop......many hold back and wait for the pullback. I believe THEY make that pullback happen for the sole purpose of being able to spread out their buildup of positions over multiple pullback opportunities so as to not wildly drive the price against themselves....which is what would happen if they all jumped at the same time. So relax, and PRACTICE allowing the setup to run a bit and see if it provides a pullback for your entry. It may not always happen, but in that case console yourself with the truth that it is better to miss a good trade now and then, rather than constantly be in bad trades!

I remember... in this case price rose, and I was looking for a Resistance Fib where any retracement downwards will be hitting Support levels, so I started at lower left corner, and followed the price to the high, then drug it back down to the 2720 level. There's pros and cons either way. Going to the high, you have price hitting the 50% right now at current levels... that' sounds good, but... You see, I had ALREADY drawn the fib to the xx20 level on the way up, so when price continued on but STOPPED at the 127% level, I was already there, not waiting for a high to develop to draw a fib from in the first place... think of it as a "preemptive fib." The additional plus for me is the fib i drew gives a yet to be reached 50% retrace at the 2650 level almost to the pip. That is also a powerful psych level and "I like it". That satisfies several criteria that frees my mind to look at the "next" thing w/o nagging things that i feel need to happen before price is released to move on into the next phase.. whether it be a continuation move up, or a further retrace down from that critical 50% level, wherever you choose to put it. PS. While posting this, Price has just gotten to with 3 pips of my 50% level. Using the actual high for a fib anchor tho, you would now have a retrace to the 38% level which might be pointing you in a bearish continuation direction, premature still imo... Hope this helps... Think of it like learning to play music. Show me a musical score and I have no idea what all those squiggles mean - show a trained musician and he/she can hear that piece playing just by looking at the incomprehensible squiggles. So I am afraid the only way to learn is practice and lots of it. I once calculated that you need at least 500 hours of screen time before you START to 'see' what is (probably) going to happen. Some traders here have 10's of thousands of screen hours behind them, so there is no quick fix. Tip would be start without any indicators, press F11 and get rid of all the clutter, especially the Terminal, then just watch how the price builds, how fast it builds, how the candles form, their shapes and as traderathome says especially how after every big move there is a retracement. Relate the movements to the time of day, trend, physc lines and read the news about the currency pair. Then gradually add the indicators into the mix and fully understand what they do and what they are telling you before you use them. Lastly really study MM as the MOST IMPORTANT aspect of trading is strict Money Management. When I first started screen trading I wrote a simple EA. All it did was look at the candles, if the candle result was positive it bought the next candle, if that was positive it bought again etc. I knew the trend so set it for only longs when the trend was up and vice versa. It actually makes a profit .. so long as there is a reasonably strong trend. It can be done, so be patient and good luck.
