--- 帖子 #6393 ---
Price DOES go in any direction, even if trending nicely. It has its own squiggly way to move from one point to another, and as soon that point has been reached, it comes back again zigzagging to a lower point than the start if it's trending down, or a higher low if it intends to keep on rising. Or the inverse sometimes. If you watch shorter timeframes, you can see that there's a decision being made almost every 10-15 pips, do we go up, let's try lower again, etc. Support and resistances are being broken, then tested, and retested, and maybe re-broken in inverse direction, ad infinitum. And it most often tends to come back to a middle level. What timeframe do you usually trade from? The mistake we most usually make is to trade from a particular setup in a given timeframe, and then try to apply or react to price patterns that pertain to a smaller or higher TF. This gets us totally confused after a while. First of all, you have to be confident with your own money and risk management, thus accepting that you might be wrong after all, and that it's ok because it is part of the game; this way you'll be able to pull the trigger without worrying too much about the outcome. If you are trading live and are freezing, go back to a demo account, or try to practice on week-ends with the simulator. Appropriate timing is a habit that has to be developed. We tend to analyze too much and react much later, usually after the fact. Time is paramount especially in small timeframes. Then you should see what the trend is up to, under several points of view, and at that particular moment (the market can change trends a lot, especially in shorter timeframes). Know the average swing expectation on each TF, so you can gauge easily if it's most likely to come back or will continue for a while in that direction. Know also which is the average time that particular swing uses to last. DRAW TRENDLINES on each. BOTH ways (there is always an underlying opposite trend going on). Chose at least two, better 3 IMO, correlated TFs to watch simultaneously. Have enough patience to wait for the exact moment to make the entry, that you will have defined in advance according to your own system and expectations, and enough swiftness to act immediately when the moment has come.

--- 帖子 #6423 ---
What timeframe are you trading off? Trade expectance in pips is equivalent (roughly) to 1,5*ATR(20) of the given timeframe (that would be half the value of the THV3_ATR_Pips indicator, to give you an idea). If you are trading off M5/M1, you can gauge the potential of continuation based on the higher timeframe, and let the trade "breathe" through coming and going inside its range (as an example, price usually goes forth 10 pips, comes back 8, then goes again 7, then 5, and back 6, forward 9, and so on...). If you are scalping, you should take what the market gives you, you can't expect much more than 10-15 pips (and maybe less depending on the volatility) in such a small timeframe. However, your management of stops (trailing, or using a stop at BreakEven when appropriate) can allow you to go further should the trade evolve into a greater range. If you are trading off a higher timeframe, you can expect much longer runs, however, you'll also have to stand through small pullbacks, price going back and forth, because that's the way it moves, three steps forward and two steps back, it takes some patience and to be able to gauge the scope or potential of a trade using multiple timeframes, supports and resistances, trendlines, being aware of the time of the day (for example this morning where there was a lot of Euro news) and in general observing Price Action closely to understand its behaviour. If you can post charts of the entries that you mention, it would be great to help you analyze them in detail. Finally, whenever you start feeling emotional about your trading, it is better to step back and remain on the sidelines, relax and observe the market, or do whatever else can bring you peace of mind, and come back refreshed. You will have a better focus afterwards.

--- 帖子 #6439 ---
Others I believe are using the 1 Hour chart; here's what I do. I want the 1H to establish the trend. First I watch for the fast Trix line to change color; this is an early alert that the short term trend is about to change. Next a cross of the 2 Trix lines. At this point I drop down to the 5M and wait for an appropriate signal in the same direction as the 1H trend. A Divergence signal on the 1H or higher also deserves attention. One thing I have added to the chart is a non-log MA set to 13; on the 1H chart this is an easy way to see the trend in this time frame. Often times there will be a number of "price cycles" on the 5M that are a small part of the larger trend on the 1H. When the 1H fast Trix line changes color, it's time to wait for a new set-up on this chart. Earlier today I did this on the AUD/USD (I'm still 'working' this pair because the 1H trend is still Bullish). HTH!

"Dual Pinches" means both BBs are pinching around the same time. The more defined the pinches and the more simultaneous, the better the results usually. I added a "-0.50" level to the built-in Fibonacci Extension tool. For a move up I first click on the lower pinch and hold and release on the upper pinch. Now it will display the -50% at the lower and the +50% at the upper, which is simply a matter of my preference as to how I want it displayed on the chart.

I can only tell you how to do this using the MT4 platform. There are two ways to access the Fib. Extension tool. One way is to click on Insert/Fibonacci/Expansion.....Insert is in the upper left of the MT4 window. The other way is two click directly on the Fib. Ext. tool in the tablet of tools somewhere above the chart. If the Ext. tool is not among those tool icons, then you can add it. Do this by right clicking on the verticle hash marks column, just left of the tool icons, to bring up a drop down menu. Select Customize which will allow you to add/delete tool icons from those shown above the chart.

--- 帖子 #6533 ---
T, can you coment on plotting points and how and why it ben redrawn - retracement or extention - if it still Fibo ratios - T, if it not big pain in S - couldyou explain it with using good-old-familiar-to-all Fibo Retracement, not Extension, please?

--- 帖子 #6534 ---
First off, using BBs is to better see the squeezing down of the range...something that protends a breakout is coming. When the breakout comes, the purpose of the Fib. Ext. is to gauge where the breakout move may likely stop. As we are not interested in measuring any retracement move, but rather in measuring the likely extent of a breakout move, we use the Fib. Extension tool. This tool applied to the squeeze point in the range will forcast likely limits to any move breaking out of that range. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #6535 ---
The concept can be illustrated as follows: Wait for the price to range. Measure the height of the range. Apply the Fibonacci Extension tool to that range span to get possible failure levels of any range breakout run. Now, measuring the range height is sometimes not easy when candle wicks are at all different heights. This is where the Bollinger Band comes into play. A well defined pinch in the BB preceeding a breakout can be used as the span across which you apply the Fib. Ext. tool. Two charts below illustrate this. The first chart shows an attempt to draw the range bottom and top lines and apply the Fib. Ext. tool. The second chart uses the BBs. Either process is valid, but the first method is subjective and can yield different results from using BBs. As you can see from the charts, the attempt to define the range may have yielded better results. And note that there was no real well defined Dual BB Pinch during the range, so the next best thing to do was to apply the Fib. Ext. to the span of the inner BB just at the breakout point. As you can see, this attempt at producing exacting predictive Fib. Ext. levels is fraught with complications when the PA is so volitile as to not give us the nice lines we look for. But exacting or not, the concept is valid and can help you capture pips.

--- 帖子 #6536 ---
Now, I have just realized something that makes me feel like an idiot. While scrambling to set up MT4 on my wife's computer (mine is down), I forgot one very important feature of the Fibonacci Extension....something that I had compensated for on my own computer but have not yet done so on my wife's. So, for the past several days I have been using the Fib. Ext. tool erroneously. In a nutshell, after drawing the Fib. Ext., you must move the PIVOT line up (let us assume the Fib. Ext. is drawn upwards) to the upper pinch point. THEN the extension lines are correct. Look at the results doing this correctly now, using the previous charts...... To move the PIVOT line (or zero line) you double click on the span line to get the dots to appear. Then you left click, hold, and drag the dot for the Pivot/zero line up to the level of the dot for the top of the span measurement line.

--- 帖子 #6581 ---
Remember that price moves in cycles inside cycles. From the higher timeframe (which bears stronger probabilities and a longer run) to the lower where changes occur fast and last very little. You can gauge the "meaning" or average potential of a particular divergence depending on each timeframe, thus being able to decide your way and the risk it involves. For example, on EUR/USD: Daily: we've got a bullish divergence that is just barely starting (thus hasn't developed its full potential yet). H4 reverse bearish divergence already performed and was of short duration, and is now showing a strong uptrend. H1 is turning down but is still in an uptrend. M30 shows some indecision, we have two opposing divergences very near one from the other, which would give the idea of a momentarily sideways market. M15 is already well advanced in its bearish divergence development. M5 showed a reverse bullish divergence which was weak as the bear movement took over. M1 is flat just now. It will all depend on which is the main timeframe that you want to trade upon. But the overall trend looks clearly defined, at the moment.

Hi All: About more than an hour ago, THV signaled out both POTENTIAL positive divergences and a hidden negative divergence; such situation may create dilemma to some traders as to whether to take the long or short trade based on these divergences of opposite 'opinion'. One way of discerning which divergence was at play is simply detecting the lower highs and lower lows; which obviously is favoring the hidden negative divergence signal and a short trade is favored. Another way is to look at this pattern; i call this the 'shakeouts' pattern; pivotal 3 &amp; 4 MUST violate pivotal 1 &amp; 2 respectively to create the longs and shorts shakeouts. The trigger is to short on break of the trend line between pivotal 3 &amp; 4. Same setup applies to a long scenario. Probability of success for this pattern is very high. Take care. --- 帖子 #6618 ---
Divergence is a very powerful indicator when properly used; and the THV indicator is excellent. I have an MT4 terminal running that is devoted to Divergence Signals. 3 charts on 20 pairs; 60 charts total. Daily, 4H and 1H with alert enabled. When an alert sounds, I take a look at that pair and include the divergence signal in my trading plan. On smaller time frames the signal may or not be of significance; take a look at higher time frames before deciding how valid the signal really is. And if you decide to 'look back' at older signals, remember the arrow does NOT show on the chart until after the candle following the signal has closed. That means you could potentially enter a trade on the third candle; that may be too late on small time frames; another good reason to watch the bigger charts for this signal.

Hi Typhoonking: My personal take is that, disregard of what type of trading styles; you will always be in the 'handicap' situation if you just stick with one time frame. I don't think THV presents any problem for the said issue. The most important thing is that the 'long-term' intraday time frame will always give you the overall posture of what the market is attempting to resolve. Though I have never use the simulator; but what I would like to suggest is that you should do the simulations separately in the 1-min, 5-min, 15-min time frame so that you will be able to have a good and solid market feelings of the said time frames. When it comes the time to go real-time, you will not be surprised by the gyrations and reactions of THV towards the said time frames. Hope this helps...Just my two cents. Have a good one Jeff

Typhoon, IMHO though you can't use a multiple timeframe on the simulator. It is still important to keep on the simulator trading. It help you to understand how price works and its behaviour. So keep on practise About THV, yes it is better to use multiple TF. I always pay attention on the 15M and 5M TF. If 15 &amp; 5 tell long, then I look only long trade. The entry is based on 1M TF. With this way, you can minimize your SL and maximize your TP (means safer trading). And last, don't forget to learn divergence. It is one of powerfull tools to pick pips .

--- 帖子 #6673 ---
Hi Typhoonking: The positive divergence is a valid divergence play. I would ignore the coral for trade entries; it helps to give you an over all directional trend bias but it's not meant for pulling the trigger. I would have entered long 5 candles later from your depicted line as it was closed above the cloud. Although, it still hasn't traded above my white trend line; all the same, I would've entered already as I'm aggressive in divergence play. The second negative divergence wasn't a valid one as price actions have been clearly demonstrating higher highs and higher lows. Case in point, the coral has already turned dark green; which is in line with our decision of taking the positive divergence play to go for long side AND refrain us from taking that negative divergence signal. Finally, during turning point of the market; the Coral will be slow in reflecting the CITs; thereby, giving you the wrong impression that, in this case, the down trend was still in force. The most reliable way of detecting trend changes is to read the market structures and price actions. Coral gives you the overall directional bias of the market and keeps you from being on the wrong side of it. Hope this helps. Have a good one Jeff

--- 帖子 #6726 ---
Kareem, you should definitely be on Build 220 but that may not be your problem with Ichimoku colors. Regarding Build 220, you need to go to your broker's website and download the latest build, which should be 220. You may want to back up your Experts/Indicators and Templates folders before downloading. I don't remember how MT4 upgrade handles them, but to be safe, just back them up to somewhere else on your computer, and then check those folders after you have upgraded. Now, for the different Ichimoku colors, you need to right-click on each Ichimoku indicator on your chart, one at a time. When you get the drop-down menu, click on ...Properties. Then go to the Colors tab. You can change the colors to whatever you prefer. You will easily tell which colors need to be changed, but lines 5 and 6 change the upper and lower borders. Line 3 changes the vertical bars between the borders. You can experiment. I think that is more your problem with colors, rather than Build 220, but as I said, one of the prerequisites for THV v3 was to be on Build 220. I am surprised you have not experienced other problems. Good luck, not difficult.

I have to look at M15 and longer-term to see the trend. I usually trade off M5 but look at M1 immediately before I "pull the trigger". As long as M5 is still a go, if M1 says yes, I execute the trade. I think we said about the same thing. Longer timeframes show a better representation of the current trend, while shorter timeframes show more "every-minute noise", which can be confusing. Bottom line, if you trade longer TF, expect to wait longer for more PIPs. If you trade shorter TF, be ready to get out of a trade with minimal PIPs, and be ready to make more trades. My two cents.

--- 帖子 #6816 ---
Ofert, there are alerts for THV Coral (upper window) and Trix indicator (lower window). In MT4 menu, go to View/Indicators, hilite one at a time and click Edit. Then go to the Inputs tab. You will see alerts, probably labeled True. Just reset them to False and you've turned them off. Remember, there are alerts associated with both the Coral indicator and the THV Trix indicator. Good luck.

--- 帖子 #6874 ---
Exact. Additionally, the problem with divergences is that very often the alert coincides with any of the Trix sounds so one cancels the other (as they can't sound simultaneously). You can set it to give a pop-up alert instead by setting "sound alert on divergence" (which would trigger the sound) to "false" so the normal alert sound and pop-up window appear instead. It is explained in the settings of the Trix.

Tools=&gt;Options=&gt;Email, setup your email info. For an email address, use the appropriate one for your cell phone. For example, if you are with Verizon, it would be 9999999999@vtext.com for a cell phone number of 9999999999. Each carrier has their own domain. The broker you use doesn't matter as the message doesn't go through them but the software on your computer and your local connection. For those of you with a non-U.S. carrier, the sender may have to pay for the message, so you may have to use an intermediary service to relay the message. Thanks for your pivot observations Ed.

--- 帖子 #6925 ---
You should use your own ISP provider email address as sender (SMTP Server) (though yahoo or gmail addresses work, sort of, it is way too slow and it takes much longer until it sets up and is much less reliable) and your cell phone email address as receiver (final "To" field). One word of caution though: beware of continuous alerts (for example when the Trix crosses the zero line repetitively, or any which will behave the like) as it could cause the receiver's mailserver to block all further messages as possible spam...

Thank you all for the kind words. I want to send a small reminder in this occasion: The biggest enemies in FX trading are we by ourselves. Most of us are not costumed to take fast decisions when it comes to trading; FX is absolutely open, you can chouse the amount you want to trade, you can trade when you want, you can buy or sell when ever you think it’s fine for you. That’s why we need to set some rules to limit our trades to a certain amount, risk, trading hours etc. Those rules come with a system but everybody should adapt it to his needs and abilities and making his own rules based on his experience and mentallity. We need constantly work on our psychology, I still make mistakes sometimes, taking a trade without researching enough and those trades are mostly losers. Part of FX is constantly studying and collecting experience. It is quite a good idea to have a log where you note all trades, at the end of the day you can study them and see what you did right or wrong to get prepared for the future trades. Before you open your live trading platform ask your self always: Am I mentally prepared to trade today? Sometimes you have other stuff in the brain that doesn’t let you take reasonable decisions and you may lose what you cashed before. Have a good one everybody.

--- 帖子 #7031 ---
While you are waiting for Cobra I can tell you my observations. I am not actively scalping this way yet (extreme scalping) but have done much practice and research. Taking profit at ATR is a good guide because the assumption is you are trading in a small range, due to market conditions. Although you are correct in that a trade could potentially become larger, most of the time it does not so it is risky to hold your position for long. However, you can try to retain the reward potential by scaling out your position. Take 1/2 or 3/4 profit at the ATR, then put stops at BE and let it ride. I can't say whether that strategy is more profitable than continuing to scalp though. The bottom line to all this is being able to identify what kind of market you are in. The time of day and market location have alot to do with this, but you also have to develop a feel for it. Once you can do that , it will greatly help in your ability to scalp.

--- 帖子 #7037 ---
THV3 ATR Pips shows x times the ATR(20) (in this case, 300% or 3x the average true range for the last 20 periods or candles). You can read more about ATR here: http://stockcharts.com/school/doku.p...e_true_range_a Indeed it has been determined that 3 times the ATR(20) is a safe value to set the stops. ATR value can also give you an approximative idea about probable targets on each particular timeframe.

--- 帖子 #7092 ---
Trading methods Seykota is a trader who in 1970 pioneered a computerized trading system (now known as System trading) for the futures market for the brokerage house he and Michael Marcus were working for. Later, he decided to venture out on his own and manage a few of his client's accounts. Much of Seykota's success was attributed to his development and utilization of computerized trading systems to which he first tested on a mainframe IBM computer. Later on, the brokerage house he had been working for adopted his system for their trades. His interest in creating a computerized system was spawned after he read a letter by Richard Donchian on utilizing mechanical trend following systems for trading and also Donchian's 5 and 20 day moving average system. He was also inspired by the book Reminiscences of a Stock Operator. His first trading system was developed based on exponential moving averages. Ed Seykota, Market Wizards “Systems don’t need to be changed. The trick is for a trader to develop a system with which he is compatible.” Seykota improved this system over time, adapting the system to fit his trading style and preferences. With the initial version of the system being rigid, he later introduced more rules into the system in addition to pattern triggers and money management algorithms. Another aspect of his success was his genuine love for trading and his optimistic demeanour. This factor sustained his efforts to continuously improve on his system although he never changed the response indicators of the system and instead fine tuned market stimuli.

Inserted Code if (!ExistPositions()) { double chaOpen = iCustom(NULL, 0, "Heiken Ashi",color1,color2,color3,color4,2,0); double lhaOpen = iCustom(NULL, 0, "Heiken Ashi",color1,color2,color3,color4,2,1); double css_a = iIchimoku(NULL, 0, 2, 3, 5, MODE_SENKOUSPANA, 0); double css_b = iIchimoku(NULL, 0, 2, 3, 5, MODE_SENKOUSPANB, 0); double lss_a = iIchimoku(NULL, 0, 2, 3, 5, MODE_SENKOUSPANA, 1); double lss_b = iIchimoku(NULL, 0, 2, 3, 5, MODE_SENKOUSPANB, 1); int fasttrix = trix("fast"); int slowtrix = trix("slow"); if((fasttrix == 1 &amp;&amp; slowtrix == 3)) { if(cloudconfirm) { if(!((chaOpen &gt; css_a) &amp;&amp; (lhaOpen &lt; lss_a || lhaOpen &lt; lss_b))) { return(0); } } if(UseSound) PlaySound(NameFileSound); if(UseAlert) Alert("Buy Signal Detected on "+Symbol()+" ("+Period()+")"); OpenBuy(); countTrade(); return(0); } else if((fasttrix == 2 &amp;&amp; slowtrix == 4)) { if(cloudconfirm) { if(!((chaOpen &lt; css_b) &amp;&amp; (lhaOpen &gt; lss_b || lhaOpen &gt; lss_a))) { return(0); } } if(UseSound) PlaySound(NameFileSound); if(UseAlert) Alert("Sell Signal Detected on "+Symbol()+" ("+Period()+")" ); OpenSell(); countTrade(); return(0); } }

When the Trix is up (green) and starts to cross down (goes red), we get a GREEN BULL CROSS. And when the Trix is down (red) and starts to go up (goes green), we get a RED BEAR CROSS. Now maybe it is just me, and I don't understand convention here....but, THIS SEEMS CRAZY! If the Trix is up and starts going down, then shouldn't any alerts be red and refer to Bears, like......RED BEAR CROSS (for, "Red warning: Bears are gaining control!"). And it the Trix is down and starts going up, then shouldn't any alerts be green and refer to Bulls, like....GREEN BULL CROSS (for, "Green warning: Bull are gaining control!") Well, it sure seems more logical to me.....at least if one subscribes to using green candles for up moves and red candles for down moves.

--- 帖子 #7212 ---
jbird43.... I will not pretend to answer for Cobra, but I would like to share with you how I like to use these indicators; they work very well for me and my style of intraday trading. First I want to establish the current trend on the 1H chart using the cloud, HA candles, Trix and trend lines I draw on the chart. If the trend is unclear, I find another pair to trade; there is always one pair showing a strong 1H trend. Next drop to the 5M chart and wait for a new cycle to begin WITH the 1H trend; it should appear within the hour. If not, go back and look at the 1H to be sure the picture has not changed. Trading against the 1H is a cross-trend trade, very risky. Why trade against a stronger trend when you can trade with it? This method works very well for me. YMMV ! The only indicator I have added is a non-lag MA with alert set to 13. When the alert sounds on the 1H chart, I take a look and potentially plan a trade as described above. HTH !

Hi Cobra and the gang, I have just finished reading thru the thread. This is my first post to this thread. Here is just my 2 cents: Obviously a lot of experience, knowledge, passion, goodwill and generosity went into making the THV system and this thread what it is. Thank you very much for everybody who contributed!!!!! IMO this is a workable system but it is still not the holy grail or the elusive "get rich quick" system. By the way, the holy grail and the genuine "get rich quick" system do only exist in "never-never land" and in our pipe dreams. FX trading is a profession and a very difficult one. Remember only about 5% of all that try it ever make a success. There is a lot of workable systems out there (unfortunately there are more scams). But none are "turn-key", meaning just plug it in and it will work for you from day one. You must always first put in the hard yards before you can expect the results. You may subscribe to all the health magazines, have life long membership at all the gyms and have the personal trading program from Mr Universe but if you do not spend enough time in the gym and break the necessary sweat and sacrifice on your eating habits,etc. you are never going to have those six pack abs you are dreaming about. Also, the THV system has been proven to be profitable and workable as it is. You can most probably not make it better by adding more indicators. You can most probably make it better by adding: discipline, focus, experience, chart time and accepting the fact that you will never have a higher success rate than about 70 -75%. So accept that there will be loosing trades (the expenses of trading) and as long as it is not due to ill discipline, breaking the THV system rules or human error, accept it as normal. As my friend Bill Poulus likes to say about trading systems: "Keep it as simple as possible but not simpler" - from ALBERT EINSTEIN. So slow down with the number of indi's you are using. The market and PA is only predictable to a certain extend. At any one point in time the price can any of a number of things: In a lot of cases it will react like it did may times before, some times it will influenced by the big players and do something different, sometimes it will do something radical (like when news come out), sometime it will do nothing (like when news come out), sometimes it will do something different and nobody knows why (although the market commentators are always after the fact ready with a explanation). The point is: in a lot of instances future PA is fairly predictable (if you have the right set of rules (system) to give you an edge) but not always. The trader always form a major part of any system. He brings with him his fears and greed, his discipline or lack thereof his experience or lack thereof, etc etc. Phycology of trading: You will only be able to be profitable with any workable system if you stick to the rules of the system. You will only stick to the rules if you have confidence in the system. You will only have confidence if you believe in the system. You will only believe in it if you have spend enough time studying and trading the system to see for your self that the system indeed work and can be profitable. That is my take on it. Now I can go and put in the hard yards (screen time) to earn the right to take profit out of the market using the THV. Thanks everybody for sharing your insight and knowledge. Boerseun

--- 帖子 #7265 ---
In the code it says its the ADX, the Sar and the AO. I have made an indicator something like that for THV. It is a MTF histogram that shows the state of the slow and fast TRIX two timeframes up. (For example if you are on the 1 minute chart it shows the 15 and 5 minute trix. It *DOES* repaint in the sense that each of 15 bars on the 1 min chart shows what the 15 min trix was doing during that minute. So for a given 15 min period you might see 5 blue bars 5 red bars and 5 blue bars. If you then add another instance of the indicator after the 15 minutes bar for that period has closed you might see all 15 blue bars for that period on the one min chart. So you can't use it for back testing. However the on the original instance of the indicator, the 5 blue,5 red and 5 blue bars do not repaint unless you initialize the indicator. I find it useful because it tells me what the higher timeframe trix is doing at any given moment. Many thanks to Cobra for this wonderful system.

--- 帖子 #7268 ---
David4u, I was just looking at stuff like this earlier today. You entered too late, as the move-up was exhausting itself. You have to have a feel for the current market, and it's been on a very tight range lately. I have two personal rules, which might have helped you: 1. Be careful entering with price far from the Ichimoku cloud. The latest move may be exhausted. The best trading condition is when Trix crosses first, followed by a price move above or below the cloud. 2. Avoid trades where Trix is running "flat". This usually means that price is uncertain, and therefore too volatile and risky. Best I can see on your chart, your slow Trix was running a bit flat also. Hope this helps. Remember, with these tight ranges, trading is extremely risky. At least you had SL set.

Hi Windelevel: These are just basic market structures of any kind of corrective pattern. a-b-c is a simple corrective in Elliot Wave Theory and a-b-c-d-e is a complex formation of its counterpart. Please take a look at thread #7267; there is an example of a-b-c-d-e corrective. You may want to start off by learning a very simple presentation of Elliot Wave Theory. Suffice to say, ANY type of corrective MUST have at least 'three legs' as a basic requirement for the resolution of a corrective. Hope this helps. Have a good one Jeff

--- 帖子 #7307 ---
Hi Scrutch, Here is the code fix you asked for. Now you can set the rows to whatever position you like, but the default is as you requested: M5 fast M15 fast, M5 slow M15 Slow. P1 is the next higher tf and P2 is 2 timeframes up (i.e for 1 min chart it is 5 and 15, for 5 min chart it is 15 and 30. 0 is the top row of the histogram and 3 is the bottom. So to set it to 5 min fast, 15 min fast, 5 min slow 15 min slow you need to set it to fast P1 = 0 fast P2 =1 slow P1=2 slow P2 =3 That is the default but you can rearrange it if you want. Also I removed the labels as you asked

If you right click on your chart, then select Object List, select the line with Analyze Sell/Buy, Trend Up/Down, Bear/Bull Cross you can safely delete these labels. When the chart is refreshed the currently active labels will return, but not the ones referring to past events. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #7378 ---
A 10 pip trailing stop is way too tight. A better way is to wait until price has moved 15-20 pips (I use M1 ATR*3) then put you stop at entry and take 1/4 to 1/2 profit. That way you won't be stopped out as easy and will have locked in profit. When you are frustrated and impatient, stop trading, step back, and reassess. When I am confused, I just start looking at charts of other TF to see what kind of trade I may be waiting for. If still confused, take a break, go for a walk, etc. to get new perspective. Some days like today are harder to find a good entry. Learn how to recognize those and avoid trading them unless fully confident.

Also good is to run back a demo (or live) traded day and see why it all went pear shaped .. Hope this helps ...

--- 帖子 #7425 ---
I am all for all info in one TF concept. In fact, I am testing with 3 Ichi cloud (not the MTF Ichi) on the 5M before the post on MTF Ichi and having good successes. Did not want jump the gun and share this prematurely until i confirmed some observations. The settings I am testing is actually very simple. I extended what the Cobra team did with 2/3/5. No idea how you guys came up with this setting but it really is very good. V2 was 3/5/8 and made it better in V3 with 2/3/5. Kudos to the Cobra team. I added 2 more clouds with the following settings - 6/9/15 and 12/18/30. Basically, it is essentially adding the 15M (x2) and 30M (x6) cloud into the 5M TF. I am LIVE trading this with good successes. I trade the CORAL without the TRIX indicator. With prior testing (back and forward), I realised that the TRIX also confirms the clouds and CORAL. So I simplified it and removed the TRIX. I understand that the TRIX is the heart of the system but the Kumo is too and what I am doing is expanding on the Kumo. This also removes the fun for divergence. Trade risks are measured based on the 3 clouds. 1. Low risk - PA obeys CORAL and cross all 3 clouds. 2. Medium risk - PA obeys CORAL but cross 1st and 2nd clouds. 3. High risk - Ignore CORAL and use cloud crossing for low and medium risk. High risk is not advisable for inexperience traders. To further reduce risk, do not take the first breakout from consolidation or distribution. Take subsequent retests of the 1st cloud. I want to share this as Cobra has always said - adapt this into your own trading style. I am a visual trader as such making things very visual for myself. My style of trading is simple with this, in with more lots for small pips. I typically target 10 to 15 pips per trade depending on the sessions. It is easier to take small bites out of the market than expect 100s of pips. I always use a trailing stop (typical distance 10, step 10) to start off a position as I am too lazy to adjust the SL. But I revert to normal SL on higher TF if it is a good run. I want to share this as my way of giving back to the THV community. They brought me back from the "naked world of forex" and clothe me (For those who remember the picture of the BIG naked man). I have since moved away from trading naked on the H1 as this is more interesting and exciting and suits my personality better. Cobra, As usual hope this sharing is ok with you - a simplified version of V3. Else let me know and I will delete this post.

Greetings, Here are some charts of trades (demo still) I took this week. (15 minute) I thought I’d share something I have been using successfully to help pinpoint when a potential high probability trade could occur. It’s straight out of the manual, but for some reason I never thought of it just this way until recently. I was going to wait until I had more examples, compose my thoughts and post on the weekend, but here's what I have so far. Hope it's clear. The highlighted area on the first chart shows a pattern that happens on a regular basis. First, the coral passes through the price and the price drops. Next, a retrace, and price moves back into (through) the cloud to the coral or, better yet, the price moves through the cloud and the coral is some distance away. Enter when the price resumes its drop through the cloud. Reverse for longs. I have found this very helpful as a tool for working with the trend. There is another example for today...more if I didn’t have to sleep during the London session. I live on the west coast of Canada and work for a living. Hope this helps someone. The second chart has more examples. Sorry for the long post. Regards

--- 帖子 #7433 ---
That's right. Think of it as a temporary reversal indicator. It does not always indicate a real trend change, especially as you get into lower time frames. It is not 100% reliable, but as you zoom out in TF it becomes more reliable. I found the M15 is more reliable than the M5. On the M5 it is better, but risker, to anticipate it a little bit, which means seeing it forming before it is indicated. It seems to have a high success rate on the hourly, and good pip yield most of the time. Of course I still use good entry rules by using the lower TF's for entry.

Hi Olly: Nice to see you here again. Sure I'm not as good as others to give you advice. But let me share what I know about your question. If you use 1H TF, you may need at least 2 more TF for references. One is on 4H TF to help you know what is the latest trend. Thus you won't trade against the trend. The other TF is maybe 30m or 15m TF. It is needed to maximize your entry so you won't need too big SL or out because SL in case you put it too tight. Another input for you for the latest market condition, the market still in ranging position for weeks. It is a little bit hard to take a swing trade and even sometimes day trade. Same think also needed with your friend. He will need 15 or 30m TF for trend confirmation and 1m for entry point. I used to trade with 5m with THV as Cobra recommended and I use 15m and 1m. Go long if all trixes on each TF are green and short if all trixes are red. Put some TL if needed and be patience . Happy Trade

--- 帖子 #7599 ---
Divergences are good on that TF... Lower TF for entries (so you can make a better use of the stops, as they can be quite wide there) and higher TF for the continuation of the swing... For M5, as in any other TF, entries should be looked for in a smaller TF so one can wait for the small retracements and get in at a better price... can your friend post the trades he missed so we can help him see what happened there? I personally work M5 in conjunction with M30 as higher trend, and M1 for better entries. Both TFs should be aligned. If they contradict, it means the pair is in a retracement and one should wait until the direction is clear on both (you can also use M15, but I find that M30 gives a better overview of M5's "long-term" scope).

If you use good lower TF entry rules, the occasional false change on the H1 should be safely mitigated.

--- 帖子 #7620 ---
One way around this is I get into a good position, using the H1 trend change and smaller TF's for entry. Then I close 1/2 to 3/4 at good TP, which typically happens in a relatively short amount of time (15 minutes to 1 hour). Then, with SL at BE I am free to leave my computer (with preset alarms that ring my cell phone if needed). I can take more profit later, depending on S&amp;R levels, H1 exit alarm or a black cat crosses my screen. The H1 TF lets you enter with a higher degree of assurance that the previous trend will not resume soon.

--- 帖子 #7621 ---
This is a personal decision. You have to figure out what you are comfortable with. I typically take 1/4 to 1/2 at M1 ATR*3, then another 1/4 at M5 ATR*3. Then I take the rest depending on higher TF trend or S&amp;R levels, or other criteria. I prefer scaling out because it assures profit and you can leave a small amount in for those really big runs, with no risk (assuming stops at BE).

--- 帖子 #7667 ---
Period converter script is built-in. Open an offline M1 chart, open Navigator, apply the script to the chart and set the period (ExtPeriodMultiplier) to "x" times the chart TF (that would be 2 or 3 in this case). You can check on the Experts tab that it has created "xxxx" records. Then you go again to "Open Offline" and search for your M2 or M3 chart and voilà! Note: You have to make sure that "Allow DLL imports" is checked in the script before running it, so the created offline chart can update in real time. Also, the corresponding M1 chart where the script is running must be there.

First, whole and half #'s: 00, 50, 00 From Fibonacci series: 21, 34, 55, 89 Also from Fibonacci: 24, 38, 62, 76 Result: 00, 21, 34, 38, 50, 62, 76, 89, 00 Many use: 00, 22, 38, 50, 62, 88, 00 Still other throw in: 33, 66 To add balance: 12, 78 Hence: 00, 12, 22, 33, 38, 50, 62, 67, 78, 88, 00 (for a well balanced SweetSpot meal!) But many simpilfy: 00, 20, 33, 50, 66, 80, 00 Of course, even more simple: 00, 25, 50, 75, 00 Then use mathematical reduction by eliminating any number with "5" in it: ...... 00 (.....by this time you are wondering if just about ANY number is a sweetspot! LOL!)

--- 帖子 #7687 ---
Indeed However, smallest price increment/decrement is usually around 5-6 pips... on a M1 chart. I have been testing the equivalence on higher TFs, using the Grid indicator that was posted here lately. I found out the grid can be set according to the mean ATR(20) and maintain some coherence throughout the whole set of timeframes... and maybe that's why it would appear to be random if taken from a single TF point of view. Some price levels trigger stronger reactions, but basically round numbers lead, in 10 pips steps: test, bounce, retest, cross, retest back, test above, and so on. "Basic" sweet spots as mentioned: 00-20-33-50-66-80, have a particularity at least 80% of the time, that when crossed, even by one pip (Bid price) they will go to the next level though not always directly (they can go back a few levels to take impulse). If the level is not to be crossed, price won't even touch the level.

--- 帖子 #7700 ---
That's what we usually do here (look for the trend on a higher TF)... (BTW the "SweetSpots" are not a formal part of THV3 system). It all will depend on your personal preferences and goals... and capitalization and amount of stops you can afford! You can perfectly aim for longer term trends, thus having to look at weekly-monthly to gauge the trend then entering at a better level on daily or H4. In my own case, I'm more of a minimalist... for me each M5 candle is a micro-trend in itself and M30 is for me the equivalent of a daily chart... and M1 of an hourly (about the time it takes between each pair of swings...). I would love to have the patience enough to wait so long for a trade to develop, and let it "breathe" up and down meanwhile it does... but paradoxically, the more I trade the more free time I have left for other things... thus I switched my aim of long termed single 100-150 pip trades (and waiting for the "perfect" entry and so on) for the equivalent in plenty of 5-pips-in-average that I can do on the spot, and not be so much concerned with the larger trend beyond the next 30 minutes. I stopped making endless long term analysis which were almost always right (though I still have a look from time to time) but when confronted to the here and now I usually went against my own predictions... The market is always moving and always giving. So now I take what it gives me, and move on... I don't know if all this answers your question, but you can take the extreme opposite view and will maybe have a hint. Here's a minimalistic equivalent to your chart above

--- 帖子 #7730 ---
Hi Cashmeer: This method is a valid method, first shown by J. Murphy back in 1985 on the RSI indicator; trend lines are drawn on both the prices and the indicator. And it has been working fine for the past 23+ years. In the case of the RSI, the indicator ALWAYS shows a break out of the trend line first than the prices. I believe the TRIX will do the same. For chart 2 and chart 3; once I spotted those divergences and trend lines are in place, I would go further to draw even TIGHTER trend lines from the second pivotal bottom to the third pivotal top; as I always want to short/buy aggressively on divergence play because of the fact that, by doing that, it will give me lots of room to get out with a small profit or at worst, at break even. And yes, "rule of three" was being mentioned some 23 years ago as well and still applicable today. Harmonic pattern also has a pattern to go for the "three drives up / down"; which ALSO makes sense in Elliott Wave as that forms an ascending or declining wedge ~ "Wedgey 5th". P/S Trend line breaks on divergence play is one way. Trend lines can ALSO be drawn on your chart 2 with hidden positive divergence for a trend continuation play. Have a good one Jeff

--- 帖子 #7841 ---
hello everybody! It's been a while since my last post on this thread, have lots to catch up I hope you are doing very well with THV, my semester at college started again so it's been dificult to attend classes, trade and post, but I'm on my way.. so far March has been a good month, only 13 trades so far, all winners =D Last month I received a few MP asking about the way I trade THV and I'm gonna post my answer because I feel it can help others here as well (it's basic stuff don't worry) ------------------------------------------------------------------ THV is a GREAT system, really, it's easy, clean and intuitive, I follow THV system since its beta versions, when they were realesed in eur/usd thread, I think I was one of the few following it since the very beggining so after 3 months it all looks "easier" to me I daresay. Thing is, with THV, following the rules, you will win some, and you will lose some. You will win more than lose. I think the average hitrate for a newbie would be around 60% winners. That along with decent MM is enough to make money. But I know what you and others starting with the system feel, it kinda take sometime to get a "feel" for it. But I wanted more (ths month I had 92% winners), so what I've been doing is: I use THV as the core of my trading, but I also use other things that I think are VERY important: zoom out your charts, use 1H or 4H or above, see the major support and resistence levels, where price usually bounces, or areas where price consolidates. Be VERY aware of that. Trendlines. Draw them everywhere. Channels too. Sometimes we see the PERFECT signal on THV, we take the trade and it seems to reverse on us almost immediatly. And then we see it reversed because it was the middle wall of the channel, or price hits the bottom/top of a trendline, for exemple. I don't trade without channels. also is good to know a few patterns like head &amp; shoulders, triangles, wedge, flags, etc, watch for breakouts and retest of them. It's good to know about candle formations, the basic ones like dojis, hammer, pinbars.. be aware of psych levels, levels to watch, especially if you scalp: 00,20, 50, 80. have your analysis template (first page available to download on THV thread) always open. Put a LWMA60 on 5M chart and watch closely how price behaves around that MA. It's almost like magic, price almost always touches it and stop, most of the time it bounces back or acts like STRONG S&amp;R I've been using this MA as exit points on my fast scalp trades this month very succesfully. If you trade 5M and below you definetely have to watch it. It's even more reliable when there is confluence of the MA wth other things like pivot points, fibs, a pinbar, etc always try to go with the trend, this is VERY important, sometimes you make a mistake, but if you are gong with the trend it will help to put you on the right track eventually. If you trade 5M, be aware of the trix on 15M, even on 30M. don't over trade (my average is 2~3 trades a day), and don't overleverage, have a decent MM (1~3% each trade is ok for me) and stoploss acorddingly to the ATR of the TF you are using. start little and increase as you win, don't trade when you feel tired, angry, remember psychological aspects play a HUGE part in forex...not trading is also trading READ. Everything. I suggest the eur/usd thread, there are very good traders there, don't blindly take their signals, think for your self, take it as a guidance only. Be aware of news (and try to correlate them with the market movements), watch to correlation beetween pairs (eur/usd and usd/chf for example). How gold is correlating to the market these days, what is oil doing these days? and stock market? You really need a global look to trade forex sucessfully, IMHO. I know, this looks complicate, too much information, and it really is, I KNOW. Believe me, you will not learn everyting in a month, or two. I can humbly say that only now, after several months trading forex that I'm really getting that "feel' for it. Takes a lot of screen time. And there's still lots to learn, always. Sometimes it will be hard, remember we can't win everytime, I had several margin calls on demo, huge drawdowns, it never comes easy, you know. But don't feel bad about it, we all go through the same steps. never give up! I hope this helps you somehow

ForexTrader1, LWMA60 is a standard moving average indicator that you "Insert" from the MT4 menu. When you insert it onto your chart, you'll get the dialog box. Just type "60" in the number box and choose "Linear Weighted" in the dropdown. Most people usually choose "Close" on the other option.

Good morning all. I just wanted to let everyone know about my experience trading EJ. I traded it very little before this week but traded it almost exclusively in both Asian sessions. I found the best setup is using the period converter to create an M3 THV chart. I also added Trix and Ichimoku histobars. However, these two indicators do not show any other timeframe and only indicate the cloud and trix status for the M3. Nevertheless, this is working fine. The M3 is working as scalping indicator. When all bars (boxes) are the same color and trix have crossed each other and the zero line, the chance for positive pips is very high. I take a small amount of pips (5-10) and then leave a small position with S/L at BE. I will also exit just as soon as any of the bars change color. Using this method, any losses are very small and infrequent, at least so far.

--- 帖子 #7866 ---
We had some hours ago an iceberg order, what that means discribed doblece on the 15th of oct. 2008 in the EUR/USD thread: Iceberg Order A large single order that has been divided into smaller lots, usually by the use of an automated program, for the purpose of hiding the actual order quantity. When large participants, such as institutional investors, need to buy and sell large amounts of securities for their portfolios, they can divide their large orders into smaller parts so that the public sees only a small portion of the order at a time--just as the 'tip of the iceberg' is the only visible portion of a huge mass of ice. By hiding its large size, the iceberg order reduces the price movements caused by substantial changes in a stock's supply and demand. Source: http://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/icebergorder.asp Here an example at Interactive Brokers: http://www.interactivebrokers.com/en...?ib_entity=llc In other words, someone absorbs all sell orders (in this case) in small portions awaiting that the price rises. It was one of the reasons that I was riding all the London session a long trade with TP 50% on R2 (previous high) and 50% on R3 I made a screenshot when it was detected to show it here.

Since we are talking about trading, I think today's article from Yahoo is relevant: We hear staggering statistics that approximately 95% of traders fail in their ability to consistently profit from the markets. What are the 10 major mistakes that these traders make that cost them dearly? 1. Having no trading plan When you don't have a plan, you don't have a template to follow. It becomes very costly when your emotions are high and you have to make decisions on the fly. 2. Using strategies that do not match your personality You hear of a trading strategy that has worked very well and you are anxious to follow it. One important factor to consider is: does it match who you are and your lifestyle? 3. Having unrealistic expectations Most traders assume that it is very easy to make money in trading. They have unrealistic expectations with regard to their initial capital, their risk profile and how much money they can expect to make. 4. Taking too much risk Usually when traders are down, they want to make their money back very quickly. Therefore, they increase their position size without thinking about the risk/rewards. 5. Not having rules to follow Most traders think if they have rules to follow, they are restricting themselves. It is on the contrary. Having rules allows you to be more flexible since you have thought about lots of issues beforehand. 6. Not being flexible to market conditions It is very important to see the markets as they are and not as you want them to be or as you assume them to be. 7. Failing to take responsibility for your results When the results are not in your favor, the tendency is to blame the markets, circumstances, advice of others... When you blame things outside of yourself, you become a victim of circumstance. When you take responsibility, you can react differently to your circumstances and become the success you know you can be. 8. Being addicted to volatility One of the reasons that people get into trading is because they like the excitement of it. If there is no excitement, they create it. This is one of the reasons that traders sabotage themselves. 9. Not having a process to keep track of your performance If you don't keep track of your results, how do you know what has worked and what has not? How can you tweak your process to get the best results that you can? 10. Not dealing with your Emotional Risk When dealing with money, there are lots of emotions involved. Emotions are part of everyday life. What separates the successful traders from others is how they react to their emotions. So what can you do to become a more consistent trader and increase your profitability? 1. Think of trading as a business and have a trading plan. 2. Make sure that the strategies you select, match your personality so you can follow them. 3. Have a realistic expectation of what your returns are. Include all the costs associated with your trading business. 4. Have an idea for your risk/reward ratio. Don't confuse trading with gambling. If you are increasing your position, make sure that your strategy warrants it. 5. Have trading rules and follow them. Think about them as contingency plans. Because when your emotions are very high, the tendency is that you make very poor decisions that can cost you your account! 6. Be flexible to the market conditions. When you see the market as it is, you have a much better chance of managing your portfolio and increasing your profits. 7. Take responsibility for your results. Taking responsibility does not mean that you have control of everything that happens. It means that you have a choice of how to react to the things that happen. 8. Find out why you are in the trading business. If it is for the excitement of it, find other hobbies or activities that you can get your excitement from. 9. Keep track of your performance. This is a way of objectively looking at how you are doing, what you did right and what you learned. Be gentle with yourself. 10. One of the most important things that people don't handle is their Emotional Risk. When emotions run high, the quality of decisions goes down. It is very important to learn how to react to your emotions and thus increase your profits. "At first, something seems impossible. Then it becomes improbable. But with enough conviction and support, it finally becomes inevitable." -- Christopher Reeves

Well, I knew there wouldn't be any divergence play on this setup. Along with others over at the THV thread, I was stalking for this setup. I finally just looked at the obvious to push for the sell button. Just using trend lines break: The BARF formation. Also, it should be pointed out that this corrective was a simple a-b-c up. Using the squaring of Time and Price to arrive at the POSSIBLE turning point of the market. In this case, TIME has arrived first at 100% where the length of "a" equals the length of "b". But PRICE needed to catch up with TIME: The "c" top was made at 127.2% Fib projection off the "b" pivotal. Take care. Hey guys...would any of you mind to explaine me a bit how to use the ATR??? I mean if in 1M TF if shows 12 pips min Stop loss....that means for any trad i do...sell or buy ?? What is exact meaning of that ATR??

--- 帖子 #7996 ---
It is not buy or sell entry. It is for SL indicator. If you trade on 1M TF and your ATR on info panel show 12 pips, you are recommended to put your SL 12 pips away from your entry. ATR = Average True Range. Just google it, you'll find a lot.

--- 帖子 #7998 ---
leñador This is the MINIMUM number of pips for your SL. If you see a lot of price action this is can be too tight, so you may have to use the ATR shown * 1,5 or maybe even * 1,75. Look back at earlier price action on the chart you are working on to decide. Best of luck

--- 帖子 #8006 ---
There's a way for using multiple TFs in the simulator. Along with the vHandsTrade simulator there comes an indicator called "Period_Converter_Opt". Multiple instances of this indicator can be placed into the main chart to update previously opened offline charts with different periodicity. A full documentation of this you find in "Strategy Testing with Multiple Time Frames" pdf in the vHandsTrade thread ( http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...&amp;postcount=208 ) Just be aware of the indicators update interval settings, because if the main chart updates 3 other charts in fast forward mode, each with the complete THV setup, the machine might run out of resources.

--- 帖子 #8141 ---
I wanted to pass on an easy way to determine divergence direction without pausing to look at a chart. Just remember these two sayings: - Bottom's up - Top down Bottom's up = when divergence is determined from bottom (underneath) slopes, it indicates PA will move up Top down = when divergence is determined from top slopes, it indicates PA will move down Simple!

--- 帖子 #8199 ---
Try the attached "PriceAlert.mq4" indicator. I came across "Price_Alert.mq4" somewhere, but it did not work worth a darn. I rewrote the code and spiffied it up. You enter the price, color, line style and line thickness (for solid line style) and select if you want either, both, or neither of the Screen Alert and the Sound Alert. The Screen Alert is the pop-up window with the alert sound. The Sound Alert is just the alert sound. Once you have it set, you can simply "turn off" the indicator if you want to keep your settings on it for the chart it is applied to, but do not currently want the line to show nor the alerts to go off. Color is set to aqua, but changeable....see chart sample below.

--- 帖子 #8238 ---
I have noticed that MTF trix histogram repaints previous bars perhaps because the candles on higher TF are not closed yet. So as and when trix changes colors in higher TF, the histogram goes back and repaint its current and previous bars. I think histogram should update only the current histogram bar when trix on higher TF changes color. Just a suggestion. Another thing I have noticed and I may be wrong on this. The fast trix updates its color for the current PA candle and its color does not get repainted once the candle is closed. However, sometimes, it goes back one more candle to repaint its portion of fast trix. Example. Lets say fast trix has been green. Current candle in prograss is red. So corresponding trix for that candle turns to red. We now have a color change on the fast Trix. Now the next candle opens. Its PA is initially red. So its correponding fast trix is also red. But before this candle closes, the PA reverses into green, so the current fast trix is updated from red to green, but it also seems to repaint the previously red trix of the previous candle to green as well. The fast trix is now seamlessly green. In a longer TF, this could pose an issue. Something to look into by the THV team.

--- 帖子 #8241 ---
Are you using the beta version posted here or the one in development? (sorry I don't know the screen names of all the developers). The beta version posted here did repaint. I believe I have fixed this in the new versions (see attached screenshot. The upper portion is a screen shot I took earlier this morning to keep track of my trades and the bottom portion is the live MTF. No repaints that I can see. However, if you add the indicator 'after the fact' the bars will not match the bars show by an instance that accumulated them in 'real time'. This is because when you add an instance after the fact, it goes back and calculates the value bars based on the closed value of the higher tf. So for example if you are looking at a 1 min chart and watching the 15 higer tf, you might see 5 green bars 5 red bars and then 5 green bars. If you add another instance after that 15 minutes is finished you will see all 15 green bars because at that point the MTF indicator only knows the final result for that 15 min period. But in the 'real time' instance the bars should not repaint. I've noticed the trix repainting 1 bar back after that bar has closed too.

--- 帖子 #8388 ---
In MBTrading 1 Lot = 10,000 units, so you will be paying $0.67 for 10,000 units (1 Lot according to MBT,0.1 according to standard convention). So, you will be paying around $6.7 for 1 standard lot (100,000 units), Hope this helps. Karun

--- 帖子 #8389 ---
Hi There, You are correct on the calculation, but this commission is for entering and exiting the trade, so your commission would actually be .67 x 2, or $1.34. Read the print above their example commissions - "Commissions are based on total dollar amount of the executed order at the rate of $0.50 per 10,000 traded, each side." As the euro goes up in price, as it did today, so will your commissions. In their example they use 1.3310 x .00005. But the eruo sits at 1.3630 - so your commission would be 1.3630 x .00005, or .68 per side. Dan

I wanted to share a trade that just happened between me seeing patients here at the office. I combine the pivot point system with THV, what an amazing pair. I wanted to make this like the anatomy of a trade to share with others what has been working so well lately. I use two screens to trade. 1. Take a look at the analysis chart, how are we trending today? UP, ok taking longs today, buying oversold and selling high. 2. Any news about to happen? No, good, all clear 3. How's the CCI look? Oversold, hooking up to bull territory. 4. Trend channel? Up, oversold out of the channel, the trend is your friend, time for your friend to make you some money. (Analysis chart) 5. How's the Trix look? Turning green in oversold territory, showing divergence. 6. Pivots? Looking to bounce off of MS1 and ride it to the FPV, in this case a good round psych number, 3600. 7. Volume and PA? moving steady, ranging tight, looking good 8. Ichimoku Clouds? Crossing short-term cloud, but still under M15 cloud, riskier entry, but all else looking good. 9. Where are you setting your stop? 3535, below the last candle low, riskier trade entry (clouds), tighter stop, but give it a little wiggle room or they will spike it and clear your stops. Thats how I trade now, playing the pivots, and THV.] McD PS. good call Jeff on mwsnap, thats exactly what I was going to share as well, easy, cool little program, great for screenshots. --- 帖子 #8559 ---
But I have one more indicator to give away This one does not tell you yes or no or where to go, it measures if you did right or wrong. It shows you the profit in pips and account currency over several periods. The total amount is calculated over the amount of history which is configured in your terminal window. If you want to show your overall performance, the account history in the terminal window has to be set to &lt;All History&gt; If you are splitting your positions, the pips for the remaining order are only accumulated if the order exceeds the closed position. For this feature it is necessary that you don't edit the order comment because that's the only way to track along such positions. The value for the open orders shows only the orders of the same currency pair as of the chart where the indicator is placed. All other values are calculated over all trades. Happy trading ...

--- 帖子 #8586 ---
Some simple points which turned my break even or demo account buster trading into the right direction. I repeat once again the link to a post from Jack Herer as everything there is true ( http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...postcount=7842 ). Although most of the time I tried to respect everything mentioned there I still could not get my account growing. As I want to start live with a small account size of about 200 € I trade also a demo account with this size. According to my MM with &lt; 2% risk a volume of 0.01 lot has to be used. Countless trades I've placed were going to 10-20 pips but I wanted more until they turned against me and I had them to close NEGATIVE. What was wrong ? The volume was to small, because the position could not be splitted. Now my MM is &lt; 2% but at least 0.02 lots. If a position is positive I can close the half position at TL, S&amp;R, pivot, psych without the feeling to have something lost if the movement continues and WITHOUT closing the trade negative, because the remaining orders S/L is set to BE. Another weakness of mine was to watch negative trades with the hope of turning the right way. HOPE will never turn a position. If you have no fundamentals, no higher TF trends, no channels, ... which tell you the position will turn just hope you can close the position because the negative pips would grow and grow and while you watch the loss get bigger you miss other opportunities. Way wrong for me was also the amount of currency pairs I thought of being able to manage. Now I've reduced them to 3 pairs. These 3 pairs and above insights - additionally to the THV of course - gave me 208 pips this week with no loss and 12 winners in a row . My last trade of today below. Just luck or the right decision, any comments of the pros in here ? Tks.

Hi Macman: I draw forks manually and, personally, this is the only genuine way to this approach. When I came over to Forex Factory, I was initially quite impressed by people written out codes for the forks, and Shi Channel is one of them. I used it for maybe 1 day and, to me, it's useless because it repaints all the time; meaning that "it tells you things in hindsight". But if the forks are being drawn manually and being identified as the correct fork, it will control FUTURE price actions and will provide you a possible path of future price actions in high probability. Now, you may ask, how to identify the fork as being the correct one to utilize? The correct usage of a fork can be identified by simply observing whether it 'describes' price actions in the best way. Here's an example of the reason when I longed at 1.4575 on the Gbp/Usd in the 15-min time frame. Please take a look at the gif, the price actions of the last few days have been set IN ADVANCE by the Blue Fork; and price actions have been acting accordingly within these three median lines and sliding parallels. It's a very lengthy subject and not very appropriate to discuss here. Let me know if you want to explore further. Take care. Have a good one Jeff

--- 帖子 #8669 ---
Hi Stitch961: Yes, it wasn't a mistype. We as traders follow the price actions and the future course of price gyrations will be contained by the median lines of the forks. The median lines are not trend lines; these are lines of vibrations that prices have the tendency to attract to them. Of course, when prices finally break out of a fork; it's a strong signal to trade in the direction of the break out; and eventually a new fork can be drawn to 'contain' the new trend in question. Take care. Have a good one Jeff

To delete any chart screen artifact left over from a deleted indicator, simply right click on the chart, select "objects list" and then scroll thru the list of objects to find the one you wish to remove. When you find it in the list, left click on it to highlight it, and then left click on "delete". Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #8798 ---
EU on M1 Chart: Point A showed PA dropping thru cloud and trix crossing down. But, Bollinger bands were not squeezed. Point B showed PA dropping thru cloud and trix crossing down. But Bollinger bands were not squeezed. Point C showed PA dropping thru cloud, and trix bouncing down off signal line, AND the inner Bollinger band was squeezed. This is where I took the trade at 1.3276 short. PA stayed pretty uniformly on the left side of the cloud as it treked down, so I made decision to exit on the Fib. Extensions already applied to the inner Bollinger band squeeze. When PA hit the -662% level, I made hasty exit at 1.3255 as I had no idea if it would bounce up quickly. PA did strike a bit lower before finally ending the immediate run down, but the trade was successful in that the Bollinger bands helped to identify the right time to enter and the cloud and BB extensions helped to identify a good exit. Bollinger bands squeezes can help identify the right entry and avoid some that go nowhere. Fibonacci extensions applied to the Bollinger band squeezes can help target possible exits as you later watch the PA action with regard to the cloud and the fib extension levels.....

--- 帖子 #8842 ---
Many traders have adopted a "rule of thumb" regarding HA candles: Five to eight candles is the average number of HA candles before a noticeable change occurs in the PA. More than eight is NOT the norm. It may just be a small period of consolidation OR it might signal a reversal. I suggest being careful at five candles and being VERY careful at eight. Because I am trading the THV method on the M15, I pay attention after three HA candles; more than five in my direction is a bonus! HTH!

--- 帖子 #8849 ---
This method is very discretionary; I am NOT saying the trade setup would be invalid. I am saying you need to pay attention to the number of HA candles in a price move as part of the decision making process. The "rule of thumb" I referred to earlier is very common with traders who use HA candles regularly (myself included). I suggest you look back at charts for the timeframe you like to trade (evidently M1...too noisy for me, thank you), and look for HA candle patterns that fit the description I have provided. Once you get a feel for the action that is commonly associated with these candles, you will be in a much better position to make a trade entry (or not) decision.

--- 帖子 #8850 ---
Bart, just a suggestion to help myself and others better see your trades......include the vertical line (red for short entry and green for long entry) at the candle time of your entry. When you exit, again include the vertical line at the candle time of exit (green to close short trade, red to close long trade). If you do this, then your entries long will be marked with a green horizontal line and a green vertical line, and your entries short will be marked with a red horizontal line and a red vertical line. Your exits from a long trade will be marked with a red horizontal line and a red vertical line, and your exits from a short trade will be marked with a green horizontal line and a green verical line. This method very clearly identifies entries and exits and their types.

--- 帖子 #8877 ---
Grats on your 500th post. You have been making significant contributions. A word about MTF and repainting: When you are getting used to this new system, be sure to watch it live and not depend too much on backtesting merely by viewing history on your charts. The higher TF's boxes will change somewhat when you close and reopen MT4. For example, a M30 trix indicator can change color up to 6 times on a M5 chart in a 30 minute period as it fluctuates with PA. When MT4 is closed and restarts, it recalculates those 6 boxes to one value because the M30 only had one value when it closed. You will see what I mean as you use it. If you post a screenshot, take it live so that others can see how it appeared "on the fly".

--- 帖子 #8916 ---
One thing you can use these indies for is to see how strong the trend is, and where you are in it. When you see that all 10 bars have just gone green, you are probably at the beginning of a reasonably strong trend, and you can probably get away with going long even if you see a negative divergence (though I personally don't do it unless I see a good reason, like a strong break of a pivot or the like). When you look at the top 1m row, you can count the number of alternating red and green waves since all bars have gone green. If you see three or four of those red/green waves, and a couple of negative divergences in a row, it's more risky to go long. even if you have 6 points.

--- 帖子 #8918 ---
Hi Emda, Indeed you cannot use the MTF indicators for manual backtesting by looking at the chart, because the information they provide looks different when recalced on load than it does when accumulated in real time, as Tradewell explained earlier. In fact, anything that initializes the indicator will cause it to recalc. Changing a setting or even clicking on it and then clicking ok will cause it to repaint. But all that is missing the point. The point of these indicaters are to enable you to see what the Trix is doing in the other time frames in real time, without having to click on the other charts so that you can get an idea of the trend, and trade accordingly. If you are scalping the 1m, knowing what the trix is doing on the 5 m and 15m timeframes right now without having to click to other screens is valuable, possibly even more so than knowing 15 minutes from now, what would have done, with certainty.

Hello all, I am preparing to stop for the day. I wanted to post something that will hopefully help a lot of you earn more PIPs. Like a lot of you, I keep a rudimentary record of all my daily trades. For each trade I always record: Trade Price - obviously, the price at which I executed my long or short; Drawdow n - how far negative did my trade go before I was either stopped out or it turned around and headed positive? " Optimal" Price - how far did price go in the positive direction after I terminated my successful trade. THV and the rules for setting SL around the ATR number generally keep me close on the drawdown. Therefore, the most important of the above items to me is Optimal price. At the end of every day, I want to know how many pips I could have gained if I'd had the patience to let my trades run farther. Today is a prime example of why it is good to track these numbers. I made 13 trades. 12 were successful, and 1 I got out of at break-even (0). I earned 69 PIPs. How many did I "leave on the table"? Believe it or not, 93 PIPs!!! Now I am not advocating greed, but I am saying that I could have optimized my trading better if I'd trusted my chosen exit points (pivots, psychs, median lines, trendlines). I bail out early far too often. I hear the same thing from a lot of other traders, so I thought I'd post this as food for thought. If you are not tracking these kind of numbers, I would recommend it. If, like me, you are missing pips, review your methods, your signals, and your TPs. Just a quick two cents worth. Hope it helps.

--- 帖子 #8955 ---
Love it very much Ed. Optimizing the trade. That's the keyword. I'm learning this thing last few months and begin to get better from day to day. This is what I learn on my optimizing learning: 1. Optimizing on entry point: Finding the best price to go short or long will help you A LOT to minimize a drawdown. On many case, sup/res line retest will play a good rule to enter the trade. Some pairs (GU and EJ) also have high volatility that even on a HA chart it will have both head and tail wick. If you go short, wait for the head wick to enter the trade. Vice versa on long trading. And of course don't forget those multiple TF indis. 2. Optimizing on exit point: For me the key here is to have a good bias whether the pair is on ranging period or trending period. On ranging period you can expect 30-40 pips on GU or 20-30 pips on EU. Enter the trade, take the profit, wait for retracement, and take another trade if it is possible. BUT don't expect more on this ranging period. My main rule when exiting at ranging market is sup/res line. I'm not depend too much on trix in this case. On trending market, sure you can play trail, closing half trade and move SL to BE, or just wait another 30 minutes to see your pips grow. My exit trade usually based on fast trix color change. If I based my entry on 15M trix, then my exit will be based on the same TF. Unless I see price reversal will high enough, I will close my trade and reentry later at better price (this need screen time experience). Sometimes on high volatility pair, moving SL to BE too earlier will just offset the profit and turn the trade into BEP trade (with heartache of course ) Well, that's just a note from me. Correction or suggestion will be much appreciated.

The order of the most important things when taking a trade. 1) Money Managment: Without good MM 98%, or all traders will blow out their account very quickly. 2) Exit: The trader needs to spend the most time developing an exit strategy. The exit is the key to enlarging your account. 3) Entry: The entry is the lowest in this short list of importance.
