--- 帖子 #8990 ---
Depends on how conservative you want to be. I take the trades when I see six lights, unless there was a preceding divergence of the opposite type. My reasoning was that when you have the trix in the majority of the timeframes going in your favor, and the 5m fast also going in your favor, and the 1m has just turned in your favor, they will pull the PA in your direction. Most of the time this is what happens, and even if it doesn't, by getting in at the first bar just as the fast 1m trix changes colors, you can usually squeeze out 10 pips. I just set the stops and targets and leave it alone, and that's how I tested it. But this also has to do with my trading style - I don't have the patience to manage trades. The trix indie itself can change colors one bar back. So far I haven't noticed the histogram doing that except when it's initialized. So sometimes I've seen (for example, a green bar in the 1m f on the histogram and the fast trix is green at that point), and then the next bar the trix turns red, and also turns the trix indie over the prior bar red. The histogram, as far as I can tell, remains green in that case. Not much you can do about it. I just take my lumps if I got a bad trade because of it If you want to be conservative, a nice safe trade is when you have six bars in your favor , preferably 4 in the first histo, and a trix cross occurs right about then, right about at the zero line. I'm posting an example from yesterday, with one safe one, and two where we got extra pips because we didn't wait for the trix cross. (My notation style is red bar for short trade, dashed red bar for exit, green bar for long trade, dashed green bar for exit, magenta for take the high road and decline to trade an ify situation.) In the safe situation you also aren't likely to get a repaint. That is also more in line with the original way of trading THV, which requires you to have a trix cross. But if you have strong trend, and you want to scalp at the beginning of each new wave, getting in when you have 6 points just as the 1m fast changes color is the way to get the pips. Just depends on your style. I'd recommend practicing with a demo first, like any other new thing.

--- 帖子 #9051 ---
I can think of a few reasons for this 1. The Trix Histo uses the Trix V5, and on the chart you posted it looks like you are using a different version. The settings are a bit different between versions, so the trix is not always the same color on both of them. 2. In the screenshot you posted, you are referencing 7:01 yesterday, but you posted today, and I'm assuming from the way the histo looks you took the screen shot today. If I look back today at that time on my screen, which has been running continuously, indeed the colors of the 1m histo don't match the trix. However, at the time, they gave me proper signals. This is because, the trix histo calls the trix with the default settings, which are 750 bars. If you look back more than that the trix itself doesn't work, so neither does the histo. 3. The trix itself does repaint by one bar sometimes. For example, if it is about flat, and above the bar you are looking at it is red and and ends red, the trix histo will be red. If the next bar has a strong up movement, the trix above it will go back and repaint the closed bar to green. In most cases that I have observed the trix histo keeps the red setting. Until the trix is fixed so that it doesn't repaint, that can't be fixed. That's all I can think of. If you see this again today can you post a current screenshot in real time and pm me so I can check mine.

--- 帖子 #9055 ---
I've had a few PMs asking me to explain how to set the timeframes in the Trix histogram. I'd recommend looking at the examples in the templates other users so kindly posted, but in any case if you want to control the timeframes: 1. Set the autotimeframe parameter to false. 2. Pick the four timeframes you want in ePeriod1, ePeriod2, ePeriod3, ePeriod4. 4. Pick which trix line you want for each timeframe. 0 is slow, 1 is fast. 5. Set the row in which you want each timeframe to appear in P1_position, P2_position, P3_position, P4_position. 6. Repeat as needed by dragging as many new instances of the indicator onto the chart as you like. If you set autotimeframe to true, it picks the next two higher timeframes (for example on a 1 m chart it will show 5m and 15m fast and slow). If you set UseSecondAutoTF to true as well, it will show the third and fouth timeframes up (for example on a 1m chart it will show 30 and 60 fast and slow.) You can use this if you want to have two instances of the histogram on a chart and then change the timeframe on the chart, without having to reset all the histograms manually.

In the attached pic you can see what I was describing about the histogram colors not matching the trix, where the yellow box is. At the very end of the 10:16 bar and the very first seconds of the 10:17 bar (GMT+3) the fast trix was green. If you look at the 10:16 bar, this makes sense, because it was a green up bar. By the end of the 10:17 bar, PA had closed down and the trix above it was red. The trix then went back and repainted the 10:16 bar to red. (I didn't take a screenshot of that because it happend in about 3 seconds at the very end of the 10:16 bar and beginning of the 10:17 bar, but I was watching it as it happened and I have taken similar screenshots in the past.) The histogram at 10:16 remained green. You could have have taken a bad trade based on that, but that is life. The histogram is telling you what happend in real time, and at the very close of the 10:16 bar and the start of the 10:17 bar, the fast trix was green. If you reload the indie, all the bars will be red. But that is hindsight and we have to trade in real time.

Hi Princess, Just to help any newbies out there struggling with this huge thread. I think the manual 1st page reads better like this: THV3 Multiple Time Frame (MTF) Rules Coded by Miss Pips, a big applause to her for all the time and efforts in this project. Edited by TradeWell, Cobraforex and the THV Team Regular Trades: 1) Trade when you get 6 green or 6 red lights total out of all Trix histograms. 2) Two of the lights have to be in the first two rows (m1 and m5) 2a) Trade direction must be away from the Coral 3) Take the trade as soon as PA touches below/above the Cloud (don't wait for a close below or above) 4) Dont trade when you see divergence in the opposite direction. Divergence not only gets you into good trades earlier, it also keeps you out of bad ones. Exit at 10 pips profit and use a 15 pip SL (or ATR, whichever is larger). The suggested setup uses 1m fast, 5m fast, 5m slow, 15m fast, 15m slow, 30m fast, 30 m slow and 60 m fast Trix histograms, and the Ichimoku histogram uses the 5 m and 15m clouds. It has been tested for use on the M1, EURUSD chart. Other currency pairs and TF's may require adjustments to these rules. Also for anyone struggling out there I have posted my chart with Coral etc marked. Basically trading away from the Coral is trading with the trend so increasing the likelihood of a successful trade. In the chart you take shorts only - away from the Coral. Hope this helps p.s. My TRIX and Cloud Histograms are not the latest versions - yet.

--- 帖子 #9066 ---
My understanding of the original rules is that PA has to be above both the Coral and the cloud for a long and below both the Coral and the Cloud for a short. I tried to stick to these rules with only two exceptions: 1. For divergence trades, PA only has to break the cloud (and you need 6 points - four of which come from the divergence), because if you wait for it to break the coral too, the divergence might have exhausted itself. 2. In the original rules, in addition to PA breaking the cloud and Coral for a regular trade, you needed a trix cross, and the fast and slow trix in the direction of the trade, and the fast trix above/below 0 in the direction of the trade. In my rules you don't need a cross or the slow trix, or the break of 0 although it's safer if you have that (but you will miss quite a few good trades if you trade only that). In my rules you can trade when a) PA breaks the coral and cloud b) The fast 1m has just turned in your direction c) The fast 5m is going in your direction d) You have 6 points. The reason I allow this, is because I figure that if you have the majority of the lights going in your direction, odds are that the change in the fast 1m trix is going to turn PA back in the direction of your trade. The Euro to me is like a big slow tanker that cant turn around too fast once it builds up steam. So even if you entered on the last wave (which I don't recommend but you never know which one it is) usually you can squeeze out another 10 pips when you have so many trixes going in your direction, and the fast 1m has just changed. Anyway, Tradewell is fixing the manual, and he is a model of clarity so when he gets done I'm sure it will be more understandable

On the first chart, the fork is not describing all the price actions; right in the middle, the 'big hump' is totally out of the fork, thereby, discounted the validity of this fork. In your case, B comes First, A comes Second and C comes Third. Hence, it is not a pitchfork.

--- 帖子 #9178 ---
You need 6 lights on the histogram (not for 6-7 bars, just lights from 6 rows in a column). Two should be in the 1m f and 5m fast rows, unless you are trading divergence. (If you are trading divergence, then you only need 2 lights from the histograms and one should be from the 1m fast row.) Also, don't trade against a previously conflicting divergence signal. The Trix for MTF histo is just the latest trix, with all the options shut off. That's because the histograms call it and we need to prevent the histograms from drawing lines on the charts where users might not want them.

--- 帖子 #9182 ---
Couple of points which may help here. Not sure if this is the best way to set up, but it is the method I use. Note here that I am not yet using the latest multi light histos. 1. Best to use M1 chart for entry/exit as this is giving you the most up to date look at what PA in the market is doing. Not much point in trying to judge an entry from an M5 chart if you have M1 available. 2. On your M1 chart have your cloud and Trix histo looking at higher TF's so on your 6 light set up you would have histos looking at M5 and M15 TFs 3. Similarly on your M5 chart set up your histos to look at M15 and M30 TF's. Your M5 chart is currently showing an M5 histo which is obviously not needed as you are looking at the TRIX on M5 anyway. 4. Decide which TF you are going to make your trading decisions from - suggest you use M5. Set up your sound alerts only on M5 and save an M5 template. Switch off sound on M1 and save an M1 template. Likewise you can switch off sound on higher TF's and again save a template. Now when you are looking at the M1 chart to judge a possible entry/exit you can see the state of both the cloud and the TRIX on M5 and M30. The problem in having an M1 histo on your M5 chart is that you will be constantly seeing it change and may be tempted to exit trades way to early. Best of luck

--- 帖子 #9198 ---
Like I said, these rules were ceveloped for the EURUSD. I view the EURUSD like a big tanker that is hard to turn around once it builds up steam. So the rules were designed to help capture more good entries than just a trix cross, and to weed out the entries based on the trix cross that might be false. My reasoning was that if you have the a majority of the lights in your favor, then if you get in right when the 1m f and the 5m f turn in your direction, there is probably at least enough enertia to sqeeze out another 10 pips even if you have gotten in on the very last wave. I based this on a lot of observation. The EY might work differently, however.

--- 帖子 #9237 ---
Adding the histos does make the overbought/oversold lines disappear. I believe that this happens because the histos call the trix itself on each tick, and the trix adds/ removes those lines when it is initialized/deinitialized in the window where it is called. So when you add the trix histos, the lines are drawn in the trix histo window (but you don't see them because the value so small compared to where the histo window is drawn.) I think we can get rid of this by giving those lines another name in the version of the Trix that is called by the histos in the next release. Meanwhile I would just add them in as a line in that window, if you want to see them. (Get the values for the lines by adding the trix to a window without the histos first.)

I am not sure if this would work, but it maybe worth a try. Go to your indicator list and go to the indicator window with the THV3 Trix for MTFHisto highlight that indicator and click Edit. Then go to the Common tab and at the bottom your see click on Fixed minimum and click on Fixed Maximum. Change those to -0.0002 for the minimum and 0.0002 for the maximum, if they are already at those levels I am not sure. But I hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #9473 ---
I picked this up somewhere and keep it as a reminder of price action... Picture a gymnasium with a ping pong ball in the center of the floor. The position of the ball represents the current price. The ball is surrounded by thousands of people. (Its more fun to picture these people dressed in 3 piece suits, but you get the idea...) Now the bigger and stronger groups (traders) are able to muscle their way down close to the ball where they can have a greater effect, but everybody in the place is trying to blow the ping pong ball the direction they want it to go or at least observe which way it is heading. The bigger traders or groups of traders are able to blow the ball the way they want to for a while, but then they get tired and either another big boy comes in and takes their place or those that want the ball to go the other way blow it back. World events can dictate where people position themselves. Sometimes, something happens where everybody gets on one side or at least gets out of the way and the ball goes for a long run in one direction. Over a period on days and months, this almost become a dance - everyone blowing on the ball - sometimes holding it in place - not because there is no force on the ball - but because the forces from all sides are equal. The movement of the ping pong ball is the price action. We study it, and can (or try to) predict where the ball is going to go. Yet, on days like today, when large groups of traders are not in the gym to blow the ball, the price action may not act like it normally does. The groups that normally would stop a bull or bear run may not be there. Thus, risk tends to be higher and what is 'oversold level' on a normal day may not be 'oversold level' when not everyone is part of the action. That is what you are seeing today. Many will sit out a day like today, and not try to trade. You may very well see things you do not normally see. Caution should the word of the day. Another thing to be aware of, some brokers and banks etc, don't blow on the ball, but try to effect the ball by just inhaling. Whatever the reason, they just suck... T...

--- 帖子 #9483 ---
On the 1m it was tested that 2 points have to come from the 1m f and 5m f, and the other four points can come from any of the other 8 rows. It was tested with a s/l of 15 or the ATR suggestion whichever is higher and a 10 pt target. I think a lot of folks manage the trade and go for more than 10. Take the trade when PA breaks the cloud and the coral. Exceptions to the rules are: Dont trade in front of opposing divergence (i.e. dont short if you see a long divergence and vice versa) Also, if you are experienced you can trade divergence plays. In that case, the divergence itself counts for 4 points, and one other point should come from the 1m f row. Take the trade when PA falls below the cloud in that case, but don't wait more than 3 or 4 bars from the point of the divergence to take the trade.

--- 帖子 #9488 ---
High to low = pips between hi and low of the day Pips to open = how many pips market has moved since day open ATR = Average true PIP range of the last 20 candles. It is shown as 3 times the ATR Daily Average = daily average pip range of last x number of days. It measures average volatility of the pair. None of these are relevant how THV is used for taking trades.

Well, I just take my lumps if a trade doesn't work out. Your chart illustrates 2 things though. 1) We didn't mention this in the manual because it isn't unique to THV and we didn't want to make the manual to complicated. But, it is good practice in all forms of trading not to take a trade too late. You should have gotten in 6 bars earlier, where you first had 6 red lights, just as PA dropped below the coral and the trix crossed. It's true that if you get in at the start of a downtrend you can catch many more 10 pip trades with 6 lights. BUT, this was far from the start of the downtrend. 2) I would not have taken even the earlier trade (though it looks to have been good), because you can already see divergence is forming, where I marked the green lines. And also you have positve divergence on the 15m tf at 16:30 and on the 30 m at 1700 (GMT+3). If the trend has been going for quite a while, you need to watch out for divergence before taking trades in the direction of the trend, because at some point, you know you are going to get a retrace.This just takes practice looking at PA so you can spot divergence before the trix warns you. You will miss a few good trades that way, but also most of the loosers.

--- 帖子 #9561 ---
Draw a trend line on the faster Trix, then draw a trendline on PA. Be sure to draw it the same on both: either on top or underneath. If the slope of the two is different (one ascending, one descending) then you have divergence. You can remember this saying to help you know what that means: Bottom's up (divergence underneath, PA indicates up) Top down (divergence on top, PA indicates down) That's as simple as I can explain it. It assumes you know about drawing trend lines.

--- 帖子 #9565 ---
I've been inspired by your post to release the MTF Divergence indicator. In the first chart below, the red line shows where your trade was. (The Trix histo looks different on my because my provider's server disconnected, so the real time data for the tris histos was lost there. But for the purpose of the MTF Divergence indicator this doesn't matter because it doesn't repaint, and doens't report real time data.) The earliest that this indicator can report a divergence on a higher timeframe is the start of the bar after the trix indicator on that timeframe identifies it, which is usually but not always two bars from the peak/valley. In the first screenshot, the green bar is where the divergence on the 15m chart was reported on the 1m chart, and the green bar on the second screenshot is where the trix knew about it on the 15m timeframe. In this case the divergence was caused by the 16:15 (GMT+3) bar on the 15m chart so it was reported at 16:30 on the 1m chart. There are no rules for using this indie. On the 1m tf I set it to 5,15,30 and 60, and I use it as a warning that the trend might be changing. As you can see from the first screenshot, it would have given you a heads up not to take a short where you did, because you had divergence on two higher timeframes. Cautionary note, like all the divergences reported by the trix, these sometimes lag what you would notice if you were watching the chart itself. But, if you are not watching those timeframes anyway, this can be a help. For this indie to work you need the same THV3 Trix for MTFHisto.exe file as you do for all the other mtf indies. This is a beta version. Another version will be released with the next release of THV.

--- 帖子 #9567 ---
Please do not think I am picking on you. I am not. But imho, paying attention to the news can be dangerous to your financial health. I will concede that knowing WHEN there is to be important releases (of news, garbage, whatever) can help you set up for a possible move. But that is all that "stuff" is worth. As far as actually LISTENING to any of it, don't bother. So called "news", releases, etc. are going to be used by the market movers to their own advantage. And that can sometimes mean manipulating the PA in just the opposite direction from what is expected. Put it this way....."news" sometimes embodies a legitimate reason to change the price, but most often it is used just as an excuse to do so. So, upcoming "news" can mean possible PA activity will occur. That is all. Don't read anything more into it. And beware that the PA activity may, or may not be suitable for trading. Personally, I find that in MOST cases, the PA will completely reverse any move made on "news". It will do so in a less frenetic way, in a more tradeable way, and will happen within a few sessions, if not a few hours!

--- 帖子 #9568 ---
Great post, McD! There is no substitute for real thinking in this trade! And, if I may add, look for sequences of highs and lows. It bears repeating that a sequence of higher highs and higher lows shows upwards price bias. And a sequence of lower highs and lower lows shows downwards price bias. The attached H4 chart to go along with McD's shows the fib retrace and this time with Highs and Lows shown. The way this can be traded is to accept the sequence here is lower highs and lower lows. Now look for a significant line of demarcation, which if the PA breaks down thru it, will present a trade entry opportunity. On this H4 chart, the 38% retracement line qualifies. A real conservative entry would be a break of the 50% (Center) line. A real aggressive entry would be to underscore the recent candles on a smaller TF chart, and enter on a break down thru that score/trend line (see second chart).

--- 帖子 #9607 ---
Hi, I think maybe your TRIX histo indicator is set up incorrectly. Your chart shows the M5 TF and AFAIK your TRIX histo should be looking at the higher TF's - M15 &amp; M30. This will then match your Cloud histo which is already looking at M15 &amp; M30, so giving you a complete picture of what is happening on these TFs. I believe the idea behind the histo indicators is to let you look at what is happening on higher TFs without having to switch screens. On your chart you are already looking at the TRIX on M5, so there is no point in having a histo square telling you what you are already looking at. Similarly on your M1 chart you should have the Cloud histo showing you the state of the cloud on M5 &amp; M15 and your TRIX histo showing you the state of the TRIX on M5 &amp; M15. On an M15 chart you would be set up to look at M30 &amp; M60 etc. Hope this helps - if I am wrong, please someone give me a shout. Happy trading

Welcome Bladerunner THV3 Multiple Time Frame (MTF) Rules Coded by Miss Pips, a big applause to her for all the time and efforts in this project. Edited by TradeWell, Cobraforex and the THV Team Regular Trades: 1) Trade when you get 6 green or 6 red lights total out of all Trix histograms. 2) Two of the lights have to be in the first two rows (m1 and m5) 2a) Trade direction must be away from the Coral – basically, only go long above, and short below. 3) Take the trade as soon as PA touches below/above the Cloud (don't wait for a close below or above) 4) Don’t trade when you see divergence in the opposite direction. Divergence not only gets you into good trades earlier, it also keeps you out of bad ones. Exit at 10 pips profit and use a 15 pip SL (or ATR, whichever is larger). My addition: I like to wait for the Trix to cross BEFORE I take the entry. The suggested setup uses 1m fast, 5m fast, 5m slow, 15m fast, 15m slow, 30m fast, 30 m slow and 60 m fast Trix histograms, and the Ichimoku histogram (Cloud Historgram) uses the 5 m and 15m clouds. It has been tested for use on the M1, EURUSD chart. Other currency pairs and TF's may require adjustments to these rules.

--- 帖子 #9633 ---
SpecialEd answered your other questions, So I'll answer this one. What you saw in your chart(10 red lamps) before you switched to other TF's is based on real time data. However after you came back from other TF's, the trix histo recalculates the previous lamps based on existing data so you see it different. Say, on 5M - 10 red lamps - this is based on real time data, or say what is happening at the moment switch chart to other tf switch chart back to 5M - now you dont have real time data only historical data, say what happend earlier. ( now you may see only 8 red lamps and first 2 gone green). Hope this helps, I'm sure MissPips has explained this clearly in earlier pages, I just couldnt find it now. Karun

--- 帖子 #9659 ---
It's good to wait until you have the lights and then a fresh cross of the Trix. See green line I drew. Beaware of continuation runs on the Trix. Sometimes they cross, both are green, and then the fast trix will turn red. then a few minutes later, it will turn green again. If you re-enter when it changes green, you can sometimes get pichned. A great example of this (but going short) is at 11:26 am PST on the 1 minute. All of my lights were red for about 2 minutes, then changed and the trade would have killed me. If I had taken it on the chnage of the trix - both red - but without the fresh cross - well - I would have lost and been stopped out. Your red line is an example of this, but in this case, it happened to work out for you I assume.

--- 帖子 #9681 ---
OK, understand the question now. I use two charts per pair being M5 and M15 on two 21" screens. Maximum open charts is eight (4 pairs) plus two analysis charts. I only use Metatrader for charting, not for placing orders, so I have another screen just for my broker software ( Oanda ). When I have taken a position I have a nice little window showing me the current price, my SL and TP and my current position in pips. If I have taken a position on say three pairs I just have three windows next to each other. I then watch the pips indicator which tells me the position. When it starts to get near TP or SL or a support / resistance area I bring up the full charts on the other screens to decide what action to take. I try not to constantly watch PA as this sometimes makes me question my original decision. Takes a little practice but I do have a reasonable idea of which way PA will go when I take the trade and the distance in pips for support / resistance. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #9695 ---
Hey Forexample, Has been a while since I last posted here. Like to add my 2 cents worth here. Looking at trend on a chart is something very visual and easy. Don't blindly believe that the trend is your friend. The key is in analyzing where Price Action (PA) will be in the next few hours if you are trading intraday. I have attached 3 charts here for illustration. They are H4 EU charts. I shaded the 2 areas where if you follow the major down trend on H4, there will be few if not no trade setup possible on the M5 for those 2 areas. Key is not just know and follow major trend but analyze using tools like Fibo or Pitchfork and decide how you want to trade them. On the charts, I have 2 Fibos and a pitchfork as examples. You can see bounces reaching 38.2% on 1st Fibo and 61.8% on 2nd Fibo as well as meridian lines of the pitchfork. If fact, the 2nd Fibo confirms the first bounce on 50% too. With this analysis or more on H1 or M30, you can move on to let's say M5 and trade knowingly or wait for a nice setup to be in with the major trend at end of those 2 bounces, both using THV for setups. Hope I make sense here. The above would have been classic trades with basic Fibo and Pitchfork analysis. For me, when I do trade, I trade both directions with analysis on the H4 and M30 chart. --- 帖子 #9733 ---
Hi windelevel, Tradewell is right. All you need is 6 points, and PA breaking the coral and cloud in the direction of the trade, on the timeframe you are trading. See attached pic. About the other divergence, this is something that is not in the manual because we wanted to keep it short, but the members of the THV team can confirm that I posted it on my screenshots during the month we forwared tested it: There are two times I don't trade when I see divergence: 1) I don't like flat divergence. If I am going to trade around it (which is risky) I want it to look convincing. That is, I want to see PA clearly going up and the Trix clearly going down (or vice versa). Flat is too wishywashy for me, because divergence trades are riskier anyway. 2) I don't like when you have divergence in one direction, immediately followed by divergence in the other. To me, that says the market is choppy and I just stay out until it makes some kind of statement (like for example, crashing through a pivot or strong support.) Sorry that that wasn't in the manual but we had some discussion and decided it was better to keep it short because there are millions of nuances that every trader has.

--- 帖子 #9737 ---
Hi Jhartteam, Yes to the first (must have 1m f and 5m f) No to the second. PA should break the cloud and coral in the direction of the trade, except if it's a divergence trade. In that case (divergence trade), it only has to break the cloud (but not the coral) in the direction of the trade. The reason for this is that I tried to stick as much as possible to the original THV rules, which called for PA to break the cloud and coral. I know that some of the experienced scalpers only waited for it to break the cloud though, so that's why I adopted that in the case of divergence, because in the case of divergence if you wait for PA to break the cloud and the coral, by that time the divergence may have alreadly played out, especially on the lower tfs.

--- 帖子 #9780 ---
Hi Rob, For the MTF setup, I tried not to change too many of the original rules of THV. The only thingsI changed are that I made some specific rules for divergence plays, and also I don't require a trix cross or the 1m s in the direction of the trade if you have 6 green lights. My reason for this is because if you have 6 green lights you are really trading in the direction of the main trend and a change in 1m f is usually enough to pull PA back in that direction. (But if you want to trade more conservatively, you can still wait for a trix cross and the m1 s, even when you have 6 green lights.) Regarding shorting only when the Coral is red - I think that is an old rule that was eliminated even before the MTF indicators arrived on the scene. You should still wait for PA to break the cloud and the coral in the direction of the trade though, except for divergence trades, in which case you may ignore the coral. I don't know about the 288 ma - maybe someone else can answer.

--- 帖子 #9795 ---
Speaking for myself, when I said I monitor the 5-min time frame and then move to the 1-min time frame simply means that I look for possible pattern occurrence on the 5-min; to filter out the noise of the 1-min. I did look at that juncture of your chart. I was looking at 5-min for potential 'double top' or a-b-c corrective; then I immediately switch to 1-min to see if there was any divergence play or refined pattern for me to work on. I simply took the 1-min signal for the shorts. Whereas, in your case, you are looking for confirmation on the 5-min and switched to 1-min; which logically the 1-min signal would've been passed long ago already. Filtering with the 5M is very different from Confirming with the 5-min Have a good one Jeff

--- 帖子 #9796 ---
Hi Proverbs. Welcome to the thread. I'm not using 1m anymore as my maximizer tf. Rather to pick 15m as an entry decision and 3m for maximizing. But the rule is just the same IMO. If you work on 5m and 1m TF, the short/ long decision should be made by higher tf (5m). So it means you have to pay attention with 5m first and then use 1m for maximizing your trade. Talk about maximizing, it does not always mean both trix just begin to get red on 1m. In your attachment, both vertical line (aqua and purple) seems a valid entry to me. If you like a bit risky trade and tighter SL, you may choose the aqua line as both 1m trix is begin to red and fast trix on 5m is also red (but still slower trix is not red yet). The purple line is more conservative entry since you have to wait both trix on 5m are red but it is ok and many times will filter you from a false signal. One most important thing is you have to wait higher tf to give you a valid entry signal before go short/long. Taking a trade with just 1m tf and hoping 5m will get red just make you a jumping gun trader. You will lose in the long run. Be patient. Just my opinion though.

Here is an indie that keeps the setting. Also you can toggle it from regular candles to HA candles to by setting regular to true or false, without all the extra clicking you normally have to do when you add/remove HA candles. Just set the chart to linegraph and the linegraph color to none in the chart properties. Then add the indie and toggle regular from true to false to see HA candles or vice versa.

Basically I just ran out of buffers and I had to choose between the two M1 trixes or the 60. I choose M1f and 60 because, as someone pointed out earlier, it isn't wise to ignore the trend on the hourly. I chose the m1 f because it leads, and if you have the trix in your favor in enough other tfs it usually is enough to turn PA back in the direction of most of the lights. I have to say though, that I don't ignore the m1 s. For a short, if it is green and flat or going flat, and all other conditions say go, I'll take it. If it is green and strongly angled up, I'll wait a bit and see if I can get an entry where it is at least flat and preferably red. This also depends on the trading condtions at the time. If PA just strongly rejected some support, and m1 s is green and strongly angled up, I'd leave it alone.

--- 帖子 #9861 ---
[quote=pattinatore;2687017] Clarification: This is not [repeat] not a trading EA [robot]. All trading robots are EA's but not all EA's are necessarily "robots". This will not trade for you. It will not place a trade for you. All it does is when you enter a TP value and SL value, when you place an instant execution trade, the robot goes to work, so there's no thought process to your trade. If you set SL to 15 like THV suggests, it will do that for you. If you have TP of 10 [like THV suggests] then it will close the trade out at 10 pips --even if it could have been better. This is designed to help keep your focus, to have guaranteed pips [in case the Greed Moster sets and you think there'll be more and more, and then there's none], or in case you believe you have a shady broker who'll spike prices on you, or to minimize losses, so you don't go chasing lost pips by staying in a bad trade that you think has the potential to turn around.

--- 帖子 #9877 ---
MT4 comes packaged with the custom indicator called "Ichimoku", which displays a non-solid cloud made up of vertical lines and border lines. As with all the custom indicators, it is of the .mq4 format allowing access to the code. However, tucked away in the ordinary indicator list is the "Ichimoku Kinko Hyo" which accomplishes the solid cloud display. Unfortunately the indicators on that list are not of the .mq4 version allowing access to the code. Perhaps someday someone will be able to provide that hidden code. --- 帖子 #9905 ---
Hi atton. Welcome to the thread . It depends on your risk profile. Entering a trade when fast trix change color but not cross yet will give you smaller SL but a bit risky since it is not confirmed yet the trend has been established. On contrary, entering on both trix crossing will give you "more certain" trend but it takes bigger SL and also smaller profit. Most of my trade is based on 15m TF and I use only fast trix color change to execute my plan since 15m will need larg SL if you can't manage it well. Note also closer fast and slow trix distance each other will give you better result when entering your trade. It's all my opinion as a user here. Btw, you can use those Attachment button on the editor to attach image rather than using imageshack.

Not having your SL on the server does not do much except raise risks in case of power failure, internet/computer outage etc. The big boys are still going to move the PA that will take out the stops even if the SL are not visible on the server. So hiding it does not buy you anything.

--- 帖子 #9918 ---
No, this is actually the same code as the "Ichimoku" Custom Indicator.mq4 in MT4. This one, with max width settings required to attempt to color fill the "cloud", comes out thicker than the std. indy, and with tiny open spots here and there. There is definately a difference between the two, so far as the coding for the "cloud". The std. indy, which is not in .mq4 format, is far, far better. One thing though, in favor of the .mq4 Custom indy.....it does not interfere with the tri-color Coral! Interesting! There is definately a difference between them. So, maybe someday, someone will post that indy's code here. Meanwhile, if you don't mind the Custom Indy cloud being slightly thicker and with occassional very small spot holes, then here is Ichimoku Cloud.mq4. It is modified from the MT4 Custom Indy code. You can leave the Colors tab alone because everything....color and widths is entered on the Inputs tab, and only ONCE does it. No longer do you have to change the color and widths four times to get the job done, as with the Custom indy. Also, it has an "On/Off" switch. So, if for some reason you want the "clouds" to just up and blow away for a while, you can turn the indy off. Furthermore, width entries can exceed the normal limit of "5", so you can experiment with using larger numbers on smaller TF charts if you are fanatical about plugging holes.........

This indy shows volume bars in different colors based on their percentage of the average bar for the volume averaging period. You can vary the height so as to place this indy in an existing window with the volume histogram shrunken towards the bottom border of the window. You can color just the graduations you want to. You can display just the bars you want to based on their graduation and omit the rest! All this and................. The text to the side displays REAL TIME the percentage of current volume bar relative to the average bar for the selected averaging period! As the bar grows in height, the percentage figure changes in real time. As the bar volume transitions from one graduation/color to another, the text changes color too! Believe me, when the big guys start pouring in the volume, this little baby's volumeometer races like a rocket going downhill! FUN, FUN, FUN! I have attached screenshots to show how this indy can be in its' own window and color coding all four graduations, and how it can co-exist with another indy and show only a couple of color coded graduations, how you can show just the graduations you want to, and how to really shrink it. --- 帖子 #9939 ---
Yes, there are problems associated with 'stacking' indicators on top of each other in a secondary window and indeed the order in which the indicators load can make a big difference. You can easily change the order of the indicators by editing the template file, which is just plain text. If you do it this way you do not have to delete all the indicators and start again - particularly useful if you have already made a lot of colour changes or set up alerts in your indicators and now want to add something to the top of the heap. If you have never done any coding, maybe best to ignore this post. If this is too off topic, someone shout and I will delete.

--- 帖子 #9945 ---
Hi Trader, When you have your MetaTrader set-up as you want it, just save the template to your desktop (for instance) by right clicking on the chart then &gt;template &gt;save template. The resulting file is in plain text but with the .tpl extension - it can be opened by any plain text editor. The structure is quite easy to follow, a bit like HTML as here: &lt;chart&gt; &lt;indicator&gt; &lt;window&gt; YOUR DATA &lt;/indicator&gt; &lt;/window&gt; &lt;/chart&gt; You can copy/paste a whole indicator section, complete with it's own settings and preferences and move it to a different location in the template file, then re-save under a different name and re-load to see the changes. The only change I make is in the variable window_num= If I am moving an indicator to the top of the stack so that it will load first, I change this to window_num=0. May not even be necessary. Hope this is useful - best of luck

--- 帖子 #9947 ---
All data belonging to an indicator sits between &lt;indicator&gt; and &lt;/indicator&gt; Here is your latest indi from a template which I am playing with: &lt;indicator&gt; name=Custom Indicator &lt;expert&gt; name=Volumes Emphasized flags=275 window_num=1 &lt;inputs&gt; VolumePeriod=10 Numbers_shrink_bars_in_display=2=1/2, 3=1/3, 4=1/4, 5=1/5, etc Enter_ShrinkNumber=12.00000000 Need_2_numbers_dividing_range=0-100 into 3 parts (33&amp;66, 25&amp;50 etc) Enter_Number_1=38.20000000 Enter_Number_2=61.80000000 Display_volume_percentages_text=1 BelowAverageTextColor_0=255 AboveAverageTextColor_1=65535 AboveAverageTextColor_2=3329330 AboveAverageTextColor_3=15570276 AboveAverageTextColor_4=13850042 Text_in_window_0123=0 Text_in_corner_0123=3 __Text_Horizontal_Indent=5 __Text_Vertical_Indent=275 &lt;/inputs&gt; &lt;/expert&gt; shift_0=0 draw_0=0 color_0=-1 style_0=0 weight_0=1 shift_1=0 draw_1=2 color_1=-1 style_1=0 weight_1=1 shift_2=0 draw_2=2 color_2=9125192 style_2=0 weight_2=1 shift_3=0 draw_3=2 color_3=55295 style_3=0 weight_3=2 shift_4=0 draw_4=2 color_4=3329330 style_4=0 weight_4=2 shift_5=0 draw_5=2 color_5=15570276 style_5=0 weight_5=2 shift_6=0 draw_6=2 color_6=13850042 style_6=0 weight_6=2 period_flags=0 show_data=1 &lt;/indicator&gt; If I now change one of the params in this indi file, like shrink number, it will change the indicator next time it is loaded. Similarly moving the whole lot to the first position in the list will mean this indi loads first and others will be drawn on top of it. Apologises to anyone who thinks this is well off-topic - maybe it helps someone?

Thanks for your efforts Miss Pips and T@H Volumes Emphasized: First off, my expression of grateful thanks to MissPips for adding the crown of glory to this effort....the real-time update of the current volume bar percentage indicator. Enhancements are added to the core coding of the copyright indicator to enable the normal volume histogram to be seen along with volume graduations generated by the core code. The histogram can be resized down in the display window (shrink it) so that this indicator can co-exist with another in the same window, yet occupy only the lower regions of the window. The ShrinkNumber "1" sets a normal sized display. Using "2" cuts the display height in half, "3" into a third, "4" into a fourth, etc. The graduation bars display as their normal height within the histogram. They can be emphasized with different colors and by varying their width from the normal bars they overlay. You can alter the graduations. Originally they were bars below average, 0-38.2% avg., 38.2%-61.8% avg., 61.8%-100% avg., and over 100% avg. The below average bars are now just part of the normal histogram. But the range from 0%-100% can be graduated differently by the user. Instead of using 38.2 and 61.8 to divide that range into three parts, you could use 33.33 and 66.66, or 25 and 50, etc. This is useful if you want to NOT show so many different colors bars, maybe showing only those between 50-100 and over 100. By selecting 25, 50 and then coloring the 0-25 and 25-50 the same as the normal bars, you will reduce the display of colored bars to just those in the 50-100 and the 100+ graduations. You can eliminate the display of selected graduations by setting their width and color to the same as the normal histogram. You can eliminate the display of the normal histogram and selected graduations by coloring them "CLR_NONE", of if this does not work satisfactorily, color them the same as the chart background color. This will cause only the remaining graduated colored bars to be shown. The Color tab of the Indicator's Properties Window allows you to set the color and width of the normal histogram, of the three graduations between 0-100, and the 100+ graduation. In addition to these, the first two items on the list are for the zero line (normally not used) and an extra, "Phantom" normal histogram. It is required to maintain the indicator window height when the display is "shrunken" within the window of another indicator. This item should always be made invisible using "CLR_NONE" as the color choice. If this does not work, then it should be colored the same color as the chart background. - Traderathome

--- 帖子 #9985 ---
Ignore the choice of colors.....use whatever colors you want. They have no specific meaning other than to distinguish one from the others. You have 6 color catagories. 1-invisible, used for items1 &amp; 2 in the color tab. Item one is the zero line and you don't need it. Item 2 is the very important Phantom volume display necessary to maintain window height when the indy coexits in same window as another indy, but is shrunk in size. You never want to see this full size Phantom volume display. Catagory 2- the normal volume display, any color you want. And this is the color you can make any of the graduations if you do not want to see them. Catagory 3-4-5-6 are the graduations, and again, any color you want. The boundaries for three of the four graduations are your choice, and the fourth is fixed at volumes 100+% of average. You can split the 0% to 100% of average into any three sizes you want to by what two numbers you input in the properties window. For example, if you input 30 and 70 then you have split it into 0 to 30, 30 to 70, and 70 to 100. It is all really very simple. You just have to think on it a while....at least I did. If you want the text color to match the four colors for the graduation, then make those choices in the Inputs tab the same as you chose in the Colors tab.

With normal volume display...... You see an upwards tall candle, and you see higher volume to go with it. Conclusion? Lots of buying, right? You see a downwards tall candle, and you see higher volume to go with it. Conclusion? Lots of selling, right? But, in the first case, suppose you could see the price spike up, and the volume percentage still is below average. And then you see the price fluctuate around the highs of the candle, and the volume start to pour on! What would your conclusion be then? And in the second case, suppose you could see the price spike down, and the volume percentage still is below average. And then you see the price fluctuate around the lows of the candle, and the volume start to pour on! What would your conclusion be then? The Volumes Emphasized Indicator can help you better see what is really happening when the market movers are at work. I hope this helps those that have PM'd me asking about how to use it. Aside from that, it can give you something new to watch while trading, to help fend off bordom! (just kidding)

--- 帖子 #10013 ---
It could be fixed but fixing it would give you less information. What happens is that the histo shows you what the trix is doing in a higher tf - minute by minute. For example, if you are watching the 15m trix on a 1 m chart it might be red for the first 5 bars, green for 6 bars and then red for 4 bars. At the end of the 15 minutes let's say the trix closed down and red. If you add another instance of the indie you will see that all those 15 bars are red. This is because if you add (or initialize) the trix histo after a bar has closed, it has no idea what happend in 'real time' with that bar. The way to fix this 'repainting' would be not to show you the real time info, and only show you the closed info 15 bars back. That would, IMHO, sort of defeat the purpose of the trix histo, which is to show you what is actually happening in tf you are looking at on the higher tf chart. If you want to know what the trix did 15 minutes ago while you are trading a 1 m chart, you might as well just flip over there and have a look at it yourself. In addition, the trix itself sometimes repaints one bar back after that bar has already closed. The trix histo does not do this (unless you initialize it), and therefore its 'real time' data is a more accurate representation of what actually happend during those minutes. This provides some valuable info - for example it is useful to know whether a fifteen mnute red trix bar was down all the time or had quite a bit of wavering in there.

--- 帖子 #10137 ---
The mtf indies, as mentioned before, 'repaint' (loose the real-time data) when initialized. So, one possible explanation is that you opened the metatrader instances at different times. For the real time info to be the same, they would have to be opened at the same time. Also if the metatrader disconnects and reconnects that initializes the indicator. So if one of the instances was disconnected and reconnected, that one would have the 'repainted' data, while the other would have the real time data.

--- 帖子 #10138 ---
Hi Wlfx Here are my thoughts: That was a divergence trade because you took it when PA is below the the cloud but not below the Coral. (The Coral is still the filter for the main trend, except for divergence trades.) Divergence trades are, by definition, more risky (i.e. more of them fail). They are less risky when : 1) PA is overextended 2) PA is bouncing off something sturdy like a daily pivot, and 3) PA drops below the cloud right after the peak is formed. (I myself don't take them when it takes PA more than 3 bars after the peak is formed to drop below the cloud). They are more risky when : 1) You have several consecutive conflicting divergences 2) PA takes more than three bars from the high of the peak to drop below the cloud (because divergence might not last longer than 5-8 bars.) 3) PA is not overextended (i.e the Trix is not in the oversold area, and there is not a nice distance between PA and the Coral.) In this case, I don't see anything in particular that PA was bouncing off of. PA is not overextended because the trix is not in the o/s area and PA is relatively close to the coral. PA took more than 3 bars from the peak to fall below the cloud, and on the previous low you had a long divergence, which conflicts with the idea of taking a short, and implies that you are in a choppy area and should wait for something decisive to happen.

--- 帖子 #10176 ---
That is a nice channel! Here is my problem with all things like channels, fibs, reverse engineered fibs, pivots, camarilla lines MAs etc. (not that I don't use them, my analysis charts are full of them. ) BUT: we can observe that PA moves in waves. I have observed that when PA starts moving it won't stop until it hits something (like a pivot or a major MA for example). When it hits a barrier it usually bounces off of it especially if it's a well known barrier, and PA is hitting it for the first time (like when it hits the pivot for the first time in a day). If it's in a downtrend it goes up for a while, and then it usually goes back down and retests whatever it bounced off of. If the downtrend is going to continue, PA will eventually break whatever was causing it to stop, and continue in the direction of the trend. Until the end of the trend, of course. Logically this has to be the case, otherwise if PA as in between two barriers and it always bounced off of them it would never move very far. The main questions are: where are the important barriers, and how do we know if PA will break the one it is next approaching or bounce off of it. Of course it's good to know where the barriers are so we don't take a trade right in front of one with no room for PA to move. BUT, since everybody has their own method (some like fibs, some like pivots, some like support/resistance, some like channels, some like patterns, and everybody draws them differently) I have come to the conclusion that it is impossible to identify them all. Furthermore, even if we could identify all possible barriers, we still would not know if PA was going to bounce or break. That is why I like divergence in momentum indicators so much. To me, momentum indicators are like using a geiger counter to locate a hidden radioactive object. Even if we can't see the object, when the geiger counter starts ticking we know it's there. When we see PA moving in one direction and momentum moving in the other, we know that there is a barrier there, even if we haven't managed to identify what it is. (If you look in your chart, just before PA is about to hit the bottom of the channel there is divergence.) That is why I recomment paying a lot of attention to divergence and not trading against it. When you see divergence there is usually some obstacle in the way of PA, even if you haven't figured out what it is. If we see PA hitting a known barrier and we also see a lot of divergence - even better. Then we have a safer trade.

--- 帖子 #10183 ---
I don't know what the trend indicator is. Re the trix and cloud histo, they call the trix and Ichimoku (respectively) for each tf specified. In the case of the trix histo, if the trix is red for that tf , the light is red for that row and if the trix is green the light for that row is green. In the case of the cloud histo, if PA is below the cloud the light is red, if PA is above the cloud, green , and if PA is in the cloud the light is yellow for that tf.

Hello all, I don't post much but have been checking out THV on longer timeframes over the past couple of weeks. My theory was (1) if one has the patience to let a trade run, there are more PIPs to be earned with safer trades on the longer TFs; and (2) THV will probably work on any TF. So far, I've proven both parts of the theory to my own satisfaction, but invite anyone to try it out for yourself. My rules for entry: 1. At least 4 out of these 5 lights (M15F, M15S, M30F, M30S, H1F) must be red for short and green for long. 2. M30 and H1 Cloud histo's must be red for short, or green for long. M30 can be yellow but should never be opposing color. It is a much better trade when both are the same color. I never trade with H1 cloud light opposing color. Rules for exit: 1. Don't be greedy. Decide how many PIPs you conservatively want to earn and TP in front of some pivot or psych. 2. TP/exit when M30F light changes colors at the close of a 30M candle. 3. Set your SL according to either the ATR or 40-50 PIPs, according to your risk appetite. Be sure to check H1 analysis chart to help confirm the trend. Always best to go with the trend. This approach is simply a longer-term version of what MissPIPs taught us with M5/M1. I like it because I'm not seeing so much "noise" and staying so darned nervous about M1/M5 price action. Be sure to backtest and forward test this approach on demo account before going live. Chart attached so that you can see my set-up, plus a picture of a good short trade earlier today. Sorry, I did not mark up the chart, but you can see it!

Continuing on with the M15 and higher discussion, here are some techniques I like to use. But first a disclaimer: (( DO NOT use any of these suggestions without doing your homework and testing; make any strategy "your own" first before trading it. Also, please don't ask me any newbie-style questions that can be answered by doing a little research here at FF or on the web with Google. Don't ask about stop losses, profit targets, money and risk management, fibs, S &amp; R levels, average pip gain, trend lines, HA candles, MAs, MT4 features, profits, divergence, how to boot your computer, clean the monitor screen or any other rookie topics. If that request offends you, stop reading right here and DON'T look at my charts. )) THV is trend trading. Earlier in this thread someone explained trends within trends (small waves or cycles within larger waves or cycles). We want to identify the larger ones and then wait for the smaller ones to align with these before we consider entering a trade. We will ride the smaller waves in the same direction as the larger ones (surf analogies are ingrained with me). Chart #1 is H1 with 2 EMAs and 2 NLMAs (I'll attach the NLMA indi) 21 EMA (gold), 89 EMA (red), NLMA 13 on open, NLMA 13 on close Look at the chart: the 89 EMA shows the larger trend while the 21 EMA shows the immediate PA as the price moves along this MA. On the left of the chart is a period of ranging; difficult but not impossible to trade for smaller gains. Farther to the right is a nice down trend followed by a great up trend. Study the MAs to get a feel for PA and trend. I refer to the area between the MAs as "no-man's-land"; dangerous territory to trade. It's usually better to wait for the price to move outside this area. On this H1 chart I'm watching for the fast Trix to change color signalling a possible trend change and I would like the HA candle to close outside the cloud. Yellow verticle lines show potential trade signals that are not the best because price is moving towards the MA; be very careful !!! White verticle lines show good potential trade signals. The fifth verticle white line from the left is drawn where the price moves up out of the "no-man's-land" AND the slow Trix line is green. This is a good signal even though the fast Trix is red (it's red because of the small preceeding price pull-back). You could wait till the next white verticle line for a safer signal. The signal is confirmed when the H1 candle closes AND the fast Trix has changed color. Now it's time to go to the M15 and see if we have an entry signal. We'll do that in the next post.

Ca$h...it's just the basic ABC pattern. If your pick A is a high and pick B is a low (pick C lower high than A) then the AL's are going to slope downward...if pick B is higher than pick A the formation will slope upwards. Don't be timid about moving the original picks, i.e. drag pick A to a close or to a bar that was the *real* start of the move. Takes a bit of practice but when you get it right you won't have to ask anyone, you will be able to see the ML testing.

--- 帖子 #10316 ---
MissPips is the author and has addressed that several times. Most all the questions can be answered by reading ALL the Posts by the authors. It could be fixed but fixing it would give you less information. What happens is that the histo shows you what the trix is doing in a higher tf - minute by minute. For example, if you are watching the 15m trix on a 1 m chart it might be red for the first 5 bars, green for 6 bars and then red for 4 bars. At the end of the 15 minutes let's say the trix closed down and red. If you add another instance of the indie you will see that all those 15 bars are red. This is because if you add (or initialize) the trix histo after a bar has closed, it has no idea what happend in 'real time' with that bar. The way to fix this 'repainting' would be not to show you the real time info, and only show you the closed info 15 bars back. That would, IMHO, sort of defeat the purpose of the trix histo, which is to show you what is actually happening in tf you are looking at on the higher tf chart. If you want to know what the trix did 15 minutes ago while you are trading a 1 m chart, you might as well just flip over there and have a look at it yourself. In addition, the trix itself sometimes repaints one bar back after that bar has already closed. The trix histo does not do this (unless you initialize it), and therefore its 'real time' data is a more accurate representation of what actually happend during those minutes. This provides some valuable info - for example it is useful to know whether a fifteen mnute red trix bar was down all the time or had quite a bit of wavering in there.

--- 帖子 #10347 ---
All, I have been trading higher time frames and have found a setup that happens over and over again that is working well for me after much DEMO testing that I wanted to share as part of my give back to this great community. Note: I find these rules work on any time frame. The entry rules I am following don't have to happen in any specific order: Entry: 1. Fast TRIX steady color or closed color change in trade direction. 2. Stoch (9,3,3) closed cross in same trade direction. (works better if coming out of overbought or oversold) 3. 4 EMA and 7 EMA closed cross in same trade direction. Note: The closer all three of these happening at the same time, the stronger the move will be. Exit: I move to break even once in a comfortable GREEN pip territory. (your risk level may very) Then I manually trail a stop loss on the high of the previous Heikin-Ashi candle. If the previous candle is an inside bar then i ignore it and wait for the next candle to form. Note: I am using a variation of the 3 bar reversal method for my exit but since the HA candles are longer than a normal candle I find the previous HA candle seems to work just fine unless there is a retracement before I move to break even. This is why I actively manage my trades and manually move my stops Enjoy! The attached picture is a trade I took earlier this evening using these rules.

--- 帖子 #10352 ---
I still use exactly the same rules as before and I count only points generated by the 1 m chart. I don't take all the trades that the 6 points setups give. You can get about 15 to 20 of these setups or more a day depending on how long you trade, and I am only shooting for 20 real pips a day, though I am logging all of the setups. while I am trading. So I am looking for only the best setups for my live trades and what I use these divergences on the higher tf for is confirmation of the best setups or rejection of the dubious ones. For example, if I see positive divergence on the 5 or 15 min followed by a positive divergence on the 1 min, I'll be more inclined to take that trade. If, on the other hand, I see negative divergence on a higher tf, and a long trade signal on the 1m I won't take that trade. Also if I see conflicting divergences, like positive on the 15 and negative on the 5, I'll just stand aside. Or even worse, positive on the 15, negative on the 5 and then positive and negative on the 1. Then I'll stay out for a while for sure. You get so many opportunities to enter that there's no reason to take any but the best ones, in my opinion (best meaning I don't want to see anything fishy looking at all.) I do encourage you to actually go over to the other tf and have a look when you see divergence on this indie, because as we know, the trix doesn't always get it right. You still need to confirm for yourself that you can see the divergence.

Attached is a little indicator I have used for many years. Just kinda handy to convert time on the chart to local time. It displays at bottom of chart, is vertical so as to be more exact, and only shows in yellow color (as far as I have ever used). Default time is 4 (hours from data feed). You can set to whatever time in your local from data feed time. Mine is set to "8", as this is number of hours from data feed time to my local time (CST). Just saves having to mentally adjust time from data feed time to local time.

--- 帖子 #10395 ---
Originally Posted by robmanz http://www.forexfactory.com/images/buttons/viewpost.gif Hi There, Does anyone know how to move the text that appear on the right of the trix indicator (Price, analyze, trend, thv) on the left side? Or is there the same indicator without any description? If I keep 4 chart on a screen the description cover the indicator. Thanks Rob Did you get an answer? If not here is how to move thoses labels ... In each THV indicator, the Inputs tab, look for something like "Show_in_chart_window_0123" this controls which window the label appears 0 for the main chart 1 for the indicators chart, 2 for the next indicator (section) down and so forth. Also in the indicator, look for "Show_in_window_corner_0123" 0 is usually Upper left, 1 Upper right, 2 is lower left and 3 is lower right(of the window or chart section you choose from previous attribute) Some Labels can not be moved. You might want to try changing font values in the indicators and then using the chart shift option in the (&lt;right-click&gt;) properties of the charts common tab. you then can use the little triangle in the top right of the main chart to resize the shift to whatever size you want. When you have moved the labels you want to move remember to save as a new template. That way you can always restore the original if you would like to. --good luck

Note the volume near the highs of the range, and the volume as the PA now drops. This display of increased relative volume at highs, to me, indicates shorting at the highs. The increased volume as the PA now drops, to me, means more are jumping on board to short before PA drops more. When we have high relative volume at the lows, to me, it means the prof. traders are supporting it then. They might do this even if they are taking on short positions, in order to hold up and then rebuild the price for more shorting....they don't want it to get too low until they are finished taking on their short positions, and they have to spread that effort out over a lot of time in order to not force the PA down prematurely. If it does drop too low, then they jump in and support it, but maybe only temporarily until they get the rest of their shorts filled.

--- 帖子 #10460 ---
Well, I don't really like to comment about a currency I don't trade, but I will make a few observations. The first one is that sometimes I do enter a trade before a bar is closed, but I'll usually wait till the last 20 seconds. I consider that pretty safe on the Euro because it's like a steamroller - once it gets going in the direction of the trend, it's hard to stop. However, in this case, even on the Euro, I wouldn't have done that, because PA has been below the Coral until where you entered. That means the trend was down, and on the Euro, at least, the trend has a tendency to persist. Therefore, I would have expected some resistance at the Coral. Also, like Cobra mentioned, if I see a giant bar, I either won't take it or will wait for a few bars of retrace and for one of the retrace bars to get broken. The last observation is that Miss Pips is very ecumenical, if you'll pardon the expression. If anybody is on vacation, I'm on vacation too. (Japanese, Brits, French, Germans, Christians, Buddhists, Wiccans, Socialists of the World - you name it and as long as they are Forex traders I observe their holiday ) I also don't trade real pips for two hours before or after a major interest rate statement. If that means I have to sit on my hands for a whole week (like this week) so be it. That is because my feeling is that a trading strategy which is based on momentum andon observations made during conditions of normal liquidity should not be used under different conditions. That's just me though - I know a lot of other people don't follow that.

Hello Friends, I'm working on top of a SL / TP and MM that I present here for you, and I would like to know the opinion of all. (Before continuing, sorry for my bad English ... For help in understanding, will use pictures to demonstrate understanding of all the best.) Well, let's go! In this rule all we use is basically on top of percentages. As an example, we use an account balance of $1.000 U.S. dollars. In time to make a trader, I use the following rules: - SL = 3% of the account balance - TP = 2% of the account balance In practice, when is a signal for an entry, you must identify how you will use the Pips SL, to set the size of the Lot you will use in that order, which will amount to 3% of the account balance. For example, the system THV of an input signal where I use the 20 pip SL, so I use 3% of SL in my account of $ 1,000 ... To make that account using the following equation: ($ 1,000 * 3% / 20pip / 10 = 0.15 Lot) ... So for this trader of 20pip of SL we use Lot 0.15 Now that I set the SL and the Lot, we must define how we will use the Pips TP, so that the trader has 2% of TP ... For this we use the following equation: (SL * 67% = TP) &gt;&gt;&gt; (20pip * 67% = 13.4 Pip) ... Then we use the 13.4 pip TP ... If your broker has not fractionated pips, you should round off your TP for 13pip or 14pip ... In short, the higher your SL, the greater should be the TP, always following the rule of: SL3% / TP2% ... Below a picture as an example: Attached Image (click to enlarge) I particularly mount in an Excel formula where I got it for only the SL and the account balance, which makes the already calculated for me the TP and the size of the Lot ... That takes the hassle out of the trader Attached Image I hope that somehow this topic might help someone ... I would also like to know the opinion of all. Thank you and good for all the weekend EDIT: If you think that SL of 3% is high or low, you can set the MM to a value that you feel more comfortable ... Example: SL 1% and TP 0.66% ..... SL 5% and TP 3.3%... etc. The TP will always be 67% of the value of SL.

--- 帖子 #10484 ---
The order of the histo's are user preference: I have my charts setup: Four fast histo's in the upper window Four slow histo's in the window below This works for my gray matter and allows me to concentrate and focus on the PA. The histo's start with the lowest time frame on top and progress downward to the largest time frame. First window all red/green I know that all the fast trix time frames are in agreement or perhpas just the top three are the same color...tells me that at least three time frames are in agreement about direction. Course at that point usually one or two of the slow histo's are the same color as well. Just less thought involved on my part while watching the PA...if PA looks right, I glance down at the histo's, and a decission can quickly be made to open (or not) a position. Back to the user prefernce...this works for me, perhaps you may want to set it up differently...make it your own style .

--- 帖子 #10525 ---
Hi Traderathome, The mtf indies call a special version of the trix (which has alerts and labels turned off insofar as possible.) Because the trix has so many external input params, I found it impossible to call it using iCustom other than with the defaults. I wasn't able, for example, to call it and allow you to change the number of bars it used, because the entire iCustom call was rejected whenever I didn't use the defaults. The default is 750 bars for that version, like in the regular trix. Changing the input bars on the regular trix will not affect the mtf indies at all.

--- 帖子 #10606 ---
Hi Tracom, A picture says a thousand words. Post those trades that failed and indicate on the chart where you entered those trades. The veterans here will be more than willing to analyze your charts and advise you. Pivots are support and resistance lines. You need to be aware that price hesitates before any move around them. Fibo is a great tool for your higher TF analysis to know where price is going next. You will also need to draw trend lines and S/R levels. The minimum analysis you need to do on the higher TF is to have a trendline and S/R levels to have a feel of where price will go or react next. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #10666 ---
I don't play by the SL~TP THV values... When I open a position I usually have a size with an emergency stop at 25 or 30p's on everything. Keep in mind that this stop is for emergency only...unexpected news flash, power failure, yada, yada...my finger is always on the exit button. Then I manage my stops and exits...depending on how the market is moving, by only trading one pair you get a better feel for this. If PA is moving quickly I will go for 20 or 25p's for first off, normaly 25% of the size. At this point my SL is at BE or BE+. Next off at another 20 to 25p's and on up till I'm 100% off. Depends on S/R levels and how the market reacts to these levels as to where my TP is. If the higher time frames show a reason for a large move the last group will get a trailing stop to let the market close me out. If PA is struggling to move I'll take a 8 or 10p exit on 'most' of the postion and move the SL close to BE but hardly ever to BE+, mostly BE-, taking into consideration the profit on the first off so if my SL is hit I still make a few. Hope this helps a bit rather than confuse.

kaizasoze.....SpecialEd.....proverbs.....thanks for the acknowlegements! Exits are challenging. You can flip a coin and enter a trade; exiting at the right time is key to being successful. Consider counting HA candles. More than eight; watch for a "pullback" or more. Switch to Japanese candle view and observe what the patterns are telling you about PA. Scale-in and scale-out as the trade progresses. Remember; you can't squeeze every last pip out of a trade. If you try, you will lose more in the long term than you will gain. Be happy with carving a nice slice of pips out of the middle of a run. This is one of the reasons I like the higher TFs. When there is a 'wave' running on H4 or H1, we want to ride that larger wave by riding smaller waves on M30 or M15 (some of you like M5 and/or M1.......not for me, thanks). Trade WITH the larger trend by following the smaller trends inside the larger one; it's NOT rocket-science. THV indicators and methods are very powerful when used properly and in the absence of greed (you can't get every pip!). We have recently been shown how individual traders have been successful by applying proven methods/strategies that are built on THV. On a final note: some of us who have been here at FF for a while have asked that the current THV EA thread mess be clarified in Cobra and his team's favor.

--- 帖子 #10704 ---
For those who like to trade M15 and higher; here is a little technique I have been using for a while that helps maximize trades by keeping DD low, avoiding range areas, providing optimal entry points and maximizing pip gain. The attached GBP/USD M15 chart from last week illustrates this very well. H1 fast TRIX has signaled 'possible' sell opportunities. Looking at the M15, we see all signals indicate a sell at the close of the 5/15, 3:00 candle. However, rather than enter at the open of the next candle, I prefer to wait until the low of that "signal" candle has been broken by at least 2 pips. This means waiting until the candle marked by the second yellow verticlal line breaks the 1.5214 level. Breaking below the 1.5214 level is the key to entering this trade. Following this techniques reduces drawdown on this trade from a possible 26 pips to only 11 pips, and keeps us out of the range area that follows the first yellow vertical line for four and a half hours (you won't be sweating about what will happen with this trade!). However..............entering on the second yellow line would be entering in "no-man's-land"; a risky situation. Waiting until the candle at the third yellow line closes would be the very best trade! Breaking the low of the 1.5198 level would have been the key to entering this trade! (60+ pips possible) Here's the technique: Price must break the high of the "signal" candle for a long trade entry or the low for a short trade entry (2 or more pips breakage for me). The next trade opportunity comes at the green verticle line (40+ pips possible).

--- 帖子 #10709 ---
creativename....... I've already discussed exit strategies in this thread; and I've posted this before too, but it bears repeating. IMO each and every trader MUST make a method "their own". One of the best ways to do this is backtesting. If you like my entry suggestions, put the indicators on a chart and go back on each pair you want to trade to see firsthand just how possible trades would have developed. This will allow you to determine appropriate stop losses and take profit targets. Otherwise how are you going to know the best strategy? Best RR and MM for you? If you don't do this, you are trading blindly and will lose your money. I'm just sharing a few ideas, not trying to provide every aspect of how to trade with THV indicators. You need to fill in the blanks according to your personality and trading style.

--- 帖子 #10711 ---
Good question: explanation required. You can backtest either way WITHOUT relying on the MTF indicators; I use the MTFs as a "guide". But because TRIX does NOT repaint after a candle has closed, I prefer to scroll back and mark charts using the TRIX only. It's very time consuming to do this, but very accurate as well. Then you can add MTF when you trade as the "guide", but still look at the other charts to confirm. HTH!

--- 帖子 #10745 ---
TakeProfit and StopLoss is the standard SL and TP. TrailingStop of 25 means EA will trail 25 pips behind price pip-by-pip. Your broker only allows you to trail a minimum of 5 pips behind price, so anything more is fine. THV CaveManager is designed for both 4 and 5 decimal brokers. No need to add another 0.

That's right. This reminds me of the DiNapoli Bread and Butter trade, which says that when there has been a really strong push up (almost vertical over about 9 bars, which you will see in this case if you look on the 5 m chart) and then a retracement, you can buy the dip and have a very high probability quickie trade (which may also develop into something longer if you set the stop on part of it to b/e where you bought). But where to buy the dip? That is what I was asking myself until the mtf trix indie came into being. The mtf trix trades (hidden positive divergence or 6 lights) tell you where it's safe to buy that dip. Vice Versa for shorts of course.

As a programmer in several languages (including EA's) if the author wishes to make their code public they will. However, I think it is not just someone copying the code and calling it their code that may be the biggest perceived problem it is more. Lets say someone de-compiles a EA and replaces their name for that of the author (But forgets to replace all of the authors name in other parts of the code) and makes a few changes to the code and sets it out into the world. Those few changes suddenly make people lose real money (Lots of it) and someone goes looking for a person to take the fall, what names will they find? Both, making the original programmer responsible in their mind as well. Even if the original code worked as planned the changes would be the authors responsibility because their name is on it. Then it gets ugly. I have made code public and I have code that will never see the light of day except on my notebook just for this very reason. Another example could be that someone de-compiles a EA and added malicious code into the EA so it will do harm to computers or servers but leaves the authors name in it so they will get the blame. BTW very interesting thread.

It has to be combined with proper analysis using higher TF, trend lines, Fibs, S/R levels and other tools you should be comfortable with to help you "know" what PA is going to be and what direction you should be trading with. These combined gives you high probability trades and THV comes in to fine tune your entry. The minimum you must do is trend line and S/R levels analysis on a higher TF to get a feel of PA and then use THV for entry. Now, with that, when the 6 lights comes on, you kind of know if it is going to be a winner or not. Cheers, CaveMan
