--- 帖子 #10893 ---
Leeky, The MTF indicators are so much more than "Analyze Buy/Sell" alerts on a single TF. The MTF Trix Histo and Ichimoku Cloud are there so that you do not have to flip through multiple charts of different TFs in your analysis thus saving you lots of time and giving you ample space to execute your entry. Spend some screen time with the MTF indicators. You should start "seeing" how multiple cycles of lower TFs adds up to cycles of higher TFs. Feel and appreciate the sinusoidal wave movements of the Trix and PA for each TF via the MTF Trix Histo indicator. With the MTF Ichimoku Cloud Indicator, you know where PA is on the other 2 higher TFs with respect to the Kumo Cloud. All these can be done on one chart - a quick visual picture of what PA is doing on other TFs. That is what the MTF indicators are for, not just flashing lights. Cheers, CaveMan

Ok, I've released a version that you can specify number of bars in to the THV team for beta testing. I hope it will be ready for the next time Cobra releases a version of THV. I want to point out, though, that the purpose of this is to reduce the load on CPU. It is NOT for backtesting . (I have seen some posts by people who are frustrated that they can't backtest more than 750 bars. ) You can't backtest - period- unless you leave the indicator running for however many bars you want to test, which is, in fact a foward test. You will note that when you add the indicator, even now, you will get results all the way back to the start of the chart, but they will not be equal to the results you would have gotten in real time, as explained in previous posts.)

--- 帖子 #10980 ---
When trading the M15 or even M30, looking at smaller TF's is IMO a way of fine-tuning the entry point. But in reality we want to trade the signals given by the primary TF; that is the TF we are looking at for the entry signal. We look "up" a TF or two because we want to ride a wave (or trend cycle) that agrees with the TF we are primarily trading. In essence we are trading "pullbacks" or "retracements" that can be seen in the higher TF. Alternately, we enter a trade at the beginning of a trend change that has started on a lower TF and will be seen on a higher TF in the future. Either approach has it's own merits and successes (and occasional losses).

--- 帖子 #10981 ---
I have attached a chart and hope it becomes more clear. 3 out of 4 lights need to be the same color of H1f,s;H4f,s as well as H4 and H1 both have to be same color. Until MA's cross to the other side, I only take trades into the direction of the Ma's. Hi Cencored, One thing you want to be careful about in your assumptions, is that in the chart below, unless your computer and mt4 were on with no interruptions during that 24 hours, the results you see may not be valid. This is because if you add the indicator 'after the fact' the results you see on a lower tf for what happened on the higher tfs do not reflect what happened in real-time. The reason for this has been explained in previous posts.

--- 帖子 #10992 ---
It doesn't actually 'repaint' if you leave it running. If you are looking at the 15 tf from a 1m chart, it will show you minute by minute what happened with the 15 m trix. Let's say that during that 15m period the 15 m trix was red for 5 bars, green for 5 bars and then red for 5 bars. At the end of the 15 minutes the trix closed red, so on the 15m chart there is a red bar and on the 1m chart there are 5 red, 5 green and 5 red. These bars on the 1m chart don't repaint. But if you now add another instance of the indicator on the 1 m chart as a new 15 m period is starting all the 15 bars representing the previous 15m period will be red, because 'after the fact' all the indicator on the 1m chart knows is that that 15 bar closed red. So it paints all the bars for that 15m on the 1m chart red. There is no way it can know, if it is added after the fact, what actually happend in real time. Therefore you can't use it for backtesting.

--- 帖子 #11065 ---
Hi Alejandro. On your MT4 Navigator window, there's a script named "period converter". Apply it on your chart and don't forget to thick the "allow dll import" on the script option. On the Input tab, you can choose the value. Example, if you put the script on the 1m EURUSD chart and you put the value 3, you can view the 3m EURUSD chart now (1m x 3 = 3m). After finish the setup script, go to File&gt;Open Offline&gt;EURUSD 3m. Now you can display the m3 chart. This topic has been discussed before on this thread. Just dig deeper, some one also has posted an indicator about this converter for easier use.

--- 帖子 #11075 ---
You will find the indi's in this thread. Entry rules: At 6.00 GMT place a horizontal line on chart, long trades only taken above and short trades below this level. Next look at 1hr chart, I take the trend as long only when the price is above hull &amp; cloud, the HA candles are green, the trend indi is green. The Trix is a little tricky, if both lines are above zero line I will take a trade on fast trix colour change, if both are below zero I prefer both lines to have changed colour. I prefer 15m trix cross for entry but 5m works too if the 15m had crossed a little earlier. Make sure you have at least top 3 lights on MTF Trix plus the 2 lights on MTF cloud the right colour, if they don't line up stay out. For short trades do the opposite. My preference is to set stop loss below previous HA candle and move with each candle, close half of trade after 15-20 pips and set to BE after 30 pips , there will be losers but this will keep them small.

--- 帖子 #11157 ---
Hello to All This has been sent to MT4 about the memory usage in this terminal Sent: Wednesday, June 3, 2009 11:59:43 AM Subject: [MT_E and I] RAM - Memory Usage Two possible flaws in current MT4 Terminal. 1) It appears that MetaTrader 4 Terminal M1 tick data received is stored in RAM. How fast memory is used is proportional to number of pairs running . When MT4 is re-started, this memory stored tick data is written to .hst file and memory usage drops. So, the more pairs that are running, the faster the memory is used. Also, downloaded History Center data is also temporarily stored in memory. After MT4 is closed, data is written to .hst file and memory usage drops. I also see memory usage increase when i open History Center. I believe this is due to calculating other timeframes from stored received M1 tick data. This may be a flaw in MT4. It should routinely auto write M1 tick data to .hst file to reduce memory usage. The only way I see to managed memory usage is to routinely re-start MT4 terminal. 2) People running the Strategy Tester could really use up memory fast when downloading History Center data. The more pairs that is being tested the higher the memory usage will be due to when History Center is opened, all previously tested pairs will be recalculated. To stop this, all .hst files need to be deleted or MT4 Terminal needs to be re- installed. If i am correct, you can see this in the Task Manager, Processes tab. When you open the MT4 History Center the memory usage for that MT4 Terminal increases. TJ

--- 帖子 #11160 ---
This is the official release of THV CaveManager v1.3 compiled for MT4 v223 and above. Some were asking about v1.2 but that was just a minor fix for a situation where a pivot level is between bid and ask price when you open a trade. New Features Advance trailing stop by percentage of floating pips by courtesy of Bemac. Combine this with traditional trailing stop to form a 2 stage trailing strategy where you can start trailing with traditional trailing stop and after a certain number of floating pips move on to trailing by percentage of floating pips. Preceding target profit (dynamic TP) that moves together with trailing stop to maximize pips instead of a traditional static TP where you trail price until your TP is hit. If the market is running, you would want to trail price and at the same time move your TP as well to capture more pips. This is what this feature does. Remember to change the settings to your trading style and TF. The defaults are settings that I am using. Cheers, CaveManager

--- 帖子 #11161 ---
well cave! thak's! i'm sperimenting it.. can u make an example? i don't well understand new features.. even if i red the manual

--- 帖子 #11162 ---
Example Settings Traditional trailing stop: 25 pips Advance trailing stop: Trigger at 80 pips and trail by 30% of floating pips. With the above setting, EA will start to trail price once more than 25 pips. It will be trailing 25 pips behind price until you hit 80 pips. After that if price moves further in your favor, trailing will be calculated based on a percentage of floating pips on the fly. If you have 100 floating pips, EA will trail behind price by 30 pips. If price move further and you have 200 pips, EA will trail at 60 pips behind price. Principle behind this is similar to how you manage a trade as your profit accumulates, you manage by moving up to higher TF and widening the buffer zone for price movements to capture more pips. Hope the example helps. Cheers, CaveMan

Hi B: Not sure if this is what you are looking for. To me, I don't need the three points being touch by the Trix be matched up with the Andrew's Lines. I draw the Trix trend line and Andrew's Line separately. And in many occasion, the Andrew's Lines break out is the true break out; which is another way of saying, it filters out the early entry (and sometimes can be premature entries) of the Trix. Please take a look at several of these Gifs. The Andrew's Lines and the Trix do give out signals simultaneously at times; and at times, one if earlier than the other. But I tend to go with the break of the Andrew's Lines as the true break out. Hope I have answered your queries. Take care. --- 帖子 #11206 ---
Hi Wlfx, Cobra is right. It is a communication error between MT4 Client and the server. It happened right at the same time when the EA sent the request to take profit. The EA will normally do a retry if it encounters such an error provided the price is still above your target. This should not occur very often unless you are using a lot of EAs on your machine and all the EAs are fighting to access the MT4 trade context. But again, that normally will present a Trade Context Busy error rather than a Trade Context Ping error. Cheers, CaveMan

You're welcome - sure works, as I use the method a lot, just make a copy of your template first so that you can go back if you mess up. You can even change indicator versions by changing the name in the template file like this: &lt;indicator&gt; name=Custom Indicator &lt;expert&gt; name=SDX-TzPivots_v4.7.2 flags=275 etc etc If you change to this: &lt;indicator&gt; name=Custom Indicator &lt;expert&gt; name=SDX-TzPivots_v4.7.3 flags=275 etc etc and save as a new template version 4.7.3 will be loaded instead. Best of luck ...

--- 帖子 #11418 ---
Hi Cashmere, I agree. That is why I coded it into THV CaveManager too. The other thing that is interesting to ponder - why do retail traders scale down/out of potential winners. Professional traders scale up/into potential winners once there are sufficient floating pips. Meaning they scale up with house money and make a potential winner even bigger. A very simplistic example 1 lot winner with floating 40 pips. Move SL to lock in 20 pips and enter another lot with 20 pips SL. Now you have 2 lots in position with house money. Repeat as market moves in favor. The potential has multiplied..... Just something to think about .... Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #11437 ---
Honestly Wlfx, I am not too sure what you are asking here. Sounds to me that you know a little of everything but not much of everything. I am not trying to be sarcastic here. Just reading off what you have written and stating my frank opinion. My best advice for you is this, spend more time to FULLY understand these 3 basic tools - trend line, Fibonacci retracements and S/R and keep your charts clean to analyze for the next trade to take. Draw trendlines the way that most people will likely draw them. Draw Fibo retracements on big moves that jump at you from the charts and pick S/R where it is most obvious. Never try to fit these tools into what you think is correct. Let the tools show you what is correct. If you cannot fit a trend line, don't draw it. If you cannot find pivots to draw fibo, don't plot it. If you cannot find S/R, don't just pick any. Only draw and plot trendline, fibo and S/R where it is most obvious. Only then will they be really accurate in price prediction. All these are based on a very basic principle of "self-fulfulling prophecy". If you are not able use the above tools to do a calculated prediction of where price will be or what PA might do, then don't trade. Chances are you are just making a wild guess. A calculated prediction has a far better chance of being correct than a wild guess of 50% chance. After the above, then do you consider using THV to further fine tune your entry on the lower TF by picking the best point of entry where trix cross and not trade against divergence. For me, I trade the H1 TF using the above 3 basic tools plus Andrew's Meridian Lines. I use THV to time entries for H1 and trade M5 in both directions (with and against the H1 trend) to kill boredom while waiting for H1 TF to line up since with my analysis on H1, I already have my calculated prediction of where price might go. Hope my reply helps. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #11445 ---
Pipnosis, that was an excellent post, a question that haunts all of us, I suspect. I too have gone back and forth on it, and cannot make that determination for sure. One thing I would suggest though - set yourself a daily goal of say 20-25 PIPs. Until you hit that goal, use the 5-10 pip TP that is common among many THV traders. Once you've hit your goal, then you're basically playing with house money. Suggest you look for the best trade set-ups. When you get to +5, +7 or +10, set your SL to break-even - or even +1. If the trade reverses on you, you haven't lost anything. If it runs favorable, then you make a lot of PIPs. You could then make yourself another rule to move SL in increments of 5 as your trade runs more and more positive. This approach would allow you to (1) use the conservative THV approach to get your daily goal; and then, (2) experiment with other trades at basically no loss. I think taking this approach will enable you to learn over time what a long-term trade looks and feels like. Then you can adjust all your rules a bit. If you decide to take this approach, I suggest that you use Caveman's "Cavemanager" for managing the movement of TPs and SLs. That's about all I have on the subject, but as I say, it's haunted me for a long time. Like everything in FX, no fixed answer. Good luck, Ed

--- 帖子 #11484 ---
Yes you can (is Obama around? ;-)) but you will never now if you had a disconnect (=repainting). ^^ The logic why a multi timeframe indicator is repainting is easy to understand. When you are on the 5 min timeframe you get 3 boxes or lights till one 15 min candle is closed. This means a 15 min period is divided in 3 parts. If the quotes move strong the 15 min trix can change from red to green to red and so on. If this happen you will see 3 boxes with different colours for 15 min. In the end the trix on the 15 min timeframe can only be red or green. When you restart meta trader or switch timeframes the trix mtf indicator can not remember the colour changes during the 15 min candle...it's green or red. Therfore you have now 3 green or 3 red lights on the 5 min tf.

--- 帖子 #11497 ---
This template is supposed to show you examples of how to set the mtf indies to any tf you want. If you switch tfs, and if you are looking at a lower tf from the higher one, of couse the results are going to be different. For one thing, every time you switch tf, the indie is initialized causing it to repaint (as explained many times previously in this thread). For another thing it is fairly meaningless to look at the lower tfs from a higher tf chart except in 'real time'. Since there are (for example) four 15 min bars in a 1 hour chart and sixteen 15 min bars in a four hour bar, of course all these can't be shown. So you are going to end up with only the result of the last of the 15 minute bars showing on the higher tf, except in real time, and even then at the end of the higher tf bar you are going to see only the result of the last 15 m bar Lastly - this system was only officially tested on the EurUsd for trading the 6 point method on the 1 min tf, looking at the higher tfs from the lower one. If you are going to use it differently you need to do your own testing.

Entry: Above Coral only long, below Coral only short Price crosses cloud - both Trix cross each other and have the same color. Best and most secure trend confirmation is a cross of the fast Trix on the zero level. Your Entry must be based on Fast &amp; Slow Trix crossover...not at cross of Coral. It is used to know in what direction to trade. Otherwise it is your decision to take trade if Trix cross happen Above/Below Coral depending on TF you are trading.

--- 帖子 #11538 ---
EU M15: Last night I was thinking "this has a good chance to go down to 1.3911/FPV", but not much later thinking "...but by way of R1!". It did, and with much tradeable up/down between. Now this has me thinking this whole area is nothing more than consolidation before a much bigger move..."PA mover" trading organizations biding their time while trying to come to a decision which side they want to be on, and once deciding then trying to get large positions without moving price too much. Regarding the questions on use of volume....much of the time it is not an important part of trading decisions. But there are times when it becomes obvious during a bar that price is moved first on little volume, and then at the price extreme of the bar heavy volume comes in.....like moving it up/down on a volume of "3" and then at the top/bottom the volume jumps to 13 -22! Or, when a few bars move the price on low volume and then the price stops moving on the next bar which has very high relative volume, in which case you may wll surmise they moved the price to where they wanted to make their more substantial trade (buy low, sell high). When this kind of volume action is evident you know they are buying at the top, or sellling at the bottom, and if that senario fits in with all else the charts are saying, it adds support to the predictive nature of certain setups.....just as the MTF Trix adds suopport to picking the best time to enter a trade based on all else the chart is showing. Volume is only a small factor in the whole picture, but sometimes on small TFs it is "screaming" about what is going on. And sometimes on larger TFs, a large spike in relative volume, is precursor to a nice, longer move. Look at the relative volume spike (tan boxes) on the attached M1 chart....it happened just before the 100+ pip run. Edit: Volume is like all indicators, which lots of the time are not saying anything in a strong way. But every once in a while an indicator starts saying something in a strong way, and then so may others....each adding support to the same hypothesis.

1. How do I get my Ishimoku indicator to be transparent, so that it does not block out the PA? Also the last bar appears way too far off to the right hand side compared to all/most other charts on this thread. Right click on the chart. Select Properties. Select the Common tab. Check chart on foreground. 2. I do not get the 'Divergence' arrows on the TRIX on the 1 min TF, but do for all other TF's In the Indicator input set Show in 1 m chart to true and set draw indicatortrendlines and draw pricetrendlines parameters to true. 3. The TEXT on the extreme RHS of the TRIX indicator is jumbled/overwritten. In the THVV3InfoPanel Indicator in the Inputs adjust the WhichCorner Parameter to suit yourself. 4. I have loaded the ATR feature onto my charts, where it appears and then disappears. no idea what you are talking about. If you have the THVIndicator Panel you don't need that anyway. --- 帖子 #11582 ---
A couple of things to watch out for. First the Bid/Ask Price, If price just touchs your T/P level the take profit order will not be filled. Price must go thru your T/P level to trigger. The second item is that you might not get your order filled if price is moving quickly or just barely goes thru your T/P level then retraces. This is not some retail store where you can buy and sell exactly when and where your want. (Well maybe a lot of MT4 broker's are) LOL. You must get the feel of your brokers fill rules and plan accordingly. Good Luck -- Mark

--- 帖子 #11585 ---
You may find that FXCM offset is actually GMT/BST +1. This means that during the winter time offset from GMT is +1, but during the summer time it is offset from BST (British Summer Time) by +1, making it offset from GMT by +2. You would then have a template with winter and summer settings if you want to be really accurate. Here is a recent link on setting the values: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=11573

--- 帖子 #11600 ---
When you took the first screenshot, if you had looked at the 5 chart you would have seen that the 5m fast trix on that chart was red at 9:35. I don't trade the GU so how do I know? I looked at the previous bar - the 9:30 bar, and that one closed red at 1.6296. The next 5 min bar opened at 1.6297 and the low of that bar was 1.6296. So we can assume that in the first 1 minute of that bar on the five m chart, the fast trix was red since the low was the same as the low for the previous bar where the fast trix was also red. When you opened and closed your mt4, you initialized the indicator. When the indicator is initialized it no longer retains a record of what happened in real time. If you, for example, reopened it at 9:37, by which time price had gone up, the fast trix on the 5 m chart would now be green for the 9:35 bar, and the mtf indie would have no way to know that at 9:35 it had been red but had turned green at 9:36. Since you in fact did the second screenshot 20 minutes later, the mtf trix would only know the final result for that 5 m bar, which was green, and would put that result in all five 1m bars (9:35 to 9:39).

--- 帖子 #11674 ---
Hi RTB: THV does not draw trendlines in the PA. THV TRIX has an inbuilt divergence indicator that will display the 4 types of divergence on the trix indicator and display an arrow. Having said that, it is not perfect and occasionally misses divergence. It also displays the arrow only after the fact. It, obvisouly, cannot anticipate divergence. Therefore I recommend that everyone try and draw out their own divergence and use the indicator as a confirmation. Hope that answers your question.

When I tested it and as I trade it I use divergence so I can't imagine trading without it. Part of the rules say to not trade against divergence, and also I find that if you take the divergence trades, especially the ones going with the higher tf trend, it gets you in on the right side sooner. --- 帖子 #11702 ---
I mean that I don't usually draw slanting trendlines on the 1 m chart to decide whether to trade. I do look for big patterns like triangles on the larger timeframes before I trade. For example if I get a long signal on the 1m tf and I see on the 4 hour tf that PA is about to hit the side of a tested triangle then I will pass on the trade until I see if it breaks or bounces. Or if it's bouncing off the side of a triangle on the 4 hour chart with divergence on the 1 m chart, then I'm happy with the trade. But on the 1 m I focus more on the horizontal lines like pivots, which are good across all timeframes and I don't draw angled trendlines. Not that that isn't a valid way to trade - I just don't do it much.

--- 帖子 #11734 ---
There are two kinds of divergence: Regular and hidden. Regular divergence is a trend reversal signal, hidden divergence is a trend continuation signal. Lets take a long example (reverse everthing for short). When you are at the bottom of a long downtrend and price is making lower lows while the indicator is making higher lows you have regular divergence indicating a possible trend reversal. For this kind of divergence to work, you want the downtrend to have had a nice run, PA to be quite extended (far from the Coral, near the end of the daily range, and preferably bouncing off something sturdy.) When you are in the middle of an uptrend, after a pullback and you see that price has made a valley with a higher low, while the indicator has made a valley with a lower low, that is hidden bullish divergence that indicates a probable trend continuation. For this kind of divergence to work you want there to have been a nice strong uptrend with a good pull back that is bouncing off something sturdy, and in the case of a long, it's nice if PA is above the coral. Since you were in an uptrend to that point (more or less - PA was pretty rangy) you should have been looking either for short regular divergence or hidden bullihsh divergence. What you took was regular divergence for long but you weren't at the bottom of a downtrend. Regular divergence at the end of downtrend (go long) Hidden bullish divergence in the middle of an uptrend (go long)

--- 帖子 #11821 ---
Okay. For this example lets say that your main TP goal is 10 pips and your SL's are all set at 10. Enter the trade with three positions of equal size. 1st position - take profit at +3 or 4 pips 2nd position - take profit at +10 pips 3rd position - once 2nd position takes profit at +10, move the stop loss for the 3rd position to break even. Set your take profit just before a recent swing high or low, support or resistance, or pivot level. Then ENJOY YOUR FREE TRADE! The reason this is so effective is that few trades immediately reverse to stop you out. Most losing trades venture at least part way into profitable territory before reversing. Using this method, a loss would net you -17 pips as opposed to -30 pips. That's a big difference in the way your losses affect your equity overall. We received numerous questions after our first e-mail regarding the new NFA Compliance Rule 2-43(b). Please note that you will be able to use entry orders to place stops and limits after July 31, 2009. Entry orders provide the ability to realize profits and cut losses. Using entry orders for stop-loss and limits after July 31, 2009: For Buy Positions: Placing an entry order to sell below the price where you got into the position protects you from additional losses. Placing an entry order to sell above the price where you got in locks in profits. For example, if you have a BUY EUR/USD position at 1.3900, you could place: a stop-loss using a sell entry order (Stop Entry, SE) at 1.3800 or a limit using a sell entry order (Limit Entry, LE) at 1.4000. For Sell Positions: Placing an entry order to buy above the price where you got in protects you from additional losses. Placing an entry order to buy below the price where you got in locks in profits. For example, if you have a SELL EUR/USD position at 1.3900, you could place: a stop-loss using a buy entry order (Stop Entry, SE) at 1.4000 or a limit using a buy entry order (Limit Entry, LE) at 1.3800. The National Futures Association (NFA), our industry's self regulatory organization in the United States, has informed all Forex Dealer Members, which includes FXCM , that it has adopted new Compliance Rule 2-43(b) regarding forex trading. Read Compliance Rule 2-43(b) This rule requires orders be executed First In, First Out (FIFO). FIFO requires that when multiple positions are held in the same currency pair, the position which was first opened will be the first to be closed. This will prevent stop-loss and limit orders from being placed on individual tickets (orders and positions). FXCM has always encouraged active risk management through the use of stop-loss and limit orders. The stop and limit orders that have been available through the “Open Positions” window are two entry orders that are linked to an individual open position. If a stop or limit order is triggered, the other is canceled. The FIFO rule prevents stops and limits from being attached to an individual ticket. FXCM is introducing a new feature called OCO (One Cancels the Other) entry orders, which will provide traders with the same functionality as they have been accustomed, except that they are not linked to any positions. Watch This Video Presentation To See How To Manage Your Risk Using OCO Entry Orders For additional information, please visit the "NFA FIFO (First in, First Out) Rules" forum on DailyFX. We will be holding live question and answer sessions within the DailyFX forum. Visit Now Do I have to change my current platform? While FXCM acknowledges the NFA's concern and obligation to protect clients, FXCM would like to extend an option to those who would like to continue using the current platform functionality. Traders can transfer their accounts to Forex Capital Markets Ltd. (FXCM UK) and continue to place stop-loss and limit orders and maintain the ability to modify and close orders from the "Open Positions" window. If you wish to maintain your current platform functionality, you can trade through FXCM UK, which is regulated by the Financial Services Authority (FSA) in the United Kingdom. If you wish to transfer your account to FXCM UK, please complete the one page form: Micro Account Transfer Form Deadline to Complete Transfer Form: JULY 21, 2009 Top FXCM UK Frequently Asked Questions: More FAQs are available on the DailyFX forums . Visit Now Q: If I switch my account to FXCM UK what protection is available? A: The FSA is the regulatory body that oversees spot FX trading in the United Kingdom. The market has been regulated in the UK much longer then it has been in the U.S. Accounts with FXCM UK are segregated in accordance with FSA client money rules. The financial services authority, one of the world's most respected financial regulatory bodies, regulates FXCM UK. Q: Can I fund my account via credit/debit card? A: Yes. We now accept payment through the two major international credit cards. You can now fund your account with Visa or MasterCard. The minimum deposit via credit and debit card is $25. Please note the maximum account balance is US$5,000. Deposit Funds Now Q: Can I fund my account by wire? A: Yes. You can make USD deposits via wire. The minimum deposit via wire transfer is $1,000. Please note the maximum account balance is US$5,000. Deposit Funds Now Q: Will I be able to place stop-loss and limit orders on individual positions after I transfer to FXCM UK? A: Yes. All FXCM UK accounts will allow clients to place stops and limits as well as close positions from the "Open Positions" window. Q: Will hedging be enabled on my account after it is transferred to FXCM UK? A: Yes. All FXCM UK accounts default to have hedging enabled. That is to say that buy and sell positions will no longer offset each other. Buy and sell positions can now be held on the same account. Clients who wish to have hedging disabled can elect to turn the function off via MyFXCM. Q: Will OCO entry orders be enabled on my account after it is transferred to FXCM UK? A: Yes. However, if the account does not have hedging enabled the OCO orders executed in the opposing direction of open positions will effectively offset those positions. Conversely, a market order to buy 100K GBP/USD will NOT be offset by an entry order to sell if the account has hedging enabled. --- 帖子 #11900 ---
Ahh..ok...thought something looked different.. Thx...I drafted up a set of rules which I incorporated into the original V3 THV rules and it seems to be working out quite well, especially on the higher time frames.. I will post them here in case it might help some. Let me know if anything can be added...everyone's input is much appreciated. Thanks again Cobra &amp; team for all of your help &amp; support. Entry: 1. Look at 4H Chart - If price is above Coral only long, below Coral only short 2. Next Look for following scenario on 5M, 15M, 30M &amp; 1H Time Frames: A. Price crosses cloud - both Trix cross each other and have the same color – THIS MUST OCCUR AT THE BEGINNING OF THE MOVE EITHER UNDER OR ABOVE THE CLOUD - ONLY TAKE THESE TRADES ON ANY TIME FRAME. B. Next look for same bias candle on next higher time Frame. (Example: if long entry signal is on 5M, then 15M candle must be bullish. If short entry signal is on 15M, then 30M must be bearish.) Remember – · If the 4H chart is above the Coral – you are only looking for bull crosses on the smaller time frames. · If the 4H chart is below the Coral – you are only looking for Bear Crosses on the smaller time frames. I have 4 Time frames up on my charts. 2 per screen as follows: Screen1: 5M &amp;15 Screen 2: 30M &amp; 1H STOP: MUST BE AT ENTRY TIME FRAME ATR. Trail stop positions once you are 30 pips in profit to below or above previous 1H candle. EXIT: 2 ways. Either initial hard stop is hit, or you are taken out by your trailing stop. NOTE: 1H Faster Trix changes color and/or touch of a known good resistance/support level can also be reasons to exit your position. Other reasons to take profit can be : Touch of a trend line, resistance or support line, horizontal psych level (00 - 20 - 50 - 80) Position Sizing: If your entry is based on 1H time frame or Higher, then you can add positions on 5 &amp; 15M crosses in same direction of your trade.

--- 帖子 #11912 ---
Trading is not about being right. It's about taking a risk with good probabilities, watching to see if you were right or not, and then acting accordingly. If you had been drawing some trend line on 5m this last 5m short would have been right into the bottom TL of a consolidation triangle, which reduces the probabilities of the trade working. In any case you could have cut the loss with the close of the first green HA candle and gotten out with a tiny loss. So even with the loss I would still see this trade as a positive in the fact that it gave you an entry, and then gave you a reason to cut the loss short very quickly. EIDT: Also the last few hours have been very choppy, PA on the smaller time frames gets like this when were are at some important long term areas. Earlier we had a stop driven move short almost down to the 3850 area, which was then pushed right back up over 3900. This system works great when we have some room to run, but when were sitting in a mess of confluence it can be choppy and very difficult to trade for profit with THV3.

Yeah, I tend to use MAs more than diagonal trendlines for analysis. I use the following MAs on my 1 m analysis chart 240 s - (gold) approximates where the coral is on the 5 m chart 750 s - (red) approximates where the coral is on the 15 m chart 950 s - (green) approximates the spine of the rainbow on the 5 m chart 1500 s -( Blue gray) approximates the coral on the 30 m chart 3000 s (Brown) approximates the coral on the 60 m chart 3000 e (magenta) - don't remember what it approximates but also gets lots of PA bounces. The rainbow colors are the Rainbowmma indicators. There's a few threads in FF about them. I like to use the rainbow and MAs for my analysis chart to help me see when we are in a trending market verses in a choppy market and which direction is the safest direction to take trades.

--- 帖子 #11930 ---
At the beginning of the day I look at all the tfs (weekly, daily, 4hr etc) to get a feel for the big picture and see if there are any patterns like H&amp;S or triangles etc to watch out for. But to decide whether to take a trade at the minute a 6 point signal is given I look at the 1 m analysis chart. If the chart shows a orderly expanding rainbow trend, and not chop and if the trade is with the rainbow, and there are no conflicting divergences, and there is some open 'real estate' on the chart with no roadblocks in the way so the trade has room to move I take it. If the rainbow shows chop, or the trade is against the rainbow (except divergence trades) or there is conflicting divergence or there is a roadblock in the way (like the pivot or the coral on a higher tf or the end of the daily range for example) I let it pass. That means I let some good trades go, because sometimes there is enough momentum to get through a roadblock, and eventually one of those choppy waves is going to be the start of a good new trend. But, if it is, I know there will be more good trades down the road after an orderly trend has started and the roadblocks have been passed, and those are the safer trades.

--- 帖子 #11931 ---
Here is what I do to help find a trending pair. At the start of the day I look through the 8 pairs in my basket using the filters as shown. The TF is 30 mins. I start with the pairs showing TRADE and reject any saying DO NOT TRADE from the noise filter. I then select the strongest looking pair(s) by referring to the ADX figures. I look for the highest numbers in the 1Hr &amp; 4 Hr bands. I then check that these pairs are still showing TRADE from the noise filter on a 1HR TF and only then fire up my charts and look for entries. At the end of each trade I go back and check that the pair I am working on is still showing TRADE, if not I drop it and look for another. Hope this helps. Any ideas to refine the process gratefully received.

--- 帖子 #11932 ---
I like the heatmap Macman, however I find it is not overly necessary. The EURUSD usually has enough trading opportunities throughout an 8hr session (of your choice). I have resorted to only trading EURUSD. It helps you get a feel for that particular pair, how it moves, etc. It also helps you concentrate purely on one pair, no distractions. If it looks choppy, I simply go away from the computer and come back later. I find that if you look at too many pairs at one time, you start to overtrade as you see opportunities everywhere. I have burned myself and now purely concentrate on one pair. There are enough signals to make you good pips. Each to his own of course, this is just what I do.

Hi Mark, The larger pic is of the 8 pairs as they show on my double 19" screens, which is why it is not very clear. The smaller pic is a detail of one of the pairs only. I have attached a template and the indi's, if you want to play with this. If it helps, I will describe my trading day - please note that I live in the UK/Europe and trade the London session, so much of this info may be of no use if you trade a different session. By the way, this only works after drinking TEA , not coffee - Basically I trade the M15 and 1H TFs, so I am looking for a pair which will (hopefully) continue to trend in the same direction for the whole of the day. I am an intraday trader, so I almost never leave an overnight position open. As explained in the earlier post the TREND/DONT TREND setup runs on M30. Often there is a lot of heavy PA action when London first opens, so I need to be ready and the M30 set-up needs time to adjust, so I have the EURGBP charts loaded and ready to go. I scalp the M1/M5 - pure THV - and take anything the market will give me. At that point I have no idea of longer term trend as the London session has a will of it's own. I choose the EURGBP as I have the most knowledge of fundamentals for this pair. After about 1 hour I start to look at the M30 TREND/DONT TREND set-up and look for a pair(s) which will run for the rest of the day. I do not trade any pair which has a high or medium news release coming up until after the news. From then on, I use the M15 and 1H TFs. I take a position on up to 3 pairs, assuming they are available. Hope this is food for thought - best of luck. p.s. don't forget you may have to compile the two .mq4 files manually before adding them to your MT4, in case your MT4 does not compile automatically.

Hi all- I've decided to poke my head in here and just say Hi to everyone and lend a hand. I'd like to answer some questions that I see recurring: and why some people are having a difficult time trading THV THV is designed to get guaranteed pips. It's not designed to catch the entire move--- your entry [if you followed the rules] will have you enter on the pull back of the move-- whether it be on a 1M, 5M, 15M...all the way up to monthly timeframes. Most of the time-- this is where the jackpot is. Right now, there is a lot of sideways motion in the market--and having read a lot of other systems, people aren't doing so well. Most systems are designed for trending markets. That's the beauty of THV--- it catches little trends. People like to look at higher TF's for "the bigger picture"-- guess what-- most of the time, by the time you've determined a trend, you're too late. Some people have the misconception that trading higher TF's is "safer"--- not really-for the fact listed above. Drawdowns are also massive--which is why THV is so appealing--- risk is minimal and you may not get the entire move like people who sit with bated breath on higher TF's and watch for the next trend, but trading opportunities are more plentiful on the smaller TF's--you're exposure to the market is limited [in and out]. I've known traders who trade higher TF's that have lost it all --yes they were trading the trend, but the trend took a pause [which doesn't always happen at fibs or news--- the major Forex pairs for scalping actually can be driven by Oil, and even more so S&amp;P and DOW futures] Just think: with a $1,000.00 account, and you traded 0.1 lots, for only 10 pips a day [trust me, you can get that in less than 2 hours at any given time of day with THV] you've just made 10% on your account for the week [$100.00 trading EUR/USD at 5 days] After that week, if you have the ability to do micro accounts, correct money management would allow for 0.11 lots at week 2--- by the end of the month you'll have a ROI of almost 50% --- that's pretty fantastic---with hardly any time invested. Why should we obey the coral? I haven't seen a good answer for this, other then "it's the trend". Sort of true. The coral actually represents the 15M trend-- the coral will look different on the different TF's--- and shouldn't be used on 15M or higher. That's the problem with most indicators-- smaller TF's need bigger number values for a more accurate result, higher TF's need smaller numbers. I'd want to know the trend is going for more than 5 minutes before entering a trade--wouldn't you? Anyway, I am attaching a template that some people might find useful for the MTF Trix. I'm not attaching any of the indicators as they can be found within the system or within the thread. template indicators: THV coral THV FF Cal -for your pertinent news needs Miss Pip's Toggle/Reg HA [minus the alert] THV ATR pips- helps determine a safe S/L determined by voloatility of the timeframe attached to it THV Ichimoku cloud indicator [2X] settings are in order 5M/1M, 15/60--trade with 3 "light" confirmation-minimum] Have 5M first because that's the 1st light I want to see. T@H's Pivots v4= this tool is very handy. Be sure to set your broker's GMT settings in the options. Not only does this indicator show you the S/R levels and daily pivot, but for those that didn't know, these calculations are based on the previous day's numbers---and happen to coincide with the daily fibs! [major number-0,38,61,100, etc] Pretty snazzy, eh? Brilliant if you ask me. MTF THV Trix- 5m-this template is for 1M trading--- the 1 mintue trix values are good, but I have found that slight modification of the a and b values for higher TF's make for a more accurate signal. 5M= At3=20 Bt3=30 15M= At3=18 Bt3=27 these are suggested values* I've also emphasized the hull line of the trix from the signal line, and added a 0 value. At the very least the thin signal line should be below for SELL and above for BUY. Your very best trades will be will PA above/below coral[and well clear of it] as well as for SELL-- the thick hull line is at or below the 0 line Buy the thick hull line at at or above the 0 line People always ask what's the best TP? Well, that's actually a difficult answer, because the market is always different. Sometimes, you'll thank your lucky stars and followed the THV's rules of 10 pips. Other times, you'll ask yourself, why did I exit so soon? I could've had more. My advice is-- if you're really worried about it, take the guaranteed 10 and be done with it. Or, hop off when the Heiken Ashi changes color, then look for a re-entry point. The main thing is to think like this: rather than think : "I could have had more" you should think:" I'm glad I didn't give any back." Greed consumes us all--- and if you're not an experienced trader and don't know how the market moves, this is my suggestion to you. The more exposure you have to the market the more likely it is you'll lose what you've gained--mainly because you *think* you can predict the future of the trend, and then you've come to realize your stop loss. If the trade happens off a bounce of a S/R or fib line, aim for the very next line on your chart. Sometimes that space between them can be 20-30-or more! pips! I also highly suggest you put in a value for your T/P instead of just hitting the button--my broker [lately] has been lagging something fierce, and I suffer requotes more often than I'd like [yes, I know, I need another broker, but my broker offers a 1 pip spread of EUR/GBP in the mornings, and I can't find anything that beats that ] Good trading to you

--- 帖子 #12034 ---
I also find I like the MTF trix indie very much because it shows you the shape of the trix. However, regarding the repainting of the trix histo - the trix histo shows you what happened minute by minute iwith the trix indie inside a five minute bar on a one minute chart (for example). If the inside that five minues the trix histo was green for two minutes and red for three it shows you two red bars and three green ones. After the five minutes is up however all it knows is the final result, not what happend in real time. If you initialze the trix histo or add it to the chart after that five minutes was up, and the final result on the five min chart was red you will see five red bars. You are going to have that problem with any mtf indie. In addition, the trix itself sometimes repaints backward one bar, making it not match the mtf indies. Here are two examples. One shows the mtf histo showing the change in the bars minute by minute from red to green on the one min chart while the mtf trix is showing green at the end of the 5 min period on the one min chart (the actual 5 m trix is red by that time), and then after you init the mtf trix on the 1 m chart, it shows red for that same period. The second shows the actual slow 15 trix red from 2:45 to 3:00 while the mtf slow trix is green. I also don't use the repainting Trix indicator [histo] I'd like to personally thank whoever created the "MTF" Trix indie-saves me from switching screens so much. Glad to help when I can-love to read the posts here.[/quote]

--- 帖子 #12039 ---
One of the advantages of trading multiple pairs is you can avoid the lottery of the News Release. However no currency pair actually moves in isolation - it is often the ripple in the pond effect. If you were trading EURGBP this morning you had no immediate news releases showing, but 1st cousin GBPUSD did have a news release and both pairs started moving at exactly the same time. So if you are trying to avoid the news release lottery, also check the other close family members. Good trading to all ...

--- 帖子 #12051 ---
Hi Twamta, You will see a lot of different charts here (some really clean and beautiful like Cobra's, Tradewell's and Cashmeer's, others messier -the guilty parties to remain nameless), but THV is really very simple. You will notice that whatever else you see on the charts, everyone is doing a few simple things in common: 1) We are all using the Coral and cloud to get the direction to trade in (long when PA is above, short when it's below ). 2) We are all using the trix to time our entry. Some are using a trix cross and fast trix above/below zero in the direction of the trade to enter, and some are counting 6 points on the mtf trix indicators to enter. But once we know the direction to trade in, we are all waiting for the trix to give us a signal for a possible trade. 3) Some advanced traders are also trading when they see divergence between the price action and the trix. However, an important point is that most people are not taking every trade they see on offer. In other words, regular good trading practices apply, including watching out for news times, patterns, pivots, trendlines etc. Therefore, besides the official toolkit, each person has their own additional analysis of the market to do before taking a trade. A lot of people have shared their own favorite analysis methods for finding good entries. Some like to see a pivot or support or fib line broken or bounced off of before trading. Some like to see a trendline broken or bounced off of before trading. Some use other methods to confirm trend strength or choppiness like the RSI or the rainbow or heatmaps. Some will take any trade at all except when the Coral is flat. All those are just the different ways that each person has of being aware of what the market is doing before they decide to take a trade, and I guess you will have to find the ones you are comfortable with. Exits: Exits are also a bit personal. Some are using a set SL 15, TP 10 with the 6 point mtf method. Some (this is the original method) are taking what the market gives them by setting an initial SL based on the ATR suggestion and TP based on at least 1/2 of the ATR suggestion, and then if the trade goes well targeting support or resistence lines, or waiting for a trix change in color before getting out. This way you can get more pips, but you have to be more patient to do it. Some are using multiple lots and trailing their stops on the additional lots.

--- 帖子 #12060 ---
Oh, sorry. The Coral is the THV3 Coral indicator. It's just a moving average and as to the exact formula for it, that's proprietary to Cobra. You will find it on the first page. We look for long trades when price action (PA for short) is above it, short when PA is below it. The cloud is the Ichimoku indicator. The correct settings for it are in the THV template which you will find on the first page. We look for long trades when PA is above it, short when PA is below it. The trix is the THV3 Trix indicator. You will find it on the first page. We trade long when the fast line crosses above the slow line and crosses above zero and short when the fast line crosses below the slow line and below zero. I would wait to try the mtf version of the system until after you have used the basic version. SL is StopLoss. TP is TargetProfit. ATR is Average True Range. THe THV ATR Pips Indicator will make a suggestion for you as to which SL to use based on the current Average True Range for the timeframe. Mtf is multiTimeFrame. You can google ATR, Trix and Ichimoku if you want to know how they are constructed but you don't really need to know that to trade THV. To get rid of the Market Hours, right click on the chart, select Indicators, select it, and click Delete. I got rid of mine a long time ago but if I remember correctly it may leave some artifacts. If you still see any notifications from it, right click on the chart, select Objects, locate whatever of its objects it didn't delete and delete them.

I was doing some reading the other day about a fellow who makes his living off of Forex and has for quite some time. He averages 50-100 pips a day [which is quite good!] and he does it with minimal risk. He spends 5-6 hours trading a day. Making 1 trade per hour, taking only 10-15 [sometimes 20] off a 5M and 15M chart setup. When he's got his trade, he comes back the next hour and look to go fishing again for another 10-15 [it doesn't take long to do chart analysis] Asked why he does this: People are obsessed with how many pips they can get in a move--- and more often than not the trend will reverse on you, and you think it will continue--then you find yourself with no pips. You've lost what you had. Then they become obsessed and start to chase and trade emotionally, and thus end up blowing their account. It also keeps the mind fresh and and you keep your sanity. He claims to have only 1 bad trade for the last year, and only because the broker had a bad tick-- [* must be a joke because I thought bad ticks you could get the fixed by the broker?] I like this approach. On most given trading days for 5 hours the trend is going somewhere- what a simple concept it is to pull a few pips out of the hour trend, go have breakfast, come back, and do it again, go watch TV, etc. for each hour and grow your account. Your risk is minimal as well, although the 100 pip mark is questionable to me as it might take a while to find a setup up and then coming back the next hour [60 minutes later]--unless they're talking about starting out trading session, taking a trade, [however long it takes] then coming back at the top of the next hour, not necessarily 60 minutes later. However, I still like this idea-- it takes the guess work out of which way you think the trend will go if you come back after some time to re analyse your chart. Perhaps this is what robots are for..however, robots lack the intelligence people do and can't be programmed with the information we can see on our charts. Good Trading- ~IP

--- 帖子 #12093 ---
There's nothing magic about it. I guess this must be a hard concept to grasp, because people keep asking about it. The trix histo shows you, on the one minute chart, what the five minute trix was doing for each of the five minutes that make up that bar. If you had looked over at the five minute chart at the very second that the trix histo showed the 5m fast to be green, you would have seen that it was, indeed, green. However, if for the next four minutes it was red, the outcome of the bar would be red. If you then, restart your application, the trix histo has no way of knowing what actually happened in real time. All it knows after the fact is the final outcome for the bar, so it will paint all those five bars red. You can demonstrate the same thing by adding another instance of the trix histo after the bar has closed. This in no way invalidates the fact that at the moment you were about to take that trade, if you had checked on the five minute chart you would have seen that in that particular minute, the 5 m fast trix was green. However, it means that you can not visually backtest results based on a trix histo added after the fact. There is one exception to this statement that if you checked the five min trix at that minute it would be green, and that stems from the fact that neither the trix nor the trix histo has a yellow condition (when the current trix is equal to the previous, or flat.) The trix itself solves this problem by repainting one bar back after it knows the final outcome. That is, if the trix was flat at that point, and it had been red, if the trend goes up the next bar, it will go back and repaint the bar that had closed red to green. I solved it in the histo by showing you the opposite color. That is, if you were in a downtrend and the current bar is flat, I show you green. The reason is to give you a heads up that the trend might be changing. If it does, you missed a bad trade. If it doesn't, at worst you are in one bar late.

This is exactly the way many of us trade.......... Use the H1 to establish trend direction. Then each hour select a trade on the M15 that agrees with this trend and take a small bite out of the trend. While the trade is developing, look at other pairs for a good setup for the next hour. This way there is no need to "baby-sit" a trade by hovering over a chart like a vulcher watching the trade progress. But this means watching more than one or two pairs. Currently I watch 15 for the very best trade opportunities. During my 6 to 8 hour typical (sometimes shorter) "Trade Day", I am researching trade opportunities and/or other Forex related matters. I am NOT watching TV while my trades are working for me. Certainly I DO eat breakfast, but it's in front of my four monitors because I consider my "Trade Day" to be just like any other workday for any other person with a "job". And trading IS a "job". In the past I have posted how I like to use some of the THV indicators to trade H1 and M15 (TRIX is my fav). But most people here prefer smaller time frames and scalping......"to each his own". However, averaging 50 to 100 pips a day this way is not really that difficult AND it is relatively stress free. Patience, discipline and not being greedy are very important to this process!

--- 帖子 #12111 ---
Right, and that is why the rules only call for 6 points. That means you can trade when only the 1m, 5m and 15f are going for you if the Ichimoku agrees without waiting for all tfs to line up. The higher timeframes are mainly there for two reasons: 1) So you can trade if the higher tfs are in a strong trend and there has been a fairly sizable retrace. Then you might get most of the points from the higher tfs, and reenter just as the 1m and 5m are turning in the direction of the trade, but the 15m has not caught up get. 2) To help you see where you are in the trend. Like, if all 10 lights have just turned green, is it really wise to take that short divergence trade? Or might the smarter thing be to wait for the divergence to finish and look for an opportunity to go long? But if you are more than 4 waves into an uptrend (more than 4 sets of red on the 1m) and you can see the 1m and 5 turning red, maybe you could consider it if there's an nice sturdy obstacle in the way.

--- 帖子 #12112 ---
Very well put. By waiting for everything to light up and the trend is near exhaustion. As mentioned, trends go in waves. Where you want to ride the waves is the 1st,2nd, and -maybe the 3rd-wave. I hardly see trends with more than 5 waves. Once you have 15M confimation, I would look at the analyse charts and wait for a setup after the pull back-- this is where a lot of traders get hit with S/L --hey-the trend is going this way--better hop on the train before it's too late!-then they get smacked with a pullback. Sometimes pullbacks in strong trends are just a pause in action, but most times you see a retracement of sorts [usually 61 sometimes 38 percent [AKA fibs!]of the initial effort after this you look for the trend to continue. Every TF has these actions--waves and pullbacks. If it isn't a false breakout, then once the momentum of the trend continues, the 60 M "lights" should come on--- the trick is to catch them right when they do and go from there--looking for 1-3 opportunities before the trend dies.

--- 帖子 #12123 ---
I thought a good topic of conversation for today was to talk about the Trix indicator and how it relates to the price action and what you see. The Trix is actually 2 indicators in 1-- the signal line [the thin one that squiggles and moves more than the thick one] is a moving average that follows the trend--not too tight and not too loose. This happens to be a non-lag MA and will change color and direction as the trend does it's thing. The thick line is the "hull line" of the indicator and is an oscillator -- similar to a Stochastic, and we use it like the stochastic in the regards to looking for divergence- higher highs on a trend with lower highs on the oscillator means the up trend is near an end. This line is also the trend momentum indicator--where some people will get confused when they see the trend go one way and the trix colors are the opposite. You'll see this instance at the end of a trend-where there's a stall in action, and one last push before an immediate reversal. Don't consider this as lost pips--- this is pips you saved thanks to the indicator that knows more than you do trying to determine the trend from what you see. You'll aslo notice in the first picture below, where the arrow is and the Trix is red... notice the struggle it's having going North---it's taking a lot of effort to get there. Divergence comes in 2 flavors-- where the PA actually goes the other way from the trend, or it just sits and stalls for a while, where PA bobs up and down for a bit before continuing. On the picture I'm attaching I followed the the trend lines of the Trix as the indicator sees the trend--the thin yellow line is the signal line of the Trix and the [sloppy] green line is the momentum line. The white lines are the middles of each wave --this is what the Trix calulates for the 0 value--so if there's 1 wave, you take the middle value of that wave and for the next wave [provided it has the same amount of movement as the previous wave] should bring the value above/below the 0 line in regards to the direction you want to go in. This is why it's so important to mind the 0 value of the Trix in regards to your trades---not just that both lines are the same color. You need to know that the trend is above/below the average of the last wave---trading by this method prevents 2 things: Suffering the bite of a nasty pull back [test of previous trendline/PA "box", and also from a false breakout-- these are different things. Pull back happen to test the previous price to make sure it's rejected--therfore it must move, and false breakouts happen by "Big Money" to make the price higher/lower in their favor to make a more appealing price to do their trading. This is where the big moves happen-- example is last night on GBPUSD where there was a 50 pip move or so south [to the DP] and an immediate reversal for 200 or so points north. [talking about the over all trend--it first went to the previous high, then took off] Slope/angle is another factor, as well as the separation of the Trix lines [lots of separation is good, I like to see high/low signal line coming towards the thick hull line] flats line are not good for trading--don't even try it. Buying thin line should be above thick and sell thin should be below line---preferably thick line above/below 0 as well, but sometimes the signal line gets through first. [on really strong moves] As long as your other indicators and your brain tell you it's safe to trade, the signal line crossing should be sufficient.

I thought another good topic for newer traders is the understanding of the Waves of trading-- and how Fibs come into action. My basket is full for today as I've made my daily goal, and I never go for more. I'm posting this chart for a greater understanding of the Forex waves, and how it relates to THV trading. This [even though tonight is relatively slow] is a Forex's trader's pure heaven, because it's very easy to know where to TP--the waves are extremely predictable First thing to note is the bear pennant shape that has formed--which means a break out to the downside will eventually happen, marked by descending trianges and a flat bottom trendline. First valid THV trade was a break of the previous swing low. Entry was at pause of trend [minor 5M bar pullback] TP at DP. 2nd trade at 61 fib after confirmation of continued downward momentum [downthrust bar] took a chance DP would be broken and I was right-- TP with my trigger finger. Also noted-if you have a confirmed trend, you don't have to wait for the thick trix line [hull] to change color--you can take trades off the confirmation of the thin signal line] 3rd trade- huge pin bar--need I say more? great effort up and an even greater effort down leaves a candle with a long wick and no body. Great trade signals. Traded to previous low, but took awhile to get there [I held on because I knew where the trend was going] bit notice that the indicators don't line up--it took me a while to get to my final destination- and probably not a wise trade for a newer trader who doesn't know how to recognize chart patterns yet. 4th trade - I had originally made a long term trade to get to the 61 fib retracement level of NY's move from the last hourly low 01.6370 from the high of 1.6480-ish.--and my 4th trade I was aiming for that TP--and as you can see it's a good thing I knew exactly what that number was--and as you see it was an immediate 40+ pip reversal to the top of the last major swing high. This is why you should always aim for your target and set a TP. It can happen so fast you hardly have time to blink. Now,with the THV template attached to the same chart and vertical lines for my trade entires, you'll notice that some of the indicators don't line up--- which is OK given that I have the knowledge that I do. The posts that I am doing [maybe I'll do a series of them] is to help people understand how Forex *usually* works-and what to look for so you can take the guess work out of your trades and hopefully prevent some bad ones. Confidence is key. Proper entries are also key-- THV allows you catch the momentum of the waves of the trend Entries at the start of the momentum of the trend--so there's minimal drawdown. This might have been a poor choice of trading pairs to show as an example= I'm sure on a more stable pair the indicators would have lined up with the trades--but this was so classic I had to share. Hopefully now you understand a little bit better why you see charts with trend lines, and a little how fibs work. I should probably mention the GBPUSD is not a recommended scalping pair for newer traders---given the example of the 2 immediate reversals shown on these charts. GBPUSD is very sensitive to fibs and one MUST have a clear understanding of how fib retracements work with this pair. Also should be noted that once the trend has broken out, [broken a trendline to either change direction or continue downward, new fibs need to be drawn from the last major swing high [happens to be that huge tweezer tops] to the new low== then we redraw our fibs and start taking trades again. What's already said about the ATR SL is Ok and answered the question, just an additional suggestion. Lets see this USDCHF chart. Let's say we took a short after confirmation on the Pin bar at 774 and the ATR said 45 Pips, that would be more than less what we want to risk but we have 50% Fib and a Historical R line, so we set the SL a little bit over that values ( in total 52 Pips) to protect our SL, we don't just set blindly what the ATR tells us. When you see that there is a very good reason that your position was wrong you might consider to get out the trade before your SL. Have a great weekend everybody.

--- 帖子 #12175 ---
Trends just don't reverse--- they start on a small TF and build into a bigger one. A classic one is starting with a small retrace from the existing trend, then heading back in the other direction, but doesn't quite make it there--[on a bigger TF looks like hangman or hammer] Making such large moves so quick isn't typical--and one might say "smells funny" - some call these whipsaws. I have never seen a trend change that starts out on a small TF like that with a 61 retrace straight away. While I've become quite good at recognizing patterns with in the trend, it's ever the constant game to figure out which sequences the retraces are going to happen--retrace from the prevailing H/L of the last wave I can see, the retrace from the next higher TF , the hourly retrace, 4hr, or even the daily....weekly, monthly... there's so many variables that it boggles the mind, and I find it hard to put into words...and it would take me loads of pictures to convey my thoughts. The singal line coming from below [ or taking a trade in this condition] means that the overall momentum of the trend had an anomoly - you took that trade when there was a surge-- what goes up fast falls fast. Glad you took that trade on the 1M level--on the 5 I definitely wouldn't have touched it. [the prevailing trend was too long, also showing hits of divergence that the overall trend was going to change with the change of the signal line. Your very best trades are going to happen when both lines change the same color really close to the 0 line and you get in on the "wave" at the very beginning or shortly thereafter this happnes. Having teh trix been a color for a while and then getting in when it crosses 0 [but has been that color for some time] puts a flag up that I shouldn't expect too much out of the trade.

Hello, SpecialED: Your post is very important. I used to trade in h1 timeframe, I guest the the rule may be simple more. 1. the entry : M1F light + H1 cloud histo's same color. 2. the exit: M30F light changes OR key lines. I just trade forex for 3 years, I want to listen opinion from you. [quote=SpecialEd;2706363]Hello all, My rules for entry: 1. At least 4 out of these 5 lights (M15F, M15S, M30F, M30S, H1F) must be red for short and green for long. 2. M30 and H1 Cloud histo's must be red for short, or green for long. M30 can be yellow but should never be opposing color. It is a much better trade when both are the same color. I never trade with H1 cloud light opposing color. Rules for exit: 1. Don't be greedy. Decide how many PIPs you conservatively want to earn and TP in front of some pivot or psych. 2. TP/exit when M30F light changes colors at the close of a 30M candle. 3. Set your SL according to either the ATR or 40-50 PIPs, according to your risk appetite. Be sure to check H1 analysis chart to help confirm the trend. Always best to go with the trend.

--- 帖子 #12227 ---
Yes. I read that this current build of MT4 will be the last supported. There is much discussion about this new MT5 and how it will only benefit the brokers, not us. For example, no more individual orders, they all get lumped together. "First in, first out" order execution. No TP/SL, have to place a buy/sell stop instead. Inability to modify an open order. No more hedging too. All since the self governing, NFA made these rules in the U.S. So none of this applies to the UK yet, BUT, MT5 will behave the same way anyway! but if you are manually trading with one position, and just adding positions, then you won't notice anything to your style, but for many folks this is a huge disappointment which just forces us to make more trades, pay the spread more etc. The NFA, as well as Metatrader work to satisfy the brokers, not us, as it seems. edit added: there is some talk or hope, that some brokers, probably mostly non-NFA members, who say they will continue to allow trades from MT4. There apparently is a platform called ProTrader which places trades in MQ4 language. FXCM has given their clients a window to move their accounts to their UK based office, so as to avoid these new restrictions.

Using our proprietary backoffice solutions, Interbank FX will allow our Meta Trader 4 platform to remain 100 percent compliant, while retaining order functionality and flexibility for customers trading. The MT4 platform will continue to function as our customers have experienced over the last several years. This includes the ability for customers to use fully functional Expert Advisors, Stops Losses, Take Profits, Trailing Stops and Limit Orders without making any needed adjustments. "Certain US competitors have decided that their solution to the new FIFO rules are to move their customers overseas, rather than being compliant," said Todd Crosland, Chairman and President of Interbank FX. "At Interbank FX, we have embraced the NFA's efforts to help protect customers and provide a seamless solution without any changes to their current trading strategies." The only modification for customers will be their daily and monthly account statements, coming directly from the proprietary Interbank FX backoffice system using NFA FIFO offsetting procedures. The FIFO rule takes effect beginning July 31/August 1, 2009. Interbank FX is currently working on a step-by-step video which will be available shortly on our web site, www.ibfx.com . http://www.ibfx.com/media/Images/NewVisitor/line.png Does FIFO apply to all of my trades? First in / First out applies ONLY to trades of the same size. Will my Expert Advisor still work? All of your Expert Advisors will continue to work with all of your pre-programmed stops, limits and trailing stops. Will I still be able to use Stops and Limits, Trailing Stops and Take Profits? Absolutely – With the IBFX solution, you won’t have to make any changes from the way that you are trading currently. No need to make any adjustments to Stops and Limits, Trailing Stops or Take Profits. Will I still be able to close any of my orders of the same currency pair in any order? Yes, with the IBFX solution, your trading will still be fully functional without any changes to your current trading strategies. How will this affect my daily statements? Interbank FX Official Statements will come directly from Interbank FX’s proprietary back office system using our FIFO offsetting and accounting procedures. --- 帖子 #12260 ---
Hello Johnny: I'll pitch in my 2 cents....Doblece put it that scalping (properly, I'll elaborate) usually has very high hit rates, and so one can still be profitable with a 1:2 ratio. I recall Misspips' hit rates were sometimes higher than that when she was testing the MTF system. If one's hit rate is 70% and you take 8 pips out that's 56 pips and 45 pips loss, net 11 pips... Having said that, a person does not only take out 8 pips, sometimes you're gonna take out more, 10, 12 15...whatever, and I, do not always let myself get stopped out. If it's is totally obvious that I entered a wrong trade, I'll cut my losses short. Therefore scalping properly should be profitable...I know it is easier said than done.... The second point is that scalping the 1 min does not mean that we're only observing the 1 min chart. Even with the MTF, higher time frames should be used at all times...there are things in the chart you cannot see clearly even when zoomed out totally. I believe that most people including Cobra, Misspips, Scrutch and the rest that do use the 1 min are entering on the 1 min based on what they see on higher time frames. They can correct me if I am wrong... The last point is that exiting, more often that not, is more difficult than finding the right entry...and in the words of Cobra, it takes serious screen time to get a good feeling of when and how to exit... Everyone should be using higher time frames and trend lines, fibs, and pivots...I hope this helps... Cashmeer.

Hi Bobkat: Creating an image on metatrader: on the program 1) click on file. 2) Next click on save as picture. 3) Then select active chart (as is). 4) Enter a name for the image. Uploading images on forex factory: 1) click on post reply. 2) On "Thread Options" click "Manage Attachments". 3) Click on Browse to find your image on your PC. 4) Click on "Upload". 5)Finally, click on "Submit Reply". Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #12388 ---
I added an auto tf feature to the MTF trix so you can switch between tfs without having to reset the indie by hand. If Autotimeframe is true it uses the next higher period instead of the current one (i.e on a 1 m chart it uses 5) If Autotimframe2 is true it uses 2 periods up (i.e on a 1 m chart it uses 15) You still need THV T3 Trix in the indies folder in order for it to work.

I would suggest adding the files one by one to a completely clean chart rather than using the template that comes with THV in order to find out which one is causing the problem. This is the setup for the basic THV and all you really need. If all is still well, try adding the other indies like the ATR and the pivots.

--- 帖子 #12404 ---
xpma is like a swiss army knife of MAs. If you want to use a t3 or JMA, yes you need them. But MODE_DEMA (4 ) which imitates the Coral is a Double Exponential moving average. I don't have either of them in my indies folder and it works just fine with type 4. From the source (which I would have posted but I lost the source that has the mtf capability somewhere) MODE_SMA 0 Simple moving average, MODE_EMA 1 Exponential moving average, MODE_SMMA 2 Smoothed moving average, MODE_LWMA 3 Linear weighted moving average. MODE_DEMA 4 Double Exponential Moving Average. MODE_TEMA 5 Triple Exponential Moving Average. MODE_T3MA 6 T3 Moving Average. MODE_JMA 7 Jurik Moving Average. case 4: { for(i=0; i&lt;limit; i++) { tempbuffer[i] = iMA(NULL,0,MA_Period,0,MODE_EMA,MA_Applied,i); } for(i=0; i&lt;limit; i++) { matriple[i] = iMAOnArray(tempbuffer,0,MA_Period,0,MODE_EMA,i); } for(i=0; i&lt;limit; i++) { buffer[i] = iMAOnArray(matriple,0,MA_Period,0,MODE_EMA,i); } } break; case 6: { for(i=0; i&lt;limit; i++) { buffer[i] = iCustom(NULL,0,"T3MA",MA_Period,T3MA_VolumeFactor,0,i); } } break; case 7: { for(i=0; i&lt;limit; i++) { buffer[i] = iCustom(NULL,0,"JMA",MA_Period,JMA_Phase,0,i); } }

What makes EY [AKA EJ. EUR/JPY, "The Dragon"] appealing to trade it almost 24 hours a day is that is has EUR [traded during London session. also attached to NY session for USD, so EUR/USD and GPB/USD will a lot of times make similar moves [mirror] JPY--Asian trading currency -'nuff said. EJ is much more favorable to trade [IMO] because everyone is trading EU--even the robots taking bites out of the market--that' s why the PA can get so choppy--those robots hop on at even the slightest divergence in the trend. And EJ will usually mirror GU's moves Only thing is this pair is more volatile, so use less leverage and bigger S/L's...trends on this pair don't sit and bounce around for awhiile deciding where to go. It alsways moves somewhere, and usually in a hurry.

Often when setting my TP, I use my H1 and M15 charts to determine where I think price is going. My TP will be around that, and I'll walk away from the trade to let it "percolate". Good luck.

--- 帖子 #12441 ---
Trendlines and knowing how to properly draw them, is an oh so important! factor in trading. As nice as it may seem, one can not just simply trade the signals given to them by indicators. down trends the trendline is by drawing a line from the highs--then you are looking for a clean break [and preferably a test] of this trendline, not just the PA crossing through and the candle closing on it. up trends are opposite, with trend lines on the bottom. Your targets after the trend is confirmed over, is that of the previous swing high/low--might have to zoomed out on the screen. then after each "wave" the next target is the 2nd previous and so on until a new trend is formed.
