Hi McFly, I can share what works for me. The trick is to have enough rules so that you aren't just taking every trade you see, but not so many that you cant take a trade because of analysis paralysis First of all I only trade EURUSD half an hour after london open to london close. (usually. I actually start watching the market 2 hours before London open, and if I see a really nice trend developing during that time I will get in) I never trade when anybody is on holiday. I never trade half an hour before to 15m after major news. I only trade in the direction of the trend (very important! I came to the conclusion that for me, divergence trades against the trend are more bother than they are worth) I only place a trade when there is room for it to go 10 pips before hitting a pivot line. When I get my daily pips I quit trading real trades. So the crucial thing for me is to define a trend. If I dont see one that meets my definitions I don't trade and that's that. How do I define a trend? I use the rainbow. (The reason I use the rainbow is because it makes very clear which direction the trend is in, or it makes clear that there is no trend.) I want to see 1) The rainbow reverse 2) 3 moderate higher highs with retracements that respect the spine of the rainbow 3) PA respecting the reversal line and the Coral 4) PA clearing the red, gold and blue MAs (representing the 5,15 and 30 coral) Once I get this, I can take trades. My favorite trade is a THV 6 point trade after I see this, where the Coral is lined up between the blue and green layers and PA has cleared a Pivot line. These are really very high probability trades on the Euro because once it really gets going it can't stop on a dime ( for example the last trade on the black screen.) I am posting screenshot with the trades you could have taken today that meet these condtions. (I didn't take any of them today because of the Canadian bank holiday though. I want all the players at the party when I play.However, you get this same situation day after day.) You can see that every one of these trades (both classic THV trix crosses and 6 point trades) were winners (i.e never went 15 pips against you before giving you at least 10 pips). I have also marked the trades I would have ignored, because they were against the trend even though they met the THV classic rules. I am also posting a screenshot of a day where I didn't trade because I couldn't find an orderly trend. Mostly however, you will have one of these orderly trends every day. (Some, however, last longer than others and some days you may have to wait a while to get one.)

--- 帖子 #12449 ---
All markets are working with Support and Resistance. That S&amp;R are the levels of prices a buyer wants to pay and a seller is willing to sell. It’s called also offer and demand. Let’s say you are a minor apple dealer, it’s early in the morning and you want to buy apples, the price is 2 $ a kilo, there are plenty of other fruits in the market with a similar price, that means the apple has competition and the market price is acceptable. The price is established since several weeks (ranging). You buy them and sell to your customers on the local market price of 2.50. Now we are in winter season and the apple price raised to 3.50$ and few other fruits are in offer, a kilo of banana is in 4.50, you want fruits and think to pay the 3.50 because you have no better offers yet, even talking to the seller in the market half an hour he resists (isn’t willing) to give you the apples in 3 $, you walked around in the market to compare prices, some sell apples in 3.90 but your resistance to buy them is 3.50 because that’s the offer of the kind mayor fruit seller you visited before. The resistance is 3.90, the highest price in the market, because people buy them for some reason, if that seller would offer them in 4.50 $ nobody would buy them and he will lose on his biz because the apples are damaged after a while. You walked around in the market too much time and was unsure what to buy and decide to get those apples from the first seller but unfortunately, as his price was cheap, he sold all of them. Now you go back to the 3.90 seller and he raised the price to 4.20, short under the price of the bananas, the resistance of 3.90 $ broke as there are no other products, this mayor seller is the only one in the market who is able to sell apples and you buy them. You lost a good opportunity to buy the apples in a good mayor market price. You had to sell these apples in your local community in 4.70 and the expected sells haven’t been good as your competence sell in 4.00$ because the bought from the friendly mayor seller in 3.50 $, you have left half of the apples at the end of the day. Next morning you hear that several trucks with new apples arrived in the mayor market with a price of 3.20 and you decide to sell yours quickly in 3.90$ and the very remaining lot in 3.70 $ before your competence arrives in few hours with the new product. The local support of 4.00 is broken. The same happens in FX, we have two different buyers, speculative ones that hold their position until they are in profit or SL hit and governments and big customers which purchase goods in other countries and need to change currencies to pay the seller. This second ones also try to get the best price to change and wait for a good opportunity. One cent or less in several millions makes a huge difference for them. How we define those good opportunities to buy and sell looking at our charts? A chart is made out of historic price levels on relation of time. S&amp;R are formed by historical highs and lows, a previous support form a resistance in the future. We want to enter and exit at these points as we can’t move the market with our low equity in relation to market makers and we need to go with the market as we can’t manipulate it. We need to think like the market maker, when to buy cheap and sell with a good gain. Market makers watch S&amp;R formed by pivots, historical S&amp;R and/or fibs, those are usually turn points of trends until they get broken. The best bet in Day trading and Scalping is the FIRST bounce back of those S&amp;R and sometimes we need to wait patiently until the price gets there. The higher the time frame you are drawing your S&amp;R, the better the probability of your trade. A second part will follow . Please let me know if this is helpful to understand market behavior or you say that Cobra has a loosen screw.

Hello, this is my first post after my more or less frustraded statement yesterday. After spending alot of time with reading and understanding trading basics and methods I have noticed there are similarities between the theories of trading and theories of sport sience. In both cases there exist a massive amount of systems which partly disagree considerably. Some examples: Trader N.1: To me price action is what it is ALL about. I scalp the 1 min tf, I don't care about fibs, pivots, higher time frames and so on. If priceaction and my indicators show go I take the trade. I take 5 to 15 pips without managing the trade. Trader N.2: I trade the higher timeframes only. Everything shorter than 1 h is noise. I buy/ sell ONLY in the direction of the major trend and I buy/sell on dips (Use support lines to guide you as to price...also "round" numbers ... I also use the 50% Fib ratio..). If the trend is up over months I only go long. Managering the trade is important. I don't use indicators or MAs. I look at fundamentals. Trader N.3: I don't worry about the fundamental side of trading, trading itself is emotional enough. I agree with trading with the trend but I will go against it if the setup is right. My system is based on MAs which act as floating s/r. I use them for balance points and price targets for profit taking... These are the summaries of system developed by well known and very successful traders which are active in the ff board. This shows that the question whether a trader is successful or not depends on the trader and not on the timeframe or the trading tools. I wouldn't say 1 min isn't tradeable or pitchforks is the ultimate trading tool. It's up to me how good things work. Therefore cobras system doesn't fit me or I make mistakes. From my point of view I know at least one mistake I have made. I tried to included as much information as possible. The forum is full of blinking and flashing indicators and tools. I think I put too much of them in the thv system and lost the overview. Too much distraction and not enough focusing. I'm sure I did that because the less indicators you use the more trading skill you need to earn pips. Skill means things like reading price action, knowing when it trends and when it's choppy and so on. I have not enough expirience to acquire this kind of skill. Thus I relyed on indicators to get more confidence.

By 6 point trade I mean trade when 6 out of 10 lights agree on the mtf histograms (1m f 5m f , 5m s, 15m f, 15m s, 30m f, 30m s, 60m f trix and 5m and 15 cloud). This method is described in the manual on the first page. There were two main ideas behind this method: 1) To provide some rules for when you can take divergence trades 2) To provide some additional entries besides just a trix cross for trend entries. (i.e you can trade when the 1m fast turns green but you don't have a trix cross or slow trix green yet). This is the reason I required that the 5 m fast also be green for 6 point trades, because trading when just the 1m fast turns green (before a trix cross and before the 1m s trix is green) is riskier (or vice versa for shorts of course). But regular THV trades (trix crosses when PA is above/below the cloud and Coral are perfectly good trades in and of themselves. [quote=bythepound;2928609]

There are lots of threads about it here at FF. I don't trade the Rainbow per say (that has it's own set of rules and you need a lot of screen time for it.) What I do is use the Rainbow to help me trade THV with the trend. (Everyone always says 'trade with the trend' but how do we know when there is a trend? On the rainbow you can see it very clearly. It's also a very good visual aid for picking out choppy price action.) So I use it as my analysis template to analyze whether PA is trending or choppy so I can know when to take THV trades, and which direction to take them in. (For example yesterday after about 915 GMT, it was clear from the rainbow that THV short trades should be avoided, even if PA was below the cloud and the coral, and the THV classic or 6 point rules would otherwise indicate taking them.) You could also use it to decide when to take THV countertrend (divergence) trades when it shows choppy price action if you wanted to though I don't do that. (Those THV trades would have worked great today)

--- 帖子 #12498 ---
Everyone's trying to find the "Holy Grail" and I'm going to tell you, you aren't going to be able to find it in Forex. People have different ways of thinking, and respond to different stimuli, so one person's setup [indicators] might not "compute" for another, thus making the system less effective for the other person. Yes, you can suffer from "Analysis by Paralysis". So many indicators on a screen that you're trying to line up every one and by that time you're too late to enter the trade, or you sit for hours... and you go stir crazy. I'm not going to criticize the Rainbow, [although pretty--you really only need 3or 4 MA's] but it should only be used for analysis. On Miss Pip's Rainbow EU chart today-- I saw 4 valid trades each 10-30 pips strictly using trendlines and understanding *fully* how to interpret the Trix indicator--- and using support/resist levels Yes, Rainbow shows trend, but if you only use 3 or 4MA's -[my MA's are different than rainbows] but perhaps if you like the rainbow, just choose 1 MA from each color -preferable the lowest one from each--so it's not too smoothed- Then you are able to see true ATR [Average True Range] as well as volatility of the PA. The more angle and separation between the lines, the better trading conditions. If all the lines are making knots or look like a spaghetti bowl, then you stay out. Just because the lines start crossing doesn't mean it's not tradeable. It's when they become intertwined. Traders need to step back and realize Forex is not a get rich scheme. I, like most, started, failed, got frustrated, went back to just a plain chart, thought I found another system-added more junk to the screen, wasn't satisfied with the action becasue the indicators were limiting, started doing weird stuff again, failed yet again--then took a real hard look at what would be realistic in terms of gains [achievable daily] I then read everything I could about Forex fundamentals--how to properly draw trendlines on every TF-- candlestick patterns, Patterns within the PA--knowing to recognize triangles and flags, understanding S/R and psych levels, reading the news pertaining to the pair[s] I want to trade, and setting a daily goal--trust me once you find a setup that works for you and you start doing good like I did, I turned crazy and literally was on the computer every single moment I could. --Not good for family life. 2% a day is very achievable on an account--even 1--- compound that and you'll be rich in a short time One needs to first decide which TF they want to trade from- each pair is different, and certain TF's are suitable for different pairs on trading--like I would never trade EUR/GBP on a 1 or 5M TF. Like wise, with the volatilty, I wouldn't trade GU/GY on 1M --as well as 30M or higher ---unless I wanted to lower my leverage and be ready for some severe DD. Then you need to decide what indicators work for you--- there are different variations of THV--- just like all systems, people have added their own flavors--- have to find the ones you think are useful and make sense to you so you can apply them to your chart. Let's keep this simple folks.

I think you kind of missed the point of my posts today IrishPips, which were not about the 'Holy Grail'. McFly stated he was having trouble and asked some other traders to share what is working for them, so I decided to put in on the line and share, in 'real time' my thinking process for the trades I was taking or not taking today as I was taking (or not taking) them. It also has nothing to do with 'understanding *fully* how to interpret the Trix indicator'. I saw those other trades too - that's why I mentioned that a trader who trades like Cashmeer using trendlines and divergence would have a field day today. What it has to do with is 1) Recognizing what type of market you are in and 2) Trading the appropriate style of trade for that market - i.e trendline breaks/divergence trades in a choppy market and trades only with the trend only on a strongly trending day. ( You have to be a pretty experienced trader to do this, which McFly has stated he is not.) OR (A BIG OR) 3) Simply deciding which style of trading you prefer and waiting for market conditions that conform to the type of trading you like to do. I personally have just decided that I find it more comfortable to trade the 1 m when there is a recognizable trend (which I have clearly defined in terms of how the rainbow should look in order for me to consider it a trend) and that's why I didn't take those other trades. As for keeping it simple I think throughout the thread you will find people advising newer traders to stick to simple trades with the trend, and avoid the trickier trades like divergence trades which were the kind of trades that were working best today. Trend trades are usually more worthwhile too - note that if you had been trading several lots, and intending to hang onto one of them none of those other trades you could have taken would have gone anywhere today. The one trade I saw which conformed to my definition of a trend on the 1 m tf was unfortunately a retrace trade contra to the daily trend so it didn't go too far either. However, in it's favor it also did not go against me at all, which is more than I can say for many of the other possible trades today. And on yesterday's trend trade there were 100 plus pips in that second lot, depending where you got in. The *BIG* problem of course is if you are going to keep it simple and trade with the trend - How do you know when you have a trend? I find the rainbow 'as is' the best method I have seen for distinguishing between trending PA and choppy PA, so that's why I use it for analysis and that's why I shared my definition of a trend using it. I'm sure that if anyone else has other methods of distinguishing between the two we would all enjoy seeing screenshots, especially in real time as it is happening.

Hi McFly, No, I had only one short trade and one long trade at 1027 GMT (1337 on my charts). The long trade was according to the 6 point rules which means I need 6 of the 10 lights in favor of the trade, and two of them must be the 1m f trix and the 5m fast trix. You can see that in my trix hist in my regular THV template, my trix histogram in my white rainbow analysis template and my mtf trix in my black rainbow analysis template the 5m trix is green. That having been said, when I have found a trend to my liking I will take THV trades of either flavor - Cobra's original rules or the 6 point rules. Only the 6 point rules require the 5m f trix to be in the direction of the trade. This is because using this method you are getting in the trade earlier(without waiting for a trix cross) when the 1m f trix has just turned in your favor but the 1m s trix may not be and there has not been a trix cross. In that case I consider it prudent to have the 5m fast in your favor as well. If I am taking a regular THV trade I don't care about the 5m trix, because these trix cross trades are pretty safe as they are in a good trend.

--- 帖子 #12542 ---
I do not trade the rainbow per se. (That has its own set of rules and you need a lot of screen time practicing to do it well.) I use the rainbow as my analysis template to help me see whether price action is choppy or trending. before I take a THV trade. I have decided that I prefer to trade THV trades with the trend, so I wait until I see what I have defined as trend on the rainbow before I enter a THV trade. The big problem with all the advice about trading with the trend is how do you define a trend? I define a trend on the 1m chart as when I see 1) Three higher highs and higher lows (preferably moderately increasing with each wave, with moderate retracements - these seem to make for the best trends.) Or vice versa three lower lows and lower highs for shorts. These have to be after the rainbow has turned, and the retracements need to respect the spine of the rainbow. 2) PA respecting the coral and the reversal line. 3) All the colors of the rainbow visible (preferably with the coral lined up between the green and blue layers of the rainbow on the yellow template or the green and gold or green and blue layers on the black tempate at about the point the trade is entered. This is not a must but I have noticed this usually makes for a good trade) 4) PA having crossed the MAs representing the 5, 15 and 30m corals. (Sometimes, if there is a lot of room between the 15 and 30 m corals and I like the shape of the trend, I will get in after it has just crossed the 15m coral. That would be in periods where we are having better ranges than we have lately though) After I see PA that meets my definition of a trend on the 1m chart, then I look for a THV regular or 6 point trade. What trading like this actually amounts to is getting in on the first decent retracement after a THV signal has been given on the 15 or 30 tfs, depending on where you get in. So I find it more relaxing than trying to grab every signal on the 1m chart. If you wanted to be more agressive, you could get in when you see a signal after 3 higher highs (or lower lows), all the colors visible, PA respecting the spine and the Coral and just crossing the MA representing the 5m coral. If you like to trade divergence trades, you can wait until you see choppy price action and then trade Thv Divergence trades too -I don't but it's up to you how you use it. If you look at my previous posts you can see my definintions of choppy and trending PA in screenshots where I think it is easier to understand than reading about it.

--- 帖子 #12579 ---
Since you are having trouble with the files, I would do the following: Remove all the THV files from your MT4 indies folder and your templates folder. Restart MT4. Is all well? Then proceed as follows: Start with just the basic THV system. Copy all the files from the V3 zip file to your indies folder, without adding any files or templates to your charts yet. Restart your MT4. Is all still well? Then proceed as follows: Start by using the basic THV and add just the minimum files which are The Ichimoku set to 2,3,5 with the colors for Tenkan san, Kinjan san and ChinKou Span set to none. (The Ichimoku comes with MT4. ) The THV3 Coral The THV3 Trix v4.01 Div.ex4. I would suggest adding the files one by one to a completely clean chart rather than using the template that comes with THV in order to find out which one is causing the problem. This is the setup for the basic THV and all you really need. If all is still well, you can try adding the other indies like the ATR and the pivots and the mtf files although if you are new to the system, you should probably start with the basic THV rather than the MTF THV until you have some experience with the system. Add them one by one so you can find out which one is causing the problem.

--- 帖子 #12605 ---
Hi McFly, Well, here a few reasons why I took that trade. 1) The actual trend was established from my point of view at the first count of 1, 2, 3 lower lows, though I didn't take a trade there because I didn't like the two higher highs I saw in the retracements. After the market has made a big push down, it can retrace a lot but I will still consider it a trend as long as the rainbow is still intact. I think I've mentioned that in a previous post (11969) that we can have a long retrace after a trend is established and still take trades, and that's also why I wrote on that screen that if you want to be cautious you could wait for another 1,2,3 sequence there but you don't have to. I could have taken the first trade there even without waiting for another 1, 2, 3 sequence, but the fact that it did go outside the spine on the black rainbow is why I decided to wait for one. 2) I use both the rainbow templates that I posted to evaluate trades. The black one is faster, the white one is more conservative about the trend (shows it turning more slowly.) On the white one PA did respect the spine. 3) You do have to use some judgement. The first excursion outside the spine that you circled is not counted in the 1,2,3 count, because it is before the first low that I count. I could see that the second one, which I did count was lower than the first one, and that they were both bouncing off the gold line, which is the 5 m coral. So I thought that was a good sign. We are talking about interest rate statement day here, so we could expect a little more volatility than normal. 4) Even I am not perfect. If I have waited all day for a trade and I see one that meets my definitions 95%, I will take it, even if for example one of the peaks or one of the retraces is a little less moderate than I would normally like. I will take overall market conditions into account. (For example, if PA has been coiled up for 3 hours in a very small range trying to crack the pivot and then cracks it with a bigger jump that I would normally like to see, I will take that into account and still count that as one of the bumps as long as there are 3 higher highs or lower lows.) In this case you could clearly see that in the big picture the trend is down, so I felt pretty safe taking that trade. What had happend that day is that the market had bounced around the MAs all morning, but worked itself slightly below them prior to news. Then it had a sharp move down on the news about the pound, and then it bounced around some more. Then it had another sharp move down on Euro news, and then a retracement. At the point I took the trade it had started back down again and the rainbow was still intact. Once the market has bounced around a good long time (as it did all that morning), and then it decides on a direction but has not yet completed it's daily range in that direction , it is not likely to just up and turn around on you just because that's where you decided to enter, before it does another 10 pips - unless there is some major support in the way of the trade, which there was not at that point. So that's why I took I took that trade.

I trade M15 these days and have a basket of 16 pairs from which to choose. So every morning I am looking for pairs which will trend for a long period. --- 帖子 #12643 ---
Hi Johnny, I know there are updates to the indicators that haven't been posted, but basically the ones on the front page work just fine. There are also two manuals on the front page that explain two methods of trading (regular, and MTF using the trix histo) and give all the rules for both methods, which have not changed. I think one of the things that confuses people is that when they see "Trading sytem" they may be expecting a mechanical system, and that they can just take a trade when they get a signal. However THV is a actually a discretionary system (as opposed to, for example, a purely mechanical system like the one in a very well known web site which trades the pound based on an MA cross, a MACD signal and a stochastics signal. In that system, when you see the rules met you take the trade.) In THV, when you see a signal, what it means, as the indicator itself says is Analyze Buy" or Analyze Sell." This means exactly what it says: Before taking the trade you need to do your own analysis of whether now is an appropriate time to take the trade. (As one example: You need to check if there is some contra indication to the trade (like a pivot in the way for example, or a divergence.) Here are some of the questions you need to answer for yourself which are not answered in either manual: 1) What will you consider a contraindication to a trade? For example: Will you forgo trades that are too close to a pivot, or are you purely momentum based and you will take them as long as there is enough momentum. Will you trade around news time? If so/not, what kind of news events will you count/ignore? And how long will the no trade window be? Will you trade if the previous peak/low had a divergence, or will you only consider mutliple divergences to be significant. Or will you consider/ignore divergence based on market condtions (choppy/trending). 2) What will you use as the TP and the stop? For example: Do you want to use the suggested 3 times the ATR for the stop and half the ATR for the TP, or do you want to use a fixed target like 15 pips for the stop and 10 pips for the target? Or do you want to manage the trade some other way, like getting out when the fast trix turns against you ? Or do you want to trail your stops? 3) What kind of trades to you prefer? For exampe: Do you prefer trend trades, or contra-trend divergence trades? Or do you like a lot of action, and want to take both kinds? And if so, are you experienced enough to tell the difference between a choppy market and a strongly trending market? 4) What tf do you prefer: 1m, 5m 15m or daily. 5) What hours and how long do you want to trade every day? Will you have any rules for when to quit (for example when you hit your daily TP or have 3 losing trades in a row?). 6) Do you want to trade regular THV trades based just the coral, Ichimoku and trix cross on one timeframe or the MTF version? If you prefer MTF, do you want a broader view over many timeframes (as the histograms provide) or is the shape of the trix and where it is in relation to the zero line more important to you (as the MTF trix provides) than many timeframes? Or can you afford three monitors? And more. It's impossible to put all these things into two small manuals, and the result of this is that each person has developed for themselves a set of answers that result in their own decisions about when to take a trade once a proper signal has been given. Some prefer to trade trend signals that coincide with bounces at support and resistance at pivots and trendlines. Some prefer divergence signals that coincide with bounces off pivots and trendlines or trendline breaks. Some prefer the 1m tf while others prefer longer tfs. Some prefer the MTF flavors, others do not. And so on.. In addtion to that basic toolkit on the trading template, many have added their own favorite indicators to their analysis template, whether it be heatmaps and rainbows to discover trend, MTF trixes, ICCE to discover targets, or commercial indicators. Each person has worked out what set of answers is most sucessful for himself (or herself) and some have shared that. That is why there is so much different looking information in the thread. You will notice however, that everyone has some things in common: everyone is basing their trades on the trix, and the position of PA relative to the Coral (except for divergence trades, then you can ignore the Coral.) I guess the bottom line here is that given the same basic toolkit, each person has to work out for himself what his favorite flavor of THV is.

Easiest fix is open your program indi directory which will be located somewhere like: "C:&gt;Program Files&gt;YOUR_BROKER&gt;experts&gt;indicators" Delete the files THV3 FFCal.mq4 and THV3 FFCal.ex4 Now copy &amp; paste the attached version of THV3 FFCal.mq4 back into the directory. Hi Folks There have been a discussion on the 25% that makes the system and 75% relies on the trader (the percentage can change with the probability of a system). There are some very important points on trading in general which I’d like to highlight with this post. I’m a trader since more than 30 years (not FX) buying and selling whatever I thought it gives me a profit. I traded from lemons to multiple families houses. Let’s say you bought a truckload of potatoes to satisfy a high, overpriced demand in your local market, you need to know what the competence is doing and when there are new potatoes with a regular price available to sell your remaining product before they arrive with a better price than you’ve paid. Also would be helpful to know how this temporal overpriced demand was created. We could call these circumstances fundamentals. It’s necessary to know about average prices during the seasons of the product you are trading. We could call that technical. You know that you need to sell your remaining product fast at be equal or maybe a little loss in case that the competence comes up with a cheaper product with the same or similar quality. We can call that our Stop Loss. The single most important mental point of trading is that you feel comfort with your decision when to buy and sell. That let you sleep well during the period of your actual business and don’t lead you to panic buys or sells . You simply know what you are doing, you studied the risk and also put on your trading plan the possible reward, at the end you decide that you are fine with that biz. In all business of the world you can win and lose, in case that the potatoe deal didn't work out look for another one, maybe there are 2 inch nails missing somewhere. Have a great day all. Add: a translater tells me that instead of competence I may use competition but important is that you know what I mean, lol.

--- 帖子 #12752 ---
Hi McFly, As has been mentioned, there are many different styles of trading THV and several people have shared their favorite setups. Cashmeer has shared his divergence setup, and his trendline break in the Trix setup. I have shared Rainbow trend trade setups. IrishPips has shared an MTF setup. And I'm sure more people have shared other setups that I haven't mentioned. If you try to work with them all, you will go nuts. My advice is: Instead of trying to grab as many pips as you can from all the setups, find just one clearly defined setup that you like. Add just the elements you need for that one, and trade just that one until you can do it perfectly (i.e. you never fail to recognize it, you never fail to pull the trigger, and you never fail to use the appropriate MM, stops and targets.) If you are trading the Rainbow trend setups, I use both the regular pivots in the pivotpointsmultitimeframe indie (daily, weekly and monthy) and the THV Fibonacci pivots. However, if you have waited until a trend has started and worked itself above/below the MAs representing the 5, 15, and 30 corals, you will almost always find a place to trade where you have 10 pips of space between the trade and the next pivot line. I personally have the Camarillia lines, the open, yesterdays low and high lines on my one of my analysis charts but I don't worry about them unless there is a big constellation of a few together. Otherwise I just worry about the pivot lines ( and the S1, R1 etc ). I also ignore sweetspots and psyche levels except the ones with 3 zeros (1.4000 etc). However if you get 3 to five different types of resistance all clustered together within a few pips of each other and you see divergence in the trix that might be a good place not to take a trade in the direction of the trend ( for example a Camarilla line, a mid pivot line, the open line and a Fib line all together within 10 pips of each other). I also pay attention to the daily range, and when it's done for the day so am I. Two good places to take a trade are: 1) After a pivot line is broken and you get a retest and bounce off of it in the direction of the rainbow together with a THV signal and you have 10 pips between the trade and the next line. 2) After a pivot line has NOT been broken and you get a THV signal in the direction of the rainbow AND the bounce caused a big enough retrace that you have 10 pips of room between the signal and where the trade is going to retest the line. Because if it doesn't break on the retest at least you get your 10 pips. If it breaks on the retest and you have 2 lots in you can manage the second lot by hand and get more.

You're welcome! Another point is that you don't have to be 100% precise. Say, for example you have a nice trend going (lots of red lights, nice looking rainbow) and it is fairly new, and you get a bounce off a pivot point away from the trend and you only have 8 pips of profit in the trade before the retest. You can decide to go for it anyway, because odds are even if it doesn't break it, it will go a few pips past it. Or you can wait a bar after the signal and see if you can get an extra pip or two on a small retrace.

Hi Folks, I would like to get the opinion of the experienced traders in this forum regarding the use of S&amp;R, pivot points, and Fibonacci lines. It would seem that more often than not, these tools actually hinder me from taking good trades and cause me to get out of perfectly good trades prematurely. Is it me, or do any of you suffer from the same problem? As many of you have done, I have spent hundreds of hours back-testing THV and many other systems. I feel that THV is by far the best of breed. The Trix indicators are among the best available, and this is way I use them as the backbone of my trading. So to be clear, my problem is not with the Trix, it’s with all of the trading roadblocks resulting from the pivots and fibo lines. I have declared many times in the past that I would not hesitate taking a trade despite pivots and fibo lines and simply trade the indicators. From a back testing perspective, I would have been far more profitable had I ignored them instead of respecting them. You see, when you back test, the fibo lines and pivot points are not there (once you go more than 12-24 hours back in time). Look at all of the good entries THV offers without the roadblocks posed by the pivots and fibo lines! Today alone I passed on a few good trades (those that would have yielded at least 10 pips) because despite the fact the Trix indicators said to take the entry, I hesitated because of the pivots and fibo lines. The one trade I did take caused me to only lose .4 pips, but had I stayed in the trade ignoring the DP, I would have made at least 10 pips, as the PA crashed right through it. I went short at 7:00 am EST and the DP was at 1.4105 (I use the SDX pivots). I see similar trades many times everyday! Sure, you should be aware that the pivots and fibos are there, but do they REALLY matter? How many times did the PA REALLY respect these lines? As a result of the back testing I have considered taking fibos and pivots off of my charts and just using good old fashioned, hand drawn S&amp;R. To me, it’s about reducing the clutter, chaos, and analysis paralysis. These are my thoughts, what are yours?

--- 帖子 #12763 ---
Hi bythepound, It depends on how you use those pivots/fib/SR. Do you use them as warning lines telling you to be aware or action lines telling you to take certain actions. Besides pivots that can be easily calculated, fib and S/R levels are dependent on the person who draws them and is thus subjective. Do they matter? Again it depends. Let me explain. If there is strong momentum, pivots/fib/SR cannot hold/contain price. But momentum will always exhaust itself and then the next pivot/fib/SR comes in play and higher chance to hold/contain price. On the contrary, if momentum is weak, any pivot/fib/SR will be able to contain price and force a price bounce or pullback. Simplistically speaking, if you see a candle with body longer than surrounding candles, then you have momentum building up. If you see two or three of them going into a steeper slope, normally it means momentum is strong. Of course there is more to it than what I wrote here. As traders, we need to gauge how strong a move is and not treat every pivot, S/R or fib level as a sure line where price will "respect". Again, by respect I mean price hesitating on those lines before moving again. Which direction? Who knows? Price Action comes into play. Higher highs or lower lows...etc.. You know what I mean. "Respect" does not mean a sure bounce or pullback. Hope this helps. Cheers, CaveMan

Gang – thanks for the reply about pivots and Fibonacci lines. Caveman, in support of what you said I did go back and found that momentum will cause PA not to respect pivots and fibo lines as much. My wife has been telling me this for months – but I stubbornly ignored such an obvious observation on her part. Momentum seems to be the biggest trump card to pivots and fibos. I show several trades from today that seem to support this. I must say that this is not always the case though – but it does happen more often than not! You will see 3 trades: Trade #1 - 9:40 PM EST: Low momentum fails to push PA up - evidenced by the M30 and M60 Trix. PA action stopped at daily high on fibo – 1.4153 and R1 – 1.4158. This trade yields little pips. Trade#2# 10:25 EST: High momentum easily pushes PA down - evidenced by the M15, M30, and M60 Trix. PA seems to glide through most of the pivots and fibo lines before losing steam. Easy pips here. Trade#3 - 4:00 am EST: Medium momentum evidence by the M15 and M30, but weakness in the M60. Pretty easy glide through several pivots and fibo lines – but do not expect as many pips unless the M60 is adding to the momentum - also more caution with the DP and important fibo lines. After looking at this, the easiest trades (those that did not seem to be blocked by fibo lines and pivots) were those that had a lot of momentum behind them – where the M5 (at least), M15, M30, and M60 were all crossed and going in the same direction. More momentum means that roadblocks (fibos and pivots) don’t have as much significance. Thanks

--- 帖子 #12820 ---
RE updating the MTF histogram indie: If you look in your indies folder after you install the mtf trix histo files, you will see a file called THV3 Trix for MTFHisto. The histogram uses a file of this name instead of a specific version by design. This means that you can copy any of the THV trixes that you like to this file name, and the MTF trix histo will then reflect what that one is doing.

--- 帖子 #12887 ---
A word of warning (and perhaps a question as to why it may occur?) ... I use the Trix V6.01 along with the MTF Trix and have found that the MTF Trix often completely change their display information if I switch from my original M1 main chart, up to a higher timeframe and back again (also happened when I was using previous version main Trix on the main chart). My standard chart is a M1, so the MTF Trix show M5 and M15 (set to 'auto up' their timeframes from the main chart timeframe). If I change the main chart up to M15 or H1 for example and then switch straight back to the M1 again, the MTF Trix that might have originally just showed both grown and a definite up trend for example, may now show red over green - giving me a completely different prognosis of the current market action. The 'difference' (ie. now red over green for example is not just the last couple of candles either, it actually has changed over the last 10 or 20 candles). Just wanted to offer it as something to watch out for so as you don't act off the wrong signal. I now always switch my timeframe up to H1 and straight back again before I trade, to ensure I'm seeing the correct info.

--- 帖子 #12929 ---
I'm going through a phsycological stage of hesitant trigger finger at the moment ... however I found an added mechanism though which may be of help to others: Using the THV M1 as the main timeframe, my actual trades are executed on the Oanda platform with a 10sec chart. I have found that incorporating the age old 1,2,3 method on the 10sec works excellently when combined with the THV M1. By 1,2,3 I'm referring to (using an uptrend move as an example), point 1 is the 2nd most previous low swing point, 2 is the most recent high swing point ... followed of course by some retracement to point 3 which is the most recent low swing point. As price now starts to move up again, the trade is entered the moment price passes point 2. A slight variation to this offering an earlier entry would be of course to look for a mini trendline break (drawn from point 2 to another lower high swing point between point 2 and 3 should there be one) ... but naturally a little more risk attached. This way you're getting in somewhere between point 3 and the climb back towards point 2, without waiting for it to get all the way back to point 2. Typically, your stop loss would be just below point 3 ... but to try and calculate trade size / money management on M1 at this speed is practically impossible, so I tend to just use the 3xATR(20) figure, or often half of this figure to try and achieve a win:loss of 1:1, rather than 1:2. It's not rocket science and this method of trading has been around for ages (and I beleive quite successful) ... certainly looking good when combined with THV in this way to narrow down the entries .

EURUSD - the good: Universally has the lowest spreads of pairs on brokers. Most traded pair of all Forex pairs. Volatility on lower TF's low on non-event days the OK--- this pair can have OK moves provided there's a decent day on the DJIA and/or oil and with news imminent [I mean pre news and after news--not in the hour before/after] the bad-EURUSD [IMO] is overall very choppy--yet the choppiness is predictable pending you have in mind the "magic numbers" AKA psych numbers that it plays around [00 20 50 80] One could literally play between S/R and the numbers taking 10-20 pips [ each time] all day looking for setups in this fashion. The ride to these numbers is often erratic and will drive you mad after while until you've had enough screentime to know the personality of the PA GBPUSD -the good--when she moves--she really moves! Better hang on for the ride and know key support resistance levels because at times once they're hit the whiplash will leave you in the hospital if you didn't exit in time. trending moves not as choppy in PA as EURUSD-- retraces are very predicatble and easy to trade off of for divergence the OK--spreads are higher but worth it as your pip take expectacy is more. Not recommended for "scalping" but for day trading/swing trading the bad--don't ever ever trade this around news times. I can't stress that enough. I don't even think about touching this pair on a day it has news attached to it. Not an hour window or 2 hour window either- I skip the whole day and look for other pairs to trade. You'll thank me later Shakeouts can happen when you think PA is exhausted [S/L hunting] only for your winning trade[now losing as your s/l has been hit] to resume in the direction it was supposed to go. Once known support/ resistances are hit--it's not uncommon to see a 20-50 pip 5M candle on the touch. This might seem a little biased, but this is just from someone who's been there and done that. EURUSD you don't have to do so much for technical studies on the higher TF's like you do for GBPUSD. Good luck PS-Cobra I'm always looking for a free snake bite from you

The truth--- all indicators lag-- there's no doubt about it. Is 6.1 "superior"? IMO, not really, as different pairs have their own personality and with the MA's that comprise the Trix indicator being tuned a number or 2 up doesn't make it the cure for better entries/ exits. it will definitely signal faster, but that doesn't mean your early entry won't suffer an immediate reversal, or for your exit to be premature So the new one might look visually better on a more volatile pair, but be terrible on a slower pair Entries are always best to use your eyes to see PA leave from one point to another-- watch leave an area--keeping in mind how the PA was doing before you decided to start watching it, wait for it to reach an area where it could possible reverse [I say could because known S/R doesn't necessarily mean PA won't plow through it] , if it reverses, look at where it reversed--is it major S/R or a fib level -- divergence trades within a strong trend aren't easy , so if PA was strong it's best to wait for the filed attempt for the PA to comeback to the point feom which you visually marked on your chart when you started watching it. After the failed attempt, you can then hop back on the prevailing trend. I personally prefer the 5.0 as the settings are changeable, and for each TF I have my own preferred At3 and Bt3 settings. The lower the TF the looser the settings need to be for accuracy. And I don't use it for entries/exits either--I use it to see momentum and divergence only and to see where the over all PA lies for trading probability--kinda like a MACD indicator in the sense to the 0 or midline The ability to tune the values on higher TF's has been invaluable to me

I've lately been dabbling in trying to attempt LT trades and I have to admit I failed miserably. Case in point -today Volume is a nice indicator, yes--- other indicators lag, but no matter what they tell, you, more than likely it will be wrong. PA is the only thing you need. Below is a 30M chart of EJ. Sorry about the mess--it might be a little more obvious if the upper TL were blue and the lower TL red. I lost a bet today, and then the person I had a bet with was kind enough to show me how to see the trend and almost exactly where it's going and exactly where the trend starts/ends--as well as where the waves will reverse and start to break down. All you need to do on a 30 M or hour chart is connect each lower low and extend the line out, same with the upper trendline. As soon as the immediate trend changes, draw the top of the wave and extend that too. Keep drawing lines in this fashion..all upper TL's extend out and all lower TL's extend them out too and if there are lines to connect --connect them This is kinda like Gartley, but with all the lines, you can see exactly where the retracements will be, where the trend's strength is, and where the breakdown happens. Shows your range tunnels For this new trend 132.80 will be the ultimate support to break once the topside gets exhausted as it was the converging point I might have missed a few lines, but you get the idea Notice as the trend is ending, the more strength it has the more space there is to move--to the left of the picture is the strength. And to the right is getting out of the congestion phase the the waves will star t to get bigger and more fluid Once one line gets breached, redraw the line --don'r remove it as it's very likely pa will bounce off this area in the futire and it might not be a SR line and you're trying to figure out why the heck PA turned there. --you will start to see a convergence point forming--that is where the trend will go to and reverse This picture paints a very different short term idea than the herd mentality for this pair. [and a lot of others] You can see from this example the first converging area wil be around 134.20 on the top side to see either a retracement of the new trend or a correction of the prevailing overall trend

--- 帖子 #12970 ---
MM depends on your risk appetite. Some people say 5% of account equity other say one, and others are somewhere in between First you have to figure out how many pips you're looking to get on a trade--figured out be where the next logical target would be. So if you're account equity was $1000 and you wanted 10 pips, , figure out you're S/L and the amount of pips you wanted Let's say we wanted a win rate of 1:1 risking 10 pips for 10 pips= 20 1% of 1000=$10 For this calulation, our pip value would be 0.1 [or 0.08 if spread is accounted for] Losing $10 [plus your spread] for $10.00 People have a tough time with MM becasue it is often revered in scalping--risking a lot more for a lot less. You should never risk more than you're willing to take

--- 帖子 #12992 ---
I have run into this before with other indicators. What I found out was that an indicator is set to place an "Object" (label, etc.) into a sub-window that does not exist. The indicator runs just fine, but since the sub-window it expects to be there is not there, that label simply does not appear. But the MT4 Experts log lets you know about it. The indicator coding is just fine and does not need changing. You can rid yourself of the Experts log entry by adding the necessary sub-window to the chart, or by changing in the Indcator Window, the sub-window # to that of one that exists currently on the chart (if the Indcator Window contains that option). In other words, when the indy code calls upon an "object" to be displayed, but the location to display it does not exist, you will get the notation of that fact in the MT4 Experts log. Meanwhile, the indy in all other respects is functioning the way it is supposed to....you just don't get to see that "object" anywhere on the screen.

--- 帖子 #13015 ---
Cobra posted an indicator by the name of "THV3 Trix V6[1][1].1 all false ". That is the one that this MTF trix uses and that is the one that you need. In theory you can tell it to work with any of them that you like, however, you will end up with some things that you may not want on the screen (like extra boxes or alarms.) Allfalse has all options turned off by default, and since the MTF trix calls the trix with it's default options, that is the best one to use.

Hi Stratman: The most important to me is whether the market(s) has nice postures to be considered in trading. I don't consider any session as unimportant. Most of the time, the Asian sessions are the time the market starting to set herself up for later tradable movements. Such behavior hasn't changed since the early 90s. Unlike some who think Asian session as unimportant; such time has to be monitored and analyzed. Be aware that London tends to 'jump the gun' before the official starting time of London session; simply because the setups done during Asian time have already been resolved. If I really need to take a rest, it will be during New Zealand and Australian session. Just my two cents. Take care. Have a good one Jeff

So, the story is in the volume, not in whether there is concerted and co-operative price manipulation.

--- 帖子 #13082 ---
I agree that volume is most often indicative of thrust but I was just wondering about whether it was brought about by the active co-operation of the big boys or a collective "jumping on the bandwagon," so to speak. There was an interesting situation in Europe in the late 1990s or maybe the very early 2000s. There was a trader who went by the nickname of "Vlad the Impaler." As I recall he dealt in the Bunde futures (specifically the German equivalent of the US 10 year note) and futures in the major currencies. Not sure but I think he was Czechoslovakian. He seemed to target the German banks. He had satellite traders in the main trading cities of Europe and of course London. He and his satellites would make obvious price probes, requests for quotes and set big buy or sell stops at the previously agreed prices along with multiple small orders along the price ladder. Because those financial instruments are exchange traded buy/sell orders are visible to other traders. When the big boys saw a lot of orders they'd think someone knew something they didn't and start loading up. Then, at a given signal Vlad's team would suddenly unload their positions and cancel the big orders. I saw a similiar modus operandi in Hong Kong in the 80s but in this instance it was carried out in the HK trading room of a UK bank. Vlad made hundreds of millions but of course it wasn't long before the German banks twigged what he was doing. They all got together, sucked him in by moving their prices suddenly to fill his large orders. He and his satellites couldn't meet the margin calls and were bankrupted. The last I heard of him he was living in London, blowing on his burnt fingers and trading in a modest way. Sorry this was so long and perhaps a little off topic. FFUser7 (aka PipHopeful).

--- 帖子 #13110 ---
Attached is an indicator that puts "Volumes" display in main chart window. Unlike the MT4 display, with this indicator using the core code from the NVO Indicator, you can color code volume graduations to make them stand out. The default colors for the above average volume graduations are per the original core code. Graduations have been changed from 38.2/61.8/100 to 33/66/100, but you can change them as you like in the hard code. You can also increase width of bars to make those in certain graduations stand out. In the second chart (M15) the below avg, 1st grad, and 2nd grad are width "2". But the 3rd grad is width "3" and the final, over 100 grad, is width "4". You can change the height of the display from the default height, which is the same as in the MT4 standard chart volumes display. The external input for Display Height accepts decimals....anything over "0", so a wide variety of height is possible. Input "0" or lower, and the indy will "turn off". There is also a "ON/OFF" external input which turns off the indy, but preserves your settings for that chart. When you alter the scale of a chart, it will affect the height of the volumes display. But the next incoming tic should change the height back to the user setting. Speed freaks should know that this requires the indy to repaint. This indicator was a fantastic idea from Cobra! May it serve you well.

--- 帖子 #13130 ---
I apologize for not mentioning that users should read the notes at the top of the indicator compile, where this information is. Based upon whatever averaging period is used (default is 10 periods) Blue means the volume at the current bar is below-to-equal to that for the averaging period. Green means current bar volume is over avg. by up to 33%. LimeGreen means it is over by 33% to 66%. Yellow means it is over by 66% to 100%. And White means it is 100+% over the average.

--- 帖子 #13132 ---
Default height is about same as standard MT4 volume indy, but again, as the notes in the compile state, height is adjustable....which you can surmise from the external inputs window also. The display height means nothing in terms of actual amounts of volume, as all bars move relatively when the display height is altered. It is just a matter of whether you want a real tall display or a short, short display, or anything in between.

--- 帖子 #13149 ---
Ok, it's not time yet for a short on that pair but I'll give you an idea where to set and why the TP. TP's should be set to well known historical S&amp;R, those depend on your trading style and TF to trade. Let's say you daytrade the 15M and aim for about 40 to 80 pips/trade. First draw fib retracements (we can't do that still as we don't know where's the top yet). Than look leftwards on your chart and draw horizontal HLs on the last highs and lows of the 15M in this case. In the actual chart we have several TPs, the DP, the first HL in gray, MS1, S1 and MS2 which is todays low. now it depends on your risk appetite where to set the TP, as more far away as more risky your trade. Sometimes its better to add to your trade than wait too long. Also, after a reasonable move in your favor (number depends on TF and trading session [Volaty]) lock SL in profit +1. Hope that helps a bit.

--- 帖子 #13169 ---
Decidence, You should configure your own settings depending on your money management and style of trading. There is no recommended settings. As for TF, you can use it on any TF. There is no tutorial as there is nothing in CaveManager you can tweak to make your trading better. It is purely a trade management EA that will execute the trade exactly the way you configure it to. If you configure it to take profit by pivot levels and the price is already near the first pivot level, CaveManager will execute when the price hits the first pivot level. The loss that you are seeing might be from slippage. Be extra careful when trading near pivot levels. Cheers, CaveMan

That was a nice trade, I switched to E/Y this London session as we are on a critical point for the E/U (1.47) at the moment. I didn't get all the run because I chickened out at S1 and re-entered at MS1. This formation is called "Rounding Bottom" and has a relative high hit rate, here what Investopedia writes about it: Rounding Bottom What Does Rounding Bottom Mean? A chart pattern used in technical analysis, which is identified by a series of price movements that, when graphed, form the shape of a "U". Rounding bottoms are found at the end of extended downward trends and signify a reversal in long-term price movements. This pattern's time frame can vary from several weeks to several months and is deemed by many traders as a rare occurrence. The chart below illustrates a rounding bottom. http://i.investopedia.com/inv/dictio...dingBottom.gif Investopedia explains Rounding Bottom A rounding bottoms look similar to the cup and handle pattern, but does not experience the temporary downward trend of the "handle" portion. The initial declining slope of a rounding bottom indicates an excess of supply, which forces the stock price down. The transfer to an upward trend occurs when buyers enter the market at a low price, which increases demand for the stock. Once the rounding bottom is complete, the stock breaks out and will continue in its new upward trend. hope that helps for the ones that didn't know that pattern yet. BTW: I copied that info two hours ago, you might want to visit Investopedia and read about Cup and Handle formations.

--- 帖子 #13213 ---
Folks, SDX-TzPivots is SDX-TzPivots, no matter where it is posted! The THV version is specified as such due to color and line style selections Cobra feels best to enhance the THV screen layout. The last version posted was _v5, but _v6 should be released later this month. And Cobra will likely fix it with the colors and other style selections to best suit THV. There are improvements from version upgrade to version upgrade, but there is no functionality difference between SDX-TzPivots, as set up for THV, and any other in use of the same version. Now, the issue at hand seems to be about the correct external inputs to make for "HrsServerTzFromGMT" and "HrsChoiceTzFromGMT" (as they are referred to in _v6). You need to input how many hours away from GMT (and in which direction) your platform server is at. You can tell this from the time line at the bottom of the chart, and by going to World Clock ( http://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/ ) and seeing how many hours away from GMT is your server. You need to input your "Choice" of time zone on which to base the pivot calculations....again, how many hours away from GMT, and in what direction. World Clock can help with this too. Cobra's preference for THV is "0", or the GMT time zone, for this input. If your server's time zone is at a location east of GMT, that input is positive. If it is west of GMT, that input is negative. The same goes for the "Choice" (Destination as it is currently referred to) input. I hope this clarifies the issue for everyone.

--- 帖子 #13217 ---
Hi guys, Explaining the pivots. You have to look at what time your MT4 clock shows. That is the time of your broker. For example, I live +3GMT and my clock on the wall shows 14:11. When I see MT4 time, it says - 12:11. (broker time) So if I subtract 3 hours from my local time - 14:11 - 3hours = 11:11 Now I have 0 GMT time - 11:11. I compare this time to brokers time, which is 12:11. And I get +1GMT. That means that LOCAL TIMEZONE entry should be "1". Now I have pivots calculations for 0GMT. Let's say I want to calculate pivots for New York session. New York is in -5 GMT. So in the destination I add "-5". That's it.

--- 帖子 #13235 ---
I appologize if I am distracting this thread but I found my issue and wanted to post a solution for search purposes. In the divergence section of THV3 Trix v4.01 if SoundAlertOnDivergence is set to true it will play the wav file you specify so can hear of the divergence, but it will not email you even if you have EmailDivergenceAlerts set to true. You have to set SoundAlertOnDivergence to false to receive the email (and also have EmailDivergenceAlerts set to true). Just a heads up, sorry if this was covered I couldn't find it in search. Mike

Only trade good setups. Simple ... yes? So ... I started looking at higher timeframes to get the big picture and then progressively smaller timeframes eg in this order D1, H4, H1, M15, M5, M1. Obviously marking up the charts on my way down. Now, even though 'strong?' counter trends exist on lower time frames, if you can get confluence among all timeframes and use THV for you entries and exits ... you can really increase your winning average. Because I trade the Asian session and start of London ... it's been real tough (low volume etc). I don't know what to call it ... it uses MT4 chart window as a 'workspace' for multiple currencies showing multiple timeframes. I like this because it gives me the chance to see my best setup ... the pin bar. Note this is still a work in progress ... big note is that I don't have the current bar showing yet ... so charts currently show 'previous' bars. I hope to code the current bar part today. If anyone has ever tried to do something like this, you will appreciate the challenges eg the chart window only updates based on a tick on the single currency attached to the chart. I am getting around this by having a 'while' loop inside the start() function.

Here's another shot with a bit of an explanation: Parameter Usage: Note: All pixel values are referenced to top-left corner of chart window ATRBars: Number of bars to calculate ATR (used for scaling chart) TopLeftX, TopLeftY: X,Y Pixel postion of top left corner of mini chart Width: Width of mini chart in pixels Height: Height of mini chart in pixels HeadingX, HeadingY: Heading position - pixel offset from mini chart top-left ScaleStartY: Scale start position - pixel offset from mini chart top-left ATRPixelsY: Used in conjuction with 'ATRBars' to determine graph scaling ie makes chart vertically larger or smaller All other parmeters are self explanatory

--- 帖子 #13320 ---

--- 帖子 #13332 ---
Recalled you asked for recommendations. These are the settings I use on the EUR/USD M5 TF. You may want to try them. TP: Target next pivot level (I don't use mid-levels. Open trade only on closed candle beyond pivot level if PA is close to it) SL: 15 NoLoss: 8 I do use trailing stop of 25 as well for 50% of my lot size to either ride a big move or break even if PA reverses. I make no attempt to intervene once I hit first target level. One more point to note, do turn on Ask line for the chart. We buy on Ask price and Sell on Bid price. So for example, if you do a Buy, Bid line has to go above pivot level. For a Sell, Ask line has to go below pivot level. Reason is simple, EA closes a Buy position we took with a Sell order at Bid price and a Sell position with a Buy order at Ask price. This will ensure that you are clear of the pivot level when opening a position close to pivot levels. Nearly forgot to put this down. I trade with the H4 analysis. I do not just follow Coral. Only when Coral is in agreement with H4 trend. That is the reason why I do not use mid levels for pivot. When I do trade counter trend or counter Coral (when PA is far from Coral and is ready to come back to the median), I do not use CaveManager. I turn off expert adviser and manage the position manually.

--- 帖子 #13333 ---
Not that much work ... only took me 2 days ... I make liberal use of reuseable code. As an example, this is my whole start() function: Inserted Code //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ //| indicator start function | //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ int start() { //---- if ( !UseMultiMode ) //UseMultiMode=false { if ( gBarTime[0]!=iTime(gSymbol[0],gTimePeriod[0],0) ) Reset(0); Update(0); } else { //UseMultiMode=true for ( int chartNum=1 ; chartNum&lt;=60 ; chartNum++ ) { if ( gTimeFrame[chartNum]!="" ) { if ( gBarTime[chartNum]!=iTime(gSymbol[chartNum],gTimePeriod[chartNum],0) ) Reset(chartNum); Update(chartNum); } } } //---- return(0); } //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

So if you take my last post, then consider: Price breaks the strong support, retests it, then you enter AGAIN, still holding your original trade, setting your stop just above the new resistance. A SL hit means very little pips lost, while a further drop DOUBLES your pip gain (from the point of the second entry).

--- 帖子 #13415 ---
Not sure this will help but here's my take on this...was in the same trade as you so perhaps I can give you a few thoughts that I had at the time. Course that would require me to remember what I thought and my ginko is a bit low at the moment. First off, understanding PA (PriceAction) will help you a lot...the bar you entered on was the high bar of this move...but...the prior bar to this and the bar following this had equal highs. This is what I call a pinch bar high but I've seen it called a pinochio bar and a few other names. This is almost always a false break out and will usually resolve to the oppisite side of the inital thrust...so you should know that you have a very good chance of a fair to good trade. On this paticular trade you need confirmation, which comes with the second bar following the thrust (bar you entered on) bar. If it can't exceed the high of the bar before the thrust bar then it's most likely going down. Then...just by setting a stop a few pips over the prior bars high (on the M15 chart) you would have been stopped out around 90 positive pips...and yes this will all pass, given enough screen time. PnS...your English is much better than my Russian... Edit: See our mentor and fine fellow types faster than I...Hi Cobra...

EDIT: The code would be even smaller if it wasn't for all the debug statements I have. I have a line like this to display every variable: Inserted Code if ( DebugMode ) Print( gChartNamePrefix[chartNum] + "gPoint[chartNum]: " + DoubleToStr(gPoint[chartNum] ,Digits)); if ( DebugMode ) Print( gChartNamePrefix[chartNum] + "gTimePeriod[chartNum]: " + DoubleToStr(gTimePeriod[chartNum] ,0)); if ( DebugMode ) Print( gChartNamePrefix[chartNum] + "gBarTime[chartNum]: " + TimeToStr (gBarTime[chartNum] ,TIME_DATE|TIME_SECONDS)); if ( DebugMode ) Print( gChartNamePrefix[chartNum] + "ATRBars: " + DoubleToStr(ATRBars ,0)); if ( DebugMode ) Print( gChartNamePrefix[chartNum] + "gATR[chartNum]: " + DoubleToStr(gATR[chartNum] ,Digits)); ... One thing I learnt a long time ago is to make sure you always write 'reuseable' code ie keep all functions small so it's easy to follow what going on. MQ4 is not a feature rich language but liberal use of arrays can really help eg this indicator can display 60 minicharts on one chart!! Here's what I mean about keeping functions small. Here's the start function: Inserted Code //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ //| indicator start function | //+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ int start() { //---- if ( !MultiMode ) //MultiMode=false { if ( gBarTime[0]!=iTime(gSymbol[0],gTimePeriod[0],0) ) Reset(0); Update(0); } else { //MultiMode=true for ( int chartNum=1 ; chartNum&lt;=60 ; chartNum++ ) { if ( gTimeFrame[chartNum]!="" ) { if ( gBarTime[chartNum]!=iTime(gSymbol[chartNum],gTimePeriod[chartNum],0) ) Reset(chartNum); Update(chartNum); } } } //---- return(0); }

Hi Everyone especially Cobra, Miss Pips and all team members. Pardon the length of this post. Been following this thread since the beginning of the year and for the past month monitored every Londen session, actually most of the trades 8h00 -17h00 GMT. My question always was: What will the result be if we only trade the 6 lights (top two green/red) and a coral cross? (basically just following the manual coded by Miss Pips on the first page) Ignoring all the Fibs, TL's, Pivots and Trend direction etc. Started on the 27 August up to yesterday 24 September 2009. I am not claiming that every trade during this period was 100% according to the rules but basically within the given parameters. So it will be possible to proof me wrong, but my aim was to get an estimate. The stats are over a 21 day period for 1 day not counted - Bank Holiday- one day early exit due to Non Farm Payrolls. Bended the rule a little bit on the coral cross- did not trade when PA already left the coral by more than ten pips. Brought in the divergences the past week. Always 10 pip TP 15 pip SL. Trade was never closed even if counter trade indication presented it self, e.g. in long trade and pa crossed coral in opposite direction and six red lights came on - rode it out and took the loss. Results: Trades=107, Winners=89, Losers=18 89X10= 890 18X15= 270 890-270= 620 pips profit = almost 30 pips pd. 70% success. Most of the failed trades could have been avoided, if the basic principles of trading were applied e.g. Don't trade the news Trendline in the way, Only trade with the trend, Don't trade against the divergence etc. Like on the 23 September the PA crossed the coral 5 times with six lights on, indicating trade long, but the trend was strongly downwards. So that day alone resulted in 5 failures. The question now is, if we bring in some trade rules (filters), with how much can the success ratio increase? Please let me know what is your opinion on this. Thanks again to Cobra Miss Pips and all team members.

--- 帖子 #13478 ---
I forward tested this strategy (demo only) before publishing it, with very similar results over about 3 months. (I did it privately first and then I posted screenshots of all trades for about a month on Cobras site for review of the method by the THV team.) I concur that even these results can be improved taking only trades in the direction of the trend (I currently define trend as whichever side the rainbow has made higher highs or lower lows on) and by avoiding trades where PA is too overextended unless they are divergence trades ( I define that visually by looking at the expansion of the rainbow, but 10 pips from the Coral sounds good too, especially since you can measure it accurately). Also results can be improved by not taking trades that are less than 10 pips from a pivot, especially if it's the first approach. (Even though if there is enough momentum PA will crack the pivot, it fails enough times to justify caution and wait till the pivot is cracked before taking the trade). It's better to let PA bounce back from the Pivot and try to catch a second attempt at cracking it where there is 10 pips of room for the trade to move or to let PA crack the Pivot and catch a bounce off of it in the direction of the trend. For live trading, these additions make life less stressful. Edit: Oh, and I forgot to mention, that for both real trading and during when I tested I used a second indicator, the Traders Dynamic Index, to confirm divergence. When taking divergence trades, results are improved if more than one indicator confirms it.

--- 帖子 #13506 ---
Hi Vitaliy No, there is no manual at the moment, you need to play with the new version a little. En general the rules didn't change and I see V4 more as a cosmetical change (the template is more organized and clean) but it gives signals when the basic rules are met and warn us when PA is OB/OS. We also have an additional, second OB/OS zone That doesn't mean that we take a trade on each signal, we should have analysed the trend on 15M and higher TF before to make sure that the probability of our position is high. I traded these weeks V4 and had good results by taking the second signal buying the dips for example when both, 1M and 5M give the signal. Also, we have to make sure that we don't take a trade aiming for 10 pips and have the Daily pivot for instance in 5 pips crossing our position and so on, but that is logical. I used it mainly for scalping but you can switch the signals off or also switch to higher TFs ignoring the Coral rule. There will be long term traders which may use the new futures as well. The V3 is still valid and if someone just start or like the more conservative template, can use it as it's bullet proved.

The new start date is the second Sunday in March (previously the first Sunday in April) through to the first Sunday in November (previously the last Sunday in October)." Check World Clock site to confirm your server Tz and your choice Tz differences from GMT.

Ok, we are ready to go, this is version V4, which doesn’t replace V3 , it’s a cosmetically update with additional options. Who likes it more conservative can use V3 which will be still available in the front page and is bullet proved. There are no rules changed, why change what workes? So the V3 manual is still up to date but I will elaborate a new one soon to explain all options included in V4. Download link is in the first post of this thread. http://www.cobraforex.com/other/V3thread.jpg Parallel to V4 we have the release of Traderathome’s new pivot indicator which is included in V4 with special color settings for our new template. This has been a huge effort for him and took hundreds of hours to get it done, we had even last updates in the last hours before release. I added a manual in the “Manual and options” zip in the first post which is a copy of TaH’s introduction in the mq4 code. Big thanks for TaH and Domas4 for their great efforts. Also thanks to Stratman for the mini charts which I included in the last moment as an official THV indicator . It will help especially traders which don’t have many monitors yet. There are two fonts included in the zip file which you can use if you don’t have them installed in your PC. Read about how to install them here . The templates are separated in a zip folder and you need to paste them in your Metatrader/templates folder. Everything else will be installed automatically with the exe file, just follow the instructions. What's new in THV V4? In THV V4 we have additional Trix extreme Overbought/Oversold zones which can be of great value in countertrend trades on important S&amp;R levels . The Trix window area paints depending on the OB/OS level. You have a user definable alarm sound reminder once on every candle in the OB/OS zone. The Trix design and template is improved for better, stress less view. The Market Price is shown in the Trix window. The Market sessions with countdown are shown in the Trix window. The Pair and TF are shown in the main chart which is helpful for identification of them in posted screenshots. The Options and Action shown in the Trix window are NOT signals, you should have additional reasons to follow those suggestions!!! This counts also for the signals given when basic THV rules are filled. The THV Info panel is integrated and re-designed for THV V4 Stratman's mini charts are shown in the main chart. Option for trading Oil and Gold included. 9 different templates included. Have fun Folks Cobra BTW: if a good programmer sees my code will , but important is that it works, I'm still a newbee in coding.

--- 帖子 #13604 ---
Attached are the new time zone shift pivot indicators, TzPivotsD and TzPivotsMW. These are the first time zone shift indicators to contain an upgrade from the Shimodax code in the SDX-TzPivots indicator. This important new core code is the work of Domas4, who generously contributed his coding skills for many hours over the past several weeks, to help create these two new indicators. Thanks to Domas4, the errant pivots which are displayed on H4 and Day charts by the SDX-TzPivots indicator, are a thing of the past. He has corrected the errors in the Camarilla formula, and created new pivot line display options! And he has worked tirelessly to fault test code as new options were added. Without the valuable help of Domas4, these indicators would not exist. He has my deepest respect and gratitude. TzPivotsD and TzPivotsMW are complementary. While shifting the time zone has little effect on monthly and weekly pivots, the time zone shift does allow seamless mating of pivot lines using different styles before and after the start of a new day…..which is just one of the new options created by Domas4. These indicators are feature laden and with many options. The external inputs have been revamped in an attempt to help keep things as simple as possible. But it is advisable that users read the manuals. They are provided in preliminary form herewith. They will help explain the effects of certain inputs, provide an overview of functions, and highlight new features. To all who use them, may these new indicators serve you well. And to Domas4, “Thank you.” for making them possible.
