--- 帖子 #13768 ---
I want to list some of the customisations I make in case it's helpful to others. The THV4 base templates are great but can't hope to cover everyones possible preferences. Some of us have our own preferences eg some like a black background, some like white. I'm writing this after reading this post from adunk1: There will be those among you (like adunk1) that haven't realised that you can customise the thv templates and save them. Preferably with a different name. Use the templates button on the MT4 toolbar: Attached Image I call my personalised template '00 THV'. That way it should be at the top of the list. My main trading system is 2 large monitors (1920x1200) and customise the template with 5 mini charts M5,M15,H1,H4,D1 I use my laptop (1440x900) in the evenings and have a customised template with 4 minicharts M15,H1,H4,D1. Also on the laptop, I have '00 thv left' and '00 thv right' templates ... see the pic I use the 'F11' key to get the largest amount of chart space then use 'Ctrl T' to show/hide the terminal. Iright-click the chart to choose time period eg I switch between M5/M1 heaps I always show the ASK line because it shows me the spread on the chart. Right-click the chart, choose properties (show ask line). If the chart is in a tight range, this visual of the spread makes it obvious. I also like to have the S/R lines and Daily pivot 'lined up' between my thv chart and my Analysis chart. In my pic, that's why the indicator on Analysis chart looks so big. I'll post another issue that will catch a few out (it's caught me many times) in my next post ... it's to do with the price scale during a tight range. Hope this helps a few of you. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #13830 ---
The 10 rows counted for points are 1. M1 fast trix 2. M5 fast trix 3. M5 slow trix 4. M15 fast trix 5. M15 slow trix 6. M30 fast trix 7. M30 slow trix 8. M60 fast trix 9. M5 cloud 10. M15 cloud The first two rows refer to the first two rows in the first trix histo (m1 and m5, as stated.) The reason for this is that the 6 point method allows you to take a trade BEFORE you get a trix cross. That being the case (since not waiting for a trix cross would ordinarily be riskier), I considered it prudent to have the fast trix on the next higher timeframe also in your favor.

--- 帖子 #13836 ---
Well, technically according to the rules I posted in the thread, no it isn't, because PA is not below the MAs representing the 15m coral and 30 m coral. If you don't have PA at least below the 15m coral, you are probably looking at a retracement (though hopefully a big enough one to get 10 pips out of) and not a new trend. I personally took a trade there because as I mentioned, if you want to be brave you can take trades where there is 10 pips of room between the trade and the next coral. Also I had more considerations: 1. PA had bounced off the 1m coral - always a good sign. 2. If you notice, the previous peak had a hidden divergence in favor of the trade (higher trix, lower PA) 2. Resistance on the 15m chart at about 1.4615 had been cracked and then PA bounced back above it. Usually when the Euro cracks a pivot or other resistance and has a retracement, it is going to have another go a what it is trying to crack unless there's a nasty divergence. For people having problems installing the new version 4 try the following. After running the install program manually copy the templates into your template folder in your directory. I had to do that and then everything worked just fine. The templates are in a separate folder labeled "templates" when you first unzip your download. Put the exe file in the same directory as your MT4 program before you run the install.

--- 帖子 #13849 ---
I see you are determined to extract all my rainbow secrets. :-) Well, since you are, if you watch the rainbow for a while you will see that there are a few types. Some are a nice smooth crescent, and some aren't. This type is what I call the seahorse trade because the shape of the rainbow reminds me of one. Sounds silly but helps me remember the shape of the pattern. Usually you will get at least two trades off this kind of rainbow, one at the hump and one as PA comes off the long nose of the seahorse. (Less poetically Joe Dinapoli calls this the bread and butter trade. He describes it as PA goes almost vertically up for at least 12 bars, and then you catch a trade off the retrace - though usually he uses it on longer tfs). For this kind of trade you don't care if the low that you take the trade off of is a lower low, as long as the up move was violent, and as long as PA hasn't done its average number of daily pips.

--- 帖子 #13877 ---
If you use: while( !IsStopped() ) inside and indicator, you need WindowRedraw(); otherwise the screen will never be updated with changes you make to objects. This is because objects only get refreshed when the start() function is exited ... in this case it never does. That is while( !IsStopped() ) keeps the indicator in its start() function permanently. The sleep(1000) means that we give time back to MT4 terminal to carry out its normal business. This causes the loop inside start() function to have 1 iteration per second ... exactly what we want for the candle clock.

--- 帖子 #13879 ---
Mini charts get updated on every tick of the main chart currency. Each individual chart gets totally redrawn at each new candle of that minichart. If you have a large number of minicharts (I have 15 on one window), the time processing them can be excessive, especially during higher volume times (many ticks in a short space of time). For this reason, I'm adding a SleepTime variable that will give time back to the terminal between each chart processing ie if 15 charts, the indicator will give 15 lots of Sleep Time to the terminal on every tick. I should have the new version uploaded to the mini chart thread shortly. Maybe those people that are finding MT4 slow with THV4 can try the new mini chart update and report back about any improvement? Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #13908 ---
TzPivotsD places the daily pivots on the chart. You can select to omit some catagories: yHL lines, quarter pivot lines mid pivot lines. TzPivotsMW places the Monthly and the Weekly pivots on the chart. These can be more significant at times than some of the daily pivots, especially the quarter pivots and mid pivots! This indicator also has mid pivots, which you can select to omit. Both indicators have an ON/OFF switch, the first choice in the external inputs window. If you do not want to show MW pivots, just turn the indicator off.

Dumb question to someone so experienced as you maybe but do you perform regular housekeeping on your PC? Clear out your browser cache, cookies, delete what you don't use, perform disc &amp; registry clean up and defrag your drives? Example: Windows installs an enormous number of fonts, most people only use a couple of dozen at most so why not delete the others? It's less for the machine to sort through. Many small improvements may add up to a lot. Outside of that one should make sure that one's graphics drivers are up to date and that there are no IRQ conflicts. Often, more and faster RAM will cure a host of problems too. For comparison purposes I am running both V3 &amp; V4 together with both your old and new MTFs. I have seven charts up on 4 monitors with a brower open to FF and Outlook Express. I run WinXP home on a dual Athlon 6000 on MB with an 800 fsb and 3 meg of DDR 800. --- 帖子 #13960 ---
My experience with Vista: when I'm put V4 (it was the same with V3) on PC, I made templates and save profiles as I need, after that I save this profiles and templates in different place on PC (for example in My documents), after that I uninstall broker Metatrader platform from PC, manualy delete broker folder from Program files, but that not enough, I also go to C disc Users, go into user name that You use, then Appdata, Local, VirtualStore, Program Files and then delete Metatrader folder of that broker which You previous delete. (C:UsersnameAppDataLocalVirtualStoreProgram Files) After that I install metatrader, put in profiles folder and template folder what I save, open my profile, after that restart Metatrader platform and then ok. It's really helps for my Vista, it use less PC capacity.

--- 帖子 #13965 ---
The MTF any Trix is not my indie. I just modified it so it has an autotimeframe feature and also so it can use any trix. It will call any trix that you specify and should work the same as that trix. ALL the trixes can repaint themselves one bar back, and will often do so if the PA is flat. I have posted other posts about this - please see those posts for more info if you are interested. ALL MTF indies will repaint (after the fact) and can't be used for back testing. I have posted other posts about this about the MTF trix histo, and also about the MTF trix specifically in comparison to the MTF trix histo - please see those posts for more info if you are interested.

--- 帖子 #13999 ---
Here's my friend the seahorse again. I like him because he's easy to recognize, and because if you don't like trading around big news times he still gives you a few good 10 pip trades off his long nose. This is what I think is the psychology behind this that makes it work: The tail is formed where some big surprise or announcment causes the market to sharply reverse. PA goes up just about vertically until people realize things have gotten out of hand and then there is a sharp correction with a divergence - forming the 'head' of the seahorse. The long nose is caused by the patient buyers who were waiting for that retrace to at least the 38 fib, picking off lots, waiting for price to fall, picking of some more lots, waiting for price to fall, picking off some more lots etc.. The first two trades are hidden divergence trades, by the way.

--- 帖子 #14025 ---
I've been lookng for a way to backtest MTF setups in the strategy tester, and I have finally found one. What you can do is take one of the older Trixes (say Trix v5) where you can specify the A and B T3 Periods. Add a trix with A_T3 period =100 and B_T3 period =175 (20*5 and 35*5) and you will get the equivalent of the M5 trix on the 1 chart. You can verify this by adding MTF Trix V1 (which uses the older Trix ) and you will notice they are the same. This works in the strategey tester so if you want to test setup where, say, you are trading when the 5m fast trix and the 1m trix agree, you can. The bottom trix on this chart is trix V5 set to A_t3 =100 and B_t3=175

--- 帖子 #14079 ---
Think of price action as the sea, and have a look at the attached. The green lines are where you would be taking 6 point long trades, when the 1m f and the 5m f line up and the red trades are 6 point shorts in the same conditions. ( I didn't show all the lights because you wouldn't be able to see them clearly. The rainbow is more clear and it is almost always the case that when you are trading it it's direction, you have the other four points that you need for trend trades.) You will notice that as long you are trading with the tide, the retreat of small waves made by the 1m trix should not stop you out, and the advance of each additional wave on the 1m trix should carry you farther toward your profit target. However, it is your job as a trader to determine the condition of the sea (too choppy or not), to make sure you hop on the wave as it is beginning and not as it is about to crash onto the shore, and to make sure that you are not catching it just as the tide is about to turn

I apologise in advance for the dismal quality of my translations but it is almost seventy years since I had to learn foreign languages and forty years since I had to use them frequently. As doctors say: "If you don't use it you lose it" so I am forced to rely heavily upon the vagaries of translators and dictionaries. Cobra has said that posting jokes is permissable so, since many non English speakers visit this site, here is a joke that in earlier times was common in European trading rooms: What do you call someone who speaks three languages? Answer - Tri-lingual What do call someone who speaks two languages? Answer - bi-lingual What do you call someone who speaks one language? Answer - An American. To any American readers: It's a just a joke guys. But if there was an element of truth in it formerly I don't think it's true now-a-days. Ich entschuldige mich im Voraus für die düstere Qualität meiner Übersetzungen, aber es ist fast siebzig Jahre, seitdem ich Fremdsprachen lernen musste und vierzig Jahre seitdem mussten sie oft verwenden. Wie die Ärzte sagen: "Wenn Sie es nicht verwenden, verlieren Sie es", so werde ich gezwungen mich zu verlassen die Kapricen von Übersetzern und Wörterbüchern. Kobra hat gesagt, dass, Witze bekanntzugeben so, da viele nicht englischen Sprecher diesen Aufstellungsort besichtigen, ist hier ein Witz zulässig ist, der in den europäischen Handelsräumen allgemein ist: Was nennen Sie jemand, das drei Sprachen spricht? Antwort - dreisprachig Was rufen jemand an, das zwei Sprachen spricht? Antwort - Zweisprachiger Was nennen Sie jemand, das eine Sprache spricht? Antwort - ein Amerikaner. Je fais des excuses à l'avance pour la qualité morne de mes traductions mais c'est presque soixante-dix ans puisque j'ai dû apprendre des langues étrangères et quarante ans puisque dû les employer fréquemment. Comme les médecins disent: " Si vous don'; utilisation de t il vous perdent l'it"; ainsi je suis forcé de répondre fortement sur des traducteurs et des dictionnaires. Le cobra a indiqué que la signalisation des plaisanteries est permise ainsi, puisque beaucoup d'anglophones non visitent cet emplacement, voici une plaisanterie commune dans les salles de marché européennes : Qu'appelez-vous quelqu'un qui parle trois langues ? Réponse - trilingue Qu'appellent quelqu'un qui parle deux langues ? Réponse - bilingue Qu'appelez-vous quelqu'un qui parle une langue ? Réponse - un Américain. Me disculpo por adelantado por la calidad triste de mis traducciones pero es casi setenta años puesto que tuve que aprender idiomas extranjeros y cuarenta años puesto que tenido que utilizarlos con frecuencia. Como los doctores dicen: " Si usted don' uso de t usted pierde el it" me fuerzan tan a contestar pesadamente sobre los traductores y los diccionarios. La cobra ha dicho que la fijación de bromas es permitida puesto que muchas personas de habla inglesa no visitan este sitio, aquí es así pues, una broma común en cuartos de comercio europeos: ¿Qué usted llama alguien que habla tres idiomas? Respuesta - trilingüe ¿Qué llaman alguien que habla dos idiomas? Respuesta - bilingüe ¿Qué usted llama alguien que habla una lengua? Respuesta - Americano. Regards &amp; good trading to all, PH

And even with that you can get cought in the trap, the market gives a sh$t on if the trix is green or red, it reacts on offer and demand and these lines in the sand you can read in historical S&amp;R. The indicators show what happened not what will happen but there are probabilities that the market reacts like ..... when happened ..... Those areas you need to study over long time to know what to do when. Now you can ask: And what the heck all systems are good for? There are systems they call click and forget, they don't work and you can forget soon your equity as they are complete mechanical. And there are systems that show PA in a different way and detect divergence etc. but requiere the traders knowledge and feeling to take the right decision, THV is one of them.

--- 帖子 #14240 ---
Above coral for long, below coral for short. I just wait until the price crosses it, not closes below/above it. I don't think it matters on the short TF. Yes, enter on the cross of the trix or after they have crossed and are the same colour. Notice on the last trade for example you couldn't enter on the cross of the trix because PA was above the coral. Once it has passed the coral (and cloud), we are free to enter. This is how I interpret it anyway. Trading the one minute can give unreliable results i've found. Sometimes it gives great setups sometimes it will hammer you. As cobra said explicitly in the manual, you need advanced skills to be trading the 1min. Memorise the rules, and trade them no matter what. Even if a set up looks like a surefire winner, but you don't have the 4 red lights (or 4 green lights), hold off until you do. Of course you must integrate common sense, draw trendlines and pay attention to S&amp;R, pivots and so on. On the 5 minute chart you will be babysitting the screen and you need discipline. On the chart I posted, there were only 4 valid trades between 9 and 6 BST, or one trade every 2 and a quarter hours. It's only natural to want to hunt pips on the 1 minute. Master the 5 minute first. Here's an exercise. You don't have to post it, but take a 5min G/U chart for today. Mark out all of the valid trades and how many pips you would have made following the rules. Of course hindsight is totally different from the emotion of live trading but it might reassure you a bit. There were two beautiful set-ups at 7am GMT and again at 10am GMT. The rest of the day wasn't great admittedly as the ATR was pretty low and no clear direction.

As always for confirming a trade I like to see a retest after break. A retest isn't necesarily testing the coral but it should retrace a bit and than continue with the trend. Hope that helps.

Morning Everyone I liked the H4 system a lot but have lost on a few and won on a few, so looking at things I noticed a few interesting things and thought I would share them with you all for comment. In the picture below under my current understanding of the signals for this H4 entry system I would have entered at point 1 (Grey circle). When the fast trix changed colour indicating bearish. This however retraced some 90 pips before turning round at point 2 and going on to make in excess of 150 pips at point 3, where the fast trix turned green, bullish, which is our exit point. So if I had taken the signal at point 1 would I have survived the draw down to point 2 ? scarey ! I probably would have been stopped out or just completely lost my cool and bailed out much earlier. However if you look a few days further down the road the fast trix crosses the slow trix and they both turn red, so my entry would have been at the yellow circle, point "A". This would have bagged me around 200 pips and avoided the stressful draw down. So my conculsion is as follows:- 1) I wait for an Arrow indication in the Trix window. (Alarm on so I dont miss it) 2) I then monitor things and wait until I get a cross on the fast &amp; slow Trix and they are both the same colour (Alarm on so I dont miss it) at which point I enter a trade. 3) For my stop I would look for a suitable place behind S &amp; R 4) Although my goal would be to stay in the trade &amp; wait until the fast trix changed colour, I would probably target several S &amp; R lines during the trade and take some profits at each point. But that depends on your risk appitite I was also considering whether or not I would trade against the over all trend or not ? Not sure on that one yet still considering it ? Anyway look forward to hearing what anyone has to say. ab1 Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #14344 ---
double FTR = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4 Trix called",2,CandleToUse); double FTG = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4 Trix called",3,CandleToUse); FTR=fast trix red FTG=fast trix green example: if (FTR == EMPTY_VALUE ) sell signal The THV4 Trix called is included in V4. For slow trix buffers: 0 = Red; 1= Green For trix buffers: 6 = fast trix; 7 = slow trix Hope that helps

--- 帖子 #14369 ---
A word of caution here...your trendlines are not correct for showing divergence. Both trendlines need to be on the same side to show correct divergence. If the trendline for price is drawn above price, then the trendline for the indicator should also be drawn on the upper side of the indicator. If the trendline for price is drawn below price, then the trendline for the indicator should be drawn on the lower side of the indicator.

--- 帖子 #14394 ---
Attached indicator calls V6 trix to signal a color change of fast trix just call this indicator with icustom call iCustom(NULL, 0, signal_THV_Color, TF, false, 2, 0). where TF is chart timeframe. ie 5, 15, 30 or 60 etc. If the value returned is -1, than fast trix color has changed to red during current candle. If +1, than it has turned green during current candle. If -2, than it turned red during previous candle. if +2 than it turned green during previous candle. Hope it helps

--- 帖子 #14403 ---
You have an incorrect value for "TF" parameter used by the indicator. You have to specify 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 or 240 depending on tf of the chart on which you have the indicator. I also forgot to mention another parm for sound alert that also needs to be passed on to icustom function. I added it only few days ago to give a sound alert when color changes but it has not tested yet. May be i should take it out. example: for 15min chart, you would say double TrixColor = iCustom(NULL, 0, "signal_THV_Color", 15, false, 2, i) The icustom should return values 1,2,3 for green color and -1,-2, -3 for red color. 1 means color has changed during that candle, 2 means color changed during previous candle. 3 means continuation of the same color. You have to have "THV Trix Called" in your indicator folder, as this indicator calls it thru icustom calls. Gold lines do not mean anything but since values in buffer 0-2 are plotted as arrows and histogram, they show up. They have no meaning. You really wouldn't need this indicator on your chart except during debugging. I was using this indicator for creating a multi-currency, multi-timeframe dashboard, that is why it is coded certain way. I also used it in a failed 4h EA that didn't work out as Trix often repaints in higher timeframes. That is why I added a sound alert so it can alert when color changes and one can manually enter trades if signal is confirmed. PM me if you find any issues. So we don't turn this thread into discussion of this indicator

--- 帖子 #14405 ---
Attached is a multi-currency multi-timeframe dashboard for THV signals for fast trix color change and diversion How to install: =========== 1) Download all indicators and place them in indicator folder. 2) Open any currency chart for 1m and place the dashbaord indicator on that chart. You need not place all other indicators on the chart 3) there are no input parms to enter or modify 3) wait for couple of min as it populate the dashboard with information. It makes lots of calls to populate the dashbaord. so it can be a cpu hog. That is why I did not place too many currencies in the dashboard. How to read the dash board ===================== each currency and Timeframe generate 4 signals 1 - large arrow = means singal has been generated on current open candle 2 - smaller midsize arrow = means signal was triggered on previous closed candle 3 - smallest tiny arrow = means signal was generated several candles ago, and it continues 4 - Tiny yellow arrow = means no signal has been generated. Color of the arrows red = short signal green = long signal yellow = no signal This dashboard is based on "THV4 Trix Called" indicator This dashboard can slow down slower computers as it has to read trix for so many currencies and timeframes for every tick. So use it only on robust computers.

--- 帖子 #14427 ---
I put together my own trading strategy using THV as my main indicators. Maybe it will be helpful for others as they develop their own systems. Day Trading the THV System Timeframe: M5 ---------------------------- Section 1 - News Check 1. Open http://www.forexfactory.com/calendar.php 2. Note news for the day for the pairs you will be trading 3. Note the times news will be released which will affect your trading pairs and avoid these times Section 2 - The Set Up 4. Move all Chart TF's to H1 5. Note Trend direction, Trend SR's, Overbought/Oversold status and RSI 6. Move all Chart TF's to M5 7. Refer to Rule #5 8. Start looking for trading opportunities that will not contradict with notes taken from Rule #5 Section 3 - Identifying a Long Trade Type 1: 9. Price is above Coral line 10. Previous candle closed above Ichimoku cloud 11. Fast Trix crossed up over slow Trix and both lines are green 12. No upcoming major resistance for at least 25pips 13. Not trading into bearish divergence 14. Not overbought or above 79 on RSI Type 2: 15. Bullish Divergence identified 16. Refer to Rules #9, #12 and #14 Type 3: 17. Resisting Trend Line broken 18. Refer to Rules #12 and #14 Section 4 - Identifying a Short Trade Type 1: 19. Price is below Coral line 20. Previous candle closed below Ichimoku cloud 21. Fast Trix crossed down below slow Trix and both lines are red 22. No upcoming major support for at least 25pips 23. Not trading into bullish divergence 24. Not oversold or below 21 on RSI Type 2: 25. Bearish Divergence identified 26. Refer to Rules #19, #22 and #24 Type 3: 27. Supporting Trend Line broken 28. Refer to Rules #22 and #24 Section 5 - Entering the Trade 29. Before entering repeat Rules #4 and #5 to make sure your position will not break Rule #8 30. Stop loss never more then 15-20pips if 3x ATR(20) is higher this trade may not be worth the risk 31. Risk a maximum 2.5% of your equity per trade ($15,000 equity with 20pip SL is 1.8 lots) Section 6 - Managing the Trade 32. Use your discretion when to get out! You may want to use Trailing Stop if you don't see any major resistance coming for 50pips or so and in others you may want to only pull out 15-20pips profit.

Attention to all THV CaveManager users, Glad to inform that after thorough investigation, it is confirmed that there is nothing wrong with the logic of THV CaveManager. It is safe to proceed in using it to manage your position. Do take note and remember that THV CaveManager functions as such by design :- Handles one position per currency at any one time. Opening more than one position will caused unknown outcome. Do not load multiple copies of THV CaveManager on different charts of the same currency pair. Doing so will cause all copies of THV CaveManager to manage the same position and result in pre-mature closing of position. An update version 1.4 is in testing at the moment and will include the following new features. It will be made available shortly. Auto setting of SL and TP using ATR value x factor Dynamic trailing stop using ATR value x factor Checks to prevent multiple copies of EA to be loaded for the same currency pair on different TF charts. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #14471 ---
Does the two THV Trix v4 lines must be above/below 0 for a long/short ?

--- 帖子 #14472 ---
No it doesn't. But you have to watch out at what level they are at when they do cross, to be sure that they are not close to being overbought/oversold (if you're trading on M1, watch the Trix on the M5 as well for that, if you're trading on M5, watch the Trix on the M15 as well). If PA is close to being either overbought or oversold, then I would wait for a better entrance and not chase the riskier trade. The best entrance as said in the manual, would be when the Fast Trix crosses the Slow Trix very near or on the 0.00 line. One reason being, that tells us that there might be a trend change if the Fast Trix crosses over the 0.00, the other reason being, there will then be more room for the PA to move in the direction we're trading before heading into the overbought/oversold zone, giving us more room for profit taking before we need to get out of the trade. Remember, both lines also must be the same color before you can go long or short. Both green for long, both red for short. Also, if you're going to enter a trade, be sure the price is not right above a pivot line if you're going to short, or right below a pivot line if you're going to long, wait for the break first then enter. As for the way I exit my trades, I exit either when the Fast Trix change color (personally, I wait for after candle closes to be sure that it does stay changed), or price reaching the next pivot level. Trading this method is still a work in progress for me as well as I've just got into it. However, I did a lot of studies on my chart and read a lot of post on this thread, trying to catch up as fast as I can. =) So far though, wow, this method is great, the chart really tells you very clearly on what's going on, and how you should approach your trades. Not sure why I waited this long to start trading THV, but better late than never. ^^

The advantage of doing it this way is that the indicator objects are usually are not affected. (I'm yet to find out if it affects the TVH stuff, hopefully not!) Just a suggestion, if you haven't tried it.

--- 帖子 #14571 ---
When you are combining the rainbow with THV, you can take either a 6 point trade or a regular trix cross, as long as you have your three lower lows (or higher highs for a long) and you can see all the colors of the rainbow. The reason is that all we are really doing with the rainbow is trying to make sure we are trading with a trend (even if it's only on the 1m chart). Trix crosses are also perfectly good trades to take and generally speaking once you have three higher highs or lower lows and you see the rainbow, the odds are that you have enough of a trend that you will get your 10 pips without getting whipsawed out of the trade (as long as you check for obstacles, of course). In a choppy situation, the trend will usually not manage three higher highs (or lower lows) plus another trix cross. It will usually reverse before that. So, you could have taken a trade where I show in the screen below. It's not ideal because the 5m trix is oversold and going against the trade, and PA is not below the 15m coral, however the odds are still pretty good for this kind of trade as long as it meets the conditions mentioned above. In its favor is that PA is bouncing off of the coral , the 15m trix is nice and spread out and you have both a 6 pint divergence trade and a regular trix cross at the zero line. The reason for waiting for PA to get below the 15m coral and the 30 m coral is that if PA can't break these two, you probably have a retrace against the main trend, and not the start of a new trend. However, when you've had a strong enough move to result in the MAs that represent the 5, 15 and 30m coral being spread out, then you can look for a retrace trade as long as you have 10 pips between the trade and the next MA - because PA will probably bounce off these MAs, and you don't know which bounce will turn the trend around.

--- 帖子 #14591 ---
I wouldn't say that scalping is safer than longer term trading, if someone didn't make his homework he will fail anyhow. To scalp you need to know the same as for day trading and a little more as you have to determinate your trading direction for your session on higher TFs. What makes scalping interesting is that you have many trades which devides the risk and you can make a living with a smaller account size that a long term trader. Let's make a comparation. Let's say you are a restaurant owner, what would you prefer, 500 clients daily or 50 daily which pay almost the same in your exclusive restaurant after costs? I prefere the 500 clients, if I lose some because they change there residence or simply found something they like more I still have a good income. At the end it's more work but you always have customers that pay you the daily bread. There are huge differences in the MM between short and long term trading but who has the money to suffer a 200 pips SL with good MM which get maybe hit after 3 - 5 days and can make a living with it?

--- 帖子 #14607 ---
szt0495 , My advice is to take profit at pivot or mid pivot levels. Depending on how many lots you are trading, exit partial as you reach a pivot or mid pivot level and set the rest to BE. If you happen to be in a huge move, you will know it as the PA will just zoom away, it those cases, just ride it. But this is very rare in my opinion unless you are stalking it with higher TF analysis like yesterday's move. Always remember that THV is a scalping strategy. I use it on the M5. Take small bites out of the market. At the end of the day, it will all add up. Don't hope for 50 pips move for every position you take. Just aim for 10 to 20 pips, exit with the profit and wait for the next entry. You will be more successful this way. A lot of newbies fail with THV because they expect to catch big moves with this. Even with 20 pips floating profit, they are still hoping for more, PA then turns and take them out at a loss. One very important point I have made in past posts is that from higher TF analysis (e.g. H4) you need to decide if you are trading with the trend or counter trend or both. Now counter trend basically means trading the retracements or pullbacks as they happen. On M5, what looks like a nice uptrend may actually be a retracement of a downtrend on H4 and vice-versa. Yes, you need to know as your analysis, preparations, psychology and expectations are different for each. If you trade counter trend, you need to know beforehand potential areas where PA may turn to continue with the trend. Lower your target expectations but heighten all your senses to exit at the first sign of problem. Never take every signal THV gives you. Know where you are in the big picture. With higher TF analysis for trend, S/R and direction, you should do quite well with THV in getting small bites out of the market. It will add up. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #14628 ---
Hi Ab1, Don't make the mistake of thinking that trend trades with the rainbow are the only good THV trades. All the posts I did about the rainbow were not intended to negate other styles of trading THV but just to help beginners find an easy to identify, and relatively very safe spot to enter a THV trade. But those are not the only kinds of trades you can do with THV. When the market is choppy and has a lot of divergence (like now), trading trendline breaks is a good way to trade. You can refer to Cashmeer's posts for lot's of examples - he is the master of trendline breaks with divergence. The only problem with these trades is that you have to be a good trader to do them, because you have to be able to recognize the market is choppy, recognize divergence in time, recognize if it's a high probability divergence (because a lot of them don't work for more than a few pips), know how to draw meaningful trendlines, make sure not to let one of those trades get away from you if the divergence or break was a fakeout, and also be patient enough to hang onto it long enough to pay for all the ones that didn't work out. Whereas, with a trend trade, even if you didn't get your entry exactly right, unless you picked the very last retracement before the trend change to enter (and there's only one of those in a trend) or you picked a place where the trend was very overextended ( and you should be able to see that on the rainbow) then you'll probably be ok.

--- 帖子 #14660 ---
Attached are the two TzPivot Indicators. TzPivotsMW_v2 has the errant pivots fixed. Thanks to grant18265 for pointing that error out! Also, label font style can be typed in for wider font choices. Arial, Arial Bold and Verdana Bold are recommended with font sizes 8-12. TzPivotsD_v2 has additional coding of the Scroll Compensator. Leave the default "0" alone and code will try to "fit" an appropriate number based on the bars per chart. This is affected by the "zoom" the user has on the chart, and also by the size of the monitor....it is a tough thing to try to automate. If there are problems, leave the Scroll Compensator off when not in use. When on, any value &gt; zero input for the Scroll_Left_Adjustment will override hard coded values.....use"1" may be best. But turn off Scroll Compensator when not in use, as the value "1" will immediately force all pivot lines to become full screen lines. By default, the Scroll Compensator is on, with a Scroll_Left_Adjusment of "0", which allows the hard coded values to function. Both indys, thanks to Domas4, have additional price label coding to allow the indys to be used beyond forex......gold, oil, stocks, etc.

--- 帖子 #14696 ---
I think you may be describing what happens when you STRETCH the screen vertically....to the point that maybe only one horizontal line appears....a situation which causes the vertical separator lines to disappear. They return as you "unstretch" the screen vertically, so that you have at least two horizontal lines showing. As far as any horizontal lines disappearing, if that is what you mean, I have not experienced that. In the previous version, during the first time frame on any chart immediately upon start of new day, the horizontal pivot lines were not drawn....not until the first time frame was completed. So, you had to wait 5 minutes on a M5 chart before the horizontal pivots appeared. They would be ok from that point on thru the day. This (hopefully) has been fixed. I am unaware of any other condition that might cause pivot lines to "come and go."

--- 帖子 #14697 ---
Click on the chart to get the indicator's external input window. Scroll down and you will see places to input what chart window (0=main, 1=subwindow 1, etc) the text is to go to. There are inputs for the corner of the window, vertical and horizontal adjustments etc. I think the default was set for window 1, corner 3....not really sure. When you first drop and drag the indicator from the MT4 list over to the chart, it opens a subwindow. Whatever that subwindow is (1, 2, 3, etc) then THAT is the subwindow number to assign to the text. I hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #14791 ---
Cobra, I know this won't help resolve your current situation, but should prevent a repeat. It is generally a bad idea to test or, some would even say, develop programs on a production machine. An excellent alternative that is easy for small guys like us to utilize is virtual machines. I would recommend Sun's free and open source VirtualBox: http://www.virtualbox.org/ (if I am causing any problems or breaking any rules by posting a link, please inform and I will edit the post). Basically VirtualBox (VBox) runs as software (only when you need it) on your current computer. You install Windows XP or whatever you need/want inside VBox. When you want to test something you take a "snapshot" of the virtual machine (involves just clicking a button in the management console), boot up, and you are set. If anything goes awry, just revert to your saved snapshot - everything goes back to how it was. Regardless, nothing ever happens to you primary install. Hope this helps. I'm a newbie when it comes to trading, but was a network admin/consultant for years. I have gleaned *so* much great information off of this tread from you, your team and some of the other experienced traders that I can only hope to one day give a small portion of that back. Thanks! ~derek

--- 帖子 #14796 ---
I'm not a programmer, so take the following with a grain of salt: It was my understanding that Metatrader does not allow the code of its EAs or indicators to make any type of changes to your computer's registry or even file system outside of the MT directory (and even in the MT directory there are tight controls). The only way that there is a possibility of an exploit would be to call a DLL that would have to be in the "/includes" directory (you would also have to check "allow DLL imports" in the options). I went ahead and looked at the contents of the zip file and there were no DLLs. So, this would make the DLL exploit impossible. If I had to guess, I would say that the EA was poorly programmed causing it to crash Metatrader and resulted in the file being lost because it was corrupted. Again, I'm not a programmer, so I can not confirm the above beyond any doubt. Maybe one of the programming gurus here (I understand you are quickly becoming one yourself) can confirm or deny it.

These changes are taking place to comply with new National Futures Association (NFA) margin rules . The effective date of the new rules is November 30; however, FXCM will be applying the new margin requirements one week early. Below, you will see a comparison of the present USD margin requirements* for some of our most popular currency pairs next to the new USD margin requirement that will take effect on November 22. NEW MARGIN REQUIREMENTS - USD DENOMINATED ACCOUNTS** CURRENCY PAIR CURRENT USD MARGIN* NEW USD MARGIN USD/JPY AUD/USD (most USD based pairs)$2.50$10EUR/USD EUR/JPY (most EUR based pairs)$2.50$16GBP/USD GBP/JPY (most GBP based pairs)$2.50$17EXOTIC PAIRSVARIABLE BY PAIRVARIABLE BY PAIR* CURRENT USD MARGIN IS BASED ON AN FXCM MICRO ACCOUNT WITH 0.25% MARGIN. Please consult our FAQs for details. &lt;/STRONG&gt;&lt;/EM&gt; Based on price fluctuations, all margin requirements are subject to change without notice and will be adjusted up or down in increments of $1. At present, FXCM does not anticipate that margin requirements will have to be changed more than once a month. Up-to-date margin requirements are and will continue to be displayed in the “Simplified Dealing Rates” window of the trading platform by currency pair. ** VIEW A FULL LIST OF THE NEW MARGIN REQUIREMENTS BY ACCOUNT DENOMINATION Important Notice: &lt;LI style="FONT-FAMILY: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; FONT-SIZE: 13px"&gt;All positions and orders established after November 22 will be subject to the above margin requirements. View Video Visit our online margin help center for more detailed information on the new NFA rule change, frequently asked questions, and steps you can take to prepare for this change. Visit Now Why Lower Leverage Is Important The combination of high leverage and volatile currencies can be extremely dangerous. Accounts that trade volatile pairs, such as GBP/USD and GBP/JPY, with the maximum amount of leverage tend to have less positive performance. On the other hand, traders that focus on less volatile currency pairs, such as USD/JPY and AUD/USD, and use more conservative leverage benefit from the reduced risk that accompanies trading on lower leverage. When trading volatile currencies with high leverage, one bad trade can wipe out the profits from many good trades. By trading with less leverage, a trader can reduce the risk of a big drawdown from one bad trade.

--- 帖子 #14862 ---
The ATR SL is a suggestion that your SL should be within that value but it's not nessesary to use the complete number. Just look for a previous high or low, S&amp;R, pivot etc. and set your SL acording to that some pips above for shorts and below for longs.

--- 帖子 #14883 ---
Hi Stratman, I couldn't agree more. As a matter of fact, no trading system can do without S/R and trend lines. Just a small suggestion here to improve your S/R. Draw only the obvious ones. You seem to have quite a number of S/R lines on your M15 chart. I had only the top and bottom one if seen from the M15. Too many lines makes managing a position very difficult. Only the obvious ones especially those that has gone from S to R or R to S in the near past or those that has more than one touch from PA. Attached my chart (M15 and H4) here for your reference. I only draw S/R off the H4 and D1. In my experience, I find them more reliable than those from lower TF. Since I am already using them for higher TF trades, I also use them for M5 with THV. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #14896 ---
Thanks heaps for your comments. Because I understand the importance of Support and Resistance to THV, I'm trying really hard to get it sorted. I know I'm over enthusiastic with the number of lines. This is my usual approach: 1. Draw on Daily chart, and then more accurately on H4 zoomed out heaps. 2. Each day, my broker gives a list of important prices ie long term S/R. I check my own study and add any lines from their list that I'm missing. I've been using their info for a while now and they seem pretty accurate. 3. I draw the lines from 1 &amp; 2 (above) in a thick width to differentiate them from any others I add in the next steps. 4. I zoom out the M15 and add any shorter term S/R that I see. These lines are done thinner than the others. 5. I also use the Round Numbers indicator which is the dashed lines shown in my picture. Attached is an example. I only had the Price Action up to the point of my vertical yellow line ie prices to the left (EDIT: my S/R lines were added at the time of the vertical yellow line ie prices to the right occurred after my S/R lines were added.). I used steps 1-5 above. The thick yellow lines are to emphasize the step 1-3 lines. The blue are my extra step 4 lines. I've circled all the points at which the S/R held to be true. --- 帖子 #14908 ---
This is caused by the auto-scaling nature of some indicators. I'll try my best to explain. If you look at the scale of the indicator you will see that the massive drop caused a large oversold condition. This caused the total range of the indicator to be larger than normal. MT4 looks at the indicator values that will be displayed (those bars on the screen) and paints the indicator such that the highest and lowest values are displayed. After that large move, the range was so large that any new 'typical' values look really insignificant. Once the large move disappears off to the left, the scale will show typical values at a respectable height again. Scroll your chart back to the left and you will see the 0.000 line moves up and down dependent on the indicator high/low values. I hope this explanation isn't too confusing

--- 帖子 #14909 ---

--- 帖子 #14914 ---
First off, higher TF's rule out over small ones. You'll be wanting to draw your trendlines from the 30 or 1hr. Then If you are a 5M or mintue scalper, take the same chart and draw just a basic upper and lower line for the current channel that has formed. Now you're looking to trade from the channel from either at the top or at the bottom of the line for an entry--or you're looking or a break of the trendline[s]. 15M is good for channel drawing. A lot of factors come into play--and THV is based more on scalping than swing trading--- so one has to keep in mind the psych numbers, but more so than those are the Big Numbers- 00 and 50. As well as the fibs and S/R So when you show a chart where price reacted, it was one of the above, or price action might test a previous known high/low. It's all a cat and mouse game really. The higher TF trendlines help though-- it shows you where the PA will/should eventually go--the bad part is having a trade go bad on you and you look at the higher TF and realize you were smack dab in the middle of 2 trendlines-- the distance between them can be vast. I myself don't draw a whole lot --I use DeMark and an auto-Gartley pattern drawer myself. Ratios between the swings can come onto play often-- which is where the Gartley patterns come in. Sorry if this this was clear as mud, but hopefully some ideas might have clicked for you.

Having had some chicken wings to fuel my brain, the best way to draw trendlines are: the lowest low/highest high of each swing-- then connect them. Usually defined by a doji/pinbar/hammer type of candle. Keep in mind that if you keep the trendlines on your chart--if the PA flips over on you then the trendline that was your support more often than not becomes a resistance.[ and vice-versa] I posted an hour chart of EJ [basic] with the trendlines I would draw on it.

--- 帖子 #14945 ---
Well, here's what helped me: 1) I switched to Strats v20 minicharts 2) in the Options I set the bars in charts and history to only 6000. 3000 is even better if you don't need longer term MAs. 3) I unchecked Save deleted charts 4) The more different charts and especially different pairs you have open the slower MT4 will be so get rid of as many as you can stand. 5) Make sure to restart the Mt4 periodically so it doesn't have to keep so much history in memory. 6) Run as few other applications as you can stand together with it. Try each of these steps separately to see what makes the most improvment. Just as an additional test, I would install a completely clean MT4 then just add the THVv4 indies and open only a couple of charts, and see how much difference that makes. If it makes a lot of difference you can sort out your priorities for how much you really need open

--- 帖子 #15005 ---
Someone asked for a proper fib picture-or how to use them They should be drawn from the highest high/lowest low of each wave--- higher TF has more relavance. What I like to do , is if I'm scalping, I use the next higher TF to draw fibs from -there's waves within waves of each candle The 0 should be placed at the very bottom/top of the wave --which can be tough to do --[never pick tops/bottoms]--but is more easily done once a trend is established. MT4 basic fib tool doesn't have all the fibs [extensions especially past 100] might want to do some research and add those in. hope this helps you

Traco, scalping is the most difficult and time intensive way to make money in FX but on the other side the most effective one, if you manage it well. The most important thing is to have an idea of the bigger picture and take your trades in the higher trend direction. That way you can give your trades enough space to breath and develope. If your SL is too low you will be kicked out very often. Maybe you should try a higher TF until you get the feeling to scalp.

--- 帖子 #15142 ---
With regard taking pips profit ... IMHO take whatever you get given ie don't leave it on the table!!! You might be out for as low as 2-3 pips and tipically 10-20 pips. While I'm learning, I take what the market offers me .... so if I see it reversing on me I take my profit immediately and wait for the next opportunity. If a good setup starts losing, I'm out ASAP .... I don't wait for a stoploss of 3 x ATR. Sometimes, you might get the full distance between support/resistance and medium support/resistance (today approx 30 pips) per trade. Due to the physicological aspects of our nature, this is unlikely though. hope this helps. Regard brokers, there's a problem here at FF if one mentions anything that can be construed as an advertisement for a commercial entity. So I wont mention the name of mine ... but look for one with a very small spread (mine has a spread of 0.9 pips on EURUSD )

--- 帖子 #15148 ---
So I have been trading this system for about a month now, finally have kinda started to hammer down a trading plan for it (which I have already changed quite a bit since the first draft I posted a few weeks ago). For any new THV traders, I would like to offer the most important thing I feel I have learned so far. If your trading the M5 like me, I highly highly highly recommend you only take trades when you have visible support/resistance covering your ass. This system provides highly accurate opportunities if you only trade the ones that have support/resistance lining up with the THV signal. Whether it be OB/OS levels, Divergence and to a lesser extent the Trix Cross (I dont trade trix cross that often), their accuracy is significantly higher with support or resistance guiding your stop loss. Don't rely purely on the THV indicators to find these levels, switch to daily chart and draw fibonacci retracement, switch to weekly and draw the obvious trend line(s) etc. Secondly, I set a BE+2 stop loss once I'm in profit by as little as 3 pips on some trades (up to 10 pips depending on pair and market volatility). I suggest setting up CaveManager EA to help you manage your trade so all you really have to worry about most of the time is finding the best opportunity to get into the market and not so much about when to get out. I have found a cool website to track your MT4 trading history and analyze the data for you, here is my demo account using my THV assisted trading plan: http://www.myfxbook.com/members/deci...ence-demo/5335 Good luck, and remember the first rule is to not lose money.

--- 帖子 #15170 ---
Use Trix called, it's made only for EAs and has no objects which could cause errors if not attached to the template. double STR = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4 Trix called",0,CandleToUse); double STG = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4 Trix called",1,CandleToUse); double FTR = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4 Trix called",2,CandleToUse); double FTG = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4 Trix called",3,CandleToUse); For Trix cross use: double FastTRIX = iCustom(NULL, 1, "THV4 Trix called",6,CandleToUse); double SlowTRIX = iCustom(NULL,1, "THV4 Trix called",7,CandleToUse); The coral color don't play any roll in THV, use for coral: double coral = iCustom(NULL, 0, "THV4CoralT@H",3,CandleToUse); Here an example how to use the Trix colors: if (FTG == EMPTY_VALUE ) { Trix_color = Green; }

--- 帖子 #15213 ---
This is not based on the normal THV trade confirmations. This is based on M5 Trix being overbought or oversold. The THV manual itself has also mentioned trading this method with good results, that's why I'm able to mention this trading method here, since the manual itself has mentioned it. However, it was up to the trader to figure out just when to enter when the M5 Trix is in overbought/sold zone. For me, it would be not close to any news and entrance at the crossing of the M1 trix, best when the M5 fast trix has also changed color, showing signs that PA is starting to move out of the overbought/sold zone. My TP for this type of trade will always be at 10 pips, nothing more. For SL I often would use 15 pips, or 3x ATR(20) SL, whichever is higher, unless the SL where I've had mine set at is close to a major support/resistance line, if so, then I'll use that line as my SL protection wall.

--- 帖子 #15222 ---
I hope you don't mind if I shed some light on your question... Latest version install instructions: _Download " V4.zip " from the first post. _Extract (unzip) to your computer hard drive (can be saved anywhere, but I will be using \desktop in this example) _run " THV V4 final.exe " from \desktop\V4\ _Follow the installer prompts. Be sure the MetaTrader install/broker you are planning on using is selected. _Finish installer but do not start MetaTrader, yet. _Extract " Templates.zip " from \desktop\V4\ _Copy the template files to \templates\ in your MetaTrader folder (this will typically be in C:\Program Files\[broker] Metatrader 4 *) _Install fonts from \V4\fonts . This can be done through Control Panel&gt;&gt;Font s (just drag fonts into window or use File&gt;&gt;Install New Font ) or fonts can be copied directly to your font folder (typically C:\Windows\Fonts ) _Run MetaTrader _On a fresh chart right-click&gt;Template&gt;[select one of the thv4 templates] You should be up and running! On the first page there is also " Manuals and optional.zip " for download. This zip has manuals and a lot of the indicators you see on some of the posted charts that have been customized. ~derek

--- 帖子 #15224 ---
When you set "allow dll imports" in the expert adviser settings (as you suggested), it will set the same as the default on all newly added indicators. Although, indicators currently on the chart will be unaffected. This is why yours was checked by default and worked. I suspect dwhiteviper never deleted the indicator off the chart and then add it back on; if he had, your instructions should have worked. However, I gave the alternate instructions because it is not a good idea to set the "allow dll imports" globally unless you are quite sure only trusted indicators are being used and you know what you are doing. I think the only change in that newer version of FFCal is cosmetics (border color to better match the V4 theme). Of course, there is nothing wrong with making your charts look as sexy as possible! And just in case someone needs/wants the newer indicator, the following is a link to it (to Cobra's upload): http://www.forexfactory.com/attachme...02009%204:11pm ~derek

--- 帖子 #15237 ---
From my understanding of the coral, the color of the coral itself does not matter when it comes to entrance confirmation. The coral is there to help decide if we'll be entering a long or short trade, price above the coral for long, below the coral for short. If everything confirms for entrance for long for example, and coral is still red color, we would still enter the trade regardless of the coral color. This is how I've come to understand it and trade it by looking at countless entrance examples. But do correct me if I'm not correct Cobra.

--- 帖子 #15252 ---
Yes Cobra, that would have been my other point but I forgot to mention that one. So the point behind my theory is that 'turnaround' points would much easier to identify. All in all, there's no big difference between the sum and the difference of the Trix lines, only that in the case if both lines begin to go upwards, you get a bigger deviation from zero. When the fast Trix is about to climb while the slow one is still sloping downwards, you'll get a zero. I think this way it's a bit easier to see the action. I've also made a short computation (60 elements, with some little mistakes) and have drawn a graph with Excel to see how stuff works. You can find it in the attachment, together with the THV HA chart. Let's see where we go from here...

--- 帖子 #15257 ---
This error can come up on almost any computer operation ranging from start up, closing a browser window, putting in a CD or shutting down. The most likliest cause though are program add-ons in Microsoft Internet Explorer (notorious offenders are Symantic/Norton and Yahoo). Do you use Internet Explorer? If so try this: Bring up your browser and go to Tools&gt;Manage Add-ons and in turn select "Add-in Types" in the left hand menu column and then right click on any item you don't want. However, I suspect that you may have a "Helper/s" enabled, if so, disable that/those first. Then, if the problem persists you can turn them off one by one to see if any are causing the problem. If you have a lot of add-ons listed it may be easier to isolate the offender by disabling them all and then enabling them one by one until you find the offender. I'm afraid it's step by step process, I don't know of any short cuts other than as a quickie you could try deleting Internet Explorer and reinstall it but decline the Add-Ins. If you reinstal Internet Explorer you may wish to decline installation of the "Add-in-Helpers" anyway. IMO, they're there to help Microsoft claim eyeballs for advertising revenue purposes rather than help the user. If the problem persists see if the address is always the same and send me a PM. PH

--- 帖子 #15323 ---
Someone has already shown the EUR/USD trade this morning so let's look at the cable. Things tend to happen in the markets around 7am-8am GMT. 1. Heads up on 5 min chart, 15 min cloud Histo (top) turns green about 7.22am. price is already through the 5 min Coral and 20 sma. 2. Price has bounced off the Daily Pivot and the BN of 1.6720. Some divergence here. 3. Switch to 1 min chart and stalk price. At 7.29am price pushes through 1 min Coral (already through 5 min Coral and sma). 1 min Coral is above 5 min Coral. 4. On 1 min chart both 1 min fast and slow Trix green and above zero. Now 5 min Trix also turned green. 5. Go long at 1.6728. Target 10 pips if scalping. Or MR1 at 1.6744 and BN at 1.6750. 6. Stop loss ideally under daily pivot at 1.6703. If you're scalping and want to be tight then place under BN at 1.6717.

This is an older version of the cloud histo that lets you put more than one instance of the indie on a chart without erasing the labels on the first one. Note to Cobra: I think I posted this code and it was lost in one of the restore from backups. The trick is this line shortname=t1+"THV MTF Cloud Histo V3.1.3 ("+Period_1+","+Period_2+")"; where t1 is in the init function like this t=TimeLocal( ) ; t1=TimeToStr(t,TIME_SECONDS); That gives every window a unique name based on the time it was added so the second instance doesn't erase the text in the first. If you have time could you update the code for V4? [quote=seller9;3226664]

Hi everyone, For my first post, i'd like first to thanks all of you for this excellent thread from which i learned so much about forex and of course to Mr Cobraforex and team for sharing this masterpiece. After picking up your work It's now time for me to offer my contribution. So, to have the original Coral from other timeframes, all you need is to change settings of the THV T3 line released in V3. You have to change the code in metaeditor otherwise your settings (color, linestyle) will be erased if you switch your template to another timeframe. From T3 line: - to have the current timeframe coral, the MA period is 60 - M5 coral on M1 timeframe, MA is 60*5= 300 - M15 coral on M1 timeframe 60*15 - M1 coral on M5 timeframe 60/5 I think this method is intersesting to place profit targets because of coral accuracy after a good thv entry. You'll find below corals for M1 timeframe only. ps:sorry, they don't change color and watch out when higher corals are in the place, we had a perfect THV setup on H1 today. cheers from Paris

--- 帖子 #15427 ---
You must use your 15 min analysis chart to help you filter trades. Firstly I would not trade after 4 pm Friday. Friday is an erratic day. However, onto your trade. The price had risen 70 pips in just 4, 15 min candles. This is strong long momentum and a bull flag had formed with the 1.4880 BN as strong support. (bounced off several times) Add to this the daily range was low, only done 82 pips so with this strong upward momentum and more of daily range still to go the odds favoured a long trade. A break of the day's high at 1.4906 (5.04pm) would have been a better trade going long. It is also London close and you get movement much of the time at London close. Wait at London close until it gives away the direction to trade. In future wait for support to be broken. In this case 1.4880 needed to be breached lower to go short. Finally if you do make a wrong trade, that is what your stop is for. Learn from it. Hope that helps.

--- 帖子 #15430 ---
"I made an order that went wrong ... I wonder if I did something wrong in that entry." Just to pop my head in here and head out again.... I think I've mentioned this before. I thought I'll do a little refresher. Scalping smaller TF's can be suicide. Not recommended for traders who aren't familiar with how price action works, I highly recommend trading the 15M charts and scalping pips. It's loads easier-- but have to remember not to be greedy. All my trade I enter on a 15M TF then scale down to a 5M to manage. It's not that it failed to go through the DP--it was knocking at the door. That also was not a bull flag in the technical sense--it was a double bottom-- clearly showing signs of buying with volume on 15M chart. [When there is extreme volume to get to someplace, whether it be resistance or previous high/low-- be VERY cautious of an immediate price reversal] There was no lower low when it started to "knock at the door" Logic would conclude that if it rejected the previous swing low, and it's already at the previous swing high, then it'll more than likely go higher. All indicators were in that favor--including using the Trix as a Stoch for divergence-- 15 M Stoch had a lower low than the previous low area--but the previous low area was actually at a lower price. So, stoch trendline that goes lower and trendline on PA that goes higher is a bullish divergence Now back to lurking..... as work resumes and I travel the country. As Johnny Cash sang.. I've been everywhere man....

--- 帖子 #15434 ---
How the Trix works: revisited I wrote a long "article" about this before. Trix consists of 2 MA's like a Stochastic--one is a signal line, te other is what I call thehull line [like the coral so to speak] Stochastics and the Trix have OB and OS levels, as well as the 0 line. Just becasue the trix line intersects with the ther doesn't necessarily mean a valid trade occurs. I would never consider takeing a trade from OB/OS levels with a Trix on any TF lower than 15M Best trades are when AT LEAST the signal line is above /below in relation to your trade [buy signal above/sell signal below] AND in regard to the 0 line. Example [long trade] Signal line above hull line and signal passes through 0- separation of lines shows impetus of movement. Short is the opposite Below is a good example of a short trade on 5M After the cross, having the trix above or below is deemed [like a Stochastic] Bull and Bear territory. 1st example is an aggressive entry [ without the technicals of the movement] Trix crossed from OB zone and 15M just turned Red. Entry into coral without waiting for pullback. 2nd entry safest. 2nd trix has nice separation of both lines and 1st trix turnedc color in our favor. Both lines for 15M below 0 so we know this is definite Bear area. This with the knowledge PA is looking for the next S/R, BN, previous swing high/low, and knowing about the wave theory. --Normal PA consists of 2-3 waves in each cycle.

--- 帖子 #15443 ---
Hi Ok explaination of my chart settings :- 1)Right click the mouse over the main chart window. 2)Select "Indicators List" 3)Scroll to top 4)Select "Ichimoku Kino Hyo" (this will allow you to edit the cloud) 5)Go to colours and pick the bottom two, "Up Kumo" &amp; "Down Kumo" 6)Also remember to select the thickest line size if you want it totally filled with the colour. You can make them any colour you like from here:- If you want to change the candle type then 1)Right click the mouse over the main chart window. 2)Select "Indicators List" 3)Scroll to top 4) Select "THV4HA" 5) Go to inputs tab and under "Indicator on ?" select "flase" 6) Go to top of MT4 and click on "candle" symbol. 7) Right click on screen again and select "properties" down the bottom, pick "colors" tab and choose what colors you want. One last thing I prefer my candles in the foreground, if you want the same after you have chosen your candle colour, click on the "common tab" and tick "chart in foreground" box. Hope that covers it.... ab1

You asked which S&amp;R are more important for me in your order: 1)daily pivot 2)weekly pivot 3)round number 4)trend line 5)D1/H4 historical line 6)fibs level I give more importance to HLs than TLs but all are important depending the TF you trade. Your 5 and 1 are my favorites. A long term trader would give no importance to a 15M Fib or 00 - 20 psych level, but I do just to maybe scalp 5 or 10 pips. If I tell a daytrader that I draw a TL on a 10 or 30sec chart (available in Oanda ) he will declare me for totally out of order but it works for many scalper folks together with fibs or pivots. Happy Birthday to the THV thread. I'd sing, but unfortunately out of the shower I don't sound that good. This is a template I created a while back, but I wanted to make sure it had sound results before sharing it with the THV community. In my honest opinion, the Trix is a wonderful piece of coding, however, like most indicators, they need to be tweaked for optimal performance for each TF. [Just my opinion] This template is meant to be purely for analysis only--and on 15M- and I hope it keeps people out of making some hasty decisions when trading. Just because it hits a certain area--sure it'll react..... but the big question is--how much and for how long? This template also helps to show weakness very visibly for trend reversals. Another note: I hate to sound like Polly the Parrot, but I must reiterate this is specifically built for the 15M TF. I do not recommend it for 1 or 5M- #1_ the Trix settings aren't acceptable [first Trix]. #2- like the MTF Trix histo- the MTF Trix can repaint. Not as likely on the higher TF's I happened to cross a decent [not perfect-but better than anything I've seen yet] auto trendline drawer--- if you mouse over the lines it'll give a description of each one. Includes: H1, H4, D1 and W1 Props to Miss Pips for Tweaking THV MTFV1 and the creator of the original THV MTF. Your coding skills have been invaluable and I would like to personally thank you. And to T@H for the new updated pivots. Thank You. Included are all the indicators used--- NOTE: Each one in the template has different settings than the default-except the auto trendline--which is optional for the template. I hope this helps the newer traders [and the older ones] to make informed trades. Enjoy. ~IP

--- 帖子 #15532 ---
Volumes Enhanced_v2 adds alert features to the real-time volume/percent of average display, coded by MissPips. You can on any timeframe chart, select an amount of volume you want to be alerted of. This amount will automatically be translated to the proper larger or smaller amounts as you change the chart time frame. A line at your alert volume level appears in the volume histogram display, and a new added label shows the alert volume amount. This label is “grayed out” until the volume reaches the alert level, at which time the label is displayed in a bright color. If you have selected one of the audible alerts, an asterisk appears in the label denoting the fact. You can select to use the MT4 Alert…..a bell rings and a message window pops up showing you the pair and chart time frame for which the alert has just gone off. However, Domas4 has coded a female voice that says, “Volume alert.” It can be selected when you want an audible alert without a pop-up message! MissPips and Domas4 have made great contributions to this indicator, which had humble origins and was based upon the core code of “NVO.mq4” by Vadim Shumiloff. This indicator is not an integral part of THV. However, with Cobra’s previous invitation to post Volumes Enhanced, the upgrade to the indicator is attached hereto. One final note regarding “volume”, it is really the volume of trades, not the amount of money involved in the trades. So, a trade of one mini-lot gets added in, with equal weight to other trades, some of which may involve many lots. It is therefore, not as revealing as with volume recorded in the stock market, where the amount of money involved is identifiable. Nevertheless, sudden spikes in volume of trades can be a valid signal, possibly of an impending run, especially when price action is such that in and of itself a run might well be anticipated. Edit: Added second chart to demonstrate the point made above. This is an example of volume rising as price heads upwards to a double top....more trades as price goes higher....traders jumping on the "SHORT TRAIN". Look what subsequently happened to the price. Volume can be a clue in an overall pricture.

--- 帖子 #15602 ---
Here's another trade I entered. This one is based on the M5 being Overbought. What I look for is this: Once the M5 is overbought, I wait for the M5 fast trix to turn red. Afterwards, I look at M1 trix for a fresh cross down for entrance. TP 10 pips, SL 15 pips. As you can see on my M5 chart, the vertical red line is where I started watching, when the Fast trix turned red. I then looked over to the M1 and entered as the M1 trix crossed down after closing of the candle, as long as the M5 is still showing overbought with red fast trix (sorry, the news calendar is blocking that cross on M1, but you all know what trix crosses look like, left end side red vertical line on M1 is entrance, second on the right is where the TP was reached). I usually always aim standard 10 pips, which usually won't take long to reach, but feel free to take TP at support/resistance pivots if you like if it comes before the 10 pips TP. I do exit my trade however if the M5 fast trix changes to the opposite color before my TP is reached. I don't look at any other indicator besides the Trix on both M5 and M1 for the overbought/sold trades, it doesn't matter where the cloud, coral or Laguerre is for me with these type of trades. I'm pretty much done for today, already reached my session goal for pips, and movement will be slow from here on out most of the days, so best wishes everyone!

When you switch to 1 min chart, do you enter right away if Trix is already going your way, or do you wait for a retracement? Thanks.

--- 帖子 #15604 ---
Depends, If the trix is already crossed down on the M1 when the M5 trix is overbought, I wait for a retracement, M1 to cross up first, and then enter at the recross down of M1 trix as long as M5 trix is still overbought and the M5 fast trix is red, if not, then I don't enter any trades. If M1 trix hasn't crossed down yet, then I enter upon the M1 trix cross at the close of the M1 candle. I always for a rule for myself, to enter after the closing of the candle, to be sure the trix stays crossed.

Reasons: The Ichimoku cloud is 3 moving averages-- [what mode they are I am unsure of but I think they are SMA on close] Since I use higher TF's to look at PA -mainly 15 and 30M to to visually see HH/LL. Not so many mixed colors on the higher TF's using these settings--however, for the same time period on any given chart on a lower TF, the colors lose clarity on these settings as there can be different candles that comprise the larger candles and during that time the MA's can get jumbled and even reversed. I think with the V4 version the new settings of 2/3/8 actually work better on 1 and 5M [which this system IMO is designed/intended for] The Trix I use this version as I can set the Moving Averages within the functions of the indicator to my own personal preference. It's a nifty Stochastic oscillator that shows momentum by changing colors [again I am unaware of the mode or the K and D values of the indicator] But it gives a nice visual-HOWEVER--I don't trade based by colors--- I trade based on where it is in relation to the mid line [0] and the angle of the slope. This oscillator [with it's fixed minimum and maximum parameters] give me an idea after seeing a higher high or lower low to let me know that the trend is changing/rather than just a divergence. It took me a year of trading and a lot of losses to realize that I'm a terrible trend scalper/trader. Truly I am. I am, however very good at spotting trend exhaustion and will wait with bated breath to hop on right at the beginning of the new trend for my pips. [Usually at known S/R levels] I don't consider this divergence trading as I will actually wait for a HH or LL on the 15M then wait for the retracement and hop on the positive trade candle. It's not about waiting for a coral break [as, if you've noticed, the same MA will be in different places on different TF's] The Ma's I've selected and use seem to work best for immediate S/R and will usually line up with the known S/R Chart attached Blue line represents a higher high after the pin bar. I don't necessarily hop on pin bars unless at THE BN [00] or known S/R. So, I wait. The only thing I have going for me is the week [and month] bottom trendline- which is the dark green line] 3 reds are entries Higher high was made, - that happens I wait for the pull back. I enter on the positive candle that confirms after the 2 pin bars- each with higher lows. Support[turned resistance] had a massive doji/pin -exit high spread [the length of the candle compared to the previous candles] and high volume drop back to previous price [not at all bearish ] Another beautiful pin bar with yet another higher high- enter on that Another high volume high spread back to support/resistance-- not a wonderful sign but trend is now confirmed up/changed. Will wait. Candle after that another doji/pin-exit. A 3rd high spread but low volume back to the bottom [know as low volume test]-- candle ends higher than the previous pin. Next candle is an inside bar [very good ] for a 3rd entry. My target on my chart is the yellow line- which is about the area of the last previous high--also a BN 1.4900 Both Trix lines above 0 to confirm bullish sentiment
