--- 帖子 #15620 ---
I want to share a new mtf histogram I've been working on. It is a swiss army knife of histograms. By setting autotf to false and mode to 1 you can combine the following types of indicators in the four rows of histogram Mode 1 ePeriod types: 0 = slowtrix 1 = fasttrix 2 =stochs 3 =trix in Thv classic mode 4 =trix in semiclasic mode 5 =cloud 6 =HA candles Trix in THV classic mode means that the fast trix is above the slow trix and is green and is above zero (for cross up) and the fast trix is below the slow trix and is red and is below zero for a cross down. When neither red nor green condition is met the histo is empty (shows the background). Trix in THV semi classic mode means that the fast trix is above the slow trix and is green (for cross up) and the fast trix is below the slow trix and is red for a cross down.When neither red nor green condition is met the histo is empty (shows the background). Mode 2 When mode is 3 all the eperiodtype settings are ignored and all the timeframes you chose are set to trix classic mode. Mode3 When mode is 3 all the eperiodtype settings are ignored and all the timeframes you chose are set to trix in semi classic mode Autotimeframe When autotf is true, the indicator works like the old one, selecting the next second and third higher timeframes for the fast and slow trix (i.e on a one minute chart, 5m f &amp; s and 15m f &amp; s trix). If use autotf and usesecondautotf are both true, then it selects the fourth and fifth higher tfs for the fast and slow trix. (i.e on a one minute chart 30m f &amp; s and 60m f &amp; s trix) Alarm The alarm only works when autotf is false The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. You will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m HA candle row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m trix in semiclassic mode (fast above slow and green or fast below slow and red). If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first and third rows are true I set countE1 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 2. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore. You can use the identifier parameter to identify which set gave the alarm Additional files You will need all the additional files I included in your indicators folder. This version uses THV3 Trix for MTFHisto which is based on THV trix v6 .1(that is the version used in v4 without all the extras). This one also includes a lower bar count (500) to reduce CPU.If you prefer some other version of the THV3 Trix for MTFHisto just copy yours over it. (But do not copy a regular THv Trix version over it, because the histo needs to use a version of the trix will all the options turned off.) This version also used HeikenAishi_DM which is Dean Malone's version of the HA candles because I knew where to get the buffer input I needed, and for some reason I could not the buffers for the THV HA candles to work with mtf ). They are essentially the same as the THV candles. There are no rules for using this indicator. You can use it with the 6 point system to get an alarm (for example set an alarm on 1f f, 5m amd then count the rest of the lights whenever this alarm goes off) or to get an alarm on any of the other types available. Lastly, there is no more yellow for the cloud when PA is in the middle of the cloud. This was necessary in order to fit it into the histo. When PA is in the cloud, the histo is empty - shows the background color If you have any questions please post them in the thread instead of PMing me so that everyone can get the answer. Edit: replaced mixed histo version due to small bug. If you downloaded the previous version please download v1 instead.

It looks like you are missing "THV3 Trix V6[1][1].1 all false.ex4" indicator. The "[1][1]" indicates the you have multiple copies of the same indicator floating around. --- 帖子 #15694 ---
A stop loss should be used to keep a possible losing trade as small as possible but we always should plan this point pretty well. A SL should be large enough to let the trade perform well but short enough to protect our equity. When a SL was touched it should be clear that the market whent defenately against us and not only a panic reaction. A SL should be protected by a good S&amp;R and it depends on the TF you trade how much pips you are allowing PA to go against you before you declare the trade as invalid. In 1M trades I don't use fixed SL as it could get touched by a simple spike, I use a mental SL. In this 15M example from today you see the entries (boxes) and SL (lime and red HLs). Let's talk about the long trade from touch of S1, PA was rejected and a short entry triggered after a confirmed doji, etc. The SL is protected by S1 and MS2 with a total of 30 pips about, a reasonable SL for 15M. Almost the same happens on the short trade. I hope that answers your post and the PM.

It could depend upon whether or not you're running the Vista 32 or 64 bit versions (not sure if Win 7 comes with both versions or runs the 32 bit as x86). I believe MT4 is written for the 32 bit version of XP only. To get around the RAM limitations of the XP 32 bit I run the 64 bit version of XP Pro (which runs MT4 in the x86 section but sees and uses all the PCs memory up to 8GB). Although initially I solved the problem of running 32 bit software on the machine by having a multi boot program (PowerQuest Boot Magic) so as to boot to the XP 32 bit OS, subsequently I have obtained drivers etc which enabled me to run all the 32 bit software that I use on my 64 bit PCs. I find the 64 bit performance to be superior in both boot up time and operational functions. PH.

--- 帖子 #15735 ---
The cloud indicator is not the same as the Trix indicator,--they are 2 separate indicators meaning different information-- and thus can give 2 different colors at the same time. The 2 different versions of the Cloud indicator have different [internal] settings- the Cloud is based on 3 different moving averages--- the newer version has settings more suitable for the lower timeframes Sorry if this seems confusing for you but that's about as simple as I can make it

--- 帖子 #15751 ---
You're welcome. The Trix Histogram is based on the red and green trix [momentum oscillator] and is able to look at what the trix is doing on different timeframes in *real* time-- I marked real because when you refresh the screen after a bit the colors can and will change. This indicator is the one with the rows of 4 colored lights [red/green] The cloud is a histogram that does not "repaint" -- it is what it is at that point in time. The 3 moving averages that comprise this indicator give an overall sense of the trend [or where it may be going] THe only problem with this concept is that for different timeframes moving averages will be at different spots on the same chart. 2/3/5 is fair for the mid time frames but the lower timeframes -with all the volatility that can happen within each of the mid to higher time frame candles--will make it look like a jumbled crayon box. The new histogram settings with 1 looser MA smooths the action out a bit for the low timeframe scalpers-- you could say they were safer settings. Good Luck in your trading endeavors--if you're just starting out I would pay most attention to the people who've been around awhile--- and perhaps the people with the vouchers by their screen name [not necessarily me though] and look for charts to kind of get the feel of where proper entries should be. Entries are the easiest--exits are very difficult-- so you must learn to be happy with a few at first--what comes can go very fast and one of the most difficult things to achieve is proper money management--not only not over leveraging, but retaining your pips.

--- 帖子 #15752 ---
The Trix histogram lights reflect what the trix indicator is doing on the different timeframes selected. To test this look at the first row which should be the 1m fast trix. If it does not match what your 1m fast trix shows then the trix being called by the histogram may be a different version than the trix you have on your screen. I'm not sure which version of the trix histo you have but most of the ones I released call THV3 Trix for MTFHisto. The latest versions of this that I posted are trix V6.1 which should match the trix released with THV V4. This histo is accurate in realtime but 'repaints' the results for the higher timeframes if added to a lower timeframe after the fact (as do most MTF indicators - see some of my previous posts on the subject) and so can not be used for visual backtesting. Re the cloud histo it reflects what the Ichimuku Kinko Hyu is doing on the different timeframes. It does not repaint because the Ichimoku is just 3 moving averages and it is always possible to know where PA is in relation to them for any increment of any timeframe. The only change I made between the versions of the cloud histo was an improvement to the text display.The defaults for all the versions I released were 2,3,5. (Perhaps in some of the templates released these defaults have been changed). You can change the default MAs used by changing MAPeriod1, MAPeriod2 and MAPeriod3 as shown.

--- 帖子 #15758 ---
Just catching up in various threads and while I don't use the THV system, there are probably other indicators consuming your CPU horsepower. You didn't mention the CPU speed you're using, but even something like a AMD X2 4200 should be very quick to respond for you. First, verify that it is indeed MT4 that's using your CPU cycles by CTRL-ALT-DEL and in the tasklist &amp; find terminal.exe - if it's over 30% or 50% you've got an indicator that's bogging things down. While there, validate there's nothing else consuming more than 2-3% of CPU time. I don't know if you have other indis running, but I've seen RSX indis that really tax the CPU. Best thing to do is to reinstall your broker's MT4 into another directory so you have a fresh install. You can have multiple copies of MT4 on your system, all running independently, even accessing the same trading account. With no indicators installed, bring up a few charts and verify things are nice and quick. Then install the latest THV indis by downloading from page 1 of this thread into your new directory where you installed MT4. I'm sure things will run much more snappy then. There are other MT4 options to look at like reducing the number of bars and history in your charts, but with am AMD x2 you shouldn't need to go there - use the process of elimination and you should quickly be able to hone in on the problem. PM me if you've got any questions.

--- 帖子 #15761 ---
The latest version of THV3 Trix for MTFHisto that I posted is the Trix V6.1 with all the defaults turned off and renamed to THV3 Trix for MTFHisto. That means that the trix curves produced by this trix should match the ones of the trix in V 4, without activating all the bells and whistles of that trix. The reason for this is twofold: 1) since the trix histo has to call the trix many times we don't want all these options turned and overriding whatever you set in the main trix you use and 2) Since the name of the trix that is called by the histo is hardcoded, I gave it one standard name so that the code wont need to be changed everytime a new trix is released, and also so that if you prefer a different version of the trix (say an older one) you can just use one from the previous releases. But anyway trix 6.1 (all false) is in the attachments dated Nov 21st.

--- 帖子 #15773 ---
Some items that I've found that will help you. When you have MetaTrader (MT4) fully loaded, open "Terminal", then chose "Experts". It will tell you if all indicators have loaded properly. When MT4 can't find an indicator that it needs, it keeps trying over and over. This will tell you what's wrong. If you don't have errors, your CPU load drops considerably. You should make sure you have enough hard drive space to handle any needed buffers too. For example, if you are getting down to 5 GB or less, this will cause majors slowdowns. Hope this will be helpful. Kevin

--- 帖子 #15774 ---
As many of you mentioned correctly, going to "Tools", "Options", then reducing max bars in chart and history can dramatically speed up loading MT4 as well as your CPU. I recommend 1000 for each setting. This will allow you to have many pairs open at the same time, if desired. You'll need to restart MT4 after making any changes for it to take effect. Another important item, when adding indy's that have an individual "bars" setting, is to keep them down to around 500. I believe that most, if not all of THV's are already this, but it doesn't hurt to confirm. You must have a fast reacting computer, because any delays can cause you to enter a trade late, which usually costs you pips. If you wish to back test, temporarily turn up your max bars while you need to. Just remember to turn it back down when you're finished. My small group has been studying THV for a few months now, and love it. Thanks for everyone's contribution. Kevin

--- 帖子 #15775 ---
Released herewith is the pair of time zone shift pivot indicators: TzPivotsMW_v3 and TzPivotsD_v3. TzPivotsMW_v3: New DST code from CaveMan automates the turning On/Off of DST so there is no need to adjust your time zone shift settings twice a year. It provides for customizing your own DST setting should you/your broker be in a time zone not covered by the DST code as it is. New code from Domas4 lets you enter a time frame, above which the indicator will not display. This lets you switch to large TF charts to make assesments without having to turn the indy off to remove a congestion of pivot lines. The external inputs section is reworked. Most notably a "Pivot Line Star/Stopt Settings" section is added along with new code that allows lines to be started at the Day Separator. This establishes greater compatibility with the "PivotsD" indy. In addition, labels for Monthly and Weekly pivots now have separate shift inputs. If a Monthly line is so close to a Weekly line that their labels interfere, you can use different shift numbers to display the Monthy and Weekly labels. Code for MaxRight label settings is removed because the current labels shift code accomplishes the same within a few character spaces. TzPivotsD_v3: This is a Benchmark advancement of the indicator, made possible by "Caveman", who generously devoted his time and programming skills to extensively recode the time zone shift section, and to add DST code which automates the turning On/Off of DST. With the new time zone shift code it is anticipated the indicator can handle any situation where there are gaps between trading days, where there are partial trading days, or both. And with the new DST code there is no need to adjust your time zone shift settings twice a year. Also, it provides for customizing your own DST setting in case you/your broker are in a time zone not covered by the DST code as it is. Other changes and improvements are as follows. The external inputs window is reworked for greater clarity and consistency of terminology. The yHL option StartLine =2 can be used even though all other pivots are using StartLine =3. The yHL labels can be aligned with the rest of the pivot labels on the right side of the Today Separator. From that setting they can be shifted to the left side of the Today Separator. Label placement for full screen lines is now expressed as "0" to "100" percent of the distance from right to left, requiring only the number be entered. Data Comments now include user input of the number of days to be used incomputing the average range. New code from Domas4 lets you enter a time frame, above which the indicator will automatically not display. With this feature, the bid line Price Label is removed and a separate indicator is provided to display price and time remaining on the candle. It is called the Bid Line Price &amp; Timer Indicator. Using a separate indicator for price and time keeps that information visible when TzPivotsD is set to not display. MaxRight settings are removed. When lines are full screeen, and if the option has been selected to show the right margin price labels, you can also "Preeminate_MarginLabels_Lines". This will bring both the lines and the margin price labels to the foreground. This does not affect the pivot line labels subordination setting. Separator label coding is modified to place labels a little closer to upper/lower chart borders; helpful when using larger fonts.

--- 帖子 #15776 ---
Bid Line Price &amp; Timer Indicator: This indicator places 3 labels in the vacinity of the bid line: a horizontal LineLabel representing the bid level, a PriceLabel based on the bid price and a TimerLabel showing the remaining time to go for the current candle. All labels can be shifted to the right of the current candle until context begins to disappear. They can be shifted above or below the actual bid line. The LineLabel can be made thicker by increasing the font size, and it can be made shorter or longer. The text of the PriceLabel and TimerLabel can be of the font style and size of your choosing. And color selection is available for each label. The PriceLabel offers 3 colors for: when price has not changed, has just increased, or has just decreased. If the chart scale is not fixed 1 to 1, and you open the MT4 Terminal window below the chart, the labels will shift down slightly. Their position becomes lower than intended by the settings. In most cases this shift down will be minor and compensated for in advance by the settings you select. This indicator can be used for both forex and non-forex items, such as stocks and gold. Credit goes to Domas4 for coding this into the price label. Prime Levels Indicator: This indicator will place up to 6 lines, at prime levels of your choosing, in a successive pattern on the chart. You can have the pattern repeated as many times as you like. For example, you might select lines to be placed at the whole number, plus 20 pips, plus 33 pips, plus 50 pips, plus 66 pips, plus 80 pips and then the next whole number again. This range of lines can then be repeated both above and below this initial range. You can have as many levels of ranges above and below the initial range as you like. Or, you can select zero additional ranges and the initial range will automatically fill below or above the next whole number as the price moves there. The lines can individually be of any color and style, and of any thickness when using solid lines. You can turn on/off each line individually. When lines are full screen wide, you can turn on/off the right margin price labels. You can select to have the lines stop at the current candle. Lines can be subordinated. To specify a level for a line just enter the last two digits of the price level. The labels for the lines can be of any color, font size and font style. You can give the labels a name of your choice (example: Psych Level) and include the price. Labels can be positioned from right of the current candle (0), to far left (100), and they can be subordinated. Zooming in and out on the chart will displace the labels, but with the next data tic, their selected position is restored. The indicator has an ON/OFF switch so you can turn the indicator off when the display of the prime levels is not desired, yet preserve your settings for the chart. You can also enter a time frame, above which the indicator will automatically not display. This enables switching to larger time frames for analysis, and having a chart clear of this indicator's display. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS: Doblece: For the code enabling the indicator to work with platforms with unconventional Point digits number (0.00001 and 0.001). Also for adding two more customizable line levels which default to 66 and 33, as these are places where price usually stops and bounces. Domas4: For the code enabling the indicator to be set to automatically not display above any time frame, as set by the user. Shimodax: For the idea and some core code to get started with (ref: SweetSpots.mq4).

--- 帖子 #15824 ---
Yes, true but in part only. It's a layered process. The small retail brokers match but they have to lay off what they can't match. Bigger straight through brokers, some of whom charge a commission, may or may not match positions before laying off what they can't pair. Matched or laying off, taking it on their books, hedging it in the FX futures market or the FX options future market, someone somewhere has taken the other side. An eventual net/net position is not possible. When it closes out someone has won and someone has lost. PH

Yes they are. I enter a trade only if the PA candle (5m) opens outside the SMA 60 levels. --- 帖子 #15837 ---

--- 帖子 #15838 ---
For GBPUSD, the first thing I check is the day hour time. The best signals for are about 6:45 - 7:45 GMT, London Time. Generally they produse a minimum of 30-50 pips movements. All the London session is good in particular during the european morning. Then I look for the last SMA 20 cross on SMA 60. If the SMA 20 is below the SMA 60 I look only for short entries; if it crossed up on SMA 60 I look for Long entries. For any entries, the PA candle has to open outside the +/-10 SMA 60 levels. I do not open a position always if all the indicator matched... I look for divergence, actual daily range of the chart, pivots, news, recent maximum/minimum peaks. Now I do not use fibos. On the 5m chart important indicators for me are the 5,15 MTF Cloud squares (need to have both of the same color) in combinaton with the colors (confirmed) of the both trix lines (I use THV v3 trix version). Generally when all them and the SMA's matched during the morning, I enter. Also I look for the THV4 Info pannel ATR value... If it is lower than 20 on GBPUSD I do not trade. 30-50 is good. Usually my maximum stop loss is 30 pips; I like to move it. Generally is about 20 but I watch for m5 trix color changes... I like to set a first take profit about 10-15 pips and a second around 20-30. When I enter a trade I also check conditions on M1 GBPUSD chart with THV set up and relationate to EURUSD movements and also take some looks on GBPJPY for referement. In my opinion THV set up is a very intelligent intraday trading philosophy.

--- 帖子 #15857 ---
I have no fixed rules. For GBPUSD SL = from 20 to 40 pips. Usually around 30. I like to move closer the SL after some candles. I relationate it to ATR value of the THV4 Info Pannel. Sometimes I put it above/below the last second candle max/min. May I use the SL as a security assurance and put it "far" and exit manually on some signals or set it close, in case PA changes rapidly direction. Better to have more TP pyramidal targets. Check support/resistence, daily average range etc.... for GBPUSD a first exit could be +13/20, second +30/50. On the first London signals you can also use a third TP, hoping to make 70-120 pips. Relate it to M15. You can use THV HA for good exits. If you re-enter in the same trade use only one, max two TP targets.

--- 帖子 #15864 ---
Got another trade in. Price moved down further than I liked before entering, but still an entrance. This trade was confirmed on M5 chart, to be safe, I waited for candle to close to make sure the Laguerre red dot stays red and not change back to green, so entered later than I would have liked, but just to be safe. This M5 Sell trade was entered @1.5059, and I took TP at the WmR2 line of 1.5049 plus spread, so TP @1.5051 for +8 pips target. A smaller target, but still good pips as for scalping, I use 10% risk. This trade won within seconds. So far today, +21 pips profit. P.S. Just so you know, for Sell orders, I always add my spread with where the Pivot TP line is, simply because for Sell, price needs to go down further to cover your spread to hit target, another words, if R1 was at 1.4000, you actually won't hit it until price is at 1.4398, which means if price doesn't break 1.4000, then you would have missed your TP because of that spread, so when I add my spread, my TP would be at 1.4002, but in reality, price actually did travel down to 1.4000 to hit my TP. We don't need to add the spread for Buy orders because it's already added at the opening of the trade.

Here my considerations and entries for the day. When I talk about TP targets (pyramidal lots), I mean first around 13/20 pips, second 30/50, third between 70/120 for GBPUSD. I evaluate the day session to set the exacly TP. After the first TP is taken, I move the SL. I adapt the TP range on the chart (support/resistence, daily range, day time, volatility, news etc.) Not always I use multiple lots if I consider possible it. Sometimes I do well, others I am wrong. But if one uses 3 different lots, it is good idea I believe, to set the first lot bigger than the other two, so if only the first one hit, the eventual lost of the other ones should be minor than the profit of the first one. Same concept with the second lot. I move the SL.. I belive multiple pyramidal lot entries gets catch better the early trends. Example: first lot 0.6, second 0.3, third 0.1. Total 1.0 I remember that I use instead of coral, a SMA 20 and a SMA 60 with +10/-10 shift levels, and I generally enter only in the direction of their cross.

--- 帖子 #15973 ---
Sorry but yes it is. There are 4 types of divergence. Regular Bullish (Price is making lower lows, but indicator is making higher lows - like in the second pic. This is usually trend reversal). Hidden bullish (Indicator is making lower lows, but price is making higher lows. This is bullish because price *should* be going lower according to the indicator but it isn't. This is usually a trend continuation) Regular Bearish (Price is making Higher Highs, but indicator is making lower highs This is usually trend reversal). Hidden Bearish (Indicator is making Higher High, but price is making lower highs. This is bearish because price *should* be going higher according to the indicator but it isn't. This is usually a trend continuation)

--- 帖子 #15974 ---
I would add to this that while they do not repaint, you don't get to see them at the close of the bar over which they are painted. It takes at least one additional bar, sometimes more before they appear. Also they are not always drawn correctly. This is why it is best to learn to recognize when divergence is forming for yourself.

Hi, maybe someone can explain,what is "stoploss acorddingly to the ATR"? And for example,in my THV windows are 3xATR(20): 13 How can i understand this indie? Best Regards to all!

--- 帖子 #16003 ---
Hope this helps. The use As a rule ATR with 14 periods is used. It's calculated both on a one-day basis, and on day-time or week and even monthly basis. Extreme values of the indicator often define reversal points or the start of a new fluctuation. Average True Range can't predict a duration or direction of changes, as well as other volatility indicators. It specifies only an activity level. The indicator's low level points out quiet trade in a little range, and high values point out intensive trade in a wide range. The long period of low ATR points out integration which, most probably, will result in fast continuation of changes or a turn. High values of ATR usually are the result of quick fluctuations and seldom stay like this for the long period. As ATR indicates absolute volatility value currency pairs on Forex with the low prices will have with other things being equal lower ATR and on the opposite. The main notion of this indicator says "the smaller is the indicator's value the more poor a trend direction is; the higher the indicator's value is, the higher possibility of a turn of a trend is". The weaknesses During a long period of ATR can be late, specifying not ongoing but previous inconstancy. Regards, Cigarguy

--- 帖子 #16084 ---
Here is an interessting idea especially for the scalpers from another trix thread in this forum: How to measure momentum? Just compare the ATR of two different periods! "What is the logic behind the working of ATR(5) and ATR(25)? If ATR (average trading range) of last 5 candles is higher than the ATR of the previous 25 candles, it simply means that trading activity has increased, conditions we are looking for before entering a trade. 5 and 25 means that you compare a period of 25 minutes with 2 hours 5 minutes, 6 and 36 is the same as 30 minutes versus 3 hours." Rules: Take the trade when the indicator is green and the thv signals say go. Stay out otherwise.

--- 帖子 #16162 ---
There are no official opening and closing times for the forex market. Web sites usually use the open &amp; close times of the stock exchanges which are mostly 9 hours or they just guess, so you made a very hard task for yourself trying to make a table of forex times. The forex market is an unregulated 24/7 market. As an example theoretically a London trader could still be trading at midnight local time, but realistically all major players like banks have 'office' hours. As these are the only guys capable of moving the market, these are the best times to use. I worked in London as a City trader for a major bank so I know the 'office' hours for the markets I stated are correct. I don't know the 'office' hours of the other centres like Wellington, Beijing etc as I never dealt with them. Here is a link for Stock Exchange hours - not the same as forex, but maybe you will have use this as your basis? http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of..._opening_times

--- 帖子 #16213 ---
Yes a line from Monty Python Happy you like the Snapshot try the Screen Capture pics in experts/files size_x - Screen shot width in pixels. ( I like 800 ) size_y - Screen shot height in pixels. ( I like 600 ) start_bar - Index of the first visible bar in the screen shot. If 0 value is set, the current first visible bar will be shot. If no value or negative value has been set, the end-of-chart screen shot will be produced, indent being taken into consideration. chart_scale - Horizontal chart scale for screen shot. Can be in the range from 0 to 5. If no value or negative value has been set, the current chart scale will be used. chart_mode - Chart displaying mode. It can take the following values: CHART_BAR (0 is a sequence of bars), CHART_CANDLE (1 is a sequence of candlesticks), CHART_LINE (2 is a close prices line). If no value or negative value has been set, the chart will be shown in its current mode. ( I set to 1)

Hello everyone, Hope you're all doing well today. I had 3 trades already finished this morning for the NY session. I don't trade within 30 minutes before news release, and within 20 minutes after the news release, so with this 50 minutes of free/break time, I'll post these trades here in case some of you also caught it. Note: The first vertical red line I drew (from the left) was the candle I entered the trade at the opening of this candle, that's why it might look a bit far away from the Trix and Laguerre confirmation signals, but it was entered when confirmed by the closing of the previous candle, which was still 2 candles within the Trix and Laguerre signals from each other. I don't enter if those 2 signals are more than 2 candles away from each other, such as both didn't confirm until after the 3rd candle closes, if so, then I don't enter. Only time I might say OK with 3 candle distance is only on M1 confirmation trades, and if the distance of the fast and slow Trix isn't far apart from each other yet (spread out). I also use the next higher time frame's Trix for confirmation. For example, if M1 confirmed for an entrance, let's say a Buy, I look at the M5 Fast Trix to make sure it is green color, if it's not, or the M5 trix has just crossed into the opposite direction, or if it's overbought, I don't enter that long trade (common sense really). Same idea follows for M5 confirmation trades, that's why I have that M15 Trix box on the bottom, to be used for M5 confirmation trades. SL wise, I use 15 pips for M1 Euro trades, 20 pips for M5 Euro trades. For both M1 and M5 Cable trades, I use 20 pips. Target, I always only aim 10 pips, unless there's a resistance/support line before it, if so, I use that for TP instead. If it's a Sell trade, and I'm taking TP at the next major resistance line, I will add spread on top of that value to cover that movement. I also don't close trades early, it either hits my TP or SL (but do whichever way you're comfortable with). All other rules are the same as THV's rules, another words, before you can start trading this method, YOU MUST FIRST LEARN HOW TO TRADE THE ACTUAL THV METHOD FIRST! (located on the very first post of this thread) Which of course, is highly recommended (no short cuts from me, sorry, you still need to do all the necessary work on your own first) =). This is basically it really rules wise, very simple way to trade in my mind. I really only need +20 pips per day, however, once I reach +40 pips during the same session, I close up shop and relax, trying to aim more pips/trades than that within the same session for me is over trading and just plain greedy. That extra risk of those +40 pips profit is not necessary or worth it in my mind. Either way however, I close up shop for the NY session at 12:30 pm EST, the volume after that is usually low, so more risk to false signals. Also, the settings for my Laguerre RSI indicator are: Level1: 0.8, Level2: 0.5, Level3: 0.2, all other values are by default. I've included the extra indicators needed and the M1/M5 templates. I didn't include the M15 template because all it is is the Trix indicator attached onto a plan chart, very easy to do on your own. All templates are made to best fit onto one 22inch screen, you can of course, adjust it as you wish to fit on other screen sizes and resolution (I have dual 22inch screens, one for each pair). ^^ The first trade was a Euro M1 confirmation trade, Entered @1.4346 TP @1.4356 SL @1.4331 TP was reached for +10 pips. The second trade was a Cable M5 confirmation trade, Entered @1.6124 TP @1.6134 SL @1.6104 TP was reached for +10 pips. The third trade was a Euro M5 confirmation trade, Entered @1.4362 TP @1.4372 SL @1.6104 TP was reached for +10 pips. That's +30 pips for so far today. ^^

--- 帖子 #16293 ---
Hi all, I'd like to share an improvement I made to the MTF trix. What I did was to create a histogram that shows the distance between the fast and slow trix. You can judge this by eye but it's easier with a histogram. What this does is give you a heads up that the trend is running out of steam when the distance between the two narrows (or picking up steam when it widens) before the trix actually changes color. In the screenshot below you can see a good example of a heads up that the uptrend that the rainbow is starting to show is not going to get too far, and the main downtrend will be resuming soon. You get a nice warning not to take the 1m trix cross up between the two red bars even though the 5m trix is still green at that point. You will also need THV T3 Trix for this to work. (this mtf trix uses this version of the trix, because you can specify the number of bars and the A_t3 and B_t3 period you want.) You can also use this as your regular trix by setting both auto tfs to false.

--- 帖子 #16294 ---

--- 帖子 #16296 ---
You're welcome. I don't have rules for it yet.It's just to show graphically what a lot of us look for anyway - the spread between the fast and slow trix widening and narowing. What I did to get the histo was subtract the fast trix from the slow trix and show green if the spread is widening when the fast trix is above the slow trix and red when it is narrowing when the fast trix is above the slow trix. When the fast trix is below the slow trix and the spread is widening it shows red, and when the fast trix is below the slow trix but the spread is narrowing it shows green. In general it's better to get into a trend as the spread between the two is still widening. When you see the spread between the two start to narrow, you have to be a little suspicious entering at that point. For example, if you look at the long trix cross on the one min chart I posted, between the two red bars it looks ok. 5m trixes are both green and not oversold, rainbow is up, you have higher highs and lows, PA is not too far from the coral. But you can see on the 5m trix the retracement trend is running out of steam because the histo is showing that the spread between the fast and slow trix is narrowing. Just add it to a chart and watch it and you will see what I mean.

--- 帖子 #16311 ---
[size=3] Entry (for the TF you use for entry) Conservative: for long, PA above the coral, for short, PA below the coral. Aggressive (require good skills): entry without considering the coral. Japanese candelsticks may be bearish/bullish anyway (some times you get a little retracement at the moment of the entry).It is better to have a good HA candlestick in your direction (or at least in the immediately higher TF). If you want consider the coral, take an entry on a candle that opens above/below the coral. Its color depends from its angulation on the chart, personally I do not take care of its color but only of the context around it (but it maybe be useful to share a possible change in trend/PA general movement...) Price crosses cloud For the candlestick color, same consideration as for the entry rule. If you want to make an instant entry does not matter if part of the candle is inside/partly outside the cloud. If you consider the coral, consider it as in relation with the PA. Perfect conditions are for long coral below cloud and below PA and viceversa for short, but not always is that way, it is not an absolute rule (in my vision)… what is important is the actual context of the chart in this TF and in the other adiacent TFs. For the candles, same consideratios as for the entry rule. Consider the cloud as a resistence that has to be broken or used as support. Trix cross and same color for both This is the entry rule for the TF you use as entry referement. Security entry is after the confirmation of the trix cross (close of candle). Watch the chart; look for good angulation between the fast/slow trix when have the cross (see Miss Pips recent discussion on this). Bigger angulation is better. Zero level trix cross Not an absolute rule; it is better if it has crossed. Some crosses very far from the zero level may be retracements or starting divergences, but not at all. You may use this rule to evaluate better the entry. Consider the context of the market. Steeply crosses may they be because of news or strong impuls; do not use only this observation to decide to enter or not. For entries on m1, search for confirmation on m5 at least; for m5 refer to m15 and always refer to the CONTEXT of the chart (trend, pivots, H/L levels, recent min/max, correlated cross pairs, day time, volatility, news, ADR etc……..). Do not enter on OB/OS, or divergence. Consider the trix cross direction in the higher TF and its color. Use THV when you have breakouts, bounces, big retracement or good volatility. Cheeeeeeerssss!!!!!

Ah, it's no problem. I didn't really explain it because it is traded like how it was shown on the chart. For a Sell, we're looking for the change of the green dot to the red dot on the top at the close of a candle, which is a sign of a possible reversal for Short, when the red dot appears on the top. Rules are opposite for Buy, which we would look at the bottom of the Laguerre indicator, when the green dot appears on the bottom, indicating a possible reversal for Long. Hello Megara, Like you, I've also had experience from the stock side before heading into the Forex world, however, as you've found out, both markets, even if some of the indicators/charting methods used are the same, are very different because of the volatility and liquidity, so methods from the Stock side, might not work well, or at all on the Forex side. Another words, one must find yet another method that'll fit for use on the Forex side. With that said however, I don't think I'll be going back to the Stocks side anytime soon, having too much fun over here the past few years, after first having to go through the first year of horror, trial and error. For me, it took around 1 year almost, but for some, it might be faster or slower, it really all depends on how much time and effort one puts into learning this market. However, I'm by no means a "pro", actually, I don't think anyone is, as this market can never truly be mastered, simply because the Market IS the master, not us. They are the Pros for which to fool its traders, not the other way around, we can't fool the market and become a Pro over the market, it's impossible. I pro of the market to me would mean he or she will never lose a single trade to the market, and can move the market as he or she wants it to move, lol, the market moves as it is suppose to, not because it has to. However, in terms of how long it took me to start achieving profits consistently, I would say around 10 months, 10 months of a lot of time on the charts, trial and error, almost going crazy, and finally, realizing the best way to trade is the simplest way to trade, not to mention, much less stressful and time consuming. The basics truly are the best methods, overcomplicate it, and it overcomplicates you.

sry for the german explanation Hallo, ganz so einfach ist es mit dem THV System nicht. Es gibt nicht umsonst noch ein "Analyse Template". THV ist letztendlich ein Top-down-Ansatz, d.h. du musst dir die höheren Timeframes anschauen und mittels Charttechnik die Situation einschätzen. Ich empfehle dir hierfür ein Mindestmaß an Wissen über einfache Charttechnik wie Chartformationen, Trendlinien, S&amp;R etc. sowie Candlepatterns anzueignen. Nun zu deinen Fragen: a) Es gibt keinen besten Timeframe. Je nachdem ob du Scalper, Swingtrader,... bist, entscheidest du dich für einen dir angenehmen Timeframe. Bedenke je kleiner der Timeframe, desto schwerer ist es diesen erfolgreich zu traden. b) Das solideste Paar ist E/U. Etwas volatiler sind G/U und E/J. Ich empfehle dir für den Anfang E/U. Mit etwas Erfahrung kannst du auch die anderen Paare beobachten/traden. c) Die Pfeile zeigen Divergenzen zwischen dem Indiaktor (Trix) und dem Preis(-chart). Wenn du nicht weisst was Divergenzen sind, schau dir das Manual nochmal an und geh auf Babypips.com und geh die Lerneinheiten durch. d) Vor allem als Anfänger (in Bezug auf THV) solltest du die Regeln befolgen! Plan your trade and trade your plan. e) Als Anfänger ja. f) Schau dir nochmal das Manual an. Ich sag nur xATR. g) Ja.

--- 帖子 #16500 ---
Hello, it really depends on each trader's own rules of entrance I suppose. As for me, when I'm entering based on the M5 chart, the only thing I really pay attention to on the M15 is the trix and nothing else really. As with the THV's own basic rules, the M15 chart isn't considered at all for the M5 entrance, at least it was not included as one of the rules to follow in its manual for entrance. Volume wise... THV's zip file does included a volume indicator, but I don't use it. After trading for awhile, you just know pretty much what time of the day you'll get low volumes for the session you're trading, NY or London, and I just avoid trading in those times. You'll also know after a bit when the volume will start to pick up, just part of the things you'll learn as you trade. As for certain time of the year, usually bank holidays, or major holidays for the pair you're trading, like the one we're in now. Each currency has its own country's holidays, so you'll just have to find out when it happens, Forex Factory has a calendar for everyone to look at that'll tell you those holidays as they happen. Dollar, you'll be looking at holidays in the States, Euro, you'll be looking at major holidays in europe, GBP, you'll be looking for major holidays in England, and so on.

--- 帖子 #16511 ---
The yellow news are low impact, and often doesn't make much difference in the movement of the pair, so I mostly ignore it. As for the orange, it is medium impact, so it does affect the PA, especially if you're scalping. Red, of course, is high impact and will often affect the PA a lot. It is of course, always best to try to avoid trading close to the orange and red news, and it's your choice if you want to leave your open trade in with those news coming, but it'll pretty much be 50/50 of its outcome with news, best is to close the trade before release, but again, it's up to you and your risk management.

--- 帖子 #16524 ---
If I'm trading off the M1 chart, all THV rules would still need to be met in order to enter on the M1 (same if you're trading off of M5), so that means price still needs to be above the coral and cloud on the main chart window to enter a Buy, so it's still classic THV rules we must follow for any entrance, if you look at all my charts, those two rules has always been met for my entrance. I do wait for the close of the candle to make sure that it does indeed close above the cloud/coral if that's what I'm waiting for, but then that means it'll be very close (within 2 candles) of the Trix and Laguerre signals. Usually it either all happens at the same time, or price is already above the cloud and coral and we're just waiting for the Trix and Laguerre to confirm, and then enter as it does with the next new candle, as we need to wait for the closing of the candle to confirm that those signals will stay as confirmed. Most of my entrances are all entered after the Trix crossed and Laguerre also showing new opposite dot color (within 2 candles of each other), with price already above the coral and cloud (if for buy signal).

--- 帖子 #16525 ---
All signals needs to be met/confirmed within 2 candles, otherwise, I don't take that trade and wait for the next movement with all signals confirm for entrance. It doesn't matter in which order the signals gets confirmed as long as they all do within close distance of each other (2-3 candles on M1 if based on M1 chart entrance, and within 2 candles on M5 if based on M5 chart entrance)

--- 帖子 #16526 ---
Yes, the trix I look for on the next higher time frame is just the Fast Trix for confirmation if that trix cross is still in the opposite direction of our position we want to enter. Meaning, we can enter the M1 confirmation trade even though the M5 trix is crossed to the opposite direction as long as the Fast Trix has changed its color back to the color of our direction we want to trade (green for long, red for short), because that means it's possible that on M5, the trend might be starting to reverse in our direction, so it'll be fine for us to enter that M1 confirmation trade. Again however, I don't enter on a trade if the higher time frame's Trix has just recently crossed in the opposite direction, or if it's in the overbought/sold zone against our position for long or short. It doesn't matter with the coral on the next higher time frame, I only look at the Trix in the next higher time frame for confirmation as explained in my rules post. I hope that all make sense for you...

--- 帖子 #16573 ---
Yup, I take +10 TP after the spread is made back. So in order to actually get +10 pips TP, price must also have moved to cover the spread as well, for example, EURUSD, if I'm aiming +10 pips, price would have to actually move +12 to hit my target if spread is 2 pips since we start at -2 once we enter our trade.

--- 帖子 #16574 ---
That certainly is one way to go about exiting a trade, and I used to do so, getting out when the fast Trix change color with closing of the candle, but now I don't. I've seen too many trades that ended up good after getting out after the fast Trix change color, so now I just leave my trade in to either let it hit my TP or SL (I do this only with M1 and M5 scalps, I have no idea about M15 or higher scalp settings of how well that would work). But either or can be the way to trade the THV, it really all depends on the individual trader's risk tolerance and risk management. Each of my trade is only using 1.5%-2% risk of my account, so I can handle that. For example: $1000 account balance, using 0.1 lot (10% risk, or $1 per pip), but managed by only using SL of 15 pips or 20 pips, that's $15-$20 risk per trade, or actual risk of only 1.5%-2% per trade, well within manageable risk tolerance for me. But again, it's all up to which way is more comfortable for you and based on your risk management. By the way, if you trade more than one pair, you might not want to use 15 pip SL as standard for every pair, since some pairs moves more than the others. Also, if you're trading higher time frame, you might need to use higher SL as well. With me, when I trade the EURUSD, for M1 scalps, I use 15 pips, but if I enter a scalp trade on the M5, then I use 20 pips. For GBPUSD, I use 20 pips SL for both, which is the lowest I'll go for the Cable pair since that pair is a bit wild, and even 20 pips SL is usually pushing it for the Cable pair. The most I'll enter at once is 2 trades, which would put my risk factor at a maximum level of 3%-4%. I recommend not going over 5% risk at any given moment in your account.

--- 帖子 #16584 ---
Yes, very unrealistic with this method, you'll need to look at higher time frames for trades like that, and I'm talking about 4H, daily and weekly if you want to expect 100 pips TP each trade, with totally different method of trading it, not this method. I wish everyone would keep in mind that this is a SCALPING method. When you see those people aiming those targets, keep in mind that for one, they are not trading this method and have their own method added to it, or they are trading a completely different method. Also at times, they can be having a drawdown of over 50+ pips in the negative before reaching their target or SL, as they will also be using a SL of at least 100 pips or more for huge drawdowns that might happen before reaching that big TP. Price will NEVER only moves in one direction for a long time, it's up and down, there will be retracements that needs to happen before a 100 pips TP can be reached, and that's what you've been seeing. Most people who aim for 100 pips target have done their homework before placing their trade, so they expect that retracement and when it might happen. They also know how to react to it, what to watch for, such as if they should stay in the trade, or get out, it's not as easy as you think, and it takes a lot of time and effort to develop that skill. You can't just ask others what you should aim your TP for when you trade off 1 hour, because there are NO set answers, as each will take TP (different amount of pips) based on THEIR OWN RESEARCH OF THEIR CHART and then set their TP amount based from their chart and method. They might be aiming a high TP amount, but it is never the same each time, or at least for what I considered as an experienced trader that actually knows what he or she's doing. If you want to try to aim for large targets just because you see others doing it, and it's temping so you want to follow, you'll only manage to lose your account in the end because now you'll just be keeping your trades open WISHING that it'll keep going your direction, and are blind to see where price might actually reverse. All you look at then are your pip numbers on your MT4 lower right corner, and not actually watching the chart to see where price might reverse. I can tell right away you've just started trading in this market, that or you're still trying to learn the basics, especially when it comes to the psychological factor of trading. Many things you've said is how most beginner traders think, first beginner mistakes they start making (we've all been though it at one point, and trust me, it doesn't end well most of the time, for me, it was giving away over $25,000 for a very expensive lesson, which never should have needed to happen if I would have known better when I first started). What you need to do is lower your expectations of taking pips, the more you aim when you only just starting out to trade, the faster you'll fail in this market with an empty account. Start small, then as you get better, you can aim more. Greed kills many in this market, so don't let it get you before you really even started. Study, study study study the charts, if you want to aim large pips, then you really need to study the PA of how it reacts to each support/resistance and other patterns for potential breakouts, draw lines and watch the chart, study it, take notes, that's the only way you're get better in this market and survive. If you have to keep asking others for help on small matters such as where you should set your TP or SL, how to trade, then you'll never improve, as you'll never figure out how to do it on your own, you'll always be following others. Many new traders come into this field thinking they will get shortcuts, have people show them how to trade and become successful in a short amount of time, get rich, all without actually doing much work themselves or their own research of chart reading. Sorry to say, but they are the ones that fail over and over again. By the way, Support/Resistance levels are there for a reason, where reversals will most likely happen, I don't even know what would make you think the pair will move in one direction for at least 100 pips first before reversing, and to actually be surprised when price reverses at the next support/resistance level before getting there.

--- 帖子 #16632 ---
There seems to be a problem with the V4 mtf template. The settings for the first histo should be 1m f 5m f 5m s 15m f and for the second they should be 15m s 30m f 30m s 60m f Instead they are both duplicated. If you want finer control over when an alarm is sounded you can used the SwissArmyHisto. (It has the same options as the Trix histo plus additional options plus you can control the alarm.) You can get the latest version here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=16263 And the files and explanation that go with it are here http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=15620 So for example if you want an alert when the 1m fast and the 5m fast are the same color : 1. set Eperiod 1 to 1 and EPeriod1type to 1 2. set Eperiod 2 to 5 and EPeriod2type to 1. 3. set CountE1 to true and CountE2 to true. 4. set CountE3 and CountE4 to false. 5. set MaxScore to 2. 6. set EnableAlerts to true. Then you will get an alarm whenever the M1 fast and M5 fast are both true. And so on. BTW for followers of Nobitacu's version, if you want an alert when you have a trix cross and the M5 f is the same color do the same except set EPeriod1type to 4. As for what went wrong with your trade, if you are using the 6 points method, you need 6 lights from the set described above plus the cloud histo (5m, 15m) to trade. You need price to be above the cloud and coral for a long and below it for a short, unless you are trading a divergence. For divergence trades you only need 2 lights, one of which must be the 1mf and you only need price to be above/below the cloud for a long/short. Divergence trades are risker, so newer THV traders should probably stick to trend trades. Also do not trade a trend trade if there was divergence on the previous peak/valley.

--- 帖子 #16645 ---
Right, you're getting the idea. However, let's say for Long, if the price is ALREADY above the coral and cloud, if that's the case, then those two are already confirmed, then we don't need the coral and cloud to confirm within said candle distance from the Trix and Laguerre confirmation, because then we're only after the Trix and Laguerre confirmation as our entrance trigger, so only the Trix and Laguerre needs to confirm within said candle distance from each other. Another words, let's turn this around to make sure you understand, If let's say the Trix and Laguerre both got confirmed at the same time for Long, but price is still below cloud and coral, in this case, then yes, the price will need to close above the cloud and coral within said candle distance from the Trix and Laguerre for entrance.

--- 帖子 #16650 ---
CountE1 and E2 are in the Swiss Army mixed histo. The alarm in that indie has more granularity. (I got smarter). In that one you can set the alarm for any one row or any combination of rows. In the histo released with V4 SoundAlertONOptimum just notifies you when all four rows are the same color if you change it to true. You can edit the setting in the inputs tab of the indicator.

--- 帖子 #16651 ---
The SwissArmy histo is not officially a part of v4. There are no rules for it. That is, you can use it exactly like the MTF trix histo in V4 and use the same MTF 6 lights rules as always, but the alarm works better (has more granularity). Or you can mix and match the various indicators. You will have to make up your own rules if you do. In my post on the previous page I point you to the latest version of that indicator, and the explanation of how to use it.

--- 帖子 #16652 ---
To answer your questions: Sorry I can't fix the template. I can't use that version because loading the template kills my mt4. You can correct it yourself by setting the second histo to 15m s, 30m f, 30m s, 60m f. Neither indie sends emails. You do not need to use the SwissArmyHisto if you dont want to. (That is the latest version of the THv mixed histo - I changed the name because people asked me to put in their favorite indicators. That is why you need the other versions of the HeikenAshi, Ichimoku, etc because it calls them if you specify those types.) The reason to use the SwissArmy Histo instead of the V4 histo is just that the alarm is better - has more granularity, and also you can mix and match the indies in the histo. So if you want it to alert you when there is a 1m trix cross, a 5m fast trix the same color and a 5 and 15m cloud the same color you can do that. Regarding divergences, both timeframes. If you are trading the 1m and you see a divergence on the 5 m against you then you should not take the trade. Traderathome and caveman will need to help you with the pivots and the EA - I don't use either of them. The THV4 Trix V1.0 and THV3 Trix for MTFHisto are the same but the histos call THV3 Trix for MTFHisto because it is a plain version with all the otpions shut of, so that when you use the histo it won't interfer with whatever options you selected for THV4 Trix V1.0

--- 帖子 #16700 ---
You can use the SwissArmyHisto in addition to or instead of the THV V4 trix. ePeriod types: 0 = slow trix 1 = fast trix 2=stochs 3=Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) 4=semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zeor) 5=cloud 6=HA"; 7=TDI (traders dynamic index) 8=AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) 9 =AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) 10=Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) 11=Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) If you just want to capture the fast and slow trix then use types 1 and 0 respectively. If you want to get notified when, for example you have a 1m trix cross with the fast trix above 0, a 5m fast trix in the direction of the trade and the 5 HA and 15 cloud in the direction of the trade then you would use the following eperiod1 = 1 eperiod1type = 3 eperiod2 = 5 eperiod2type = 1 eperiod3 = 5 eperiod3type = 6 eperiod4 = 15 eperiod4type = 5 You would set the Count E1-4 params to true and Max score to 4. If you want to see the 15 cloud in the histo but not include it in the alarm you set CountE1-3 to true and CountE4 to false. Then set Max Score to 3. And so on...

--- 帖子 #16721 ---
This is a long answer so grab a pot of Yorkshire tea and settle down to read. Then find some examples for yourself to test. Firstly yes, I get a heads up on the 5 min chart and then go to the 1 min for entry. Here's the procedure with an example... TIS Execution Procedure The pre-session routine is done and the intra-day routine is in effect as detailed in the Trading Plan. (See my earlier posts) In particular note the trend on the 15 min and 1 hr charts. Trading with the trend is preferable. Also note whether or not there is enough ADR left in the direction you intend to trade. Trading Long 1. Monitor the 5 min chart. The heads up is the 5 min IC histo turning green (top Histo). (This is what I need the alert for) 2. Next look at where price is in relation to the 20 sma. Is it above or below? Price above the 20 sma is better/less risky when the trade is taken. Are the 20 sma and Coral lined up correctly? For a long the 20 sma should be above the Coral when the trade is taken. 3. Now move to the 1 min chart . “Stalk” the price action and only take a long trade when the (Ichimoku Cloud (IC) and price is above the Coral. Looking at the 1 min chart price must be above the Coral and both top IC histos must be green when you trade. 4. Both the 1 min fast and slow Trix must cross each other and both be green. (Best and most secure trend confirmation is when the fast Trix crosses above the zero level). 5. If the 1 min fast Trix is overbought wait for the next wave when the fast Trix turns green again. 6. On the 1 min chart you can see the 5 min Trix. Safest long trades are when at least one (usually the fast trix) is green. Ideally both are green. 7. All the time monitor the 5 min chart to see if the price is above the 20 sma . (Also the safest trade is when the second Histo, the 15 min Histo has turned green so both Histos are green .) 8. If more than 10 pips to resistance take the trade long. Again this is not an absolute rule but most conservative. 9. Place a stop loss as detailed in the plan, ideally below the last 5 min Swing Low if not too far away and is within your money management rules. 10. Exits can be a flat 10 pips, Sweet Spots, trendlines, pivot points or other support and resistance. It is also possible to scale out with 50 % at the first target and 50% at T2, whilst bringing the stop closer to breakeven. Please read the section on ADR. Trading Short Exactly the opposite but change up for down, long for short, below for above, green for red etc... More aggressive trades can be taken (going for only 10 pips) by ignoring points 2, 6 and 8. In other words you’re not concerned with where price is in relation to the 20 sma; you’re not concerned about the colour of the 5 min Trix and you are not concerned about trading into support or resistance. Trade example (Short) EUR/JPY 1. Downtrend. (Not shown) Heads up on 5 min chart when the 5 min IC Histo turns red at 0700 hrs. (They both turn red at the same time which is better) 2. Price is moving below the 20 sma and the 20 sma is below the Coral which is good for a short. 3. Looking at the 1 min chart (below) price falls below the Coral and both top IC histo lights are red. (0701 hrs 4. Both the 1 min fast and slow Trix have crossed each other and both are red. (Also fast trix crossed Zero line) 5. 1 min fast Trix not oversold. 6. Both 5 min fast and slow Trix are red. 7. Back to the 5 min chart, the price is below the 20 sma . Both IC histos on 5 min chart are red which is good. 8. There are more than 10 pips to support so the trade is taken short at 129.74. 9. A Stop Loss is placed above the Swing High at 129.91 (total 17 pips which is good). 10. A limit order is placed at the Sweet Spot 129.50 to exit the trade. Please note if you are purely scalping for 10 pips then you’d exit at 10 pips profit. Just try a few examples for yourself. This seems long winded but with practice you look for these 10 points almost by instinct and it takes SECONDS. Don't forget after the heads up on the 5 min chart you may have to wait for the price to cross the Coral on the 1 min chart.

--- 帖子 #16731 ---
Have a read of the full trading plan post 15399 page 1027. That's a start. 1. 20 sma from MT4 indicators 2. 1st IC is 5 min second one is 15 min (on 5 min chart) You don't have a fast and slow Ichimoku Cloud 3. Use the THV Info Bar in the download. It gives ADR for you on screen. Average Daily Range (ADR) The average daily range of a currency pair will usually be completed between 4 hours before the end of the Tokyo session and the end of the London session. This is important. I trade intraday so I need to know the ADRs of the pairs I’m trading. This is because I always want to know how much further a pair could realistically move given its ADR compared to today’s range. This information is useful for profit targets and stop placement. If the ADR of cable is say 210 pips and at 1pm GMT it has moved only 100 pips then chances are another move of size is still to go. (Usually with the trend) We can use this to our advantage in our trading. This is because once a day (at least) a currency pair will make an extended run towards its ADR. We just need to decide which way. This will depend on time of day, how early/late it is in the session and the current trend. The extended run is almost always due to a news item. If only half the range has been done for example, I could scale out of a position hoping for the big run to ADR. I usually scale out at 10-20 pips on the 5 min chart and 20-30 pips on the 15 min chart or so to reduce risk. Then bring stop loss to break even plus 5. If a pair like the EUR/USD has an ADR of 150 pips and during a given day it has been trading at the top of this range with the session end approaching it would not be prudent to open a new long position because this would not be a high probability trade. In addition if the ADR is greatly exceeded in an extended move, then watch for a pullback to the average range area. This is sometimes good for counter trend trading after London closes. I use the ADR calculated over the last 5 days as my ADR. I also watch the 20 day ADR too as a possible extreme and as a test of volatility. Software is available on the internet to calculate the ADR for each currency pair. See trading plan for more details 4. See trading plan. Human psychology Sweet Spots 00, 20, 50 and 80 are sometimes called Sweet Spots. These can be good support and resistance levels. The market tends to slow down or consolidate at these numbers especially with the GBP/USD and EUR/USD (most of the majors too). They are good for profit targets and also excellent points to enter the market. Sweet Spots are ideal technical areas for placing stops especially if they coincide with recent highs and lows. These are used extensively in our methodology in preference to pivot points. Why do Sweet Spots work? – Well we know the forex market price action and levels are the sum of the human psychology of those people taking part in it. (See Trading Psychology in Chapter X) As humans we like order and we like round numbers. Just think about it. 10, 35, 65 and 90 are mid range numbers (MN). These are weaker but can be used as entries or targets. Also I'm writing a book at the moment and here's my thoughts on systems... Some Thoughts on Trading Systems To be a successful trader you need to use your judgment. A trading system is a style of trading, not an automatic turnkey operation. To benefit from a system, you must test its parameters and fine-tune them until that system becomes your own, even though originally it was developed by someone else. Winning takes discipline, discipline comes from confidence, and the only system in which you can have confidence is the one you have tested on your own data and adapted to your own style. You are under no obligation to buy or sell. You have the freedom of standing aside, but most traders throw away this awesome advantage. People get sucked into the excitement of the game. They jump in instead of waiting for the best trades. Remember, the idea is to trade well, not to trade often. Finding a profitable trading plan once you have grasped the basics of forex trading is not the most difficult part of trading. The real difference is the ability of the trader to stick to the plan and trade it consistently, without fail, time after time. The reality is that 90% of traders simply cannot do that and that is why they fail. Sticking to a trading plan/system and trading it consistently with discipline is what separates the winners from the losers in the end. TIS Execution Procedure The pre-session routine is done and the intra-day routine is in effect as detailed in the Trading Plan. (See my earlier posts) In particular note the trend on the 15 min and 1 hr charts. Trading with the trend is preferable. --- 帖子 #16769 ---
You don't need to add these indies that the Swiss Army histo calls (the Ichimoku and the Trix for MTFHisto) to your chart. You can use the corresponding indies that come with V4. These indies just need to be in the experts/indicators folder so that the Swiss Army histo can call them. The Trix for MTF histo IS the V4 trix with all the bells and whistles removed to reduce load on CPU and to prevent it from changing the options on the chart when it is called. The Ichimoku necessary because I couldn't get code for the one that came with MT4, but it is extremely similar, and the one that came with MT4 (called by the V4 template) looks nicer so you can leave it. Likewise for Heiken_Ashi_DM, I couldnt get the code to work with the histo. The THV MTF mixedhistoV1 was renamed the SwissArmy Histo because it contains other non-THV indies that people requested, so just use the latest version of the SwissArmy histo if you want to get alerts for any of the combinations it provides.

Here's a version I improved a bit. If you don't want the histogram set showhisto to false. To get one tf up set autotimeframe to true. 1. Yes. 2. Yes, but coral and cloud, except divergence trades, then you don't need to wait for the coral 3. No. But the more extended price is (however you measure it - distance from coral or rainbow) the less good the chance of a sucessful trade. What I usually use to keep me out of bad trades is I don't take a trade if there was divergence against it on the prior peak/valley. Also bear in mind that price moves in waves. You only get so many waves (change in color) of the 1m trix per 5m change of color, so the ones closer to the 5m trix change in color are better than, say, the 5th one.

If you select mode 2 the light is green when the fast trix is above the slow trix and above zero, and red when the fast trix is below the slow trix and below zero. However, the fast trix could be green, but below the slow and below zero and the light would still show red. However if you select mode1 and type 3 (which is also named classic) you get the same except the light is only green or red respectively if the fast trix is also green or red. That is it is green when the fast trix is above the slow and the fast trix is also green and red when fast trix is below the slow and the fast trix is also red. So I should have given that a different name. In either case, this was not how I tested the system. Therefore, If you are using mode2, you are no longer following the 6 point system as I tested it. --- 帖子 #16831 ---
Pretty much exact same trade as mine, good job. Most often it actually is if its close to a major psychological level. If you watch PA enough at major psychological numbers, price will more often than not, break above it for a bit, then do a retrace down below it again before figuring what its real move's going to be. I believe that's just the broker trying to get the price to cross up a bit to take out those SL people has placed a bit above it, then after that, price goes back to normal, and back below the major psychological level. What some traders might do however is this, let's say the major psychological level is above the current price level, they will place 3 entrance points a little above that level for Short, and then watch as price goes above it a bit to hit those short entrances, and then price moves back down below that level after the broker takes out those SL traders has placed there for quick TP scalps. The Euro 1.4500 did exactly that just now.

--- 帖子 #16849 ---
System Idle Process is not what the CPU is actually using, it is what the CPU is NOT using, so that's why it's usually always above 90%, which is actually a good thing. What you should fine is what's using the most CPU other than the System Idle Process (which is actually opposite), then from there, from how why it is using that much CPU. If that program is the MT4, then yes, as EMP suggested, it might be because you have too many charts open at the same time and your computer isn't fast enough to handle all those CPU/Ram demand. Hope that helps a bit.

--- 帖子 #16874 ---
Emp, Traco1 has the right idea, only that it's not about the zero line, it's about the distance between the Fast and Slow Trix being already too far apart from each other. The movement is already pretty much over when you entered looking at the Trix, and also, like others said, do watch the pivots as well, especially during low volume times when they are stronger since there won't be much strength in the movement to help break it. You're also trading Euro when they are sleeping in Asian, which is usually a bad idea, best to trade a different pair if you want to trade in Asia, not eurusd or gbpusd and so on when you know they are sleeping, the volume is just too small during these times for it, and you'll get more false movements. Also, the reason why I have that M15 Trix there is because it needs to be looked at if you're entering based on everything being confirmed on the M5 chart. It's the same concept like when you see everything confirm on the M1 chart, you need to look at M5 Trix for confirmation. I don't use the M15 Trix with my M1 entrances, but I use it for my M5 entrances, just like how I use M5 for my M1 entrances. When you trade because you're trigger happy, it'll cost you, this is a apart of the psychological aspects of trading for which you still need to work on. You're forcing trades and taking more risk instead of waiting for the good trades with less risk to come to you. It's not only the learning of a trading method you need to understand, you also need to understand the market hours, how each currency reacts to each market sessions and most importantly, understanding MM and trading psychology. I highly recommend you to read up more on those last two parts.

--- 帖子 #16896 ---
If entering based on trade being confirmed on the M5 chart, the M15 fast Trix must be the same color of the direction you're trading. This is the same rule when enter with M1, as you need to then look at M5 Fast Trix to make sure it is the same color of your direction. As I've stated, don't enter a trade if the next higher time frame's Fast Trix is in the opposite color, or its Trix recently crossed into the opposite direction of your trade, or if it's oversold/bought against your direction.

--- 帖子 #16921 ---
Hi All, Here is a new version of the Swiss Army indie. Changes in this version: 1. I added the option to monitor the coral. This means that you can set this indie to give an alarm when all THV condtions are met (Price above/below coral, above/below cloud and Trix cross). This version is configured by default to display an alert when the THV conditions are met. You can also use it to get an alarm for Nobitacu's method (more or less, you have to check the Laguerre by yourself, but you can get an alarm for the THV conditions plus the m5 test. ) To get this alarm change the defaul settings so that countE4 is true and maxscore is 4. 2. I added a changeable identifier to the alert message in param MessageID. You can change this so you will know which instance of the indie gave the alert. 2. Sorted out the lack of user friendliness in the modes. I changed the name of Mode 2 to "demi-classic" since it really shows you when the fast trix is above/below the slow and above/below zero, but not if the fast trix is still in the direction of the trade. (That is, fast trix could be below slow and below zero, but not red anymore) So now the modes and types are Mode 1 looks at ePeriod Type, which can be the following ePeriod types: 0 = slow trix 1 = fast trix 2=stochs 3=Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) 4=semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) 5=cloud 6=HA"; 7=TDI (traders dynamic index) 8=AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) 9 =AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) 10=Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) 11=Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) 12- Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) 13 -Coral Mode 2 ignores eperiod type and sets all tfs to demi classic mode (fast trix above/below slow and above/below zero, but may have changed color against the trade. Mode 3 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to classic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade and above/below zero) Mode 4 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to semiclassic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade but not necessarily above/below zero) In addition to the files previously posted for this indicator you will need THV HelpY1 in your indies folder (not on your chart) for the coral histo to work. This is slightly different from the V4 Coral but not enough to make much difference. If you haven't previously used this indie, see this post for the other files that go with it and the explanation of how to use the alarm. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=15620 You only need the files in your indie folder, not on your chart, and you do not need the THV Mixed Histo (that was the previous name of this indie, so that is the first version of it.)
