--- 帖子 #16965 ---
With mode setting of 1, the indie looks at whatever you configured the ePeriodtype to. (With modes, 2,3, and 4 it ignores ePeriodType). I can see from your screenshot that you have, for example configured mode 1 and set the first row to 1m fast trix, which is different than classic mode. If you added more than one instance of the indie with the alarm set to true, each of them will give you an alarm. I can see from your screenshot that the first alarm is on the EuroUSD and the second is on the EUROJPY for instance. Also if you configure Maxscore to 3 but set countE4 to true then you will get an alarm when you have four points as well as three. This is intentional. If you don't want to include the fourth row in the alarm, set countE4 to false. I added the coral to the indie. This means that if you use it with the defaults I posted, you will get an alarm when there is a trix cross on the 1m, price is above/below the cloud and above/below the coral (i.e THV trade conditions are met.) The picture does show divergence, as you can see by the red arrow in the trix indie. There have been lots of posts and even a cheat sheet about divegence posted in the thread if you want to find out more about it.

--- 帖子 #16989 ---
1) Actually that template is not my template and I don't use it. The correct configuration for the 6 point method, if you are using it is 1m f trix 5m f trix 5m s trix 15m f trix the second histo to 15m s trix 30m f trix 30m s trix 60m f trix Cloud 5,15 You may, however, configure the Swissarmy histo in any configuration you like. 2)Classic mode is when the fast trix is above/below the slow, fast trix is above or below zero and is still green or red for a long or short trade respectively. 3) In your screenshot, if the red line on the chart indicates the matching time for the message, a good deal of time has passed between the message and the current state of the chart. I would have to see this live (i.e a screenshot where the message matches a time that is the rightmost column in the histo) in order to answer. Also, as has been discussed many times in the mtf indicators can repaint (compared to what you would have seen in 'real time' ) if initialized, which can happen if you change the timeframe on the chart or if you get a broker disconnect. In other words, if you went away and left your chart, and came back an hour later, and found that message, and compared the time on the chart (assuming the red line is the correct time of comparison) and your mt4 had disconnected and reconnected, the indie could have recalced and wouldn't match what you would have seen in real time. Also the trix itself can repaint one bar back (which has also been discussed many times) so any indicator based on it, which the histo is, can do so as well.) 4) As downloaded the last version of the SwissArmy histogram will give an alert when a)fast trix is above/below slow trix and fast trix is above/below zero and fast trix is still green/red b) price is above/below the coral c) price is above below the cloud. The classic THV trade conditions call for a trix cross, price above/below cloud, and above/below coral for a long/short respectively. Fast trix above/below zero is also recommended, though not, I believe mandatory. Classic mode for the trrix gives an alarm both if there has been a trix cross and also if there has been a previous trix cross (say up) and the fast trix has changed to red, and then changed to green again (without crossing back down over zero or over the slow). You need to check the chart itself to verify which case, but this condition is one that many people also trade.

--- 帖子 #17023 ---
Hi Nobitacu, Burton has pointed in the right direction for the setting for "HrsServerTzFromGMT" which is basically the number of hrs difference between your brokers server and GMT. The setting for "HrsChoiceTzFromGMT" will depend upon what you consider as close of the day for calculations of pivot points. As many brokers consider close of NY as the close of the Forex Trading day, then it should be set to -5 as NY is 5 hrs behind GMT. Incase, NY has daylight saving time also then this setting has to be adjusted accordingly. I read somewhere that some Traders who are active in the Asian markets change the settings to suit close of Tokyo. Trust above clarifies Cheers

--- 帖子 #17030 ---
First, no system has 100% hit rate even if you follow it perfectly. Second, the hours this system was tested for were one hour before German open to London close, because we need some good volume for it to work. This trade is outside those hours. Third, even though it seems to you like this should be a purely mechanical approach it is not. Your results will be determined by how well you pay attention to where you are. If you are at a major support resistance, there will be choppiness. You can usually see this support as divergence in the 1m or 5m trix if you are paying attention (even if you don't know what's causing it), and therefore you should not trade when there is divergence in your tf or the next higher one. You need to wait to see if that support is broken first. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) Fourth, another aspect of paying attention to where you are is paying attention to the daily range. We are now in a narrow up channel that is part a bear flag on the daily chart. The daily range has been about 90 to 100 pips lately. The market had already done that range when you took that trade. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Lastly, you entered the trade a couple of bars late (even though you would have been stopped out anyway. In summary ,it is not a high probability trade to take when the market is at the end of its range and at major support, shows divergence, and the trade is outside of main market hours that might drive it farther down. Edit - now we are here. See how the London open provided volatility so that market went down to the next fib level and how it respected the next fib level once it broke support near the previous one? (I personally didn't trade that. When the market is too near the end of it's usual range I stay out until it either reverses or gives a good pull back. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

It may seem like THV is a mechanical system, but it is really a discretionary method. While no trades should be taken in violation of the rules, each trading opportunity needs to be analyzed as to what can go right or wrong with it in light of prevailing conditions ( is this a good time to trade, where is support, where is resistance, where are the pivots, how many times have they been tested, how strong is momentum now and how long has it been going in the current direction, is there a major fib or trendline nearby, when is news, where is the trade in relation to the daily range, is there divergence, was the signal caused by a freak oversize bar and more, and all these have been discussed many times in the thread.) --- 帖子 #17158 ---
Well here is a new version of the Swiss Army indie including divergence. In order for it to work you need the attached indicators in your indicators folder (not on your chart). If you want the divergence setting to work on the 1m chart you need to redownload THV3 Trix for MTFHisto, because that setting was turned off in the previous version. If you don't need to see divergence for the 1m tf in the histo you can stick with the previous THV3 Trix for MTFHisto if you already downloaded it. Changes 1) Added a type for divergence - type 14 2) Added lines between rows and the ability to show/hide them (showlines param, LineGap param,HighLine_Color param ,Line_Style param) 3) Changed all the trix types except the divergence type to use the T3 trix instead of the THV3 Trix for MTFhisto. This means you can set the number of bars the histo goes back ( in TrixNumberOfBars param) and adjust the histo to match the trix version you use ( in the hot param, 0.7 matches 4.01 div and 1.2 matches THV V4 Trix V6 trix and THV V4 Trix V1. However the divergence type matches only latter two and cant be changed. Also this version of the trix uses fewer resourses. However if you set the number of bars to a very large number it may slow down your MT4) So now the modes and types are Mode 1: ===== Mode 1 looks at ePeriod Type, which can be the following ePeriod types: 0 = slow trix 1 = fast trix 2=stochs 3=Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) 4=semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) 5=cloud 6=HeikenAishi; 7=TDI (traders dynamic index) 8=AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) 9 =AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) 10=Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) 11=Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) 12- Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) 13 -Coral 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Mode 2 ====== Mode 2 ignores eperiod type and sets all tfs to demi classic mode (fast trix above/below slow and above/below zero, but may have changed color against the trade. Mode 3 ====== Mode 3 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to classic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade and above/below zero) Mode 4 ====== Mode 4 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to semiclassic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade but not necessarily above/below zero) Autotimeframe =========== When autotf is true, the indicator works like the old trix histo, selecting the next second and third higher timeframes for the fast and slow trix (i.e on a one minute chart, 5m f &amp; s and 15m f &amp; s trix). If use autotf and usesecondautotf are both true, then it selects the fourth and fifth higher tfs for the fast and slow trix. (i.e on a one minute chart 30m f &amp; s and 60m f &amp; s trix) Alarm The alarm only works when autotf is false The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. You will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore. Edit: Changed version of indie to 11 - fixed small problem with lines

Forex is not an easy market, you can score big one or two days and lose everything in one day. This is all about the trader and little to do about the markets. If you want to learn about THV you should really take the time to read the thread from the beginning...sorry that this is probably not what you want to hear but believe me you will learn a lot. Everyone has their own trading style and TF and trying to follow someone else's will only lead to losses. You need to demo trade and make it your own system. You may not need all the indicators that's been added and you can be quite successful with using the basic rules and develop them as you go along. Take the time to read and be patient and success is guaranteed...best of luck.

Well, I'm slowly absorbing the intricacies of the THV method of trading, but my biggest obstacle has been self control. When I first open up the trading platform in the morning, I have an overwhelming desire to place a trade. That urge tends to make me overlook the rules, and that is a BIG mistake. I need to come to grips with my biggest problem.....ME! I have had a pretty good record of winning trades vs losing trades using THV, even with that shortcoming. And once I get that "trade urge" under control, I expect the wins to come more often. One thing I love to do. When I do have a losing trade, I "capture" it and then go back and analyze what took place. Usually, the problem is obvious - broke the rules again! I firmly believe that two of the most important components of Forex trading are: #1 Self control (learn to follow the rules) #2 Money management (setting parameters BEFORE a trade to protect capital and enhance profitability) Seems so simple, but we all know it isn't. However, once we master these two areas, potential for profitable trading will increase. I welcome everyone's thoughts on the subject.

--- 帖子 #17217 ---
LOL, sorry, missed your post somehow. For the TP and SL targets, just read the first few post of this thread on page one, and on the THV manual, it'll have answers there for you on what you should aim for TP and what you should do for SL, then just trade and test it out on your own. We can't give targets of how many trades we will trade per day because we simply take trades as they confirm and comes to us, so we don't know on a daily bases how many trades we'll receive within a said time frame... For example, I trade from NY Open until 4 1/2 hours after, and I usually get 1-3 trades per pair that I'm trading, but it really depend from day to day, there was one time that I received zero trades to confirm during the 4 1/2 trading hours. If you meant Pip wise for target, again... it depends on your own personal way to trade this, for me is 20 pips per session as target, and I don't always reach it, or at times I'm over by 10-20 pips, again, it depends on the trading day. But really, ALL of your answers can be answered on its own after you actually try trading the THV for a bit and read the first few post of this thread (do try to read most of this thread if you can however), don't try aiming a lot when you start, just aim small daily pip goals, after you improve enough, you can try to aim more if you develop more ways to enter QUALITY trades. If trading THV alone with its original rules/method of trading, it will not get you 50 pips within 3 hours, very unlikely anyways if trading only 1 pair. Just start trading yourself, take notes on each of your trades of why you entered that trade, and what might have caused the trade to lose if it lost, and then also write down on average how many pips you get per day, or lost, after that, set your target based on that number, and see if you can improve it slowly by improving your trading method, by reading all the notes you've took before on each trade. Your own experience is your best teacher. A good trader can turn any losing method into a good method, while a bad trader can turn any great method into a losing method.

--- 帖子 #17241 ---
First I never taking trade based on M5 confirmation. If you will see most times you got first confirmation on M1 and after that confirmation on M5. I have just one exception when I am taking trade based on M5, it's bounce from important line (support, resistance, round numbers), but always watching M1 trix. For example: I got sell confirmation on M5, all conditions are met (important M15 Fast trix must be red, 30 min Fast trix can be red too for safety entry). After that I watching M1, if I see bounce from important line, price is below Coral and cloud, Fast trix is red so I am taking this trade. But mostly I take trades with M1 confirmations. M5 confirmations are very risky for me.

It's your choice. For example: when you got SELL signal on M5, M15 Fast trix MUST BE RED. If it will become red after some candles it's wrong signal for me. One more thing about your sell trade on M5. It was too late. All conditions must agree between 2-3 candles. If it's 4-5 candles between all confirmations it's wrong signal. I always did this mistake, while Nobitacu explained it for me. This info is in Nobitacu trading rules, but I didn't think it's too important. Now I am trading just with this rule. Buy signal on M5 was perfect, because all confirmations was in 2 candles distance.

Dear all, Just sharing.I found the THV system more powerful using divergence technique.When the TRIX indicates divergence on TF 5M and TF 1M , time to go short/long.I always keep an eye on the TRIX (this is the best oscillator IMHO) and THV Histo. Just wait until each time frames have the same 4 lights on their TRIX histo. It won't take long to get 10 pips or more. Watch out the opposite divergence on TF 1M.If you see it,close the trade even when you just get less than 5 pips.Wait for the next divergence on TF 1M goes to your favour. My own rules using THV is Entry :divergence on TF 1M and TF 5M Exit:opposite divergence TF 1M Re-entry:divergence on TF 1M Happy trading

--- 帖子 #17276 ---
The most important part of the TzPivotsD indcator is the "Tz" part.....the time shifting code that allows the "day TF" for the pivots calculations to be shifted in accordance with the time zone the user wants, instead of the time zone the user's platform server is located in. While the Tz code worked well most of the time, it failed miserably over X-Mas and New Years holidays when there are partial trading days, and gaps between trading day stops and starts. Caveman completely overhauled that Tz code so that it figures out every possible such situation and deals appropriately with it! That was a daunting task, which Caveman freely donated his time to accomplish in order that the indicator would be competant......in order to help others! Without time shiting code the TzPivotsD indicator would be no better than any other standard pivots indicator. Just more elaborate. And without Caveman the Tz code would not be the perfection it now is! My hat is off to Caveman!

--- 帖子 #17290 ---
Ah yes. I have a trading plan I haven't shared with the forum because it contains trade 'templates' that are not all strictly THV. That particular one is one of my favorites. The first coral bounce after the trend has changed is almost always good. (Of course it needs to be a trend, cant just be chop so you have to be able to recognize a trend) It's even better because usually you can see it take off right away. Even if it fails (goes in the opposite direction of the previous trend to start a new trend), it almost always comes back for a retest of that new trend so you can get out. (That's what I do. If it wasn't strong enough to take off from the bounce I get out when it comes back for the retest.) The odds of a bounce (on the 1m for example) are better when the trix histo (type 12 measuring the whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing, or you can see it in the MTF trix I modified to show a color histogram) on the 5m is in favor of the trade. My advice is to use two lots and set the second one to b/e because in a good trend you'll get a few more bounces and that s/l will never get hit.

--- 帖子 #17291 ---
Just use the THV T3 trix Cobra posted last June. You'll find it in the attachments. It's a lot easier to work with because it has fewer external variables so you can actually use iCustom to call it with the values that you want. All the other variations of the trix have so much code and so many external variables that I've never succeeded in calling them with anything other than the defaults. Here is an example trxfastcurr = iCustom(NULL, prd, "THV T3 Trix",TrixNumberOfBars, A_t3_period, B_t3_period_ac,hot, MODE_MAIN, yy); trxslowcurr =iCustom(NULL, prd, "THV T3 Trix", TrixNumberOfBars, A_t3_period, B_t3_period_ac,hot, MODE_SIGNAL, yy); Either modify the code from Cobra's post to accept hot, or use the exe file I posted with the Swiss Army Histo here http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=17159 For hot, 0.7 is the old trix and 1.2 is the newer trix.

--- 帖子 #17297 ---
I"m NOT making trade recommendations on this. I was replying that I have (I thought) a similar strategy as one of my trade templates in my trading plan (that I haven't shared because it's not all THV). At least I think it's similar - maybe I didn't understand what he's doing. What I do is when there is a trend change, if there is a pull back to the coral I trade a bounce off it in the same direction as the trend change if it meets my criteria. I look for the first one of these after a good trend change (which I define as the rainbow flipping with 3 higher highs or lower lows while all the colors are visible), and I look for the spread between the fast and slow trix on the 5m tf to be moving in the direction of the trade. On the first lot I take 10 and then I move the stop on the second to B/e because a lot of times that first retest is never hit again until the trend flips back, which can be a good long way. Here's an example of what I mean by one today ( although I didn't take it - I couldn't get any trades in today there was so much news.) Attached Image (click to enlarge) If the spread of the 5m is also in the direction of the trade it usually works. If it doesn't work, then you probably are in for chopiness, and if the rainbow has flipped again against the trade, price will probably come back to retest the coral again so you can get out (barring major news shocks of course that's why you need a stop anyway.) Here is an example of a first coral retest after a trend change that you wouldn't want to take Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #17315 ---
Hi Emp, Generally speaking trades close to the coral in line with the longer term trend are better than trades farther from the coral. If it were me, I'd replace the cloud with the spread on the 5m trix (type 12 on the SwissArmy Histo.) You might try just adding an additonal histo and comparing the trades suggested by that one and the one you are using. The reason is that I think you will find that 90% of the time when price breaks the coral in the direction of the longer tf trend for this trade type, it also has already broken the cloud. So you can do without the cloud in this instance. In addition I think you will notice that if you take the ones where both the 15 m f trix and the 5m trix spread are in favor of the trade it will go against you less often.

Further edit: I've been thinking a lot about how I see the market lately, and I've kind of got the idea in my head that the path to positive expectancy is to build a case behind each and every trade that you take. That is to say, it's best if you can give a number of reasons for and against taking any one trade, and on the balance of these decide whether the positives outweigh the negatives. In this vein, I think higher time-frame analysis has the potential to help greatly when you are scalping, as the more factors you look for, the more aware you are of what the market is reacting to. By this I mean that there are hundreds of thousands of traders out there. They are all watching different things, different time-frames and so on. What you want to do is have as many of these traders as possible on-side. You don't want to enter into a trade and realise that you're trading straight into a significant fib retrace or T/L on the monthly, daily or hourly charts. In the case where these higher time frame S&amp;R lines agree with your pivots and 1M &amp; 5M T/L's you've got good confluence and can look for potential trade setups. See this post http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=15374 or use the THVHELPY1 that I posted. Just change the MA period to 180 on any of those indies. (The idea is that on the base tf chart the MA is 60. So you divide the higher tf period by the lower and multiply the result by 60. For example to go from 1 m to 5m on the 1m chart it's 5*60 =300. To go from the 5m to the 15 on the 5 m chart it's 3*60=180 for the MA period.

Notice the first red line in the attached screen shot. Notice how right after it, you have a trix cross up and everything looks set for a long trade. Both the fast and slow trix on the 1m , 5m and 15m tfs are green, price is above coral - go long right?. The 15m fast and slow trix are still green, so you might think that the longer tf trend is up. But the histogram on the 15m has already turned red, giving you an early warning. Type 12 just incoroporates this into the MTF SwissArmyhisto, because that one updates in real time. Unfortunately the MTF histo that actually draws on the chart sometimes fails to update unless you click on it, so you need the Swiss Army histo to tell you when the one that actually shows the trix is out of sync.

--- 帖子 #17341 ---
Here is my latest rainbow template. I replaced the MAs which were only approximate with the T3 5m and T3 15 min indies that someone kindly shared. These replicate the higher tf corals more accurately on the 1m chart. I also redid the colors (this rainbow is named after Bemac because he was the first one to think of using variable MAs - brilliant idea but the original color scheme was really ugly), and I changed some of the lower MAs to be more like the Guppy MAs so you can see the turn better. The dark gold is like the fast guppy and the green between the blue lines is like the slow guppy. The light gold is like the distance between the fast and slow guppies( so you can gauge how it is behaving). This is approximate because these MAs are not exactly like the guppies, but I find this setup as useful as the guppies, maybe even more so because of how the VarMAs behave. About the entries on that post - yes, that was not coincidental. Those were the 6 point entries. If you take the 6 point entries, you are getting in when the 1m fast trix and the 5m fast trix have just changed color. You will usually get good trend entries if you also take only the 6 point entries that - are in line with the Rainbow direction (i.e green entries when rainbow is going up, red when it is going down). - are the first one or two waves of the 1m fast trix after the 5m fast trix has just changed color -have a nice indentation of the rainbow (retrace) with reasonably moderate price bars forming a nice arch or double arches at that point. - are free of divergence on the previous peak or forming divergence If I want to do countertrend divergence trades I also look at the state of the rainbow. That is, I will only do these trades when the rainbow is either choppy or near the end of the daily range or a major support resistance AND also is very over extended. The conclusion I have come to is that contrary to how it feels when you are doing it, you are really safest trading at the extremes. That is, you are safest trading when the rainbow has compacted and is just coming out of an arch, as long as you are trading in the direction of the trend and catching a new wave. Or you are the safest trading when there is a divergence and the rainbow has been extremely overextended, and is starting to contract away from whatever support or resistence caused the divergence. This is a lot tricker though because you have to be careful not to do this in a strong trend. You always know how far the rainbow can contract (that is it can contract right back to the middle and even if you misjudged and price overshoots and the rainbow flips as though to start a trend on the other side when it gets that compressed it will usually chop around and touch the middle again at least once before it takes off so you can get out) but you never know how far it can extend. As tempting as it is to call the bottom, you can be right only once, and wrong with each new wave down. Whereas if you are trading price coming out of a contraction of a wave in the direction of the trend you can be right many times (with each new higher or lower wave) and wrong only once. Therefore to trade countertrend you need a good reason. About fibs, I know that the fib on the last swing down on the weekly works really well so far. About the daily ones what I do is put a likely looking one on my chart and then I watch to see what happens. If it provides support resistance for a few tests and retest then I know I got it right (saw what the majority did) and I can use it for the future (until it wears out of course). I've posted two that seem to be working well now in my recent posts.

--- 帖子 #17352 ---
I use a few strategies with the rainbow- 1) Either regular Thv cross or 6 point trend entries in the direction of the rainbow after the rainbow flips and price makes 3 higher highs or lower lows to establish a trend. After the flip and the 3 higher highs or lower lows I take the next THV cross or 6 lights trade, as long as there is 10 pips of room for the trade to move before it hits a pivot or something I know is a strong resistance. That's described in these posts: 11913, 11943, 12041,12466,12445, 12467,12469,12478,12515,12613. Those are the safest in my opinion and also very easy to monitor because you get lots of warning when one is coming. When I am feeling lazy (like most of the summer) these are the only trades I do. 2) 6 lights entries as described in the manual on page 1, except that I now limit them to either trend entries only in the same direction as the rainbow (i.e a don't take a 6 point short when the rainbow is up unless its a divergence trade) or to taking divergence trades when the rainbow looks choppy or over extended. I do fewer of these because they are riskier, so I wait until I see price bouncing off something that has a good record of working, or until I see around 4 divergences in a row on the 1m tf or a divergence on the 1m tf and also a divergence on a higher tf. These 6 point trades (both types - trend and divergence) require you to pay a LOT of attention to what you are doing because you always have to be aware of divergence and potential divergence, and whether the market is in a strong trend ( and if so, where you are in the trend), a counter trend ( i.e a trend but one that is part of a retracement of the major trend) or just chopping around. I tend to do more of these in the winter and early spring, when I find it easier to concentrate. [quote=cigarguy;3394831]

It's fine, just remember to start cutting back your risk as you increase your account capital. Even when trading live, the emotion of trading a $100 account is nowhere near the same as trading a $10,000 account, even if you already pretend to see it that way when you're on a $100 account. Looking at a -$60 to -$80 negative in one trade is not the same feeling as seeing a -$6000 to -$8000 in negative in one trade lol. Trust me, I've seen a -$6000 floating in my dumb days on live, and it's not fun. I still think you should lower your total risk capital to not any larger than 5% no matter the account size. My max risk capital at any given time is only 3.5%. On a single position, my total market exposure is only 1.5% - 2% risk. Just remember, baby steps will lead to great length, while trying to take large giant steps will only get you tripped in the end. My account can sustain 66 losing trades in a roll before hitting margin call, while yours, not even 2, think about it, which account will have a better chance at surviving in this market?

--- 帖子 #17427 ---
Using windows explorer, browse to your MT4 directory, right click on it, and click properties. Look at the total size for the folder. If it's larger than 500MB then you might have some very large log files sitting in there. Even 500MB would be a bit large, although you could have a lot of tick history in there. You could then browse into the logs folder of your MT4 directory and delete the log files. The other folders in there to check are under experts, then logs, and also tester then logs.

--- 帖子 #17508 ---
No. If I'm trading with the trend I will want the fast trix to go red on both 1min and 5 min but not necessarily to cross. IC. Ichimoku Cloud Histo kind regards of Miss Pips. She has a new version 3.1.3 I believe. However you can get it from the Swissarmyknife too. Ichimoku Kinko Hyo is a technical indicator published over 30 years ago in Japan. It measures market momentum and trend and also outlines levels of support and resistance. Ichimoku means 'one look' in Japanese and this reflects the indicator’s intent to measure multiple aspects of the market at once. I only use the “kumo” or cloud part of this indicator. My mentor was very keen on this. The kumo is the very heart and soul of the Ichimoku Kinko Hyo charting system. Perhaps the most immediately visible component of Ichimoku, the kumo ("cloud" in Japanese) enables me to immediately identify the prevailing trend and price's relationship to that trend. The Ichimoku cloud (IC) gives us the decision on which direction to trade; above the cloud only long, below only short. A break through the cloud and a subsequent move above or below it will suggest a better and more probable trade. The MTF version is used which shows us the status of the IC on multiple timeframes. On the diagram below the IC is shown as a dark cloud almost like a 3-D ribbon. Instead of cluttering the chart with this cloud the MTF version is used at the bottom of the chart. The lights turn green when price has moved up through the cloud. They show yellow when the price is inside the cloud and the lights turn red when the price falls through the cloud. This gives us an instant visual, a “one look” if you like as to where price is in relation to the IC. Credit has to be given to Miss Pips from the THV forum on Forex Factory. She has done a fantastic job of making the MTF indicator which translates the IC ribbon into lights for ease of use and clarity. She makes this indicator freely available. Well done to her! My mentor was totally impressed when he saw it. On the 1 min chart I have the 1min and 5 min IC histos and both must be green/red for a long/short. (except divergence when only 1 min IC histo light needed.) On the 5 min chart I have the 5 min and 15 min histos. 5 min light in direction of a trade is a must and 15 min is a bonus showing trend. Ichimoku Cloud is important in my trading. Hope that makes sense.

--- 帖子 #17511 ---
You should be looking at next higher TF to confirm your trade, not lower TF. When someone saw something on M5 and goes to M1, that mostly means they found a confirmation on M5 to enter a trade soon, then goes to M1 to find best entrance, usually earlier than what you would have got if entered on M5. If we're entering trades on M1, we look at M5 or to some, even M15 or higher for confirmation, when we enter on M5, we look to the M15 for confirmation or higher, and so on.

If you are using the SwissArmy histo, set it to alert you when just the first row changes color. (Set EnableAlerts to true, Popup Alertrs to true , maxscore to 1 and CountE1 to true, the rest of the CountEx to false) Then when wait to see if you get an alarm when the color changes. If it is late check the experts tab to see when it was recorded as triggering. If it is recorded in the experts tab as triggering at the same time as you see on screen but you don't get an alert then my guess is your MT4 is overloaded. Try it with only one chart open to test this. In the example I am posting you can see that my alarm is triggering when the first two rows change color, and you can see the Experts tab recording the time (one minute after the change because the alarm sounds at the open of the next bar.

--- 帖子 #17591 ---
Re the trix, the old versions could repaint one closed bar back. I've posted several posts about this explaining under what conditions this occurs - you will find them in the thread. Regarding the newest version of the trix I don't know. I don't use it, but Cobra did mention that Statman had improved the code. I don't know what the improvements covered though. Re the signal you want, no not really. The histo is limited to 4 rows so you can get the fast and slow trixes for two timeframes. You can also use type 4. THe code for type 4 is trxfastcurr &lt; trxslowcurr &amp;&amp; trxfastcurr &lt; trxfastprev That is fast trix below slow and fast trix red or trxfastcurr &gt;trxslowcurr &amp;&amp; trxfastcurr &gt; trxfastprev That is fast trix above slow and fast trix green. However that is not the same as both trixes being the same color in every case -though in most cases it is. You might try checking over in the EA thread - maybe it can do it.

--- 帖子 #17604 ---
Tradewell wrote a very nice manual explaining the 6 lights method, which you can find in the zip file on the first page. Regarding the rainbow, there is lots of information on FF - all you have to do is search 'rainbow' or LinnuxTroll. I do not trade the rainbow per say however (that is a whole different system). I just use it as a longer term trend filter in addition to the Coral. For example if there is a THV signal saying to go short (6 lights, thv cross, PA below cloud and coral etc,), but the rainbow is pointing up then I don't take that signal unless it is a divergence signal and meets some other criteria. For me it is easier to 'see' which way the trend is going (up, down or sideways) using the rainbow rather than the coral. (Some people can do this with no indicators - just looking at PA but I like the rainbow because it is more graphically easy to understand.)

Trade Example 5 EUR/USD 1. PA been in short-term uptrend for more than a day. Heads up on 5 min chart (below) when the 5 min IC Histo turns green at 0825 hrs GMT. 2. Price is above the 20 sma on the 5 min chart and above the Coral. The 20 sma is also above the Coral which is good for a long trade. 3. SS agreement. (See 5 min chart below then turn to 1 min chart) 4. Looking at the 1 min chart (below) price moves above the Coral at 0829hrs and both top IC histo lights are green. 5. Both the 1 min fast and slow Trix have crossed each other and both are green. (Also fast trix crossed Zero line) 6. 1 min fast Trix not overbought. 7. 5 min fast Trix is green which is good for long trade. 8. Back to the 5 min chart, the price is still above the 20 sma and there is stochastic agreement. Both IC histos on 5 min chart are now green which is good. 9. Wait for the price to break the 1.3980 Sweet Spot. There are more than 10 pips to resistance so the trade is taken long at 1.3982. 10. A Stop Loss is placed below the Swing Low at 1.3969 (total 13 pips which is good). 11. A limit order is placed at the 1.4000 Sweet Spot to exit the trade. Please note if you are purely scalping for 10 pips then you’d exit at 10 pips profit. You could also exit at 1.4000 and the other Sweet Spot of 1.4020 if you have two lots to trade.

--- 帖子 #17650 ---
You cannot change broker time settings. There are two indicators that maybe you have confused, the PivotsD indy and the TzPivotsD indy. The TzPivotsD indy allows you to change the time zone that the pivots are calculated by ("Tz" stands for "time zone shift"). With the TzPivotsD indy, the broker time settings (your broker server time as shown at bottom of all charts) are not what is changed. What is changed is the time zone.....from that which the broker server is in, to some other you select.....for the purpose of computing the pivots. I hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #17664 ---
Let's not be so hasty there. That was a good 6 point trade. If you run a fib from the top of the double high from April to June 2008 to the bottom of the double bottom fromed from Nov 2008 to Feb 2009, you will see that the 38 level is right there where price got stuck and bounced down. Not coincidently, there was divergence there on the 1m and divergence forming as a result on the 15 m. In addtion that was the daily open line (at least on my broker) which often causes a bounce. So we had 6 points, bouncing off somthing sturdy (the open is pretty sturdy and that fib is also). If you knew that fib was there - great. If you didnt divergence would tell you about it. Also , if you look at the rainbow, you see it has this kind of overextended bubblehead look to it - it 'looks right' for a short. I don't usually post those kind of trades because I don't think it's a good idea to encourage relative newbies to trade against the trend, and I haven't found a good way to describe the 'bubblehead' look. (The closest description is the 6 points divergence trade, but the rainbow makes it easier to see. ) But its a legit trade in the sense that it's a probable one if you can recognize it. Like Cigarguy said, if you work with one currency, and especially with the rainbow which makes things easier, you get to where you just recognize good situations - even without counting the points. After all that is how I came up with the 6 points method to begin with. First I began to notice probable good trade situations and THEN I quantified them (and by the way it's possible that there are better ways to quantify them). I hope this isnt too confusing but what I'm saying is that first I traded so much that I began to intuitively recognize the probable situations, and then I came up with a method that quantified it - not vice versa. I assigned the points and the rules to make them fit what I was observing. In Cigarguy's case he just doesn't need to count the 6 points because he already recognizes those situtions - probably the same way - by trading so much it just becomes intuitive.

--- 帖子 #17733 ---
All alarms you have set to true must be met for an alert to be given. You only get one alert when all conditions are met that are orange, regardless of which Time frame. So if you have the following selected you will only get one alert when they are all met. M1 Coral, M1Cloud, M1F-trix, M5S-trix, M30Coral, M60Cloud, LagRSI. All of these would have to pass and all would have to be Green or all Red, then you would get one alert, all red for short and all green for long. You can't get an alert for each one, it is a LOGIC AND function. The new release of TzPivotsMW brings better alignment matching of pivot labels with those of the TzPivotsD indicator, for the variety of line placement settings. The new release of TzPivotsD involves a number of improvements. You will have the option to NOT display the labels for mid-pivots, and for the yHigh/yLow lines, even though the rest are displayed (see attached chart differences). You can uncheck OHLC in Chart Properties and have the Data Panel move up and automatically display the pair ID and TF for a neater chart (see difference in chart examples). For neater alignment of negative and positive numbers in the Data Panel, there is now a control to left shift negative numbers (swaps and Tz numbers could be negative). And if you have selected to show the Data Panel, it will now remain on the higher TF charts even though the pivots have been set to not display.

--- 帖子 #17746 ---
You only get one alert when all conditions are met that you have set to true. The coral will be green or red as long as the price is above or below it. If the price happens to be the same a the price it may be yellow untill it goes above or below. When using the MAs, if for example you use the default of 20, 60, 200. To get a green light the 20 must be above the 60 which must be above the 200. You don't get the alert on just the cross, but when they are all in alignment. For red the 20&lt;60&lt;200. If you use 2 then it would be 20&gt;60 for green and 20&lt;60 for red. If you use 1 then it would be PA&gt;20 for green and PA&lt;20 for red. It works the same as the coral if only using one MA. The cloud works the same, your either above it or below it. The X-Trix, which is the trix cross does not trigger only on the cross but shows that the trix may have crossed in the past and still has the same configuration. So if the fast trix crossed up through the slow trix 8 bars ago it will stay green until the fast trix crosses back down through the slow trix and then it will change to red until it crosses back up again. I was just looking at the code and noticed that the coral and cloud bar colors may get hung on either Green or Red, this doesn't affect the alert but may be confusing so I fixed it in the code, here is the update. Attached File(s) Alert.zip 93 KB | 514 downloads

Hi Novice198, 1. CaveManager will not overwrite your SL and TP if you have set them when you open the trade position. It will only modify the order if either SL or TP is zero. 2. CaveManager will close positions based on what you have configured it to do. 3. I don't quite understand your question. CaveManager will always take the latest settings. If you change it while it is managing a trade, it will take the new settings to manage the trade once you save the new settings. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #17822 ---
Not sure which flavor of THV you are trying to trade. If you are trying to trade the 6 lights version, there is a manual that explains it on the first page. It was tested for the 1m tf not the 5m tf and has its own rules, explained in the manual. The other rules of THV do not apply (except that the price has to be above/below the candle and clould for a long/short respectively, and above/below the cloud only for a long/short divergence trade, respectively. I.e you don't need to wait for a trix cross or for the 1m slow when using the 6 point method.) Please note that the second histogram that comes with the V4 template does not have the correct settings. The correct settings for the second histo for trading the 1m tf are 15 m s 30 m f 30 m s 60 m f Also not sure which you mean by the bottom histo since I dont use the V4 template, but it sounds like the clould histo. For that to work you need the Ichimoku indicator ( found in the thread) in your indies folder as well.

--- 帖子 #17849 ---
To get the correct settings for the second histo change the eperiod and the ePeriodType (0=slow,1=fast) Attached Image I don't use the standard thv template. I posted the template I use and the indies it needs in this post: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=17341 I don't use v4 because I don't like the black background and the stuff on the side that the new trix has. Also Stratman's mini charts in the V4 template slow my MT4 down. V4 and V3 are the same really - just some cosmetic changes to the templates - so you can use either one. Consistent results depend on the trader, not the template. I do use the 6 lights, but I have two modifications: 1) I only take trend trades in the direction of the rainbow (see my template) 2) For divergence trades I prefer that the spread (ePeriodtype 12 on the SwissArmyhisto) between the two 5m trix lines is in the direction of the trade (i.e red for shorts, green for longs). I also don't use Stratman's dashboard. I do not trade based on fractal breaks as he does, but rather on buying the dip/selling the top (retracements or Ross Hooks) after a fractal has been made, as soon as momentum returns to the direction of the trend. (That is what you are doing when you use the 1m f and 5m f trix as your signal in the direction that you have 6 points.)

--- 帖子 #17859 ---
When you select the MissPips option and set it to true it uses the correct alerts in an "AND/OR" logic. If you set any others to true they will be used along with the MissPips and be "ANDED" to MissPips. So if you want to do Only the MissPips 6 lights then leave all the THV settings to false. If you set "ShowInacAlarms" to false and select MissPips only the alerts for MissPips will be displayed on the upper right of the chart. Good Luck

--- 帖子 #17863 ---
Attached are TzPivotsMW_v3.5 and TzPivotsD_v3.5 and the summary of changes is as follows: TzPivotsMW_v3.5 - 1) In forex mode you can now display either the 4 or 5 digit format. If your platform is 4 digit and you choose the 5 digit format, a "0" is added to the displayed numbers. If your platform is 5 digit and you choose the 4 digit format, numbers are rounded off to 4 digits. This is was the only format previously available. Now you can display 5 digits on a 5 digit platform. 2) You now have the option to not display the line label for each catagory of pivot lines. Under certain conditions, not showing certain labels makes for a cleaner chart, but still totally comprehensible. 3) The label code for the various line placement options is modified so that the labels should now align exactly with the TzPivotsD_v3.5 labels for the same line placements. 4) The External Inputs Window is re-arranged. TzPivotsD_v3.5 - 1) Same as "1)" above. 2) Same as "2)" above. 3) The unused Scroller feature is removed. 4) The Relabeler feature is changed to hard code and it's Comment panel is removed. 5) Five new features are added to the Data Panel. One- Choose to not display the chart OHLC info in the upper left of the chart, and have the Data Panel display the pair ID and TF for you. This makes for a cleaner chart. Two- Negative numbers (swap numbers) are shifted to maintain proper alignment. Three- If your platform is 5 digit and you identify it as such in the Data Panel settings, then the range and spread information will appear normal/ same as on a 4 digit platform. Four- You can separately select to display the spread in 5 digits. Five- You have the option to display the time to the next candle, or not display it. Six- Even if there are higher TF charts on which the indicator has been set to not display the pivots, if the Data Panel is selected then it will appear on those higher TF charts. 6) The External Inputs Window is re-arranged. Two charts are attached. The first demonstrates the chart OHLC information in upper right above the TzPivotsD Data Panel, and all pivot lines shown have their labels. The second chart demonstrates no OHLC, and the mid-pivot lines are without labels. The second chart is just as comprehensible as the first, but less cluttered. A note about OHLC. This is selected/de-selected in Chart Properties. To remove it, you must do so yourself by unchecking it in Chart Properties. Then, if you input in the Data Panel settings that the OHLC is not shown, the Data Panel will automatically shift up and show the Pair ID and TF for you. A note about 5 digits. Some brokers already have 5 digit MT4 platforms, though some are "beta" for the time being. But MetaQuotes is going to release MT5, eventually, and maybe this summer I am told. One purpose of the 5 digit platform is that it allows brokers to be "more competititve" with spreads . So, maybe that means eventually they will all be offering it. Some indicators may have to be "altered" to work on MT5. Currently, I do not know how the TzPivots may be affected. But the addition of the 5 digit option allows those of you already using 5 digit MT4 platforms to display pivots in the 5 digit mode now, if you want to. I encourage you to read thru the notes in the compile of the TzPivotsD_v3.5 indicator. The explanation of each input has been reworked.

--- 帖子 #17894 ---
You're welcome. Actually neither one is correct because I see at the far left side of the chart you have another one. I don't advise taking every one of these that you see because you only get so many per trend. You are looking for one as close as possible to the point where the rainbow flipped over and below the coral and then price comes back to retest it. You may get more than one of these per trend but the most probable one is the first one after the flip that meets the conditions. I do wait for a bar to close below the coral on these, or at least I wait until the minute is almost up and I see that the bar won't be able to retrace enough to make it close above the coral. You don't need to wait for 3 hh s or lls for this trade, just for the rainbow to flip and for price to retest the coral while the 5m histo spread and 1m f are in favor of the trade.

--- 帖子 #17972 ---
I agree with what someone else said, but as someone for a long time who has had a quota to achieve of my own... 1. Break your pip goal (think of it as a goal not a do or die level... a goal!) into days, ie you are close enough to just call it 20 pips per day. 2. Break your goal in half and work on consistently getting 10 pips per day. When you go way over, not over trading, stop and let the pips build in your acct. Train yourself at that level, even for penny trades, just train yourself for the actions there. 3. When you can meet 10 pips per day consistently, day after day... slowly reach to 15, then 20 as your daily goal. A, for before any of the above... figure out what time frame you see and live with the best, totally on demo. Some find themselves great on the 5 or 1 but absolutely get killed on the 1 hr because they can't take the wiggle needed for many trades...some can handle that much better than being in a trade for a few minutes at a time and moving on. Figure out what is your personality really, then start at 1. Brian

--- 帖子 #17974 ---
The trix you need is in the zip file, it is "THV4 Trix called", you need this one in your indicator folder or the alerts will not work as the code calls this indicator for its values for trix, thats also the one thats on the template. It may be a little different from some of the later versions of the trix but it is close enough. In the examples I showed I only used the M15 chart, I did not look at the M5 or M1 for the entry. When I got the M15 alert I just looked at P/S/R points. You could add the M1 or M5 alerts if you want to the present M15 ones, let us know if you do and if its better. Some traders do use the next lower time frame for their entry. Example Long Alert M15: All GREEN If Bid&gt;R1 but Ask&lt;R2 I look to see how much room there is left to move before I hit R2. If I want 10 pips of TP, can I get it before I reach R2? If the answer is yes I take the trade. I also make sure I am not close to yesterdays high or low, I use those values the same as I just used R1 and R2, if I am above yesterdays low will I hit YH before I get my 10 pips. Also I make sure there is no news, actually that should be first along with am I within my trading hours. Depending where the PA is I look at R5 - P - S5 and if it is outside of either R5 or S5 I don't take it. Also look at the Range to see how it compares to yesterdays range, if it has already moved a lot there may be nothing left in this direction but maybe a pull back when and if it signals a short. Also if it is very early in the session and the range is very small you may want to wait until it is 40 -50 pips. Everyone has there own way of picking a good trade, find a time frame you are comfortable with and a few pairs and work with them. The alert is only to get you started, it doesn't mean its a good trade. If you find something that is consistant for you please post it. I probably said a lot of what you already know but it may help others. I learn something new every day. Good Luck Edit: Sorry for the error, I just noticed I had THV3 Trix Called on the template and I am using THV4 Trix Called in the Alert, please change the template to THV4 Trix called so they match. THV4 Trix called is the one thats in the zip folder. Another slip up, thanks for the heads up.

--- 帖子 #17998 ---
Novice198, I am not too sure what you are asking. Thus, I have extracted what is in the manual for you here. Can't explain it any better than what is written in the manual. UseTrailPriceByPercentage This option was added based on the idea from Bemac of Forex Factory. It allows trailing behind price by a percentage of floating profit ( PercentageTrailBehindPrice ) after accumulating a minimum amount of pips ( MinPipsToActivate ). It is a more advance form of trailing stop. Use_Preceding_TP This option is used together with trailing stops to move Target Profit (TP) to precede price. What it means is that your TP is constantly adjusted to be ahead of the price by the number of pips you set together with your trailing stop adjustments making trailing stops and preceding target work in tandem. The advantage this has over a standard static TP is that if market moves and your trailing stop start trailing price, it will eventually hit your standard static TP limiting your profit. Imagine as market moves, your SL and TP are both moving and shifting with price. This will maximize your profit for major market moves. ** Never use the default settings that came with the EA. It was used in testing only. ** Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #18037 ---
Indicators don't lag, they only tell us what happened not what will happen in the TF we use 'em. They can be used as a repitition law, PA does that when it did this before in x % of the time. What lags is the market which changes his mind every one and ever.

--- 帖子 #18038 ---
Hell yes, indicators lag! They are based on past prices. And whatever they are designed to tell us, based on those past prices, by the time we get the "message" those past prices are over and done with.....a new bar has arrived! And, like you said, this new bar might reflect the market having changed its mind.....off in the OTHER direction, and trashing all those indicator "messages" in the process! But. we all use them, even if it is just the Price, S&amp;R, and something else thrown into the mix. Like you discerned, they create pictures, maybe making it easier for our minds to relate. And we learn what individual picture to look for, because that is the one with the highest historical record of being followed by what we are looking for.

--- 帖子 #18042 ---
It is possible to get MTF simulation working using the Vhands Trading Simulator. Here is how to do it: 1. Install and get familiar with Vhands Trading Simulator. You can follow the posts on how to get started by Blueruby on the Vhands Trading Simulator thread and you should be up and running in about 10 minutes. Or follow the instructions in vTerminal.pdf. Vhands Trading Simulator thread http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=60849 Posts by blueruby on how to use the simulator http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...04&amp;postcount=1 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...11&amp;postcount=2 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...15&amp;postcount=3 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...25&amp;postcount=4 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...44&amp;postcount=6 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...91&amp;postcount=8 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...4&amp;postcount=15 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...4&amp;postcount=16 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...0&amp;postcount=28 2. Install and setup the MTF vhandstrade version. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...&amp;postcount=233 This version Vhands Trading Simulator uses offline charts to run simulations in multiple time frames. After you have installed and setup MTFvhands you should be able to run simulations in multiple time frames in separate charts. However most MTF indicators will not work. As non-standard time frames are being used, most MTF indicators have to be modified to support them. 3. Modify MTF indicators to work with non-standard time frames and to update correctly: Since most of the source code for the THV system is not available, you are on your own here. Maybe the proprietors of the code will be kind enough to release versions that work in simulation mode. Here is what needs to be done: We will be working with offline charts with the following designations: (Time Frame -&gt; Chart Name) M1 -&gt; M2, M5 -&gt; M6, M15-&gt;M16, M30-&gt;M31, H1-&gt;M61, H4-&gt;M240 and so on. Depending on the indicator some or all of the following modifications will be needed: a. Allow the indicator to accept the non-standard time frames: Update the ValidateTimeFrame function to include the offline . ++ denotes added line: int validateInput(int iPeriod) { bool bReturnValue = FALSE; switch (iPeriod) { case 1: bReturnValue = TRUE; break; ++ case 2: bReturnValue = TRUE; break; case 5: bReturnValue = TRUE; break; ++ case 6: bReturnValue = TRUE; break; case 15: bReturnValue = TRUE; break; ++ case 16: bReturnValue = TRUE; break; . . . etc b. Add the non-standard time frames to the Time Frame to String conversion function. ++ denotes added line: string tf2txt(int iPeriod) { string sPeriod = "unknown"; if (iPeriod == PERIOD_M1) sPeriod = "M1"; ++ if (iPeriod == 2) sPeriod = "M2"; if (iPeriod == PERIOD_M5) sPeriod = "M5"; ++ if (iPeriod == 6) sPeriod = "M6"; . . . etc c. Modify the number of bars updated/repainted when the indicator is called. I have almost no experience programming in mql so this is a quick hack and is not perfect, but it does the job. Maybe someone more experienced has a better solution. It seems some of the indicators do not update enough bars for the higher time frames so we will have to force it to do so. int start() { . . . iCountedBars = IndicatorCounted(); ++ i = Bars - iCountedBars; ++ if (i&lt;2) i = 10; . . . To run a simulation for the MTF Trix method in its simplest form, you will need two MTF indicators: THV4 MTF Cloud THV4 MTF Trix THV4 MTF Cloud actually works but cannot update the non-standard text labels. The tf2str function needs to be updated. THV4 MTF Trix does not work. One needs to modify the validateInput, tf2str and start (bar update/redraw) functions in this case Cheers!

We as a trader need a reason to enter or exit a trade. That is what systems are for, together with experience and MM they make a method. Most use indicators for building a system, others PA, Fibs or pivots. Best is a mix, but the rule is: less is more. A cluttered template will give an overload of info and it'll take too long to take a scalping decision. My setup is always the same: basic THV in 4 TF, 4H heatmap with horizontal S&amp;R levels and a candlestick 15M template for TLs, Fibs and Pivots. The rest is feeling, good MM and a portion of luck. Boring, isn't it?

That indie is just a series of calls to the trix itself and then tests to see if the previous value for signal line or trix line is greater than or less than the current one. You are better off just calling the trix with icustom rather than the histogram - it will be a lot simpler. You can find examples of how to call the trix and and test the values in the THV T3 Trix MTFv1.5w..mq4 code posted in the thread.

--- 帖子 #18119 ---
The basic THV is based on the idea that we want to grab pips out of the middle of a trend by buying dips in a uptrend and selling rallies in a downtrend. Here are some helpful basic rules: How do we know whether the trend is up or down? Rule 1: Trend is up when price is above the coral and down when it is below it. Rule 2: In an uptrend we buy dips, in a downtrend we sell tops After we have determined the direction of the trend, how do we know when to buy a dip or sell a rally? 2a. We buy a dip in an uptrend when the fast trix has crossed back up above the slow trix and price is above the Ichimoku , indicating that momentum has resumed in the direction of the uptrend 2.b We sell a top when fast trix has crossed below the slow trix and price is below the Ichimoku , indicating that momentum has resumed in the direction of the downtrend. Best trix crosses are near zero and when both trixes are the same color as the trade. Reason: When the trix crosses near zero and price has crossed but is still near the coral, the trade has room to move Some people like to wait until the fast trix has crossed zero in the direction of the trade, but that is optional. It is also best to trade in the direction of the trend on the next higher timeframe, or alternately to go one timeframe lower to look for a good entry. That is, if you are trading the 5m chart (top down) and you get a signal, check the one minute chart to make sure the 1m is not way ovebought/oversold when you enter. Alternately, trading bottom up , it is best to trade when higher timeframe agrees with the direction of the trade. For example if you get a signal on the 1m chart, it is best if it is in the direction of the 5m trend. How do we know when not to trade or not trade? Rule 3: Do not trade against trendlines, pivots, support/resistance or divergence. We need to watch out for trendlines, pivots and major support and resistance, and not buy or sell right on top of any of these. Instead we should wait for a break, or even better a break and retest. Reason: We are trying to grab pips out of the middle of a trend and any of these can spell the end of the trend. So we don't want to be too near them when we trade (too near meaning that we dont have enough room to hit our target before hitting one of these potential obstacles.) For example, if you are about to take long trade, and the daily pivot is 3 pips above your entry, better to wait and see if you get a break first. We should also watch out for divergences, and not trade against them. Rule 4: Trading times: Trade when there is enough volatility but not during news It is best to trade when there is enough volatility to get pips - which you can measure by which sessions are open and by the ATR (above 10 is better). However it is best not to trade just before or after news. Rule 5: Use Good Money Management: Set stops and do not risk too much of your account. Stops and targets: Either use the THV ATR suggestion or use 15 pip stop 10 pip target (that's my personal suggestion for the Euro, plus spread for each of them. For other currencies that may differ. You can try 10 times the spread for the stop ). Or you can put the stop below/above the previous swing low/high, and trail it Risk: Don't risk more than between 1 to 5 % of your account on any one trade. One percent is conservative, 5% is cowboy style. 1.5 or 2% is pretty average. The rest is what people have customized according to whatever indicators they favor, mostly in order to make sure that they are really taking a signal during a good trend and not a signal in a ranging market.

Here is the latest, I have added another piece that goes along with the TDI alert, this one uses the Heiken Ashi candles with the 5 SMMA channel as a buy/sell indicator that goes along with the TDI buy/sell. You get an HA buy when the candle closes above the chanel and a sell when the candle closes below the channel. You should use both the TDI and HA together. I have enclosed a template and set file for the M15 time frame. I am testing it using the following settings. M15: F-trix, S-trix, X-trix, Stochastics 8,3,3, TDI, HA You need the Heiken Ashi indicator in your indicator folder, there is one in the zip file if you don't have it. --- 帖子 #18150 ---
Here are a couple of indicators that will make it possible to run MTF simulations with MTFVhandsTrade. See this previous post for instruction on how to set it up: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost.php?p=3548477&amp;postcount=18042 The "THV4 Cloud MTF.ex4" works as is, however without labels. You have to switch off autotimeframe and set the periods to 6 and 16, or whatever you are using. A copy of " THV T3 Trix MTF.mq4 " from this forum has been modified to allow non-standard time frames. See attachment below. Here too you have to set the periods to 6, 16, 31 etc - whatever you are using - and leave autotimeframe set to false. An MTF Trix bar indicator has been made based off the " THV T3 Trix MTF.mq4 " indicator. You can enable/disable the Fast trix and the slow trix. Set the periods as required. 2fast, 6fast-6slow, etc. With these one can run a basic MTF simulation in vHandsTrade. The higher time-frame offline charts - M6, M16, M31, M61 - have to be open as the generate data for the MTF indicators on M2. Placing and managing trades is done on the strategy testers M1 chart. You have to let it run a bit to generate data for the higher timeframes.

--- 帖子 #18151 ---
Very impressive!. Personally I have a dual core so I havent wanted to mess with this. What I do is the following: I use T3 M5 and T3 M15 (posted in the thread) to get the 5 and 15 m corals on the m1 chart. Then I use T3 Trix MTf (posted in the thread) to get the 5 and 15 m mtf trix on the m1 chart The way I do this is by multiplying the A t3 period and B t3 period accordingly (i.e 100 and 175 for 5m and 300 and 525 for 15m). You also have to increase the number of bars counted and let it run for a while to get the data. I have also made a modified cloud histo that works on the m1 chart. None of these are exact, but really they are close enough.

The MTF cloud displays the status of the Ichimoku cloud on the higher timeframes, not the status of the Coral. If you want to see the higher tf corals on the 1m use the T3 M5, T3 M15 etc indies or use the SwissArmy Mixed histo ePeriodType =13.

THV is technically a trend-following system. However, it is highly recommended to have a separate chart with regular candles and pivots, to use in conjunction with the THV chart. This way you can use THV while analyzing PA at the same time. This brings up a good point: THV is a system which should be used only when a trader has studied and understood basic PA, candle patterns, fibs, pivots, etc. Also, keep in mind that even PA is lagging - your feed gives you a price that was already traded.

Hi traders Everyone must be on vacation spending their Forex winnings as the forum is rather quiet compared to what it used to be. Here are 2 trades I took today trying something a little different. I used the following alerts. M15: F-trix, S-trix, X-trix, Stochastics 8,3,3 offset 0, HA D1: HA This is a stripped down alert I am just experimenting with, you can't do both the M15 and D1 HAs with the regular alert I posted. You will need to eyeball the D1 chart to get the overall trend of the HA. The settings for the HA are 5 SMMA high and 5 SMMA low to create the channel. These 2 trades worked out rather well in a choppy market with no real long trend on the M15 chart. My stop loss was set at the highest price of the last 5 candles plus the spread. The take profit was set at 5 times the stop loss. This is quite a large TP target but I was using the 2 candles closing inside the channel as my exit. This exit also gets you out faster if the trade goes against you so you don't have to wait for the 5 bar back stop loss to be hit. Sometimes this is good other times its bad, but hopefully you will have more winners to offset this. It will be interesting to see how this strategy works when I get some of the real long M15 trends. You will also notice that you may have wanted to try for a long trade in between these 2 short trades, but the daily trend was telling you to go short. Also the overall M15 trend was down. Good Luck Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #18282 ---
You will need to change times in THV TRIX and daily/ monthly pivots Bring up a H1 chart, place your mouse on the last bar, that will be the opening time for that bar, most likely in GMT format 24 hour not 12 go to http://wwp.greenwichmeantime.com/ make sure you switch to 24 hour eg 7pm will be 19 Right mouse click on the chart and bring up indicators list or Ctrl + I Now for your pivots. You can set your HrsServer for me Alpari +2. However Hrs Choice for me is +1, I use London Now for THV Trix settings. You will have to game it because some people do daylight saving and others dont, then you have your server thingy in there as well For example in the winter your London times would be Open = 8 and close = 17 Big Ben is =0GMT winter and +1GMT summer New York is -5GMT winter and -4GMT summer Now that things are thoroughly confused there'll be a test at 11am, oops 15GMT

--- 帖子 #18283 ---
Also go here for this http://www.2010.worldmarkethours.com/Forex/index.htm And I like this because it shows "clock time" in your time zone http://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/ I have the following GMT's London 0900GMT (8am) to 1800GMT 8 to 5 New York 12GMT (8am) to 21GMT 8 to 5 Sydney 0000GMT (10am) to 1700GMT 10 to 5 Now for Tokyo because of GMT stuff 0000GMT to 1700GMT Should be 9 to 5 The last can't be right because that is the same as Sydney so I'll have to game it

That indie just uses iCustom to call the Ichimoku indie like this: Senkou_Span_A=iCustom(NULL,prd,"Ichimoku",MaPeriod1,MaPeriod2,MaPeriod3,5,yy) ; Senkou_Span_B=iCustom(NULL,prd,"Ichimoku",MaPeriod1,MaPeriod2,MaPeriod3,6,yy) Then just check where the price is in relation to Senkou_Span A and B. --- 帖子 #18321 ---
1) It is best if the Fast Trix is above the zero line and crossing down, this one was already below. The next short signal would have been better as it was above and crossed down through zero for a short signal. 2) SL is a matter of preference, I sometimes use the highest high of the last 5 bars if going short, others use a fixed 10 or 20 pips, its a gut feeling sometimes. Could also depend on where overhead resistance is located, round numbers etc. 3) TP, Look for your next support when going short. If you are just scalping on the short time frames play it safe and take 5 - 10 pips profit and get out. You need to look at the big picture and not just go with an alert. The alerts are there just to get you to take a look, the rest is up to you to decide on what to do. If the alerts worked everytime I would have made it into anEA and have been rich by now. But you must make the final decission as what to do. Good Luck

Here is a new version of the Swiss Army indie. See this post for all the indies you need in order for all the types to work and a description of the previous types. http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...74#post3375274 Note that if you get all red or all green rows for one of the types when you don't think that you should, then it probably means that you haven't downloaded one of the indicators that the SwissArmy indie needs to work with from the above post Changes from V4.11 are: For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not). Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Note that the hot parameter determines which trix is being used. 1.2 corresponds to the THV V4 trix, .75 to Trix 4.1 div. Edit: If you downloaded v 17 please redownload v18 - there was an error in the type labels.

Hello. 1. What is the signal criteria for MTF if price action has passed the coral line and retraces and lines up for a new trade in same direction and the Coral line is behind you from the past signal. Is it the light signals combined with Cloud or trix cross or maybe not covered in the system and you have to wait for a new coral cross? Attached Image (click to enlarge) 2. If you have to wait a candel or so passed coral line to get this setup it is still valid or does the light signal and the actual crossing happen in same candel? --- 帖子 #18416 ---
You need 1) 6 lights, two of which must be in the first two rows. 2) Price must be above the Coral and cloud for long, below them for short - except for divergence trades - in which case price only needs to be above/below the cloud. That's it for the original 6 lights method. I myself now add as an additional filter that I only take trades in the direction of the rainbow. You dont need to wait for a new trix cross or coral cross. The whole point of the 6 lights method is to let you take trades with the trend when the market is trending and you have missed the first coral cross or trix cross, but there is a good retracement as indicated by the six lights. Keep in mind however that the trend is your friend until it ends. So if this is the fourth or 5th 6 light signal since the trend flipped, and/or price is very far from the coral and/or price is past it's normal daily range, you'd probably do well to wait for a better setup. You are safest taking trades after a new trend has been established (123 reversal has occurred, price has crossed the coral, the rainbow flipped, the bottom histo has recently turned the color of the trade), price then retraces and compresses for a while near the coral, and then heads back in the direction of a relatively newly established trend. Another point to keep in mind is that since the trigger for a signal is the first two rows, and since the 1m f will usually change color a few times during a 5m trix cycle, you will get a few signals after the 5m fast trix changes color as the 1m fast trix cycles. The signals closer to the initial change in color of the 5m fast trix are usually better. A last point (and I bring this up because of the recent volatility on the Euro) is if you get a signal triggered by an abnormally large bar on the 1 m - say around 20 pips or more in a one min bar you need to either wait for a retrace or adjust the recommended stops because the 6 lights method is counting on the Euro moving in about 30 pip waves and trying to grab about 10 pips of that, and so a bar that is 20 pips may have already used up the target the 6 point method is shooting for.

--- 帖子 #18419 ---
Another good re-entry, which I am using as an additional filter is Bollinger Bands with a 12,2 setting. Once I have been limited out or close, I wait for an opposing candle to form and then place an entry order at the upper/lower price of the bands as long as the Trix, cloud, and other indicators line up. This way, if price breaks a new low/high on the BB, I'm in, if not, I've been saved from a losing position. The most important thing is to base your re-entrys on sound information and not dumb luck. The THV is excellent at providing you as much market information as you can absorb, but you still need to analyze what it's telling you. All in all, and after several years of trading, I believe the THV is the best system I've ever seen. You could not literally ask for a more complete manual system.
