--- 帖子 #18431 ---
Hi MajorHunter, I developed the MTF 6 point system last winter-spring (2009) . I forward tested it (Demo) for about 3 months and posted screenshots of all the trades on Cobras web site before it was approved for release. Testing was on the EURUSD pair 1m chart only, from about the 7am my time (GMT+3 currently) to the London close (6 pm or 7pm my time depending on daylight savings). No trades allowed 30 mins before or after red or orange colored Euro news. No trades allowed when divergence showing against the trade or conflicting divergences. All divergence trades taken. My results were between 65% (on very choppy days to 85% (on very trending days). (Results may vary as they say with all the diet programs because it depends a lot on if you correctly identify the places where divergence is going to make the trade go against you.) On average I believe about 75%. (The PC where I had the screenshots from those tests bit the dust.) However, other traders have PMed me that they have gotten similar results. THe stops and targets for this method, as I have confessed several times were a result of my own limitations as a trader - that I didn't have enough patience to stick with a trade. You will certainly do better if you use multiple lots and stick with the winners. Trading all the entries is grueling believe me because among other things you have to watch out for divergence froming on the 1m and 5m timeframes to warn you off bad trades. You can't just rely on the trix to tell notify you - you need to watch for it. Now that I am trading live money not demo I don't trade all of the 6 point entries. I just look for the really good ones (i.e the ones with the rainbow, and earlier in the trend or coming out of an area where price has compressed and where the signal has been triggerd by a nice steady move and not a violent one bar move.) The really good ones also usually don't go against you much. A nice setup is to wait for the rainbow to flip, then count to see if you have three higher highs and higher lows (or vice versa) and then take the next 6 point setup or trix cross, whichever comes first (often it will be a 6 point first). For this trade you can ignore conflicting divergence because entry is early in the trend, but you need to leave 10 pips of room between the trade and major resistance like a pivot and you need the higher highs/lower lows to occur after the rainbow has flipped and the colors are in order where each peak/low occurs This trade is usually worth sticking with. Another trade I like is a retry where price has tried to crack some point, failed, retraces and compresses and then slowly starts back for another retry. A 6 point signal that includes a recent signal from the 5m fast trix will usually get you in at a good point.

--- 帖子 #18443 ---
Just a comment about things I have learned about Forex trading. You MUST choose a method of trading that you feel comfortable with. Once you have made that decision, you need to really dig in and study how that method works. You also have to be constantly vigil and watch what the market is doing. It can, and will, change directions at almost any moment. So you have to be prepared for that to happen. Set hard stops far enough away from the price that they don't get hit on a normal price fluctuation, but definitely set a hard stop to protect the account from a major trend change. You really can't "set it and forget it" in this market. Things "happen" and you need to be prepared to react to it. Don't be afraid to take additional trades on retracements. If you are relatively certain of a trend direction, and a trade you have already placed has headed in a negative direction, a retracement trade can provide some additional positive pips as the general trend continues. But again, you have to keep your eye on the ball for an actual trend reversal. You don't want to get into a situation where you are throwing good money after bad! The most important thing I have learned along the way is NEVER stop adding to your Forex education. I try not to blindly follow everything I run across, but many times I can take bits 'n pieces of other methods of trading that I can apply to the method I am using that will make it perform even better. Happy trading to you all

--- 帖子 #18455 ---
To all CaveManager users, Just want to clarify one point raised by MikeFT. Even though CaveManager is not designed to handle or act on pending orders, it will still work once the pending order becomes an opened order. The only thing to take note of is that once you open a pending order, CaveManager will go into an order monitoring state and the status displayed will be as if an order has been opened. This may confuse some of you. If you are confused, you may want to download this copy here that I just updated so that CaveManager does not go into an order monitoring state if it sees pending orders. The version number will stay the same as there is no change to the functionality of the original version in any way. Be sure to always ensure that no matter how many pending orders you use, there should only be one active opened order for CaveManager to manage. Cheers, CaveMan

You can call VarMA using iCustom and get the value for buffer 0. The brown MA is this one: Attached Image For the Trix histo use iCustom to call the T3 trix like this: trxfastcurr =iCustom(NULL, prd, "THV T3 Trix",TrixNumberOfBars, A_t3_period, B_t3_period_ac,hot, MODE_MAIN, yy); trxfastprev =iCustom(NULL, prd, "THV T3 Trix", TrixNumberOfBars, A_t3_period, B_t3_period_ac,hot, MODE_MAIN, yy+1); trxslowcurr =iCustom(NULL, prd, "THV T3 Trix", TrixNumberOfBars, A_t3_period, B_t3_period_ac,hot, MODE_SIGNAL, yy) trxslowprev =iCustom(NULL, prd, "THV T3 Trix",TrixNumberOfBars, A_t3_period, B_t3_period_ac,hot, MODE_SIGNAL, yy+1);// and check the values like this if ( trxfastcurr - trxslowcurr &lt; trxfastprev-trxslowprev &amp;&amp; trxfastcurr &lt; trxslowcurr)//red histo else if ( trxfastcurr - trxslowcurr &gt; trxfastprev-trxslowprev &amp;&amp; trxfastcurr &lt; trxslowcurr)//green histo if ( trxfastcurr - trxslowcurr &lt; trxfastprev-trxslowprev &amp;&amp; trxfastcurr &gt; trxslowcurr)//red else if ( trxfastcurr - trxslowcurr &gt; trxfastprev-trxslowprev &amp;&amp; trxfastcurr &gt; trxslowcurr) //green

--- 帖子 #18462 ---
You can be slipped on your entry order, stop loss, and take profit orders. All orders must be matched to an opposing order, or the broker must be willing to carry it at their own rick of loss. So, yes, trading on margin does give you the ability to lose more than is in your account. If a situation like the "flash crash" occurs, for example, and your SL is at a level (price) where there are no matching orders in the opposite direction, you will be filled at the next closest price; unless they take on the risk themselves. There is an excellent thread by DarkStar called, "The Structure of Forex Brokers". Read that and you will understand all. The man is a truly insightful human being. Typically , most FX brokers will guarantee stops and profits on mini accounts ; not so many on standard accounts; but you should check with your broker. IF they don't, all the bitching in the world doesn't make them legally responsible to fill you at a given price. I wouldn't sweat it too much. Choose your broker wisely. Most marriages have a 1 in 2 chance of succeeding. The trader/broker odds are like, 1 in 1000. You really need to dig deeper than, "I like the way their platform looks" or "they use MT4". I chose Oanda because they adhere to a trader "Bill of Rights" that coincide with my beliefs...hence...I'm loyal to Oanda. You've got to believe in your broker as much as you do your marriage......hopefully.

--- 帖子 #18467 ---
There is an explanation of how to trade using the 6 lights method in the Manuals and Optional zip (Thv MTF). The only change I personally now make to this method is that I use an additional filter - the rainbow - to filter trades. That is, I view the rainbow as the major trend indicator and the coral as the minor trend indicator and I take 6 point trades only when they both agree on the direction of the trend. I do not take any 6 point trades when the coral says (for example) take long trades (i.e price is above the coral), but the rainbow says take short trades (i.e. the rainbow is flipped to the downside.) My reason for this is that in this situation the long suggested by the coral is a retracement against the major trend, and while it might get you some pips, or might even be the bottom and a trend reversal, odds are you are better waiting for price to reverse back again to the major trend. See below for example of what I mean. Attached Image (click to enlarge) The SwissArmy histo is just an improved version of the Trixhisto indicator. For 6 point trades you use it just like the Trix histo. The improvements in it are basically that you can combine other indicators besides the trix in it, and other ways of viewing the trix, like the trix histo, and also get a better alert on any combination of rows. However, you don't need this to trade the 6 point method.

I don't know how much more clearly I can put this: I trade THV trades The instructions and settings for trading THV trades (regular and 6 point trades) are centralized on page 1. In addition to the rules and settings on page one I personally now use the rainbow as a trend filter. That is, I eliminate THV trades that are against the rainbow. This is because, since I trade on the 1m timeframe which can get choppy, I find that the coral is too fast as a trend filter and that adding the rainbow as an additional trend filter helps me trade in the direction of bigger picture trend. In addition, the rainbow also helps me see when price is overextended or has retraced and consolidated and then starts expanding again, so this is another way it helps me filter trades (i.e the better THV trades are just after a trend change or after price has consolidated and starts expanding, the risker ones are when price is far extended from the last consolidation.) For this, I don't think there's any subsitute for screen time - just watching price action expand or contract. (Some people actually learn to see this without the rainbow, but I find it easier to see as the rainbow colors graphically put it.) This thread discusses THV. If you want more information about the nuances of trading the rainbow itself there are other threads, such as the one by LinuxTroll that discusses it. In addition I have shared one specific setup - the 1-2-3 THV trade (look for 3 higher highs or lower lows right after the rainbow has flipped and then look for a THV 6 point or regular trade), which you can find by reading my previous posts.

I've been tracking my progress since January of this year, and my winning trades percentage has been pretty darned decent. I've had an average in excess of 75 percent over that time period. However, I had one month with total negative dollars earned. The winning percentage that month (April) was about 64 percent, but I gave up $250 that month. To me, that just shows how important money management is to the process. I had a hard stop set waaaaaay away from the trade as an emergency safety net. The idea was to cancel the trade long before it reached the stop, but I let the trade run overnight and the Grim Reaper visited the trade and stopped it for me! It just goes to illustrate that even though we have some "plan" to trade with, things can still happen. And without money management, those things can sting pretty bad! The market is always changing, and we need to be prepared for the times those changes appear by instituting as much protection as we reasonably can. I've been averaging around 500 pips per month since January, even with that negative pip month, so I feel as though I'm making progress. It triggers an alert Long (GREEN) if F-Trix is above S-Trix and difference between the two is increasing. It triggers an alert Short (RED) if F-Trix is below S-Trix and differnce is increasing. There will be 4 different alerts on the screen, just like the previous ones, but only one of these will be present at one time, the 4 are. 1) His X Up - Possible Long, Green or Orchid color - Green means F-Trix above S-Trix and difference increasing. Orchid means F-Trix above S-Trix and difference decreasing. 2) His X Dwn - Possible Short, Red or Orchid color - Red means F-Trix below S-Trix and difference increasing. Orchid means F-Trix below S-Trix and difference decreasing. You will need the indicator "THV T3 Trix" in your indicator folder as the alert calls it for its information, its in the zip file if you need it. Hi Seller 9, I just want to clarify something about the trix histo (the spread). The one I did (and supplied the code for from the Swiss army histo) colors a square red if the fast and slow trix are above zero and the fast trix is above the slow but the spread between them is getting narrower. Later, Strat used the idea of adding a histogram for his trix, but in that same situation he colors that part of the histo dark green. Likewise, if the fast and slow trix are below zero and the fast is below the slow but the spread is narrowing I color that green whereas his is dark red. I dont know which one nando is trading from but anyway the code I supplied is like mine not like Strat's

--- 帖子 #18626 ---
We need to differentiate here between two issues here: 1) Actual repainting where the trix itself (on which the mtf indie is based) goes back and repaints after a closed bar 2) The difference between what an MTF indie tells you as you watch it minute by minute to see what the higher tf is doing vs what it will look like it told you if you added it after the fact rather than in real time. Re 1) The trix itself does go back and repaint one bar back on occasion - that occasion being when it has been flat and then choses a direction. (At least the older versions did. I don't know about the one Strat coded.) The fact that the trix itself may later go back and repaint itself is not a relevant issue here because the mtf indie is just trying to show you what you would have seen if you had been watching the higher tf at that minute. You are no worse off by watching the MTF indie. In other words if the trix was red on the higher tf, you get a red dot on the lower one. The MTF indie is not to be blamed if the trix later repainted itself green after the bar closed, and in fact it is more accurate because if watched in real time it doesn't repaint those bars even if the trix itself on the higher timeframe repainted that bar after it closed. You can check my previous posts if you want more info on this. Re 2) The info you get from most mtf indicators looks different when they are added after the fact and not watched in real time. That is, in real time a 15 min bar that ends red may have included several minutes where the trix was green before closing red. If you are watching the MTF histo on a lower tf in real time it will show these several bars of green in that 15 minute period. If you add the MTF histo after the fact i.e. after that bar has closed on the 15 m chart), it has no way of knowing this, and will show all 15 bars that comprise the 15m trix bar on the higher tf as red. You can check my previous posts if you want more info on this.

--- 帖子 #18627 ---
Normally a template will not work unless you have added all the indicators that come with it to your indicators folder. However, this template is based on indicators that I have shared before so perhaps you already downloaded them. If you want to be sure that you see all the indicators that are supposed to be in the template then copy all the ones that I supplied with it to your indicators folder. The second trix (the mtf trix), for some reason, does not look like it is showing the higher timeframe. You need to set it to do so (assuming of course that you want to see a higher timeframe) by setting autofimeframe to true. The arrows are just the regular trix divergence arrows. You can read about using trix divergence in the thread.

Same sl and tp - 15 plus spread and 10 plus spread or Atr suggestion whichever is greater. Personally, I still use the 6 lights method - that is, entry on 1 f and 5 fast plus another 4 points, in the direction of the rainbow, and also the 123THV Trade ( i.e -Make sure you have three higher highs or lower lows and then take the first legit THV trade you see - 6 point or trix cross - in the direction of the rainbow as long as there is 10 pips of room for the trade to move) You can see that I had 10 short trades this week and were not 10 short entries using this method during my trading hours. Some of those 10 were six point trades that didnt have the 1m slow and the 5m slow in their favor or 123 THV trades. (As you can see from my sceen shots, I have several 1m templates that I look at while trading and I will take a good trade that I see on any of them. Personally I like more information while I am trading and I like to see different views of the same thing, but a lot of people get overwhelmed by too much info and see the point much better with a relatively empty screen.) You will actually usually get a better entry using the 1m f and 5m fast or the 123THV trades than waiting for the 5m s to turn also - if you know how to weed out the bad ones. However, for all practical purposes I've noticed that when you enter in the direction of a rainbow that is showing all the colors and have both the 1m fast and slow trix and the 5m fast and slow trix in favor you always have the other three points anyway (though that is not the only way you can get 6 points). Hi all I've made some more improvments to PeterD's Mtf trix. You've probably noticed that it didn't update properly (and also had broken lines on those occasions) and if you wanted to know what the trix was actually doing on the higher timeframe for sure, you either had to check the appropriate histogram row, or click init to make it update. I've fixed this version so it updates minute by minute when used on a lower timeframe to look at a higher one. (This saves also keeping the histogram on the chart to see where things really stand). Unfortunately I can't get it to do the same when used on TF0 (to see the spread between the lines, or histogram). For that if you want a trix with a histogram you will need to use THV T3 Trix with color or to use Stratmans version. For the MTF indicator you also need the THV T3 Trix in your indies folder in order for it to work.

--- 帖子 #18695 ---
Three things: The prior versions of the MTF trix didn't update properly (when watching a higher tf trix from a lower tf). I uploaded a version yesterday (1.9) that fixes that as far as I can tell. (But I still can't get it to update properly on tf 0 so if you are using to see the histogram on tf 0 you need to use THV T3 trix color or the version of the trix coded by Statman.) 2. Check the hot parameter. It has to be the same in order for them to reflect the same color. 0.7 is like Trix 4.1 Div (used in THV V3) and 1.2 is like Trix V 6 (used in THV V 4) I've changed the default around a few times so they may not match between the histo you are using and the MTF trix 3. The histo is more reliable for one thing. Both the trix itself and the histo don't have a yellow condition for when the trix flattens out and the current value is equal to the previous. (The trix itself handles this by repainting) I handled it in the histo by showing you the opposite color. That is if the trix was green and then it flattens out and is equal I show you red (but not the opposite - I don't do it with red to green). This is just because in my experience its better to get a heads up when the trend is about to change to the downside because the fall tends to be a lot harder than the rise up from a downtrend.

--- 帖子 #18710 ---
Up to you really. What I do is try to pay attention to what the feel for the day is. There are some days that PA will pay strict attention to o/b and o/s on the 5 minute and others when it ignores it for long periods. You can check the previous cycles and see how they acted. How PA has been acting is usually how it will continue to act unless something dramatic happens to change that. Also, and this is hard to describe, but you have to get a feel for which trix or trixes really have or are going to get control of things. For example, if the 30 trix has just crossed up, the 15m trix has crossed up and is not oversold, the 5m trix is in oversold and the 1m has just turned up, it's going to be hard for PA to go down much even if the 5m is in oversold (usually), But if everything is in oversold and has been there all day and PA is at the end of it's range and there is a lot of divergence, then that 5 minute turning might be the one that tips all the others. About the 15m - put the 5m mtf trix and the 15m mtf trix on a 1m chart and watch them. I think you will notice that a really nice settup is when the 15 f and slow have just turned color, or crossed, the 5 f and slow are also crossed in that direction and the 1m f turns in that direction. Try watching this for a while before you decide to give up on the 15m slow. (I havent been showing lately this on the charts I post because it isn't a must but when I see it it gives me extra confidence in the momentum. [quote=vasi;3788812]

--- 帖子 #18729 ---
That trade was fine by the regular 6 lights rules. In the regular 6 lights method a divergence counts for 4 points and you just need two more points - one of which has to be the 1m fast ( and it's better if the other is the 5 m fast). You don't need the coral and it's better if the rainbow looks extended and you can see that the lower low (or higher high) is not much lower (or higher) while the divergence is pronounced and the lower low wasn't much lower than the prevous. You had pretty good divergence on both the 1m and the 5m and it was around the pivot so we could expect some buying there. I don't like to show divergence trades here because they are tricky - you have to have a good feel for what kind of a day it is. If the market is on a tear, they can get you in more trouble than they are worth, especially newer traders. But if it's bouncing around without much direction they can be the best trades, especially if you have been trading long enough to have a good feel for how the pair is acting.

Hi MissPips, I've got your rainbow template for several days and wonder how to use MTF color hist. What does it represents and how to use it ? The other thing is about MTF cloud that I don't understand very well. Do you use it in your 6 light strrategy ? Many thanks for your time and help.

--- 帖子 #18747 ---
The histogram represents the distance between the fast and slow trix. The trix is a momentum indicator.For example, when both the fast and slow trix are green and the fast trix is above the slow trix positive momentum is increasing. When the histogram is also green, not only is momentum increasing but the rate at which it is increasing is also getting faster. The 5m cloud and 15 m cloud can count for 2 of the 6 points that you need for the 6 light method. There is a manual in the zip file on the first page that explains this method.

--- 帖子 #18841 ---
Entry was too early. We are not just looking for a 1m trix cross when 5m has also crossed. We are looking for one of those with a nicely developed spine. Not that I'm saying these trades can never fail, but it's harder for price to go back against the trade when you get the two timeframes moving together AND the rainbow spine is well developed. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Also in this case you had a triangle going on the 15 m tf. That entry was where price broke the trendline but didn't close below it on the 15 m chart. Attached Image (click to enlarge) At the right entry, where the rainbow was well developed, it had closed below the trendline. Temping as it is to enter early, in my experience if you wait for the rainbow and the trixes to line up you will still get your pips, and as a rule you will suffer less, because by the time the rainbow has spread out, the market has made up its mind which direction it wants to go in. (Naturally this doesn't go in indefinately. The first couple of entries after a true flip are the best.) Here are the other entries from today besides what you posted. Notice that even if you wait for the crimson layer to show, you are still getting plenty of pips. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #18919 ---
The VARMA is a complicated piece of code that calls a lot of functions and uses 8 buffers. In addition on the latest rainbow template I call it using I custom from MAinColor in order to get the color to change based on the direction so that's more calculations. However these calculations are only done on the entire chart when it is loaded (or inited as in a tf switch). After that it only calcs the current bar. Therefore you can: 1) Reduce the number of bars in the chart drastically. If you are scalping you shouldn't need more than a few thousand bars. 2) Keep different the charts open for the timeframes you need so that you don't cause recalculation of everything by switching timeframe. 3) Use one of the regular rainbows not the VARMA rainbow. They put a lot less load on the CPU. The idea is just to use the rainbow to see the major trend and take THV signals in that direction, so any of them really work.

--- 帖子 #18936 ---
Yes I am. But I think Artful Dodger is right - I should stop confusing the newbies. So I'm going to answer this last question and then I will let you know if I decide to get my own thread. I added part of the 5m rainbow to the 1m chart on one of my charts. The reason is that not all trades are equal. In my experience, most trades where we see the spine and have the fast and slow trix on the 1m and 5m tfs in the direction the trade, will work out for at least 10 pips However, it still is safer and potentially more rewarding to get in a the beginning of a trend than near the end, and that goes for across timeframes as well. If you see a trade on the one min chart that is also occuring a the start of a new 5 min trend, it's potentially a better trade than one on the one min chart after the 5 min trend has been going for a long time. Also if you see an uptrend on the 1m chart and it's the first one after a new 5m downtrend, odds are it's just a larger than usual retracement and isn't going that far. When you see a lot of choppiness, if you zoom out to a bigger picture you can see better whether people are still buying the dips or selling the tops of a trend that is waining, and who wins in the end. Here are some examples Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) And that's all folks. I'll let you know if I decide to get my own thread to discuss rainbow-filtered THV.

I think it`s better when your pivots are the same as here: http://www.livecharts.co.uk/Members/...rex_pivots.php or at actionforex.com I use TzPivotsD 3.5, my Broker is GMT 0, so I set HrsServerFromGMT 0 (broker time), HrsChoiceFromGMT 3 (the end of NY session), use_day_formula true. Thus I receive pivots almost the same (+- 2 pips) as "official pivots" at actionforex.com. But some traders use the end of London session as the end of the day (HrsChoiceFromGMT 0), so their pivots might be slightly different

--- 帖子 #19003 ---
Hi ArtfulDodger, Glad you decided to stay!I think it's very important to have new perspectives in the thread - that's what keeps it alive. Regarding the rainbow , it is only about THV indirectly, since THV is a trend trading methodology and the Rainbow is about helping visualize the direction and strength of the trend. Some people don't need the rainbow to do that - they can see it with one or 2 moving averages (instead of 50), and others (the ones who trade naked) can do it just by looking at the price bars. Personally I find I can unstand what the trend is doing by looking at the interplay of the colors (and where price is in relation to them) much better than by looking at the price bars alone. The odds are in your favor more if you trade with trend and if you sell a top/buy a dip reasonably early to middle trend rather than late. That's all there is to it. If you can already see the trend without the rainbow then you don't need it. But if you do watch it then it may show you some things you woudn't have seen other wise. Here is one example that I have come to recognize that I don't think I would have seen otherwise. When I see this what I call 'unsupported' price action and then the rainbow flips it's usually look out below (or above). You dont see this too often but when you do it's usually meaningful. Attached Image (click to enlarge) You can see the exact same pattern in the one min tf in this post here from a few months (took me a while until I cottoned on to it but that's what I mean that if you watch long enough you may start to recognize some patterns you wouldn't have seen otherwise..) http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=18246 I'd have recognized the triangle in both cases, but not the direction in which it was likely to break out.

--- 帖子 #19006 ---
Had an email this weekend from one of our fellows here. He asked what is more important, the entrance or exit. My answer is that both are important but your MM depends 100% on your exit and that makes your account to grow or not. When you enter you have to have a clear idea when your position is valued and when it’s over. This depends a lot on the TF you trade but also your MM, don’t add never a position to a trade that runs against you, execute it in TP or SL but do it. You have to have a trading plan with a clear entry and exit point, don’t be afraid to execute a SL, that is part of the game, you only have to care that your MM let you win more than you lose. The exit point depends much on your TF, use a reasonable SL, Yen pairs should be more flexable than E/U as they are more volatile. You have to be very hard with your decision and don’t move your SL which is well thought out. To the above question: this system or better called method is made for a 40 pips daily target but you have days in which you can’t get it so don’t force yourself to take an avenger trade, just take it like it is, a new day is a new day with the same ol’ rules. Hope that helps

--- 帖子 #19041 ---
You will only get an arrow when all conditions are met (Red or Green), TRIX, RVI, Histo, and all of bar graph. Blue = false(condition not met) You will get a Red or Green arrow the first time the conditions are met and then you won't get another arrow untill you get a retrace of the 4 fast moving averages in the opposite direction, this resets it for the next trade. It will not take more than one trade in the sme direction without a pull back of at least the 4 shorter moving averages. They would be the four lights at the bottom of the indicator, starting with the one next to the 0 %, or the 4 fast MAs in the Rainbow, starting with the Brown one. I am still tweaking the indicator on demo accounts so it may not be optimal yet. You may only get 1 or 2 alerts durring a session. It is looking for the longer trend on the M5 chart. Good Luck

Hi, the TRIX is an oscillator Attached Image and like many oscillator it can show you momentum, the bests entry points (when fast-trix cross slow-trix); divergence (often followed by a good momentum); oversold &amp; overbought periods (when PA may reverse) the downward white line on the chart and the upward white line in the Trix window show you a divergence

--- 帖子 #19135 ---
I think it depends on market conditions and price action. For example, is there a strong trend that is relatively new or is it and old trend and divergence is occuring? Is the trend you want to trade against really a retracement against the daily trend or is it with the daily and how new is the daily trend? Have the swings with the trend been getting shorter and smaller and the swings against it been getting stronger? etc. But in general there's a reason for the saying that 'the trend is your friend'. (The 'until it end's' part of that saying is where you can think about trading against it but make sure you recognize when that is.) The thing is that you can never predict what the market is going to do. But there are certain situations where (in the absense of some new factor like unexpected news) it's more likely to continue doing what it has been doing and I prefer to trade those. Here is an example. This morning the Euro has chopped around and only done 33 pips since the open. But heres a situation where the 15 5 and 1 trix are all newly crossed down and you have both rainbows showing in the direction of the previous 5 m trend which was down. And boom, there's your ten pips. Try scrolling back in history and see how often you see that situation and the trade goes wrong. I try to remember that just because I'm sitting in front of my screen doesn't mean I have to trade. I just wait until I see something that I recognize and have seen work out hundreds of times. --- 帖子 #19142 ---
Yes that means you cant use mtfs for a visual backtest. Also the trix mtfs histos are limited to the number of bars they store so even if you leave your computer on, beyond that number they wont be right either. The thing that needs to concern us is: If I'm looking at the trix histo now and it's showing me that the 60 m fast trix is red and the 30 trix is red etc, if I look at the real 60 fast trix is it really red this minute? Because that is the purpose of the histogram - to help you if you don't have multiple monitors so you dont loose time flipping between charts. If you really want to backtest then you can approximate by using the MTF trix that shows the trix itself in steps and only using the closed values for your estimates. Sorry but I dont understand what you are trying to say in the rest of the post.

What I meant about not being able to backtest past a certain point even if you leave the computer open is that the trix histo values are only good for the number specified in TrixNumberofBars. I.e if you specify 750 and go back and look at the 760th bar that value is not good.

--- 帖子 #19159 ---
When you open your mt4 you cant use the mtf trix histo for backtesting. That is because when it is added after the fact (instead of watching the trix in realtime) it doesn't know what happened inside a 15 m bar(for example) just how it closed. For example if you already had Mt4 open and were watching a 15m fast row on a 1 m chart live, the 15 m fast trix might have been green for 5 bars, then red for 5 bars, then green for 5 bars and closed green. So that's what you'd see in the 15 fast row on the one minute chart -5 green bars, 5 red bars and 5 green bars. But if you now add another copy of the trix histo after that 15 minute bar has closed you will see that all the 15 1m bars that make up that period are green (and of course if you check on the 15m chart you will see that the 15 f trix was green too so it will look like the trix histo was accurate. But if you had been trading you might have made a trade based on one of the red bars. That doesn't mean that wasn't accurate - because if you had looked at the trix itself in real time it would have been red then even though it subsequently closed green.) And I am leaving aside here the problem that the trix itself sometimes repaints one bar back after that bar has closed. This happens when it has been flat (for example) but closed green, and then if the next bar is strongly down, sometimes it will go back and repaint the closed green bar red (or vice versa of course). But the trix histo that you had open in real time on the 1m chart will still show those bars green. This is a problem of the trix itself and not of the histo. If you leave your mt4 open continuously the most that it can be accurate is up to the number of bars specified in the TrixNumberofBars parameter. I'm not sure which version you have - only the later versions of the Swiss Army histo have that option. I don't know how many bars are specified in the trix histo that came with THV V4 - I didnt compile it myself.

Well of course. First of all no system has 100% results, and second THV and its variations are really methods not systems. That is, they supply tools but rely on your discretion as a trader. I know that sounds weasly, but it's the truth. Here is an example of a failed trade todaythat meets all my normal criteria, even preferrred criteria because both rainbows flipped together (except maybe I would have liked to see a little more spread on the 5 m trix) Attached Image (click to enlarge) Did I take that trade? No. Here's why: as you can see in the picture it was hitting the top of a down channel with a long history and also the 23 fib of the up move. and the 1 hr trix is down We might crack those but I wouldn't expect it to happen in the Asian session. So I didn't take that trade. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Personally I think it helps to trade only one pair. That way you get a feel for how it usuallly acts and where the kinks are (most of the time - nobody is perfect. And there are always surprises, but if you look at my posts you can see that the times that I've posted predictions about where price is going or areas where price was going to react they've been pretty good. I'm sorry I didn't post that channel yesterday - I though about it but I decided I'd been hogging the posts too much.) Anyway, if you look at the posts about the rainbow you can see that I've actually posted 5 types of trades 1) 6 lights in the direction of the rainbow 2) Count three higher highs/lower lows and then take the next good THV trade (6 lights or trix cross) in the direction of the rainbow. 3) Trade when you see the dark blue/dark red spine and 5m f and slow and 1m f and slow are in favor of the trade 4) Trade when you see 15 trix crossed up, 5 m trix crossed up, the 1 m trix crossed up or 1m f up especially if both rainbows are in the direction of the trade. 5) Trade when price makes a bump above the rainbow spine, and then exceeds it the 15, 5 and 1 trixes are all in favor of the trade , especially if preceded by a pattern like a double top/bottom or head and shoulders and divergence. So the question is: why so many different types if they all work? And the answer is: because there are different types of markets. I don't really know how to explain it, but here are some days where, for example, you will never see Trade type 3. Or other days where you never see type 4. I think it has to do with how big the swings are between the highs and the lows and how strong buying pressure is (for example) in a downtrend (or vice versa). What I do, is I start watching the market about two hours before London open, and I just look to see what's working that day. Because whatever has been working is usually what's going to continue working. I try to notice if the swings up and down are huge, or is the flow mostly one direction with small retraces. Are the retraces going to the 23 fib or to the 50. I also look at the stochs and I notice if price is reacting at once when it hits o/b or o/s or does it carry on a lot of bars before reacting? Is the market strongly trending or is it rolling up and down in swings that match one of the trixes (and it can be any one of them) etc. If it's going down is it acting like it wants to or is it resisting? Is there a daily trend and the four hour trend and is this trade with or against those? What did yesterdays candle look like and can I make any assumptions about todays probable trend based on that? Was there a pinbar on a higher tf against the trade? I also try to look for only the best trades and sit on my hands for the others. Even if a trade meets my criteria, if there's some other good reason not to take it (like above) I sit on my hands, which I think is an important trading skill to master. (That's why I have so much tiime to post. There are times when I know I'm not going to be trading until some obstacle is overcome or certain things line up like I like). Even if it looks like a really strong trend and good trade, if the Euro has done it's daily range I'll still sit on my hands, for example. Anyway, that's what I do. If you get good results with some of the other pairs please post them because I'm sure everyone will be interested. My reason for picking the EURUSD was because of the low spread, and the relative inertia of its moves. But if results can be improved by using another pair that would be nice to know. By the way, if you would use 5 as a tp what would you use as the stop for the Euro? Edit: BTW, here is a retry of the above failure example. Notice the difference in how they look.The trick to getting 10 pips is to get in on a retrace when you have enough momentum to get them so we want to learn to see that momentum. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #19230 ---
If you want to see the actual logic you can look at the source code of the THV T3 Trix which is posted in the thread. In non math logic: The trix is a momentum indicator. Even though the trend is still up there, the momentum of the increases in price has fallen because just before that the jumps in the price bars were large and now they are small in relation to what happened previously. Hence the trix stays red until those bars work their way out of the equation, even though price is still going up.

One cold winter morning a young man walks five miles through the snow. He knocks on the Jademaster’s door. The Jademaster answers with a broom in his hand. “Yes?” “I want to learn about Jade.” “Very well then, come in out of the cold.” They sit by the fire sipping hot green tea. The Jademaster presses a green stone deeply into the young man’s hand and begins to talk about tree frogs. After a few minutes, the young man interrupts. “Excuse me, I am here to leam about Jade, not tree frogs.” The Jademaster takes the stone and tells the young man to go home and return in a week. The following week the young man returns. The Jademaster presses another green stone into the young man’s hand and continues the story. Again, the young man interrupts. Again, the Jade-master sends him home. Weeks pass. The young man interrupts less and less. The young man also learns to brew the hot green tea, clean up the kitchen and sweep the floors. Spring comes. One day, the young man observes, “The stone I hold is not genuine Jade.”

--- 帖子 #19320 ---
Hi Al Agha, You're welcome. I don't think I understand what you are asking here. What the indie does is at the very beginning of each new bar it checks the previous bar and sees if it was red or green and alerts if there was a change in the trend from one to the other. If it were to check at the beginning of a bar whether that bar was red or green there would be no meaning to that because it would be based on the first tick of the bar only and that could change back and forth many times during the course of the minute.

--- 帖子 #19328 ---
The 6 point method was designed for and tested only the 1 m chart. If you use it on the 5 min you will have to adjust it and test it yourself. For the system on the 1m the usual THV rules apply (i.e price must be above/below the coral and cloud) except that you can trade when the 1m fast trix turns color without waiting for a trix cross provided that you also have 6 points and two of them are from the 1m fast and the 5m fast. To avoid being late to the party try to trade as close to possible to fresh signals (i.e a fresh color change of the 5m fast together with a fresh 1m color change of the fast near a coral cross. The more times you use a signal that is based on a 1m f trix color change after the first time the 5m fast has changed the riskier it gets because you only get so many 1 m waves per 5m trix cycle before the trix changes to the opposite color and there is a more serious retrace.)

First of all, Hi ... I'm new here but I've literally been trading since I was 10, and trading forex since 1998, so I'm not exactly "new" either :-) I've messed around with THV a little bit, and it's a good system. I don't use it because I have my own system that is "just a bit" less complicated. With the preliminaries out of the way, look, it is exceedingly unlikely that you are "processing" the trading rules the same way as another trader. That means your entries WILL NOT be the same as some other traders UNLESS you happen to be in some sort of live trading room where you are "following a leader." While trading rooms might be okay to initially learn a system or some technique, I absolutely DO NOT recommend any sort of "follow the leader" approach. So ... this is what YOU have to do, assuming you want to continue using THV. 1) Run the system as you understand it, sticking to the rules as you understand them LIKE GLUE. Do this ONLY ON A DEMO ACCOUNT for a minimum of 2 weeks ... 1 month would be better. 2) Analyze your results. If the system is profitable as it sits and the system "mentally" agrees with you (meaning you aren't pulling the hair out of your head every time you place a trade) then consider sticking with it for another 2 weeks to 1 month, trading in demo before going with a live account. 3) If you analyze your results and you are finding some significant percentage of the time the market "reads your mind" and instantly moves against you ... consider that perhaps you are simply misinterpreting the rules. SIMPLY FLIP THE RULES AROUND. When the previous rules, as you understood them, said to open long ... instead open short. Now, stick the the NEW RULES LIKE GLUE for at least 2 weeks ... and 1 month would be better. 4) Analyze your results. If the system is profitable as it sits and the system "mentally" agrees with you (meaning you aren't pulling the hair out of your head every time you place a trade) then consider sticking with it for another 2 weeks to 1 month. (see where this is going?) 5) If you get here and you aren't running your system for one more "go" in demo mode before going live with it then you need to look for a new system! Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #19394 ---
I'm glad you asked this question. I'm really trying hard to articulate what I do as fully as possible, and sometimes you just do things so instinctively after all those hours looking at a screen that it's hard to really put your finger on all the nuances of what you are really basing decisions on. A few comments before I get to the main point. First, I use this method on the EURUSD only so I'm not sure all the patterns work the same on the other pairs. You need to test them yourself to see if they do. I did make some comments on the EJ trade in the post above because some things are the same for all pairs (like it's safer to trade with the big picture main trend and to stay away from trades with a lot of divergence showing). Second, if you are going to use this method you should use a 15 pip stop plus spread for the EU. My reason for this is that the EU tends to move in about 30 pip waves. IF you are getting in on a retrace and the trend is continuing on, then it shouldn't retrace more than half to 68 percent (and you are getting in on a dip/top so it has already done some of that). You can do two lots and set the second one to breakeven to see if you can catch more of the move after you get the first 10 pips. (Of course if you see the ATR stop has jumped up to 20 or 25, which it sometimes does then you need to adjust the stop and target.) Third and this is a big point. This may be day trading but it isn't a day job. Just because we are sitting at our desk doesn't mean we need to trade every chance we see. We need to take into account the big picture and to use our judgement. What do I mean my 'use our judgement'? . First we need to consider the overall condtions. In this case 1) It's Monday morning 2) The market hasnt picked a direction for the day or week yet. Attached Image (click to enlarge) 3) The range has been 35 pips so far. 4) There's an uptrend on the four hour chart, but it's over sold. and lots of divergence (both positive and negative.) Attached Image (click to enlarge) 5) A trendline was broken on the 4 hour chart and is being retested. My Conclusion: I'd like to see a decisive move before jumping in, because the EU looks like it might turn around, and as you know it hates doing that. The EU has the turnaround time of an aircraft carrier - lots of wallowing around before it gets completely turned. Or it could be consolidating before it carries on. Who knows? The only thing to do is wait for a decisive move. Now about the specific trade on the EU - I didn't take that one in light of the above and also in light of the particular characteristic of the trade, namely 1)that the 15 m trix was not freshly crossed but on its third attempt to turn down after two prior attempts that failed. 2) Also the previous failure to crack the open included a very strong spike up which did not respect the turnaround down trendline. The safest trades are when 1) both the rainbows are freshly crossed (one is also ok if the other conditions merit it) AND 2) you see lower highs and lower lows (or the opposite) with the spine respected AND 3) the 15m trix and 5m trix are freshly crossed with a nice wide spread on the 5m trix and a widening spread on the 15m trix AND 4) Then you catch a retrace on the 1m trix which has not made dent in the higher tf trix. At most, in a strong looking trend, I'd go for a second turn of the 15m fast, but not third after two prior failures to make any headway. I'm posting two examples of what this looks like, but if you look at my previous posts you will see that they mostly all look like that. Just memorize the way these pictures look and go for it when you see this. The main points: 1) !5m trix is freshly crossed and the spread is widening respective to the previous bar 2) 5m trix is nicely spread out 3) 1m rainbow is nice and wide and the spine has been respected 4) It doesn't hurt if there was a failed attempt to go up/down with double top/double bottom with divergence in the previous trend either! Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) There are enough trades that look like this each week so that you don't have to take the less than perfect looking ones.

--- 帖子 #19396 ---
Re Fresh Cross - I would take a second attempt of the fast trix on the 15 m to go up or down in the direction of the slow, but not a third attempt after two failures like in that trade this morning. Sometimes a big retrace will cause the 15m f to turn against the direction of the slow trix, but then if it resumes and turns the color of the slow again, and if the 5m trix has a good spread and is fresh and the rainbow has a nice spread I would take it. But I wouldn't take a third attempt - that's asking too much. Re widening: I would take a trade where the spread on the 5 was narrowing (represented by the histogram having the opposite color) as long as the trix cross was fresh (not a second attempt where the fast went against the direction of the slow and then changed back to the same color as the slow) and as long as both fast and slow were still the right color for the trade. But I definately think the spread on the 15 has to be widening. Re the two rainbows agreeing - if you want to be super cautious you can have that rule. But I would take trades based on just the 1m if the 5m rainbow was very expanded and there was a lot of divergence and the trixes all line up perfect. I wouldn't load the boat though.The time to load the boat is when both of them have been compressed and then start expanding together, and the trixes all line up perfect. Re analysis timeframes: I look at all of them from monthly to 5m before I start trading for the day and make note of any patterns I see and what I think of them (so that the next day I can see how good my analysis was) and then look at the 4 hr, 1h 30 15 and 5 periodically. And frankly I also look at what the Swissy, the cable and sometimes the AudUsd and EurGBP are doing too during the day.

--- 帖子 #19412 ---
Hi Al Agha, I think I've come as close as I can get to it. The problem is that the usual way to get the results for the open of a bar is this code: bool NewBar() { static datetime lastbar; datetime curbar = Time[0]; if(lastbar!=curbar) { lastbar=curbar; return (true); } else { return(false); } But if you check the buffers for the HA bars at time[0](the exact start of the bar) they are empty. So what I did is to check them as soon as they change (which is when the buffers get filled) BUT I added a parameter called MaxSecs. So what happens is that the change is caught when it happens and counted for notification purposes if there are more than MaxSecs left to the bar when it happens. Without this parameter you do get notified when there is a change BUT for example if the previous bar closed red, and the current bar opens red but changes to blue with thirty seconds left you will get notified, but only once per bar. (If you like this, you can set MaxSecs to 1, otherwise leave it at 55). So the way it works now is it has three alert types: 1) Alerts at start of current bar when previous bar has a different color than the bar before it. 2) Alerts whenever the HA direction changes color whenever that happens to be 3) Alerts when the open color of the current bar is different than the open color previous bar. One alert per bar, but MaxSecs lets you choose how far into the bar you want to count as the open. If you only want to count about the first tick leave at 55. Note that this option can look a little confusing because the previous bar could have opened red and then ended up being a blue bar. So if the current bar opens blue you will still get an alert because the previous bar opened red, but it may not look clear why that is, because as you look at the previous bar on the screen you see blue and you no longer see that it opened red.

--- 帖子 #19434 ---
The basic idea behind THV is that we want to grab pips out of the middle of a trend by buying dips in a uptrend and selling rallies in a downtrend. Here are some helpful basic rules: How do we know whether the trend is up or down? Rule 1: Trend is up when price is above the coral and down when it is below it. Rule 2: In an uptrend we buy dips, in a downtrend we sell tops After we have determined the direction of the trend, how do we know when to buy a dip or sell a rally? 2a. We buy a dip in an uptrend when the fast trix has crossed back up above the slow trix and price is above the Ichimoku , indicating that momentum has resumed in the direction of the uptrend 2.b We sell a top when fast trix has crossed below the slow trix and price is below the Ichimoku , indicating that momentum has resumed in the direction of the downtrend. Best trix crosses are near zero and when both trixes are the same color as the trade. Reason: When the trix crosses near zero and price has crossed but is still near the coral, the trade has room to move Some people like to wait until the fast trix has crossed zero in the direction of the trade, but that is optional. It is also best to trade in the direction of the trend on the next higher timeframe, or alternately to go one timeframe lower to look for a good entry. That is, if you are trading the 5m chart (top down) and you get a signal, check the one minute chart to make sure the 1m is not way ovebought/oversold when you enter. Alternately, trading bottom up , it is best to trade when higher timeframe agrees with the direction of the trade. For example if you get a signal on the 1m chart, it is best if it is in the direction of the 5m trend. How do we know when not to trade or not trade? Rule 3: Do not trade against trendlines, pivots, support/resistance or divergence. We need to watch out for trendlines, pivots and major support and resistance, and not buy or sell right on top of any of these. Instead we should wait for a break, or even better a break and retest. Reason: We are trying to grab pips out of the middle of a trend and any of these can spell the end of the trend. So we don't want to be too near them when we trade (too near meaning that we dont have enough room to hit our target before hitting one of these potential obstacles.) For example, if you are about to take long trade, and the daily pivot is 3 pips above your entry, better to wait and see if you get a break first. We should also watch out for divergences, and not trade against them. Rule 4: Trading times: Trade when there is enough volatility but not during news It is best to trade when there is enough volatility to get pips - which you can measure by which sessions are open and by the ATR (above 10 is better). However it is best not to trade just before or after news. Rule 5: Use Good Money Management: Set stops and do not risk too much of your account. Stops and targets: Either use the THV ATR suggestion or use 15 pip stop 10 pip target (that's my personal suggestion for the Euro for the 1m tf, plus spread for each of them. For other currencies that may differ. You can try 10 times the spread for the stop ). Or you can put the stop below/above the previous swing low/high, and trail it Risk: Don't risk more than between 1 to 5 % of your account on any one trade. One percent is conservative, 5% is cowboy style. 1.5 or 2% is pretty average. There is also, of course, the manual on the first page. In addtion to the basic method there are several other ways that people trade using the tools provided by THV including: - MTF THV using the 6 lights method or the 6 lights method with a rainbow filter. - Divergence trading comparing the trix to price and taking a THV signal when there is both divergence and price bouncing of something solid. The main reason you see so many different type of screens is that in order for a trend trading method to work you have be taking trades that ARE with the trend. So your basic problem is to identify when you have a trend. (THV rules specify that when price is above the coral it is and uptrend and below it a downtrend, however price can be above the coral when the market is flat or above it for a small retrace in a major downtrend.) Everyone has their own favorit method of identifying when there is a trend. The most common are: Trendline breaks or bounces Pivot breaks or bounces Pattern breaks or bounces (like triangels, H&amp;S) Moving averages (like crossovers or the rainbow) Divergence (to get in at the start of a new trend, one hopes). Several higher highs and higher lows (or vice versa) in sequence That mostly accounts for all the different charts you see.

--- 帖子 #19505 ---
Well if you look at the places where the red and green line cross, you'll see that they are very close to the trix crosses (the trix is just a bit smoother) But the TDI has the bollinger type bands on, which I've never figured out how to get on the trix. So I use the TDI as a kind of proxy for the trix, and I look for when it squeeses above 68 or below 32 as a proxy for a squeeze on the trix. I also use it to confirm divergence - which is safer when confirmed by more than one indicator.

--- 帖子 #19652 ---
HI Badass I have not found an accurate MTF ADX that displays all the multiple entries on the page like the pipware charts and MTF Trix. What I use is a blank chart with the ADX on, and just switch back and forward between timeframes. The ADX has 3 lines ...ADX, -DI and +DI ADX gives strength the DI gives direction .....+DI long and -DI short. I Watch on all 3 time frames but Use the 1M and 5M for the gauging the exits Example:- So if I am long and the -DI starts to show strength, then I know I need to start looking for the Exit... I would watch the 5M ADX to see is the change on the 1M has accumulated to a change there. If not It's a good chance it is a fakeout. The "Cross" refers to the two Di switching ... where one was dominant, they flip and the other now comes ontop..... what this mean is that a trend reversal is occurring especially if the ADX is trending up There are so many nuances of it that the only way is to spend some screentime. for additional info, videos on utube for practical instructions Inserted Video (i not affiliated with this, just found some of it useful)

--- 帖子 #19720 ---
I trade of the M1 so All Trix (M1, M5, M15) are heading in the same direction (ideally all freshly crossed in this order M1,M5,M15 Check the Direction of the overall trend is in the direction of the trade, depending on action this may be of the H1 or H4 Check for Price cross on the Ichi (M1, M5 and M15) Also Check for Coral on M1 and M5 Check ADX:- M1 - ADX &gt; 25 and +DI for long &gt;25 or -DI for long &gt;25 M5 - ADX &gt; 25 and +DI &gt; -Di and heading UP (for long) or -DI&gt;+DI and heading UP for Short M15 - ADX Heading UP, better of over 25 Check Entry in relation to Major support and resistance Check Entry for conflicting Divergence (from M15 and M5) I also have charts running with the CleanRainbow developed by MissPips, I cross all entries against these(hey it never hurts to double check). How that rainbow looks give an idea of the price action that MAY be developing. (MA squished, Color of spine etc etc) My setups may sound like that of a Indicator junkie, but the amount of pairs I trades, i look for quick confirmation instead of trying to evalute from scratch, expecially trading of the M1 ...2 minutes on a volatile pairs can cost you the trade Ideal entry should be at a retrace/dip in the Trend, this is usually the best as you go almost immediately into profit as price starts to re-assert it self in the direction of the trend. If a trade starts to go bad, (1 - 3 minutes in) i may re-evaluate the SL, this depends on cost, trend, volatility. I posted links to some youtube videos, they do a great job in showing the principles in action..my only addition is the adx Exit for me is usually done 2 way, depending on the pair I may have an Automatic TP/SL in place (typically 10), since whipsaw and retrace can happen quickly. For manual trades I use the ADX most times, with comparison on 3 time frames. Again this depends on the pairs as Support&amp; Resistance plays a major role. I recommended that if you are new to the process, focus on the EURUSD as the majority of experienced members trade that pair and you can get comparisons. Even with all the above, THV is still NOT a totally mechanical system, there are degrees of subjectivity to reading the indicators that can only be gained screen-time. Aside from the above, it is critical that you KNOW your indicators, exactly what they indicator, an idea of how they are built, it is in knowing this that you can decide how best to push the system.

--- 帖子 #19727 ---
Done for today, it may have a few bugs as I haven't tested it on a live feed, but here it is if anyone wants to play with it. This alert is designed around the M5 time frame but can be placed on any time frame chart but still will take its signals from the M5 time frame. Here is the present alert logic. Trix: 1) M1 = Fast of Trix either Green or Red 2) M5 = Fast-Slow-Cross of Trix either Green or Red. 3) M15 = Fast-Slow of Trix either Green or Red. 4) M30 = Fast-Slow of Trix either Green or Red. Coral: 1) M5 = Bid above coral for buy and ask below coral for sell. 2) M60 = This is used for direction to buy in and compares todays bar to one 20 bars(hours) ago. ADX: 1) M5 = ADX&gt;25, +DI&gt;25 for Long, -DI&gt;25 for Short 2) M15 = ADX&gt;25, +DI&gt;-DI and headin up for LOng, -DI&gt;+DI and headin up for Short. 3) M30 = ADX Heading UP and greater than 25. If all the above conditions are met an alert window will open. This alert is similar to my other alerts, so if you have used them this one is similar, I have just removed a lot of the alerts that are not needed. Below is a screen shot that points out a few things. I have included a zip file with the "M5_ADX_Alert" and the indicators you will need to make it work along with a template if you want it that looks like the screen shot below. This is untested at this time, so it may have some bugs yet. I haven't put together any help document yet, as I don't know if this will be of any use. If it does prove to be helpful I can write up something at a latter date after all the bugs are out. Feel free to make comments for improvements. --- 帖子 #19795 ---
The strategy is: 1) Trade with the trend 2) In an uptrend buy dips; in a downtrend sell tops 3) Use the coral to determine trend. Price above coral = trade long, price below coral = trade short. 5) Use the trix and the Ichimoku to determine when to buy the dip, or sell the top. Enter on a trix cross in the direction of the trend, if price is also above/below the Ichimoku cloud and Coral (for long/short). 6) Use the ATR suggested stop from the THV infopanel indicator for stops and targets. Thats it. If you know how to recognize a trending vs a ranging market and when a trend is getting stronger or weaker or is approaching a potential reversal point you can skip the rest of the thread

--- 帖子 #19843 ---
On a non volatile 2 bars in may not be an issue, so the indi alert will work, On a volatile pair 2 bars may mean 1/2 thru the trade. Divergence is calculated on the TF you are lookin at. There are two ways to use Divergence.... to Take Trades and Avoid Trades Type 1.) You want to make sure you are not going long in a bearish divergence being formed on either the current TF or the immediate higher and the opposite for the short. If you rely on the indi you will go into the trade only to realize 2 bars in the short term trend is opposite. Type 2.) You can wait for divergence to form and trade the type of divergence being formed (what i referred to in earlier post ...should have been a bit clearer...sry) ... Of course THV core rules still apply for each. For the purposes of THV Scalping, I use the divergence to avoid trades. I aslo trade Divergence as a method but that's on higher TF and not THV Screentime ...and more screentime As a example turn on the draw trend lines on the M1 on the Trix indicator and observe how it is formed and when it is displayed

Here is the reworked M1 Alert to match up with what TREAD had in a previous post. I think I have most of the bugs out, will let it run on 10 pairs and see what happens. It also has the High?Low triggers if you want to use them. Read previous posts to make sure you have all the indicators it calls. It can be put on any chart time frame as the code is just for the M1, so it doesn't matter. Here are the rules. M1 LONG: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and +D1 &gt; 25, Bid above Ichi, Bid above Coral M1 SHORT: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and -D1 &gt; 25, Ask below Ichi, Ask below Coral M5 Long: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and +D1 &gt; -D1 and heading up, Bid above Ichi, Bid above Coral M5 SHORT: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and -D1 &gt; +D1 and heading up, Ask below Ichi, Ask below Coral M15 LONG: ADX heading up, Bid above Ichi M15 Short: ADX heading up, Ask below Ichi M5 LONG Trend: 89 EMA, 144 EMA, 200 SMA, not in any order, Bid must be above all of them. M5 SHORT Trend: 89 EMA, 144 EMA, 200 SMA, not in any order, Ask must be below all of them. Good Luck Attached File(s) M1_ADX_Alert.ex4 40 KB | 623 downloads Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Well a few comments, general ones first. 1) Sometimes trades fail. Sigh, what to do, that's part of trading. 2) It's a bit safer also to check the 15m trix and make sure at least the 15 m fast is also going your way. 3) This method really depends on momentum, so the best time to use it is when you have London and Asia or London and US or at least London open. The ATR in Asia or after London closes is usually to low for it to work well. 4) According to my provider, it didn't fail. The signal was complete at 4:29 (GMT+2) (5m fast trix both closed red and 1m fast and slow both red) so you could enter at 4:30 at 1.2800. The highest high on my provider before it went back down into profit was 1.28133 and the method calls for a 15 pip stop/10 pip target plus spread on each so it should have worked because it didn't go 15 pips plus spread against you.

Here is what the criteria is in the last M1, all these must be met. In addition you could also add on the High/Low trigger lines if you select that option. M1 LONG: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and +D1 &gt; 20, Bid above Ichi, Bid above Coral M1 SHORT: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and -D1 &gt; 20, Ask below Ichi, Ask below Coral M5 Long: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and +D1 &gt; -D1 and heading up, Bid above Ichi, Bid above Coral M5 SHORT: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX &gt; 25 and -D1 &gt; +D1 and heading up, Ask below Ichi, Ask below Coral M15 LONG: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX heading up, Bid above Ichi M15 Short: Fast-Trix, Slow-Trix, ADX heading up, Ask below Ichi M5 LONG Trend: 89 EMA, 144 EMA, 200 SMA, not in any order, Bid must be above all of them. M5 SHORT Trend: 89 EMA, 144 EMA, 200 SMA, not in any order, Ask must be below all of them. Sorry for taking up so much bandwidth, hope no one minds. --- 帖子 #19985 ---
Yes it was, however I do not use the trix going into overbought/oversold as an exit.... The reason for this is that price can stay in this zone, which is an indication of a strong trend. You should not ENTER a new trade in the OB/OS Zone, but never exit if the signals are strong. You would have banked about 17 - 20 pips on that trade and that very good here is what i did a bit different. After 5 Bars (5 mins) I started to look at the ADX on the 5M Chart, after 10Bars (10Mins) I switch the entire chart to the 5M time frame and watched the ADX...i saw the +DI start to increased and the -DI decrease .. I got out then with a NET 36PIPS ...could have exited @ 42Pips but I waited for the +DI to confirm .. The Idea here is to let the winners RUN for as long as you are comfortable. That extra 16 Pips would go to into the PipBank to offset other trades

The criteria for the M1 alert is at post 19997. The M1 alert is at post 19957. The Alert V20A is at post 18763. The M1 alert criteria are based on some of the settings Tread was using. Use the V20A alert if you want to select your own combination of alerts, although it doesn't have the ADX, but you could just put that indicator on your chart by itself. The charts I posted earlier were M15 charts using the M1 alert. I want to see a bigger picture than just M1 shows and it also gets me past some of the noise in the M1. I never trade using just the alert, or any alert, it only alerts me to the fact that a pending move may be about to happen. This way I can monitor 10 charts while doing other things. Of course if you move out to longer time frames you may need to check in once a day, just depends on your method, everyone is different. Every trader does things a little different, so take your pick of what works best for you and create your own method that you understand and works for you. M1 takes time to learn how to trade, new traders may want to start out with a longer time frame before they move into the M1. There is no alert that works 100%, they are only there to get your attention. Good Luck

--- 帖子 #20049 ---
Okay, having been where you are, here is my take, see pic for why Technically you should have stayed in the Trade. Now to deal with the psychological aspects. Entering into a trade is a gamble, you analysis helps stack the odds in your favor, but you are still gambling. Now with that firmly in mind .... You never gamble what you cannot afford to loose, when you put in a stop loss (a respectable amount) you are saying "This is how much I am willing to lose in order to make a profit" Now this leads to a second question . What is your lot size in relation to your account? Since its the loosing of the money that causes the panic, if you panic when you are 3 pips down that mean you are definitely trading the wrong lots. Typically 1 - 2% of the account as a maximum should be risk. So if I have a 100 dollar account (yes I have been there), then 1% is 1 Dollar, if I want to have a 10 Pip Stop Loss, then my MAX lot size is 0.01 At this point when I enter the trade, worst case scenario ...i lose 1 Dollar, it might be less if the indicators suggest that the trade is not working out. There are many ways to deal with this (search the forums), but short of learning the hard way (blow your account), I suggest you open a demo account (free money) with a Realistic Account value and leverage that you would trade LIVE . Then see if you can increase that account. Once you are fully confident in your skill then trading with a couple of pips down will not faze you. My favorite watch words "Optimism means expecting the best, but confidence means knowing how you will handle the worst. Never make a move if you are merely optimistic." Optimism can be a speculator’s enemy. It feels good and is dangerous for that reason. It produces a clouding of judgment. It can lead you into a venture with no exits. Even when there is an exit, optimism can persuade you not to use it. You should never make a move if you are merely optimistic. Before committing your money to a venture, ask how you will save yourself if things go wrong. Once you have that worked out, you’ve got something better than optimism. You’ve got confidence. My last bit of Advice, get some books written by Traders...read them ... you may not adopt their style, theory etc etc ... but it will give you a breath of scope that allows you to think about the big picture ... Okay.... Im done with the sermon

--- 帖子 #20079 ---
Chiba When im trading the direction the ADX and Di is important. You do not want to get into a trade where the ADX line is above 25 but pointing down. THat shows that the trend currently has no strength. The perfect textbook trade with ADX is when both are pointing up at a 45 degrees angle. I suggest you watch the ADX video that Tread posted. For me, i ONLY take signals where both THV and ADX lines up. Anything where there is uncertainty then could be a risky trade. I tend to take the risky trades ONLY if the DI is above 25 pointing the right way with ADX not far off 25 WHEN ADX and DI on the 5 min is above 25, ie a trend continuation move on the 1 min. Best thing for you is add ADX from the standard indicators in MT4 and look back historically on your chart. Its the only way you will learn. STart to notice the patterns between ADX and THV signals. Then when an alert comes you can spot things quickly to execute the trade.

Folks, on vacation here, so no charts to post, here's my 2cents on the ADX before the Forex police (aka Wife) shuts me down. Watchin the M1 ADX is critical for entry. Treat it the same way you woud the M1 Trix When using MTF Entries, think of it like a foundation, with M1 as the foundation that all the entries stand on. Also the better the separation between the DI's indicates a stronger trend, where the DI is stronger than the ADX crossing the 25 line, and the space between DI is opening rapidly, this represents a breakout, Just load up a chart and add the ADX and watch the history of strong trends and the ADX behavior
