--- 帖子 #20128 ---
Well here is a new version of the Swiss Army indie including Treads ADX method. . In order for it to work you need the attached indicators in your indicators folder (not on your chart). If you want the divergence setting to work on the 1m chart you also need to redownload THV3 Trix for MTFHisto if you didnt do so in one of the previous versions of the SA histo, because that setting was turned off in the previous version. If you don't need to see divergence for the 1m tf in the histo you can stick with the previous THV3 Trix for MTFHisto if you already downloaded it. Changes 1) Added types 23 t0 28. 2) Added ability to specify trix hot param per row.Note that the hot parameter determines which trix is being used. 1.2 corresponds to the THV V4 trix, .70 to Trix 4.1 div. 3) Added Currenttf param. This causes the eperiods to be ignored and the current timeframe to be used for all etypes when set to true. (Use if you have a particular set of indicators that you like using all on one tf and you want to be able to see them when switching the chart tf.) So now the modes and types are Mode 1: ===== Mode 1 looks at ePeriod Type, which can be the following ePeriod types: 0 = slow trix 1 = fast trix 2=stochs For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) 3=Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) 4=semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) 5=cloud 6=HeikenAishi; 7=TDI (traders dynamic index) 8=AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) 9 =AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) 10=Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) 11=Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) 12- Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) 13 -Coral 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not). Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 21 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is red, empty when none of the above Type 22 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is red, empty when none of the above. Type 23 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction. Green sloping up, red sloping down Type 24 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction, and also in order ( i.e, 3 above 5, 5 above 8 etc, or vice versa) Type 25 - Three specified MAs have crossed and specified stochastics poining in same direction. Type 26 - Three specified MAs have crossed and are above the Coral. Type 27 - Fast trix, slow trix and trix histogram all the same color Type 28 - Treads ADX setup: Green when PlusDI above MinusDI, Plus DI increasing, PlusDI above specified value, ADX above specified value, ADX increasing or red when vice versa Note that ADX , PlusDI and Minus DI price mode values are as follows: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4 This is different from the MTFADX indie Tread released, which uses the high price for all three by default (an error in my opinion because it seems to scew things to the positve side, but you can choose what you like). If you dont care whether the ADX is above a certain value, just that it be increasing set ADXMinVal to 0. Likewise if you don't care if the DI value is above a particular level, just that it be increasing set DIMinVal to 0. Mode 2 ====== Mode 2 ignores eperiod type and sets all tfs to demi classic mode (fast trix above/below slow and above/below zero, but may have changed color against the trade. Mode 3 ====== Mode 3 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to classic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade and above/below zero) Mode 4 ====== Mode 4 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to semiclassic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade but not necessarily above/below zero) Autotimeframe =========== When autotf is true, the indicator works like the old trix histo, selecting the next second and third higher timeframes for the fast and slow trix (i.e on a one minute chart, 5m f &amp; s and 15m f &amp; s trix). If use autotf and usesecondautotf are both true, then it selects the fourth and fifth higher tfs for the fast and slow trix. (i.e on a one minute chart 30m f &amp; s and 60m f &amp; s trix) Alarm The alarm only works when autotf is false The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. You will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore.

--- 帖子 #20143 ---
This has been discussed numerous times in the thread. First of all, the trix itself repaints. It can repaint one bar closed bar back, particularly when it is flat. Second, the trix histogram does not 'repaint' in that sense but it can differ from the actual trix for several reasons: 1) The trix histo keeps track of what the trix is doing minute by minute on the lower timeframe, so if the trix on the higher timeframe has repainted one closed bar back the trix histo on the lower timeframe will differ from what you see on the higher timeframe chart when you look back. If the trix itself was red on the higher timeframe and repainted itself green one bar back after that bar closed, those bars will still be red on the histo on the lower timeframe. In this case, the histogram reflects more accurately what you would have seen in realtime if you had been looking at the actual 5 minute trix (for example) on the chart. You are no worse off by using the histogram than if you had actually been looking at the 5 m trix, which subsequently repainted itself. 2) If you do anything to cause the histogram to init (like changing the timeframe) it no longer knows what happened minute by minute. Here's an example using the 5 minute timeframe. Suppose you are taking a signal when the 1m fast and 5m fast trix turn the same color. Now in the first minute of the five minute period the 1m fast is red and the five min fast is green. In the second minute price drops enough to turn the five min fast trix red. If you looked over at the real five m trix it would be red. You enter the trade based on the histo signal. Same for the third and fouth minute. But in the 5th minute, there is a big spike up - big enough to turn the 5m trix green for that bar and subsequently stop you out. Well, you already took the trade based on the trix histogram, but if you had looked at the actual trix on the 5 m chart in minute 2 you would also have taken the trade anyway. Now if you refresh the chart (by switching timeframes) all those five bars will be green and you will be thinking " the indicator repainted". However it didn't. The purpose of the histogram is to show you what is happening with the higher timeframe trix on the lower timeframe chart in real time, so that you don't have to go flipping between charts. When the histogram is added or refreshed after the fact it doesn't know what happened in real time. All it knows is that that particular five min bar closed green, so it paints all the 5 bars that comprise it on the one minute chart green if it is added after the fact or refreshed for any reason (including if your mt gets disconnected.) This is, of course true for any timeframe, so if the trix was red for half of a one hour period and green for the second half, and closes green, and you init the histogram on the 1m chart, 60 squares will repaint instead of 5. For example: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) 3) There's a limit to how many bars the histo stores. I think its 750 by default in the old histos. Data before that is not accurate. I have posted other posts about this, you can search for them if you want more info.

--- 帖子 #20148 ---
Price mode is whether the indie uses the high price, low price, close price, median price etc to do its calculations. It made sense to me that it would use the high to calculate the plus Di but why use that for the ADX or the minus Di. The low makes more sense to me for the minus DI, and either the close or typical for the ADX. Possible values are: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4. So that's the difference - the previous version uploaded used the high for all three so I fixed it so that you can choose what you want. The standard mt4 indie uses the close for all three. History just affects the load on your CPU unless you set it to a very small number. TF adjustment means which tf do you want to see it for. 0 means the current chart, 5 means the 5m chart etc.

--- 帖子 #20157 ---
I dont have a system. I use THV, which is a method, not a system and the tools it provides, to which I have added a rainbow as an additional trend filter. Basically I trade when the rainbow and the coral agree on the trend, and I prefer to trade when the 5m trix and 5m rainbow also agree on the same direction. Then I look for THV trades in that direction from one of several setups that I've shared, which you can find by reading my posts. Since there are different kinds of markets you need to adapt the setup you use to the market (for example - is it a new trend just starting, is it a trending market but the waves have a lot of amplitude, is it a very strongly trending one-way market, is it a range bound market, but the range is big enough to get in some waves that provide trades, or is it a completely choppy market?) That's the main trick - like in any profession you need to be able to recognize which tools you need to use in the given conditions. I also base trading decisions on patterns, trendlines and support lines on higher timeframes and use THV signals to confirm a break or bounce.

Attached Image (click to enlarge) But price went down in the next few minutes, and the trix went back at 17:05, and repainted that bar that had closed green to red. --- 帖子 #20183 ---
The original THV method is to trade the 5m chart. When you get a good signal on the 5m chart (price above/below coral and cloud, trix cross in direction of trend, preferably near zero) you then check the 1m chart to make sure it's not overbought over sold. For example, there is a trade signal at 10:55(GMT+2 ) that meets these conditions on the 5 m chart. Price is above the coral and cloud, and there is a trix cross near zero. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then when the bar is complete at 11:00 you go to the 1m chart and make sure that it's not overbought. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Ok, it's perfect, same conditions so you can take the trade. Of course you can accomplish the same thing by just watching the 1m chart with the MTF trix. It's kind of a matter of semantics, whether you want to trade bottom up or top down. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hi Looking at your long entrys you are getting in far too early. Best and most secure trend confirmation is a cross of the fast Trix on the zero level. Based on your long, you entered long under coral and whilst in the cloud. Its probably best is you re-read the manual before procedding so you are fully aware of how to view this system. Also, dont forget to look for convergence and divergence between PA and Trix. Yes. Here is a new version with the digits removed. Please see the following post for helper indies and a description of types. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20144 This version also has some new capabilities. ePeriodType 29 - Like type 28 except ignores if ADX is increasing. Only checks if DI is increasing and DI and ADX are above specified min vals Also you can specify a different period for the ADX value and the DI value. For example the default in this version uses an ADX period of 8 and a DI value of 14. Also you can specify ADX/DI params for each row in the histo.

--- 帖子 #20312 ---
Ok, in this version autotf works for all the eperiod types. If you set useAutotf to true you will get the next two higher timeframes for whatever eperiodtypes you have selected. That is, if you are on the one m chart, row 1 will show 5m, row two will show 5m, row 3 will show 15m and row 4 will show 15 m. (This is to stay consistent with the showing the fast and slow trix for the next two tfs up) If you set useAutotf to true and useSecondAutoTF to true and you are on the one m chart row 1 will show 30m, row two will show 30m, row 3 will show 60m and row 4 will show 60 m for whatever types you selected. See the previous posts for the helper files and explanation of types.

IN THIS ORDER!! 1.) Study and Master Elliot Wave (how you predict the trend, and when might it end?). Only trade during impluse periods (NOOB)... Wave 1, 3, 5, A, Cs..... Trade other waves (MASTER) Waves 2, 4, B 2) Understand Fib retracements and how they line up Elliot Wave Counts (this give confluence) 3) DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY Pivots (These levels are used by the big banks) 4) How does price action REACT to PSY levels.... BIG Numbers ie 1.5 1.4 1.3, middle ones 1.55 1.45 1.35, small boundaries 1.3980 1.3920 (basically every 20 pips) 5) MONEY AND RISK Management (only risk 2-3% of cash per open trades), if you go up 5% on a day (strongly considering stopping), if you lose 10% during your trading day(STOP!!!!!), take 1 day off and do 100 pushups for being stupid. 6) Select Trading System (Master the Entries and Exits) 7) Consider staying away during BIG news days (like yesterday) 8) Managing trades, I like to use the following formula for S/L, T/P, and Trail.... S/L 300% of ATR(20), T/P (1/2 position) at 2 X S/L, and trail remaining position at .75 of S/L..... So 20pips S/L, T/P at 40 pips, asnd trail at 15 pips after reaching 40 pips. At 20 pips move to B/E... 9) Violate these 8 guidelines you will pay those who do 10) Only look at chart during prime hours (0300 - 1400) est. AVOID ALL OTHER HOURS

--- 帖子 #20408 ---
That is exactly what I do, I use the EA to set the basic conditions, then evaluate and place the trade. I Monitor for M1 Trix Slow M5 Trix Fast M5 Trix Slow M15 Trix Fast M1 Cloud M5 Cloud M15 Cloud Once i get a signal, I will then cross check MTF ADX MA Condition M1 Trix Fast S&amp;R Level(Pivots, Trendline Patterns etc etc) The trick is not to set the EA or the Alert to monitor for the full condition or you will always be late to the party. Which is why i do not monitor for the M1 Fast Trix , I look for this manual;y, same with the M15/M30 Slow Trixm depending on the time frame I am looking for. I will repost the EA monitoring setfile on that thread a little bit later. the problem with this is that it chews up lots of resource, it kills a Quad Core 4G Ram depending on the number of pairs you are looking for. Also because it runs as an EA, you cannot run your own trade management EA. What I have been working on is using seller9 indicator ... Ind_AlertV20 on a lot of the pairs. See attached for a template ...apply to a bank chart for the pair you want to monitor. I test using two clients to monitor like this (24 pairs). If you try to use one client to monitor 24pairs it will crash it. I tend to perform a lot of triage, i look for the consolidation and breakout since this gives the most pips, and it is the easiest manage (they tend to go in profit quickly) To work with so many pairs, you need to have a plan, your work space must be set up properly to allow for the most efficient movements. Now it sounds like a lot, the most trades I have running simultaneously is usually between 4 - 7.

Hi Vasi Indicators do not allow for setfiles to be posted. I posted the template above, which configures the indicator with my settings. To take an entry you want the EMA to line up in order 13, 21, 55, 233 this indicates a trend is in place. The take trades based on the direction of the EMA. The consolidation of the EMA which leads to a breakout, I take if i see it happening. The primary purpose of the EMA is to set trend. 13, 21, 55 line up is an absolute prerequisite for taking the trade they must be line up in the correct order and fanning out. The 233 is discretionary based on the other indicators (trix and adx) .

With regards to using the EMA, watching the trend form can be difficult. Bill Williams shifts the EMA for the alligator, to allow use to have a better view of what is happening If you are finding it difficult to see the trend forming, use the following shift values EMA 13, Shift 3 EMA 21, Shift 5 EMA 55, Shift 8 EMA 89 Shift 8 EMA 233 Shift 3

--- 帖子 #20446 ---
I'll post some example of exits tomorrow of trades I'll take in the EU Session, but pull up some of my old charts with the ADX, all lot of them are marked with the ADX used as exit, with details. The basic premise is that you watch the current timeframe for weakness... DI approaching each other, DI crossing .... and wait for this to be reflected in the higher timeframe ADX. Once the Higher Timeframe Di start to move toward each other that is when you exit. With the implementation of the EMA's. Watch the 13 EMA for signs of flatting, this is also as indication that the steam is running out of the current move. That can be use as an exit. The constant narrowing of the distance between the 13 and 21 EMA is a bad sign and you should exit.

--- 帖子 #20474 ---
The 13/21 getting closer is a guide that the trend may be reversing. I almost never use trix for exit (if the trade goes immediately wrong I might look to the trix to get an idea when it may correct in my favor). if all the adx/di is below 25, then you are in a ranging period, you do not trade. Watch the upper and current timeframe, you do not want to enter into a ranging market Remember this is an addon, so it should not replace any of the previous requirements. The adx signals stength, but is slow in high volatility, the MA will detect the trend faster than the adx, Wait for the adx to catch up before entering. You may decide not to use a 3 timeframe anlaysis on the ADX, but you want to ensure that the trend has strength on the current timeframe and immediately above. There are infinite permutations that can be use, the chief idea is to confirm the strength of the move. The trix is an oscillator, so it will at times be contrary to the direction of the move. Entering when both are in the same direction is always better. I rather earn less than loose more, but the rules have saved me a lot

--- 帖子 #20483 ---
See the attached for trade taken earlier on the USDJPY, ideally that is how you want your EMA to look. 1.) In order 2.) Expanding 3.) The EMA themselves are fairly straight (no bumpy) The EMA represents an alignment of the trend, if it all mixed up, then it is indicating to stay out. Notice how you stop loss was minimal, when you get all three timeframe to show the same trend. Here is an exercise... see how many time the EMA on three time frame compress together an open out in one session on your favorite pairs They are the safiest entries to take (when use with ADX and THV rules) and lead to some good pips... you get 2 - 3 of these per pair per session. Even if you take 10 Pips per trade and 2 times per pair and you trade 4 pairs that is 80pips per session with low risk entries. Now I am not saying there is no risk, it is very risky, but the multitimeframe EMA comparison improve your odds

--- 帖子 #20485 ---
Some thoughts on selecting Pairs 1.) Spread is important, but should be taken in context of the overall picture. A nice trend on a higher spread pair I will take, rather than force a trade on the low spread. That being said....stay away from the GBPNZD and EURNZD...those pairs are not for scalping... i jut cannot win consistently on it. Some of you might, i just find it is very hard work 2.) Look at the economic calender and see what pairs have news out in the coming hours. 3.) Try not to overtrade a movement, what i mean is, in the Asian Session the JPY was really moving to a lot of pairs were dropping, the greedy person would have traded the movement of the EJ, GJ, UJ, but you are in effect exposed your self to a high degree of risk for the same movement. Manage the expectation that you have to fully exploit the move. 4.) If you are have multiple trades running, it is a good idea to have a script that can close ALL trades in automatically. There have been times when for some reason I see a swing in the market and trades start to go bad. I just launch the CloseAll script. At that stage I am trying to end up with a good NET position rather than worry about individual trades which may be in profit or lost 5.) You need to prepare yourself for each session, go thru the charts, check up on the news etc etc.... you need a plan that you follow eveyday. Do not launch the application and start looking for a trade. It is like taking a pop quiz and not being in class the day before...

Hi All Here is a new version of the Swiss Army Histo. Please see this post for a description of the types and for the helper indies that go with it. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20144 This version, V4.36 1) Fixes a bug in type 26 (three ma cross + coral). This should have checked when the 3 specified MAs for the period specified were lined up in order and all beneath the coral for the period specified but instead it checked whether they were below the coral for for the chart timeframe. This has been fixed, so now you can use this to moniter whether Tread's ma method is lined up for three MAs plus the coral on various timeframes. 2) You can now specify which pair to monitor - i.e you can watch EURUSD on the USDJPY chart. 3) Includes type 29 - like type 28 but doesn't check if the ADX is also increasing - just the DI. 4) Includes type 30 - Using the params firstlowertype 30 and firsthigher type30, seccondlowertype20 and secondhighertype30 you can check whether the PlusDI on a lower tf is higher than PlusDI on a higher tf and MinusDI on a lower tf is lower than MinusDI on a higher TF and ADX is rising ( and vice versa of course). Green when PlusDI&gt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&lt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&gt; PlusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Red when MinusDI&gt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&lt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&gt;MinusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev,

Another new version of the SA indie. This one 1) Removes debugging comment left in error in prior version 2) Adds type 31. Same as type 26 except uses 4 MAs instead of 3 MAs plus the coral and also checks of the distance between MA 1 and 2 is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3, MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA2 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green.

--- 帖子 #20498 ---
Let me pose some questions, when you enter a trade, where in the cycle are you entering? Is the trend nearing exhaustion, are you at the start of the trend? In the middle? had the major run complete? Are you in a minor swing? Being forced to observe the EMA you get an appreciation for you entry position. To get a bit more specific, you have a brand new trend being formed (major, minor etc), it is being reflected across three timeframes, this to some degree is you edge, you are catching a breakout. Now let me ask you for the trades where all the TF lined up .. how large a stoploss was needed? Of the all signals where the 3 tf lined up, how many failed? In your example 3 trades not taken and 1 lost trade means... 1 lost trade. The point of the ema's is to not just increase probability of success, but to reduce Risk per trade, as in, I an use a smaller stop loss. Trading is not only about growing the capital, it is also about protecting it. The session i refer to is London/US. I typically trade the Asia Overlap/London/US Overlap.. about 12 hours. The best time to trade is the London session. My sucess rate with the adx addon is a bit higher, about 86% on entry. however it has been months since I closed a session in negative pips using the THV. With the ema, I am a little bit over 90. Sed a trader posted a 92% trading just the basic THV, remember tho you still need to look for the basics. support and resistance is critical,

The real question is, what is the traders current sucess rate, and will this method improve his ratio. Never worry about trades not taken. The market will always be there. Worry about your risk and profit. Taking 4 trades that have a 60% chance of winning or 1 trade with a 75%? Okay..small disclaimer here, the % is really subject to the individual trader. Good questions!! Actually the trix cross are very important. In the previous example where I showed the M1, M5 and M15 you would notice that the trade was taken on the M5 Trix cross. So you want to make sure that this still is the case. The EMA sets up the trade, as before, you still pull the trigger when the Trix Cross on M5, ideally i wouldhave liked to have the M1 cross also but it is heading in the right direction, if i had waited 3 minutes the M1 Crosses then and would have been a lot safe (bwtween 2:11 and 2:14 there was a small retrace). I am still using the ADX to monitor for exits. I entered of the M1 ..... as the trade continued, very early in the ADX crossed up a couple of times.. but I was early in trade I monitored the effect of the crosses on the ema. Price retraced but it was not significant. As the trade got older (bar count going up) I switched to the M5 chart and monitored from there. At the trade continues profit grew, now I am watching the ADX on the M15 for the DI approaching each other an the cross occurring om the M5. I would bank the 15Pips... The EMA now gives you additional information so instead of blindly exiting on the ADX rules, you can have one extra piece of information to use as correlation

A simple work flow:- Wait for the compression to occur on the M1 Chart, then wait for it to translate to the m5 and m15... I watch the M1, when it occur I move the chart to the M5 ... and progress to the m15....One i get to a M15 Chart and it occurs there...I switch to the M1 and look for the Trix to line up to take an entry (ADX/THV Rules).That way you have an particular order to your scanning and it will not get frustrating. Do this for 14pairs and no way will you be bored. If you want to push it a bit. i mentioned earlier that the 233 EMA on the higher TF can be ignored

Hi Thread, I read few posts ago that you are interested in the EMA 34, according to Raghee Horner's work. I do use THV system, on which I added this indy, to detect potential huge movements. Actually, I use it also on french CAC40 index, with success. Please find attached an indy that I developed last year, that points out when PA&gt;EMA (34) (high) and CCI&gt;130 or PA &lt; EMA (34) (low) and CCI&lt;-130 An algorithm avoids multiples arrows on consecutive bars. You can adjust the parameters. Here are mine, they help me everyday... Timeframe= 0 CCi_Period= 20 CCI_UP_Limit= 130 CCI_DOWN_Limit= -130 UP_Color= LightGreen DOWN_Color= Tomato About the colors: The first three colors are for drawing the 3 EMA(34) ribbon: (low,close,high) Please note: this indy is supposed to be visualized ONLY IN M5 Regards

--- 帖子 #20554 ---
Which charts have I posted that do not respect the cross, i will advise, some charts i post the end result sometimes an m15 or m5, if the entry was on the M1 you would not see it?, I indicated in earlier post that the cross is critical for entry, it may be the M5 or the M1 or both occurring within a couple of bars of each other is best. I also said that I respect the ob/os.... to be able to respect the OBOS you need to understand what it is telling you. OBOS does not mean do not enter. It indicates that price has a higher probablity of turn above these location. So, we have a trend just starting, an indicator is heading to the OBOS zone on the breakout ... it this confirmation to stay out of the trade or confirmation that the instrument is trending. Remember an extended stay in the OBOS zone means that the instrument is trending. I've just posted 2 trades taken earlier ... one gave 12 pips before reversing and the other 14 pips Trades taken gbpusd entry 13:42GMT exit at 13:55GMt 61 Pips entry 17:06 exit 18:19 48 Pips Over the past 8 hours I took about 9 trades varying between 13 and 69 pips and several of those i added to the trade. Also, the old rules still exist and you can trade those, and just use the ema a guide to the trend.

--- 帖子 #20555 ---
There is a post giving the shift values to add to the EMA. This will allow you to see the order of the EMA easier. The breakout is only one type of entry, you can trade any entry once it satisfies the THV rules..So yes I would re-enter once the thv rules were met. Always keep in mind, the EMA's are there to give you an accurate trend, trading the breakout just gives you a high probability entry The compressed state just indicates that the market is about to start a new trend.The higher Time frames are suppose to support the breakout, but nor necessarily be in a breakout, i do not think i have stated that the EMA on the higher TF be in a breakout.... the EMA's just need to be in order

--- 帖子 #20605 ---
This indicator is based on an idea of Dean Malone's. What he says is that when the HA candles are between the price action channel you shouldn't trade. So this indicator calculates the PA channel (5 period smoothed MA high and 5 period smoothedMA Low) and checks where the HA candle closes in relation to the channel. It's green when the candle closes above it, red, when it closes below it and yellow when it closes in it. Go over to CompassFX and watch his videos on synergy trading to find out more about the price action channel. The MA period is just some code I left in by mistake from the cloud histo. I cant give you the code for this because it is based on the Cloud MTF indicator which is part of THV and Cobra doesn't allow the THV source code to be published.

--- 帖子 #20610 ---
Attached is a indicator that will scan all the major pairs for the EMA to be in the right order It is default to:- MA1 - 13 MA2 - 21 MA3 - 34 MA4 - 55 But you can change it to any EMA you wish to monitor. Note keep EMA in Ascending order if changing values (ie do not put 34, 13,233, 21) keep it in order. The is also a consolidation zone it monitors it is default to:- Channel - 3(Pips) The default colors are: - Green - EMA lined up for long Lime - EMA Lined up for Long and Consolidated Crimson - EMA Lined up for Short Red - EMA Lined up for Short and Consolidated but can be changed It is a bit raw, some error checking needs to be done, but it works quite well so far. Place on any M1 Chart to start using

--- 帖子 #20620 ---
SA histo in Mode 1 lets you select any etype and tf you want for each of the four rows of the histo by setting the values in in the ePeriod1 ePeriod1Type params. Type 5 is the cloud Type 14 is divergence. Type 18 is the chop indie Type 26 is three MAs in order and above Coral. ( ThreeMACrossMA1Per,ThreeMACrossMA2Per, and ThreeMACrossMA3Per set the MA lengths) Type 31 is 4 MAs in order (without Coral) and distance between MA1 and MA2 increasing. For example to monitor the chop indie for the 5m tf in the first row of the histo and divergence on the 30 tf in the second row, set ePeriod1 to 5 and ePeriod1Type to 18 and set ePeriod2 to 30 and ePeriod2Type to 14 Please see these post for more info about etypes http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20144 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20507 http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20509

You got to remember that Trix show momentum and gives short term direction. The whole idea is to stick with the trend, which is why the EMA and ADX (our primary trend tools) are monitored. The momentum will ebb and flow throughout the trade that is a given. Once the trend remains in place, then you are still trading the trend. It also helps going in to know exactly how you will will risk on a trade Also the longer you are in a trade, you need to consult the higher time frames so see what is happening. The big issue is the news , this will blow this thinking out of the water, so plan your entry around you calender. EDIT #: I also take a partial close in my trades.It covers the risk.... After that, I can either break-even or move more into profit. Once it starts moving i may even add to the position. Once I am no longer risking my captial what is there to worry about

Protect you gains and capital. I rather commiserate leaving pips on the table rather than risk loosing it all.

I am working on a dash Board for the THV M1, M5, and M15 time frames which I hope may be useful. It uses a custom indicator to gather all the information and then saves this info to a file which the Dash Board reads. The DB will handle 12 pairs and any combination of alerts on each pair can be selected. Below is a screen shot of the DB as it will look so far, the gray squares indicate which alerts are active for that pair. The DB is not an MT4 product, but rather a stand alone .exe program. You would put the MT4 collector indicator on each chart and the DB program would read each one of these files created and would then use these inputs to determine if there is an alert for anyone of the pairs determined by which alerts you have selected. The collection indicator calculates all the alerts shown and you will be able to select from 1 to 4 MAs to determine the trend. It may be a few weeks yet as I am now working on the code behind the image shown below and then testing. I will post it when it is ready if anyone is interested. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #20702 ---
I'll post it in bit. here is what i think you are missing, and what I went thru also. You are not doing any homework. You know the method, but you are trying to learn on the job so to speak. You need to do:- Pull up and chart from last night, go thru it, so where all the rules were met, mark up the chart with entry/exit etc. do this for as many charts as possible. The objective, spotting the conditions that are profitable. No matter how much you may think you know the method, you still need the learn to spot it. Its like a cricket game. just because I explain the rules (Go West Indies!!) does not mean you can go on the pitch and start batting. Scroll the charts, over and over and over until you can explain why you took certain entries and why you did not on others. I still do this after every session. You biggest edge in this is the ability to spot a setup, and for that you need to do the homework. And trading on demo is NOT homework ,that is playing around and getting ready to loose your money. Knowing the method and spotting the setups is the learning stage.Once you do that then you move to demo,then live. In cricket terms, you are still in the locker room reviewing past games. Demo is practicing on the pitch, trading is like playing the Aussies live in front of 40000 fans in an away match. Yeah ...i get to play cricket today, hence the comparisons.

--- 帖子 #20746 ---
Yes, some pairs are positively or negatively correlated. Now this is not a permanent position, the correlation changes, use this link: http://www.mataf.net/en/tools/01-01-correlation A general rule of thumb for me:- If a currency is falling, do not try to trade all the related pairs. you might as well focus on one pair and use the lots on it. The reason, when the reversal comes you will be stretched thin to close When I have multiple trades open, most of the times they are not connected to each other. So if im i scalping GBPUSD and I see a nice setup on EURUSD, i will not take it.

This is the legend for the MA SCAN Green - EMA lined up for long Lime - EMA Lined up for Long and Consolidated Crimson - EMA Lined up for Short Red - EMA Lined up for Short and Consolidated You can set the consolidation size in Pips, under the Channel input in the properties. However as indicated earlier, consolidation is not enuff. You need to know where you are in over trend before taking a trade. I use the 233EMA and zoom out and watch how the EMA and Price is interacting. Google the 200 or 233EMA to get more information

--- 帖子 #20825 ---
You can create the background using a Webding Font ...use "g" to create the rectangle panel something like this ObjectCreate("ArunDBBackGround", OBJ_LABEL, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0); ObjectSet("ArunDBBackGround", OBJPROP_CORNER, 1); ObjectSetText("ArunDBBackGround", "g", 300, "Webdings"); ObjectSet("ArunDBBackGround", OBJPROP_CORNER, 1); ObjectSet("ArunDBBackGround", OBJPROP_XDISTANCE, 1); ObjectSet("ArunDBBackGround", OBJPROP_YDISTANCE, 1); ObjectSet("ArunDBBackGround", OBJPROP_COLOR, Black); I may have left some stuff out... but that the basic idea

--- 帖子 #20860 ---
As it happens I found something to do. Here is a new version of the SwissArmy Indicator V4.40. Please see the following post for the helper indies it needs and description of the previous types if you have never downloaded it before. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20144 Improvements to this version 1) Added autopair. When true the indie works like it did before - using the pair for the chart it is added to for all rows. When false, uses the pair specified in the 'Pair' variable. 2) Added etype 32. This type checks to see if the MAs specified in MACrossMA1 to MACrossMA4 are in order and are compressed to the width specified by Channel (ala Tread's channel - thanks Tread!). Red when compressed and MA1 is less than MA2, MA2 is less than MA3 and MA3 is less than MA4, vice versa for green.

--- 帖子 #20861 ---

--- 帖子 #20862 ---

--- 帖子 #20863 ---
Red when: - Absolute value of MACrossMA1 - MACrossMA4 is less than the value specified in the channel param (i.e compressed) and - MACrossMA1 is less than MACrossMA2 and - MACrossMA2 is less than MACrossMA3 and - MACrossMA3 is less than MACrossMA4 Green when - Absolute value of MACrossMA1 - MACrossMA4 is less than the value specified in the channel param (i.e compressed) and - MACrossMA1 is greater than MACrossMA2 and - MACrossMA2 is greaterthan MACrossMA3 and - MACrossMA3 is greater than MACrossMA4

--- 帖子 #20987 ---
It's because most who come and leave forever are newbies and it's almost axiomatic that newbies believe they can look at a few charts, make money and within months start checking out the prices of private jets. When they find that they can't they go off looking for another set of charts. If they're thinkers they'll already know that the Internet abounds with charlatans and learn that FX has many of them. If they frequent forums they'll learn to "read between the lines" and realize that some posters have hidden agendas. They'll blow out their trade account a few time, realize what they're up against and start to do some serious studying before they risk their money again. Here's a couple of simple examples of what the retail trader is up against: 1) Major banks have offices in all the major FX capitals of the world with the most advanced computers, programmers and connections available. I know of one US bank that has 12 mathematics PHds on their staff who develop programs to exploit momentary international price differences. 2) I have a number of FX brokerage accounts. I don't use MQL4 brokers for trading but I keep some up on screens because there's so much software available for the MQL4 platform. This morning, for a few minutes before 8:30 AM EST and for 10 minutes afterwards there was a lag, sometimes of over 20 pips on the EU pair between that of other non MQL4 brokers' quotes and that of the MQL4 brokers. Of course some will say that this is a classic example of why one shouldn't trade around news release times. Others may say that it may also be indication of MQL4 brokers' servers being overwhelmed and cynics may say it's the MQL4 brokers manipulating the data. When it comes to FX it pays to develop a cynical streak. Good Luck! PH

--- 帖子 #21007 ---
This is a great example as to why you have to monitor support and resistance levels with any trend-following system like THV. Even when all your indicators line up perfectly, and there has been a very strong trend, you will very frequently see hesitation at major S/R level. There may be hesitation and continuance, or price could reverse, a little or alot. We just don't know so those levels are good for entry when broken and confirmed, and they are also great places to take some profit. BTW, thanks MissPips and Tread for keeping up the thread.

--- 帖子 #21008 ---
My success rate over the previous year was close to 80%. However this is not the only setup that I take. It is possible that you wont see this particular setup during one trading session but there are usually a couple of double rainbow flips a week. If there is a strong trend the 5m may not flip. Then you may have to be satisfied with just waiting for things to get good and compressed and then trading the 1m rainbow in the direction of the strong trend. Of the really perfect looking ones, truthfully I cant remember even seeing one go wrong. Really perfect means that you have - a fresh 5m cross and -a fresh 15 m cross ( not just a failed attempt to change direction but where the trix has actually crossed in the opposite direction and crossed back) and - both trix have a nice distance between the lines and - the trend in the previous direction ended with a recognizable pattern like h&amp;S or double top/bottom with divergence and - you have that pizza pie like shape fanning out on both rainbows with at least three layers visible on the 5m and all layers visible on the 1m and - you are taking the retrace is a a moderate distance and the fast trix is above zero or near it for a short and below it or near it for a long and the slow trix is not in ob (for a long) or os (for a short) or steeply slanted against the trade but preferably flattening out near zero - and the retrace hasnt turned the 5m trix histo against the trade. Now this one doesnt come along that often, most of the less perfect looking double flips also work but so far I can't remember seeing this one fail if all these conditions are met. The reason is that the only way you can get this particular look of having both the rainbow in that expanding pie shape together is when the pair has bounced off of something and then consolidated and then is just starting out moderately but with decent momentum in the other direction. Here's a picture of a near perfect long and short. Notice the differnce in the first screen how the blue double flip in the first screen shot. Even though it works for 10 pips at the point where you take the first retrace of the fast trix you don't have 3 layers of the bottom rainbow showing and expanding. At the point where you do have that the fast trix is already red. Also you dont have a fresh cross of the 15 m trix For the second lot I dont have any set method . I usually trail the stop manually behind where I think the support/resistance is.

--- 帖子 #21010 ---
Hello dear Postiga, It's the defaults in my new version, attached. This version adds the following types ePeriodType 33 - 3 MAs in order (instead of four) Same as type 26 except uses 3 MAs without checking if they are above or below the coral Red when all MAs in order - MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3. Vice versa for green. ePeriodType 34 - 3MAs narrow&amp;expanding Same as type 33 except also checks if the distance between MA 1 and 3 is less than the value specified in Channel and is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green. ePeriodType 35 - DI&amp; min vals Red when minus DI is above plus DI and greater than DI min val and ADX is greater than ADX min val. Vice versa for green. ePeriodType 36 -3MAs narrow Same as type 34 but doesnt check if the mas are expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3 and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green. ePeriodType 37 - 4MAs narrow"; Same as type 36 but for four MAs Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA4 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green If you have never downloaded this indie, please see this post for a description of the previous types and alarm and for the helper indies that go with it. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=20144

--- 帖子 #21061 ---
ahhh. very helpful sir. thank you. edit: i think as a very good tip, as beginners, (like myself), we have to take it one step at a time, otherwise, we ain't ever going to make it. so we need a gameplan. not something that will work for sure. but something that can get us started in a safe way. this gameplan in my opinon, will help newbies a great deal: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STEP ONE ONLY trade using 5m. Take ALL trades anytime you get a trix cross that agrees with the trend on the 5m (for trend: look at the ema's or rainbow. do not trade against it, just like you would not trade against the coral). take a 20 pip TP or 15 pip SL. you'll win some, you'll lose some. you are going to win more than lose. only problem is...the darn spread. so this ain't gonna cut it. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STEP TWO do all of the above, except look at the adx on the same tf. if it looks real ugly, try to pass on those trades. as newbies, we may still take the trade. don't worry, it's still an OK trade. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STEP THREE as time passes, you are pleased that you ain't losing your shirt, BUT you are curious, as you begin to get this feeling that after the moment you enter a trade, you feel helpless in knowing the direction your trade will take in the ensuing 2-4 minutes. after you've done step one and step two for maybe 50-&gt;100 trades, this is the inevitable question you will ask yourself. assuming you are a complete newbie, you would have made at least SOME errors, or like me, many. which means at this stage, you should be in the negative overall (although i truly, truly believe any individual doing nothing else but avoiding trades or liquidating trades before the news and only doing step's 1&amp;2 will be in PROFIT). So step three is, do everything you did in step 1&amp;2, except just b4 entry, flip to the 1m trix JUST to see what it is doing. that's it. don't try to make any meaning of it. just look at it. still take the trade off the 5m as you would in the past. heck you've been doing it all this time and you've been fine, why stop now? but your brain will begin to piece the 1m trix into the context of your trade plan through time. your brain will begin to memorize how 1m trix pictures effect the outcomes of your 5m trades. the 1m is either going to be both red, one red, or both green, not to mention, different heights etc.. it's impossible to post all the nuances of what is going on in the 1m that will effect your 5m. even if all 30 possible scenarios were posted, it still ain't going to help anyone, because the brain has to make meaning of it in a very short amount of time to use the information properly. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STEP FOUR at some stage, it will click, and when it does, the confirmation of the ema's on 15m and 1m and adx off the 15m and 1m adx, and if your good, even the 15m trix will come naturally. at that stage, when you are asked to mentor someone, you will have a hard time. because even you don't know at which point it clicked. This is already your shortcut, as miss pips said, 10,000 hours screen time. but with the help of thv, this is like a super crash course. if you set everything up and have never traded. and move IMMEDIATELY to do step one and worry about nothing else, you will be pleased. you will only lose a little. Now, a complete newbie might think, "i've got an idea...why don't i do step one, two and three all together? after all, step three is pretty easy and will speed things up". you can try, i did, but it confused me. i guess it would be "ok" if you don't try to make any sense of what your seeing, but if you are trying to use step 3 as an added filter to judge whether you should take the trade or not in step 1&amp;2, as a newbie your going to hurt your already slim win rate. you try to do too much, too fast. you end up with nothing. even if your a great looking guy, it's not a good idea to court 3 different girls from the same classroom. if you just focused on one (at least at first), success. you do it all together, it's going to backfire (they might talk amongst)

--- 帖子 #21131 ---
Hi Pumlitch What I can advise is that when taking the trades you want as much momentum on you side as possible. So look to the trix to notice the following:- 1.) Space between the Slow and Fast - The space should be opening between them, but it should not be too far apart 2.) If trading on the M5, time the entry on the M1, on the second trade if you use the M1 to time it you should have seen the trix where moving up signify a counter-move to what was shown on the M5. Once that counter move was completed and the M1 Trix where in the right direction it would have been a good time to enter then. You have have taken that trade and moved into profit almost immediately. On the first trade I would not have taken it as the Coral was still green and heading up. Since you are using the coral for trend direction until the coral has confirmed a new direction you should not trade counter to it.

--- 帖子 #21135 ---
No offense Petar but your screen shots do NOT show the first version of THV or even V3. The MTF trix with histogram you are using to show the 15m trix while trading a 5m chart was modified by me rather later in the game (as was the idea of showing a higher tf mtf trix as a filter on a lower tf chart) . So I think it is safe to say that even you have incorporated some of the improvements after the first version into your trading. Many people, including Cobra, use additional indicators that are not part of the official THV package. Some people can gauge the direction and strength of the trend just by looking at the price bars - others need more graphic reminders. The main idea of THV is to trade with the trend when there is one with good momentum and buy dips in an uptrend/sell tops in a downtrend. Whatever helps the trader see the trend and the dips/tops best is what he/she should use.

--- 帖子 #21229 ---
Ok all, last and FINAL stab at the repaint issue. Here is an example. In the first pic at the red line at 20:26 the 5 m fast and slow trix are red and the corresponding bars for those rows in the histo are red. Attached Image (click to enlarge) I verified that the trix itself on the five m chart matched what you can see on the mtf 5m trix. If you had been basing a decision to go short here at 20:26 to 20:28, whether you had been looking at the 5m chart itself OR the MTF trix on the 1m chart OR the trix histo you would have gone short based on what you saw at that moment. In the next pic, you can see that the 5 m trix has repainted itself green at the red line marking the bar from 20:26 to 20:29. This is because in the very last minute of the 5 minute bar (20:29) there was a large enough up movement to change that bar to green. So the 5 MTF trix and the 5m trix itself closed green for that five minute bar, even though for three minutes of the five it was red. Attached Image (click to enlarge) NOTE THAT THE TRIX HISTO DID NOT REPAINT. IT IS STILL SHOWING YOU WHAT YOU WOULD HAVE SEEN IN REALTIME, WHICH IS THAT FOR 3 OF THOSE 5 MINUTES THE TRIX WAS RED. Between the green bars a similar thing happend though I was not fast enough to catch a screen shot of the trix in a red state before it repainted to green. The trix histo still shows that the trix was red there for those minutes, though the trix later repainted itself to green. (When the trix is flat this can happen a lot, which is why it is best not to trade when the trix is flat). Now here is another screenshot some minutes later. Note that the trix histo is still showing what had been the true situation if you had been making a decision in real time based on the color of the 5m trix at 20:26. No repaint in the histo though the trix has repainted. Attached Image (click to enlarge) And now I have inited the trix histo. Now it matches the trix itself. What do you know? It 'repaints'. This is because when it is added after the fact (or inited) it only knows the final outcome of the bar, and not what happened during each of the (for example) individual 5 minutes that make up the actual 5m bar. However if you had been making a trading decision in real time this is not what you would have seen. You would have seen that the trix was red for three of the 5 minutes. THIS IS WHY YOU CAN NOT USE THIS TYPE OF MTF INDICATOR FOR VISUAL BACKTESTING. Attached Image (click to enlarge) In addition to the above, the trix itself can go back and repaint itself one closed bar back where it is flat as shown in the pics below, which further complicates the issue because this would be another reason that the histo might not match the trix, even if the histo indie had not been initialized. However to the best of my knowlege the histo does not 'repaint' unless it is inited or added after the fact. Even it did (which I do not think that it does) as long as it does show you correctly what you would have seen had you been looking at the higher timeframe trix itself, then it is serving its purpose. Below are some old screenshots showing the trix repainting a closed bar. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) Deathless: I can see from your screenshots that the timestamp on the two versions of the indicator for the UCAD that you are comparing is different. Therefore, exactly like in the example above the values in the histo may differ because one was added at a different time than the other. If you can show me a screenshot where the timestamp is the same and the values differ for closed bars of the histo then I will agree that it repaints although as long as it actually showed you in realtime the true color of the higher timeframe trix at that moment then it's serving its purpose. Note to all the folks who are now about to post screen shots showing that the trix histo bars don't match the actual trix - please make sure that the hot params match. And one last note - in order to reduce memory usage, there is a limit (TrixNoofBars param) to how many bars the histo goes back. So even if you leave it running in realtime it wont show more than that number of bars correctly backwards.

Ah, yes, I've written about it more times than I care to remember. The number of bars depends on the strength of your computer. Stronger - you can have more, weaker less. 750 is about half a day on the 1m chart so it also depends which chart you need. Neither timestamp is 'better'. The point I was making was that since they are different you can't necessarily expect the histos to match since one was keeping track of the trix in realtime and the other was added 'after the fact' with respect to the bars being kept track of by the first.

--- 帖子 #21263 ---
The chop histo is derived from Dean Malone from CompassFx's suggestion that you should not trade a pair when the HA candles on the four hour chart are between the 5 period smoothed MA based on the price high and the 5 period smoothed MA based on the price low. I adapted this as a signal for any time period, not just the 4 hour because when you are trading the 1m chart you can still get trades when the four chart is in the channel but when the 15 and 5 charts are in the channel it's tough. It is red whe the HA candles are below the channel, green when they are above it and yellow (or empty in the case of the SAH ) when they are in it. He also uses it as a signal to trade when the candles are above or below it, though we should wait for confirmation from THV. The code for calculating the values of the chop histo is in this post http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=18526

Aside from Pumlitch comments which are totally right, the news can crucify you. If this trade was being setup in when no news were present you want to look at: 1.) A price channel is existing between 1.40530 and 1.40470, so you want to wait for decisive break out of this channel. 2.) Also, look at how many time the price is breaking the coral in a short space of time, it is showing inconsistency on the trend at that timeframe, you want the price to break the coral and remain on the correct side and show indication of continuing (price expanding away from the coral) 3.) The coral is also green and heading up, which indicates a long trend, so going short against the coral is not a good idea. 4.) Also regarding the Trix notice how the history show small high and lows? This indicates weak momentum, which mean that should you enter, it may not necessarily sustain the entry. My advice is to scroll some of the charts, look at the the areas that gave nice trends and observe how the indicators behaved at that point. Remember, do not try to catch the beginning of the trend as this can be disastrous, with this setup, you want to get in after the trend has established and then take profit of it. So wait till the trend is established. For More Tips check out these post by MissPips http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...65#post3921365 http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...92#post3998192 http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...73#post3389173

--- 帖子 #21356 ---
The SAH is not an official part of THV. I created it so that those traders who like to add an additional filter (whether it be the TDI, stochs, ADX or whatever among the 30 plus choices it offers) can have a way to see that conveniently and get alerts. It is up to you to configure it as you see fit. The various configurations in the various versions are just things that I might have been looking at at the time I released it. Re the TDI go on over to Compass FX and check out the videos by Dean Malone. He has a wealth of info on it. Basically the red and green lines are like the trix lines except the trix is smoother. However the TDI shows you the BB squeeze on the lines which the trix doesn't and also the longer term overbought or oversold relative to 0-100 which the trix does not. Re the ADI search Treads posts - he's posted a few places where you can get info on it.

--- 帖子 #21359 ---
hey misspips or tread, please tell me a little bit more about the channel that you're using for MA's. In SAH default was five. but for what is this used for? if i change tf, must i change the channel too or what? thanks for help and best regards, derox

--- 帖子 #21360 ---
Hi Derox The channel is the Pip Range that you want the MA to exist within. The idea is identify when all the MA are close together. This would imply at a breakout/trend is due to form. So using EMA 13, 21,34, 55 and a channel of 5, mean that when all the EMAs are in within the same 5 pip bracket we would get an alarm. The indicator has the ability to tell when all are in order and in the channel range (like the above) or when not in order yet still in the range. ================= ----------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------- ================== The distance between the the upper and lower green line form the channel the colored lines in between represents the EMA.. The smaller the channel the tighter the range you are looking for. I tend to use a 3 pip range I would post a pic but not close to that computer

--- 帖子 #21362 ---
3xATR(20)SL is broken down this way: 3 times the 20 period moving average of the Average True Range would equal the amounts of pips to your stop loss. If the ATR(20) was 15, your stop loss would be 45 pips.

--- 帖子 #21364 ---
The following are 10 most common but deadly Trading Mistakes, which traders should avoid at all costs. Anyone of them can literally destroy one's financial dreams and goals! 1. Trading for excitement &amp; thrill Not for profits. Many traders consider stock market as casino and trade for thrill and fun only. As soon as one has a losing trade, he wants to quickly make back the lost money. He thinks about the other things he could have done with the money, regret taking the trade and want to recover as quickly as possible. This in turn leads to further mistakes. Be patient and wait for the next high probability opportunity. Don't rush back in. 2. Trading with a high ego. Many individuals who have remained highly successful in other business ventures have failed miserably in trading game. Because they have a fairly big ego and thought they couldn't fail. Their egos become their downfall because they can not except that they would be wrong and refuse to get out of bad trades. Once again, whoever or wherever has any one come from does not concern the markets. All the charm, powers of persuasion, number of degrees &amp; diplomas of business management on the wall or business savvy will not budge the market when you are wrong. 3. Three 4-letter words that will kill you! HOPE--WISH--FEAR--PRAY If you ever find yourself doing one or more of the above while in a trade then you are in big trouble! Markets has own system of moving up &amp; down. All the hoping, wishing and praying or being fearful in the world is not going to turn a losing trade into a winning one. When you are wrong just use a simple 4-letter word to correct the situation-GET OUT! 4. Trading with money you can't afford to lose. One of the greatest obstacles to successful trading is using money that you really can't afford to lose. Examples of this would be money that is supposed to be used in any other business, money to be paid for college/school fee, trading with borrowed money etc. Ultimately what happens is that when someone knows in the back of their mind that they are risking the money they can not afford to lose, they trade out of fear and emotion versus logic and no emotion. If you are in this situation It is highly recommend that you stop trading until you earn enough to put into an account that you truly can afford to lose without causing major financial setbacks. 5. No Trading Plan If you consider yourself a trader, ask yourself these questions: Do I have a set of rules that tell me what to buy, when to buy and how much to buy, not just for the next trade, but for the next 10 trades? Before I enter a trade, do I know when I will take profits? Do I know when I will get out if I am wrong? These questions form the first part of a trading strategy. There simply cannot be any expectation of success if we can't answer these questions clearly and concisely. 6. Spending profits before you make them. Nothing is more exciting then getting into a trade that blasts off and puts you into a highly profitable situation. This can cause major problems however, because this type of trade puts you in a highly euphoric state and leads to daydreaming about the huge profits still to come. The real problem occurs as you get caught up in the daydream and expectations. This causes you to not be prepared to get out as the market reverses and wipes off all your profits because you have convinced yourself of the eventual outcome and will deny the reality of the situation. The simple remedy for this is to know where and how you will take profits once you enter the trade. 7. Not Cutting Losses or letting Profits run One of the most common mistakes made by traders is that they let their losses grow too large. Nobody likes to take a loss, but failing to take a small loss early will often result in being forced to take a large loss later. A great trader is not someone who has never had a loss. Great traders have made many losses. But what makes them great is their ability to recover quickly from a string of losses. Every trader needs to develop a method for getting out of losing trades quickly. Research and learn to apply the best methods for placing protective stoploss orders. The only way to recover from many (small) losing trades is to make sure the winning trades are much larger. After a series of losing trades, it becomes difficult to hold a winning trade because we fear that it will also turn into a loss. Let your profitable trades run. Give them room to move and give them time to move. 8. Not Sticking to your plans &amp; Changing strategies during market hours If you find yourself changing your strategy during the day while the markets are still open, be mindful of the fact that you are likely to be subject to emotional reactions of fear and greed. With rare exception, the most prudent thing to do is to plan your trading strategy before the market opens and then strictly stick to it during trading hours. 9. Not knowing how to get out of a losing trade. It's amazing that most of the traders don't have any clear escape plan for getting out of a bad trade. Once again they hope, pray wish and rationalize their position. It must be kept in mind that market does not care what you think. It does what it does and when you are wrong you are wrong! The easiest way to keep a bad trade from going really bad is to determine before you get in, where you will get out. 10. Falling in love with a stock (Just Flirt). Many traders get fascinated by just a stock or two and look for opportunities to trade in those stocks only ignoring the other profitable trading opportunities. It is because they have simply fallen in love with a stock to trade with. Such tendencies can be suicidal as for as trading is concerned. It may cost any one dearly.

--- 帖子 #21443 ---
I think I see what you want to do, you want to trail your negative stop forward before the +18 is hit. So, the stop moves right with price right from the get go as you entered instead of just waiting to hit +18 before it starts? If so I'm not aware of any borkers that offer that. Would be great though, as this is a great technique for taking risk out of a trade as price moves, instead of putting the trade at BE right away and risking getting stopped out at 0 a lot. Here is how trailing stops work with my borker IBFX, I think most are similar: 15 pip trailing stop. Price has to hit +16 before it kicks in, because it is a 15 pip trailing stop. At +16 , +1 is locked in. So, from there if it backs up 15 pips you are out at +1. If it keeps going it keeps trailing and locking in, at +17 you have +2 locked. I personlly don't use automatic trailing stops, every time I tried them with short term trading they seemed to always just stop me out of good trades a whole lot. And since they don't kick in, until you are in profit, your original SL is in place, so they don't help with the risk end of the trade.

But it also depends where I think we are in the trend . For example in choppier markets there is one trade I look for when there is some reversal pattern followed by a rainbow flip and three lower highs and lower lows ( or vice versa) and then a big enough retrace to make the 5m trix go against the trend. If the 15 trix and 5m adx are still good with the trade and not more than 3 15 m bars have passed since the trix cross on the 15, and the 5m slow is still with the trade or both 5 m lines are against it but going flat then I will trade a trix cross on the 1m in the direction of the rainbow if its the first retrace after a rainbow flip and price is above/ below the coral, and above/ below the rainbow edge. I wouldn't do that more than once per trend though becasue the reason is that that trade happens right after a trend reversal and some people are still trying to buy the dips (if was an uptrend) enough to reverse the 5m trix but not the longer term strength of the reversal and that top that is created by people still trying to buy the dips is often a nice place to enter (in a reversal to the downside) even if the 5 trix hasn't switched back over yet. Like here for example

--- 帖子 #21472 ---
Yes I think that helped. It looks to me like the timestamps in the lefthand corner are different in the two screenshots (though I'm not 100% postive - the old eyes just aren't what they used to be). This means that at some time in between when you took the first pic and the second, the indicator has been initialized either because you switched timeframes, or opened and closed the mt4 or just clicked on the indicator to check something and then clicked ok, or it can even happen if the MT4 looses its connection and then automatically reconnects itself. If the indicator had been initialized then the squares will not match after the init what was shown by the indicator when it was collecting the info in realtime. This is the infamous 'mtf repaint' issue, which you can read about in many of my prior posts.

--- 帖子 #21488 ---
There is a manual for trading the MTF lights that came with V3 and those rules havent changed. The manual does state the correct params and also that these rules were only tested for the 1m EURUSD. I don't know if anybody else has tested them for the GU. The reason that they work for the EURUSD is because it is a behemoth that usually needs a lot of time to turn around so once you get the 1m fast trix and the 5m fast trix supported by the higher tf trixes you can usually get 10 pips. Of course, as has been stated many times, you also have to do your own analysis when you get a signal regarding where you are with respect to pivots, support/resistance, daily range, etc. I devised and tested that system, and I would like to point out that I don't use it exactly the way it is explained in the manual anymore. First of all I don't take those trades anymore if they are against the rainbow trend, only the ones that are with it. Second, at the time I didnt know that there was an mtf trix that you can actually see on the one m chart. Since finding that, I have discovered that some of the 6 lights trades are better than others. For exampe, you get the 1 trix crossing up near a fresh 5m cross with a nice distance between the lines and also near a fresh 15 m cross with a nice distance between the lines, the odds are much better than say, for the fourth 1m trix cross up on the fourth 5m trix cross up for the same 15m trix cross. So I find it pays to be able to see the trixes themselves on the chart. Here is an example. The trade at the first green line shown is one of my favorite setups - 5 trix is newly crossed up, 15m trix is newly crossed up, both in direction of a double rainbow flip, and then you get a signal from the 1m trix. The 1m trix fast up signals just to the right and just to the left of the green line also work because the 15m trix color change is fresh. The second trade at the black line shows an example of a failure. Even though you would have six points here it fails because the 5m trix up part of the signal occurs two far into the 15 m trend and too far after the reversal. More points to clarify: The stops for the EU are 15 pips PLUS spread or ATR suggestion whichever is higher and 10 pips target plus spread or .7 of the ATR suggestion if the stop is higher based on a higher atr. That is plus spread and as far as I can see if you used those then you would have been ok if you went short at 8:30 GMT plus 1. However, you may need to modify the stops if you are trading the GU to adjust for its greater volatility. For either of them you have to take volatility into consideration. The 15/10 stop and target for the EU are based on an ATR in the THV info panel of about 10 -15 which is where it is most of the time during the London session. When that goes up you have to adjust the stops. And lastly, unless you get a very strong signal you shouldnt take a trade right on top of R1.It is better to wait for a break and retest, and then sell the retest. (For me that would mean a double rainbow flip, new 5m trix cross, new 15m trix cross, nice spreads , and even then I'd probably like to see a retest). Attached Image (click to enlarge)

"ye i think the stock exchange data makes the dollar move,hows that exactly correlated?why does the eurusd go the same way as the sp500?" Because foreigners who buy the S&amp;P have to buy USD to pay for it in USD. Even if foreigners have a USD demoninated account they still have to fund it by buying USD. However, remember that just because something correlates doesn't mean that it results in causation. Similarly, neither does it prove it doesn't.

--- 帖子 #21532 ---
Hello iMAG Simply put 3xATR = 3 times the ATR value over a fixed period (typical period are 10,14 or 20). The ATR (iATR(NULL,0,14,0) value is given in decimal values, so you would need to normalize this value to pips (you would need to cater for 4 digit or 5 digit brokers). Example, on the EURUSD and ATR value of 0.0003 would be equal to 3 pips Once you apply the multiplier (in this case the 3x) you can then use this value in your EA . Just search this forum for atr trailing stop to get examples like this

As the day progressed, it would drop from there....maybe averaging 40 to 50% unless something "happens" out there and it would be up near 100%. Background processes typically was around 62. Now I have an additional computer that has fixed all this and some of you may be interested. I won't say what computer I now have because this is not an advertisement for same. Hello vitali, yL = Yesterday Low yH = Yesterday High S1 = Support R1 = Resistance MR1 = Middle Resistance (between two resistance lines) MS1 = Middle Support (between two support lines) FPV = Pivot There is also open line and monthly and weekly S/R on higher timeframes. You can also read TzPivotsD.pdf from the first post in the Manuals and optional.zip file. please try out this site. Maybe you can find other useful information on babypips too. http://www.babypips.com/school/forex-pivot-points.html http://www.babypips.com/school/suppo...esistance.html

That is why I like to use the rainbow and not just the coral to see the trend. If you look at any of the various rainbow templates I've posted you can see that the rainbow hadn't flipped there. I thought PA today was pretty erratic which can happen when you have a day where it is retracing against what has been the main trend because some players in the market still think it's a downtrend and are selling while others think a new uptrend has started and are buying. For example for most of the day it couldn't hold the 15 trix, the 5 m trix and the 1m trix in the same direction with a nice spread, and the 15 m trix was red against the uptrend for a good part of the day. And it spent a lot of time in the chop zone. Personally I find days like this hard to trade and if I dont see anything I like I just stay out. However a few comments: If you look at the screenshot below you can see the difference in how the rainbow looks for the trade that works and the one that doesn't. I didnt take that trade either because I didn't like all that MA support there and the top of the range that it was in last night there at 1.3050. Also if you look to the left of where you took the trade you will see that price stalled there a few times and then went up. There is a Camarilla line there and the 60 EMA from the 1 hr tf right there too. So if you were going to trade there then you would like to see that broken and retested. Also if you look at the screenshot you will see yellow there in the chop zone indie which matches the price action. When you see that you know that somebody big is either accumulating or distributing or the market is just waiting for something to happen. BUT since you are not one of the big boys you dont know which. So it's better to see a decisive move, which you can see when the chop zone rows both turn one color. Also in this case that trade was 20 minutes before a red item news which in my opinion is not a good time to trade. And lastly, I did do a post yesterday afternoon http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=21575 about all the divergence across multiple timeframes and the double bottom at 1.2970 and warn everybody about being very careful with shorts. When you see that much divergence combined with double bottom you really should be careful about not shorting until there is a clear signal that the downtrend has resumed (like at least the 5 minute trend reverses back or maybe a retest of the daily trend line that was broken and a move back down)
