--- 帖子 #21612 ---
Unless you have a proper methodology for entering and exiting the market you will be prone to blowing your account. This cannot be emphasized enuff. You have to have a check list for every time you press that buy or sell. While the thv method is sound and persons can be very successful with it, you till need to develop other areas of strength, S&amp;R, Trendlines, Chart Patterns are all critical. Do not trade THV in isolation. Regarding methodolgy, decidence posted his method a while ago. I advise you to come up with a similar plan and practice sticking to it. For now make sure you have this list posted close to your screen. It may seem childish, but aside from method you also need to learn discipline. In my opinion, your execution should become as mechanical as you can make it, having it in point form will help take some emotion out. Post from Decidence I put together my own trading strategy using THV as my main indicators. Maybe it will be helpful for others as they develop their own systems. Day Trading the THV System Timeframe: M5 ---------------------------- Section 1 - News Check 1. Open http://www.forexfactory.com/calendar.php 2. Note news for the day for the pairs you will be trading 3. Note the times news will be released which will affect your trading pairs and avoid these times Section 2 - The Set Up 4. Move all Chart TF's to H1 5. Note Trend direction, Trend SR's, Overbought/Oversold status and RSI 6. Move all Chart TF's to M5 7. Refer to Rule #5 8. Start looking for trading opportunities that will not contradict with notes taken from Rule #5 Section 3 - Identifying a Long Trade Type 1: 9. Price is above Coral line 10. Previous candle closed above Ichimoku cloud 11. Fast Trix crossed up over slow Trix and both lines are green 12. No upcoming major resistance for at least 25pips 13. Not trading into bearish divergence 14. Not overbought or above 79 on RSI Type 2: 15. Bullish Divergence identified 16. Refer to Rules #9, #12 and #14 Type 3: 17. Resisting Trend Line broken 18. Refer to Rules #12 and #14 Section 4 - Identifying a Short Trade Type 1: 19. Price is below Coral line 20. Previous candle closed below Ichimoku cloud 21. Fast Trix crossed down below slow Trix and both lines are red 22. No upcoming major support for at least 25pips 23. Not trading into bullish divergence 24. Not oversold or below 21 on RSI Type 2: 25. Bearish Divergence identified 26. Refer to Rules #19, #22 and #24 Type 3: 27. Supporting Trend Line broken 28. Refer to Rules #22 and #24 Section 5 - Entering the Trade 29. Before entering repeat Rules #4 and #5 to make sure your position will not break Rule #8 30. Stop loss never more then 15-20pips if 3x ATR(20) is higher this trade may not be worth the risk 31. Risk a maximum 2.5% of your equity per trade ($15,000 equity with 20pip SL is 1.8 lots) Section 6 - Managing the Trade 32. Use your discretion when to get out! You may want to use Trailing Stop if you don't see any major resistance coming for 50pips or so and in others you may want to only pull out 15-20pips profit.

--- 帖子 #21722 ---
To get rid of the o.oooo you need TrendLineBuy and TrendLineSell alerts set to yes and then you need to draw them on the chart using MT4 tools Horizontal Line or Trend Line. Then be sure to rename these lines to Buy and Sell in order for the indicator to read them. You can do this by double clicking the line to activate it and then right click the line to open an edit box. When active the line should have some little squares on it. You can also when active drag these lines around if you like to change their position. Be sure to have only 1 Buy and 1 Sell line on the chart. Sometimes its hard to get the edit window for this line if you have a lot of other lines on your chart to open. In this case right click the chart and open the Objects window and find it there and edit it. The indicator creates the files under Expertsfiles, thats an MT4 function that places them there, I haven't seen that problem. Looking at the top left of your screen I see it says the Data File was updated, so it must be putting it someplace.

--- 帖子 #21740 ---
You need to set up an exclusion rule. I have not use norton in a while but the steps should be along this lines 1. Open Norton Internet Security and select the "Norton Internet Security" tab at the top of the window. 2. Click on "Settings" and then "Auto-Protect" and choose "Configure." 3. On the left pane of the window select "Exclusions." 4. Click on "New" and then navigate to the file you wish to exclude from scanning. After you have added the file click the "Apply" and then "OK" buttons. I think the new versions of Norton allows for Folder Exclusion, so it may be easier. EDIT............. Try this to also navigate to the Exclusion Setup 1.) From the main Norton Interface: Computer Settings &gt; Exclusions &gt; Scan Exclusions &gt; Configure. 2.) In the lower portion of the Scan Exclusions Window under Auto-Protect Exclusions, click the Add button. 3.) In the Add Item window, navigate to the path of your program, such as "C:THVDB" and select it. "Include subfolders" should remain checked. Click OK, Apply and OK your way out.

--- 帖子 #21747 ---
You need to use the MT4 horizontal line tool or trend line tool to draw these 2 lines, you can find these icons to draw these at the top of the chart, these are MT4 drawing tools. Once drawn you then must rename them by double clicking the line to select it and then right click the line for a edit box where you must rename them to Buy and Sell lines. The values of these lines should then appear in the top left corner of the chart if you have them set to true in the Indicator settings. If you don't get any files created in the files folder be sure to check your permissions on that folder, you must have Read/Write rights for these to be created. Right click the files folder and check the properties.

--- 帖子 #21754 ---
I have few questions about the THVDB (1) I haven't got any signal from the THVDB. I wonder to know what kind of alert will be showed and when the alert will be announced? Attached Image (click to enlarge) (2) Should I wait for retest of breaking out support / breaking out resistance and then see whether it's good time to sell/ buy on the dash board? What I have been doing is setting the alerts in the indicator as shown in previous posts. Just before my trade session starts I place my "Buy" and "Sell" lines on the chart. For their placement I look for support/resistance areas. This is a judgement call, use what you are familar with. If the Pair is in a channel set them up for a channel breakout. If the PAIR is trending you may want to use a trend line rather than a horizontal line, its your call. These lines work nice as a filter to keep you out of some of the false alerts. or Trade with the dash board (all light on with same color) and then see any other support/resistance. If not, enter it. I wait for all the alerts I have set up to be Red or Green and then an alert is triggered. You can add or delete which alerts you want to use by setting them in the indicator untill you get a group of alerts and time frames that seem to give you a positive money flow. The alerts only get you part way there, when you get an alert it is up to you to make the final call as to Buy or Sell. (3) Why you simply add Buy &amp; Sell Line on the chart without any other indicator (e.g. trend line, fib level)? Is they must be place before trading hour session? You can use fibs and other indicators on your chart to help you place these lines. Just be sure to name them "Buy" and "Sell", as that is what the program looks for. The DB is only to help you filter trades and also it will keep you from needing to set in front of the computer all the time looking at charts. The DB is just another tool for us novices, if nothing else it has a lot of nice bright colors. Thanks!!!!! Really appreciate for your help!!! Keep going!!! THX![/quote]

--- 帖子 #21799 ---
to summarize, you have TP1 - 9 Pips TP2 - 14 Pips YP3 - 19 Pips You need to make sure that your Trade Size (number of lots) is divisible by the percetages you listed above Lest say that you traded 1lot Size, then the system would close TP1 - 9 Pips - 0.1 lots TP2 - 14 Pips - 0.2 lots TP3 - 19 Pips - 0.3 Lots Then the remaining lots will run this TP or SL is hit If however your lot(Trade Size) cannot be broken down as above, then cave manager will close TP1 and TP2 according to plan and then close the entire trade at TP3. Also make sure that the TP_1st/2nd.3rd Batch Lots Percent is also configured but the percentages aside from the TP_1st/2nd.3rd Pips. Post the set file you are using, so it can be reveiwed

--- 帖子 #21827 ---
I don't really use the lights anymore since I found out about the MTF trix. What I do these days is look at the relationship between the 1, 5 and 15m timeframes, which is similar to the lights but you can get more info by seeing the actual trixes. (I have found that there is a certain 'look' to the colors of the rainbow and the trixes that usually makes for a good trade. In other words I want them to be not only green or red but have a nice spread between the lines and preferably freshly crossed. ) What this 'look' actually is is a certain relationship between the indicators that shows a new trend that is just getting strong enough to go somewhere - i.e when the 5 and 15 m trixes can both hold their colors and a nice spread even though the 1m trix is going against them, then when the 1m trix turns back that's the trade I like, especially if the 5m rainbow is also with the trade or even better newly flipped. This post shows pictures of what I mean. http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=21024 Once a trend flip has been established then i might take a trade based on the 5m fast trix and the 1m fast trix as long as the 15 trix and rainbow look ok - depends on how strong I think the trend is, but really I prefer to look for trades that are retraces on the 1m 'inside' at least 5 m trix cross

--- 帖子 #21833 ---
I am wondering whether there are any defined rules for possible overbought/oversold situations for MissPips's system?

--- 帖子 #21834 ---
No. You need to use your judgement. I tend to think of in more in terms of time that has passed since the higher tf trix crosses and where the trixes are in relation to each other. I like to see a fresh trix cross on the 5 m and if not then on the 15 min. It's like Goldilocks. I don't want trades that are 'too hot' or 'too cold'. This method is looking for the ones that are 'just right' which is usually when the 5 and 15 m trixes have flipped near each other at the point where you enter, or where a 5 m trix flip has gone on for a bit but has led to a fresh 15 m flip near where you enter or a second 5m entry on a 15 m trix where the 5m fast has tried to change color against the 15m direction, has not suceeded and has gone back in the direction of the 15m. We dont want to take trades where it's, say, the third or fourth 5m trix signal for the same 15m trix cross or when when price is near the end of its ADR. I don't look at how overbought or oversold the 5m trix is so much unless both the fast and slow lines are really way in o/b or o/s - like more than 0.0004 But again you need to use your judgement - in a ranging market or for a signal that is against what has been the main daily or hourly trend up to then .0003 might matter whereas in a major panic or in a short covering rally after a breakout .0005 might not make any difference. Same for the 1m. If the 5m and 15m have just flipped together then I don't mind if the 1m is near ob or os because it will have to be in ob or os if the two higher tf trixes are to carry on with their momentum. I don't like to see the 1m in ob or os if the 5 and 15m trixes both flipped 8 bars ago (for example) , and I don't like to see the 1m slow strongly slanted against the trade. I'd rather see it flattening out near zero.

--- 帖子 #21837 ---
SL is 15 PIPS plus spread tp is 10 pips plus spread usually. But if the THV info panel shows an ATR suggestion that is higher than 15 pips then I adjust the SL to that and the TP to 70% of that. That's for EURUSD only - for other pairs you will need to find your own. My reasoning is that the EURUSD moves in about 30 pip chunks at a time. So it shouldnt retrace more than half that if the trade is still good.

--- 帖子 #21851 ---
Well I dont think this answer is going to be that helpful but here goes: Re adding more rows or connecting two indicators see ths post: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...ostcount=12083 The only way to do it is with an EA. Seller9 has one that might fit your needs. I think it also includes the rainbow. I had added the rainbow to the SAH but removed it because it is a real CPU killer and if someone added it to four rows their PC would probably stop . Also I didnt find it that useful because for me the colors themselves have meaning. You can use types 23 (all guppies sloping up or down), 24 (all guppies sloping up or down and in order ), 33 ( 3mas in order) or 37 (4 Mas in order and narrow) as proxies for the rainbow (adjust the MAs and the channel for type 37 say 200, 55 31, 13 for the MAs and make the channel large) Re "Both fast and slow trix" with ePeriodType = 15 I get less alarms with more support from higher tf's but now the trixcross on M5 is often too old to enter the trade." That's a function of reality not of the alarm, i.e a function of where the crosses are occuring in time, not of when the alarm is alerting you. Not all the 5m crosses are positioned well from the point of view of being fresh at the time that they have higher tf support. Re suggestions setting parameters for higher timeframes - cant help you because I only trade the 1m. You'll have to do your own testing. Re deactivating rows not needed - you cant but you can not include them in the alarm using the countetype params. Re little arrows - the indie is limited to 8 buffers as mentioned in the referenced post above and they are all in use. Also an indie can be either in the chart window or in a separate window but not both .If you use alerts instead of sounds you can give each one its own name in the messageid param. I think seller9's ea might have that feature though. Re the other suggestions, yes I see your points and thank you for sharing your ideas. What you have to understand is that I only trade EURUSD and so I don't need a lot of features. In fact I dont even use the alarm since I am watching the pa when I trade except during news breaks. So what I mostly do is if I think I will use an idea I include it in the SAH and if I like it then I share it. But basically I don't take requests for development that I'm not planning to use or at least try out myself anymore. This may seem selfish but otherwise I just get innudated with requests from people who are looking for someone to program their ideas for them for free. I'm not trying to be disparaging of your ideas - its just that I only have so much free time and I'd rather spend my time working on my own ideas than someone elses unless I think that I might use those ideas also.

--- 帖子 #21917 ---
No. I thought about it but didnt for the following reasons: 1) I don't like to see the 1m slow sloping up against the trade and just coming up out of oversold. I like to see it flattening out near zero. 2)I didnt like that the bars were just hanging there far from the edge of the rainbow That is what I think of as 'unsupported' price action because price has gotten too far from the varmas and it usually wants to at least go back to them. I like to see it coming out of a contraction where the Mas have contracted and then it drops below them not hanging below one of those flat levels because those mean a fight is going on and you dont know who is going to win. Usually if you see one of those flat levels forming you need to wait until it's broken and then you can scalp in the direction of the break. Or you can wait for a good retrace and then scalp a trix cross as it starts to go back and take out that level. For that it's best if the 15 m trix is still recently crossed and 5m adx is rising in favor of the trade. Sometimes the 5 trix will be negative. What this means is that there are still buyers or sellers in the direction of the move but they are waiting or a good discount before getting in - one that has been strong enough to move the 5 against the trend but not enough to kill it off. 3)I didnt like that it had just moved 40 pips with no retrace to speak of. Usually it moves in 30-40 pip chunks and then retraces so I though one was overdue. 4) I didn't like that this move was against what has been the main trend for the last days. 5) The main uptrend for the last few days (which is a retrace of the monthy downtrend) has it an area where historically there has been a lot of supply. It's also in the vicinity of the 200 MA on the daily chart. To me that says we are in for some choppiness as it either consolidates and goes further or reverses. Therefore i would like these trades to be perfect looking for this period or I won't take them. (1m trix cross is near zero, near a fresh 5m cross (no more than 3 or 4 5 m bars) trade is near a 1m rainbow flip up after a flip down or vice versa timewise and pipwise.)

--- 帖子 #21941 ---
Yes because even though you dont have both 15 m trixes in favor you have a nice multi-tf divergence there, a nice spread on the 5 m trix and a trix cross near 0 on the 1 and the trade is with the 5m trend and the intermediate trend Rainbow flips are when the colors reverse from warm to cold or vice versa and are in the right order again. The oriiginal rainbow just had layers of color that didnt change from warm to cold so a flip also means when the layers are in order. Also the original rainbow only had 1 tf on it. This one has two - part of the layers from the 5m and all of the layers from the 1m which replace the missing layers from the 5 m so that you can see what is the trend in both those tfs. Fresh flips mean recent with respect to the tf - i.e on the 1 min not one that happened a few hours ago. You can still trade 15 5 1 signals if the flips are not fresh but you will usually get better trades if all the flips (rainbows and trixes) are relatively fresh. The reason is that when this happens price is breaking out of consolidation and you can get a longer run if you are letting an addition lot or lots run. -

Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #21983 ---
Yes. First 9:50 GMT+ 2 was 10 mins before Euro news and personally I find it's best not to trade so close to news. Second, for the classic version of this trade the 15m trix should be crossed above not just near crossing. You might take it when they are both green but not crossed if all the other conditions are excellent (like say a double rainbow flip there and 1m and 5m trix look great), but you have to remember that if you take it when they are just green but not crossed above you can end up with a 'trix failure' where the trix changes color and tries to cross but fails Also when I take this trade I like to see the fast trix coming up from below zero and the slow trix at least flattening out near zero and preferably also turning green. I don't like to see them both angling down sharply while they still above zero with a wide spread between them in that kind of 'wishbone' shape that you see here. When you see that shape it usually means price has further down to go before turning around. Lastly that trade is right on top of the 1440 ema, which is the daily median. As I've mentioned in previous posts, price has a tendency to bounce off that, and so I like to see it broken and retested before entering if the trade is close to it

--- 帖子 #21988 ---
I didnt see a nice looking one either. This setup is trying to get you into a trade when price has compressed, noting agreement and then broken out of that with a lot of momentum so you are trading in a one way market more or less. The Euro has been going up for 17 straight days with no retracement to speak of and yesterday it hit the 68 fib of the recent down move from Nov to Jan. So now it isn't such a one way market any more. A lot of times when you see a day like that the next day will be a reversal day compared to the previous trend or very choppy day because what causes a day like that is that you have sellers selling into the uptrend which is preventing the rainbow and the trixes from looking right. You notice that while yesterday was a big up day it didn't break out of the range and make that move until near London close, and this morning London has been selling also.-*** Edit: when you have a choppy market you wont get this setup. The whole point of it is that we want to trade when the relationship between the trixes is such that the two higher tf trixes hold their colors even when the 1m trix dips and preferably that the slow trix stays around zero during a dip which doesnt happen unless you have a lot of enthusiastic buying and selling

--- 帖子 #22006 ---
[quote=FXler;4377580]Hello seller9, Is it possible that you add another value to the settings under XtrixP1 (also for P2, P3 and P4) like XtrixP1time for minutes? For example if we set it to 5 minutes: The trix cross is invalid when five minutes are over. Try this and see if it works the way you want. I have not tested it so you will need to test. I have enclosed both versions with and without the Rainbow, they have both had the same code changes made to the trix cross. The way the trix cross works now is it will only give a signal at the time of the cross and you can set how long you want that cross signal to be valid with the "XtrixP1-P4time" in minutes. So if you set the time for 2 minutes and you get an either "UP" cross or "DOWN" cross, that cross will stay valid for 2 minutes and no other cross will be looked for in that 2 minute time period. If you want it to be less than 1 minute do it this way, "0.5" for half a minute, be sure to put "0" in front of the decimal point. Hope this works the way you want it to. --- 帖子 #22021 ---
Most traders struggle with number 4. but although the received wisdom is supposed to be that one should never add to a losing trade (I.E. take the loss and move on) for me I think that whilst that may be OK if one is scalping, and THV is supposed to be a scalping system, sometimes it's the wrong approach. The FX market in total is moved by fundamentals and the BIG banks, and the BIG players. So, providing one has read one's cards correctly, for me it makes sense to view say, a stop hunting spike or dip, especially during a period of low volume, as an opportunity to add to my position rather than close it for a loss. A classic example was this past Friday afternoon. All the macro indicators and more importantly the fundamentals pointed to a decline in the EU and I was short. Then, after lunch towards the close, it spiked on a stop hunt and some big players running up the price to add to their shorts - so I did too and came out of it overnight and this Monday morning with 90 pips. The moral of the story, for me, is to look at the big picture. Good Luck! PH

--- 帖子 #22024 ---
If I may say so, newbies shouldn't start with THV. As a beginner, what you need to develop is two things: 1. Market understanding enough to have 2. The discipline to stick to the rules of the system traded Neither is helped by a system that is more complex than necessary, and the Trix readings aren't that easy to interpret without experience and market understanding. Essentially it's a smoothing of OsMA, which is a divergence indicator more than a momentum indicator - at least at first change of colour - and I bet many newbies get bitten entering counter-trend based on such readings. The problem is that the system gives lots of signals before momentum has changed - only the experienced trader is able to filter out the false ones, and even fewer are able to time their trades perfectly. And trading a higher time-frame is just a way of postponing your becoming a trader. Instead, the newbie should trade a system that gives signals only after momentum has changed. In that way the two main skills mentioned above may be developed, after which the trader may use the skills acquired to choose/develop a system that fits his/her perception and mental make-up. DISCLAIMER: The views expressed here are not an expression of personal opinion, but a recommendation to any and all beginner traders following this thread. I get piles of PMs asking for advice, and the recommendations stated here are the ones that would be given to anybody asking about how to make it in trading.

--- 帖子 #22025 ---
This is a point that Cobra, THV's developer, has mentioned several times. In fact, I would add that a newbie should not start out with a system at all. As medici points out, you have to have an understanding of price action and the nature of the market you are trading first, before you even use any indicators. Otherwise you don't really know what the indicators mean. There is no holy grail and you can't make money instantly and sustainably just by following a system. These indicators are tools, and assist you in your buy and sell decisions. If you are new, do yourself a favor and read some books, read some of the threads on FF, and watch countless hours of PA before you even start to trade. If you get in a hurry, you will blow your account.

--- 帖子 #22026 ---
Hi everyone, my first post here. I have to say that I've been testing out THV for almost a year now and it has really augmented my trading. To be more specific, yes the system is very accurate in delivering signals, however it is up to the trader to decide on the quality of the signal in regards to situational factors such as time, s&amp;r levels, the kind of market, recent/upcoming news releases, etc., (the list goes on) which of course you only learn through experience. Yes, a trader with a system learns to become disciplined, unemotional and systematic in their trading style. However just relying on the system alone (i.e. the thought process of "hey it system says I should go long/short now, so I will" without any understanding behind why you actually agreed to make the trade other than "the system told me so" won't get you far! That's definitely similar to just trading blind (pseudo-gambling? lol), but with the guise that you're using a system. Bottom line is that THV has made me more alert during key times in the market (during which the system generates a signal), allowing me to be much more sharper (earlier entries, quicker analytical reasoning) in getting into confirmed breakout trades.

--- 帖子 #22035 ---
Price is king. For a long I like to see higher highs and higher lows and for a short I like to see lower lows and lower highs. If price is making lower lows for a long then something is not right. I like to see normal looking waves, for a downtrend 3 to 5 bars down 1-3 smaller bars up. The point of this particular trade is that I am trying to reduce uncertainty as far as possible by stacking the odds in my favor (like for example when the rainbow hash just flipped and the two longer term trixes are near their flips and there's nothing that I can see in the way, and the market is rising or falling in normal size waves then the odd are it's going to keep going that way for the one more retrace that I need for the 10 pips. If the trixes cant line up together or the waves don't line up right then there is too much dissention in the market about direction and I am more comfortable wating for a better looking trade. What I might do though is look at what caused the lower low (say some MA causing resistance or a fib) and then if that gets broken and if there are fresh 1m and 5m fast trixes that agree then I might enter there. That's just me though 2. In the second case I'd check the guppies If they had flipped then I'd see where price was with respect to the spine. If it was above it and the rainbow had started to flip but not completely flipped I might take it. It would depend how strong I thought the trend was though. If the long signal was just as price was about hit the spine and the trend was pretty strong I wouldn't do it because a lot times price will retrace right up to the spine and then turn around. 3. Usually I just leave the trade. The only exception is that if price tried to break something four times and didn't succeed then I get out because usually it breaks by the fourth try.

--- 帖子 #22057 ---
1) This trade is meant to be taken at the first point where you have the 15 m trix crossed up, the 5m trix crossed up and the 1m trix fast in favor of the trade - which in this case looks to me like it happened on the previous fast trix color change from red to green. There is also a time element to watch out for here. If the first time you get a signal is more than 3-5 bars after the 5 m trix has flipped you should think twice about taking the trade. (Wisdom from Dean Malone) 2) I have tested this trade specifically only for the EURUSD pair. The logic behind it is that this pair is like an aircraft carrier. Once it gets going it with the kind of momentum it takes to flip both rainbows and get all three trixes lined up it usually can't just turn on a dime, so we are counting on that inertia for the 10 pips. I'm not sure how true that is for other pairs. 3) We are also counting on the EURUSD dominating the market which for the most part (with some exceptions like month EC payments at month end and interest rate statements it does). I don't know how the cable was today but the London traders were massively long the EURUSD from the open. That means that the day traders have to get short the EURUSD starting at somewhere about 16:44 GMT+1 in order to go home flat. (For example if you look at the EURUSD pair for that time you see that you dont have a long signal and that it was already turning, and all the dollar buying that involves can affect the smaller pairs, which is why I prefer to take signals on the EURUSD). You can see this happen often about 45 minutes to an hour before the London close. 4) You need to pay attention to the shape of the 1m trix. You don't want to see the 1m trix in that 'wishbone' shape with the fast trix sloping strongly down and the spread between them still widening. You want to see the fast trix flattening out near zero and the spread between them narrowing as in fact is doing at the previous cross up which was the correct entry.

--- 帖子 #22063 ---
It would be correct if the trix was crossed in favor of the trade. But this setup enters (for a long for example) when the 1 m trix has crossed down, not up, so we want the spread to be narrowing as the fast trix turns green not widening. Since we have the two higher tfs in our favor we dont wait for the cross but we also dont want to see the spread widening.

--- 帖子 #22111 ---
Ahh i might've confused people a bit, the reason why I found THV trix called useful on daily is the consistency on the Arrows coming up that leads to 1-3 days of nice trade if the signal's accurate Problem with the Arrow is, it doesnt show up on the Latest candle so you dont know when to enter, the time you see the arrow its already too late to enter. that leads me to believe that the Option on the right hand side that comes up on the daily chart would tell you a nice place to make your entry on the daily basis, hence ive set the trix called indicator to pop up an alert every 00:00 when a signal to short or long comes in. Say midnight of 12th you receive a signal to Short blah blah, you try to open a trade as instructed as close to the Daily open as possible, then Put SL to be the Value of that box that shows 3xATR(20), Using that value then divided by 3 say for an example 3xATR(20) shows a 240, that means what ever trade entered, the SL will be 80 now so if its a Long, SL will be 80 pip below open and if its a sort Sl will be 80 pip above, simples... Leave TP open because you're only gona move SL. Now after a day's worth of trade, if the daily candle you opened ur trade in leads you to a -pip when candle closes Leave SL untouched... however if you have a +pip when candle closes, use the 3xATR(20) value to calculate your new SL, but this time, on the Open of the New Daily candle, hope this helps...

--- 帖子 #22119 ---
i have been testing the various options for managing the stop loss on cavemanager and have reached to the following conclusions: if you plan to use UseLoss_by_Batch or Use_Trail_By_Candle_HL the Stop_Loss option should be set to 0, otherwise in the case of UseLoss_by_Batch the options are never triggered if they are lower than the Stop_Loss value, and in the case of Use_Trail_By_Candle_HL it generates contradicting settings (i could see that the platform alternates between both SL values when this option turns active). so i think that an example of the correct settings for this options should be as follows: UseLoss_by_Batch=1 Loss_1st_Batch_Lots_Percent=70 Loss_2nd_Batch_Lots_Percent=20 Loss_3rd_Batch_Lots_Percent=10 Loss_1st_Batch_Pips=10 Loss_2nd_Batch_Pips=15 Loss_3rd_Batch_Pips=20 Stop_Loss=0 Use_Trail_By_Candle_HL=1 Pips_Behind_Candle_HL=1 Activate_After_Pips=20 could someone tell if my conclusions are correct or if its the correct way to use it? best regards!

--- 帖子 #22120 ---
Capital protection protects your capital when price moves a certain number of pips in your favour without you having to move your SL to breakeven. So if price turns around, the EA will close the trade at breakeven for you. As for NoLossBuffer, you will use this if your broker has bad slippages and you want the EA to take that into account for you when closing trades. You would not use this in normal cases. I would suggest a change of broker if you are always in need to use this option. From what I can see from your chart, it is not the capital protection that took you out. It is the trailing behind price of last close candle that took you out. Cheers, CaveMan

--- 帖子 #22121 ---
Both options are meant for different purposes. One is to contain your losses and the other is to maximise your profits. If you are using UseLoss_by_Batch, it is only right that your hard SL is further away. Otherwise there is no point in setting UseLoss_by_Batch as it will never be activated as your hard/system SL will kick in first. Trailing by last close candle actually move your hard SL for you to maximise your profits. Cheers, CaveMan

I dont think you can really. The SAH uses icustom to call different indies and then calculates whether the light should be green or red based on the current and previous values. --- 帖子 #22224 ---
The indicator has a validate tf function that makes sure that the input is 1, 5, 15,30,60 etc. It doesn't accept 0 unless CurrenttF is true.. You can try setting Currenttf to true and then it wont validate the timeframes. But I think it will just use the chart tf (Period()) for all the rows if you do that. Regarding the other error message - I don't know why you are getting it. If you just use the indicator as an indicator you don't get this message. Usually this message shows up when the trix (or some other indicator), which needs to be first in it's own window, is layered on top of a different indicator, because it is trying to put its own labels and things in the window and it cant find the window because the first window has the window name. I vaguely remember something about getting this error in the beginning of the THV EA thread and solving it by having the EA over there call a very stripped down version of the trix which doesn't but labels or anything fancy in its window. But in this case I think you are calling the SAH with each tick , which, when called also needs its own window in order to place and update its labels, so maybe this is the problem. If it were me, for what you are doing with this EA I would just call the trix directly and not bother with the SAH. I don't know much about EA programming actually. I'm not even sure that you can use icustom to call an mtf indicator that uses icustom itself inside an EA. Maybe they can help you over in the other thead.

--- 帖子 #22230 ---
Mode 1: ===== Mode 1 looks at ePeriod Type, which can be the following types: Type 0 - slow trix Type 1 - fast trix Type 2 - stochs For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) Type 3 - Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) Type 4 - semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) Type 5 - cloud Type 6 - HeikenAishi; Type 7 - TDI (traders dynamic index) Type 8 - AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) Type 9 - AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) Type 10 -Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) Type 11 - Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) Type 12 - Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) Type 13 -Coral Type 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not). Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 21 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is red, empty when none of the above Type 22 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is red, empty when none of the above. Type 23 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction. Green sloping up, red sloping down Type 24 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction, and also in order ( i.e, 3 above 5, 5 above 8 etc, or vice versa) Type 25 - Three specified MAs have crossed and specified stochastics poining in same direction. Type 26 - Three specified MAs have crossed and are above the Coral. Type 27 - Fast trix, slow trix and trix histogram all the same color Type 28 - Treads ADX setup: Green when PlusDI above MinusDI, Plus DI increasing, PlusDI above specified value, ADX above specified value, ADX increasing or red when vice versa Note that ADX , PlusDI and Minus DI price mode values are as follows: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4 This is different from the MTFADX indie Tread released, which uses the high price for all three by default (an error in my opinion because it seems to scew things to the positve side, but you can choose what you like). If you dont care whether the ADX is above a certain value, just that it be increasing set ADXMinVal to 0. Likewise if you don't care if the DI value is above a particular level, just that it be increasing set DIMinVal to 0. Type 29 - Ignores whether the ADX is increasing. Just checks whether ADX is above the specified value, whether DI is above the specified value and whether DI is increasing. Type 30 - Using the params firstlowertype 30 and firsthigher type30, seccondlowertype20 and secondhighertype30 you can check whether the PlusDI on a lower tf is higher than PlusDI on a higher tf and MinusDI on a lower tf is lower than MinusDI on a higher TF and ADX is rising ( and vice versa of course). Green when PlusDI&gt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&lt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&gt; PlusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Red when MinusDI&gt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&lt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&gt;MinusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Type 31 4 Mas in order and expanding shows you when the four selected mas are in order and when the distance between the first and second is expanding Type 32 -4 Mas in order and narrow- Red when 4 MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA4 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green Type 33 - 3 MAs in order (instead of four) Same as type 26 except uses 3 MAs without checking if they are above or below the coral Red when all MAs in order - MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3. Vice versa for green. Type 34 - 3MAs narrow&amp;expanding Same as type 33 except also checks if the distance between MA 1 and 3 is less than the value specified in Channel and is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green. Type 35 - DI&amp; min vals Red when minus DI is above plus DI and greater than DI min val and ADX is greater than ADX min val. Vice versa for green. Type 36 -3MAs narrow Same as type 34 but doesnt check if the mas are expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3 and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green. Type 37 - This is a duplicate of type 32 and has a bug. For future use Autotimeframe =========== When autotf is true, the indicator works like the old trix histo, selecting the next second and third higher timeframes for the fast and slow trix (i.e on a one minute chart, 5m f &amp; s and 15m f &amp; s trix). If use autotf and usesecondautotf are both true, then it selects the fourth and fifth higher tfs for the fast and slow trix. (i.e on a one minute chart 30m f &amp; s and 60m f &amp; s trix) Alarm =========== The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. You will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore.

I acknowledge that in the last six months the world has seen more than the usual number of world shaking events (Japan, the Middle East, the US and the Antipodes) and that six months isn't very long in the FX world but it reinforces the view that one should trade what one sees and not what one thinks or reads. --- 帖子 #22291 ---
No and No. A valid setup is both higher tf trixes crossed and then the 1m fast trix changes color in the direction of the higher tf crosses, preferably together/near a recent rb flip. I personally don't trade 2 hours before and after interest rate statements but that's just me. (I know you can miss big pip days but you also miss whipsaws that way and I figure that if it's really a trend change it will last more than a few hours.) Also these kind of big moves usually mess up the 5 m trix which is what I am used to trading with. You get this big drop in the beginning, so compared to that the 5m trix is green afterwards because momentum slows down even though price is still falling. If you are going to trade this kind of parabolic move you are better off using the 5 ADX which shows direction not momemtum to judge the trend, and using the 1m trix crosses to sell the tops until the 5m adx not longer shows negative direction.

--- 帖子 #22303 ---

--- 帖子 #22304 ---
You need to take into account the higher timeframes and the general situation. For example, when the pair is in a range like it was until the end of last week, then it's good to pay attention to the o/b or o/s conditon of the trix. But if the pair has recently broken out of a range in which (for example) all the higher tfs were overbought, then it stands to reason that in order for the higher timeframes to get back down to a normal range, the lower ones, like the 5m are going to have to get stuck in oversold for quite a while in order for this to happen. (You can see this if you look at the 5m trix for the last three days.) In this type of situation, where you have had a recent breakout from a range at the top of an overbought area, you are better off using the ADX to judge the 5m trend, as mentioned above.

--- 帖子 #22377 ---
Hi all, Here is a new version of the SAH. It has a couple of new types related to the TDI, and mainly, the ability to send email alerts. I have received a lot of requests for this so I am adding it. I don't use this myself, but I have tested it to make sure it works. You will have to configure your MT4 to send emails in the Tools-&gt;Options-&gt;Emails tab in order to use this new feature. IF you have any problems with it, please make sure you attach a screenshot of your MT4 journal tab showing a message that it has sent a test email successfully. Please do not PM me asking for help with problems with this feature unless you have successfully configured your MT4 email option and please do not PM me asking for help configuring your email. (Anticipation of a large number of such requests is the main reason I haven't added this feature before, and I am going to ignore anybody who does this.) If you downloaded previous versons, you will need to download the new TDI indie for the TDI related types to work in this version. If you've never downloaded the SAH please download and compile the helper indies. Mode 1: ===== Mode 1 looks at ePeriod Type, which can be the following types: Type 0 - slow trix Type 1 - fast trix Type 2 - stochs For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) Type 3 - Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) Type 4 - semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) Type 5 - cloud Type 6 - HeikenAishi; Type 7 - TDI (traders dynamic index) + Market sentiment (TDI yellow line) increasing or decreasing for red or green Type 8 - AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) Type 9 - AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) Type 10 -Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) Type 11 - Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) Type 12 - Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) Type 13 -Coral Type 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not). Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 21 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is red, empty when none of the above Type 22 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is red, empty when none of the above. Type 23 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction. Green sloping up, red sloping down Type 24 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction, and also in order ( i.e, 3 above 5, 5 above 8 etc, or vice versa) Type 25 - Three specified MAs have crossed and specified stochastics poining in same direction. Type 26 - Three specified MAs have crossed and are above the Coral. Type 27 - Fast trix, slow trix and trix histogram all the same color Type 28 - Treads ADX setup: Green when PlusDI above MinusDI, Plus DI increasing, PlusDI above specified value, ADX above specified value, ADX increasing or red when vice versa Note that ADX , PlusDI and Minus DI price mode values are as follows: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4 This is different from the MTFADX indie Tread released, which uses the high price for all three by default (an error in my opinion because it seems to scew things to the positve side, but you can choose what you like). If you dont care whether the ADX is above a certain value, just that it be increasing set ADXMinVal to 0. Likewise if you don't care if the DI value is above a particular level, just that it be increasing set DIMinVal to 0. Type 29 - Ignores whether the ADX is increasing. Just checks whether ADX is above the specified value, whether DI is above the specified value and whether DI is increasing. Type 30 - Using the params firstlowertype 30 and firsthigher type30, seccondlowertype20 and secondhighertype30 you can check whether the PlusDI on a lower tf is higher than PlusDI on a higher tf and MinusDI on a lower tf is lower than MinusDI on a higher TF and ADX is rising ( and vice versa of course). Green when PlusDI&gt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&lt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&gt; PlusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Red when MinusDI&gt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&lt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&gt;MinusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Type 31 4 Mas in order and expanding shows you when the four selected mas are in order and when the distance between the first and second is expanding Type 32 -4 Mas in order and narrow- Red when 4 MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA4 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green Type 33 - 3 MAs in order (instead of four) Same as type 26 except uses 3 MAs without checking if they are above or below the coral Red when all MAs in order - MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3. Vice versa for green. Type 34 - 3MAs narrow&amp;expanding Same as type 33 except also checks if the distance between MA 1 and 3 is less than the value specified in Channel and is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green. Type 35 - DI&amp; min vals Red when minus DI is above plus DI and greater than DI min val and ADX is greater than ADX min val. Vice versa for green. Type 36 -3MAs narrow Same as type 34 but doesnt check if the mas are expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3 and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green. Type 37 - This is a duplicate of type 32 and has a bug. For future use New Types: Type 38 - TDI band breakout. Green when the TDI green line breaks out of the blue bands to the upside, red when it breaks out of the bands to the downside Type 39 - Like type 7 but ignores whether market sentiment (TDI yellow line) is rising or falling. This is the original Synergy signal - 7 was a modification of it Type 40 - TDI band squeeze. Green when distance between blue bands is less than BBSqueezelimit param and TradeSignalLine2 is above market sentiment, red when it is below it. Mode 2 ====== Mode 2 ignores eperiod type and sets all tfs to demi classic mode (fast trix above/below slow and above/below zero, but may have changed color against the trade. Mode 3 ====== Mode 3 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to classic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade and above/below zero) Mode 4 ====== Mode 4 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to semiclassic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade but not necessarily above/below zero) Autotimeframe =========== When autotf is true, the indicator works like the old trix histo, selecting the next second and third higher timeframes for the fast and slow trix (i.e on a one minute chart, 5m f &amp; s and 15m f &amp; s trix). If use autotf and usesecondautotf are both true, then it selects the fourth and fifth higher tfs for the fast and slow trix. (i.e on a one minute chart 30m f &amp; s and 60m f &amp; s trix) Currenttf =========== When true, ignores the eperiod and uses tf 0, or the current chart. Alarm =========== The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. You will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore. New Param EmailAlert: Set to true if you want to get email alerts. EnableAlerts should also be set to true and it would be best to leave AlertMode type as 0 (alert on newbar when last bar has closed with a signal) rather than 1 (interbar)

Hi all, I have made another improvement to the SAH. When autotf is false, you can use new tfs: 0, -1, -2 and -3. TF 0 will show you the indicator in ePeriodType for the current chart TF -1 will show you the indicator in ePeriodType for the for the next higher chart TF -2 will show you the indicator in ePeriodType for the for the chart 2 periods up TF -3 will show you the indicator in ePeriodType for the for the chart 3 periods up For example if you want to see the cloud and coral on the 1m chart (when you are trading the 1m chart) and the trix histo (spread between the trix lines) for the 15 and 30 min charts you would configure ePeriod1 = 0 ePeriod1Type =5 ePeriod2 = 0 ePeriod2Type =13 ePeriod3 = -2 ePeriod3Type =12 ePeriod4 = -3 ePeriod4Type =12 If you switch to the 5m chart you will still see the cloud and coral for the 5m chart and you will see the trix histo for the 30 and 60 m chart. This saves having to configure the SAH separately for each tf. Please download the helper indies from the post above.

--- 帖子 #22410 ---
The SAH is mainly so you can get alerts if you want to try something that is not part of the standard THV. For example some people like to trade when the slow trix crosses zero, some when the fast trix does, some when they have confirmation from an additional indicator like the ADX. I never used the THV EA. I personally consider THV to be not a system, but a method, consisting of the following three parts: 1) Identify a trend 2) Wait for a dip in an uptrend or a top in a downtrend 3) Enter when PA comes out of the dip/top and resumes in the direction of the trend. THV uses the Coral ( to identify the trend) and the trix and cloud to identify the dips/tops and resumption of trend, but there are many methods that apply the same principles. However in order for any of them to work you need to be able to identify when the market is trending verses ranging, and where you are in the trend, so that you can buy/sell a good dip/top. (In otherwords, in most cases you want to buy a dip near the start/middle of a trend and you dont want to buy a dip just as the market nears the end of the ADR and is two pips away from a place where there have been pinbar reversals the last two times it got there, and you don't want to buy/sell trix crosses when the market is flat and consolidating or when it is about to enter an area where it is going to consolidate. I think that ability to distinguish between those situations comes with screen time and experience and is very difficult to incorporate in an EA. (Just consider how much money banks and funds have to pay their top traders. If it were possible to write an EA which would consistantly make money whenever it was applied in any market conditions, why would they bother paying for traders. They'd just get the EA and apply it wouldn't they?)

--- 帖子 #22411 ---
It's not possible to make this type of on/off indicator with more than four rows (that I know of) because mt4 limits you to 8 buffers per indicator. In order to get more you either have to write an EA or a dashboard type indicator which can show more things, but not the progression over time. Both selller9 and arunsideas have written those types, if you are not interested in seeing how things are progressing over time. If you ever see one of these types of on/off indicators with more than four rows let me know.

--- 帖子 #22417 ---
I am having trouble understanding your post. 1. Are you saying that the version of the SAH that I requested that you download to a clean chart does NOT freeze your platform? If that is the case, please try some other etypes (0 and 1 for example) but keep the period the same as the chart. If this still doesn't freeze the platform then I think the reason it may be causing your platform to freeze is that you were calling indicators for timeframes that you don't have the history downloaded for. The latest version (previous to the one I asked you to download to a clean chart) was set to automatically look at the 3 higher timeframes up from the chart you used it on. So if you didn't have the history open dowloaded for those, then the platform could freeze while it downloads them for all those timeframes for whatever number of bars in chart you have your mt4 set to and if this is a very large number then that could take a long time. Another reason it could freeze is if you are using a very large number of bars on your chart, even if you already have the history downloaded. The SAH just calls other indicators and some of those are not very efficient, so if you have a large number of bars on your chart and you call a lot of the inefficient indicators then the platform can also freeze, depending on how strong your computer is. The reason that I asked you to download THAT particular version of the SAH is that it looks at only tf 0 ( the chart you put it on), and only calls MAs supplied by MT4 which are efficient. Since this one works, it shows that the problem is not witht he SAH code but either with the history not being downloaded, or with more indicators that are inefficient being called than your CPU can support or that you didn't download the helper indicators that go with the SAH indicator. 2. What is it you want me do look at about the indicator you uploaded? Do you mean that it also causes the m4 to freeze. Then it can be one of four causes 1) You dont have the history for the higher timeframes that it calls (M5 and M15 downloaded) 2) You do have the history downloaded but you have a very large number of bars in your chart . (This isn't likely though because I limited the MTF trix to 750 bars anyway) 3) You have an old computer and a lot of other charts with a lot of history open. This mtf indicator calls the trix four times and the trix is not very efficient so if your computer is old and you have a lot of other stuff open that could be a problem. 4) You didn't download the helper indicator that it needs. The code for this one ( even though I don't have it for V4 ) is very similar to the SAH, so if the problem gets solved for one of them it should get solved for the other.

--- 帖子 #22469 ---
Yes. Thv should work for the foreseeable future because it is based on one of the oldest and most tried and true trading methods: 1) Trade only in the direction of the trend 2) In an uptrend, buy the dips and in a downtrend sell the tops. 3) Enter the trade as price is accelerating out of the dip/top, preferably as it bounces off of something sturdy (like for example a pivot or a nice solid support or resistance line) THV supplies the tools to help you do this (the coral, the cloud ,the trix and the THV pivots), but it is a method, not a system. The trader still has to evaluate whether a trend exists, whether it has enough momentum, whether there is a clear road ahead or one with a big roadblock 2 pips away, whether the daily range has played out and it is therefore not worth entering a trade, whether there is news that could reverse the trend in 5 minutes before placing a trade ,to manage the risk, etc. It is your ability to do this, rather than any given indicator or set of indicators that is the make or break factor here This comes from a lot of time in front of the screen learning how the pair or pairs you trade look/act when they are in a trend vs consolidating in a range, and from knowing through experience/chart reading where they are likely to get stuck or go into free fall. ( Once you learn to 'see' a trend and S/R, then you can do the same THV type trades with about any MA and a momentum indicator of some sort, though the THV trix and Coral are among the better ones. Some people can even do it without using any indicators at all - just by looking at price)

--- 帖子 #22512 ---
If you want to use the chop histo you have to use mode 1. That is the only mode that allows you to see other indicators besides the trix and mix other indicators together with the trix. The other modes just autoconfigure various combinations of the trix as described below automatically for the two higher tfs relative to the chart you are on. These modes are preset - you cant add the chop histo to them. Mode 2 ====== Mode 2 ignores eperiod type and sets all tfs to demi classic mode (fast trix above/below slow and above/below zero, but may have changed color against the trade. Mode 3 ====== Mode 3 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to classic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade and above/below zero) Mode 4 ====== Mode 4 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to semiclassic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade but not necessarily above/below zero) However, in the latest versions I did add a feature that will autoconfigure the timeframe for you for the other indicators in mode 1. For example, if you enter the tf as -1 when you are on a 1m chart you will see the 5 m chop histo and when you switch to a 5m chart you will see the 15 m chop histo. So you can use the following and select the combination of trix/chop that you want. 0 : current tf - 1 : up one tf -2 : up two tfs -3 : up three tfs. If you use this feature make sure you have the history for the relevant tfs already downloaded or your mt4 may hang while it tries to download it.

--- 帖子 #22516 ---
Hi All, Here is a new version of the SAH. Changes: New etypes 41-44. Also cleaned up the interface a tiny bit and tried to improve the documentation. If you have a bug to report or questions about something that is not properly explained in the documentation, I will be happy to answer them and I will try to improve the code/documentation for next time. However please do not PM or post me with questions just because the documentation looks too long and complicated to read or because you haven't completed the prerequisites. The reason the documentation is long and there are many prerequisites is because I have added many indicators/options that people have requested, and if I spend my time answering questions that have already been answered then I have less time to do that. Prerequisites: Please make sure that you have downloaded all the helper indies and history for the timeframes you intend to use or your mt4 version may hang. In addition, before you ask me any questions about the email not working, please make sure that you can demonstrate that your mt4 is properly configured to send email by showing that a test email is working. Modes: Mode 1: ===== Mode 1 looks at ePeriod Type, which can be the following types: Type 0 - slow trix Type 1 - fast trix Type 2 - stochs For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) Type 3 - Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) Type 4 - semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) Type 5 - cloud Type 6 - HeikenAishi; Type 7 - TDI (traders dynamic index) + Market sentiment (TDI yellow line) increasing or decreasing for red or green Type 8 - AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) Type 9 - AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 10 -Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 11 - Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 12 - Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) Type 13 -Coral Type 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not) . Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 21 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is red, empty when none of the above Type 22 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is red, empty when none of the above. Type 23 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction. Green sloping up, red sloping down Type 24 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction, and also in order ( i.e, 3 above 5, 5 above 8 etc, or vice versa) Type 25 - Three specified MAs have crossed and specified stochastics poining in same direction. (Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 26 - Three specified MAs have crossed and are above the Coral.(Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 27 - Fast trix, slow trix and trix histogram all the same color Type 28 - Treads ADX setup: Green when PlusDI above MinusDI, Plus DI increasing, PlusDI above specified value, ADX above specified value, ADX increasing or red when vice versa Note that ADX , PlusDI and Minus DI price mode values are as follows: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4 This is different from the MTFADX indie Tread released, which uses the high price for all three by default (an error in my opinion because it seems to scew things to the positve side, but you can choose what you like). If you dont care whether the ADX is above a certain value, just that it be increasing set ADXMinVal to 0. Likewise if you don't care if the DI value is above a particular level, just that it be increasing set DIMinVal to 0. Type 29 - Ignores whether the ADX is increasing. Just checks whether ADX is above the specified value, whether DI is above the specified value and whether DI is increasing. Type 30 - Using the params firstlowertype 30 and firsthigher type30, seccondlowertype20 and secondhighertype30 you can check whether the PlusDI on a lower tf is higher than PlusDI on a higher tf and MinusDI on a lower tf is lower than MinusDI on a higher TF and ADX is rising ( and vice versa of course). Green when PlusDI&gt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&lt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&gt; PlusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Red when MinusDI&gt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&lt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&gt;MinusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Type 31 4 Mas in order and expanding shows you when the four selected mas are in order and when the distance between the first and second is expanding (Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 32 -4 Mas in order and narrow- Red when 4 MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA4 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green (Uses MACrossMA1 etc nd ChannelWidth) Type 33 - 3 MAs in order (instead of four) Same as type 26 except uses 3 MAs without checking if they are above or below the coral Red when all MAs in order - MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3. Vice versa for green. Type 34 - 3MAs narrow&amp;expanding Same as type 33 except also checks if the distance between MA 1 and 3 is less than the value specified in Channel and is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green. Type 35 - DI&amp; min vals Red when minus DI is above plus DI and greater than DI min val and ADX is greater than ADX min val. Vice versa for green. Type 36 -3MAs narrow Same as type 34 but doesnt check if the mas are expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3 and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green. Type 37 - Ha Candles above/below Coral and cloud. Red when HA candles are below both Coral and cloud, green when HA candles are above both coral and cloud, blank when both conditions are not met. Type 38 - TDI band breakout. Green when the TDI green line breaks out of the blue bands to the upside, red when it breaks out of the bands to the downside Type 39 - Like type 7 but ignores whether market sentiment (TDI yellow line) is rising or falling. This is the original Synergy signal - 7 was a modification of it Type 40 - TDI band squeeze. Green when distance between blue bands is less than BBSqueezelimit param and TradeSignalLine2 is above market sentiment, red when it is below it. Type 41 - Slow trix above/below 0. Red when slow trix is below 0, green when it is above it, with out regard to the slope of the trix New Types: Type 42 - Slow trix above/below 0 and sloping up/down. Red when slow trix is below 0 and sloping down, green when it is above it and sloping down, blank when both conditions are not met. Type 43 - TDI green band is above Market baseline. Green when the TDI green line is above the market baseline (yellow line) red when it is below it, without regard for whether it is also above/below the red line. Type 44. All THV plus OB/OS. Like type 19 except signal is not given if the fast trix is in overbought or oversold. (Uses TrixxxOB and TrixxxOS params where xx is a timeframe like M1 M15 etc) Note: The useHACandles param affects type 5, 9,10,11,13 19, 20,21,22, 25 and 44. When true, the ePeriod types that compare where price is in relation to something such as the Ichimoku cloud or the Coral compares the close of the HA candle instead of the regular close. Mode 2 ====== Mode 2 ignores eperiod type and sets all tfs to demi classic mode (fast trix above/below slow and above/below zero, but may have changed color against the trade. Mode 3 ====== Mode 3 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to classic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade and above/below zero) Mode 4 ====== Mode 4 ignores all ePeriod types and sets all selected tfs to semiclassic (fast trix/above below slow and still in direction of the trade but not necessarily above/below zero) Note: Modes 2-4 only work for the trix. They autoconfigure various combinations of the trix setting for the two higher timeframes, relative to the chart you are looking at. Autotimeframes =========== When the autotimeframe param is set to true, the indicator works like the old trix histo, selecting the first higher timeframe for the first and second rows and the second higher timeframe for the third and fourth rows. (i.e on a one minute chart, 5m , 5m 15m, 15m). If autotimeframe and usesecondautotf are both true, then it selects the third and fourth higher tfs for the fast and slow trix. (i.e on a one minute chart 30m 30m 60m 60m) If you want to autoconfigure timeframes in a more granular manner using mode one, you can set both autotimeframeand usesecondautotf to false and use the following settings in eperiod: 0 : current tf - 1 : up one tf -2 : up two tfs -3 : up three tfs. -4 : up four tfs Alarm =========== The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. When EnableAlerts is true, you will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore. EmailAlert: Set to true if you want to get email alerts. EnableAlerts should also be set to true and it would be best to leave AlertMode type as 0 (alert on newbar when last bar has closed with a signal) rather than 1 (interbar)
