--- 帖子 #22546 ---
There is no emode parameter. There is a 'mode' parameter. If you want to use any indies besides the trix, you need to use mode 1, which is the default. The other modes just auto configure various combos of the trix. Some types have either a red or a green cube, others have either red, green or blank, depending on whether only two conditions are checked, or more than two. For example the ichimoku cloud type has red, green or blank, because price can be below, above or in the cloud. The SAH currently has 44 types of indies or indie combos, but it is limited to four rows. If you need more than four you can use multiple instances of the SAH.

--- 帖子 #22581 ---
In this case, it should give you an alert when the score adds up to three or the score adds up to four, and this may or may not be connected to the third and fourth light - for example the score can be three when rows 1, 2 and four are all green or all red and row 3 is missing from it. The last score refers to the last score previous to the alert being given, not the last alert score. For example the last alert score may have been when three lights were green. Then the SAH may have then dropped to 2 green and 2 red, then gone to all four green. The current score when the alarm is given in that case would be four, but the last score would be 2, not the previous alarm score of three.

--- 帖子 #22598 ---
Hi All, Here is a new version of the SAH. Changes: New etypes 45-50. Fixed duplicate label issue (I hope) Removed all modes besides mode 1. Since there are now timeframes 0 and -1 to -4 the other modes are redundant. You can now use mode1 to auto configure timeframes for any of the indies, not just the trix. Removed Autotimeframe and currenttf params for same reason. Internally recoded some stuff so the exe file is smaller, and hopefully runs faster. If you have a bug to report or questions about something that is not properly explained in the documentation, I will be happy to answer them and I will try to improve the code/documentation for next time. However please do not PM or post me with questions just because the documentation looks too long and complicated to read or because you haven't completed the prerequisites. The reason the documentation is long and there are many prerequisites is because I have added many indicators/options that people have requested, and if I spend my time answering questions that have already been answered then I have less time to do that. Prerequisites: Please make sure that you have downloaded all the helper indies and history for the timeframes you intend to use or your mt4 version may hang. You can get them here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...10#post4788110 In addition, before you ask me any questions about the email not working, please make sure that you can demonstrate that your mt4 is properly configured to send email by showing that a test email is working. Modes: EperiodTypes: ===== Type 0 - slow trix . Green when fast trix is sloping up, red when it is sloping down Type 1 - fast trix Green when slow trix is sloping up, red when it is sloping down. Type 2 - stochs For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) Type 3 - Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) Type 4 - semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) Type 5 - cloud. Green when price is above Ichimoku cloud, red when it is below it. Type 6 - HeikenAishi. Green when HA bars are greeb, red when they are red. Type 7 - TDI (traders dynamic index) + Market sentiment (TDI yellow line) increasing or decreasing for red or green Type 8 - AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) Type 9 - AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 10 -Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 11 - Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 12 - Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) Type 13 -Coral. Green when price is above coral, red when it is below it. Type 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not) . Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 21 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is red, empty when none of the above Type 22 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is red, empty when none of the above. Type 23 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction. Green sloping up, red sloping down Type 24 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction, and also in order ( i.e, 3 above 5, 5 above 8 etc, or vice versa) Type 25 - Three specified MAs have crossed and specified stochastics poining in same direction. (Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 26 - Three specified MAs have crossed and are above the Coral.(Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 27 - Fast trix, slow trix and trix histogram all the same color Type 28 - Treads ADX setup: Green when PlusDI above MinusDI, Plus DI increasing, PlusDI above specified value, ADX above specified value, ADX increasing or red when vice versa Note that ADX , PlusDI and Minus DI price mode values are as follows: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4 This is different from the MTFADX indie Tread released, which uses the high price for all three by default (an error in my opinion because it seems to scew things to the positve side, but you can choose what you like). If you dont care whether the ADX is above a certain value, just that it be increasing set ADXMinVal to 0. Likewise if you don't care if the DI value is above a particular level, just that it be increasing set DIMinVal to 0. Type 29 - Ignores whether the ADX is increasing. Just checks whether ADX is above the specified value, whether DI is above the specified value and whether DI is increasing. Type 30 - Using the params firstlowertype 30 and firsthigher type30, seccondlowertype20 and secondhighertype30 you can check whether the PlusDI on a lower tf is higher than PlusDI on a higher tf and MinusDI on a lower tf is lower than MinusDI on a higher TF and ADX is rising ( and vice versa of course). Green when PlusDI&gt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&lt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&gt; PlusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Red when MinusDI&gt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&lt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&gt;MinusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Type 31 4 Mas in order and expanding shows you when the four selected mas are in order and when the distance between the first and second is expanding (Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 32 -4 Mas in order and narrow- Red when 4 MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA4 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green (Uses MACrossMA1 etc nd ChannelWidth) Type 33 - 3 MAs in order (instead of four) Same as type 26 except uses 3 MAs without checking if they are above or below the coral Red when all MAs in order - MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3. Vice versa for green. Type 34 - 3MAs narrow&amp;expanding Same as type 33 except also checks if the distance between MA 1 and 3 is less than the value specified in Channel and is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green. Type 35 - DI&amp; min vals Red when minus DI is above plus DI and greater than DI min val and ADX is greater than ADX min val. Vice versa for green. Type 36 -3MAs narrow Same as type 34 but doesnt check if the mas are expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3 and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green. Type 37 - Ha Candles above/below Coral and cloud. Red when HA candles are below both Coral and cloud, green when HA candles are above both coral and cloud, blank when both conditions are not met. Type 38 - TDI band breakout. Green when the TDI green line breaks out of the blue bands to the upside, red when it breaks out of the bands to the downside Type 39 - Like type 7 but ignores whether market sentiment (TDI yellow line) is rising or falling. This is the original Synergy signal - 7 was a modification of it Type 40 - TDI band squeeze. Green when distance between blue bands is less than BBSqueezelimit param and TradeSignalLine2 is above market sentiment, red when it is below it. Type 41 - Slow trix above/below 0. Red when slow trix is below 0, green when it is above it, with out regard to the slope of the trix Type 42 - Slow trix above/below 0 and sloping up/down. Red when slow trix is below 0 and sloping down, green when it is above it and sloping down, blank when both conditions are not met. Type 43 - TDI green band is above Market baseline. Green when the TDI green line is above the market baseline (yellow line) red when it is below it, without regard for whether it is also above/below the red line. Type 44. All THV plus OB/OS. Like type 19 except signal is not given if the fast trix is in overbought or oversold. (Uses TrixxxOB and TrixxxOS params where xx is a timeframe like M1 M15 etc) Type 45 - TDI RSI A/b Market baseline BB expanding. Green when the TDI green line is above the yellow line and the blue bands are expanding, red when it is below it and the blue bands are expanding Type 46 - Trix, cloud, coral, TDI yellowband, stochs. Green when price is above the cloud and coral and the TDI yellowband and stochastics are rising. Red when price is below the cloud and coral and the TDI yellowband and stochastics are falling. Type 47 -TDI Fan squeeze. Green when the slope of the TDI green, red and second market baseline are increasing , green is above red, red is above the second market baseline, the green line is above the yellow line and the blue lines are expanding. Red when the slope of the TDI green, red and second market baseline are decreasing , green is below red, red is below the second market baseline, the green line is below the yellow line and the blue lines are expanding. Type 48 - Green when ATR is increasing and plusDI is greater than minusDI. Red when ATR is increasing and minusDI is greater than plusDI. Type 49 - Green when ATR is increasing and price is above the cloud. Red when ATR is increasing below the cloud. Type 50 - Trix Cross. Green when fast trix is above slow trix, red when it is below it. Note: The useHACandles param affects type 5, 9,10,11,13 19, 20,21,22, 25 and 44. When true, the ePeriod types that compare where price is in relation to something such as the Ichimoku cloud or the Coral compares the close of the HA candle instead of the regular close. Configuring auto timeframes =========== If you want to autoconfigure timeframes using mode one, you can use the following settings in eperiod: 0 : current tf - 1 : up one tf -2 : up two tfs -3 : up three tfs. -4 : up four tfs That is, if you are on a one min chart and you set ePeriod to -1 you will see data for the 5 m chart. For -4 on a 1 m chart you will see data from the 60 m chart. Alarm =========== The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. When EnableAlerts is true, you will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore. EmailAlert: Set to true if you want to get email alerts. EnableAlerts should also be set to true and it would be best to leave AlertMode type as 0 (alert on newbar when last bar has closed with a signal) rather than 1 (interbar)

--- 帖子 #22623 ---
The rainbow chart is actually pretty easy to understand. In the one below, representing yesterday, when you see all the green disappear, and all the trixes flip together - go short. When you see a double rainblow flip to the green side after mixed colors, three trixes crossing together and all green look for an awesome trade. The reason is that the only time you see the rainbow look like this is when there is a breakout after consolidation. If you check the 5 m chart you will see that both those trades are where the 5 m consoladation breakout traders would be entering. Sometimes you get a little better entry on the 5 m but most of the time you get the better entry on the 1 m chart . Attached Image (click to enlarge) Its true you can learn to read the price action from bars alone. For me though, its partly psychological - seeing all that green helps me remember never to short that sucker when it looks like that. Here it is on the 5 m chart - but whereas a five m trader might be tempted to short the resistance there at the green line a 1 m rainbow trader would NEVER short anything that looked like the rainbow and trixes look at the green line on the chart. Attached Image (click to enlarge) And here's today (I didnt trade this - my rules prohibit trades 30m before news, but it was a good one). Again, same principles for those to whom the chart is not clear - Double rainbow flip All three trixes crossed down ( in some cases the m1 can have the fast trix in favor of the trade if the angle is right i.e. theslow trix is not too steeply against the trade - TAH's famous 'wishbone' look in the making.) Chart all red. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Again right about where the 5 m consolodation traders would be trading a breakout. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Please,enlighten us. [/quote]

Thought I'd post a loss today on a short and I'm pretty sure I know why - the bigger picture . Despite more than 6 MTF lights on the histogram (initially the first two lights were red, but repainted), a previous trix crossover, and trading with the coral and cloud, the PA decided to move long rather than short. Also, on the 1M chart, using HA candles, you can see that the PA clearly closed beyond the trend line (albeit just slightly). However, in the 15M chart, the candle never closed beyond this trend line using the regular candles. Next time, I need to be more aware of the bigger picture, keeping an eye on any candles that CLOSE beyond the trend line, rather than merely touching it. Also, I can see that the trix immediately looked indecisive despite the cross beforehand, so I probably should give more importance to the current trix movement rather than the previous. --- 帖子 #22676 ---
Well what was right about it was that you took it in the direction of the trend on a fresh m5 fast trix change. Fresh is one of the key things to look for. Unfortunately, on the 15 m chart you had a fresh trix cross up against the trade, bouncing off of a fib extension that had been providing very reliable support, and forming a W or double bottom pattern. So you should think that it's going to bounce up to restest a prior support, and be thinking about entering it on the way back down. The red line on the chart below shows how your 15 m chart looked just before you took the trade. Attached Image (click to enlarge) If the 15 trix is crossed against the trade you should a least wait for a fresh 5 m trix where the 15 m trix is starting to loose momentum, which you can see when the histogram of the difference between the two lines turns back red again as it does a bit to the right. That's the place to enter on a fresh 5m fast trix. The trade you took would have worked out ok if the stop was bigger. But what you have to remember when you are trading the 1m chart is that if one of the two higher timeframes starts retracing, the ATR for a 15m bar, say. can exceed your 1m tf stop. That's why it's better to actually look at the trixes on the two higher timeframes and see what they are doing. Even though I invented the 6 lights method, when I did it we didnt have the mtf trix that you can see. Now, personally I prefer to have the trixes themselves on my charts so I can see what they are doing. For example, If you look at the chart below, you can see that what you actually had where you took the trade has both higher timeframe trixes crossed against the trade, after a double bottom followed by a higher low, which is not very auspicious for a short. Personally, I won't take a trade even if the 5m trix change is fresh unless I see the 15 trix starting to turn in favor of the trade also. And really, I only do that in a strong trend like we have been having lately. When the market is choppy I'd rather wait for a fresh 1m trix change inside a 5 m and 15m trix cross in favor of the trade as proof that a direction is emerging. . Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I've finally read through all 1500+ pages of this thread, and to anyone out there who is considering reading it all then I suggest you do, or at least until page 1000... everything after that (although helpful ) is what I would consider optional, or at least for me anyway. To be honest if you get to page 1000, you might as well go the whole way anyway... there's some great stuff throughout this thread! Basically, what I've discovered about the THV method, which has been often noted by the many veteran traders on this thread, is the necessity of applying one's personality and set of rules to the method. Again, this has been said many times before now, but I believe its important to recongnise that as much as possible. When reading through this thread, I found myself getting the impression from many posters, particular newbies like myself, that this is a "Holy Grail" method of trading, which naturally it is not... or at least not by itself anyway. In order to make this a "near-Holy Grail" method, you would need to apply your own tried and tested method, as well as adopt important fundamental trading principles, such as fibs, trend lines, S/R and so forth. Its so easy to jump into the deep end with this method and get caught out... I know I did once or twice and I'm sure many others did too. In many respects, THV's relative simplicity is bit of a double edged sword... when used correctly by the experienced its a money maker, but when trader's fail to examine nothing other than the trix then it'll kill your account. Again, I know this has all been said before and to many it is common sense, but its so easy to get caught up in this seemingly easy way to make a quick bit of dosh (or "money" if you prefer ) Overall though, if you're patient, analytical, and responsible then this system is fantastic. I've not been trading for very long, but I've gone through many, many systems and I've collected so many indicators (yes, the dreaded indicator hunting!!!), yet I do believe the THV method seems the most effective, at least to my way of trading anyway. In my opinion, the best thing THV teaches you is to look past the indicators themselves and look at the price action. For me, its taught me much about fibs, S/R etc., and ultimately, helped me to realise that indicators aren't everything. Without such fundamental principles, no system would ever succeed. Anyway, sorry for the long essay... just thought I'd share my thoughts after so many pages of other people's thoughts... seems I should only get my own back sometime -Pigeon

--- 帖子 #22716 ---
Thanks for the kind words Well, it's not exactly that I'm no longer using it. When I tested it I just took every instance of 6 lights according to the rules. But after we got the MTF trixes that you can see, then I started to notice that some combinations of 6 are better than others. For example now I think the 15 minute trixes matters more t han I originally thought , and it also matters if the crosses are fresh. So I still trade based on mtf, but I wont trade if there are 6 lights but the 15 min trix has a fresh cross against the trade. (under the old rules you just needed 6 points and only the 1m and 5m fast were required.) And I also examine the higher tf trixes themselves. If a signal is given by the 1 m trix but the change to the 5 m fast trix is 20 5m bars old I'll usually give it a miss. Similarly if there is a fresh 5 m trix cross and the 15 m trix is 20 bars old and weakening and the other higher tfs are in agreement in a strong trend I'd probably take the trade. I also examine the higher timeframes trend and S/R - If there's a really strong downtrend on the hourly even if there is a long signal on the 5 and 15 I might not take it but just wait for the 5 and 15 to agree with the higher tf trend, unless, say, I think it's a bounce after compression off a really solid level of support . So in a way you could say that what I am really doing is trading the 5 m tf when it is supported by the 15 m and the longer trend ( or where I thing the longer trend might change or retrace based on S/R), and using the 1m to time the best entries instead of just mechanically taking a trade whenever there a 6 lights.

--- 帖子 #22822 ---
When using the MTF trix, If you set autotimeframe to true and autotimeframe2 to false you get the next higher tf one period up, i.e on a 1m chart you get the 5m trix If you set autotimeframe to false and autotimeframe2 to true you get the next higher tf two periods up, i.e on a 1m chart you get the 15m trix If you set both autotimeframe and autotimeframe2 to false you get the current tf, i.e. on a 1m chart you get the 1m trix [ quote=DJxtrad;5057369]Please Miss Pips could you tell me why the THV T3 (M5) doesn,t look in my charts the same as in yours? I downloaded the files you sent but it,s looking different ... Perhaps a change in the settings would do? Thanks[/quote]

--- 帖子 #22828 ---
Well basically you can ignore that. I know it's not very user friendly but I use it for debugging. When people have problems or ask me questions about the SAH it helps me to understand what is going on. This message pops up whenever an alarm is triggered. What it saying in the first one is that currently one row meets your criteria, previously none did. You also must have set the alarm on all the rows and the max score to 4. In this case you will get an alert when: One of any of the four rows meets your criteria and in addition subsequently you will keep getting alerts when each of the other three rows meets your criteria. If you only want to get an alert when all four rows meet your criteria, then set maxscore to 4 If you only want to get an alert when one of the rows meets your criteria then set maxscore to 1 and set count Ex (where x is 1 to 4) to true for that row only.

No he wont, because he has the 1st mtf trix set to false false. DJ-If you want to see a chart like I posted, on any tf, you need 1. In the first window - any of the regular trixes that you like (you dont need the mtf trix to see a 5m trix on a 5m chart) 2. (this shows 2 tfs up from the chart you are on.) Or just use the posted template, without changing it, after making sure you downloaded all the indies.

--- 帖子 #22837 ---
Let me try to give an example. Suppose you are trying to catch a trend right at the reversal, and you have noticed that the first thing that happens when a downtrend (for example) reverses is that price crosses the cloud. So your strategy is that you want a heads up when price crosses the could to the upside. You want to add to the trade when price crosses the coral, add more when the 1m fast trix turns green and more when the 5m fast trix turns green (I'm assuming here that you have some other criteria for identifying a reversal like some reversal pattern in price as it bounces off SR, maybe with higher tf divergence). So in this case you would set maxscore to 1 and CountE1-4 to true (where the four rows are the cloud, the coral, the 1m fast trix and the 5m fast trix). So each time you will get an alert (assuming the trend really did reverse in that order). When price crosses the cloud the alert will say the current score is 1, previous score was 0. When it crosses the coral, the alert will say the current score is 2, previous score was 1. When the 1m fast trix turns it will say current score is three, previous score was 2. And finally when the 5m fast trix turns it will say, current score is 4, previous score was 3 (assuming things happen in that order.) On the other hand, lets say that the only trade you are interested in taking is when price is above the coral, the 1m fast trix is green, the 5m trix is crossed up and the 15m trix is crossed up (for longs). So you set CountE1-4 to true, but you set maxscore to 4. Then the only time you will get an alert is when all four of the rows are green and the alert will say that the current score is 4 and the previous score was 3 (or maybe something less than three if several trixes turn together)

--- 帖子 #22882 ---
Installing OpenType or TrueType Fonts in Windows We recommend installing only one format — OpenType, TrueType, or PostScript — of a font. Installing two or more formats of the same font may cause problems when you try to use, view, or print the font. Choose Start &gt; Settings &gt; Control Panel Note: In Windows XP, choose Start &gt; Control Panel Double-click the Fonts folder. Choose File &gt; Install New Font . Locate the fonts you want to install. In the Drives list, select the drive and the folder containing the fonts you want to install. In the Folders list, select a folder that contains the fonts you want to install. ( Make sure you have unzipped them first .) The fonts in the folder appear under List of Fonts. Select the fonts to install. To select more than one font, hold down the CTRL key and click each font. To copy the fonts to the Fonts folder, make sure the Copy fonts to the Fonts folder check box is selected. Note: If installing fonts from a floppy disk or a CD-ROM, you should make sure this check box is selected. Otherwise, to use the fonts in your applications, you must always keep the disk in the disk drive. Click OK to install the fonts.

--- 帖子 #22894 ---
I like to trade inside a 5m trix cross when both the rainbows are in the direction of the 5m trix cross. I look for some pattern or patterns that I recognize (like Head and Shoulders, Double Tops or Bottoms Trendline break, S/R break and retest, lower highs and lower lows or vice versa) to confirm that price action is following the trix and then I buy dips or sell tops (when the 1m fast trix turns) I also like for the 15 m trix to be crossed int he direction of the trade, or at least to have both fast and slow just turned the right color for the trade, and I like for at least one of them to have crossed recently. I also like the 1 m trix to be flattening out near zero, or at least not in o/b or o/s. Like this, for example. (Reasons for trade in pic) I actually prefer the 15 trix cross to have a wider spread than this, but in this case since we are in a pretty strong downtrend, and since waiting for the 15 m trix to cross further would mean taking the trade too close to news and to S1 I took it as shown, based on how the rainbows and PA looked. I don't like to see green in the rainbow or the 5m fast trix if I am taking a short trade or red if I am taking a long trade. I also don't like to see a long flat edge to the rainbow where I'm taking the trade because that indicates stronger S/R that needs to be overcome. I like to see the rainbow expanding, and the retraces forming nice orderly looking little arches of a few bars, where price stays below or sticks pretty close to the edge of the rainbow and then closes down below it again. (These are what a little profit taking, that has now resumed in the direction of the trend looks like) I look for 10 pips on the first lot (stop loss 15 + spread) and trail the second. --- 帖子 #22896 ---
You're welcome 1. I use the SAH to alert me to when I have a 5 m trix cross and a 15m cross, and then if I get that alert I watch the screen and wait for a setup. I am more or less at the computer from a bit before Franky open to London close, but there are times when I am watching the screen and times when I'm not. I like to watch the opens, and see how price acts for sure. Then there are other times when I can see that price is going to go nowhere (or nowhere where I want to be trading anyway) for while and then I'll take a break for an hour or so. Learning how to wait for a good setup, and getting a feel for when one is going to materialize soon or not materialize for a while is definitely one of the skills you need to have 2) Re the 1m trix, the right look (usually) is when the fast has gone below zero (for a long) or above zero (for as short), and the slow trix is near zero and flattening out, and you can see the distance between then is narrowing. Also I prefer when this is the first trix dip after the 5m trix has crossed. This is a case of where you have to judge where you are in a trend, and how strong it is. In a strong trend or a good reversal you can get away with a couple of them, but if it's a counter trend that you are hoping will be a reversal, it's better to stick to the first dip inside the 5 m trix cross. 3). From Franky open to London close you will usually get 2-5 setups It varies though. Some days you barely get one, because what can happen is (for example) there is a downtrend, but the buyers on dips are buying enough to turn the 5m trix up, and then the two trixes can fail to agree for most of the day. (This happened yesterday for example. This in itself is usually a warning of a consolidation/reversal coming up) I am happy with one or two trades a day. 4) For the second lot I set it to b/e when I get out of the first and then I trail it manually after there's some dips/tops to put it behind. I usually have an idea where I think price might be going and I'll get out when it get's there if I'm not stopped out first. 5). My stop is 15 + spread. If it stops out it stops out. If PA is looking normal I will stay in a trade. I f it suddenly starts behaving erratically, and the trade has gone against me nearly to the stop and come back to then entry I will sometimes get out at b/e, because it means that the premise of this trade (which is to trade when everyone is in agreement, and just get in on the dips/tops caused by minor profit taking) is not working. Either some news has happened or I have failed to notice some higher tf pattern or SR. If you look at the screen enough, you can see the difference when PA looks like this and when it doesn't. I don't take every setup there is. I like the ones that where the trix 'looks right' and that are combined with some pattern, like I explained in the post above.

--- 帖子 #22923 ---
Those indicators you see at the bottom of the chart are showing you what the trixes on the higher timeframes look like. I originally developed a method for trading based on getting 6 points using two sets of mtf indicators with four rows each and an mtf indicator for the cloud. (There is a manual for using this method on page one). But now I like to actually see how the shape of the trixes look and where they are in relation to the zero line and the o/b and o/s lines so I switched to using the ones you see on the chart you posted. I have posted many examples of how to trade using these - just look at some of my previous posts. Mainly, the idea is to trade 'inside' a 5m trix cross, when it is supported by the 15m being in the same direction, and to look for a good entry inside that 5 m trix cross on the one minute chart. The SAH is better version of the 4 row MTF trix. It has better control over timeframes and better alerts (more granular) and it also incorporates other indicators besides the trix. (Again, you can find it, and an explanation of how it works in my previous posts). People mainly use it to get alerts for when whatever combination they are looking to trade occurs or is about to occur. It is not strictly a part of THV because I have added many other indicators to it. (A lot of people use THV and one other indicator to make their decisions, and I have added a lot of them to the SAH.)

--- 帖子 #22936 ---
Entering the trade before the fast and slow trixes cross is the whole point of the 6 lights method and its variation using just the 5m and 15m trix. What I am doing is trading inside a trix cross on the 5 min chart, when it is supported by the 15 m trix also, and buying a dip on the 1 m chart to get a better entry. A lot of times there will be a thrust in one direction that causes the 5m trix to cross, and then there will be some profit taking, and I'm trying to get a better price by taking advantage of this. Because the 5m and 15 m trixes are crossed I dont wait for the 1m trix to cross, as long as I see that price is stalling, the slow trix is going flat, and the 1m fast trix is indicating that the original move is resuming. This way you usually pick up a few extra pips as opposed to if you wait for the 1m trix to cross. The ADR - no. I tried it but I don't find it to be more helpful than the trix. I don't understand what you mean by thick envelope lines. The vertical bars in that post were because someone asked me to elaborate what I meant about the shape of the trix. So they were pointing out in real time where the trix looked like what I had described.

Yes of course. I look for the usual suspects: Double tops Double bottoms Triangle formations Flags Channels Head and Shoulders Pinbars Divergence Consolidation break Reversal patterns off strong S/R, major fibs, Pivots, Trendlines Then I look for a entry on the 1m that confirms that price is indeed going in the direction we would expect it to, based on the pattern. If you look at my charts you will see that many times I've annotated these patterns as larger waves on the 1m chart. Edit: Here's an example of taking into consideration the larger timeframes Here is my setup. Inside a new 5m trix cross, trixes approaching zero, slow trix going flat. But what's that down iin the corner? Attached Image (click to enlarge) Oh it's this. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Doesn't look so inviting anymore does it? Now, this trade hasn't stopped out yet, and it might still be ok. There is an argument to be made for it since it has broken and bounced off that upper trendline and the yellow area we see here. But why take the chance when there are too many arguments against it. (23 fib, divergence, bounce off of lower trendline that's been holding for days., pinbar on 5 m chart) There are enough setups without taking one that is ambiguous. The only thing that is clear here is that there is going to be a fight between the sellers selling the pivot.the 5m coral, that upper trendline and the yellow area, and the buyers buying bounces off those two trendlines in the H1 chart and the fib. Why get involved when we don't know the outcome. Better to wait until one side wins and then jump on the bandwagon. Attached Image (click to enlarge) And here is the fight. The trade still hasn't stopped out but instead of a quick 10 pips before we can even get the chart annotated we have to put up with a long and suspenseful fight. And we still don't know the outcome - London will probably determine it. Not my cup of tea. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Edit. The original trade turned out ok, but here is where I entered. Looks like the fight has a winner - cloud trend lines and fib broken with momentum, 5m trix crosses together with 15m fast turning back down and 30m trix crossing - result 10 pips in 3 minutes. --- 帖子 #23022 ---
I look for some area that I think it's going to test, like s/r lines, flag lines, triangle lines, trendlines, previous area of compression, etc on the higher timeframes Then I look for price to compress around that area and then bounce or break, preferably with some confirming pattern like H &amp; S, DT DB, pinbar etc. Then I confirm that PA is making higher highs and higher lows or vice versa and that there isn't something in the immediate vicinity of the trade that could block it. (For example if it bounced off a range top, is the range so narrow that by the time it looks like it's getting a trend going it hits the bottom?) Then I look at the rainbow and the higher timeframe trixes to see if there's momentum. I like to see the rainbow colors the right color and the layers expanding so that the aqua or gold layer is visible and I like to see the 5m and 15 m trix in agreement with each other and expanding, not flat. If I see all those things confirmed then I'm pretty sure a new trend is starting and I try to buy a dip/sell the a top 5m trix cross. I prefer that a least one of the higher tf trixes be fresh It seems like a lot to do, but basically I am kind of lying in wait for one of those areas, and then when price hits it and starts reacting I try to follow along with what the market is doing (is it trying to make a DT? a H&amp;S? has it started to make higher highs/higher lows, did it break and retest etc). There's time to do all this because these things take a while to develop and I'm not going to trade without the 5m trix cross anyway Once that happens I get ready to look for a good entry point on the 1m chart. I've posted many chart examples of this type of entry.

--- 帖子 #23059 ---
There is none. Price can only do one of four things Trend up Trend down Consolidate in some pattern and continue the previous trend Consolidate in some pattern and reverse the previous trend If you are already such a good trader that you can tell from looking at a naked screen which of these price is doing ( particularly when it is about to start consolidating and which direction it is going to go in next after consolidation), then, in fact, you do not need THV or any other system.

--- 帖子 #23061 ---
This is a good question. I think something like the framework provided here is important to help people develop a way of looking at the markets, but providing them with a "trigger" - i.e. a repeatable setup that they can use. Making winning trades is pointless if you don't know why it won or can't find the same setup and again and trade it the same way everytime. So for me, I've scalped off a naked 1M chart with S/R, trednlines, etc, but each time feels like more of a guess than a repeatable trade - this leads to second guessing and overanalyzing and of course missing trades. Why I switched to this THV framework is because there are indicators here that do the same thing I'm thinking price will do and then create a a repeatable "indication" to confirm my thoughts and that can be traded consistently. I think of it not so much as a system, but as a framework to apply your mental pattern recognition abilities, your thought processes to to define a repeatable entry and exit to your positions.

--- 帖子 #23067 ---
What highlighted part are you talking about? As for what I look for, my first mentor told me this - "get very good at drawing horizontal lines on your chart". That's all he uses to trade. He has a 30 minute, a 5 minute, and a 1 minute of multiple securities up and just draws horizontal lines (and also has a well tuned perception of the supply and demand forces behind those horizontal line levels). So a large part of what I think about is that. Its always stuck with me despite me choosing a much different ultimate style. But this is the thought - at each horizontal line drawn from a previous significant meaningful high or low, something is going to happen with the price. Either its going to move through it or be stopped at it. Its up to you to decide how you will know that happens. That is where I like THV indi's. It provides me with a consistent approach to entering a trade at a decision point like that. There were a number of double tops/double bottoms on the chart Friday. While THV (mostly the cloud and a fast trix color change) will get you in a little later, its more of a secure entry than just trading as soon as you see price hit a horizontal level. One other thing to think of, and this is more symbolic of the THV cloud is trendlines. Just as people draw trendlines on a 4hr chart or daily chart, you can do that on a 1 minute chart. Price will break through them ultimately and that usually indicates a reversal. My FAVORITE trade and sort of my 100% take it anytime it happens is this - price has been heading down, it makes a bottom and crosses up throug the downwards trendline - you don't trade here because price often moves back down to the trendline from the other side (trendline resistance into support). If this is at the same location as that previous low it made, its beyond a high probability trade. I've attached an image of this although its a short, not a long, but same concept. Notice that the trendline broke and was retested, and went short. Then retested again at the previous high. Two scalp trades right there for 5 pips at least each. If you took the stochastic overbought buy with the coral direction on the leg up that's another 5 pips. 15 pips in about 10 minutes if trade perfectly. I'm far from that, but I'm getting to the point where I can do 1 out of those 3 consistenly, 2 out of 3 occasionally. 3 out of 3, I end up making an ass out of myself.... someday Also take note how the THV cloud is fairly representative of the trendline. Its like an auto, dynamic trendline in my mind. Anyway, those are my thoughts for now. I got rid of that BBMACD, I can't make it relate to how I trade. A simple 14,3,3 stochastic traded in the direction of the coral is almost perfect. The second example is a little off topic because it has nothing to do with THV, but it shows you the trendline break strucutre I'm talking about. (Look at that beautiful head and shoulders - this is a 1 minute chart - up on the top highlighted box) There's an ebook probably obtainable for free called Rapid Forex - its from some mass marketer guy, but the ebook is about trendline scalping is actually quite insightful.

--- 帖子 #23096 ---
hi thx but what the aim of this new version? has it be tested better than the trix on the V4 version? are the settings a bit different tha, the traditional V4, so entry can be not the same? thx in advance, the trix is very decisive in the system

--- 帖子 #23097 ---
It's so you can see higher timeframe trixes on your chart, if you like to trade that way. For example I like to trade on the one minute chart, but I look for setups after there is a trix cross on the 5 minute chart. The default hot param is like v4 but you can change it if you like. The improvements in this version are just the addition of o/b and o/s levels that suit the timeframe of the trix you choose to show, and a better way to select which higher timeframe trix you are looking at.

--- 帖子 #23214 ---
The only part of the standard Ichimoku that is used on the v4 template is the Kumo cloud, (see colors tab) with parameters 2, 3 and 5 (parameters tab). This makes the cloud very thin and allows possible breakouts to be identified much earlier. The parameters on the standard version are 9, 26 and 52 which makes for a much deeper cloud.which eliminates more false breakouts. So Toranaga San is completely correct - it is the same.

--- 帖子 #23231 ---
Hello Isolanki, I cannot answer this question on behalf of cobraforex, so I will just give you my personal thoughts. I am not sure if you are experienced in how computer languages work, but to get a program to work you need the source code (the code the program was written in, using English words) which is then automatically complied (translated into computer language) by the Metratrader application. So, for MT4, the source code would be program_name.MQ4 which is then complied to program_name.EX4. With MT5 it will be program_name.MQ5 which is complied to program_name.EX5. Now, cobraforex and the other programmers who developed the system have not put the source code on this site, which is entirely fair, since it was their efforts that developed the system, and they do not want other people to copy it and sell it on to users. So, in my view there will be at least 3 or 4 solutions to the problem. 1. I really do not believe that MT4 will disappear overnight, and I think that many brokers will continue to offer MT4 for a considerable period of time. You might possibly have to switch to a broker that continues to offer MT4, however. 2. Cobraforex and others may be willing to generously contribute their time to translate the project to MT5. Perhaps you could go on to cobraforex's site and ask him, very very nicely, if he has any plans to translate the system to MT5. 3. If we take the bare essentials of the application, it consists of Ichimoku Kumo cloud, TRIX and Cobra indicators. In fact the source code for Ichimoku and Trix is in the public domain, that is the source code is freely available in MQ4 and the code is already available for MQ5 as well. The source code for the Cobra indicator is not available, but I think it could be replaced with some other long term trend indicator, where the code is available in MQ5. So, this means that a competent Metratrader programmer could produce an MT5 system fairly quickly. It would not be as good as this system, it would not have all the functionality, and it would not look so professional, but it could be used for trading purposes. 4. The guys at Pipware may also have some plans to produce a MT5 version, and again, you might like to ask them, very very nicely if they have any plans to do this. "Sorry" for the length of my reply, but it is a subject of some importance in the long term.

--- 帖子 #23238 ---
I also can't speak for Cobra - it's his system and thread. However, actually all the source code for the basics of the system is available. The THV T3 Trix contains the basic code for the Trix, and Cobra published it here in the thread ages ago. It just isn't fancy with changing colors based on the slope of the trix lines, divergence lines and analyze buy and analyze sell notifications. But it gets the job done. The Coral is also here in the thread (see the code for T3 M5 or HelpY), except these also don't change color when the slope of the MA changes. If you need that you can find it in XPMA, type 4, MA length 21, and the code for that is available in FF. The Ichimoku is part of Metatrader - THV just uses different settings. The MTF trix is the same as the basic code for any of the other MTF indies that you see around FF and you can find it in the MT4 codebase. It just calls the trix instead of (for example) HA candles. THE SAH is also the same except it has some other goodies like the ability to mix and match indicators besides just the trix, and better control over how and when you get alerts. Also I don't doubt that with all the millions of users of custom MT4 indicators a solution will have to be found - either by Alpari modifying MT5 so that it is backward compatible, or by providing conversion software that will convert MT4 code to MT5.

--- 帖子 #23240 ---
The SAH is an updated form of the MTF trix. Since this is Cobra's thread, I can't post updates on the first page, so that is why you will find it in my posts and not on the first page. (Also since it provides other indicators besides the trix, it isn't strictly part of THV). The difference between it and the MTF Trix is that by using the SAH you can mix and match different types of indicators (such as the ADX or moving averages) or even different trix conditions ( such as trix divergence or trix lines above/below 0) in the four rows, while the MTF Trix only lets you check the condition of the fast and slow trix on different timeframes. The SAH also provides more control over alerts. For example you can get alerts for any combination of rows, and you can get them intra bar or at bar close. And you can get email alerts, which the MTF trix doesn't provide.

--- 帖子 #23246 ---
Hi Trader2012, I'm speaking purely from memory so I might be speaking complete and absolute rubbish! I think the "problem" is that, for performance reasons, brokers only retain a certain amount of data which can be accessed readily, e.g. 1,000 bars for each timeframe. And I don't think it is easy to download, say 10,000 bars of data from the broker (can't remember why!) Technically, you can download as much data as you want from the Metaquotes History Centre (Tools -&gt; History Centre -&gt; Download) but will get a warning that the Metaquotes data may differ from your broker data. The simple fact is that each broker will have slightly different quotes at each time interval, so you now have a mixture of Metaquotes data and say, Alpari data in your MT4 platform, and this will reflect on the signals you may or may not have seen in the past. In other words, you cannot rely on the mixed data for back-testing. Now if you are really keen on doing this, let me know because some-where on my laptop I have guide on how to merge the data "properly" for reliable back-testing. HTH

--- 帖子 #23247 ---
If you use the SAH instead of the MTF Trix you can use the TrixNoofBars param to control how many bars the indicator goes back. However you should be aware of 2 things 1) The trix is very resource intensive, therefore setting this param to a high number can slow down your MT4. 2) If the reason you want to do this is to 'backtest' please read my previous posts about why you can't use MTF indicators to backtest (unless you leave your computer and MT4 on (and hope it doesn't disconnected) for the entire period you want to 'backtest' - in which case it is really a forward test not a backtest.

--- 帖子 #23252 ---
See this post http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...11#post3923911 and this one http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...24#post3923924 for all the THV 4 indicators without any exe or zip file if you are having trouble with them. See this post http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...55#post4901555 for the latest SAH and this one http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...05#post4864505 for an explanation of how to use it. The SAH lets you see multiple timeframes as well as multiple indicators. It is a more advanced version of the Trix MTF, providing better control over timeframes, indicators and alerts. For example you can get alerts for any combination of rows you want. It also has a better auto timeframe feature. For example, using the Trix MTF on the one minute chart you might use the 1m f trix, the 5m fast trix, the 5m slow trix and the 15m fast trix. Now suppose you change the chart to the 5 m and want to keep the same relationship. Using the Trix MTF you have to reinput 5m f trix, 15m f trix 15m slow trix, 30 m fast trix. Using the SAH, in the first case you input the timeframes as 0, -1, -1 and -2. On the one m chart that showed you the 1m, 5m, 5m and 15m timeframes and when you changed the chart to the 5m timeframe it automatically shows you the 5m, 15m 15m and 30 m timeframes Also you can get more options for the trix - for example some people like to trade only if the fast and/or slow trix is above zero, so I put that in there. Or some people like to trade when both trix lines are the same color but they don't mind if they have crossed yet, so that's in there. Or you can get alerts for when all the THV conditions (coral, cloud, trix) are met. Also you can use other indicators. For example a lot of people like confirmation from the ADX because it confirms direction and not just momentum, so that's in there. Or some people like to trade trix signals after squeezes, so there are a variety of ways find the squeezes, like the TDI band squeeze or the MA squeezes.

--- 帖子 #23260 ---
Re no labels on the SAH. Is your chart background black? If so change the text color to white instead of black. If your chart is not black try zooming out, and if you can see the labels after you zoom out then you may need to adjust the h_shift param so that you can see them at your preferred magnification. For instructions about the options the SAH offers, see this post: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...05#post4864505 If you mean instructions for how to configure it to find the 6 lights setups, explained in the MTF manual, you can configure it the same regarding the etypes (i.e 0 = slow trix, 1 equals fast trix) but for the periods you now use 0 , -1, -1, -2, -2, -3,-3, -4 which corresponds to 1m, 5m, 5m,15m, 15m, 30m,30m and 60m on a one minute chart, but keeps the same relationship between the timeframes if you switch to a higher timeframe chart (i.e on a 5m chart it is 5m, 15m, 15m, 30m, 30m 60m, 60m and 240m). Re has anything changed in my trading On a 1m chart I now mostly prefer to trade 'inside' a 5m trix cross, when it is supported by the 15m trix. I have posted many charts showing this setup. I do sometimes also trade when I get the same relationship on a 5 m chart (i.e the 15 and 30 are newly crossed up and the 5m fast switches to the same color). For me the main key is that I am looking for the trixes (and the rainbow and chart patterns) to confirm a trade for me in an area where I expect there to be one. For example, I will look for an area where I expect good support or resistance, then watch to see if there is a lot of chopping around on the rainbow or if a pattern like a 1-2-3, double bottom or h&amp;s forms, then enter if the trixes and rainbow confirm that a new trend has started. Or else where they confirm that S or R has broken and the trend is continuing. If you mean instructions for how to configure it to find other trade setups, there are none. That is up to every trader how he or she wants to configure the SAH. A few people have been kind enough to share their other configurations, which you can find by reading the thread. Re the THV4 trix, I wasn't part of developing it and don't use it (I don't like the black configuration and the extra bells and whistles. ) I think Cobra and Stratman did it so you might ask them what the bars are for. Or I think you can find an explanation in the thread. I remember that someone did explain it once but I didn't pay attention to who it was because I don't use it myself so I won't be able to find it any quicker than you will yourself.

--- 帖子 #23289 ---
You have it exactly backwards. The trix itself does 'repaint' not only before a bar is closed (which is not really repainting, but if you are making a decision before a bar closes can affect you) but it ALSO repaints closed bars on occasion. See the last two screenshots in the following post. The trix histo (or SAH) preserves the original condtion that the trix was in before it repainted (both legitimately, because the bar was not closed, and illegitimately after the bar was closed) until it is inited in some fashion. However, as you correctly note, the trix histo can't be used for backtesting because when it is added to a chart 'after the fact' it does not show the same info as it would have in real time. http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...06#post4130806

--- 帖子 #23290 ---
Well, I don't advocate using the MTF approach while paying no attention to S/R and trend lines. On the contrary, I advocate using it to confirm that a line is going to 'stick.' This particular setup, which I have shown many times is very successful. Just today you had four of them - all good with 15 p/10 pip (+ spread) SL/TP. And this on a day where the range was about 40 pips. You look for a place where you think a trade will be based on S/R and then you use a simultaneous RB/higher tf trix flip to confirm it's going to stick and trade the first flag/dip (or as close to the flip as you can get with the indicators confirming it) The criteria are: 1) Reversal pattern at S or R (like H&amp;S DT DB or 123) 2) Rainbow compresses and flips 3) 5 m trix flips 4) 15 m trix flips (preferably or at least both the same color as the trade) 5) Trade first dip ( as indicated by 1m trix) 6) Price is above the coral 7) The outer layer of the rainbow is the right color (i.e green for longs, red for shorts).This is instead of using the ichimoku - it is usually more stringent. Check that there is room for the trade ( i.e no pivot closer than 10 pips, if in range the edge should be at least 10 pips away) Invalidated if the first dip indicated by the trixes all lining up is far away from the flips, as can happen when there is a giant move with no retrace) or higher tf trix in o/b or o/s Attached Image (click to enlarge) and the reverse Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #23341 ---
The very latest is v4.76 (just like .75 but removes some debugging code I forgot to remove. The SAH just gives alerts for whatever you tell it based on the indicators you choose. I don't give advice about how to use it. The closest it can get at the moment to the two conditions you requested is alerting you when price is above the coral on the 5 m and when there is a simultaneous trix cross with that, but it doesn't know when the Coral is red or green. There is a chop indicator in it, which is based on Dean Malones synergy method of not trading when price is inside the two bands created by the smoothed 5 period moving average high and the smoothed 5 period moving average low. You can try it and see how you like it. The best way to avoid chop that I know is to learn to recognize when it's going to occur. You're going to have chop whenever there's a range. In my experience there are three times when the market will range. The first is when it's waiting for something such as NFP or a big speech or crisis resolution deal or something. The second is when it goes into a holding pattern overnight and during Asia because the market has made a decisive move the day before, and everybody is waiting to see what London is going to make of it the next day. The third is when it hits a technical area where there 'has' to be chop (in the absence of some crisis driving right though that area.) Those are areas usually where you've been going in one direction for a good while, then you hit pretty strong higher tf support or resistance and get a reversal sign like a double top or bottom. Normally you should reverse with one of those but if, right below (or above in the case of a double bottom) is a pretty strong looking S or R that's going to be defended, then you're usually going to get chop until somebody wins.

The eperiods should be 0 if you only want to see the values for the indicators on the 5m chart, while you are looking at the 5m chart. If you want to see where price is in relation to the coral on the 15 m chart while you are looking at the 5m chart then it should be -1 Or if you want to see where price is in relation to the coral on the 5m chart while you are looking at a 1m chart then it should also be -1 You can combine any types you want as long as you only use one type per row. The entire point of the SAH is to let people experiment with different combinations to see what suits them. In my last post I forgot to mention the other way to avoid chop, which is to wait until there is some consolidation , and then wait for price to break out of it. There are a few types in the SAH that show that pretty well like 34 and 38.

Prerequisites: Please make sure that you have downloaded all the helper indies and history for the timeframes you intend to use or your mt4 version may hang. If your MT version does not hang when you drag this version of indicator onto the chart without changing the defaults and does hang when you change them you have probably not completed the prerequisites. You can get the helper indies here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...10#post4788110 In addition, before you ask me any questions about the email not working, please make sure that you can demonstrate that your mt4 is properly configured to send email by showing that a test email is working. Modes: EperiodTypes: ===== Type 0 - slow trix . Green when fast trix is sloping up, red when it is sloping down Type 1 - fast trix Green when slow trix is sloping up, red when it is sloping down. Type 2 - stochs For type 2 (stochastics) you can set each row to use a different stochastic. Use Stochsignal for row1 , secondstochsignal for row2, thirdstochsignal for row 3,fourthstochsignal for row 4etc.) Type 3 - Thv classic mode (fast trix above slow trix and fast trix above 0 and fast trix green or the opposite for short) Type 4 - semiclasic (fast trix above/below slow trix i.e trix cross but not necessarily above zero, and fast trix still in direction of trade) Type 5 - cloud. Green when price is above Ichimoku cloud, red when it is below it. Type 6 - HeikenAishi. Green when HA bars are greeb, red when they are red. Type 7 - TDI (traders dynamic index) + Market sentiment (TDI yellow line) increasing or decreasing for red or green Type 8 - AboveBelow0 (fast trix above 0 and fast trix green - or the opposite for short) Type 9 - AboveBelow Tenkan (Price above/below Tenkan) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 10 -Above/Below Kijjun (Price above/below Kijjun ) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 11 - Above/Below Tenkan &amp;&amp; Kijun"; (Price above/below Tenkan &amp; Kijjun ) (Uses second cloud settings) Type 12 - Trix Hist (shows whether the distance between the fast and slow trix is increasing or decreasing in the direction of the trade) Type 13 -Coral. Green when price is above coral, red when it is below it. Type 14- Divergence - Catches the divergence arrows show by the Trix on the higher timeframes. Note that divergence arrows do not appear in realtime - it takes a least two bars for the trix to catch it, and it is also not always right. So it's better to catch it manually yourself, but if you missed it this will give you a heads up. Type 15 - Both fast and slow trix. Red means both fast and slow trix are red, green means both fast and slow trix are green, empty means one is grean and the other is red. Type 16 - The angle of the stochastic signal line. Red means the line is sloping down green means it is sloping up (regardless of whether there has been a cross or not) . Type 17 - Same as type 16 but the signal line is greater than 20 and less than 80. Type 18 - Chop signal based on the TDI. Red when price is below the TDI 5 period high and low smoothed channel, green when price is above it, empty when price is inside the channel. Type 19 - All ThV. Green when price is above coral and cloud and both trix lines are green, red when price is below coral and cloud and both trix lines are red. However trix does not have to be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 20 -All ThV Plus Trix Cross Same as type 19 but in addition trix must be crossed in the direction of the slope. Type 21 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Slow Trix is red, empty when none of the above Type 22 - Green when price is above Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is green, Red when price is below Coral and Cloud, and Fast trix is red, empty when none of the above. Type 23 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction. Green sloping up, red sloping down Type 24 - All Guppy MMAs are sloping the same direction, and also in order ( i.e, 3 above 5, 5 above 8 etc, or vice versa) Type 25 - Three specified MAs have crossed and specified stochastics poining in same direction. (Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 26 - Three specified MAs have crossed and are above the Coral.(Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 27 - Fast trix, slow trix and trix histogram all the same color Type 28 - Treads ADX setup: Green when PlusDI above MinusDI, Plus DI increasing, PlusDI above specified value, ADX above specified value, ADX increasing or red when vice versa Note that ADX , PlusDI and Minus DI price mode values are as follows: PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4 This is different from the MTFADX indie Tread released, which uses the high price for all three by default (an error in my opinion because it seems to scew things to the positve side, but you can choose what you like). If you dont care whether the ADX is above a certain value, just that it be increasing set ADXMinVal to 0. Likewise if you don't care if the DI value is above a particular level, just that it be increasing set DIMinVal to 0. Type 29 - Ignores whether the ADX is increasing. Just checks whether ADX is above the specified value, whether DI is above the specified value and whether DI is increasing. Type 30 - Using the params firstlowertype 30 and firsthigher type30, seccondlowertype20 and secondhighertype30 you can check whether the PlusDI on a lower tf is higher than PlusDI on a higher tf and MinusDI on a lower tf is lower than MinusDI on a higher TF and ADX is rising ( and vice versa of course). Green when PlusDI&gt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&lt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&gt; PlusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Red when MinusDI&gt;MinusDIHTF &amp;&amp; PlusDI&lt; PlusDIHTF &amp;&amp; MinusDI&gt;MinusDIPrev &amp;&amp; ADX &gt;ADXPrev Type 31 4 Mas in order and expanding shows you when the four selected mas are in order and when the distance between the first and second is expanding (Uses MACrossMA1 etc) Type 32 -4 Mas in order and narrow- Red when 4 MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,MA3 below MA4 and the distance between MA1 and MA4 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green (Uses MACrossMA1 etc nd ChannelWidth) Type 33 - 3 MAs in order (instead of four) Same as type 26 except uses 3 MAs without checking if they are above or below the coral Red when all MAs in order - MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3. Vice versa for green. Type 34 - 3MAs narrow&amp;expanding Same as type 33 except also checks if the distance between MA 1 and 3 is less than the value specified in Channel and is expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3,and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is greater than for the previous bar. Vice versa for green. Type 35 - DI&amp; min vals Red when minus DI is above plus DI and greater than DI min val and ADX is greater than ADX min val. Vice versa for green. Type 36 -3MAs narrow Same as type 34 but doesnt check if the mas are expanding. Red when all MAs in order, MA1 below MA2, MA2 below MA3 and the distance between MA1 and MA3 for the current bar is less than the specified channel. Vice versa for green. Type 37 - Ha Candles above/below Coral and cloud. Red when HA candles are below both Coral and cloud, green when HA candles are above both coral and cloud, blank when both conditions are not met. Type 38 - TDI band breakout. Green when the TDI green line breaks out of the blue bands to the upside, red when it breaks out of the bands to the downside Type 39 - Like type 7 but ignores whether market sentiment (TDI yellow line) is rising or falling. This is the original Synergy signal - 7 was a modification of it Type 40 - TDI band squeeze. Green when distance between blue bands is less than BBSqueezelimit param and TradeSignalLine2 is above market sentiment, red when it is below it. Type 41 - Slow trix above/below 0. Red when slow trix is below 0, green when it is above it, with out regard to the slope of the trix Type 42 - Slow trix above/below 0 and sloping up/down. Red when slow trix is below 0 and sloping down, green when it is above it and sloping down, blank when both conditions are not met. Type 43 - TDI green band is above Market baseline. Green when the TDI green line is above the market baseline (yellow line) red when it is below it, without regard for whether it is also above/below the red line. Type 44. All THV plus OB/OS. Like type 19 except signal is not given if the fast trix is in overbought or oversold. (Uses TrixxxOB and TrixxxOS params where xx is a timeframe like M1 M15 etc) Type 45 - TDI RSI A/b Market baseline BB expanding. Green when the TDI green line is above the yellow line and the blue bands are expanding, red when it is below it and the blue bands are expanding Type 46 - Trix, cloud, coral, TDI yellowband, stochs. Green when price is above the cloud and coral and the TDI yellowband and stochastics are rising. Red when price is below the cloud and coral and the TDI yellowband and stochastics are falling. Type 47 -TDI Fan squeeze. Green when the slope of the TDI green, red and second market baseline are increasing , green is above red, red is above the second market baseline, the green line is above the yellow line and the blue lines are expanding. Red when the slope of the TDI green, red and second market baseline are decreasing , green is below red, red is below the second market baseline, the green line is below the yellow line and the blue lines are expanding. Type 48 - Green when ATR is increasing and plusDI is greater than minusDI. Red when ATR is increasing and minusDI is greater than plusDI. Type 49 - Green when ATR is increasing and price is above the cloud. Red when ATR is increasing below the cloud. Type 50 - Trix Cross. Green when fast trix is above slow trix, red when it is below it. Type 51 - Tenkan above/below Kijun. Uses secondcloud MA periods Type 52 - Price above/below MA Uses PriceXMAPer PriceXMAMethod, PriceXMaAppPrice params Type 53 - CCI above/below level specified in CCILevel Type 54- Outside bar Price reversal. Red when previous bar was green and current bar is red if current bar' high is above previous bar high and current bar low is below previous bar low. Green when previous bar was red and current bar is green if current bar' high is above previous bar high and current bar low is below previous bar low. Does not work with HA candles. Does not wait for bar close so if, for example you are watching for 30m bars on a 1m chart it may show you an green outside bar that in the end closes red. However for the minute you are looking at it was green Type 55 - Price above/below coral and coral is appropriate color - i.e green when price is above, red when price is below Note: The useHACandles param affects type 5, 9,10,11,13 19, 20,21,22, 25 and 44. When true, the ePeriod types that compare where price is in relation to something such as the Ichimoku cloud or the Coral compares the close of the HA candle instead of the regular close. Configuring auto timeframes =========== If you want to autoconfigure timeframes using mode one, you can use the following settings in eperiod: 0 : current tf - 1 : up one tf -2 : up two tfs -3 : up three tfs. -4 : up four tfs That is, if you are on a one min chart and you set ePeriod to -1 you will see data for the 5 m chart. For -4 on a 1 m chart you will see data from the 60 m chart. Alarm =========== The way it works is that for each row in the histo you can choose whether to count the row in the max score by setting countE1-4 to true. Then you set a Max score. When EnableAlerts is true, you will get an alarm when the total score is greater than or equal to the Max score. For example: Suppose I have the following settings. row 1 is the 1m f trix row2 is the 1 m coral row 3 is the 1m cloud row 4 is the 5m fast trix. If I want to get an alarm when all four rows are the same colour I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 4. If I want to get an alarm when 3 of the four are true I set countE1-4 to true and max score to 3. In this case when any three of the rows are the same color you will get an alarm. (You will also get an alarm once when the fourth row turns color as well) If I want to get an alarm when only the first, second and third rows are true I set countE1, countE2 and countE3 to true, countE2 and countE4 to false and max score to 3. In addition the score for each row is reset if the histo row changes color. So if you have an alarm on the first,second and third rows, and max score set to 3, when all three change to the same color (green for example) you will get an alarm. If the second row changes color (to red for example) but the first and third rows stay green, when the second row changes back to green you will get another alarm. You will get the alarm at the start of the next bar following the bar in which the total score was greater than or equal to maxscore. EmailAlert: Set to true if you want to get email alerts. EnableAlerts should also be set to true and it would be best to leave AlertMode type as 0 (alert on newbar when last bar has closed with a signal) rather than 1 (interbar)

The MTF system is separate. I tested it for about three months in 2009,and posted the trades in Cobra's private site. My hit rate was about 80%. On really choppy days it could go down to 65%. BUT that included taking all the trades there were to take between Frankie open and London close (except for on holidays and within half an hour either side of news.) One of the things was that I took all the divergence trades (divergence itself counts for 4 of the 6 points and you don't have to wait for price to cross the coral) and you are not ever allowed to trade against divergence. This means you have to be very good at spotting where divergence is even before the trix tells you about it, because it is late by two bars. The 15 and 10 pips was plus spread or the ATR suggestion, whichever was higher. My spread was about one so I would exit at -16 or +11. Three would be two high for this type of scalping in my opinion. Since this is really hard work paying attention to all those trades for all those hours I've moderated out a bit and use a different setup which doesn't occur as often. So I don't know what the hit rate is now for the 6 lights method.

--- 帖子 #23447 ---
You can't backtest using that indicator. The only way you can use the SAH or variants to backtest is when the indicator only uses the current tf (tf 0). It is useful in this case to flag instances of the trade we are watching for, in case our eyes missed them. (For example on a 5m chart we might be looking for a case where price is above the 5 m coral, the 5m fast trix is green, the 5 m stoch is up and the 5m adx is greater than 20. This is something we might best identify using the SAH rather than by eye. But if you are trying to enter, for example, on a one m chart when the 1m, 5m, 15m and 60m fast trixes are green you can't use the mtf indicators to backtest, because the results are only valid when the mtf indicator gets the results in real time, not when it is added 'after the fact'. When it gets info in real time, for example the indicator may know that during a 5m red bar, the trix was green for four minutes and red for the final 1 minute, but the last minute value was large enough to make the whole bar red. If you add the mtf indicator 'after the fact' it has no idea what happened during those 5 minutes. All it knows is that the final result was a red bar, so it will show all five of the minutes that comprise this bar on a 1m chart as red. Thus, if you are looking at the indicator when you added it 'after the fact', you will think you could have entered short in the first minute, whereas, in real time you could have entered only after the fifth minute, and you will mistakenly think that your profits would include the difference from the 1st to the fifth minute, whereas in reality they would not have. For more info, please read my previous posts.

--- 帖子 #23451 ---
If you mean that the trix etype loses info, you can adjust how much it keeps in the TrixNumberofBars param. But it will still disappear if anything happens to reset it, which can be changing tfs, or clicking on the indicator and changing any params or even if your mt4 loses its connection momentarily and resets it. Yes, this is part of the so-called repaint issue. I don't consider it repainting if the indie shows different values when added after the fact from what it shows when it gets them in real time, but some folks do. To me, repainting would be if, while running the mtf indie showed you a green cube at 9:15 on the 1m chart and 10 minutes later at 9:25 it went back and repainted that red without having been reset in some way. To the best of my knowledge it doesn't do that, although the trix itself WILL do that sometimes, which I have posted screen shots of in my previous post. That's another reason why sometimes the mtf indie won't match what you see 'after the fact' in the trix. This is too long and complicated to explain in a readme inside the indicator. Also it is not (except for the trix itself repainting) specific to my indicator. All mtf indicators do this.
