okay, now I know what happened to the sah cubes that change... For everyone using the SAH: If you compare both screenshots you can see that now the information is lost due to a reconnect of my internet connection. That means, when MT4 noticed that the connection is back it refreshes and loads the information from history file even if you did let MT4 run for the whole time of the session. The red line is where MT4 started collecting live data. If you want to use the SAH for backtesting it only works when you let MT4 run and collect life informations. Don't change the timeframe, don't restart MT4 and don't lose your internet connection! Many people have set their internet connection to autoconnect so you won't notice if your router or windows reconnects. The same refresh should happen if the broker doesn't give you a good data feed. For example, when the market moves fast with news or something like that, some brokers lack. Another case could be when your computer is overstrained with your MT4 or other programs. If MT4 can't calculate the chart informations it is possibly that MT4 hangs and refresh. But I didn't test that. How to Backtest with SAH? You can check if MT4 (SAH) stayed connected when you mark the SAH cubes(s) with something (Arrow etc.) like I did. Just mark cubes that differ in the timeframe you actually watch for that row. For example: If you watch the M15 Fast Trix ROW with the SAH on a one Minute Chart take a look at the clock. When did the 15 minute begin? When does it end? If the cubes are different with red and green, mark them. Start with the oldest time, the start of life data. If MT4 refreshed, you will see that for these 15 minutes the cubes change to one single color. If it refreshed you can't use it for backtesting this way. The only way it always works is as we know with the same timeframe for SAH Rows and the Chart. http://s14.directupload.net/images/1...p/mn9qui5d.jpg http://s1.directupload.net/images/12...p/qkjr39yi.jpg

Hello MissPips, yes, I have an example for that with a marker for price and candle. It's an indicator which I asked for at a german forum. One guy was so kind and coded it, so I have the source code as well. To help you understand what it does: This indicator was supposed to give a popup and/or sound alarm when the market moves faster than before, maybe through news, breakout or from a quiet period. It looks at previous candles (Ext_BarRange) and calculates the average. Then it multiplicates the actual candle with a factor (Ext_Breakout Factor). Three lines are displayed. One for average, one for average plus factor and the breakout line for the actual state. When an alarm occurs it marks the chart with two arrows. One for the candle and a second marker for the price where the alarm appeared. If the blue line crosses the red line the alarm comes up. Green is the average line. I use it all the time but without the window. I drag the window down so I don't see it and get the alert with a sound. It's great to get informed live when the market is in action especially when you trade. The arrows are not working 100% correct (as far as I remember the price arrow is wrong sometimes). It seems there is a litte coding mistake but it works for breakout purposes. Maybe it has to do with the option to choose HA or normal candles. If you decide to integrate it to the sah it would be great if you could code the option to choose two colors for the arrows too for long and short. That is made for the breakout indicator too. You can explore how it is done. If you need me to translate german to english from the sourcecode, I can help you. Just PM me. Good luck!

--- 帖子 #23459 ---
OK, I looked at the code and thought about it and I realized that this isn't going to solve the backtesting problem. It's just going to duplicate it on the upper chart. The reason is this. This is how these indicators all work: Let's say you have 2000 bars on the chart when you add the indicator. So it goes and calculates the values for all the existing 2000 bars on the chart first and then as each new bar is added it calcs a new value for each added bar as they happen. So lets say you are watching the 5m trix in row 1 on the 1m chart for a signal and you set the alarm on row 1. And let's say that in reality, in bars 1996-2000 on the 1 m chart, the 5 m trix was green for 4 bars but the last bar was so large a down move that the entire 5 m bar turned red. The indicator would show all 5 bars (bars 1996-2000) as red, because it was added 'after the fact' and all it knows is that that bar ended red, so it paints all of the 5 one minute bars that comprise it red. In bars 2001-2005 lets say the same thing happens. Now the indicator shows bars 2001-2004 as green and 2005 as red, because when the indicator calculates in real time it is aware of value of each 1 minute bar that make up the 5m trix, and you can see when you got the signal properly. But if the indicator is now reset, it will repaint all bars 2001-2004 to red, because when it is reset after those minutes have occurred it doesn't know what happened during those minutes anymore. All it knows is that that 5 m bar ended red, and it assumes that all 5 minutes were red, just like in the first instance. Now lets say that we set the alarm to sound whenever row 1 changes and we add an arrow to the chart, whenever the alarm sounds. Since the location of the arrow will depend on the calculations of the indicator the same thing will happen in the chart window that happens in the mtf bars. If you added the indicator just as bar 2000 finished the first arrow will be at bar 1996 for the first red trix (even though in real time 4 of the bars were green and only the last was red), and at bar 2005 for the second red trix, which is calculated in real time. But if you reset it, the arrows will also be reset, because they depend on the calculations of the trix, and now the first arrow will be at bar 1996 and the second at bar 2005 instead of 2001. So it won't help with backtesting.

--- 帖子 #23463 ---
That wouldn't solve it either, if I understood you correctly, because there can be cases where all 5 or all 15 cubes (for example) can be the same color, because the trix (for example) really was red all the time or green all the time. I really can't think of a decent way to solve this issue. I thought of having another indicator which called the SAH using the same parameters you had chosen for the SAH, and which put a line on the chart when it got a signal from it. This indicator would only collect data going forward in time. (++ instead of -- loop). But even that wouldn't work because if you did anything to initialize the chart or this new indicator (restarting MT4, changing tfs, etc.) then this indicator too would then erase all the forward data it had collected. The only way to get around THAT would be to not have the indicator erase anything when it was initialized , which would make the charts extremely messy and pretty meaningless to deal with after one or two rounds of use. And, if you wanted to start fresh you'd have to erase everything manually. And it would mean maintaining the second indicator's call to the SAH, each time I updated the SAH, and releasing a new version of it for each new version of the SAH. Since both parts would be very messy and complicated (the input and the output) I think it would generate a lot of questions, complaints and PMs from people who weren't using matching versions together or didn't understand why lines were left on the chart or didn't match the input of the two indicators correctly etc. So all things considered that idea doesn't seem to be very practical and I can't think of any other solution at the moment. There might be one other way to solve it which is to backtest using the mtf simulator that someone posted in this thread previously.

I haven't posted any rules for the SAH. This is on purpose for several reasons: 1) It isn't really part of THV since it includes other indicators. This is because a lot of people have their own favorite indicator that they like to use in addition to the standard THV (like the ADX or stochastics) and many have asked me to include these in the SAH so they can get alarms and emails when these give a signal that concurs with THV. Or they have a favorite way to trade THV which isn't part of the standard method, like entering only when the slow trix is above below zero and they wanted alarms. 2) I didn't provide settings because I wanted to encourage other people to share their ideas. A few people have been kind enough to share their settings for it, like toafdawg and neild1971 and if you look in their posts I think you will find some templates.

--- 帖子 #23487 ---
Thanks a bunch! Here's a fix for mt4 build416. If you are downloading this for the first time be sure to download the helper indies from this post. http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...40#post5395640 . If you don't have that build you don't need to download it. There's a bug in the build. The way you create this type of indicator is that for each row you have two buffers and you get the different colors by setting one buffer to 1 (for example the green value for the first row) and the other one (for example the red buffer) to empty for that cube in that row. This build has a bug in that for the first row it displays both the buffer you set to one, and below it it shows an additional row (which is theoretically impossible since it only is supposed to have 8 buffers) which displays the OTHER buffer you set to empty, which it shouldn't show. That's why this extra row is the exact inverse of the one that should show up So I fixed it by initializing the buffers to -1 instead of to the empty value and limiting the indicator so it can only display values from 0 to 4. This isn't the best thing, and that's why I think you don't need to download this unless you have a build with this bug.

--- 帖子 #23493 ---
Starting to watch the past of the SAH where the cubes aren't consecutive for the timeframe isn't right either because sometimes that is legit (and sometimes it isn't) and you don't know which is which when it's added after the fact. In a very strong downtrend you'll get lots of consecutive reds, for example, and if you discount that then you are skewing the results of your backtest. It is possible to write an indicator that works only 'forward' -i.e on real time data only and fills the cubes only forward from the moment it is loaded and sets a marker when an alarm is given (which is essentially the same data as in the cubes, so it doesn't really add much.) But this data is still going to get erased and restarted (forward in real time) when the indicator is initialized, just like the cubes do. Also doing it this way (forward in realtime only) would remove the legitimate use of the SAH for backtesting, which is when you want to see how a combination of indicators works as a filter for the SAME timeframe. (i.e you want to see how a trix cross, the coral, a the cloud and a longer moving average than the Coral work together, or how a trix cross, the cloud, the coral and the ADX for the same timeframe work together.) So I don't really want to make the SAH work that way. Probably the best way to back test using MTF values would be to try the MTF simulator that was posted. I don't know a good place to learn mql. I just press F1 and read the help when I want to know how something works.

--- 帖子 #23495 ---
Yes, I think we are talking about different things. What I mean is that suppose you start the SAH in the morning and leave it running. You come home and you want to see if it disconnected so you look to see (for example) if you have 15 consecutive red bars in the row watching the 15 slow trix (if I understood what you are doing). But what I am saying is that when you have a strong downtrend you can get 30, even 45 consecutive red bars in real time, and that is what really happened (because in downtrends people panic more it seems, even though I've never understood this because since forex is two sided what is a downtrend for the EUR in EURUSD is an uptrend for the USD). Anyway, if you looked at that and decide that isn't real data because there are too many consecutive red bars, you would skew the results of your backtest. Someone posted an MTF version of vhands trade (called MTFvhandsTrade), which although I remember it rather vaguely, supposedly does let you backtest the 5 m trix (for example) on a 1 m chart. That was the whole point of it. Regarding not erasing the markers, the markers would be in the same place as the cubes, since they would have to be based on them. For example suppose you want an alert on the fast trix, the cloud, the coral and the fast trix one higher timeframe. So you set each of the four rows to those, and set the alarm to look at all four rows and set maxscore to 4. So you'd get an alert and a marker whenever all four rows were the same color. The four rows being the same color and the marker would be showing the same information, and based on the same information. So when if the cubes got wiped out ( by the indicator being initialized) then the marker would also get erased.) It is possible to not have the marker erased on init, but what would happen in this case is that you'd have two sets of markers. You'd have the first set (which was the real time set that didn't get erased) and then you'd have the second set (which would be the set that would be recreated 'backward' if the indie got reset (by a disconnect for example), just like the cubes are recreated backward in time. So you'd have both sets of markers, but it wouldn't be clear which was which. The only way to get around it would be to have a second indicator which only went forward in time, which read data from the SAH, and which also didn't erase the markers. That would work because you'd always only have markers that were created in real time, even it it got reset. If it got reset, you'd still have the markers that were created and not erased, and then you wouldn't have duplicates after the reset because it would only go forward in time. But then you'd have to erase all the markers manually (more or less - I could put in a feature that would do it on request) when you wanted a clean chart. Maybe next time we get a long holiday I'll give it a shot.

It says MissPips because it was my idea and I wrote the version of it between V3 and V4. The SAH is better than the THV MTF because, for one thing, even if you are only interested in the trixes, the alarms are better. You can set them for any combination of rows, you can get an email alert and you can get alarms intra bar if you want instead of end of bar. Also control over the timeframes is better. Also you can fit 'more' trix info into the bar if you use the 'both' option (type 15).

--- 帖子 #23511 ---
He took a bit of a break from forex factory due some health problems with his eyes and some other business interests. Personally, I would not take on republishing all the indicators for MT5 by myself. THV was created by a team with Cobra as the 'head of development.' But many people - around 6 or 7 participated, because it is a lot of work. Even supporting just a couple of indicators as I do is quite a good bit of responsibility I wouldn't want to take on the whole lot on top of learning the newest version of MQL. I wouldn't have the time or patience for for all of them together. Also, my philosophy about contributing to the forum is to do things that I am interested in or need for myself, and then to share them if I think they are worthwhile - but not necessarily to take on something because somebody asks me to because they happen to need it, unless I also happen to need it, or I happen to be interested in it at the time. I think that that approach is fair enough, because I find that what they used to teach in Econ 101 is true - peoples wants are unlimited, and my time is limited. Furthermore, I do not believe that MT4 is going out of business so fast or that MT5 will catch on without backward compatibility, except in the US. I think it was rushed into production for the US based brokers so that they could comply with the Dodd-Frank requirements. I guess that in the rest of the world MT4 will be around for quite some time, and that by the time it disappears there will be conversion utilities.

--- 帖子 #23520 ---
Hi Fx Hog, Well, I don't know if 'anybody' is trading it. I have changed the way I trade a bit, for a few reasons. First I found it to be just too tiring to take all those trades on the M1, because it gives you quite a few, and the statistics that I did were for the results if you took ALL of them from the German open to the London close, not if you pick and choose. You also have to be really alert to watch for divergences, because the tests included making sure you didn't trade against divergences on the 1m or higher timeframes. Second, at the time I didn't know there was an mtf trix that you could put on the chart and see the actual trix. Third, maybe I am just getting older but now I am pickier about my trades and I like to first look for a place where I think one will happen, and then put them on only if THV confirms them. So anyway, what I do is look for a place that I expect a trade to occur ( for example at an SR line or big fib lineand then I look for both price action (like double tops, double bottoms, higher highs and higher lows or vice versa) and THV to confirm or deny it. For example, in the screenshot below, at the red line, we have an Asian session range that has been tested a few times, and this range is in a place where there was a big drop on the 1 hr chart last time we hit it, and we have a close below it with lower highs and lower lows. The trixes and corals all confirm the trade, so I took it. (The green MA is the 1m coral, and the orange one is the 15m coral, and in practice I checked the 1m tf to make sure the 1m trix was turning back down after the small retrace you can see in the next bar, but it's easier to see on the 5 m chart. I didn't wait for a full retrace up and turn down on the 1m chart because with range breakouts the move is often sharp and a lot of times you don't get very good retraces until it's too far gone. ) At the dashed red line, we have another place I would expect a trade to occur ( a retest of the range break and continuation, but the trixes, corals and price action do not confirm the trade so I didn't take it. So that's an example of how I use the 6 lights now, but like I said I don't take every setup anymore. At the green dashed line you can see an example of a 'good' 6 lights trade (and if you had taken it on the 1m chart according to the 6 lights rules it would have worked) that I wouldn't take these days because I'd be expecting a bounce a the 15 min coral (the orange line) and the upper triangle line. The Euro might make a break to the upside because there's divergence on the 1 hr chart and a bear flag on the DXY but I'd rather wait and see the outcome and then take a trade if price gets above them and above R, or if price breaks and retests the lower trendline.

--- 帖子 #23521 ---
The coral is just a 60 period T3 where b =0.4, and which has had color added to it according to the slope. So if you want to see a 1m coral on a 5m chart you just find that T3 (posted here many times) and change 60 to 12, or if you want to see a 15 coral on the 5 chart you change 60 to 180 etc.

--- 帖子 #23569 ---
Hi Neild1971, In response to "Here is a question to anybody that has EA programming exp, can an EA be made which opens an order based on the information a pop up alert gives or is the pop-up part of the SAH and not the MT4 platform". An EA opens an order based on the logic of several indicator values (standard MT4 and Custom). An EA cannot directly open an order based on a POPUP Alert, however if the conditions that cause the POPUP Alert are exposed through MT4 buffers it is possible. You would not use the buffers of the SAH you would go one step back to the buffer values of the Indicators. I can provide you an insight of how the EA would be coded if you can provide the following information: What indicators do you want your EA to use ? If it is the SAH what settings? What are the entry conditions for the EA ? Best Regards Joss

--- 帖子 #23595 ---
Looking forward to seeing your charts. Actually I am not a good programmer. Real programmers who see my code usually fall on the floor laughing. The SAH works like this. For each of the four rows you have a eperiod field and a eperiodtype field. In the eperiod field you select the timeframe you want to see. You can enter an absolute value (1, 5, 15, 30 etc) or relative value (-1,-2,-3-4 etc.). For example if you are on the 1m chart you can enter 5 to see the 5 min timeframe. Or you can enter -1 which will show you the 5 timeframe (1 timeframe up) on the one minute chart and the 15 min timeframe if you switch the base chart to 5 minutes (1 timeframe up from 5 minutes is 15 minutes.) The etypes have codes which each represent one indicator. These are explained individually since each indicator works differently but in general red is the short value (for example for eperiodtype 1 which is the fast trix it is red when the fast trix is red and green when the fast trix is green). Or for type 16, which is a stochastic, it is red when the stochastic is pointing up and green when it is pointing down. You can get alarms on any combination of rows. The way you do this is to include or exclude the row in the alarm score by setting CountE1-CountE4 to true or false, and selecting the appropriate score. For example if you want an alarm on all the rows, you set all the CountE1-CountE4 to true and set maxscore to 4. If you only want an alarm on the first row you set Count E1 to true and the others to false.You set maxscore to 1. The difference between the versions is just new features or indicator types. The indicator versions are not configured to represent any particular trade recommendations - you have to do that for yourself. P.s I hope you don't mean 'bought' literally. It really pisses Cobra off when somebody sells the THV indicators.

--- 帖子 #23631 ---
Good comments. I would add: 1) The MTF indies only work from lower to higher timeframes. That is, you can use them to see the 5m trix on the 1m chart correctly but not the 1 m trix on the 5m chart correctly. 2) The MTF rules state that you should not trade against divergence. I've mentioned this few times too. You need to trade, if anything, with the divergence and you have it on the chart where you took the trade. I want to explain something about what the 6 lights method is trying to do. I developed it based on the following idea: When the 5m fast trix changes color and price crosses the cloud in the corresponding direction, you have a swing high or a swing low, or at least an attempt at one (sometimes they fail without getting very far.). Now what is it that causes these swings? Support or resistance (or supply and demand or order flow or what ever the latest jargon is). Now, we can analyze the charts from here until tomorrow, and we can find areas on them where we think there will be support or resistance but the fact is that we can't predict ahead of time whether the support or demand line or fib line or pivot line will hold. So what we have to do is react to what price does at the line. Some people do this by looking a candlesticks or other PA patters.THV uses the trix, so the 6 lights method is based on what the trixes are telling us about whether support or demand will hold. That is why the requirement of the 6 lights method is for the 5m fast trix and the 1m fast trix to have freshly turned in the direction of the trade you want to take, because it is trying to get in near the start of a 'good' swing. I'm posting a chart of todays PA showing this on the 5 timeframe. (It's easier to see the swings and the 6 points on the 5m timeframe. The reason for entering on the 1m is that you can often pick up a few extra pips that way by waiting for a dip on the 1m chart, but the point is that you want to be entering near the start of a swing that has a good chance to succeed. ) In this chart, each place you see a red line a swing high is topping out and price is starting to swing down. Each place you see a green line, a swing low is forming and price is starting to go up. Also in each place the trix is changing color and price is crossing the cloud. Where the lines are dashed, the trixes are saying "don't do it". Where the lines are solid, the trixes are saying "go for it". Where the lines are yellow, the trixes are warning that things are ambiguous, because there is divergence, or the different timeframes do not agree. Notice that where you have 6 lights (which you can see in the mtf trixes, that is where you also have PA showing higher lows for longs and lower highs for shorts, and where you have 'good' swings, in the sense that you have a swing with enough momentum to get you 10 pips.) Also notice that where you have the trixes showing ambivilence is right on the pivot. So, that is what I was trying to do with the 6 lights method -find an entry near a swing high or low, in a place where there would be enough momentum to continue for 10 pips and keep out of trades where things are ambivalent. Of course you should also look at the charts to see where you are, and what trixes are trying to tell you and not just rely on the lights. For a long trade you want to see higher highs and/or higher lows and for a short trade lower highs and/or lower lows together with the lights, and ideally you would like to have an idea of what it is that is making price swing. And you want to be near the start of the swing, and not entering on the fourth or fifth 1 min retrace after the 5m start of the swing. I would also add that you have to take the ATR into consideration. The system was tested when the THV ATR suggestion on the 1m chart was on average between 10 and 15, and the EURUSD itself was doing about 130-150 pips a day on average. Lately we've been seeing 50-60 pip days, with 100 pips being outstanding. So you have to adjust. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #23641 ---
Normally we look for only longs when price is above the coral. However, when you have divergence (which Ahniel had) according to the 6 lights rules, you don't have to wait for price to cross the coral. At that point it's too late,because what you are doing in that trade is trading when price is too overextended and trying to return to the coral.

--- 帖子 #23648 ---
There are different ways of trading THV. The regular way the setup for a long is 1) Price has to be above the coral and cloud. 2) Trix crosses up and both trix lines are green. The regular setup for a short is the opposite: 1) Price has to be below the coral and cloud. 2) Trix crosses down and both trix lines are red. That's it. Then there is the MTF way, whereby you have to have 6 points in order to trade and two of them have to be from the 1m fast trix and the 5 m fast trix. This method is trying to catch the start of a 'good' 5m swing on the 1m chart. Using this method, we don't wait for the trix to cross, but base the trigger for the trade on the 1m and 5m fast trixes. The reason is that we are catching a swing when the underlying trend is in our favor, as represented by the higher timeframe trixes. Price should still be above the cloud and coral for a long and below it for a short on the timeframe you are trading. The exception is when you have divergence in which case you don't have to wait for price to cross the coral. The ideal setup is when you can see a lot of momentum on all the timeframes, close to the start of a move - for example like this:

--- 帖子 #23651 ---
For long trades, price should be above the coral and cloud, and the trigger is when you have 6 green lights, two of which must be the 1m fast and 5m fast. For short trades, price should be below the coral and cloud, and the trigger is when you have 6 red lights, two of which must be the 1m fast and the 5m fast. The exception is when you have divergence. Then that in itself counts for 4 points, and you dont have to wait for price to cross the coral. You must still have the 1m fast trix in your favor, and preferably the 5m fast trix as well. Try to keep in mind that we are trying to catch swings, not just hitting buy or sell when we see 6 lights. We are using the trixes across timeframes to get an idea if support or resistance is going to hold or break so we can trade accordingly. It's also a good idea to use the price action on the chart, for example patterns like double tops, h &amp; s, and higher highs/higher lows (or vice versa) to confirm trades.

--- 帖子 #23669 ---
The buffers are the same in all the versions (except the bug fix for 416.) - buf1_up, buf1_down... buf4_up, buf4_down. They show either the empty value (except for the bug fix for 416, where they show -1) or a value &gt;0 (depends on what the user puts in Pn_position and Gap) in order to fill up the appropriate cube in the row. That's how all the mtf indies like this work - that's what makes them put the lights in the right color and position. So if you want to test for if a row is red (for example) you test if buf1_up is empty and buf1_down is &gt;0). If you want the exact values that the indicators on which the cubes are based are returning you don't need the SAH. Just write an EA using whatever combination of indicators that you like in the SAH.

--- 帖子 #23678 ---
You can try your request over in the THV EA thread, although I would suggest phrasing it a bit more politely. This thread is for manual (i.e discretionary) traders. One thing that is slightly misleading is that THV is , in my opinion, a method and not a system (in the sense that a system is a set of predefined signals where you always take a trade when you see them, with predefined risk, target and money management). That is one reason why the classic method says "Analyze buy" or "Analyze sell" and not "Buy" or "Sell". This means that most traders in this room probably won't take a trade everytime they get a signal, nor will all of them use the same money management or set the same stops or targets. Also probably a lot of people here trade more than one way. I know I do, depending on the market. If there's a really well behaved trending market , I'll use 1m rainbow entries and not be too picky but if we're in a 60 pip chop range I'll look much harder and rely more on higher timeframe divergence at a place where I'm really pretty sure there will be a trade. before I enter. I did test the 6 lights method for about three months in the winter/spring of 2009 and post all my trades on Cobra's private site. I did take all the trades were a signal was given and the results were between 65 to 85% hit rate, depending on the day. The average was around 80%, with some days being 90% and very few days being 65%. But even that hit rate was predicated on correctly identifying divergence on the 1m and higher timeframes, and always trading with it and never against it, which in itself is a skill you have to acquire because the THV divergence arrows are often too late. In addition, the market has changed since then -it is more choppy, and the daily ranges are smaller. (The average range even six months ago was 140 pips, lately it's been about 70 or less.) It's also my impression that the trends are less well behaved (a lot more huge 1m bars followed by consolidation and then another huge move rather than gently rolling waves like there used to be - probably a lot more HFT bots at work than there used to be. Any veteran trader will tell you it's harder to trade the market now than it was two or three years ago.) That's why we're manual traders over here - we believe you have to adapt your trading to market conditions and that first you learn how to trade and then you use THV appropriately to help you find a good entry point. Therefore seeing someone else's results from this thread won't tell you much because it won't tell you if you have the ability to recognize and correctly adapt to different market conditions.

The volume indicator ("Volumes Enhanced_v2" - purposefully made for the SonicR System), is an extra indicator I use. It simply gives me a little more confidence on trades. I like to see a greater degree of volume when making a trade prior to entry, especially if volume changes to a stronger colour, indicating more volume in the direction of the trend, and as a result, a decent trade in that direction. I've copied and pasted the details of the colours from the SonicR instruction manual regarding the volume indicator below (I've also changed the colours around from the original settings to suit the white background): If you do intend to use the Volumes Indicator, or any other volume measuring indi, be sure to know how to use them first. Theres a host of information on the Internet on how to use Volumes correctly and in multiple ways, so I'd look on how to use them effectively first. I've found volumes to be quite useful indeed in my limited trading experience, but its different for everyone. Ultimately, the most important thing about this system is to understand general trading dynamics - the system probably won't work so well without that. It does take a long time to learn, and I'm still trying to get the hang of it! Understanding S/R points, Higher/Lows etc., volumes, fibs, Price Action (the hardest to learn IMO!) and so forth is a lot to take in. I've not even started properly trading yet... just getting to grips with it. To be honest, the more screen time the better you'll perform in my opinion. --- 帖子 #23743 ---
That was a good setup. It was a BRC(break,retest and continuation) with momentum, and it broke the low where there was divergence. My experience with divergence is that the trix is problematic with divergences at certain times. When price is consolidating near the coral and the trix is flat near 0, it can show fake divergence. If you are trading divergence in the direction of the rainbow trend it's one thing because the odds are in your favor, but if trading against the main trend it's better to get confirmation that price has really diverged far enough that it wants to pull back some. My rules are that I don't trade divergence against the trend unless it's at least a third price wave. Also for divergence against the trend I want to see the CCI and the TDI confirm it, and I want it to look pronounced . In the case of the CCI I want at least one of the waves to be over 200 and in the case of the TDI I want the RSI line (green line) one wave to be outside the blue bands and for the second wave inside. Having the trix outside it's overbought or oversold lines is also a plus. This is my way of verifying that it's not divergence inside consolidation that wants to expand in the direction of the trend when it's done, but real divergence where price is really too overextended and wants to return to the mean. Also I'd rather trade the second one in a row of two that are close together because the EURO has a nasty habit of stopping the first one out by a couple of pips above/below the high/low and then, having shaken out the weak hands, doing a nice reversal. If you get divergence against the trendinside consolidation near the coral (while the price is compressed near the spine of the rainbow) you can usually ignore it, especially if it breaks the high/low. Attached Image (click to enlarge) The trick is to notice if the divergence is happening while the rainbow is compressed and trying to expand, or while it is overextended and trying to contract. I put that yellow/aqua stripe where it is in the 1 and 5m rainbows for a reason. If you look at what it is doing compared to the previous waves it will help you distinguish between expansion and compression. Notice how the yellow stripe looks in each of the waves that make up the fake divergence verses how it looks in each of the waves that make up the real divergence. In the fakeout, the yellow band is expanding in each wave as price goes lower and in the real deal the yellow band in the 1m rainbow is contracting with each wave even though price is going lower. Also in the real deal the edge of the waves themselves are getting higher as price goes lower, while in the fakeout the edge of the rainbow is going lower as price does.

I prefer but the chances of getting it in that situation aren't good because the 5, 15 and 30 trixes all flipped together right there, together with a double bottom with divergence on the 5, 15 and 30 m charts. I don't use the CCI that much but I do have a separate chart with it and the TDI for checking if I want to take a divergence trade against the trend, and I do find it's useful to filter those trades on the 5 m chart. Since trading against the trend is riskier you want to make sure it's a real good divergence before doing it, or alternately if the TDI and CC don't confirm, you can rule out not taking a trade with the trend just because there was 'fake' divergence caused by consolidation that's likely to carry on with the trend. I love the rb as a visual aid too. I know that there are people who can read PA just looking at the bars, but I find having the colors in there really helps me see what's going on.

--- 帖子 #23768 ---
I don't need to see the periods and etypes - I can see that from the text. I need to see the params that configure type 52, as per the documentation for the SAH etype 52 in the link I sent you (i.e PriceXMAper etc.) Edit Ok, I see the updated pic now. The problem is that you want to see the 200 SMA put you have 10 in the PriceXMAper param instead of 200. This is the code that type52 calls PriceXMA= iMA( Pair , prd, PriceXMAPer, 0, PriceXMAMethod, PriceXMaAppPrice, yy) ; Here is the MT doc for iMA(). double iMA( string symbol, int timeframe, int period, int ma_shift, int ma_method, int applied_price, int shift) Calculates the Moving average indicator and returns its value. Parameters: symbol - Symbol the data of which should be used to calculate indicator. NULL means the current symbol. timeframe - Timeframe. It can be any of Timeframe enumeration values. 0 means the current chart timeframe. period - Averaging period for calculation ma_shift - MA shift. Indicators line offset relate to the chart by timeframe. ma_method - MA method. It can be any of the Moving Average method enumeration value. applied_price - Applied price. It can be any of Applied price enumeration values. shift - Index of the value taken from the indicator buffer (shift relative to the current bar the given amount of periods ago). Moving Average calculation method used with iAlligator() , iEnvelopes() , iEnvelopesOnArray , iForce() , iGator() , iMA() , iMAOnArray() , iStdDev() , iStdDevOnArray() , iStochastic() indicators. It can be any of the following values: Constant Value Description MODE_SMA 0 Simple moving average, MODE_EMA 1 Exponential moving average, MODE_SMMA 2 Smoothed moving average, MODE_LWMA 3 Linear weighted moving average. Applied price constants. It can be any of the following values: Constant Value Description PRICE_CLOSE 0 Close price. PRICE_OPEN 1 Open price. PRICE_HIGH 2 High price. PRICE_LOW 3 Low price. PRICE_MEDIAN 4 Median price, (high+low)/2. PRICE_TYPICAL 5 Typical price, (high+low+close)/3. PRICE_WEIGHTED 6 Weighted close price, (high+low+close+close)/4. You can also find this documentation the the MT4 Language Editor.

Er nobody.... I only say that for the 6 lights method it was tested on 1m EURUSD, and the stops and targets are based to 20-30 pip (meaning that when it's behaving normally the eurusd moves in waves of about 25-30 pips at a time, and by the time you get a signal 10 are probably gone. So you are shooting for about half of whats left with a 15 pip stop putting the stop a few pips above/below the start). So if somebody wants to use it on another pair/tf they have to adjust that. (Similar to what the dustbin traders over in the useless thread do when they shoot for 12 pips, except they wait for levels to break once they see a trend and the 6 lights method quantifies what a 'trend' is and waits for the trix to break in its direction.) But a good pattern or method should work on any timeframe or pair, if you adjust it properly. I've been demo trading my favorite pattern (double rb flip, triple trix) on gold lately (my contingency plan for the Euro falling apart) and it works great so far.

--- 帖子 #23794 ---
Re-entry: Use the same rules for entry everytime. Each trade should be a new setup, if you are angry you left some pips on the table, just chill out another one will come along. If you are desperate though to reenter, I would -check for S&amp;R lines close to your entry and potential TP, avoid if you see some -Check RSI for overbought or oversold, avoid trade if it is -Check the TRIX has not changed colour, and is not flattening out too much -Confirm with stochastics (THV version) that it is not entering a yellow period (flattening out and changing direction) -Check SAH colours all still go for launch. Basically - you are not re-entering you are doing all the same checks for another setup except the Coral and Cloud, which assuming your last trade was successful and there is still momentum are likely to be still on your side (Above -short, Below - long). I'm a newbie - so confirmation from someone with more experience would be good :-)

Use the middle option "Active chart (as is)", which only saves the actual chart window. It does not save any of the "banner" information above/below the chart. Save a chart in this manner and confirm this for yourself. -tah

Sending notifications can be disabled in the settings. The ID can also be omitted. Now this off course would have to be added to the THV4 trix as part of the notifications.

--- 帖子 #23836 ---
The SAH is my work (based on some from the freely available mt4 code base), and while I don't publish the source for it out of respect to Cobra, because the MTF Trix histo code, which I also did, is similar, I don't feel very strongly about people decompiling it (other than a bit embarrassed because I know that real programmers probably laugh their heads off when they see the code). In fact I know it can be found decompiled already all over the Internet, as can the other THV indicators. I don't actually think that not publishing the source helps very much since, as you point out, it is very easy to decompile and anybody who'd sell it on eBay would have no qualms about decompiling it. In my opinion, the only thing it really does is make sure that the real newbs are actually using an authorized version and not something they have messed with and then are claiming doesn't work. As far as I'm concerned I don't care if you decompile the SAH, which should give you any notifications that you need.

--- 帖子 #23850 ---
My point was, buying currency is kind of like buying a house to rent out. If I'm buying a house, first of all I shouldn't buy one that's more expensive than I can afford to maintain if something goes wrong and I can't rent it out for a while. (position size small enough so I won't panic if it goes against me a few pips) Then I should consider the economy and demographics. If there's a housing glut maybe I should stay out of the market, whereas if there was a baby boom twenty years ago and the economy is also booming I should get in and specialize in one-bedroom places (consolidating vs trending market). Then I should consider my tenants. If it's somebody I know or who knows somebody I know, I can charge a bit less, because they are less likely to trash the place or stiff me. (Am I entering with a pattern I am familiar with and know to be pretty trustworthy? Are we talking London open breaking consolidation or Franky Fake hour?) And lastly: Location, location, location. (If I'm shorting, for example, is my stop going to be in a good place relative to both my money managment and to a location that price should not go above if I'm right about the trade. And is there room to the downside for the profit I want, both in respect to my money management and to where the likely bumps in the road that might make it bounce are? Where is the short with respect to the higher timeframe? Am I shorting at a major bottom or at the top of a channel in a major downtrend? Are the stochastics in every timeframe oversold or are they overbought in every timeframe?) And then of course it depends on what currency, what timeframe, what time of day, and general market conditions (is there a major panic on or are we in the summer doldrums?) It took me a couple of years, but I was dumb enough to waste a lot of time following a method that was being blogged about as a successful system at a very well-known and popular site for beginners. The blogger kept posting winning trades and pip total summaries showing winning months and I kept having losing month totals. It took me quite a while before I figured out it wasn't me - it was that the blogger was not religiously taking every trade (as he claimed you should do) but was very cleverly posting some loses ( to sound credible I suppose) while other times he would have an unexpected day off just on very a bad day for the system, or his stop would be missed by 1 pip while on all the platforms I checked it would be hit, or once in a while he'd do something that was against the rules and just say 'I couldn't resist'. I think that once he even fudged how one of the indicators he was using looked on a chart. The idea was just to attract viewers to the site, and once it got popular enough (and people started commenting on this kind of thing) he gave up the charade and just went to only posting only every few days and not posting monthly totals anyway so the omissions wouldn't look so obvious. Now of course, there's nothing wrong with entering trades on a discretionary basis - I am all for it and I think that to be a successful trader that's what you have to do because you have to adapt the kind of trade you put on to the kind of market you are in, and when you put on a trade you need to have a good look around first to see where you are on the chart with respect to S/R and the higher timeframes, pay close attention to divergence, and not trade just because you got a signal. But that wasn't what he was claiming to do of course - at the time he was claiming to have profitable system if you just followed the rules in order to attract followers, whereas what he was probably actually making most of his money from was advertising on the site. It was a good lesson though, although not exactly in the way intended.

Glad to see that I'm thinking like the best!. Here's an explanation of what I look for in a 'gap.' If you look at the chart below, the red rectangle shows a couple of wide range bars that open and close at both their lows and highs. Market makers need to manage risk, so they try to drive price down back to the start of these wide range bars. Once that happens, I like to look for rainbow, or 8-light trades in the direction of the wide range bars. This was a perfect set up that I missed last night. So I think to keep up the majors, and Dow on 15 min charts and look for these. Then I go down to the 1 minute using your techniques. This has been very successful over the last month, as I've only seen 1 EURUSD trade go more than 20 pips against me. What are your thoughts?

--- 帖子 #23960 ---
The 15 pip sl, 10 pip target was my idea for how to trade the 6 lights method scalping the 1 m chart. There were two reasons for it. The EURUSD at the time I developed it was moving about in about 25-30 waves (still more or less does though some days the range is smaller now so the waves are more like 20-25). About 10 pips could go by from the top/bottom of the wave (as signaled by the 5 fast trix changing color) until you get the signal to enter, and you need the stop above/below there so that's about 15 pips to be on the safe side (plus spread). Then you have about 15 pips to work with to get a profit in, and to be on the safe side you don't want to wait to the last pip of the wave to take it. (This is similar to the idea behind the 'dustbin' trades over in the Useless thread). Usually scalpers have lower RR. The other reason(which I have already confessed in prior posts) was that, at the time, I was a fairly new trader, and I just found I traded better if I set the trade and left it rather than watching it. Since my hit rate was 67%-90% depending on the day (about 78-80 % average this worked out ok). Now for the theory How much money you make with a system is determined by How much you make when you win *number of winning trades/total trades minus How much you make when you lose*number of loosing trades/total trades. Of course there is also more to it (leverage, and what is largest expected string of winners/losers in a row), but I'm assuming that you keep your position size and leverage small enough so that a string of loses won't wipe you out. Also you need to consider the how many opportunities per week the system gives you. A system that gives you 10 opportunities a day to trade, risks 15 and makes 10 with hit rate of 70% will make you more money than one that risks 1 and makes 100, but gives you 1 opportunity to trade a week, even with the same 70% hit rate (which isn't likely because the smaller the stop is in relation to the target, the worse the hit rate is going to be, unless for example you are very good at picking to the pip where price is going to reverse). So it's going to be harder to find good entries that are shooting for a 30 pip target (for example) with a ten pip stop than it is to find good entries that are shooting for a 10 pip target and an 15 pip stop and therefore you will have fewer opportunities to trade (which you may or may not view as an advantage.) What I do personally now (having learned to trade better) is use multiple lots and trail one manually. The other thing you can do if you want a 1/1 ratio is put the stop above/below the peak/bottom where you entered on the 1 m and go for the same target that you risk. However, that's not so good for the 1m min because brokers know people do that so a lot of times they'll just take out the stops above that peak (assuming a short trade) with one higher high and then reverse straight down without giving you a good entry at another lower high (the old shake and fake before the move) and you will be stopped out whereas your original entry would have made money with a wider stop. So it's better to put the stops at the peak above the peak where you entered as price came back down on the 1 m, but then that will usually put you back in the 15 pip range with the stop just above/below where the5 m fast trix changed color. Here is an example of what I mean that happened twice today : two 6 point trades that would get stopped out with a stop just above the peak where you enter by the fake and shake before the big move, but are good with a 15 pip stop (not that I traded today because my rules don't permit trading on hols). The first one actually depends on your spread - with a 2 pip spread you'd be stopped out but with a 1 pip spread you'd be ok with a 1:1 RR. Attached Image (click to enlarge) The main thing is to try to take entries where the stops you set make sense in terms of where support and resistance are - i.e. if the stop is 15 pips make sure that the swing high is below that for a short, and if the target is 10 pips make sure that there's room for that before the next support and also to be comfortable with whichever method you are choosing and the place you are entering (i.e a trade signal near where price has been compressed an is expanding is usually safer than one where you are selling a top but after extended move that has just bounced of strong support)

Regarding "take profit" and "stop losses"...I think using fixed values is bad. Why? Because I want to let my winners run as faaaaaaaaar as possible, which a fixed system won't allow. I mostly use the EMA as stop loss, and it allows me to ride a large part of the moves. Sometimes I'll set the initial stop loss above a resistance line or below a support line until a trade takes off, or if price is still too close to the EMA. Also, I use this mostly as a breakout strategy. However, if price bounces back and forth between a relatively narrow support/resistance line, I buy/sell as of the 3rd bounce unless Trix is against me. My problem with the original system was that for me, the coral is not enough to define the trend. If you look in my post above, in the areas I labeled fake and shake, you will see small areas where the rainbow starts to turn green and blue. In those areas there are numerous trades where you have a trix cross up with price above the coral and cloud and they all fail if you are going for 10 pips. Most of them also fail if you are going for 1:1 RR with the stop below the 1m swing unless you have an extremely good spread and no slippage. Also, for me, I find there is a psychological advantage to the rainbow, in that when I look at the screen and see all that red it reminds me not to go long (for example) no matter how tempting a level looks, which is good, most of the time they fail. This is where R:R comes in. If you think about it, if you trade with the trend you are going to be right every single time until the last time, which is the time that it reverses. So the money is in two places: it's either in getting in a short (for example) near the start of the trend and either trailing one or adding on OR it's in getting in at the exact top or bottom (buying a support for example) AND being good enough to pick the ones that are going to hold AND picking the right R:R so that the times you are right make up for the times you are wrong AND having the discipline to hold the trade even if it comes back down and retests support again before reversing. So I find it's just easier for me to see trades and to hold them using the rainbow and also to avoid choppy areas.

Example: If you see a perfect THV entry setup and the ATR is 11 you can be sure (99%) that will be a nice move, to the next pivot, Coral or depends ho do you determine you trading.. The same setup with Atr 4 is much more riskier respectively behaves completely different. imo

--- 帖子 #24078 ---
Sorry no can do. I put it on the simulator and watched it. Not only will it go back in time and remove a signal that it announced previously (for example at 8:45 it will announce a sell signal, but at 9:10 it will erase it) but what is worse, it will also go back in time and add a signal that wasn't there, and sometimes it will add and remove a signal repeatedly after the fact until it makes up its mind. Attached is a screenshot of what I mean. Where you see red lines and arrows, it gave a sell signal that stuck (and vice versa for green lines and green arrows. Where you see red lines and no arrows, it gave a sell signal that it later erased ( and vice versa for green) Where you see long dashes it gave a signal that it turned on and off over the course of several bars until it finally made up its mind some bars later. And where you see the bright green bar with short dashes at 5:13 is the most interesting case, where it went back and added a long signal 5 minutes after the fact with no previous indication that something was happening there. In order to do an alarm I need something to 'grab onto'. For example the number in the corner is the number where the previous buy signal was. (Technically its what's in the buffer that puts in the buy arrows.) If that were accurate, then I could put a trap in to catch when that changed. However, since the indicator goes back 'after the fact and if it has put in a bad signal sometimes reverts that number to the number of the previous signal and sometimes reverts it to zero when it has made a 'mistake', and since it also sometimes puts the arrows and that number in 5 or more bars after the fact, there is nothing to 'grab onto' that won't give either false or late signals. This is because if I put in a trap to catch when that number changes you will get (in addition to the 'real' signals, signals when the indicator goes back and erases its mistakes (and sometimes multiple instances of this as it changes its mind over the course of several bars about an old arrow), and also late signals when it goes back and adds arrows after the fact. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attachment

You can use either version of THV (V3 or V4). They both work fine. The rainbow is my attempt to visually color code whether the trend is up, down or sideways on a major and minor timeframe. (If you look carefully you will notice that you can see according to the colors when both the major and minor time frames are falling or rising or when the major is going in one direction and the minor in another. You can also use it to see where you are in the trend (for example expanding with momentum right after a compression, fully extended or compressing). These are useful things to know, and I find personally find it easier to see them using the rainbows, but if you can see them without it then you don't need it.

Damiani Voltameter: If green &gt; red =&gt; TRADE If green &lt; red =&gt; DON'T TRADE Super simple...but it works.

--- 帖子 #24122 ---
Great screen shots! That's actually a bug in my documentation. Type 16 just looks at the slope of the fast or slow and I wrote that type 17 is like 16 but with o/b and o/s. But actually type 17 shows red when fast is below slow AND fast is sloping down AND not oversold. It shows green when fast is above slow AND fast is sloping up AND not overbought. In both those places not all the conditions are met. If you look on the hourly chart you will see that in the first instance fast is below slow but fast is sloping up and in the other fast is above slow but fast is sloping down. So that's why you have those gaps there.

--- 帖子 #24130 ---
Hi D-TickTrader The green line on the charts is SSL Fast-nrp, it's the same as Gann Hi Lo indi. I like this one because it has an alert that works well. Usual setting for the Look Back (Lb) is 10, but I adjust it to match the waves. The strait Green and Red lines are I-RegrBands HL. They come in useful when determining tops / bottoms. It repaints. The yellow / cyan line is the SuperTrend NRP &amp; alerts. Full description is in the Symphonie thread. The candles are HA with the THV cloud, and Coral. The first window below the chart is the TDI indi. Here is a good link that explains it's use. The blue line (green on original install) is actually an RSI, with the other lines (Red &amp; Yellow) are Ma's. I use this one a lot to determine OB/OS levels and for my entries. The black squiggly line is a fast stoch (5,3,3) used for entries. The next window actually shows a TRIX with different color settings. The Red/Blue indi on the zero line is SSL_4xLA.org. It's a Gann Hi Lo indi with a faster Lb setting. The white/black dots is ThePitchV3.2 is actually a non lag dot indicator. I keep the setting at 80, and it shows overall trend cycles. The yellow line is ma-wpr Baseball 2.2 which is a moving average of a Williams %R. I use that to determine OB/OS levels. The black squiggly line is a slower stoch (14,3,3). The vertical bars show tops and bottoms, however they repaint. They are Symphonie_Extreme_Cyle_Indikator_2 from the Symphonie thread. They have to repaint since they are semaphor based like the ZigZag. Finally, the histogram at the bottom is the Symphonie Matrix Indikator v1.7 from the Symphonie thread. I like this one because you can adjust it's Extreme settings to match the Extreme indicator, however it does repaint since the Extreme row is semaphor based. That is why you must wait / confirm a signal either from TDI or THV or Stochs or HA's or whatever your preference once all four lights change to the same colour. I am trying to cut down on my indis, however right now I am using this template for pull back entries, and trend reversals, hence the large variety of indicators. I hope this helps, Cheers, Pete. Hi Cobra, hats off to you to g a ve such a good system, just I want alerts for THV Ichimoku Cloud Histo indicator, so that I am requesting here. Hi coding friends including Cobra :- ) , need help to set alerts for THV Ichimoku Cloud Histo indicator, may be it takes few minutes to coding for you. So please help. Alert for single color light:- Please take THV Ichimoku Cloud Histo indicator in M1 timeframe window. Now showing the indicator 2 rows which are related timeframes M5 and M15. Then… Green light coming in M5 row then alert coming as “M5 Green”. Yellow light coming in M5 row then alert coming as “M5 Yellow”. Red light coming in M5 row then alert coming as “M5 Red”. and want same alerts for M15 row in the indicator as below Green light coming in M15 row then alert coming as “M15 Green”. Yellow light coming in M15 row then alert coming as “M15 Yellow”. Red light coming in M15 row then alert coming as “M15 Red”. Alert for two lights in the same color:- Now alerts for both lights (taking from M5 and M15 rows in the indicator) which are in same color. “M5 &amp; M15 Green” if two Green lights coming same time from M5 and M15. “M5 &amp; M15 Red” if two Red lights coming same time from M5 and M15. “M5 &amp; M15 Yellow” if two Yellow lights coming same time from M5 and M15. --- 帖子 #24310 ---
GBPUSD 6000 PIPS + Double Top(m theory)The Double Top occurs when the forex tests a resistance level twice and is unable to break it, and eventually breaks downwards and a bearish move begins. We usually trade this pattern when price breaks the neckline and we join the trend at the pullback to the broken neckline. This chart pattern usually has 73% win rate which is very good and can provide consistent profits. Attached Image (click to enlarge) 61 M.A weakly touch-back confirmation The most accurate and predictive way to use the SMA is in the bounce method: we wait for trend to establish, but instead of randomly entering, we wait for price to retrace to the moving average and bounce off it. Once a reversal signal is given we enter a trade in the direction of the trend with stop loss right below the moving average, thus entering at a tactical point with small stop loss and huge reward. ELLIOT WAVE THIORY Attached Image (click to enlarge) EE3.6 Fibonacci retracement and support and resistance confirmation The first method is for trending periods, and it include waiting for price to retrace to the moving average (confirm that the moving average is sloped and not flat) and bounces off it. Once the bounce is confirmed and price proceeds to continue the previous trend - we join the trend at a tactical point and profit. This is a very powerful trading method that can get you in trends with little risk and very high reward, and it is very accurate. It doesn't require any other Forex trading system besides the MA. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Triangle break. The triangle is one of the most neat chart patterns, as it is very easy to identify and also has a remarkable win rate of 76%. It consists of a triangle that has one trend line and one horizontal level that price eventually breaks through. As with the Double Top, we enter such trades after price pulls back to the broken horizontal level, with tight stop loss and only if risk:reward is at least 1.5:1.

--- 帖子 #24335 ---
TRIX seems to be an unbelievable indicator!!! I came across this thread a while ago and have incorporated Trix into my trading for a while now. As you might have noticed, Trix makes a really nice shape when Fast crosses slow Trix relatively close to 0 and they cross each other, especially at the beginning of a move, especially in trend direction. It's almost like Trix shows the market getting into sync to push price in either direction. I carried out an interesting test recently. I used trade sim to look for entries when you get this nice Trix shape crossover with Double CCi for confirmation of trend. I also used colour change of slow Trix for exit - now here is the clincher .... I took my candles off the chart so I was literally making entries based on Trix only. This was on EU M5 chart for one week. Results: 16 trades made using a stop loss of only 10 pips. Max draw down was no more than 6 pips, usually just spread with one possible loss of 10 pips. Total pips made - 260!! All other trades didn't even come close to stopping out as they progressed immediately. (Based on using BE if trade does not progress - total of 3 BE trades). WTF!!! This also showed me something much more important and probably the reason why so many experienced traders (I am definitely not one) keep saying 'keep it simple'. It showed me how much extra stuff I think about which stops me getting into winning trades, stops me staying in winning trades that give many more pips and gets me into losers. Way too much head static. Going back in my journal to look at some old losing trades, I am literally dumbfounded as to how I could have entered that trade in the first place lol. I suggest to people that this might be a good test of your strategy and how clogged your mind is. Try trading it with no candles (if possible).

--- 帖子 #24507 ---
Hi Alex, Yes, I'm still here. Since the only difference between the THV trixes (except for some bells and whistles like alarms and so on) is the hot param, and since the MTF trix calls a stripped down generic version of the trix that accepts the Hot param as input, all you have to do is change the hot param in the MTF trix and you will have the appropriate version of the MTF trix. (i.e if you change the hot param to 0.7 you will have an MTF trix for V3.) You can verify this by changing the hot param to 0.7 and setting the timeframe in the MTF trix to 0, and then adding the V3 trix to the same chart, and you can see that they are the same.

--- 帖子 #24514 ---
Oh, I thought you were referring to the indicator in the screen shot in that post. I don't have the source code for the indicator you attached to that post, as I wasn't involved in the release of V4. However, I have released many versions of the SAH (Swiss Army Historgram) which includes a bug fix for the extra line in the MTF cubes that showed up after one of the MT4 updates. Although the SAH does many other things besides the trix, it also does that, and you can specify the trix params for each row. You can also get an alarm on virtually any combination of rows. To get the trix, set ePeriodxType ( where x is the row) to 0 for the slow trix and 1 for the fast trix. You can find it in this post http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...84#post5471784 (and you will need to download the helper indicators referred to in that post) Documentation is here http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...10#post5379610

The following shows a tentative solution: 1. Right click on the chart. 2. Select the Object List. 3. Find the Labels named ZTHVinfo_Pxx where xx is from 10 to 34. 4. Select a Label and click Edit. 5. Check "Draw object as background" and click OK. 6. Repeat #4 and #5 for all ZTHVinfo_Pxx Hope this helps you!

Hi Anderson82, I asume you are using the new MT4 version 4.00 build 600 and up. There is a new way of where you must install your indicators and expert advisors. If you open MT4 goto file in the top left corner. Then select Open Data Folder. You will see new directories. Templates go into this Templates folder. For Indicators and EA's first select the MQL4 folder. EA's must be put in the Experts folder and indicators in the Indicators folder. I hope this clarify it for you.

... I already tried the newest ... it works!!! well done thanks ... To the other who complains that it doesnt work : this indy is working if it doesnt work maybe you put in the wrong directory because since MT4 build 600 ... the directory for indy is changing it is NOT in the directory under MT4 anymore but in the user apps data (win7). The easiest way to know where the indicator to save : 1. Open your MT4 (build 600+) 2. Click File - Open Data folder - (MT4 will open the user app data metaquotes) 3. Copy your indy to MQL4/indicators (under user app data metaquotes) 4. closed your MT4 5. run MT4 6. click View - Navigator - custom indicators 7. Drag your indicator to chart - it works! Hope it helps ...

--- 帖子 #24881 ---
Hi all. Someone just asked me for an MTF Coral so I'm sharing one with the thread. This one works on both absolute and relative scales. If you put a positive number in the eperiod1 field it will show you that coral no mater what the tf of the chart is. That is, if you put in 60, it will show you the 60m coral, whether the base chart is a 5m chart, a 60m chart or a 4 hr chart. If you put in 0 or a negative number it works like all my other mtf indies. That is, 0 = current tf, -1 = next higher tf, -2 = two tfs up and so on. For example, on a 5m chart 0 shows you the 5m coral, -1 shows you the 15m coral and -2 shows you the 30 m coral. But when you change the period of this chart to 15m you will have the 15m, 30m and 60m corals on it. Enjoy

--- 帖子 #24896 ---
Hi Ricmi, Thanks for catching that. There was a bug in my attempt to use HA candles to calculate. I think it's fixed now. If you use the default setting (which doesn't use HA candles) the SAH should now match the THV V4 MTF cloud. But, the THV V4 MTF cloud doesn't use HA candles for its calculations. If you DO want to use HA candles for the calc, then you can now set the UseHACandles param to TRUE and it will use them when checking if the candle closed above or below the cloud. (Usually there isn't a difference but on occasion there is. ) You need the helper file HeikenAshi DM (which you probably already have from the previous versions but if not here it is) Anybody downloading this for the first time should remember to download all the helper indies that the SAH needs. You can get them here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...40#post5395640 Documentation is here http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...10#post5379610

--- 帖子 #24962 ---
Aha. You don't need the mq4 file to add a file to MT4. If THX still doesn't show up after you restart MT4 then we may have located your problem because it is actually the TDI renamed. It is extremely well written with no problematic code that would cause problems and futhermore, since you don't have the mq4 file, the new compiler wouldnt make any problems for it anyway. What this probably means is that the indicator files are not in the right place. The later versions of mt4 moved where the real files are (while still leaving the old location in place) so even though you think you are copying the files to the right place you might not be, and probably the old installer doesn't put them in the right place either. You have to find out where the real indicators folder is and copy the THV files there manually. After the trix is installed in the right place you will see it in the indicators list and be able to turn that message off.

--- 帖子 #24963 ---
how to fix v4 install issues install the exe, you will see it install all the indicators before you click next look at the installation paths of everything, and go find all the installed indicators in the wrong folder. The path in stalled was experts/indicators I think, this is the wrong path with the newest versions of metatrader. Open metatrader, then go File&gt;Open Data Folder Navigate to MQL4 and there you will have your experts and indicators folder, copy everything from the wrong installed directory.

--- 帖子 #25139 ---
You can use the SAH set to etype 20 for multiple pairs. This type is red when the price is below the corel and cloud, and when the trix is crossed down and both fast and slow trixes are red. Vice versa for green. This one set for that by default and is using EURUSD GBPUSD AUDUSD AND EURJPY on the 30 minute charts. You can change those defaults by changing the ePeriod, etype and pair, of course Be sure to download the helper indies here http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...40#post5395640 . Documentation is here http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...10#post5379610 .

--- 帖子 #25357 ---
Hi, Apologies I only saw this now. I am new to trading as well but I will try my best to answer based on what I am currently reading through: It is a good question and there is no right and wrong answer to this, it really depends on what you are comfortable with. In regards to S/R and Overbought/Oversold it's best to always keep in mind that they are a result of traders decisions and as such, the further back you go the less influence they have on traders current decisions (so me personally I would look at the previous night and not the previous days). However, and this is important, just keep a look out for significant levels on the higher time frames such as the Overbought and Oversold levels on the daily charts as they will still have some level of influence to traders. I hope this helps.

The advantage this has over a standard static TP is that if market moves and your trailing stop start trailing price, it will eventually hit your standard static TP limiting your profit. --- 帖子 #24254 ---
The thing is, the oldtimers in the thread have been doing this for a long time, and after a while it gets boring answering the same questions over and over again when new people show up, especially when you know that all the information they are looking for is already in the thread and you know that the reason that they don't know the answer to the question they are asking is simply because they haven't read the thread and you know (from experience) that people who are not prepared to invest some effort (for example reading the thread) are not likely to succeed (in most things in general, and in trading all the more so). In my opinion, the name is wrong. THV is not a 'system'. ( A system being a method that tells you that everytime you see x condition, you pull the trigger and you will get y result, with hopefully positive expectancy over time). THV is more a set of tools that lets you see a good entry point WHEN market conditions are right. To understand when market conditions are right requires experience, hence the value of Ricmi's posts (and of reading the thread.) It's true that Cobra did a fantastic job of managing the thread when he was here, but he is an exceptional individual, and not many are as goodhearted and patient as he is and as you have to be to manage a thread for so long. I take my hat off to him and to Ricmi for continuing to post his trades.

Hi, To my knowledge, no custom indi can be used on MT4 Android/iOS You may try Tradeinterceptor platform for android and iOS. They have a built in trix and it is a smooth platform. The only thing I am not sure of is how the trix is smoothed in this platform. So I do not know how close the trix they have to the one used here in THV system.

--- 帖子 #25626 ---
Good Day No matter how many crosses you have for buying or shorting, the first thing to check is your overall price action. Ask yourself first: What is the overall price action context on either daily or H4 or H1 etc.. (Is it with trend trade or a counter trend one or is it a range on Higher Tfs and we are just scalping smaller Tfs within this range? and so on. It is helpful to check the daily candle to find the momentum of the day for scalping. Is there any significant Support, Resistance, Trend Lines. Is there any divergence against you on Higher time frames. If there is, then is it over or not yet? - very subjective.

Hello I hope this wonderful thread picks up soon as it used to be. I thought of sharing with you one of the ways of how to trade any system including the THV one. The way I trade is by analysing Higher Timeframe (key S/R, Trend Lines on H4, daily, weekly, etc..) and then trade divergences with break of trend lines for confirmation on smaller time frames. (It could be MACD, RSI, CCI, Trix, or any other indicator.) Once you identify the bigger picture, it will be the easiest thing to trade smaller timeframes because you know the direction you should be looking for. Any system you use will easily fit and give you premium signal. In this GBP/JPY H4, we can easily (without any guessing or effort) find a strong support of which price always visits and bounces off it. and by shifting to smaller TFs, the picture gets clearer to where we can enter with the right divergence/break of trend line combo. The key is find an entry that is as close as possible to the beginning of the move with a justified reasoning. It is a trade off between entering a bit late with confirmation or earlier. Your decision..Your call. Attached H4 and M15 I hope by sharing this, I will encourage others to interact and show what they see in the bigger picture of HTFs and how to timely enter their trades. I wanted to share more but felt the thread is dying out. I hope not! If you decide to post : Please share your view of the bigger picture and your bias before going to M5 and M15. Thanks @Ricmi I just have a comment please. Your are posting trades based on Harmonic patterns, and I am afraid this might confuse traders who are learning the THV system. I am a guest here for sure and you are one of the landlords. It is just my view that traders who are struggling with technical analysis might find harmonics off the topic and gives the impression that THV system is ditched out. What do you think? I would also kindly ask you and any other trader to give us his/her analysis of the bigger picture (HTFs). If it was just M5 and M15, and a cross of Fast trix with Slower Trix, we all would have been millionaires in no time. Thanks again for your dedication with other THV members through the years. Although I entered long before this break out I marked, but if you are conservative (which is a great thing), you could have entered at the vertical line. The reasoning behind your trade would have been anticipating a strong bullish bounce off the weekly support. We do not know how far price would bounce off and we are not predicting the market. We just believe "Market repeats itself" and "reacts" to previous S/R zones or trend lines on Higher Time Frames. NB: I attached MACD not to say that it is better or worse than trix but to demostrate that any system or indicator will nicely fit into your trading decision if "you read HTFs and pull the trigger accordingly. I am embarking on my THV system journey by participating in the MFF 50k evaluation. I will continue to post updates on my trades and the statistics of my MFF account. I'm not sure if this holds any significance, but I hope this thread becomes active again. If not, I'm content with treating my posts as a personal journal. Regarding my trading approach, I strictly follow the original rules outlined in the first post: Entry: Both Trix cross each other and have the same color at 0.00 level Price should be above/below coral as a trend filter. Price crossing Ichimoku. (my personal extra) Heiken Ashi candles should not be excessively large or have long wicks. Exit: SL/Manual close: I set SL mostly at HA bar high/low +spread, Swing Hi/Lo or Ichimoku instead of ATR. So it might be really risky but IMO, these level is kinda solid for this system, especially Ichimoku when I want to do trailing sl. TP: I choose to exit trades only at support/resistance levels and pivot lines. However, I may also adjust my risk-reward ratio if necessary (for example, when I don't want to hold a trade overnight , when my profit target is reached, or when I don't need to monitor the trade closely, etc.).
